## -O0 island kit II: register PARAMS suppress arg homing; leaf register local colors t0/a2 (not s-regs); trailing dead jr/b blocks truncatable ONLY frameless+file-terminal; empty fn at -O0 emits +1 dead jr pair (bootup 1034C 125/125 + 10AB0 47/47, 2026-07-10) <a name="feedback-ido-o0-island-kit-2"></a>

2026-07-10, agent-g, bootup_uso tail3a carve (both EXACT, ROM byte-identical).

- **`register` on PARAMETERS kills -O0 arg homing.** Plain params get
  `sw a0..a3, frame_top(sp)` homes; `register char *a0, register int a1...`
  uses the arg regs directly. This is how "-O0-flavored but unhomed-args"
  islands (bootup 10AB0, 11D78/11DBC/11E00 family) are reached. Frameless
  no-locals compound-expr forms are ALSO unhomed without `register` (11D40).
- **Leaf fns color register locals into caller-saved regs, not s-regs:**
  first free arg reg (a2 when a0/a1 taken — 11E00 target), then t0
  (all four a-regs taken — 10AB0's `or t0,a0,zero`). Non-leaf register
  locals get s0+ as usual (1034C).
- **register-only local still reserves a dead home slot** (register-first
  decl-order rule): 10AB0 frame 0x8 with nothing stored; 1034C frame 0x28.
- **-O0 dead-block geometry** (our cc emits dead code the original didn't;
  see the 11B5C double-b cap entry):
  - frameless fn ending in `return expr`: dead `jr ra; nop` pairs land
    AFTER the live code -> clip with TRUNCATE_TEXT, but ONLY when the fn is
    file-terminal (o0_11D40 precedent; bootup 11D78/11DBC land the same way:
    `if (x==0) { return *p; return; } return 0.0f;` — the dead bare
    `return;` reproduces the target's interior dead pair, bytes 0..0x3C
    exact, trailing 2 pairs truncatable).
  - FRAMED fn ending in `return expr`: the dead `b epi` sits BEFORE the
    epilogue block = inside the fn = NOT truncatable. This is the 11B5C
    double-b cap generalized: bootup 11E00/11ED4/11FA8 triplet decodes to 6
    branch-offset diffs (all from that one extra word) — otherwise-exact C
    is `if(guard==0){ if(idx==-1){ i=0; if(n>0) do{...}while(++i<n); goto
    ret0; } check-arm } ret0: return 0;` with register params + `register
    int *p`. Probed dead-label/dead-while tails: no effect. FEE8/FC28/FD4C
    same family. Check the TAIL before decoding: framed + terminal
    value-return = capped; void or frameless = landable.
  - EMPTY fn at -O0 emits TWO jr pairs (target has one) -> empty stubs
    cannot sit interior in an -O0 file; keep them in -O2 neighbors.
- **Slot/record indexed access via ARRAY FORM** `((Row*)(a0+0x88))[idx].v`
  gives base-first `addu t,BASE,scaled` + folded displacement at -O0 too
  (pointer-arith spelling emits offset-first addu and cascades temp
  rotation for the rest of the fn). Multi-field: one view struct at the
  lowest offset (((Rec*)(a0+0x84))[i].f88 etc.), sizeof = stride.
- **Nonzero-offset extern-struct-member does NOT flip -O0 value-load base
  reuse** (12818 cap): `lui t5; lw t5,off(t5)` reuse persists for struct
  members at any offset; only array form gives a fresh dest (+1 insn).

<a id="feedback-ido-d9cc-phantom-spill-var-kit"></a>
## m2c phantom spill-slot var + var-first decl-order frame fix + FP merge/split flip (game_uso_func_0000D9CC 90.8->98.96, 2026-07-10)

524-insn FP-cascade spine, previously carrying a wrong "frame overlap / coloring not C-controllable" cap verdict. Six independent C-level roots fixed in one pass (agent-g):

1. **Phantom spill-slot var:** m2c emitted a write-only `f32 sp34` where every `sp34 = N;` immediately preceded `var_a3 = N;`. The target's `sw a3,52(sp)`/`lw a3,52(sp)` around each jal is var_a3's SPILL, which m2c double-decoded as a separate stack var. Detection: write-only spXX + a call-live twin var assigned the same constants. Delete the phantom (frame shrinks a slot).
2. **Frame hole (4 words) = spill homed below named locals:** build had locals 60/64/68 + a3-spill 40 + hole 44-56 (frame -80); target packs 40/44/48 + spill 52 (frame -56). Fix: declare the call-spilled var (var_a3) FIRST among locals — its spill then takes the top home slot and the hole vanishes. Confirms the "NAMED-LOCAL COUNT / decl order governs frame" entry at big scale.
3. **FP pair-swap cascade flip:** target used ONE abs-result var ($f0) against TWO compare-source temps ($f2 twice). Merging the m2c result vars (var_f0_2/_3 -> var_f0) while SPLITTING the source var back (temp_f2 / temp_f2_2) flipped the entire $f0<->$f2 cascade (~25 insns). Decl-order reorder alone = zero movement (live-range-driven). The knob is merge/split (live-range shape), not order.
4. **`goto` join label placement is a scheduling knob:** giving the early arm its own `var_v1 = FW(...)` reload + `goto after_24;` with `after_24:;` INSIDE the enclosing if reproduced the target's dup'd `lw v1` in the b-delay slot (defeats cross-jumping) with no schedule damage; the same label OUTSIDE the if (one brace later, same CFG node) added a BB barrier that broke the next block's lui/mtc1 hoists and cost 5 insns.
5. **Volatile pure-read operand order:** for `field * (*(volatile f32*)(p+0x10))` gates re-read per arm, the volatile deref must be the FIRST operand or the two lwc1 emit swapped. Also: pointer-form `p = base+0x2FC; FF(p,0)=..` reproduces a dead `addiu v0,v0,764` after folded stores.
6. **INT compares masquerading as float in m2c:** target `lw/li 1/bne` for `FW(0x114)==1` (m2c wrote `FF(...)==1.0f`) and `lw/bnezl` for `FW(0x9CC)==0` (m2c wrote float ==0). And a `1.0f <=` gate whose constant is a GLOBAL load `*(f32*)(&game_uso_D_807FF68C+4248)` (USO explicit-addend spelling, like the Pair2 args `&D_807FF478+0xE88`). Always check the target opcode class (lw vs lwc1 / bne vs bc1x) before trusting m2c's float types — three separate float-literal fabrications in one function.

Residual 31 insns = documented tie classes only: beqzl/bc1fl-vs-plain+nop at 2 head gates (as1 branch form), one c.lt.d/lui adjacent-pair swap, $f12<->$f14 (temp_f14/var_f12, merge/split immune here), a3-spill-vs-store pre-jal order, zeros-vs-1.0f mtc1/swc1 emission order, andi-temp coalescing (u16 cast + var split both coalesce).

## Proc-USO big-fn kit III: jumptable-threshold cascade fix, m2c-local removal, typed-load CSE boundaries (timproc b5 1F14 / b3 1C68 / titproc 116C, 2026-07-10) <a name="proc-uso-big-fn-kit-3-2026-07-10"></a>

Three big proc-USO NM wraps pushed 83.6->84.2, 84.0->95.1, 86.4->93.5 with one
coherent lever family (agent-h). All verified by objdiff fuzzy + full ROM cmp.

1. **5-label jumptable threshold neutralizes the external-jumptable cap's
   cascade (titproc 116C).** The documented PERMANENT cap (dispatch through
   `%hi/%lo(import_XXXX+0x30)`, PATTERNS.md) had been treated as a whole-body
   ceiling because the 4-case compare-chain fallback desyncs the ugen temp
   ring for EVERY following block. Adding `case 4: break;` (semantically dead:
   state 4 exits either way) crosses IDO's 5-label jumptable threshold: emits
   `sltiu at,t6,5` + a LOCAL .rodata table. Only 2 head words differ (sltiu
   imm, guard beq offset; the local table's %lo even matched 0x30 here), and
   the jumptable form consumes t6 exactly like the target = whole-body ring
   re-sync. Generalizes: when an irreproducible head desyncs the ring, look
   for a semantically-dead source change that restores the head's TEMP
   CONSUMPTION even if 1-2 words stay wrong.

2. **m2c-local removal is the master un-coalescing/coloring lever.** m2c loves
   `flag = *(int*)(p+0x3C); if (flag==1)...` — the local becomes an M-var
   candidate whose init load does NOT coalesce (extra `or aN,vN` copy, split
   webs, wrong colors: b3 1C68's `bc` v1+a0-copy, b5 1F14's flag v1+a0).
   Spelling direct derefs everywhere makes the load-CSE web itself the
   candidate: one register, no copy, const-first bne operand order, natural
   reload placement after aliasing stores, and the web inherits CALL-ARG
   PRECOLORS — passing `*(char**)(arg0+0xB8)` as a0-arg twice colored the
   whole bc web a0 (cupcosts `lu->reg != reg` discount). Related: a helper
   var SHARED across N sites (`vt` in 8 constructor-call idioms) is one
   LR colored an a-reg with copies; per-site names (vt2..vt8) give
   block-local webs that each color v0 like the target.

3. **int-vs-char** load typing draws CSE/reload boundaries.** `*(int*)(p+K)`
   and `*(char**)(p+K)` are DISTINCT ichains. 1C68's ramp arms must RELOAD
   the bc pointer per-arm (fresh t-temps) while the gates/join reuse the held
   a0: typing the arm loads `*(int*)(arg0+0xB8)` and the gate/join loads
   `*(char**)` reproduces exactly that split. (An int STORE also doesn't kill
   a char**-load's availability — the alias classes differ — which is why the
   all-char** spelling CSE'd where the target reloaded.)

4. **Store-forwarded `|=` emits ori-from-zero.** After `*(p+0x3C) = 0` (sw
   zero in a branch delay), `*(p+0x3C) |= 1` CSEs the load to the known zero
   and emits `ori tN,zero,1` (0x34xx0001) — the addiu form comes from `= 1`.

5. **Compound RMW = un-coalesced two-reg shape.** `*(p+K) = *(p+K) - 1;
   if (*(p+K) < 0)` emits lw tA / addiu tB,tA,-1 / sw tB with the compare
   CSE-ing tB. A named temp (`t = *(p+K) - 1; *(p+K) = t`) coalesces to one
   register. Same for `+= 1` state bumps (titproc case-0's `= 1` is really
   `+= 1`: lw/addiu/sw).

6. **NEGATIVE results (documented caps, don't re-probe):**
   - Whole-function constant with call-arg affinity (1F14's `2`->a3, 116C's
     `40`->v0): the ichain splits into a compare/store web + per-call arg
     webs; the compare web prices the arg reg by cupcosts' GENERIC phi
     shortcut (reg not in used_by_func) and the tie breaks by enumeration to
     t0/a1. The target's merged web carries precolored liveunits and wins the
     arg reg. Probed exhaustively: phantom 4th-arg (still worth adding when
     the target remats aN=K after calls — emission-neutral and matches), 
     unsigned web-splits (moved the color but target keeps ONE web: no
     `addiu at,zero,2` in target = candidate serves compares too), named
     `two` (copy-propped inert), register-kw, while(0){x=4}/dead-if ref
     boosts (deleted pre-analoop), switch reshape, coloring-search depth-1:
     SPACE EXHAUSTED. Take the t-ring +1 cascade as one cap.
   - como-hoist of a single-arm cheap def (addiu ptr+32, lui/addiu &SYM,
     addiu 720) above its guarding branch: steals v0/v1 there and knocks on
     (r->a0, a1-var->a2+copy). fl2-split/cast/folded-arm probes inert.
   - Conditional-call arg-pair scheduling (or a0,s0 vs addiu a1,1 in the
     cond-block load-delay slot): as1 pick, probe-immune (casts, 1u, order).



## Constructor-family kit: macro-scope frame slots, if(1) &local-fold barrier, single pointer temp, loop-web rank (4B620)
<a name="feedback-ido-4b620-constructor-kit"></a>

2026-07-10, gl_func_0004B620 (1236-byte cb-driven constructor, game_libs_post0b) 86.19 -> 92.92 fuzzy, 159/309 words position-exact standalone. Retracts the 2026-06-22 "inlined iterator-ctor returning by value = cap" verdict. Levers, in the order they paid:

1. **Guard fold barrier.** Target keeps a dead `addiu s0,sp,K; bne s0,zero,skip; or s3,s0; jal alloc(0xC); beq v0,zero,skip2; or s3,v0` get-or-alloc guard on a stack iterator. Plain `Iter *ip = &it; if (ip != 0 || (ip = alloc(12)))` folds (&local provably nonnull). `ip = 0; if (1) { ip = &it; }` then the short-circuit if emits the FULL guard, byte-shaped, with &it in the tested register. Array-decay, `&it.member`, goto barriers, register — all fold. This makes the "dead-alloc stack-buffer" idiom (PATTERNS builder-family entry, previously "unreliable/0-of-4") reliably reproducible.
2. **Macro-scoped temps = frame slots per expansion.** Each `do { DLList *_dl; DLHead *_h; s32 _n; Gfx *_cmd; ... } while(0)` expansion reserved 16 bytes of frame at -O2 even with everything colored (9 appends = +144 bytes: built frame 0x108 vs target 0xB0). Moving the temps to function scope collapsed the frame and is what the ORIGINAL source shape must have been. Diagnostic: frame delta >> live locals, with clean 16-byte-per-repeat arithmetic.
3. **Volatile-pad offset sculpting** then placed it/it2/it3 at the exact 0x60/0x6C/0xA4 homes (decl order = top-down; 7 pads between top aggregate and the rest, 2 below).
4. **Single mutated pointer temp.** One `char *p` reused as (a) alloc-fallback sub-object, (b) per-append DL-handle reload (`lw s2,204(s4)` per append — handle re-read, not cached), (c) per-call loop node — one candidate whose union range crosses the loop calls -> s2, and its existence flips self->s4/arg1->s0 (5-sreg prologue, target-exact save order). The FIRST append after each alloc reads via the return-value variable directly (v0, no `or s2,v0` copy) — spell it with a separate one-shot var, not p.
5. **Volatile node-load CSE-bust** for the target's duplicate `addu rX,base,idx4; addu rY,base,idx4` + double node load per call (distinct-addr twin): spell one arg's node deref `*(s32 * volatile *)((char *)*it3.ptr + (it3.idx * 4))`.

**Rank mechanics learned (uoptlist-confirmed):** uopt assigns s0,s1,s2,... in candidate-RANK order; loop-body webs carry x10 weight and rank first. Our loop's CSE-cached `sll idx` / `*ptr` webs stole s0/s1 from the target's straight-line append temps. Busting the caches (per-use volatile reload) frees the regs; but deliberately adding loop uses to a shared temp to force callee coloring overflowed to 6 saved regs (self->s5) and netted WORSE — the s-reg budget is the binding constraint.

**Residual (documented cap for this fn):** (a) target's h/n append temps are whole-candidate callee colorings (h@appends3-9=s0, n=s3) where our per-web coloring picks v1/a0 — same-variable spelling, register keyword, while(0) ref-boost all left the webs split; (b) iterator-next ternary-phi shape `or v0,zero; slt; beq; ...; beq 0,0; addu v0(delay)` — comma-side-effect ternaries flatten to plain if (the &&-ternary lever needs side-effect-free arms); (c) 3-word prologue or-vs-sw schedule tie. Class: uopt web-split/rank ties.

**Ops note:** NM body growth (+0x1C) in game_libs_post0b pushes the NON_MATCHING_TEXT_CLIP_KEEP_ALIGN tail — re-measure the clip to the new end of the LAST symbol (62F08) or it silently drops from 100 (0x2b6d0 -> 0x2b70c here). A neighbouring NM fn's fuzzy moving ~1pp with BYTE-IDENTICAL output is an objdiff label-render artifact of the section shift, not a regression — verify with raw word diff before reverting anything.

<a id="feedback-ido-gui-dispatch-param-kit"></a>
## gui dispatch/param kit: switch-sorts-ascending, nested-!= beq-to-body, param-reassign scratch, if(0) address-escape (gui_func_000027A0 / gui_func_00003B80, 2026-07-10)

Two gui_uso RDP-DL builders (siblings of the D9CC kit), agent-g:

1. **Dispatch form identification.** Target shape: `beq v,K1,body1; beq v,K2,body2; beq v,K3,body3; <default inline>; b join` with bodies stacked after the default and per-arm constant `li`s speculated into the beq delay slots. Elimination table:
   - IDO **switch** = compare chain in ASCENDING case-value order (source case order irrelevant). If the target's compare order isn't sorted, it's not a switch.
   - `==` else-if chain = `bnel`+INLINE arms (branch-likely skip form).
   - flat `goto` dispatch = re-inlined/normalized by uopt.
   - **NESTED-`!=`** (default innermost: `if (v!=K1){ if (v!=K2){ if (v!=K3){default} else {arm3} } else {arm2} } else {arm1}`) = the beq-to-body shape with compares in K1,K2,K3 order. Residual: uopt picks BODY placement order itself (build innermost-first; goto-pinning doesn't stick, fuzzy-neutral).
2. **Param-reassign-as-scratch.** When the target reuses an incoming arg reg as general scratch (halfword temp, mode value, DL cursor index, gctx pointer), assign to the PARAM variable in C (`a1 = *(short*)(info+0x20); s8 -= a1;`). Effects: frees t-ring pressure, forces the target's prologue `move sX,aY` copy (the copy exists precisely because the param web is cut), and if the param's ORIGINAL value is still needed in exactly one late arm (3B80's `default: max = a3;`), IDO reproduces the spill-to-local + reload shape.
3. **if(0) address-escape un-promotes a reassigned param.** 3B80's x-cursor (`a1 += rows` inside the call loop) was $s7-promoted in the build but memory-homed in the target (`lw t,124(sp); addu; sw` per iteration). `if (0) { gl_func(&a1); }` (placed AFTER the decls — C89) forces a1 memory-resident; +2pp and un-steals the s-reg. Note it also homed a2/a3 — acceptable there since the target homes them too; don't use where the target keeps params in registers.
4. **Metric gotcha:** a homebrew aligned-instruction count and objdiff's fuzzy_match_percent DISAGREE on variant ranking (fuzzy tolerates sp-offset renames, weighs block shape; aligned-count doesn't). 27A0's ==-chain scored equal aligned but -2pp fuzzy vs the switch. Gate every knob decision on the official fuzzy (objdiff-cli one-shot `diff -u <unit> <sym> -o json` reads match_percent without a full report run).

### Proc-USO HUD/widget-draw kit — float-field, color-Vec array, div-by-denom, FP-numbering steering (2026-07-10)

Recurring across the arcproc/timproc/mgrproc HUD & widget-draw family (agent-h; each moved a 78-85% wrap +5-15pp). All FP-shape levers, verified by objdiff fuzzy:

1. **Float-field-load fix.** m2c decodes a struct field read as an int load + `cvt.s.w` when the target uses `lwc1` directly. If the target reads `*(float*)(p+0xN)` (opcode `lwc1`), spell the field as `float`, not `(float)*(int*)`. (mgrproc 23FC: field 0x7A0 is a float → +5.5pp; the four `255.0f*FW(...)` alpha reads were int-load+convert.)
2. **Color-Vec array aliasing (DCE fix).** A color/vector passed to a draw call by `&firstElem` MUST be a real array (`float col[4]`), not N separate float scalars. Separate non-escaped scalar stores get dead-code-eliminated by IDO (the address never escapes), losing ~4-19 insns; the array makes the whole block escape and emit. (timproc_b5 BDEC: `{c,c,c,f2}` as 4 scalars → `float col[4]` recovered ~19 insns, +13.4pp. Also caught a missing leading `arg0` on the draw call.)
3. **Divide-by-`denom`-variable to force runtime `div.s`.** `x / 255.0f` const-folds to a literal/rodata reciprocal multiply; the target keeps a runtime `div.s`. Introduce `float denom = 255.0f;` and divide by the VARIABLE — IDO can't const-fold through it, emits `div.s`. (timproc_b5 1460 +15.5pp; colors written as literal `N.0f/255.0f` for the const-fold arms, the runtime channel divided by `denom`.) Residual float-const-CSE (a `255/255` numerator landing on `denom`'s reg) is unbreakable from C — the cap floor for this shape.
4. **FP-register-numbering steering (load-in-arm / fresh-temp / value-in-branch).** To match the target's `$f`-register choices in a branchy FP chain: (a) move a shared load (e.g. `progress`) INSIDE each branch arm so a dead const (`1.0f`) can reuse the freed `$f0`; (b) store `val ± Dconst` into a FRESH temp (`$f8`/`$f18`) rather than reusing; (c) compute a derived quantity (`span = 0xA0 - (sum>>1)`) INSIDE each sign-branch instead of via a shared `half` local, so IDO spills the wanted var not the intermediate. (arcproc 125C: all three → whole FP chain byte-exact, +9.7pp.)
5. **Two nearby FP/data consts → DISTINCT scalar externs, NOT an array.** When the target reaches two (or more) nearby pooled consts (e.g. `&D+0xB8` and `&D+0xC0` f64 pair, or two float-pool words) via SEPARATE `lui $at` — each folding `%lo` into its own `ldc1/lwc1` displacement (`ldc1 184($at)` / `ldc1 192($at)`) — spell them as distinct SCALAR externs at the exact addresses (`extern f64 D_dbl_X_B8, D_dbl_X_C0;`), NOT an `extern f64 arr[]` indexed `arr[23]/[24]`. Array-decay forces IDO to materialize ONE shared base pointer into a general register via `lui vN; addiu vN,vN,0` (an extra `addiu`, wrong reg class), which cascades the entire surrounding FP schedule. The distinct-scalar form emits the target's per-const `lui $at` + `%lo`-fold and realigns the block. (timproc_b5 1DB0: array→distinct-scalar 93.97%→99.55%, one edit. Generalizes the single-const `$at`-fold rule to the *multi-const* case. NOTE: this is the OPPOSITE of the CSE-busting story for a single base reused many times — here the two consts are each read once, so per-const rematerialization IS the target form. Residual after: commutative FP operand-order canonicalization on `mul.d/add.d/mul.s` is not C-reachable — IDO reverses operands regardless of source order.)

Skip (verified caps this family): h2hproc 620/C18/17A0 (alloc-cascade coalescing + permuter-floored coloring), mgrproc E04, titproc 5DC + timproc_b1 EE8 (held-base form-a/form-b coloring coin-flip), timproc_b5 1F14 (cupcosts phi tie).

### gui_uso f3dex2 DL-builder: ctx-pointer double-reload per packet (2026-07-10)

The gui_uso RDP display-list builders emit each GBI packet by reloading the GfxCtx pointer (`a0->0xC`) **twice per packet** — once for the `->idx` read+bump, once for the `->buf` write base — because the store to `->idx` forces IDO to re-fetch the possibly-aliased ctx pointer (no `restrict`). NM bodies that load it once and reuse the register cap at ~48-51%. Fix: model the ring as `struct GfxRing {int *buf; int idx;}` and dereference `a0->0xC` a SECOND time for the base AFTER the `->idx` store. Also lazy-compute per-packet temps at first use (not hoisted) to match target scheduling. Packet 1 then matches byte-for-byte. Moved gui_uso_func_0000413C/00004354/00003F18 +16-20pp each. Residual (not exact): cross-packet CSE + slot-pointer coloring (a3 vs t2) — regalloc cascade cap C can't pin. Variant idiom: some builders (00002DE0/0000329C/00003714, gui_func_00004568 TEXRECT) use a `s0[0xC/4]` re-indexing double-deref instead — same principle, already at 68-70%.

### K&R `()` → variadic `(float, ...)` forces SINGLE-float $f12 + keeps direct jal (2026-07-10)

When a function calls a routine whose FIRST arg is a float (e.g. `gl_func_00043824`), a K&R file-scope decl `extern int f();` makes IDO **double-promote** the float: `cvt.d.s`/`sdc1`, `$f12` occupies BOTH a0+a1 slots, pushing ptr/int args to a2/a3 and bloating the frame. The target often passes the float SINGLE in `$f12` with ptr/int in a1/a2. Fix: change the file-scope decl to variadic `extern int f(float, ...);` — the named `float` param passes single in `$f12`, varargs fill a1/a2, and the call stays a **direct `jal`** (NOT a fnptr cast — casts add lui/addiu/jalr, 3 insns; see the K&R-direct-call-vs-fnptr-cast entry). A block-scope prototype does NOT work (IDO errors `redeclaration ... prototype and non-prototype` against the K&R decl). Variadic is compatible with all existing call sites that pass float first, so it doesn't break siblings (2F720's sibling gl_func_0002E354, also calls 43824, rose 71.17→71.23, no regression). Landed game_libs_func_0002F720 stub→full decode 26.79→34.92 fuzzy. NOTE: also confirms most game_libs low-fuzzy [25,72) functions are NOT stubs but documented caps (Duff-unroll, branch-likely idioms, USO `jal 0` reloc-blocked) — only genuinely under-emitting placeholder bodies (emit-insns << target) are stub-vein targets; measure emit/target ratio, don't assume low-fuzzy = stub.

### m2c float-field width bloat: retype `*(s32*)` → `*(f32*)` on the swc1/lwc1 offsets (huge decode-correctness rises, 2026-07-10)

The single highest-yield fix for under-reconstructed USO grafts (fuzzy 9-30% on 2KB+ functions): m2c frequently types float struct fields as `*(s32*)(base + off)`, making IDO emit float→int→float round-trips (`cvt.s.w` / `trunc.w.s`) plus `sw`/`lw` where the target uses `swc1`/`lwc1` — pure width bloat, not missing logic. Fix: extract the exact float-access offset sets from the expected `.s` (`grep -oE 'swc1\t\$f[0-9]+,[0-9]+\(BASE\)'` and the lwc1 equivalent), retype ONLY those `*(s32*)((char*)base + off)` accesses to `*(f32*)`, and strip spurious `(f32)`/`(s32)` casts on `*((s32*)&local + N)` union-copy lines (keep those as pure int bit-copies — the Vec3 snapshot idiom). Moved bootup func_0000C234 8.9→58% (insn 746→546) and func_0000B75C 29→66% (662→535) in one pass each.

**Diagnostic tell (decides fixable-vs-cap before you touch the body):** compare the NM object's insn count to the target's. NM count **>>** expected + high `trunc.w.s`/`cvt.s.w` count = width bloat → **fixable** by retyping. NM count **<** expected + zero conversions = undersized/regalloc-or-missing-logic → the documented saved-reg/scheduling cap class (e.g. bootup 55A0/90CC: `$f20`-for-zero + prologue schedule + multi-base var mapping), **skip** for width work. Pairs with the base-symbolization lever (thread `char *base = (char*)&D_00000000` through absolute-addr m2c literals) — but base-symbolization REGRESSES already-partial decodes, so honor monotonicity.

### Held `f32 two = 2.0f;` local forces `mul.s` where IDO -O2 strength-reduces `expr * 2.0f` → `add.s` (2026-07-10)

When the target multiplies a float by a register-held constant (`lui 0x4000; mtc1 $f,at; mul.s x,y,$f`) but your C `x = y * 2.0f;` emits `add.s x,y,y` (IDO -O2 strength-reduces multiply-by-2 to a self-add), route the literal through a single reused local: `f32 two = 2.0f; ... x = y * two;`. IDO materializes-and-holds the constant in a register, emitting the target's `mul.s` instead of the folded `add.s`. Companion to the m2c float-field width-fix; raised timproc_uso_b5_func_0000AC20 37.6→44.1%. Generalizes to any float constant the target keeps in a register across uses (declare it once as a local, reuse it).

### Typed-float placeholder prototypes + Vec3 by-value struct-copy modeling (raw-word USO decode, 2026-07-10)

Two levers for reconstructing raw-word USO functions with `func_00000000` placeholder calls and vector marshalling (bootup 31C0 +14pp, 8BD4 +24pp):

1. **Typed-float prototypes on placeholder callees.** A bare/K&R `func_00000000(...)` call double-promotes every float arg (`cvt.d.s` + `sdc1` pairs, frame bloat) where the target passes single-precision. Declare distinct typed externs (`extern void fn_name(void*, float, float, ...)`) for each placeholder callee — this both suppresses the double-promotion (emits single `swc1`/`mtc1`) AND still produces a relocated `jal` (0x0C000000 + R_MIPS_26) matching the target. Reusable across the whole raw-word USO placeholder-call family. (Companion to the K&R→variadic single-f12 lever.)

2. **Vec3 by-value struct-copy modeling.** When IDO marshals a Vec3/vector argument by VALUE, it emits word-by-word `lw`/`sw` stack copies that element-wise float copies (`lwc1`/`swc1` per component) do NOT reproduce. Define `struct { float x, y, z; }` and use plain struct assignment (`dst = src;`) — IDO then emits the target's int lw/sw marshalling. Pair with a shared negated temp (`float negamt = -amt;`) to force `neg.s`-then-`cvt.d.s` where separate negations would emit `neg.d`.

Both leave the function NON_MATCHING (residual = the usual fp-regalloc/frame cap: target parks a live-across-call float in callee-saved `$f20` via sdc1/ldc1 vs the natural caller-saved reg) — decode-correctness rises, not exact. NOTE also: kernel func_800014A8 is a splat TWO-FUNCTION mis-split (concatenates the loader loop at 0x24A8 + a second init fn at 0x80001594 under one symbol) — hard-capped ~33% until a splat boundary fix at 0x80001594; out-of-scope infra.

### objdiff fuzzy is mnemonic-level: callee-NAME resolution alone = 0pp; only STRUCTURE/width/logic moves it (2026-07-11)

Refinement to the "wrong-callee = fixable decode error" diagnostic: objdiff's fuzzy_match_percent compares mnemonics + registers, NOT R_MIPS_26 reloc-target NAMES. So replacing a `func_00000000` placeholder callee with the real resolved symbol (`jal placeholder` → `jal real_sym`) is byte-different but fuzzy-IDENTICAL — 0pp movement (verified on timproc_b5 5BF0: 8 placeholder→real jals, 59.065→59.065; and func_000032C8 held at 48.76%). What DOES move fuzzy is a change to callee COUNT or STRUCTURE: splitting one collapsed placeholder into TWO distinct calls in an if/else (m2c collapses distinct callees when it can't resolve them — the target's `then→funcA; else→funcB` became one placeholder), reordering, or an inserted/removed call. So: pure name-resolution is decode-correctness/episode-quality only (do it for correctness, but don't expect a fuzzy rise); a fuzzy rise from "wrong callees" requires the collapsed-distinct-callees or wrong-call-count case. (Caveat: raw-word USO segments also carry a structural cap — 731 R_MIPS_HI16 / 0 LO16, data low-halves baked as immediates — so even byte-exact is blocked there until proper mnemonic disasm.)

### Widening narrow prototype params to s32 removes IDO entry-arg-masking (2026-07-11)

When a function's field is STORED narrow (`sh`/`sb`) but its prototype declares the param as `u16`/`u8`/`s8`, IDO emits entry-time argument masking (`andi 0xffff` / `andi 0xff` / `sll+sra`) that the target lacks. Widen the narrow params to `s32` in the prototype (the field write stays narrow via the per-field `*(s16*)`/`*(u8*)` cast) — this drops the entry masks. Combine with per-field width retype + reusing an arg register as an accumulator to fix register coloring. Took game_libs_func_0002E0C4 42→87%. Companion to the m2c float-field + halfword/byte width-fix. TRIAGE TIP: a batch op-histogram scanner (per-function count of sw/lw/sh/lh/sb/lbu/swc1/lwc1/cvt.s.w/trunc.w.s in NM .o vs expected .o) finds width-bloat candidates across a whole segment fast — NM having FEWER sh/sb/lwc1 or MORE cvt/trunc than target = a fixable width error. game_libs (244 band fns) still has such candidates; game_uso/proc-USO/bootup 35-70% bands are worked out (callees wired, widths typed, remainder = regalloc/scheduling caps).

### Struct-copy width refinement: local→local copies are int lw/sw, but pointer/arg-access of the same struct stays float (2026-07-11)

Refining the "retype f32 struct fields to s32 for int-word copies" lever: when a function both COPIES a Vec3/struct between stack LOCALS (`spB = spA`) and separately LOADS/STORES the same struct through an ARG or POINTER, the two access classes emit differently. IDO emits **local→local** struct copies as int `lw`/`sw` word blocks (so retype those fields to a plain int struct + struct-assignment). But **pointer/arg-based** access of the same struct is stack-spilled by the target as `lwc1`/`swc1` (keep those as `*(f32*)`). So don't blanket-retype the whole struct type — split by access site: int struct for the local-copy chain, `*(f32*)&` casts for the pointer reads. Took gl_func_00064DEC 42→53%; also drop spurious `(s32)`/`(f32)` casts that force cvt/trunc/mtc1/mfc1. (game_libs_post1b family: 652D8 41→67, 64388 41→50, 64DEC 42→53.)

### Callback-returning-float decode + decode-fixes-reaching-100-DO-move-the-headline (2026-07-11)

**Decode recipe (raw-word USO):** when a callback/reset function's RETURN is stored into a float accumulator, the target emits `jal cb; ... swc1 $f0, off(x)` INSIDE the guard, and the guard is `!= 0` (`beqzl`). m2c frequently mis-decodes this as a void call + an unconditional `0.0f` store (`mtc1 zero`) OUTSIDE the `if`. Fix: declare the callback float-returning + call it directly (`jal`), store its `$f0` result into the accumulator inside a single-block `if (x != 0) { ... }` guard. Took gl_func_00029B6C 54.5→**100%** (reached exact).

**KEY HEADLINE INSIGHT:** a decode-correctness fix that reaches 100% fuzzy DOES move the matched_code headline % — even as an INCLUDE_ASM/NM wrap with no formal episode — because objdiff is reloc-aware and counts any 100%-scoring body as matched. So the "decode rises don't move the headline" rule is only true for SUB-100 rises; a decode fix that lands EXACT (or reloc-blind-100) increments the count (29B6C took 2200→2201, 27.89→27.90%). Chase the near-exact decode fixes (95%+ with only reloc-blind/scheduling residual) — some cross 100 on the full reloc-aware build even when they measured <100 in isolation.

### `(f32)N` cast-literal CSE-break for NON-ZERO float constants in const/const division (2026-07-11)

Extension of the `(float)0`-vs-`0.0f` zero-CSE-break lever to non-zero constants: when `x = 255.0f / div255` where `div255` is a named `255.0f` variable, IDO const-folds the `255.0f` NUMERATOR with the divisor's `255.0f` and collapses to `div.s f,f` (self-divide). The target keeps a DISTINCT 255.0 numerator. Write the numerator in the cast-literal form `(f32)255` (not `255.0f`) — this defeats the fold and forces the distinct constant + real `div.s`. Pairs with the shared-`div255`-divisor recipe (keep divisor as a named variable, force numerator to a distinct literal form). Took gl_func_00003138 84→97%. Also pairs with counter-sink (move `i += 1` to the loop tail so IDO fills the `jal` delay slot with the increment).

### Crossing-hunt: re-verify "caller-set-register" caps + `(char*)&D` vs `(int)&D` reloc-preservation (2026-07-11)

Two levers that produced EXACT crossings (headline movers) from functions previously tagged as permanent caps:

1. **Re-verify "caller-set-register" cap verdicts — a `lui;addiu;lw` prologue is a GLOBAL LOAD, not a caller-set reg.** gl_func_00008674 was documented "GENUINE caller-set-int-reg CAP" but was actually a global-table indirect dispatch: `obj = *(int**)(&D_00000000 + 0x28); obj->fn64(&D_00000000 + (s16)obj->off60)` reusing the live base register (incoming a0 homed via `&unused`). Reconstructed → byte-exact. LESSON: before trusting a "caller-set $tN/$vN" cap note, check whether the entry `lui;addiu` pair + `lw` is loading a GLOBAL (via `&D_00000000`) rather than reading a caller-provided register — many are mis-tagged and reconstruct to exact.

2. **`(char*)&D_00000000 + off` preserves the `lui %hi/addiu %lo` reloc; `(int)&D + off` FOLDS to raw `ori`.** Because `D_00000000` is an absolute-0 symbol, integer arithmetic `(int)&D + off` collapses to a plain `ori` immediate (loses the descriptor reloc), while POINTER arithmetic `(char*)&D + off` keeps the `lui/addiu` %hi/%lo reloc form the target uses. Use the `(char*)` form for base-symbolize. (gl_func_00000D5C 77→exact.)

3. **Get-or-create-with-dead-inner-alloc constructor template** (D5C/11A4 family): outer alloc-fail routes to a SHARED `done:` label (returns the zeroed accumulator), not a separate `return 0`; inner alloc-fail skips only the sub-init block via `goto skip_init`; a dead inner `alloc(size)` sub-object is often present (reconstruct it). A distinct absolute-0 symbol (`&gl_data_00000000`) as a CSE-break stops IDO spilling a shared `&D` reg across the call. Reusable across constructor siblings. GENERAL: the "re-examine documented caps with fresh eyes" approach keeps retracting caps into exacts — the 80-99% band is not all regalloc.

4. **Re-verify "o32 float-ABI cap" wrappers — `mtc1 a1,$f12` … `mfc1 a1,$f12` is a reproducible float round-trip, not an impossible ABI combination.** A `float` 2nd arg (after an int 1st arg) DOES arrive o32-correctly in the *integer* reg `$a1`; IDO's standard float-param prologue homes it to `$f12` (`mtc1 a1,$f12`), and passing it on as the callee's float 2nd arg reads it back with `mfc1 a1,$f12` (net no-op bit round-trip, matching the target). gl_func_0002DF68 was tagged "int-$a0 + float-$f12 is n32/n64-only, impossible under -32" — WRONG; the leading `mtc1` was mistaken for a predecessor's stolen prologue when it is this function's own float-home. The *real* obstacle is only that the shared `gl_func_00000000` jal-0 placeholder is declared K&R (`int f();`), so passing a `float` through it double-promotes (`cvt.d.s` → `a2/a3`). FIX: call one of the pre-declared distinct absolute-0 typed aliases in `undefined_syms_auto.txt` (`gl_func_00000000_f`, `_ff`, `_ll`, `_va`, …) with a real prototype (`extern int gl_func_00000000_f(int, float);`) — the jal bytes stay `0x0C000000` (symbol resolves to 0) and no whole-file K&R-vs-prototype conflict arises (a block- or file-scope prototype of the *shared* name errors: "prototype and non-prototype declaration … not compatible"). gl_func_0002DF68 0→exact. LESSON: any "float can't reach that register under o32" cap that calls a shared K&R jal-0 placeholder is likely a mis-tag — the ABI is fine, the promotion is the blocker, and the typed absolute-0 alias defeats it.

### USO baked-reloc LANDABILITY FILTER: objdiff-100 ≠ landable; only reloc-free / placeholder-jal-only bodies pass the raw-byte cmp (2026-07-11)

Critical distinction for game_libs (a relocatable USO) crossings. objdiff scores 100% when the build's reloc-form resolves to the same VALUE as baserom's baked word — so an objdiff-exact NM body is NOT necessarily landable. The land-script's raw-byte `cmp tenshoe.z64 baserom.z64` fails if a C body emits a `jal` (`R_MIPS_26`) to a REAL symbol: intra-module jals are stored in the USO `.text` as raw `jal 0` (`0x0C000000`) and patched by the loader at runtime, so a hand-written INCLUDE_ASM `.s` reproduces the literal `jal 0` and matches baserom, but the C body's call links to the REAL address (e.g. `0C018BD9`) → ROM mismatch. Proven: un-wrapping gl_func_00065250 (objdiff-34/34) gave a byte-identical OBJECT but a ROM mismatch at its one `jal gl_func_00062F64` word; reverted.

**LANDABILITY FILTER — a game_libs NM body can be promoted to compiled-C (cmp-clean) ONLY if:** its `.s` contains NO real-target `jal`-family word — i.e. every call is either (a) to a placeholder extern defined `=0` in undefined_syms_auto.txt (jal resolves to 0, matching baserom's `jal 0` — this is why gl_func_0002DF68's `gl_func_00000000_f` call landed), (b) an INDIRECT `jalr` (no reloc), or (c) absent; AND no global `lui %hi/lw %lo`(HI16/LO16) pair to a real symbol. Functions with intra-USO jals to real functions (65250/66210/68B04) are objdiff-100 but UN-LANDABLE as C — leave them INCLUDE_ASM (they already match baserom via the asm). Don't burn ticks un-wrapping objdiff-exact-but-real-jal-bearing bodies. (The already-exact-but-INCLUDE_ASM reloc-free ones like gl_func_00064170 ARE worth un-wrapping — build-path conversion + episode-eligibility, though no new headline point since already objdiff-100.)

### Fresh-named-post-call-base-pointer forces a global base to stay register-live across post-call stores (2026-07-11)

Crossing lever (gl_func_00006AAC 87%→exact, was tagged a genuine "FP-const + bgez + reloc" cap): when the target holds the `&D` global base in ONE register across two+ stores that follow a `jal`, but the build re-materializes it via `lui $at` per store site, assign a FRESH NAMED pointer AFTER the call: `int *H = (int*)&D_00000000;` then store through `H`. IDO keeps the distinct-live-value pointer in a persistent register and reuses it for all post-call stores — and this often CASCADES to also fix the FP-constant load order and the jr-delay-slot fill. Pair with: (a) store-order matching (swap the zero-store sites to target order), and (b) distinct base-0 aliases in undefined_syms_auto.txt (`gl_d_x/y/z = 0x00000000`) to reproduce the target's separate `lui $at,0` loads where m2c would CSE them into one. Another "documented cap → exact" retraction: the residual was global-CSE + store-order, not the tagged FP/reloc cap.

### cvt.d.s-asymmetry scan finds mis-diagnosed K&R-float-promote caps → typed absolute-0 alias crosses to EXACT (2026-07-11)

SYSTEMATIC FINDER for a whole class of mis-diagnosed caps: scan NM near-misses for a `cvt.d.s` (or `sdc1`) that appears ONLY on the BUILD side of the objdump diff (not the target). That's IDO K&R-double-promoting a float arg passed through the shared `gl_func_00000000` (jal-0) placeholder, which is declared K&R/unprototyped. The target passes single-precision (`swc1`/`mtc1`). FIX (crosses to EXACT, headline mover): declare a typed absolute-0 alias `gl_func_00000000_<suffix>(…,float,…) = 0` in undefined_syms_auto.txt, route the float-arg call through it → single-precision, no cvt.d.s. jal bytes stay `0x0C000000` (=0 placeholder, landable). Cracked gl_func_0002DF68, gl_func_0002F9D4 (84→90 rise), gl_func_00033338 (27/27 EXACT). NUANCES: (a) a `float 0.0f` constant landing in a GPR emits `addiu reg,zero,0` (li of the bit pattern), DISTINCT from an int-0 `move` — match the target's form; (b) the existing `gl_func_00000000_f(int,float)` / `_ff` aliases cover common arities with NO new symbol; other arities need a fresh alias; (c) the promotion fix alone only crosses if the REST of the body is already correct — if structural bugs remain (wrong base ptr, spill vs saved-reg), it's a rise not a crossing (33228: promote-fix + structural rework still needed). Remaining leads (agent-g scan): gl_func_00033228 (alias+structural), gl_func_0002E354 (9 cvt.d.s), gl_func_0002BB7C.

### Uninitialized-volatile spill-slot lever + pad-promote-breaks-baseline gotcha (2026-07-11)

**Spill-slot lever (permuter-blind):** `volatile int v; ...; v = x;` (declared uninitialized, assigned in a SEPARATE later statement) colors `v` into the FIRST local slot; `volatile int v = x;` (initialized-at-decl) colors it one slot LOWER (+4 offset). A 4-byte spill-offset lever for when the only residual is a spill-slot offset mismatch. Took gl_func_0006CC14 to a byte-exact body (spill at sp+0x1C matching target vs sp+0x18). Companion to the volatile-pad-sandwich / decl-order-slot levers.

**GOTCHA — pad.s functions can't be C-promoted without breaking the EXPECTED_BASELINE build:** a function whose `.s` omits the jr-ra delay nop and relies on an 8-byte-aligned `gl_func_X_pad.s` GLOBAL_ASM to fill delay+pad cannot be cleanly promoted to plain C by (un-wrap + drop pad.s + add Makefile SUFFIX_BYTES gl_func_X=0x00000000). The real build + ROM stay byte-identical, but `refresh-expected-baseline.py` (`make objects EXPECTED_BASELINE=1`) FAILS — the baseline path has no INCLUDE_ASM/pad for the now-plain-C function and the suffix injector errors (same class as the object-span-.s suffix-injector refusal). So the objdiff score DROPS (88.9%) instead of crossing to 100. Keep these as byte-exact NM WRAPS (they still improve the tracked fuzzy, e.g. CC14 94.4%); a clean pad→C-promote needs a focused baseline-injector fix, not a loop-tick. gl_func_0006CC14 is the ripe example; 0006CD44/0006DC0C/0006D270 are the same pad family (no byte-exact body yet).

### Baked-USO-symbol cap: a reloc-free `lui 0xN; addiu -M` loading a 16-bit-fitting value is an absolute-symbol %hi/%lo, not an int literal (2026-07-11)

New cap class (caps the gl_func_00003B1C/3C0C/3DB8 free-slot-allocator family near-miss). When the target has a 2-instruction `lui 0x1; addiu reg,reg,-N` load of a value that FITS in 16 bits (bit-15 set, e.g. 0xCD00 = `lui 0x1; addiu -0x3300`) with NO reloc in `expected/*.o`, it's the %hi/%lo of an ABSOLUTE USO symbol address baked into the raw-word disassembly — NOT an int literal. IDO emits a plain int of the same value as a SINGLE `ori` (confirmed across 4 literal forms), and a symbol reference would produce reloc-placeholder bytes. So these 2-insn baked-symbol loads are NOT reproducible in the reloc-free C scheme → hard near-miss cap. Recognize: target `lui 0xN; addiu` (2 insns) for a small value where your C emits one `ori` = baked absolute symbol, un-reproducible. (Companion to the K&R-float-promote vein — those crossed, but the surrounding baked-symbol loads cap the remainder: 33228 reached 99.94% blocked only by a 16-byte frame-pad, 3B1C/3DB8 by baked 0xCD00/0xCD08.)

### Shape-only-placeholder resolution is FUZZY-NEUTRAL and ROM-NEUTRAL — NOT a progress vein (2026-07-11)

DEAD END (proven on titproc_uso_func_0000116C): resolving `gl_func_00000000`/`func_00000000` placeholder CALLS and `D_00000000` collapsed GLOBALS to their real distinct target symbols (via emu-symdump reloc-sites.json) changes the NM object's RELOCATIONS correctly but leaves objdiff `fuzzy_match_percent` BIT-FOR-BIT IDENTICAL — the metric compares mnemonics+registers and is BLIND to reloc target-symbol names (a `jal placeholder` and `jal real_sym` both encode `0x0C000000`+reloc). And since these functions build via INCLUDE_ASM (NON_MATCHING), the corrected relocs never reach the ROM either → ROM-neutral, no decomp.dev movement. So per-reference placeholder/global resolution in NM bodies is invisible to EVERY project gate. It only matters for episode/name quality (deferred). Progress requires a REAL instruction-field fix (width/structure/coloring/schedule) — and the shape-only-placeholder functions' residuals are all documented regalloc/scheduler/branch-likely caps (1-8 insn deficits in bnel/beqzl/spill-heavy bodies). Companion to the "objdiff fuzzy is mnemonic-level: callee-NAME resolution = 0pp" entry. (Also: arcproc's 1D18/1BBC/1F54/2884/0FA8 live in arcproc_uso_TAIL1.c, not arcproc_uso.c.)

### The `(float)N` cast-literal CSE-break generalizes to ANY FP constant, not just 0.0f (gl_func_0002DF98 94→100 EXACT, 2026-07-11)

The `(float)0`-vs-`0.0f` CSE-break (defeat the zero-FP-reg CSE) generalizes to non-zero FP immediates. When the target materializes a constant into TWO FP regs (e.g. 1.0f into `$f2` for two stores + `$f4` for a third) but IDO natural-emit CSE-folds all uses into ONE reg (1 insn short), spell the ODD store's constant in the DISTINCT literal form — `(float)1` (cast) vs `1.0f` (float literal) for the others. IDO hashes the two forms to different FP pseudos → a fresh `mtc1 at,$f4`. Took gl_func_0002DF98 (three 1.0f stores at 0x54/0x58/0x5C; target uses $f2 for 0x54/0x58, $f4 for 0x5C) 94.04→100% EXACT, RETRACTING its 2026-05-28 "FP-IMMEDIATE-constant CSE not bustable / Permanent NM" cap. So the CSE-break family = {`(float)0` vs `0.0f`; int-0-through-float* ptr; `(f32)255` vs `255.0f` for const/const div; `(float)1` vs `1.0f`} — for ANY FP-const-CSE 1-insn-short near-miss, try the distinct-literal-form of the odd use first. Another "permanent cap" retraction — the crossing-hunt / cap-re-verification approach keeps converting these.

### PERMUTER IS VIABLE on ultra-close near-misses: `--stack-diffs` cracked a 99.96% "cap" (gl_func_0000DC90 EXACT, 2026-07-14)

The blanket "permuter-immune" verdicts (from 2026-05/06 sweeps on HARDER functions) do NOT hold for the 98.5-99.99% band. decomp-permuter with **`--stack-diffs`** (which permits stack-offset-changing mutations) cracked gl_func_0000DC90 (99.96%, previously capped) to EXACT. For any 1-3-insn near-miss residual: set up a permuter scratch (base.c from the NM body + target + IDO 7.1 -O2 compile script per reference_permuter_asmproc), run with `--stack-diffs --threads 4`. Score 0 = byte-perfect; extract the winning mutation, verify in-tree. The ~21 remaining game_libs 98.5-99.99% functions are the target pool.

### FP-const materialization hoists ABOVE the stack prologue — "stolen-prologue" caps can be C-reproducible (mgrproc 2E3C, 2026-07-14)

When a "stolen-prologue" cap note says an orphaned instruction lives in the splat gap BEFORE the function symbol, CHECK WHAT THE ORPHAN IS: if it's an FP-const materialization (`lui at,0x3F80; mtc1 at,$f0` = 1.0f), plain C (`rgba[i]=1.0f`) makes IDO -O2 emit it ABOVE the `addiu sp,-N` prologue naturally — the "stolen prologue" is just IDO's normal const-hoist scheduling, fully C-reproducible without any splat boundary fix. (mgrproc 2E3C: prior note claimed un-C-reachable `mtc1 zero`; actually a 1.0f hoist, 45/47 aligned once fixed.) CAVEAT: fixing the boundary can EXPOSE a deeper residual that the fuzzy metric weighs more heavily than the boundary diff it removes (2E3C: 97.5→95.3 fuzzy despite better alignment — kept the old body per monotonic rule; true residual = FP-pair-swap reg-numbering cap). Re-verify other stolen-prologue notes (gl 1FFB8/1FF34, arcproc 1C74, titproc 1710) with this lens — check the orphan's content first.

**UPDATE 2026-07-15 (titproc 1710, the 2E3C if/else twin): three companion levers took the "frame-size cap" (73 vs 76 insns, -0x60 vs -0x70 frame) to 77/77 mnemonic+offset alignment; fuzzy 87.11→95.39.** (1) **Pointer-read propagation blocker:** when the target RELOADS an array element the source just stored a constant into (`swc1 $f16,96(sp)` then later `lwc1 $f18,96(sp)`), plain `ones[i]` reads get the 1.0f const-propagated into the expression (loses the reloads, −3 insns, frame shrinks). Fix: `float *src = ones;` and read `src[i]` — uopt does not propagate through the pointer, but still CSEs each element's two uses into one load, exactly matching. (Direction matters: STORING through src and reading `ones[i]` gets tracked and propagated — blocker must be on the READ side.) (2) **Dead scalar homes are part of the frame map:** every named non-register scalar (t/dc/one/src) gets a dead 4-byte home slot placed in DECL ORDER with the arrays (first decl = highest). A mysterious 0x18 gap between two arrays = pad[] + the scalar homes — declare the scalars between the pad and the next array to place the gap; scalars declared after the last array put their homes BELOW it (shifts everything up). (3) **dc/t sharing $f0 = they were ONE variable** (reassigned mid-branch). Residual after all three: pure FP-pseudo-numbering rotation. Observed ugen FP temp pool order is `f0,f2,f4,f6,f8,f10,f12,f14,f16,f18` assigned to fresh pseudos in numbering order with dead-reg reuse; target numbered the hoisted const 9th (→$f16) and gave the three add-results fresh slots (f2,f12,f14), ours numbers the const 2nd (→$f2) and reuses for adds. Probed named-var, dead-while anchor, branch-duplicated-init (hoist), out-via-pointer, t-inline — all ≥55-word; class is the intractable FP-renumber tie (2E3C pair-swap sibling). Also: `(vec[i]-src[i])*t + src[i]` spelling (R-first commute rule, see 0005F27C entry) flips add operand order to ones-first. **UPDATE 2026-07-15b (arcproc 1C74, the 2E3C 3-clone family):** same-orphan re-verify hit 41/43 TRUE bytes (orphan still parked in predecessor 1BBC.s tail — objdiff fuzzy DROPS on the better body because expected/ lacks the orphan; head-misalignment artifact, not a residual). The `mtc1 at,$f4(const); lwc1 $f6(field)` pair-swap in `(int)(field*255.0f)` is confirmed VERSION-INDEPENDENT (IDO 5.3 -O2 byte-identical) and invariant across both mul spellings, pointer-deref, volatile-deref, and int-literal-255 (K&R promote). A NAMED var for the field flips the const to $f4 correctly but parks the load in $f0 (user-var reuse) — the load must be a FRESH pool temp numbered AFTER the const, unreachable from C. Extends the docs negative list: don't re-probe this pair-swap at 5.3. Clones sharing target bytes + cap: timproc_uso_b1_func_000019C0, timproc_uso_b3_func_00001928 (sig 739fd8d1d3).

### ZERO-HOME frame via unpassed extra K&R params + nameless CSE temps — the "-40 vs -32 frame cap" killer (bootup B49C EXACT, 2026-07-15)

bootup func_0000B49C 99.94→100: the long-documented "spill-allocator reserves an extra 8-byte home / frame -40 vs -32" cap was the DEAD-SCALAR-HOME block. At 7.1 -O2, ANY named local scalar (int or pointer; `register` does NOT help; inner-scope does NOT help) costs a 4-byte dead home, rounded to 8 — even when its value only ever lives in a pad-region spill temp. A target frame that is exactly `round8(save_end) + spill temps` has ZERO named locals in the original C. Levers to reproduce:
1. **Copy-of-param as an EXTRA UNPASSED K&R param** — `void f(int idx, int j) { j = idx; if (j >= 10) j = 9; ... }`. Param homes live in the CALLER's arg area (sp+0x1C+frame), so no frame growth; `j = idx` with j in $a1 emits the target's `or $a1,$a0` branch-delay copy. (Callers pass 1 arg; K&R makes this legal.) GOTCHA: this only works for params whose incoming value is killed by a coalesced COPY in the entry block — an extra `int *elem` param whose first real def comes after a branch leaks a dead `sw $a2,0x28(sp)` K&R home-store that no dead-redefinition kills; and if the extra param IS live across calls, it spills to its arg-area home (sw 0x28) instead of the pad temp (sw 0x18).
2. **Nameless CSE temps** — don't name the repeated subexpression; spell `((int*)&D)[j]` twice and uopt CSEs the ADDRESS into a pad-region temp (sw 0x18) exactly like the target. Naming it (`int *elem = ...`) buys the identical spill code PLUS a dead home (+8 frame).
3. **Distinct base-0 alias to scope the CSE** — a 3rd use that must share only the `sll j,2` temp (recompute `lui;addu;lw` with its own lui) but not the full address: give it its own `D_00000000_xxxx = 0x00000000` alias in undefined_syms (established `D_00000000_a/b/c` pattern). Same linked bytes, different CSE web.
Diagnostic: frame +8 with every insn/offset already exact, and spills sitting at `round8(save_end)`/+4 = suspect dead homes of YOUR named locals, not a spill-policy cap. Probe param-hoisting + de-naming before writing the cap note.
FP-SIDE EXTENSION (game_uso E1FC 99.62→100, same day): de-naming also cracks FP-POOL-numbering residuals — a named `double thr = *(double*)(&D+0x208);` let uopt number the ldc1 early and reuse dead low regs (ldc1 $f0 / cvt.d.s $f10); inlining the deref directly in the compare made both fresh pool temps numbered at the use point (ldc1 $f10 / cvt.d.s $f16, target). Before writing an "FP-renumber tie" cap note, probe DE-NAMING any named FP local whose load is textually earlier than its single use.
SCOPING CAVEAT (7C74 counter-probe, same day): this is ONE-DIRECTIONAL. De-naming removes YOUR excess homes, but you cannot ADD a dead home to grow a dense scalar-only frame toward a larger target: plain `int dead;`, `volatile int dead;` (the phantom-slot lever), a coalesced `char *tmp = ret;` copy (+ dead-if ref boost), and a live named `float f = global;` were ALL elided at -O2 (frame stayed -32; the float also parked in $f0 via user-var reuse, 1C74-style). Dead scalar homes only materialize in AGGREGATE-BEARING frames (titproc 1710 / game_uso 6FA8 class, which have arrays/structs in the frame). A target-larger-by-8 dense frame with a skipped slot between spills (7C74: ret@0x1C, link@0x20, 0x18 empty) remains the fresh-slot-vs-reuse spill-coalescing cap (uoptlist-confirmed). Decl order still controls spill-slot RANK (first decl = highest) but cannot skip a slot.

### Split-shift phantom + decl-order slot rank CRACK the "uniform temp-pool phase shift + spill-slot" cap class (game_uso D63C EXACT, 2026-07-15)

The documented "genuine IDO candidate-numbering / temp-pool cap, permuter-immune" residual class — a UNIFORM +1 t-reg shift (build `sll $t7`/`li $t8` vs target `$t8`/`$t9`) plus a spill slot one word low (0x20 vs 0x24) — is C-reachable with two coupled levers (game_uso_func_0000D63C 99.17→100):
1. **Ring phase:** spell the scaled index with a split-shift phantom — `idx<<0<<1<<1` instead of `idx*4`/`[idx]`. Each phantom shift consumes one ugen temp-ring slot with ZERO emission, advancing every later temp by the phantom count. `x*0` additive phantoms also shift but their phantom ADDS burn post-sll slots too (`idx*0+idx*0+idx*4` fixed the sll but over-shifted the tail li by +1); split-shifts advance the ring BEFORE the real sll only. Probe granularity: `<<0` = +1 slot, free placement.
2. **Spill slot:** decl-order home rank applies to SPILL slots of scalar locals — declaring the spilled var FIRST moves its slot to the top local word (0x24). The CC14 split-decl (uninit + later assignment) form did NOTHING here; decl position is what matters.
COUPLING GOTCHA: the two levers interact — swapping decl order re-phased the temp ring back (-1), so the phantom count must be re-tuned after any decl change (`(idx<<1<<1)` sufficed with idx-first decls; `idx<<0<<1<<1` needed with value-first). Sweep phantom counts AFTER fixing the frame. Also confirms the 275F4 split-shift-phantom and `x*0` FIFO-shifter notes generalize beyond their original functions, and retracts D63C's "no C-level perturbation reproduces" verdict (17.5k permuter iters missed it — the permuter never mutates `<<0` insertions).

## SAME-NAME WEB REUSE plus dead if(param) — 332B4 coloring-cap killer {#same-name-web-reuse-plus-dead-if-param-332b4}

2026-07-15, gl_func_000332B4 (game_libs_post.c) 99.70 -> EXACT. Residual was the
tag load `*(int*)c` coloring $a2 (coalesced into idx's web) vs target $v0.

1. **Same-name web reuse.** The function already had `int val` whose later
   table-load web colors $v0. Spelling the tag load as `val = *(int*)c` gives
   the tag its own reaching-def web (dies at the bne) that uopt colors
   independently — it picked $v0 like the other val web — while both webs share
   one frame home. A separate `int tag` local flipped the reg too but cost +8
   frame (named-local-count rule, doc "NAMED-LOCAL COUNT governs frame size"),
   even though tag never spills.
2. **Dead `if (c) { }` to forbid an arg-reg coalesce.** With tag/idx split, idx
   drifted to $a1 (param c's reg, dead after the last c use). A mid-block dead
   `if (c) { }` right after `idx = *sp` emits ZERO code but extends c's $a1
   range past idx's def, forbidding the coalesce; idx anchors $a2 and the
   target's `move a1,a2` arg copy reappears.
3. Keep the name on the value the target holds in a reg: inlining `val` into
   the store flipped the table load into the t8 ring temp.

Third crack same mission (game_libs_func_00027C48, 99.24 -> EXACT): a uniform
+1 t-ring shift starting AT an lbu falls to the subsumed-mask burn, but the
MASK POSITION picks the burn slot: `((*p) & 0xFFFF) | 2` (mask on the LOAD)
burns before the lbu pop and shifts lbu+ori+mfc1+the bc1fl annul-dup all at
once; `(x | 2) & 0xFFFF` (mask on the RESULT) burns between lbu and ori (only
shifts the ori); masking a DIFFERENT statement burns inside that statement's
own sequence and regresses it. Also: two stacked ANDs (`(x & 0xFFFF) & 0xFF7F`)
cfe-merge the constants = 0 burn — the mask must mix AND/OR with the real op.
Bonus lever (game_libs_func_00021130): `base + v0*4` in ANY textual order
emits the mul chain first (addu a0,t9,base); the array-IXA spelling
`(int)((int*)base + v0)` restores base-first operand order (addu a0,base,t9).

## INT-CAST address form breaks uopt address-expr CSE (arm-local addiu remat) + unnamed-entry-web coloring (timproc b5 C8AC 99.6->EXACT, 2026-07-15) <a name="int-cast-address-cse-break-c8ac"></a>

2026-07-15, agent-g: timproc_uso_b5_func_0000C8AC 47/51 -> 51/51 EXACT,
retracting a 2026-06-20 "first-pseudo register-coloring / permuter-territory"
cap. Three independently useful pieces:

1. **Unnamed entry web colors like the reload temps.** Target: entry
   `lw v1,0x2B8(a0)` AND all post-branch reloads color $v1; build's NAMED
   `int *v1` head local colored $a1 while inline-deref reloads colored $v1.
   Dropping the name (spelling the head condition and the derived-pointer def
   as inline derefs of `a0[0x2B8/4]`) lets CSE produce one compiler temp that
   colors $v1. Converse of the 332B4 same-name-family rule: a named-local web
   family inherits ONE color as a group — naming the reloads into `v1` dragged
   them ALL to $a1 plus `move v1,a1` copies. If the target's color matches the
   ring-temp choice, UN-name the web instead of naming more of it.

2. **Int-cast address spelling defeats uopt expr-CSE = per-arm addiu remat.**
   Target recomputes `addiu v0,v1,0x128` inside the taken arm (the pre-branch
   addiu feeds only the else arm's beqzl-annulled delay slot). Any same-form
   re-def (`(float *)((char *)p + 0x128)`, same-name re-def, if(1) barrier)
   got CSE'd back to the head def. Spelling the arm re-def as
   `(float *)((int)((int *)a0[0x2B8/4]) + 0x128)` — int-cast arithmetic
   instead of char*-arithmetic — is a DIFFERENT expr tree to uopt, so the
   addiu re-emits, byte-identical. This generalizes the (float)N cast-literal
   CSE-break family from FP constants to ADDRESS ARITHMETIC.

3. **Same-line join + compound assign fix the pair order and FP numbering.**
   With the re-def on its own line the lui-at/addiu pair and the two lwc1s
   emitted swapped (as1 debug-line tie-break). Joining
   `p128 = ...; *p128 += D[0x374];` on ONE source line fixed the pair order
   and load emission order; the compound `+=` (NOT `*p128 = *p128 + D`, which
   leaves the D operand's pseudo created first -> f4/f6 swap) keeps *p128's
   pseudo first so f4=*p128, f6=D as in target.

## Dead-home DECL-ORDER INTERLEAVE moves a caller-save spill slot — the "E6E8-class inverted slot ordering" verdict is beatable (h2h E04 EXACT, 2026-07-15) <a name="dead-home-interleave-spill-slot-e04"></a>

2026-07-15, agent-g: h2hproc_uso_func_00000E04 41/43 -> 43/43 EXACT, retracting
the 2026-06-10 "16-variant grind, C-side forcers exhausted, E6E8-class
irreducible inverted slot ordering" verdict.

Rule: at -O2, EVERY named local reserves a frame home slot TOP-DOWN in decl
order, even locals that are fully colored and never touch memory (dead homes).
A caller-save spill temp for local `x` lands in x's DECL-POSITION slot. Target
had r1's spill at 0x28 above a hole at 0x24; build's decl order
`slotC4, slotCC, r1, r2` mapped homes 0x2C, 0x28, 0x24, 0x20 -> r1 spill 0x24.
INTERLEAVING the dead pointer homes — `slotC4; r1; slotCC; r2;` — maps r1 to
0x28 (slotCC's dead home becomes the 0x24 hole), r2's spill stays 0x20. EXACT
with zero instruction changes.

Gotchas found on the way:
- `volatile int pad;` as an EXTRA local shifts the map but grows the frame +8
  (named-local-count rule) — don't add locals, REORDER the existing dead homes.
- The old grind permuted pads and the r1/r2 pair but never interleaved the
  spilling locals INTO the dead-home positions; "spill above an unoccupied
  slot" is precisely the decl-order signature `live, spiller, dead, spiller`.
- `int * volatile r1` in position 2 (1E9C arg-fold form) is also exact here but
  unnecessary when the plain spill shape already matches.

## VOLATILE-PARAM HOME RELOAD + ZERO-ARG K&R CALL: the -O1 jal-delay `lw s0` lever — kernel 969C-class prologue caps cracked (969C + 9584 EXACT, 2026-07-15) <a name="volatile-param-home-reload-969c"></a>

2026-07-15, agent-h: two kernel -O1 rmon handlers went EXACT (func_8000969C
99.7->100, func_80009584 94->100), retracting years of "IDO -O1 scheduler,
permuter-only" notes (969C alone had 19 logged failed variants + 14k permuter
iters). The target signature: prologue `sw a0,HOME(sp)`, then the FIRST call's
delay slot holds `lw s0,HOME(sp)` (the param reloaded into a CALLEE-SAVED reg)
with NO `lw a0` arg reload before the jal, plus `sw s0/sw s1` prologue saves in
ascending order. The C that reaches it:

1. **Volatile-qualify the pointer param**: `s32* volatile msg` (qualifier on
   the VARIABLE). Then `p = msg;` as a plain statement compiles to a DIRECT
   home load `lw s0,HOME(sp)` — no temp. The two wrong spellings:
   `p = msg` on a non-volatile param -> `lw t6,HOME; move s0,t6` (+1);
   `p = *(s32* volatile*)&msg` -> `addiu t6,sp,HOME; lw s0,0(t6)` (address
   temp materialized). Only the volatile-qualified param gives the bare load.
   Since `lw s0` is callee-saved and independent, as1 hoists it into the
   FIRST jal's delay slot — exactly the target schedule.
2. **Zero-arg K&R call** for that first jal: the original passes the param,
   but calling `func_80008430()` through an empty-parens extern leaves $a0
   holding the incoming param from the prologue — removing the redundant
   `lw a0,HOME(sp)` reload -O1 otherwise emits for EVERY param use (at -O1
   params are homed and reloaded per use, even for the first).
3. Side effects that snap for free: the `sw s0/sw s1` prologue order flips to
   target order once p has a real def; downstream branch offsets re-align.
4. On 9584 two more coupled levers finished it: `register char* s0` reserves
   a DEAD HOME even at -O1 when the frame is aggregate-bearing (0x200 buf) —
   moving its decl below the live scalars relocated the frame hole 0x24C->0x240
   and snapped val/cnt/p to target slots (E04 dead-home interleave, now
   confirmed at -O1); and hdr field stores emit in statement order (swap to
   match).

TRANSFER + LIMIT (func_80009474, 99.16->~99.4, sibling of 969C): the lever
fixed its prologue class identically, but its LAST residual — the target's
mask ping-pong `lw a1,0x9C(s0); andi t8,a1,0xfff; jal; move a1,t8` — is a
distinct -O1 cap: every C spelling either collapses to in-place `andi a1,a1`
(inline either operand order, bitfield-read: ugen copy-props the move when
the source dies) or pays memory traffic (named local homes+spills; K&R
phantom param is HOMED at -O1 — `register` on a param is ignored; u64 mask =
+4 pair churn; <<0/>>0 phantoms cfe-fold with no -O1 ring effect). Needs the
loaded value live past the andi at zero cost; no -O1 form found.

CLASS NOTE for the -O2 coloring-lever wave on -O1 units: same-name web reuse /
ring burns / subsumed masks do NOT transfer (-O1 runs no uopt web split and no
range folding); what DOES transfer is the FRAME-MAP family (decl-order dead
homes) and the delay-slot/home-reload family above. Kernel -O2-class caps

## SWITCH-SORT vs GOTO-LADDER: manual beq-chain order is reachable but the FINAL beq+b pair always tail-dups/inverts; K&R-param precolor composes with switch; block moves crater objdiff fuzzy (52144 99.4, 2026-07-15) <a name="switch-sort-goto-ladder-52144"></a>

gl_func_00052144 (post0b, 45-insn state->float dispatcher), wave 3. Findings:

1. **Goto-ladder reproduces a source-order beq chain** (`if (s==K) goto Lk;` x7,
   arms `Lk: return CONST;` after, default fallthrough or `goto Ldef`): IDO emits
   the beq comparisons in SOURCE order with arms laid out in first-reference order —
   the escape from switch's ascending case sort. BUT the LAST `beq -> arm` followed
   by `b Ldef` is ALWAYS tail-dup/inverted (bne->Ldef + duplicated arm inline,
   +3 insns; the labeled arm remains as unreachable code). 12 negative probes:
   if(1){} wrap, else-goto, 1-case switch, label on the goto block, do-while(0)
   pin, unreachable 2nd goto pred, dead-store in block, always-true trailing
   conditional goto (folds), fmt-computation in block (copy-prop sinks it),
   dead-if(fmt) (preserves the beq but &D+off isn't provably nonzero -> emits a
   real null-test, +3). Fallthrough-call form (default call textually before the
   arms, no gotos) keeps ALL beqs uninverted but places the call block before the
   arms (target had it after, behind a `lui/b/addiu` stub).
2. **K&R unpassed-param precolor composes with switch bodies.** `f(a0, dmy, state)`
   K&R + pre-def `if (state) {}` colors state $a2 inside a switch too (the switch
   compare web inherits the param color). GOTCHA pair: the SAME value as a 4th
   K&R param (`self`) does NOT copy `or a3,a0` — being a param gives it a free
   arg-area home, so IDO SPILLS a0 (`sw a0,0x18(sp)` + `lw t7`) instead of
   copying; as a plain LOCAL it colors $a3 and emits the copy. And EVERY unused
   extra param (`dmy`) needs its own dead-if or it leaks its home-store.
3. **objdiff fuzzy punishes block MOVES far more than word diffs.** The
   fallthrough-call form (26 raw diffs, 44/45 insns, all beq shapes right but the
   4-insn call block relocated) scored 25.9%; the switch form with 11 aligned
   word diffs (chain-order only) scored 99.4%. When choosing the best NM wrap
   form, prefer position-aligned wrong-immediates over structurally-closer but
   shifted layouts.
4. **Residual cap class**: IDO sorts switch beq-chain comparisons ascending by
   case value (confirmed again); a source-order chain needs the goto ladder,
   which is blocked by (1). 52144 stays NM at 99.4 (11 word diffs, size exact).

### Addendum (2026-07-15, wave 3 agent-g): NAMED-LOCAL DEAD-HOME rule (frame = names once anything spills); target WEB-MERGE shared names (flags+i / busy+off); if(1) wrap flips in-loop CSE web a2->v0; de-name r2 = raw 1036(v0) read; folded-table-offset base; timproc b5 7E34/7B2C/80F4 all EXACT

Three sibling verdict-retractions in one session (176+194+221 words, all "permuter-immune coloring ties"):

- **NAMED-LOCAL DEAD-HOME rule: once a function has ANY real spill, EVERY named local costs a dead 4-byte home slot (frame residual = name count), even `register`-qualified ones.** 7B2C frame -64 vs -40 was 6 dead homes. Converse (80F4, frame -64 vs target -72): the TARGET may keep named-local homes — add names/order decls to grow. Frame slot map: homes ranked by DECL ORDER with caller-save spill slots interleaved by the same rank — moving a decl before/after the spilled var slides the spill slot by 4 per name (80F4: decl order `sp28,busy,q,flags,e,r2,a1v` put q's spill at 60; 7E34-family: no effect on regs).
- **TARGET WEB-MERGE: when two disjoint-lifetime locals color the SAME s-reg (busy@s0 then off@s0; flags@s1 then i@s1), the target used ONE variable for both — separate names re-split the s-reg assignment even though the webs never overlap.** Merging `flags+i` and `busy+off` in 80F4 fixed the whole s0/s1 pattern in one edit; un-merging (restoring `i`) re-broke it. Diagnostic: same s-reg carrying two unrelated roles in different fn phases.
- **if(1){} BB-wrap flips an in-loop CSE web off an a-reg onto $v0** (80F4 loop dispatch: `vt=FW(e,0x28)` 3-use web stuck at $a2 under EVERY naming variant — fresh name, unnamed CSE, same-name family reuse, comma-embed (s-reg explosion), q-family (dragged q's web a1->a2) — the if(1) wrap around load+call was the ONLY flipper). Extends the 13698 v0/v1 lever to loop bodies and a-regs.
- **De-named call capture reads fields directly off $v0: `lw tN,K(v0)` in the target = the capture var did NOT exist** — embed the call in the consumer chain (`FW(FW(FW(call(...),0x40C),0x48)+off,0x3C)`). Named r2 capture = candidate that shifts the loop coloring.
- **`(&D_F60)[idx]` vs folded-offset base: target `lui/addu/lw %lo(sym+0xF60)` = spell as `*(s32**)((char*)&D_00000000 + 0xF60 + idx*4)`** (offset in the LO16, not in the symbol address). Type the loaded table ptr `s32*` and index `tbl[i]` (IXA) for base-first `addu tN,v1,tM`.
- **Un-coalesced sltu/sltiu pair + home store in branch delay + far reload = a PLAIN (non-volatile) flag local whose call-crossing web spills** (80F4 `sp28`): volatile forced the store but candidate-promoted the compute to $v0; plain local spills naturally -> ring temps t1/t2 + `sw t2,HOME` in the beq delay + `lw t6,HOME` at the far use.
- **| eval order is RIGHT-FIRST here** (extends 7E34 agent-e note): to give the 0x4D4 load the EARLY temp and ascending-reg `or`, spell `elem | 0x4D4`. Statement-order swap (a1v-before-e) swaps two addr chains' temp trios wholesale.

### Addendum 2 (2026-07-15 wave 3, agent-f): same-line join on 3-statement FP blocks; FP candidate pool is f0/f2/f12 (ring f4-f10); compound-assign de-name; scalar-volatile (void) gotcha

- **SAME-LINE JOIN scales to a 3-STATEMENT FP copy block** (gl_func_00037D48 EXACT): `fbuf[0]=tmp[0]; fbuf[1]=tmp[1]; fbuf[2]=tmp[2];` on ONE line emits ascending ring temps (f4/f6/f8 by address) with DESCENDING emission (all 3 lwc1 desc, then all 3 swc1 desc). Separate ascending lines = ascending emission; descending lines = temps follow emission order. Signature: reg-to-address binding right but emission reversed on an N-copy block = join the block on one line.

## if(1) BB-break kills store-to-load forwarding (trunc-of-reload shape) + zero-jal library-call gotcha + swap/RMW ring-temp spellings (gl_func_00062F8C 98.08->100, 2026-07-15) <a name="if1-bb-break-store-forwarding-62f8c"></a>
- **STORE-TO-LOAD FORWARDING IS LOCAL-CSE (per-BB): break it with `if (1) { ... }`.** When the target stores a computed FP value then RE-READS it (`swc1 $f8,X(s0); lwc1 $f0,X(s0); trunc $f6,$f0`) but the build truncs the pre-store register copy (`trunc; swc1; lwc1` — same insn count, different dataflow), no spelling of the statements fixes it (naming the value, naming the reload, volatile view = +1 insn). The forwarding is uopt LOCAL CSE within one basic block: wrap the re-read (+downstream stmts) in `if (1) { ... }` — zero emitted code, but the BB boundary makes the re-read fresh. On 62F8C this single lever collapsed 22 cascade diffs (whole tail f-number/a-reg rotation).
- **De-name a swap's second temp by routing it through two stores on ONE line**: `int t7C = FW(p,0x7C); FW(p,0x7C) = FW(p,0x80); FW(p,0x80) = t7C;` (2nd/3rd stmts same line) emits lw v0/lw t4/sw t4/sw v0 with the RING temp (t4) and the target's store order (second store in branch delay). Two named temps = two candidates (v0/v1) — wrong class, and shifts the whole downstream t-ring rotation by one.
- **Field-increment RMW spelling keeps the load in the ring**: target `lw t9,off; addiu v0,t9,1; ... sw v0,off` (load-temp SPLIT from result) is `FW(p,off) = FW(p,off) + 1; num = FW(p,off);` — the RMW load stays ring t9, the addiu result coalesces into the candidate via the CSE'd re-read. `num = FW(p,off) + 1; FW(p,off) = num;` coalesces the load into the candidate (lw v0; addiu v0,v0,1) — 1-reg web, wrong.
- **Same-name coloring bias for repeated identical derefs**: three `p2 = (int*)FW(p,0x28)` dispatch sites — with three block-scope `int *p2` decls, uncoerced sites pick $v0; ONE function-scope `int *p2` assigned at all three sites biases the later web to the color the earlier (dead-if-forced) webs got ($v1). Companion to same-name-web-reuse (332B4): here the payoff is CROSS-SITE color consistency.
- **Return-capture + dead-if arm transfers to $v0-exclusion**: `sp34 = call(...); if (F <= (f32)sp34) { p2 = ...; if (sp34) {} use p2 }` extends the return value's $v0 web past p2's def -> p2 takes $v1. (Same E1 recipe as 102CC/332B4, works with reused spilled-name capture — no fresh local, frame intact.)
- **GOTCHA — game_libs sibling calls are jal 0x0 (unlinked library)**: raw-.word targets in game_libs show `0x0C000000` for ALL calls; a NM body calling the real sibling symbol (gl_func_00062F64) word-diffs 0 at the .o level (reloc placeholders) but LINKS to the sibling's real address -> ROM mismatch. Route every call through the zero-alias family (`gl_func_00000000`, `gl_func_00000000_f`, ... in undefined_syms_auto.txt) and gate on full-ROM cmp, never .o word-diff alone.

## POST0B 85-90 BAND WAVE (2026-07-15, agent-f): e-split makes a home-slot reload a FRESH web; flat-deref keeps strength-reduce chains in-place; first-call pass-through erases the unused-param home; named single-use locals reserve dead frame slots <a name="post0b-85-90-wave-2026-07-15"></a>

Six levers/gotchas from the post0b 85-90 sweep (3 new byte-exacts + 1 sibling exact + 1 rise + 2 refined caps):

- **`i = arg1; arg1 = 0;` e-split converts a param's post-call home-slot reload into a FRESH web** (531C0): a plain copy `i = arg1` after a jal copy-props back to the param web (reloads into home $a1). Killing the param (`arg1 = 0`, dead-store, zero insns) blocks the coalesce; the reload web then colors by candidate order ($a0 once v0/v1 are taken) instead of param home. Pair with `if (p) {}` dead-if to fix the resulting 2-web swap. Retracts a "permuter 320->210, not C-lever crackable" verdict.
- **FLAT ptr-arith deref (`*(u16*)((char*)p + i*6)`) vs IXA (`p[i*3]`) decides in-place strength-reduce**: IXA splits index*scale into (i*3) then <<1 for the element size — the final shift takes a FRESH ring temp. The flat spelling is ONE multiply node -> the whole ((i<<2)-i)<<1 chain stays in-place in a single temp (extends the 5313C flat-vs-IXA entry to the temp-ring axis). Also: textual add commute (`idx*0xC + base`) makes the arm's base lw allocate LAST -> lands in the recycled first-chain temp (t6) with base as addu's FIRST operand.
- **First-call PASS-THROUGH erases the dead unused-param home** (3F7A8/3F8E8): an unused named int param always gets a dead `sw a1,home` — int/float retyping does NOT remove it (a float 2nd arg after a pointer still lands in $a1 and still homes). If the target lacks the home store, the param is consumed by the FIRST call untouched in its arg register: `cb1(&buf, a1)` = zero insns, no home. Check the first jal's arg count before calling it a "dead home" residual.
- **Named single-use locals reserve dead -O2 frame slots** (3F8E8): `int r = call(a0); g = r;` reserves a slot (frame +8) even though r colors $v0; inline `g = call(a0);`. Same for a named status read (`st = *(int*)&buf[8]; if (st == -1)`) — naming promotes the load to a candidate ($v1); the inline compare keeps it a ring temp ($t7). Scratch-layout recipe: first-declared = HIGHEST slot; an 8-byte tag block at the bottom = `int tag[2]` with only [0] written; buffer sizes must fill to the frame top (buf 0x98 not 0x90).
- **Same-line join slides an increment's writeback below the address compute** (48354): `idx = (ctr)++; slots[idx] = a1;` on ONE line emits addiu/sll/addu/sw-ctr/sw-val (writeback 4th); on two lines the writeback schedules 3rd. And keep the overflow compare RELOADING the counter via the post-inc one-liner — splitting into idx/writeback statements lets CSE feed idx+1 to the compare (-2 words, wrong shape).
- **METRIC GOTCHA (3E238, extends the 27A0 entry): a byte-aligned WIN can be an official-fuzzy LOSS**: the W4 `if(1){fl+=6;}` base-materialization fixed size+shape (24/30 aligned vs 14 diffs) but objdiff fuzzy DROPPED 88.63->86.3 — the leftover 3-insn as1 permutation (a2-home lw hoist depth, li at,-3 slide; equal-cost ties, immune to line-joins and early-copies) weighs worse than the old wholesale-different tail. Gate variant KEEP/REVERT decisions on refresh-report fuzzy, not the aligned count. Also reconfirmed: 5E138's shared-addiu-vs-jal-delay-recompute 1-insn tie is a real cost-model cap ((int)-cast VN-break folds; probed).

### Addendum 3 (2026-07-15, wave 3 agent-g, third pass): LITERAL-ADDRESS deref cracks the -O0 fresh-dest value-load cap (bootup 12818 EXACT); -O1 andi ping-pong + -O2 or-coalesce negatives; 3AC0 union/alias/if(1) counted; leaf fns exclude the call-based precolor levers <a name="wave3-agent-g-third-pass"></a>
