## Custom guLookAtF decode (5F5F0 45.3->82.3): gu-shape first; (f32)1 CSE-break; low-rank guard-sqrt var memory-homes; escape-array + join-scalar clamp (2026-07-30 agent-f) <a name="gulookatf-clamp-5f5f0"></a>

1080's `gl_func_0005F5F0(f32 mf[4][4], eye, at, up x3)` is
`references/libreultra/src/gu/lookat.c` guLookAtF with three deltas: no
guMtxIdentF (constant row/col stored explicitly at the end), sqrtf as a
baked-USO external jal (word 0x0C000000), and a leading distance clamp:
`if (far2@D+0x205C < d2 || d2 < 10.0f) { normalize-or-(0,0,1); scale look to
10; d2 = 100.0f; }`. Levers proven against the target bytes:

1. **Direct K&R extern calls, never fnptr casts** — each
   `((f32(*)())fn)(..)` cast costs lui/addiu/jalr vs the target's single
   baked `jal 0` (+reloc, byte-equal). Biggest single chunk of the 45->82 rise.
2. **Clamp temp = escape ARRAY + separate join scalars**: `f32 v[3];`
   stored `v[0..2]=look` only on the else path, `norm(v)`, reload into
   plain `x,y,z` scalars; then `look = x*10 ...; v[0..2] = look;`. The
   then-arm `(0,0,1)` stays in pure regs (no stores) only if it writes the
   JOIN SCALARS, not the array.
3. **`z = (f32) 1;` cast-literal CSE-break** (generalizing the DF98 entry):
   without it IDO CSEs the `d2 < 1.0f` compare literal with `z = 1.0f`
   into one CALLEE-SAVED reg (range spans the else-arm jal), wasting an
   f2x and cascading the whole FP coloring. Target has two separate mtc1.
4. **Guarded sqrt result in its own low-rank var**: `slen = sqrtf(...); if
   (slen < eps) {...; slen = 1.0f;} len = 1.0f/slen;` memory-homes slen
   (store-def / store-guard / reload-div) like the target; folding it into
   the reused `len` var keeps it in a register (wrong). Do NOT use
   volatile — that also reloads for the guard COMPARE (+1 insn); target
   compares the live call-result reg.
5. **Up-vector must REUSE the xUp/yUp/zUp params** (libreultra style) so
   ups land in callee-saved f22/f24/f26. Residual cap: written-to param
   candidates appear entry-anchored in uopt — my reused yUp refuses to
   timeshare f22 with the dead 10.0f-const range (target: ten f22 ->
   yUp f22; mine: yUp f24, shifting xLook/yLook one reg and spilling
   yLook). Local-copy `yu = yUp` does NOT fix it (tested, worse). ~18
   insn-diff residual is this single coloring shift cascading.

Also: shrinking a post0b NM body forces a NON_MATCHING_TEXT_CLIP_KEEP_ALIGN
re-probe (clip errors "smaller than requested"); lower the clip to the new
.text total and re-verify sentinel 100s via objdiff report.

## sw a2,0x8(sp) in jal delay = 4-byte struct passed by value; char*volatile local = spill-slot-below-array save; unused scalar decls hold frame slots (bootup 13D40 52.4->88.5, 2026-07-30 agent-g) <a name="struct-byval-a2-home-volatile-save-13d40"></a>

Three levers cracked on func_00013D40 (get-or-create ctor + 6 child blocks,
168 insns, structure-exact at 168/168 mnemonics+offsets):

1. **`sw $a2, 0x8($sp)` in a jal delay slot (caller side) = the 3rd argument
   is a 4-BYTE STRUCT PASSED BY VALUE.** IDO homes a one-word struct local
   (e.g. `typedef struct {int v;} Val; Val p;`) at a frame slot, stores the
   value there (`sw` lands in the preceding bne delay), then at the call
   reloads `lw a2, home` and ALSO stores it to the outgoing arg-home slot
   `sw a2, 0x8(sp)`. A plain int argument NEVER produces the 0x8(sp) store
   (probed: K&R callee, varargs prototype, extern-int all negative). An
   8-byte struct arg3 stores both 0x8 and 0xC (t4 probe); struct as ARG0
   additionally stores word0 to 0x0(sp) — absence of that store rules
   arg0-struct out.

2. **`sw a0, X(sp)` before jal + `lw a0, X(sp)` after, where X sits BELOW
   the homed array** = `char * volatile w;` local used as the save slot
   (`func(w = c, o, p, 1); c = w;`). A plain local or one-word-struct field
   PROMOTES (scalarizes) and its spill slot lands ABOVE all locals (top of
   frame) instead; `char *C[1]` array form reloads per use (block-granular)
   and needs a `q = C[0]` temp but degrades scheduling. Volatile scalar is
   the only shape that pinned the slot between the struct home and the
   array while keeping single store+reload.

3. **Unused scalar decls still consume frame slots** in this shape: an
   unused `char *q;` decl was load-bearing for slot layout (dropping it
   shifted every local down 4 and changed the frame). Opposite of the
   usual "unused decls trim" assumption — keep/probe dead decls when slot
   addresses are off by 4/8.

Residual cap (73/168 words, ~25 standalone-cc variants all stable): uopt
coalesces the six per-block `p.v` value webs into ONE global web colored
v0 where the target keeps six block-local t-cycle temps (t7/t2); same
root cause reserves 3 extra spill words (frame 0x60 vs 0x50) and offsets
the post-call temp-pair numbering (t8/t9 vs t0/t1: target numbers a2/a3
arg temps per-block, consuming 2 more cycle slots/block). Distinct
x1..x6 temps, Val p1..p6, Val P[1] array element, union, pointer-to-p,
scoped decls, goto-CFG, -g3: all still coalesce. Plus [or a1/li a3/sw]
3-insn window rotation (li/move const-first scheduling class). Sibling
family: 1438C / 8124 / 84A0 / 90CC / 6808 share the idiom (grep
AFA60008 in bootup asm) — same recipe applies.

2026-07-30 harvest addenda (1438C 65.0->87.9, 8124 69.5->94.5, both
recipe-confirmed; residual = same allocator-web cap):

4. **Tail variable-REUSE lever (8124, `move v1,s0` fingerprint):** when a
   ctor's tail loads a child (`lw v0,0x40(t6); beqz v0; move s0,v0` with
   the object saved via `move v1,s0` + spill 0x4C), the source reuses the
   OBJECT variable for the load: `v = o; o = *(char **)(arg0 + 0x40);
   if (o != 0) { func(v + 0x10, o); ... o->0x14 = v; } return v;`. Do
   NOT introduce a separate `d` with `o = d` inside the if — that splits
   the web and spills o off s0 entirely (+5 insns, whole-body regalloc
   shift). Assignment-in-condition vs separate statement: identical.

5. **Dead-decl PAIR placement (8124):** locals needed +8 with a hole at
   0x28 between p (0x24) and w (0x2C): declare `char *q2;` between w and
   p AND `char *q1;` after p (`... A[5]; volatile w; q2; p; q1;`) —
   last-decl-lowest, so q1 takes 0x20, p 0x24, q2 0x28, w 0x2C, A 0x30+.
   One dead decl shifts by 4; position in the decl list picks WHICH slot.

6. **Incoming arg homed to caller slot (`sw a0, frame(sp)` prologue +
   late reload)** falls out naturally when the arg's only use is after
   the call cascade — no source lever needed.

7. **Odd-parity local-area pad (84A0 62.5->93.3):** when target locals
   start at 0x24 (not 0x20), the homed-word count is ODD and IDO pads
   the BOTTOM word. Hitting p@0x24/hole@0x28/w@0x2C/A@0x30 took
   `int A[6]` (one element oversize, indices unchanged) + a single q2
   dead decl = 9 homed words -> pad 0x20. Tuning knobs: dead-decl count
   sets parity, array size sets the A-region span; q-pair vs A-oversize
   reach different (base, hole) combinations.

8. **Cross-symbol addend folds into %lo ONLY for extern-array refs:**
   `func_0000CACC[3]` (extern int[]) emits addiu %lo(sym+0xC) folded;
   `(char *)func_00007620 + 0x70` where the symbol is a REAL function
   in the TU emits lui/addiu %lo(sym) + separate `addiu +0x70` (+1
   insn, temp renumber ripple). No workaround found when the name is
   already a typed function — permanent 1-insn residual class.

## do-while(0) macro = 2 BBs per expansion — Chow span denominator bloat demotes EVERY loop var from s-regs (46050 48.5->80.1, 2026-07-30 agent-f) <a name="dowhile0-macro-bb-bloat-span-demotion-46050"></a>

**Tell:** a function whose target has a full s0-s8 prologue (loop invariants, hoisted compare constants, param cursors all callee-saved) builds with a HUGE frame (-168 vs -64), zero-to-two s-regs, and t-reg values explicitly spilled/reloaded around every jal (`sw t1..t3,NN(sp); jal; lw t1..t3`). uoptlist shows dozens of `not colored (-ve save)` candidates. Every documented promotion lever (`register`, param-as-cursor, ref boosts) moves only single vars.

**Mechanism:** a `do { ... } while (0)` statement macro contributes ~2 flow-graph BBs per expansion (visible as the alternating label rows in the `-Wo,-zdbug:6` flow graph). With a 17-expansion straight-line header block that is ~34 phantom BBs; Chow priority = savings/SPAN, and every variable live through the header (all the loop's invariants, loaded at entry) takes the full span hit -> priorities go negative -> spill homes for everything. Rewriting the macro body as a plain `{ ... }` block (call sites are all `EMIT(...);` statements, so the dangling-else guard is not needed) collapsed the header to one BB and restored the entire 10-reg prologue in ONE step (pos-match 4/462 -> 156/462 after temp-scoping below).

**Companion scoping result for the shared emit temps** (`_c = ctx; _q = _c->0xC; _n = _q->4; _q->4 = _n+1; e = (_c->0xC)->0 + _n*8; e[0]=w0; e[1]=w1` DL-append kit):
- fn-scope `_c/_q/_n` + BLOCK-scope `register void *_e` = target shape: stable `_c`=v1/`_n` colors across expansions, `_e` rotates through the ring with NO frame slot, frame lands EXACT (-64).
- ALL fn-scope (incl. `_e`) = +32 frame (named homes) at same insn shapes.
- ALL block-scope register = whole trio becomes rotating ring temps (22/462 — far worse).
So mixed scoping is load-bearing; pick per-temp by whether the target color is stable (fn-scope candidate) or rotating (block register temp).

**Also on this function:** if/else-if chain (`==10`, `==9`, `==0x30`) — NOT switch — is what hoists the compare literals into s5/s6/s7 loop-constant regs (switch lowering re-materializes `li at,K` per compare); dead `if (charw) {}` in the loop body flipped a charw/lineh s1/s2 priority tie (emission-free boost, cf. a7b4/d418 entry); jal-region emit ORDER read straight off which lui feeds the delay-slot store (w0 lui appears ~1 emit early — the store in the jal delay identifies the true statement order; prior decode had two emits swapped).

## volatile-reread reproduces a genuine reload that plain reread CSEs away; dropping an FP-expr local can CSE 1.0f into a mov.s return (29978 43.5->71.8, 2026-07-30 agent-h) <a name="volatile-reread-reload-fclocal-cse-29978"></a>

Two levers from the gl_func_00029978 tween-stepper redecode (game_libs, raw-.word USO):

1. **Target reloads a same-base u16 across an intervening float store — plain C reread will NOT reproduce it.** Target's mode==1 path does `lhu v0,0x18(obj)` again before its decrement even though v0 already holds that value: uopt's offset-based disambiguation happily CSEs `*(u16*)(obj+0x18)` across a `swc1` to `obj+0xC` (same base, distinct offsets), so writing the reread in C just reuses the old register (and mints extra `move` copies). `*(volatile unsigned short *)(obj+0x18) - 1` emits the genuine reload and kills the copy pollution. Rule: a "spurious" reload in target asm that survives across provably-non-aliasing stores is a volatile fingerprint, not a scheduling accident.

2. **Keep the float local in a `(x-1.0f)*(fc*k)+1.0f` tail.** Inlining `fc = *(float*)(obj+0xC)` into the return expression made uopt CSE the three `1.0f` uses (two `return 1.0f` sites + the tail) into one `mtc1 at,$f2` + `mov.s $f0,$f2` per return — +1 insn and wrong regs everywhere. With the local, each site rematerializes `lui at,0x3f80; mtc1` like the target.

Also confirmed (probe, negative): IDO canonicalizes commutative `add.s` operand order — `cur + delta` vs `delta + cur` in C emit identical bytes; can't source-flip `add.s fd,f0,f6` vs `add.s fd,f6,f0`.

## Single-prec $f12 call arg with no cvt.d.s = PROTOTYPED float(float) callee; (f32)(s32) trunc-arg = decode error (2840 42.9->89.5, 2026-07-30 agent-h) <a name="prototyped-float-callee-s32-trunc-2840"></a>

gl_func_00002840 (game_libs) levers, generalizable to any USO fn calling blank externs:

- A `jal` whose delay/setup passes a SINGLE-precision float in `$f12` with no `cvt.d.s` pair means the callee has an ANSI PROTOTYPE `float f(float)` — K&R externs always double-promote. Declare a typed blank variant (`extern f32 gl_func_00000000_sqf(f32); gl_func_00000000_sqf = 0x00000000;` in undefined_syms_auto.txt, joining the existing `_f/_ll/_va` family). A fn-ptr cast call `((f32(*)())gl_func_00000000)(...)` is doubly wrong: jalr instead of jal + promotion.
- `trunc.w.s` + `mfc1 a1` feeding an int arg register = plain `(s32)` cast in the arg. m2c's `(f32)(s32)(...)` emits trunc->mfc1->mtc1->cvt.s->cvt.d->mfc1 a2/a3 garbage (double round-trip).
- `lwc1` from a data global = float load; m2c often types it `*(int*)&D_X` (lw + mtc1 + cvt.s.w). Check the consumer: straight into mul.s means f32 global.
- Negative probe: `if(0){ f(&local); }` address-escape on the twice-assigned spill pair made things WORSE (reordered subs, zero-store); the m2c literal shape (named sp-slot locals assigned before and after the if, plus separate reg temps) reproduced the target's two-store/one-slot-pair pattern best.

## do-while(0) BB-bloat as a DOSED demotion lever: 3 wraps kill only the constant hoists, 6+ hit the 46050 wall (454C4 29.8->62.1, 2026-07-30 agent-f) <a name="dowhile0-bb-bloat-dosing-454C4"></a>

Inverse application of the 46050 finding: when the BUILD hoists loop-invariant
constants into leftover callee-saved regs that the TARGET leaves free
(`lui s6,0x300` preheader hoist; 255.0f web in `$f22` where the target remats
`lui at,0x437f; mtc1 at,$f0` per region), the span-denominator bloat can be
dosed to demote ONLY those low-benefit webs:

- Each `do{...}while(0)` wrap = +~2 BBs in every web that spans it. Constant
  webs (1-3 uses) go priority-negative first; high-use var webs (rec/args/
  counter, 10+ uses) survive.
- Dose-response on 454C4 (0x7EC colour-quantize batch, target s0-s5+f20):
  - 0 wraps: s0-s8 + f20 + f22 (constants hoisted; 61.8%)
  - 3 wraps (loop DL-append + both mid-tail appends): s0-s5 + f20 + f22
    EXACT int prologue, `lui 0x300` hoist gone (62.0%)
  - 6 wraps (all DL-append sites) or wraps on the head FCSR-dance/clamp
    statements: 46050 wall — ALL s-regs die, s0-s3-only prologue, frame wrong.
- Wrap the sites that look like original statement MACROS (gfx DL-append
  blocks); nonlinearity is sharp, so add one wrap at a time and re-diff.
- Companion lever: `char * volatile` on linked-list cur/next iterator locals
  memory-homes them (target `sw/lw 60/64(sp)` shape incl. the volatile load
  duplicated into bnel/beql delay slots) and releases s6-s8/f22 pressure in
  one step. Declared-only volatile, no (void) cast.
- Residual caps on 454C4: (a) unified 255.0f web takes $f22 while target
  remats into caller-saved $f0 after each jal — every spelling probed
  ((f32)255 split moves the web to f20/f22, per-site distinct spellings

## jal-delay `sw v0,SLOT(sp)` + post-call `lw v0,SLOT(sp)` = PRE-CALL base spill, not call-result respill (3395C, 2026-07-30 agent-h) <a name="jal-delay-sw-v0-is-base-spill-3395c"></a>

Shape: `jal cb / sw v0,0x1C(sp)` then `lw v0,0x1C(sp)` right after the
call, repeated at each call site with the SAME slot. Easy misread: "p =
cb(...) respilled to sp+0x1C" (an old NM note called it an unmatchable
respill cap and decoded `p = cb(...)` chains). Actually the delay-slot
`sw` stores the OLD v0 (a base pointer computed before the calls) and the
`lw` RESTORES it — the call results are discarded. This is plain IDO -O2
spill-slot coloring for a value that spans calls when uopt doesn't give
it an s-reg: decode as `rec = BASE; if (rec->flag) { cb(...); ...
rec->field = 0; }` with `rec` a plain local. gl_func_0003395C: 28/29
first compile at unit-default 7.1 -O2 -mips2 once the 7-word stolen
prologue (game_libs_func_00033940 = the addr compute + first field load)
was folded back in; the last word (`&local` at sp+0x24 vs 0x20) is the
decl-order lever — declare the scratch `int local` BEFORE the record
pointer. Checklist trigger: entry reads an unset register (here t8/v0)
=> hunt the preceding orphan .s before believing any cap note.

## Block-scope prototyped ALIAS extern = unpromoted single-word f32 arg with direct jal; fn-ptr cast gives jalr, same-name block prototype = cfe redeclaration error (36224 82.1->85.1, 2026-07-31 agent-f) <a name="blockscope-alias-prototype-f32-arg-36224"></a>

Target shape: K&R placeholder callee (`int gl_func_00034458()`) called with a
float 5th arg stored as a SINGLE word (`lwc1 $f4,68(s0); swc1 $f4,32(sp)` in
the outgoing-arg area). A plain K&R call promotes float->double (sdc1/2 words);
`*(int *)` spelling gives integer lw/sw — both wrong.
- `((int (*)(...,f32))fn)(...)` cast: IDO emits `lui/addiu/jalr` + a v1 spill,
  NOT jal (confirms feedback_knr_direct_call_vs_fnptr_cast_jal in game_libs
  raw-word context too). Dead end.
- Block-scope re-declaration of the SAME name with a prototype: cfe hard error
  ("redeclaration of ...; previous declaration at line N").
- WORKS: nested `{ int fn_p5(Vec3 *, char *, Vec3, Vec3, f32); ... }` with an
  ALIAS name (`gl_func_00034458_p5`) scoped to a bare block around just those
  call sites -> direct `jal` + `swc1 32(sp)`, byval Vec3 args unchanged.
  Safe ONLY for NM wraps: build/non_matching objects are compile-only (never
  linked) and the expected/ .o is reloc-free, so the alias symbol neither
  breaks the link nor scores against the target. Do NOT promote such a body
  out of its NM wrap without restoring a linkable callee name.

## Union-member overwrite (write .v fields, overwrite via .p[i] or vice versa) defeats uopt dead-store elim while KEEPING register forwarding; volatile-cast store forces reloads, do-while(0)/if(1) BB-breaks nuke the frame (36224, 2026-07-31 agent-f) <a name="union-member-overwrite-dse-defeat-36224"></a>

Target keeps "dead" plain stores (`vecA.x = tmp.x` stored, then overwritten by
`vecA.x = vecA.x - 160.0f` a few insns later) AND the subs use the forwarded
tmp registers (no reload). With `Vec3 vecA` all plain-store spellings
(self-reference `vecA.x = vecA.x - C`, alias pointer `pA=&vecA` passed byval,
tmp-read subs) get dead-store-eliminated; `*(volatile f32 *)&vecA.x = ...`
keeps the store but materializes a base pointer AND forces the subs to reload
from memory (wrong shape); do-while(0) or if(1) BB-breaks around the subs
demote the whole s-reg/frame layout (541/537-line diff blowups vs 370).
WORKS: declare the local as `union { Vec3 v; f32 p[3]; } vecA;` and spell the
initial copies and the overwrites through DIFFERENT members
(`vecA.p[0] = tmp.v.x; ... vecA.v.x = vecA.p[0] - 160.0f;`). uopt treats the
cross-member store as may-alias (store survives) but the same-offset read
still forwards from the register. Which member is used for which access is
canonicalized away — .v-then-.p and .p-then-.v emit identically. Residual cap
here: load order z,y,x + early z store vs scheduler's y,x,...,z sink —
statement-order probes don't move it (list-scheduling tie).

## Stack-arg-5 byte home + mutation-base candidate rank (2F578 / 22464, 2026-07-31 agent-h) {#arg5-byte-home-and-mutation-base-rank-2026-07-31}

**Tell 1 — `sb X,(frame+0x10+3)(sp)` written in one arm, `lbu` read on ALL paths:** not an
uninitialized local — it is the byte home of a FIFTH (stack) char parameter (arg5 word slot
= frame+0x10, byte at +3 big-endian), conditionally OVERWRITTEN then forwarded to a callee.
Declaring `unsigned char b` as param #5 costs zero prologue insns (value already in the
caller-written slot) and fixes both the frame size and the "uninitialized" read
(game_libs_func_0002F578 34.61->99.89; residual = placeholder jal name only).
Companion tells there: `w = v + 15.0f` as a SEPARATE float local = fresh $f2 web while the
f32 param stays $f12; trunc.w.s duplicated into a beql/beqzl likely-delay = ONE source
trunc after the if-join.

**Tell 2 — held whole-fn base that refuses its target s-reg:** for a base whose web is
ONLY %lo-foldable `lw/lh` derefs, three spellings behave differently under high (9-candidate)
s-reg pressure (gl_func_00022464):
- plain `B = (char*)gl_d;` — colors an s-reg but REMATERIALIZES per-site at loop heads;
- proxy sum `B = (char*)gl_d + (int)&gl_d_proxy;` — non-remat-able, so uopt SPILLS the
  whole web to a stack slot (reload per outer iter);
- mutation base `B = (char*)gl_d - 4; if (1) { B += 4; }` — variable web, held whole-fn
  with NO remat and NO spill (the 2119C-proxy behavior at high pressure).
BUT the mutation-held base still ranks BOTTOM of the candidate order (all-load use web =
cupcosts lu->reg discount), so a target coloring of base ABOVE the index/induction webs
(s5 vs s6/s7) stays unreachable: decl order is inert for the trio, and the rotation costs
~15-20pp of objdiff fuzzy (every base/index insn arg-mismatches). Treat base/off/i
rank rotation as a residual cap unless uoptlist shows a demotable competing web.
Also validated there: nested single-statement ifs do NOT split an lb reload the way a
one-site `volatile` cast does (volatile site1 + plain sites 2/3 = load1 / shared load2).

## if(1)/goto pointer-mutation addend-bake FAILS on FUNCTION symbols (bootup func_00007288, 2026-07-31)

The form-a LO16 lever (`p = &sym; if(1){ p += K; }` committing `+K` into the `addiu %lo`)
only works when `sym` is a DATA extern (mgrproc C14, timproc 2BE4). With a FUNCTION
symbol base (`src = (int*)&func_0000027C; if(1){ src += 6; }`) IDO emits the plain
`lui/addiu %lo+0` pair for the function address and a SEPARATE `addiu src,src,24` —
the addend never merges into the %lo. Where a target shows `addiu r,r,%lo(func_X)+0x18`
(e.g. bootup 7288's 25ce0018), the original compiler saw a real rodata symbol
(D_00000294) that splat later folded into the preceding function; the addend word is a
splat re-anchoring artifact and is NOT C-reachable — score the surrounding shape
(loads at 0/4/8/12 off a materialized base) and accept the one-word imm diff.

Same-function coloring notes (95.4 final):
- De-named per-use global-slot derefs (`*(int**)(base+0x254)` inline) put the reload
  temps in the t-ring exactly like the target (t9/t1); NAMING the value promotes it to
  an a-reg web ($v0/$a1) — de-name unless the target shows a single held load.
- A named per-region `char *base` local vs the macro-inline form flips the base color
  (v1 vs a1/a2), AND the choice is coupled to the OTHER region's BB layout: adding an
  if(1) split in region 2 flipped region 1's base a2->v1 (byte-exact region) while
  costing +2 tail insns (net fuzzy 91.3 vs 95.4 without). Base-color ties are global —
  measure whole-function fuzzy per probe, never per-region.

## IDO -O3 whole-TU interprocedural custom linkage: "caller-set $s0-$s4 args" caps on STATIC libc fns are the -O3 signature — compile the ENTIRE source TU at -O3 and donor-splice all its functions (73904/_Genld + 73E74/_Ldtob, 2026-08-22 agent-h) {#ido-o3-whole-tu-sreg-custom-linkage}

**Recognition.** A function whose prologue stores CALLEE-SAVED regs above its own frame and then masks them as its parameters (`sw s2,40(sp)` with frame 24; `sll/sra 16` on s2/s3, `andi 0xff` on s4) is receiving its arguments IN s-registers. No standard-ABI compile at any opt level can produce or call it. This is NOT a permanent cap: it is IDO **-O3 whole-TU interprocedural register allocation** giving a **static** function a custom linkage (all callers visible in the TU). Companion signature in the same TU: small statics (e.g. `_Ldunscale`) get fully integrated into their caller at -O3, so a fn documented as "family classifier redecode" may just be the inlinee's head.

**Recipe (1080 game_libs xldtob.c, both fns first-try exact at IDO 5.3 `-O3 -mips2 -32`):**
1. Compile the whole reference TU (libreultra `src/libc/xldtob.c`) standalone at -O3; word-diff each emitted region vs the raw target words. Expect exactness modulo reloc fields only (.rodata %hi/%lo with one consistent base; blank extern jals; the intra-TU s-reg-linkage `jal`, baked in the USO image at its ORIGINAL link address, e.g. 0x87F70 for a fn at USO 0x73904).
2. -O3 drops static-function symtab entries entirely (only global entry points survive), so REPLACE_FUNC_BODY can't key on them: the donor rule runs `scripts/add-elf-func-symbol.py $@ name=off:size ...` as POST_COMPILE (symbol METADATA only — .text bytes untouched; not instruction patching). Sizes from the target symbols (include the target's trailing-pad word where the .s carries it).
3. asm-processor rejects -O3 → donor needs the direct-CC rule pair (6AF0C precedent).
4. Pins in undefined_syms_auto.txt: `<fn>_rodata = <base>` for the renamed donor-local .rodata relocs (one base serves all, e.g. 0x2540), `<fn>_text = <baked jal addr>` for the renamed intra-TU call reloc, `gl_func_00000000_*` = 0 for blank externs (rename `memcpy`/`ldiv` in the donor via `#define` — names don't affect codegen; prototypes MUST match the real headers: `ldiv_t {long quot; long rem;}`, `memcpy(void*, const void*, unsigned)`).
5. One donor TU serves multiple REPLACE_FUNC_BODY specs (`fnA=$(D) fnB=$(D)`); splice order follows the spec list, layout self-heals per splice.

**Where else to look:** any "caller-set s-reg/v-reg arg" cap whose fn sits next to siblings from one known source file (libc, libgcc, middleware) — the whole file is one -O3 TU. The 73904 wrap sat 2+ months as a documented permanent cap ("IDO C cannot receive args in s-regs") and fell to the first -O3 TU compile.

## Whole-TU donor generalizes beyond -O3: vimgr.c pair at -O1 — in-TU GLOBAL DEFINITION flips $at-sharing on extern-store bursts, and as1 32-byte-aligns dead epilogues (74EFC/osCreateViManager + 7507C/viMgrMain, 2026-08-22 agent-h) {#whole-tu-o1-in-tu-def-at-share-dead-epilogue-align}

The -O3 recipe's real lever is the WHOLE-TU compile, not -O3 itself. The 1080 game_libs VI-manager pair (gl_func_00074EFC = osCreateViManager 65.0%, gl_func_0007507C = viMgrMain 32.6%, libultra vimgr.c verbatim) is first-compile word-exact at IDO 5.3 **-O1** -mips2 as one TU (98/98 + 115/115), spliced with the identical pipeline (REPLACE_FUNC_BODY + add-elf-func-symbol.py POST_COMPILE + section-reloc pins). -O3/-O2 probes were WRONG here (filled jal delays, s-reg allocation — target is -O1-shaped). Three transferable findings:

1. **In-TU definition vs extern declaration of a global changes codegen.** `OSDevMgr __osViDevMgr = {0}` DEFINED in the TU → IDO shares one `lui $at` across the whole field-store burst (`sw t2,0(at); sw t3,4(at); sw t4,8(at); sw t4,c(at)`), materializing the stored values FIRST. Declared `extern` → cc re-luis `$at` per store (+5 words). If a near-miss's residual is per-store `lui at` vs a shared-at burst on a symbol whose target reloc fields look blank, suspect the original TU DEFINED the symbol. (Corollary: in a 0-based USO data segment, "blank-looking" lui/lo 0 fields can be a REAL baked address 0 — game_libs .data starts at 0, .rodata 0x2540, .bss 0x44080; __osViDevMgr lives at data offset 0.)
   **Second instance (6FBE4 = `__osTimerServicesInit`, agent-g 2026-09-09): the same lever governs a 64-bit
   (u64/OSTime) ZERO store at -mips2.** `extern OSTime __osCurrentTime; __osCurrentTime = 0;` emits two
   independent at-macro halves, hi first (`li t6,0; lui at; sw t6,%lo(sym)(at); lui at; li t7,0;
   sw t7,%lo(sym+4)(at)`); with `OSTime __osCurrentTime;` DEFINED in the TU it is one store with a
   shared `lui at` and the LOW word stored first (`lui at; li t6,0; li t7,0; sw t7,4(at); sw t6,0(at)`).
   Identical at 5.3 -O1 and 7.1 -O1; no flag/type/volatile/0LL spelling reproduces it with an extern.
   Tell: `lui at` FIRST, two `li`, then `sw ..,4(at); sw ..,0(at)`. The donor's .bss definition is
   imported by the splice as an UND symbol (pin = 0), so defining it costs nothing downstream.
2. **as1 32-byte-aligns an UNREACHABLE dead-epilogue block** (epilogue after `while(TRUE)`): a run of 0x00000000 words appears between the loop back-branch and the dead epilogue, sized by the epilogue's offset in the TU's .text — i.e. by the PRECEDING function's size. A mid-function zero-run in the target that no C shape seems to produce can be pure alignment that falls out for free once the earlier TU functions compile to their exact sizes. Don't burn probes on the gap itself; fix the neighbors.
3. **Forward-declared statics resolve *UND* in the donor symtab even at -O1** (`static void viMgrMain(void*);` + later def → symbol *UND*, body only reachable via the .text section) — so the add-elf-func-symbol.py POST_COMPILE injection is needed for whole-TU donors at ANY opt level, not just -O3. The static's fn-ptr materialization relocates against `.text` with the fn's donor offset as addend: pin `<fn>_text = <baked addr> - <donor offset>` (74EFC: 0x896E8 - 0x188 = 0x89560).

Also retracts: the 7507C "-Olimit allocator quirk we cannot reproduce / uoptlist-class" verdict — the s0-resident switch value with no spill slot and the 0x38 frame both emit naturally from the whole-TU -O1 compile (the standalone probes' +8 frame was a single-function-compile artifact). When a low-opt near-miss resists standalone probing with a phantom frame slot or unexplainable saved-reg residency, try the whole-TU compile before reaching for uoptlist.

## All-4-args-homed + zero-s-reg prologue at -O2 = K&R INT params reinterpret-cast in body (63964, 2026-08-22 agent-g) {#knr-int-args-reinterpret-all-homed-2026-08-22}

Shape: `-O2` scheduling but prologue homes ALL FOUR reg args (`sw a3,frame+C; move a3,a0; sw a0,frame+0; sw ra; sw a1; sw a2`), NO s-regs saved, arg0 cached briefly in **a3** and re-loaded `lw a3,frame+0(sp)` after every call, and a float spilled into an ARG HOME slot (`swc1 $fN,frame+4(sp)` = a1's home).

That combination is NOT -O1 (7.1/5.3 -O1 probe gives a different, longer body), not varargs, not struct-by-value, not `-g3`, and plain `&arg;` statements fold dead. The trigger is a **K&R definition with all params declared `int`, with the body accessing them through reinterpret casts**:

```c
void f(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3)
char *arg0; int arg1, arg2, arg3;
{
#define parg0 (*(char **)&arg0)   /* every use */
#define farg1 (*(f32 *)&arg1)    /* f32 accumulator living in a1's HOME slot */
```

The `&arg` inside a real access is address-taken-in-use, so uopt keeps the param memory-resident in its home slot (reload per region, a3 as the scratch), uses no s-regs, and float writes hit the a1 home directly. Prototyped ANSI or bare K&R WITHOUT the casts still promotes arg0 to s0. (Found on gl_func_00063964 22.6->73.3; residuals there: one extra 8-byte compiler temp slot (frame 0x150 vs 0x148) and target reloading va/vb components after their own stores where build forwards — forwarding-kill lever not yet found; f32*-alias rewrite was inert.)

Frame-gap corollary: the decl-order local map had 6 interior gaps (0x20/0xC/4/0x10/8/8) reproduced exactly by `int padN[k]` arrays between the Vec3 decls — unused int arrays DO take stack at -O2 and slot in decl order.

**Addendum (3D7F8, 2026-08-22 agent-g) — three sub-levers, and MIX the treatment per param:** a param the target keeps register-resident (homed only across a call) must stay PLAIN typed in the K&R decl (`int *arg0;`); cast-accessing it makes it memory-resident everywhere (56-insn blowup). Only the params the target homes at entry get `int` + reinterpret casts. Two companion levers for the residuals:
- **Dead `sw a1,4(sp)` in a jal delay slot (outgoing-arg-slot store, frame unchanged)** = the call passes that arg **struct-by-value**: `f(p, *(struct {int x;} *)&arg1, i2)`. An `int tmp[1]` array copy also emits the store but costs +8 frame; the struct-byval keeps the exact frame.
- **Double reload of a cast param's home (test reg + base reg, both uopt TEMPS t8/t9) feeding a `bnezl` annul-fill, then an alternating-t1/t0 4-word copy** = the copy is a **struct assignment** `*(struct q*)((char*)p+0x48) = **(struct q**)&arg3;`. Element-wise copies via a named local color the base to $v0 (candidate, not temp — 8 reg diffs) or, with per-use casts, reload the home per element (&arg escape = may-alias with pointer stores).

## mtc1-before-lui / live-in FP regs at "entry" = stolen PRE-prologue in the PREDECESSOR .s (addiu-sp is NOT insn 1); alias-ladder for mixed $at-single vs based-triple D-loads (4F2DC/4F2F4 12.6->83.8, 2026-08-22 agent-f) {#stolen-preprologue-livein-fp-alias-ladder-4f2dc}

1. **Recognition: a raw-.word fn whose first FP op reads registers never set (`sub.s f10,f6,f8` with no prior defs) AND has an `mtc1 $at,fN` BEFORE any `lui $at` is a mid-function splat boundary.** IDO -O2 hoists arg-conversion chains (`move t6,a1; mtc1; lui 0x4320; mtc1; cvt.s.w; lui 0x42F0`) ABOVE `addiu sp,sp,-N`, so the tiny "function" before it (here game_libs_func_0004F2DC, 0x18, no jr ra) is the real entry. The dangling `mtc1 $at` consuming the ORPHAN's last `lui $at` is the smoking gun. Fix = forward-merge per the 26B48 precedent (unified symbol at the orphan address, size bump, drop successor .s + INCLUDE_ASM, refresh expected/ for that segment only, clip re-probe if the unit is NON_MATCHING_TEXT_CLIP pinned). The pre-prologue hoist then reproduces from plain C — first 6 rows matched with zero levers.

2. **Alias-ladder for a fn mixing one-shot D-offset loads with a based triple:** target emits `lui at; lwc1 off(at)` for each SINGLE `&D+off` load (0x128-entry, 0x1BA8, 0x1BAC, glob word) but a materialized base `lui t1; addiu t1,+0x128` with 0/4/8 offsets for the 3-vector read twice across a jal (remat, NOT s-reg). Plain `*(f32*)((char*)&D_0+off)` everywhere makes uopt build ONE whole-fn base = &D+0 with folded offsets (wrong). Split-NAME fix (reloc-masked USO fuzzy only): distinct scalar extern alias per singleton site (D_0B..D_0E) keeps each on the $at pattern, and an ARRAY alias `extern float D_0F[3]` for the k-vector makes uopt base t1 at the array address (= &D+0x128 in target coords) with clean 0/4/8 accesses + post-jal remat. Composes with: volatile-pad hole ladder between Vec3 locals to hit an exact holey frame (8/8/16/8/16 -> frame 0x1A8), and a nested-if body with ONE trailing `return 0` to get shared-exit `beqz/bltz -> v0=0` + `b`-over-epilogue on the hit path (separate early `return 0;` statements emit per-site blocks instead).

Neutral/negative probes: if(1){} barrier after vecC8[0] (-3.9pp — killed the legitimate cross-statement overlap); member-copy source order z,y,x vs x,y,z is scheduler-tied (~0.1pp); scale-first mul spelling +0.1pp. Residual ~16% = whole-fn FP temp-ring rotation seeded by the entry y-cvt getting fresh ft4/ft5 instead of reusing the x-chain's ft0-ft3, plus a1-vs-v0 copy-address coloring — classic endgame, no structural diffs left.


## Scalar homes are the holes (3CBB4)
<a name="scalar-homes-are-the-holes-3cbb4"></a>

**2026-08-22, agent-f, game_libs_post0b gl_func_0003CBB4 30.2 -> 91.9 (0x3E0 swept-sphere proximity test).** The prior NM body was a width-poisoned m2c graft (s32-typed fields -> subu/cvt.s.w; the real fields are f32 -> sub.s + swc1/lwc1). Full re-derivation levers, in the order they moved the needle:

1. **Unused scalar homes = the frame holes.** IDO 7.1 -O2 reserves a 4-byte stack home for every register-candidate scalar local (pointer or float) EVEN IF the home is never referenced, and places it in strict declaration order among the aggregates (same top-down decl->descending-offset rule as arrays/structs). So a target frame with "dead" gaps between aggregates may not need `volatile int pad[N]` at all — the gaps can be the homes of scalars visible elsewhere in the codegen. Here: `s32 ret; f32 *av; f32 *bv; Vec3 dv;` put ret's spill home at 0xCC and av/bv's unused homes at 0xC8/0xC4 (the 8B "gap" under the spill), and declaring `f32 fzero, tz, ty, tx;` in place of `volatile int pad4C[4]` put their four unused homes exactly in the 16B hole between `dvel` and `sum` (frame went from +16-with-pads-elsewhere to byte-exact). `register` qualifiers and block-scope declarations do NOT suppress or move these homes; only decl position does.
2. **f0/f2/f12/f14 batch shape = source-level float temps.** Three concurrently-live sub/add results in f0/f2/f12 with batched stores (x,y,z subs then three swc1) plus an f14-colored rematerialized 0.0f mean the source had `tx/ty/tz` scalars and an `fzero` variable: `tx = av[0]-bv[0]; ...; dvel[0]=tx; ...` and `fzero = 0.0f` used in every compare/zero-store. Without the vars, uopt colors the zero/1000.0f consts f2/f12 and keeps sequential compute-store per axis (ring temps).
3. **ABS(assignment-expr) roundtrip needs a struct-member lvalue.** `#define ABS3(x) (((x) < fzero) ? -(x) : (x))` with `x` = `dv.z = a->z - b->z` (Vec3 member, struct address-taken later via fn(&dv)) reproduces the store+reload-per-evaluation (swc1; lwc1; c.lt.s / arms recompute+store+reload+neg). The SAME code with `f32 d[3]` array elements compares the register value with NO reload — array-element vs struct-member lvalues differ in IDO's re-read of an assignment's value.
4. **Struct-assign vs member-copy addressing.** `*(Tri3i *)apos = *(Tri3i *)(arg0 + 0x18);` emits lw/sw pairs whose DST goes through the precolored call-arg base regs (a0/a2, CSE'd with the later `fn(apos, ...)` args); member-wise `*(s32 *)&apos[i] = ...` copies go sp-direct instead. Chained `tmp = dvel; rel = tmp;` as two cast struct-assign statements reproduces the store-then-reload-0(v0) interleave.
5. **Pointer bases survive folding only if assigned a block OUT.** `av = (f32 *)(arg0 + 0x24)` assigned in the SAME block as its uses folds into direct 36(s1) offsets; assigned one gate earlier (uses in the next nested block) it stays a materialized addiu base with 0/4/8 accesses.
6. **Prototyped jal-0 callees for float args:** baked-USO callees needing `mfc1 a3,$fN` (single float 4th arg) or a bare `$f12` first arg must be locally-prototyped unique externs (`extern s32 gl_func_00000000_3cbb4r(f32*,f32*,f32*,f32,f32*)`); K&R would double-promote.

Residual ~8% = whole-fn FP temp-ring rotation + int copy-addr coloring (gate temp v0-vs-t6, ret t0-vs-t1, addr temps) — the documented 4F2DC endgame class, no structural diffs left. Gate note: shrinking the NM body shrank .text below the pinned clip; re-probe = last-symbol offset + full expected size (62F08 @0x2c734 + 0x50 -> clip 0x2c784), else the last sentinel silently drops from 100.

## guOrthoF twins crack: write the NATURAL nested loop and let the pipeliner emit the guard; f32 reg-arg-vs-stack-arg reload/cache asymmetry IS the mixed-decl tell; operand-order + drain cells are TU-CONTEXT-sensitive (5F3E0 52.49->97.6 / 70694 52.49->100, 2026-08-22 agent-g) {#guorthof-natural-loop-pipeliner-mixed-f32-args-2026-08-22}

Byte-twins gl_func_0005F3E0 (post0b) / gl_func_00070694 (post1c), guOrthoF-shaped
(setup 7 matrix cells then scale all 16 by arg7; jal at top = identity ctor).
Four independently reusable findings:

1. **Software-pipelined loop shape (preheader loads + rotated body + drain
   block + `beq` guard + `move v1,zero` + `addiu v1,v1,1`-not-`li 1`) is IDO's
   OWN pipeliner output from a plain nested `for` — do NOT hand-pipeline the C.**
   Hand-written rotated do-while (m2c's shape) fights the scheduler: hoisted
   preheader loads, f20/f22 spills, +8 insns. `for(i=0;i<4;i++) for(j=0;j<4;j++)
   *mf++ *= s;` reproduces the whole pipeline exactly (inner unrolled x4, outer
   pipelined; guard/counter oddities are pipeliner artifacts, unfoldable
   because they're created AFTER const-prop). A VARIABLE loop bound (`i != n`
   local) instead triggers the x4 UNROLLER on the outer loop — literal bound
   only. Manual `mf[0..3]` inner unroll flattens 16x (no loop at all).

2. **Mixed f32 param classes = the reload/cache tell.** ANSI signature
   `(int *m, f32 a1..a3, f32 a4..a7)`: REGISTER-passed floats (a1-a3, int regs
   homed to arg slots) RELOAD from home at EVERY use — never cached; STACK-passed
   floats (5th+) load ONCE into a caller-saved f-reg (f14/f16/f18 in first-use
   order) and behave as candidates. When target asm reloads some float args
   per-use but caches others, the split IS the register/stack boundary — declare
   them all plain f32 and the asymmetry falls out (no casts, no locals needed).
   Extends the K&R-reinterpret lever family: this fn needed NO K&R at all.

3. **Walker-form drives int coloring:** `*mf++` inner-inc coalesces the inner
   counter j into the pointer IV -> ptr=v0, ctr=v1, lim=a0 (li a0,4). Indexed
   `mf[j]` + outer `mf+=4` leaves a j-IV phantom that eats v0 and rotates all
   int colors +1 (dead-if and while(0) ref-boosts do NOT un-rotate it); but the
   outer-inc form orders the pipeline-DRAIN block store-then-addiu while
   inner-inc pins addiu-before-stores. If the target wants inner-inc colors AND
   outer-inc drain order (5F3E0), that combination was spelling-unreachable
   (16-combo sweep) — 2-word cap. Twin 70694's TU wanted inner-inc both ways = exact.

4. **TU context flips commutative-operand and load-order cells for IDENTICAL
   source.** Same body in post0b vs post1c: [12]'s l/r load order needs
   -(arg1+arg2) in one TU and -(arg2+arg1) in the other; [13]'s add.s fs/ft and
   the drain order also flipped between TUs (callee defined in-TU vs extern is
   the suspected input). Consequence: when porting a cracked body to a byte-twin
   in another file, RE-SWEEP the commutative operand orders there — and never
   conclude "spelling-unreachable" for a twin from probes run in the other TU.

Gotcha (workflow): a python splice `s[:start]+new+s[end:]` with end<start
silently DUPLICATES the region between — the corrupted double-TU still compiled
(dupes inside #ifdef NM range) and poisoned a 16-combo negative sweep. Assert
start<end in splice scripts; rebuild from HEAD on any unexplained +30k-line diff.

## Memory-serialized FP sampler kit: volatile state-ptr loads + VOLATILE Vec3 locals + interleaved-scalar frame gaps + multu-by-u32-var (gl_func_00054264 49.2->85.1, 2026-08-22 agent-g) {#volatile-vec3-serialized-sampler-54264}

Target profile: FPU-heavy straight-line sampler where EVERY row operand reloads from sp slots, the state-struct base fields (`lw 0x68(a0)`/`lw 0x60(a0)`) reload per vertex despite no intervening pointer stores, all 4 args home in the prologue, and index scaling is `multu` by a register-materialized constant. Five composable levers (probed in-tree, gl_func_00054264):

1. **Per-vertex base-field reloads = volatile deref through the state ptr.** `#define FWV(p,o) (*(volatile int*)((char*)(p)+(o)))` reproduces the reload-per-use pattern; plain FW gets CSE'd (and even hoists the NEXT vertex's lhu). The derived lh/lhu through the computed pointer stay plain.
2. **All-operands-from-slots + strictly serialized per-vertex convert/store blocks = `volatile` STRUCT locals** (`volatile Vec3 va,vb,vc;`). Non-volatile structs still let as1 interleave vertex N stores past vertex N+1 loads. The copy-through temp (sp24) stays NON-volatile: its member is read once and CSE-shared between the slot-copy store and the row mul (single lwc1 feeds swc1+mul.s).
3. **Frame gaps between addressed locals = reserved home slots of REGISTER scalars, placed by declaration order** (first-declared-highest). A 16-byte gap above va and below the call-spill home is 4 scalar decls (`v,t,w,idx`) declared between `u` (declare FIRST -> spill home lands at frame top, 0x74) and the structs; second gap = `mult,vp,one,extra` between structs and sp24 (declared LAST -> 0x24). This replaces volatile-pad guessing: unused register scalars reserve slots without emitting insns, and you likely NEED the temps anyway.
4. **`multu` by 6/12 = `u32 mult = 6; ... mult = 12;`** — constant-fold gives sll/addu shape instead. The two ranges + the arg1 reload all share $a1 in the target (6 -> arg1 -> 12); u16*u32 keeps it multu.
5. **`addu base,product` + tri-table-load-first BOTH: spell the fetch `(idx_expr * mult) + FWV(a0,0x60)`** (product textually first). IDO evaluates the RIGHT operand of `+` first (so base-first spelling loads 0x68 first but emits `addu product,base`), and addu operand order follows evaluation order — product-first spelling got both the target load order AND base-first addu, and snapped the t-reg rotor to byte-exact on all 3 vertex addus. NOT universal: the second-half (0x58 normal-table) fetches matched with base-first spelling — probe per site.

```c

t = *dp;                    /* lw rX,0($11) — address held */
...
dp = (char * volatile *)&D_00000000;   /* re-def after the call region */
```

- **`div.s` by 2.0f**: literal `x / 2.0f` strength-reduces to `mul.s` by 0.5f. A local `f32 two = 2.0f;` and `x / two` keeps `div.s` (constant still materialized lui 0x4000/mtc1).

## Reloc-free-expected refinement of the external-jumptable cap: plain switch + post-inc-temp idiom reproduce the whole dispatcher .text (gl_func_0003AC5C 46.1->97.5, 2026-08-22 agent-g) {#relocfree-external-jumptable-switch-3ac5c}

Context: a game_libs token-stream dispatcher whose target dispatch is `sltiu at,cmd,5; beqz at,default; sll; lui at,0x0; addu; lw t6,0x1A90(at); jr t6` — the classic "external USO jumptable" shape documented as a structural cap. **In a reloc-free baked expected .o unit (game_libs_post0b class), it is NOT a %-cap:** the build's local-.rodata table dispatch emits the identical 7-insn head except the table-base `lw` offset word, and that word sits at a reloc site, which objdiff scores as matched. 97.48% reached; only true residual was 4 scheduler-order insns.

Levers that made it byte-shaped (all in one function):
1. **Plain `switch(cmd)` with cases 0..N + default.** A hand-written `if ((unsigned)cmd < 5) { switch ... }` guard compiles the switch inner body to a beql compare chain (no table at all, ~50%-class). The bare switch regenerates sltiu+sll+jr exactly.
2. **Post-increment temp idiom** `q = p; p += 1; ... use *q;` materializes the target's per-case `move v0,s0; lw rX,0(v0); addiu s0,s0,4`. GOTCHA (fold trap): any spelling where `p` is NOT reassigned between `q = p` and the `*q` use (`v = *q` before `p = q+1`, or `*(q = p)` inline) gets copy-propagated to `lw 0(s0)` and DROPS the move (-1..-3 insns). The reassignment-in-between is the fold blocker.
3. **Args as persistent registers.** `p = arg1; self = arg0;` locals split the stream pointer into two webs (entry copy in s3, loop web in s0, +1 insn). Deleting the locals and using `arg0`/`arg1` directly gives the single `move s0,a1`/`move s1,a0` entry homing.
4. **if(1){} around the loop** flipped the cmd/q temp pair from a0/v1 to the target v1/v0 (the known v0v1 BB lever — 4-for-4 now).
5. **Nested-goto alloc-guard** (`if (!arg0) { arg0=alloc(); if (!arg0) goto ret; } ... ret: return arg0;`) merges the null-return into the shared epilogue as `beqz v0,<epilogue>` + delay `move s1,v0` (a `return NULL` emits a separate `move v0,zero` + b block, +2 insns).
6. **Case-index->body mapping is .text-invariant**: bodies lay out in source case order; only the (runtime-relocated, statically unrecoverable) rodata table encodes which token hits which body. For %-purposes write cases in target stream order.

Residual class (accepted): per-case scheduler order — one case emitted `move; addiu; lw a2` vs target `move; lw a2; addiu`, another filled the `b` delay with the lw instead of the addiu. Explicit-temp and increment-order respellings either trip the fold trap (2) or keep build order. NEGATIVE (54E78 rider): assignment-pin `(t = two) * prod` does not flip mul.s fs-operand order and costs +8 frame.

## Constructor-cascade web spelling: volatile-vs-plain sub webs distinguish "twins"; per-site read-alias kills &D lui CSE; named per-arm reload colors bgezl arm loads (097C/994, agent-h 2026-08-22) {#ctor-cascade-web-spellings}

Three levers from the timproc b1 097C (67->95) / b3 994 (72->97) redecode, same source-shape family but DIFFERENT web classes per sibling:
1. **Triple-reload signature = pointer-volatile local.** If a spilled local is reloaded from its home once per consecutive statement with NO call between (lw t4,48; ...; lw t5,48; ...; lw t6,48), it is `int * volatile x` (pointer volatile, pointee normal). A plain spilled web loads once and reuses. Its twin sibling (994) instead carries the same variable in a2 with normal call spills — plain `int *`. Do not assume twins share storage class.
2. **Same-symbol &D CSE spawns an s-reg.** `gl(&D, 0)` near `*(int**)((char*)&D+0x138) = x` CSEs the lui into a callee-saved reg (s1) and poisons the whole frame. Split with a per-site alias extern (`extern char D_x_g; *(int**)((char*)&D_x_g+0x138)`) keeping the offset in C so the %lo imm stays baked. Same for a six-call block reading `*(int*)&D` while passing `&D` as arg: alias the READ base only — target materializes lui a1(read)+lui a3(arg) separately per call.
3. **bgezl if/else arms whose loads must land in a specific reg:** spell each arm with a named reload temp already colored there (`m = (int*)self[0x6A8/4]; m[0xB4/4]=11;` per arm) — anonymous `((int*)self[X])[Y]=k` arms go to the t-ring instead (t5/t6).
Registration-block def split: `gl(slot, n = X); m = n; if (m[5]) m[1]=1; m[5]=self;` gives the single post-call reload (a3) with uses off it; residual: n's def still colors a3+copy vs target's direct a1 (open).

**2026-08-22 addendum (agent-h, mgrproc 0E04 76.7->79.2 / 23FC 83.7->97.2):** three more members of this family:
- **4-stage alloc cascade, middle stage all-memory:** if a cascade stage's variable shows NO move-copy (its def is the `sw` in the bnez delay slot and every later use is a fresh `lw` from one slot), that stage is `char * volatile o2;` with the alloc result routed through a plain temp (`tmp = alloc(80); o2 = tmp; if (tmp == 0) goto ...`) so the null test stays on v0 while the store lands in the beqz delay. The neighboring stages stay plain (o1 = caller-saved-colored web with per-call sw/lw spill pair; o3 = plain a0 web). 0E04's cascade went shape-exact in one edit after this.
- **store-then-reload of a just-written field** (`sw t3,F(s0); lw t4,F(s0)`) = the read is `*(char * volatile *)(base+F)`; plain spelling gets store-forwarded. Also applies to a call ARG re-reading a field already held in a reg: spell the arg `*(volatile int *)(base+F)`.
- **FP const-vs-mem temp numbering** (`mtc1 $f4(const); lwc1 $f6` vs ours `lwc1 $f4; mtc1 $f6`): operand-order flips and cast-literal spellings are no-ops (cfe canonicalizes); what worked in 0E04 was STATEMENT order — the expression whose constant must number first has to be the earlier statement (its store may still schedule later). If two adjacent FP stores disagree with source order, swap the statements, not the operands.
- **Size-check corollary (23FC):** a placeholder-callee NM body (every jal to one local stub) can hide wholesale-wrong data bases too; expected/.o `objdump -r` is the only callee/base ground truth. 23FC's "coin-flip &D CSE" residual note was fiction — the two forms were two DIFFERENT import symbols (held-in-s0 `&import_80263D30` vs per-site `&import_8024CAF8`).

## uopt spill liveness is POST-CSE: an in-loop bound operand (`i != n*13`) cannot be kept live from C; and uopt temp-slot RESERVATION count (not layout) can block exact home offsets (mgrproc 23FC, 2026-08-22 agent-h) {#post-cse-liveness-temp-slot-reservation-23fc}

Target loop tail spills/reloads THREE regs around an in-loop call (`sw t0(i)/t1(lim)/t2(n)`), where t2=n is the bound operand `i != n*13` — reloaded every iteration but never used (13n is CSE'd to a preheader temp). Every C spelling that references n per-iteration in source failed to reproduce the spill: do-while `while (i != n*13)`, in-test assignment `while (i != (lim = n*13))`, in-body `lim = n*13;` before the test, and a dead post-loop `use = n;` all compile with n DEAD after the preheader — **uopt computes spill liveness AFTER CSE/LICM**, so source-level per-iteration references don't extend the live range. A `for (; i != n*13; i+=13, ...)` spelling reaches instruction-count parity (277/277) but via a WRONG extra `beqzl` zero-trip guard (the `if (n>0)` dominator's non-zero-trip proof is lost in for-form; W65-70 corollary) — reject that shape. In-loop `*(volatile s32*)&n;` reloads but restructures (+24 diffs). If the target's extra in-loop spill is a post-CSE-dead bound operand, treat it as a cap.

Companion frame finding: 4 unused `volatile s32 pad;` decls after the first pointer local made frame 0x120 byte-exact (aggregate one[]/buf offsets + sp-arg addiu all snapped). But the named-scalar HOME block stayed +0x18 above target: ours reserves **3 uopt temp slots** at the frame bottom vs target's 1 (only the lim spill temp), and `min = 0x30 + 4*temps + 4*below-min-decl-count` — with 3 temps the homes can never reach target offsets while keeping the ghost interleave. Temp reservation count proved not C-steerable (decl reorders, address-pinning the spilled pointer via `char **tp = &tim;` — the pin itself WORKS, relocating tim's spill from a bottom temp slot to its decl-order ghost slot, but reservation stays 3). Diagnostic: map both slot sets (`sw/lw N(sp)` roles); if build-minus-target offset is a CONSTANT across all homes, it's temp-count, not decl order.

## Block-scope case locals each reserve a frame slot — flatten to function scope + reuse temps for VM-interpreter frames (gl_func_0002BB7C 16.4->77.8, 2026-08-22 agent-g) {#block-scope-case-locals-frame-slots}

## volatile extern defeats the loop-invariant-global saved-reg hoist that distinct externs cannot — but ONLY with C read-site count == target static load count (E68, agent-f 2026-08-22) {#volatile-defeats-invariant-hoist-load-count}

bootup_uso func_00000E68 had a documented cap: "loop-invariant grid-dim read is hoisted into callee-saved $s1; distinct externs do not defeat it (value invariant across both loop phases, IDO colors it to a saved reg regardless) — solvable only by identical allocator coloring". WRONG: `extern volatile s32 SYM;` forces a fresh folded `lui/lw` at every read site and the value never gets a saved reg.

The catch: volatile alone REGRESSED (70.48->70.31) because the C had 5 read sites vs the target's 3 static loads — volatile emits one load per C site, so the C must first be collapsed to the target's load count (hold the derived bound in a local across the do-while; single-read the global before a `/64 > 0` guard instead of reading it in both guard and body). With counts equal: 70.48->71.74, -10 insns. Read the target's load sites off expected disasm (folded `lui rX/lw rX,K(rX)` pairs) and mirror exactly that many C reads.

### Loop-hoisted FP const into callee-saved $f20: cast-literal spellings do NOT break it; per-site extern f32 loads do (gl_func_0002C7A4 78.3->80.3, 2026-08-22 agent-g)

When the SAME FP constant (127.0f) appears in 4 switch-case bodies inside a call-heavy for(;;) loop, uopt unifies them into one loop-invariant web and hoists it into a callee-saved FP reg -> spurious `sdc1 $f20,24(sp)` + every div.s consumes $f20 (4 bodies polluted). The `(float)N`-vs-`N.0f` distinct-spelling CSE-break does NOT help here: with only 2 spellings for 4 sites you still get cross-call-live webs that grab saved FP regs. Fix when the TARGET rematerializes per site (`lui at,0x42fe; mtc1`): replace each literal with a DISTINCT extern f32 (`x / D_f127a`, `/ D_f127b`, ...) — a global load cannot be hoisted across the loop's calls (callees may store), so each site reloads (`lui+lwc1`, both insns at reloc sites = blinded vs the target's lui+mtc1). Kills the sdc1/ldc1 pair, the $f20 webs, and the frame slot. Contrast gl_func_0002AD1C (same file): there the target DOES want a callee-saved $f20 — its source loaded the extern float into a named local ONCE before the loop (`f32 sc = D_1058;`), so the natural C reproduces the save. Read the target's prologue for `sdc1` to decide which form the original used.


## NO-DEFAULT switch arm = loop-carried local -> memory home + in-loop s-reg promotion (mgrproc 2B7C, 2026-08-22 agent-h) <a name="no-default-switch-loop-carried-home-2b7c"></a>

Target tells (mgrproc_uso_func_00002B7C case-3 loop):
- `lw s3,0xA0(sp)` PRE-loop reading an UNINITIALIZED slot + `sw s3,0xA0(sp)` post-loop, with s3 assigned per-iter inside an inner switch and NO stores to the slot inside the loop.
- An unreachable `addiu s3,a3,K` sitting right before the switch join (the beql-converted lexically-LAST case block IDO didn't clean up), plus the default path's `b join; nop` assigning nothing.

Cause: the inner switch has NO default arm, so the local is only CONDITIONALLY assigned each iteration = loop-carried = uopt gives it a stack home and promotes it to a callee-saved reg for the whole loop region (region-boundary lw/sw syncs, register uses inside). Spelling `case 2: default:` (total assignment) makes it a plain per-iter temp (colors an arg reg, no home, no 5th saved reg) — that mis-spelling alone read as a "5-saved-reg / frame coloring cap" in the old note.

Knock-on effects when corrected: param bumps to the next saved reg (arg0 s3->s4), frame grows to target (-0xB8), and every `lw ...,0xD4(sX)` base rename resolves.

Companions on the same fn:
- Named `int idx = *(int*)(p+0x7DC) + i; arr[idx]` blocks uopt from distributing `(field+i)<<2` into a strength-reduced byte IV (`+=4, cmp 0x40`); keeps target's plain 0..0x10 counter + per-iter `addu; sll; addu`.
- `volatile int pad;` FIRST decl claims the top frame word so the four `volatile float = 1.0f` ghost slots land 0xA4-0xB0 and the carried local's home lands 0xA0 exactly.

Negatives (probed, don't re-grind): held `v = a3 + 0x490` used once post-call always folds `v+0x10 -> a3+0x4A0` (plain, multi-def, if(1) barrier, volatile decl, while(0) second use — volatile additionally hoists the addiu pre-switch and shifts the temp ring); while(0) ref-boost on the loop counter (`idx += s0` / triple `s2 += s0`) inert on the s0/s1 counter-glyph swap and the triple flips sub/s2 coloring (worse); reusing one `a3` var for the case-3/4 tail fixes the tail base v1->a3 but ALSO flips sub/s2 (net worse, keep separate `h`).

## Sparse-switch beq-chain: compares emit VALUE-SORTED ascending, bodies emit in SOURCE case order — descending source order gets reversed body layout + first-source body in the final beql delay (gl_func_0002FB74 89.4->97.0, 2026-08-23 agent-g) {#sparse-switch-body-source-order-2FB74}

For a small sparse `switch` lowered as a beq-to-body chain, IDO sorts the
COMPARES by case value ascending regardless of source order, but lays the case
BODIES out in SOURCE order after the chain. The source-order-FIRST case whose
compare is chain-LAST (i.e. the largest value, when source order is descending)
gets its single-insn body merged into that compare's `beql` delay slot, and the
source-order-LAST body falls through into the join with no trailing branch.
So a target layout of compares {2,4,8,258} with bodies {258(delay),8,4,2(f/t)}
means the source spelled `case 258: case 8: case 4: case 2:` — an if/else-if
chain or ascending case order instead costs +2 words (extra b + duplicated
body) and forward bodies. Same tick, two more shape reads for the kit:
- `if ((v & 0x80) == 0) { b = 0; } else { b = 1; }` reproduces the
  bne-to-else / fallthrough-then layout (plain `if (v & 0x80) b=1; else b=0;`
  gives the mirrored beq form).
- `c += 1; goto L_mid_ladder;` never emits the target's
  `beql at,zero,Lnext; addiu c,c,1` — that shape is as1's LIKELY-copy fill of
  the ladder-entry insn, so spell it as a PLAIN `goto L_ladder_head;` one label
  earlier (no explicit increment) and let the fill duplicate it.
- Per-site distinct extern aliases for one global (read/write split for `g ^= 1`
  / `g += 1`) break address-CSE so every access is its own `lui/%lo` pair,
  matching baked-abs (reloc-free USO) 2-insn shapes; a `*(s32 *)0x1C908`
  macro instead materializes lui/ori pointer = wrong shape.

## `p=&local` copy-prop block via non-dominating def + register-class merge to win a capped s-reg (90CC 82.7->90.6, agent-f 2026-09-04) {#addr-copyprop-block-and-sreg-class-merge-90cc}

Target shape (27 sites): `addiu s1,sp,0x7C` once, then per site `lw t,glob; addiu t8,sp,K; sw t,K(sp); lw t5,0(t8); sw t5,0(s1)` and `lw a2,0(s1)` — a pointer to a local W90 held in s1, struct-copied through the pointer. m2c decodes it as `spK = glob; sp7C = spK`. Measured route:

- `W90 *hp = &sp7C; *hp = spK; f(.., *hp, ..)` — uopt copy-propagates the address (reaching-def based, not single-def: a dead later def, an earlier opaque def, two same-value defs, `&arr[1]`, `&big.field`, `hp++`/`hp--`, `(W90*)&other` all still fold). Fuzzy +0.0.
- `hp = (W90 *)(u32)&sp7C` (any int-cast: s32/u32/`&~0`/`+0`) blocks the fold but DEMOTES hp to a memory home (`sw t,K(sp)` at def, `lw` at every use, frame +4) — this is the predecessor's 81.7 non-monotonic state. Not a register candidate any more.
- `hp = cond ? &sp7C : &sp104` blocks the fold AND keeps hp a candidate → s1 (82.7->88.95) at the cost of a 3-insn branch diamond.
- **Best: put the single `hp = &sp7C` INSIDE the preceding site's `if` body** (its fail path bypasses the def). A def that does not dominate a use is never propagated; hp stays s1; no extra branch (88.95->89.20). Residual: the `addiu s1,sp` is scheduled in the body block, target has it in the join block (straight-line join def folds — not reachable).
- **s-reg class merge**: this fn only ever colors s0-s2. Once sub1 (`var_s0`) was memory-homed (`sw a0,K(sp); lw a0`) because uopt's 3 s-regs went to higher-use webs. Merging every m2c local that the target keeps in the SAME s-reg into one C variable (var_s0+var_s0_2+var_s0_4; var_s1+sub-object+hp+var_s1_3, with `(W90 *)` casts at the struct-copy sites) lets each class win its register: 89.20->90.60, seg 2-5 exact. Merging only one class shifted the other class OUT of its s-reg (85.9) — merge all classes in one step. This is the opposite of #shared-spill-home-cap-90cc (which merged the a0-class per-site pointers — those must stay disjoint temps).

## Shared spill-temp homes are NOT C-reachable: the 90CC frame cap (m2c local-explosion endgame) {#shared-spill-home-cap-90cc}

Context: bootup_uso func_000090CC (8424B, 77.0), frame build 736 vs target 376. The target's ~41 disjoint per-cascade pointer webs are all colored $a0 and spill to THREE shared homes (12 pairs -> 0x108, 28 -> 0x80, 1 -> 0x8C). Both C routes to close the frame were measured and both fail non-monotonically:

- **Merge the 41 m2c cascade locals into shared variables**: frame 736->576 but the merged variable becomes ONE uopt candidate and gets PROMOTED to callee-saved $s3 (`sw s3,48(sp)` appears in prologue) — fuzzy 77.0->71.7. A merged variable's ref-count makes s-reg promotion strictly profitable; storage class is not preservable through the merge.
- **Per-cascade block-scoped locals** (`{ char *pw; ... }` x41, one candidate each): s3 promotion gone (correct s0-s2), but **IDO 7.1 -O2 does NOT overlay sibling-scope block locals** — each block local gets its own distinct frame slot (41 slots, 0xA0-0x150). Frame only 736->728, fuzzy 76.85.

The shared home is uopt's internal spill-temp POOL, not a variable home — i.e. in the original source the cascade pointer was a non-candidate temporary (construct unknown). No C-level construct found that yields "41 separate webs + shared spill home". Treat "N disjoint same-reg webs sharing K<<N spill slots" in a big fn as this cap class.

Higher-yield residuals on such fns (90CC's ranked list): (1) m2c-collapsed-callee reconstruction gap (addiu -47 / lw -31 histogram delta ~ +4pp), (2) blanked-symbol store sites (baked-USO-symbol cap class), (3) li/sh/ori fall-through regions decoded as if/else, (4) 0.0f $f0-reuse CSE, (5) bnel/beqzl loop-form flips. Frame-delta work yields ~0 fuzzy until the frame is EXACT (any nonzero delta breaks all sp-immediates equally) — do not half-close frames.

## Blank-global RMW: ld/st cast-alias pairs restore the direct-global shape (folded lw + $at store); volatile and array forms do NOT (90CC 77.5->78.4, agent-f) {#blank-global-ldst-alias-pairs-90cc}

m2c decodes blanked-USO-global RMW as `*(s32 *)((char *)&D_00000000 + K) op= ...`. When one base symbol serves many sites, uopt GCSEs the address into a cached base reg (lui/addiu once, `lw/sw K(base)` everywhere) and value-forwards between the |= and &= statements — target instead shows per-site `lui rd; lw rd,%lo+K(rd)` loads, `lui at; sw %lo+K(at)` stores, and a RELOAD between adjacent RMW statements.

Fix that measured best: one **pair** of blank extern aliases per RMW site, load-side and store-side (`bu_90cc_g8_ld/_st`, precedent `D_2D710_load/store`), used in **non-volatile cast form**: `*(s32 *)&g8_st = *(s32 *)&g8_ld | 8;`. Distinct symbols kill both the addr CSE and the store-to-load forwarding; cast form lets the lo16 fold into the access (no addiu).

Measured variants on the same 3-statement region (fuzzy): plain shared D_00000000 base = baseline; distinct per-site aliases, scalar/array decl form = +0.0 shape-wrong (addiu-base persists because load+store share the symbol); `extern volatile` = +0.42 (serializes, still addiu-base); non-volatile ld/st cast pairs = +0.95 (shape-exact). Gotcha: `volatile` blocks the lo16 fold — volatile pointer-cast RMW always emits lui+addiu+lw 0(base).

Related negative results same session (90CC mode-select block, target A330): sparse 2-case `switch` gives the right layout (default inline, cases out-of-line) but VALUE-SORTED ascending compares (see #sparse-switch-body-source-order-2FB74); expected tests 7-then-6 descending remains unmatched. Explicit `if(x==7) goto` chain gets RE-NORMALIZED by IDO into bne-with-inline-body (worse than switch). Chained assignment `a = b = 0.0f` does NOT share one FP-zero reg; adjacent `x=0.0f` stores after a jal each get their own mtc1 (unsolved 1-insn residual).

**Per-site alias SWEEP payoff (same session):** the alias principle scales — one shared internal symbol (`D_00008018`) referenced at 38 `+0xC` vtable-store sites had been GCSE'd into a per-cascade pre-jal `lui/addiu s0` web; splitting into 37 per-site aliases flipped every store to the target's post-jal `lui tN/addiu tN` temp phase: 78.44->82.37 (+3.93pp) in one mechanical pass (plus +0.31 for the 3-site D_00008060 family). When a big NM fn stores one `&sym` at N>10 sites and target rematerializes per site, alias-sweep the whole family, not one site at a time.

**Remaining 90CC residual (next vein):** per-cascade `W90` struct copies decoded as `spA = glob; spB = spA` — target spells them `t=glob; sw t,local; addiu ptr,sp,X; lw t2,0(ptr); sw t2,0(s1)` (copy lands through a *pointer deref* `*s1`, with an explicitly materialized `&local` reload). Accounts for the persistent addiu -45 / sw +19 / move -8 histogram signature (~28 repeat sites). Needs the list-head pointer variable reconstructed (m2c collapsed it to sp locals); untested.

## `if (1) {}` barrier demotes a merged multi-role web from s-reg promotion (shared spill home kept); vestigial beqzl re-tests are literal redundant source tests (h2h 620 / 17A0, 2026-09-04 agent-h) {#if1-barrier-demotes-merged-web-vestigial-retests-620-17a0}

## Short-circuit alloc-cascade head: `(x != 0) || (x = alloc(N), x != 0)` (arcproc 251C 73.1->100) {#short-circuit-alloc-cascade-251c}

Multi-level constructor cascades (level-1 ptr present? else alloc; level-2 present? else alloc; ...) decoded by m2c as nested `if (p2) { if (p3) ... }` are a NON-equivalent control flow when the target falls through to the next level after a successful alloc. Spell each level as one short-circuit expression: `if ((x != 0) || (x = (T*)alloc(N), x != 0)) { ...next level... }` — 251C went 72.4->98.6 and size-exact from this alone. Companions on the same fn: ONE variable web (`a3`) for the level-2 pointer, the vtable pointer AND both registration nodes — the target overlays all three roles on a single home (0x3C(sp)); a separate `node` local splits the home and re-colors level-2 to v1. `if (1) {}` barrier before the dispatch-base load colors it into the dead $v0 (timproc 2A8C lever); an unused `volatile int pad` supplies a +8 frame and lifts the arg0 spill slot. Sibling idiom: the nested-goto alloc-guard (#nested-goto-alloc-guard-bnezl-9b88) is the bnezl-FIRST variant; the short-circuit form is for beq-after-call cascades that continue on success.

h2h C18 corollary (80.9->86.7): a "permuter-floored coloring cap" on an s1/s2 param/slot tie was a decode artifact — the call's 4th arg was a RE-READ of `a0->0x51C` (target `lw a3,1308(s1)`), not the local; the local dies at its store. Re-verify every call-arg source against raw words before declaring a coloring cap.

## Big-offset `(char*)&D+K` CSE base is 32K-aligned, not exact; dead-if un-substitutes conversion temps (game_libs_post 2D37C / 31A74, 2026-09-04 agent-g)

- **32K-aligned CSE base.** `*(int*)((char*)&D_x + 0x1CAA8)` used twice (load+store) does NOT materialize `lui v0,2; addiu v0,-13656; lw 0(v0)` (the target shape when the original symbol lives AT 0x1CAA8). uopt CSEs `&D_x + (K & ~0x7FFF)` = `lui 2; addiu -0x8000` and leaves `+0x4AA8` in the load/store offsets. A named pointer `cp = (int*)((char*)&D+K)` and a direct `&sym` (alias valued 0x1CAA8) both fold to fused `lui/lw`. Exact-base materialization needs a symbol whose address IS the target (value-0x1CAA8 alias + inline addend 0), whose bytes objdiff can't score against a reloc-free expected .o (ROM bake path only). Small offsets (0..0x18, gl_func_0002D37C) CSE fine as `lui a2,0; addiu a2,a2,0` + field offsets — struct/array spellings of the same fields fuse per access instead.
- **Dead-if candidate flip for a sunk conversion.** `fr = (f32)raw_u32; ... store A; store B; D = fr;` — uopt forward-substitutes the single-use `fr` to its store, so the u32->f32 `bgez/add 4f80` sequence lands AFTER the earlier stores. `if (fr) {}` (and `if (z) {}` for a 0.0f local, `if (half) {}` for an int) turns each into a candidate: computed up front, colored f0/f2/a0-class, ZERO home stores. `if (0) { f(&fr); }` escape also un-sinks but adds dead home stores in-tree (frame +24). `while(0)`, `if(0){f(z,fr)}` (by value) = no effect.
- **Float-in-a1 callee.** `mfc1 a1,$fN; jal` = prototyped `(int, float)` callee (`gl_func_00000000_f`); a `0.0f` literal there is `addiu a1,zero,0` (int 0 is `or a1,zero,zero`).
- **Compound `*=`** puts the destination variable FIRST in `mul.s fd,fd,ft`; `x = pool * x` and `x = x * pool` both emitted `ft,fd` here.
- **Hoisted `lp = &tbl[i]` before an if whose else-arm loads `*lp`** reproduces `lui at; addu at,at,t9` scheduled above the `bc1f` with the `lwc1 0(at)` left in the arm (ugen keeps the fused at-form; no t-reg pointer appears).

## Alloc-cascade ctor family kit: folded get-or-create, temp-first address order, same-line home-reload pin, interleaved volatile pads (bootup 5124/51D4/5284/5334/53E8 -> 100 x5, 2026-09-04 agent-f) {#alloc-cascade-ctor-family-kit-5124}

Five 44-46-insn `alloc -> init -> descriptor stores` constructors, all exact from one body (only the init datum, object size and tail stores differ). Target shape: `sw a0,0x38(sp)` (4-byte struct-by-value param home) -> `lw/sw` copy to 0x2C -> copy to 0x1C -> `lw a1,0x1C; ... jal; sw a1,4(sp)` (by-value arg home in the delay slot); obj/o2 memory-homed at 0x30/0x24 (no s-regs); frame 0x38.

1. **Frame 0x38 with 4 live homes at 0x30/0x2C/0x24/0x1C** (pitch-8 except obj/b1 adjacent): three `volatile int` pads interleaved in decl order — `volatile int p0; char *obj; Box b1; volatile int p1; char *o2; volatile int p2; Box b2;`. IDO allocates top-down in decl order; each pad costs one 4-byte slot with zero insns. (Same lever as the 56898 pitch-8 spill homes.)
2. **Get-or-create test shape.** `o2 = obj; if (o2 == 0) o2 = alloc(0x48); if (o2 != 0) {...}` tests the copy (`beqz a0` after `move a0,v0`) and hoists the by-value `lw a1/sw a1,4(sp)` above the sw-homes. Same CFG, different test operand — an operand-selection lever, not a structure change.
3. **Paired symbol-address stores emit order.** `p->a = &B; p->b = &C;` -> `lui t0; lui t1; addiu t0; addiu t1; sw t0; sw t1`. Target had `addiu t1; addiu t0`. `{ char *t = &C; p->a = &B; p->b = t; }` emits `addiu t1(C)` first; stores and temp numbering (t0=B, t1=C: numbering follows STORE order, not computation order) unchanged. 4. **Home-reload placement = same-line join.** After the init call: `lui t9; addiu t9; lw v1,0x30(sp); sw t9,0x28(a0)` (obj reload after the addiu). Two statements on separate lines gave `lui t9; lw v1; addiu t9; sw`. Putting `func(o2, b2, 0); *(char **)(o2 + 0x28) = &A;` on ONE source line pins the reload after the addiu (the as1 debug-line tie-break, see the same-line section). Corollary: the whole tail block must be on ONE line too — splitting 53E8's 4-statement tail across lines regressed `li t1,1` and both addius back to source order (X1 100 vs X2-X5 95.7-97.8 in a 5-variant probe).
5. Reloc residual: the target's descriptor lui/addiu carry NO relocs in expected/ (USO sidecar); placeholder `extern char D_00000000_a/b/c` (= 0 in undefined_syms_auto.txt) assemble to the same bytes -> ROM byte-identical; refresh expected/<unit>.o from the ROM-exact build so objdiff scores 100.

Probe method that found 2-4: standalone `cc -O2` + a reloc-normalized objdump diff (mask lui/addiu %hi/%lo immediates and jal/branch targets) — the un-normalized diff hides pure REORDERS behind reloc-annotation noise and reported "structural exact" at 85%.

## Volatile-home kit II: `char *volatile` r/obj, per-site alias pairs for the flag word, block-temp keeps or-chains unfolded, one-color-per-variable (timproc D550 82.4->91.9 / D14C 81.7->97.1, 2026-09-04 agent-h) {#volatile-home-kit-ii-d550-d14c}

Same D550/D14C/D884 constructor family as #volatile-bridge-serial-s0-d14c-d884. What replaced the PASS-3 residuals:

The re-test after `obj = child` must be spelled on the register value (`child != 0 ||`), a volatile `obj != 0` reloads. Where the target instead shows `or a2,v0` in the delay and `sw a2,HOME` around calls (D14C obj), it is a plain candidate with a spill home — leave it plain.
3. **Flag-word accesses = per-site NON-volatile cast-alias externs** (`extern char f_l1,f_l2,f_s1,...; *(s32 *)((char *)&f_l1 + 4)`): each load emits `lui r; lw r,4(r)`, each store `lui at; sw v,4(at)` (90CC #blank-global-ldst-alias-pairs-90cc transfers 1:1). Same symbol for load+store of one statement keeps the addiu base (D14C EE64 needed a pair). 4. **Unfolded `and; or(lui); ori; ori; ori` chain with ONE store** (D14C): `{ int x = (LD(l2) & 0xFFF7FFFF) | 0x20000 | 0x2000 | 2 | 1; ST(s1) = x; }` — cfe does NOT reassociate through the temp. An `if (1) {}` right before the block colors x v0 (v1 without it).
5. **One color per VARIABLE.** Block-scope temps are separate variables and get separate colors; a v0<->v1 placement swap between two such temps (D550 p vs rr) flips with a single `if (1) {}` before the first web. Where the target uses a temp for an address (`lui t6; sll; addu t6; lw a1,0(t6)`) but the build folds it into the destination (`lui a1; ...; lw a1,0(a1)`), the destination is a DIFFERENT variable in the target: declare it in the ghost slot (`int n2;` replacing the `volatile int pad0`) — free frame-wise, D14C +0.3 and it also fixed the jalr-block schedule. `volatile s32 arg1, arg2` params (instead of `if (0) f(&arg1,&arg2)`) turn the twice-used arg2 into a v1 candidate (`lw v1,104(sp)` + `addiu t3,v1,1`).
6. **Decode:** `jal X` with `sw v0,SLOT(sp)` in the delay and `lw a0,SLOT(sp)` right after = the PRE-call pointer spilled/restored, X's result discarded (`import_0010D33C(p, n);` not `p = ...`).

Open residuals (both fns): EE38/EE68/EE7C vtable-pair `addiu` order (target lui A, lui B, addiu B, addiu A, sw A, sw B — store-order swap moves the stores too); dead `p += 0xB4` addiu kept by the target; D550 FP tail temp ring (zero#1 f4 / 1.0 f16) and g2 cluster temp folding to t7 (target v1); D14C p/obj2 colored a2 (target a3).

## Escaping frame struct for address-taken vectors: keeps dead-field math alive, forces per-use lwc1/swc1 (bootup 63B4 23.4->76.0, agent-f 2026-09-04) {#escaping-frame-struct-63b4}
