## A comma expression is emitted right-to-left but ring-numbered left-to-right; `!= (0, 0.0f)` = operand-first `c.eq.s`; a named squared length drops $f16 out of the ring (gl_func_00064DEC EXACT 157/157, 2026-09-11 agent-g) <a name="comma-expression-emits-right-to-left-64dec"></a>

Target (post1b, -O2, 157 words, frame 0xA8, s0 + ra; 5 blank jals): integrate two Vec3 fields, snapshot
`delta = vel - prev` through THREE stack temps (`sp70 -> sp7C -> sp54`, word copies, then float stores to
+0x330), `prev = vel` through `sp7C`, three more Vec3 copies after a call, then `len2 = x*x + y*y + z*z;
if (len2 != 0) { len = sqrtf(len2); dir = vel / len; } else { zeros }`. The 91.5% wrap had the right shape
for ten weeks; every residual was a colouring/emission-order effect, measured standalone (`probe.sh`, jal masked):

| step | spelling | words off |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | wrap as landed (named `sumsq`, if(1)-materialised `pB`/`pC`, z,y,x diffs) | 91 |
| 1 | `spA4[0] = dy*dy + dz*dz + dx*dx; if (spA4[0] != 0.0f) { r = sqrtf(spA4[0]); ...}` (no named sum) | 36 |
| 2 | `while (0) { dz = pC->x; }` anchor before the `FF(0xB8) +=` line (pC coloured $v0, pB $v1) | 31 |
| 3 | + `FF(0xFC) = sp34.z;` BEFORE `FF(0x100) = FF(0xD8);` (last pre-jal ring pair) | 26 |
| 4 | + diff block inside `do { ... } while (0);` (&sp7C web no longer hoisted above pC's loads: $a2 -> $v0) | 9 |
| 5 | + diffs in x,y,z order, anchor names `dx`, later block reads 318->dy / 320->dz / 31C->dx | 9 (same 9: the schedule) |
| 6 | + `dx = pB->x - pC->x, dy = pB->y - pC->y, dz = pB->z - pC->z;` (ONE comma expression) | 1 |
| 7 | + `if (spA4[0] != (0, 0.0f))` | **0** |

What each one is:

1. **A named float that is stored AND tested across a branch is a candidate; the target's is not.** Named
   `sumsq` coloured $f14 (4th FP colour after dz/dy/dx = f0/f2/f12), so the 0.0f constant (5 uses across the
   arms) took $f16 -- and a candidate holding $f16 removes it from the ring for the WHOLE function: every
   temp from the second `lwc1` on was one phase early (`lwc1 $f18,792` where the target has `$f16`). Spelling
   the sum as an array element that is re-read by address (`spA4[0]`, #store-forward-ring-across-bb-and-scaled-index-first-675a4)
   makes it a store-forwarded ring temp (`add.s $f8; swc1 $f8,164(sp); c.eq.s $f8; mov.s $f12,$f8` for the
   sqrtf arg) and the constant colours $f14. The 5.3-style `struct { f32 v; }` home lands at 0x28, not 0xA4;
   `Vec3 spA4[1]` grows the frame 8; the 1-element float array is the only home that sits at the frame top.
2. **The `while (0)` anchor's ASSIGNED variable gets the ref boost too.** `while (0) { dz = pC->x; }`
   coloured pC first (target $v0) but also promoted `dz` to $f0; the target order is dx f0 / dy f2 / dz f12 =
   plain bitpos order, so the anchor must name `dx` (the variable that is first anyway).
3. **An address-of-local CSE web (`addiu v0,sp,124`, 12 uses over two call-separated regions) is
   hoisted to the top of its basic block.** In one flat BB it is defined before pC's loads, interferes with
   both pointer webs and with a0/a1 (both regions), and colours $a2; a `do { } while (0)` around the diff
   statements puts the BB start after pC's last use, and the web takes $v0 (pC's colour, lowest free).
   `if (1) { }`, a do-while around only the copies, or around only the subs all work the same.
4. **cfe emits the operands of a comma expression right-to-left.** Three assignment statements in x,y,z
   order give ring numbers x = f4/f6, y = f8/f10, z = f16/f18 AND an x-first schedule; in z,y,x order the
   ring numbers move with them (z = f4/f6). The target has x-first ring numbers with a z-first schedule
   (`lwc1 $f18,8(v0); lwc1 $f16,8(v1); ... sub.s $f12,$f16,$f18` first): the comma expression numbers the
   ring in source order but emits the assignments last-first. Store order of the three results is
   irrelevant (uopt emits each store right after its sub either way); chained `sp70.x = dx = ...` regresses
   (+5), an indexed `for` over the three floats is not unrolled (+150).
5. **`x != (0, 0.0f)` = `c.eq.s x,zero`; `x != 0.0f`, `0.0f != x`, `!(x == 0.0f)`, `x != (f32)0`, `*p`,
   `p[i].v`, `((Vec3 *)p)->x` all = `c.eq.s zero,x`.** The #comma-constant-const-first-mul-5d754 rank
   rule transfers to compares: the comma makes the literal an expression operand and the (forwarded) memory
   operand outranks it. `x != 0` / `x != 0.0` / `x != -0.0f` change the constant's materialisation (+3).
6. **Colours are per-variable across dead gaps.** The later block (`lwc1 $f2,792; $f12,800; $f0,796`) reuses
   the diff-block colours, so it must read 0x318 into dy, 0x320 into dz, 0x31C into dx and sum
   `dy*dy + dz*dz + dx*dx`; any other naming swaps f2/f12 there.
7. **A dead `f32 sumsq;` declaration is load-bearing** (#named-scalar-dead-homes-frame-bottom-659cc): dropping
   it moved both arg spill homes (`sw a0,40(sp)` / `sw a1,36(sp)`) down by 4 = 33 words. Keep the ghost.

Also: the sqrt-family callee must be the PROTOTYPED `f32 gl_func_00000000_sqf(f32)` blank
(undefined_syms_auto.txt) -- a K&R extern promotes the arg to double (cvt.d.s + mov.d) and an in-TU stub
would link a real address.

## `for (i = 0; i != N; i++)` vs `i = 0; do { } while (i != N)`: same 102 words, but the do/while spelling lets as1 schedule `or s1,zero,zero` between the hoisted `lui s5` / `addiu s5` sym+K pair; the for-init keeps the pair adjacent. Also: an exact that calls a K&R-defined in-TU stub links to a REAL address -- the byte gate passes, the ROM gate fails (gl_func_00066D54 EXACT 102/102, 2026-09-11 agent-g) <a name="for-init-vs-dowhile-preheader-lui-addiu-adjacency-66d54"></a>

Per-slot poll loop (post1b, -O2, 4 iterations, 10 calls, s0-s8 all live). Three findings:

1. **uopt hoists the loop-invariant constants itself; naming them costs a frame slot and
   reorders the s-candidates.** Target preheader: `lui s5,2; addiu s5,s5,0x2570` (message base
   `D+0x22570`), `or s1,zero,zero` (i), `addiu s8,zero,10`, `addiu s7,zero,0x68` (stride),
   `addiu s6,sp,83` (&sp53). Writing `msgbase = D + 0x22570; ten = 10; stride = 0x68; psp53 =
   &sp53;` as locals (the 97.99 wrap) gives frame 96 and a different s-order. Leave every one
   of them inline (`(char *)&D_00000000 + 0x22570`, `var_s1 * 0x68`, literal `10`, `&sp53`).
2. **`== 10` / `== 0` on a call result is an if/else CHAIN in that order**
   (`bne v0,s8,L0; ... L0: bnez v0,JOIN`), not a `switch` -- the switch lowers its compare
   chain in case-label order (`beqz` first, then `bne ..,s8`), 2 words off with identical arms
   (#switch-arm-order-is-test-chain-and-layout-309ac).
3. **The loop spelling controls the preheader schedule, not the words.** `var_s1 = 0; do { ...
   var_s1 += 1; } while (var_s1 != 4);` emits the same 102 words but as1 places
   `or s1,zero,zero` BETWEEN `lui s5` and `addiu s5,s5,0x2570` (it fills the lui->addiu gap
   with the independent init). `for (var_s1 = 0; var_s1 != 4; var_s1++)` keeps the pair

derives the block-copy destination cursor from it, hence the `or` rather than a second `addiu`). On separate lines the
line order wins (ra-save first); on ONE line the copy init sinks first.

|---|---|
| `{` / decls / `buf1 = *src;` on their own lines (the wrap) | 2 |
| `void f(int s0, struct B384 *src) { struct B384 buf1; struct B8 buf2; buf1 = *src;` (one line) | **0** |
| `void f(int s0, struct B384 *src) { struct B384 buf1 = *src; struct B8 buf2;` (initializer on the brace line) | **0** (landed) |
| decls on their own lines, `buf1 = *src; gl_func_00000000(&buf1);` joined on a LATER line | 2 |

| spelling | words / diff lines |
|---|---|
| hand-stepped cursors, any decl order (the wrap) | 30 / 8-16 |
| **`for (k = 0; k < 10; k++) { *(int *)(D + k*0x44 + 0x3C) = 0; f(D + 0x18 + k*0x44, D + 0x30 + k*0x44, 1); }`** (also `k != 10`) | **30 / 0** |

inits are ordinary statements, emitted in source order and never reversed. The trip test lands on the

like A670's last-arg 0xD388 cursor; `k` has only linear uses, so no `or vN,zero,zero` corpse remains

until after its init is emitted; untested here). The typed-struct spelling loses because cfe folds the field offsets
differently (the +0x3C store is no longer its own product). So the lens now has three signatures:
rotated s-colours with a dead zero move (A670), `lui/addiu` pair adjacency (66D54), and a REVERSED init

## 688F8: inlined derived/base ctor pair; local decl order picks the jal-delay spill slot (gl_func_000688F8 EXACT 26/26, 2026-10-14 agent-g) <a name="inlined-ctor-pair-decl-order-spill-slot-688f8"></a>

Target shape (frame 0x20, unused `a0` homed at 0x20): `jal alloc(0x30); beqz v0,end; or a1,v0; bnez v0,store; or v1,v0; li a0,0x20; jal alloc; sw v0,0x18(sp); lw a1,0x18(sp); beqz v0,skip; or v1,v0; store: v1[7]=&D1; skip: a1[7]=&D2; end: return a1`. ```c

```c
p = alloc(0x30);
if (p == 0) goto end;
b = p;
if (b != 0) goto store;
b = alloc(0x20);
if (b == 0) goto skip;
store: b[7] = (int)&D_00000000;
skip:  p[7] = (int)&D_00000000_688f8;   /* distinct base-0 alias */
end:   return p;
```

Same-size near-misses with a jal-delay `sw v0,X(sp)` one slot off: permute local DECL order before reaching for volatile pads.

## 6337C: address-taken iterator locals let uopt forward the head pointer; advance through `next` keeps the ring temp (gl_func_0006337C EXACT 64/64, 2026-10-14 agent-g) <a name="address-taken-iterator-locals-forwarded-ring-6337c"></a>

List walk whose `cur` / `next` live in adjacent stack slots (sp+44 / sp+48) and are reloaded after the call. A `volatile struct { int *cur, *next; } it;` reproduces the slots but forbids store-to-load forwarding, so the head pointer has to be a NAMED local `n` -> a uopt candidate -> `$v1`, and every following ring temp shifts (97.81%). Target instead keeps the head in the load's own ring temp (`lw t8,48(s0); sw t8,48(sp); beqz t8; sw t8,44(sp); lw t0,4(t8)`).

Fix: plain locals made memory-resident by the 69B94 barrier (`if (1) { bar = &cur; bar = &next; }`; decl order next, cur gives next the higher slot). Memory-resident but non-volatile -> uopt forwards `cur = next` from the value just stored, and the pointer stays a ring temp:

```c
next = (int *) self[0x30 / 4];
cur = next;
val = cur ? (next = (int *) cur[1], cur[0]) : 0;
while (val != 0) {
    ... cur[0] ... call ...
    cur = next;
    val = cur ? (next = (int *) next[1], cur[0]) : 0;   /* next[1], NOT cur[1] */
}
```

The loop tail needs the advance read through `next` (the reload): with `cur[1]` the reloaded value is shared by three uses and becomes a `$v1` candidate (14 diff lines); `next[1]` (or `val = (cur = next) ? (next = next[1], cur[0]) : 0`) keeps it in ring `$t7`. Probed-inert tail forms: if/else arm, `cur != 0`, `*cur`, block-scope `n`, same-line. The 69B94-style single rotated `while (cur = next, ...)` copy also lands the head in t8 but colours `val` v1 and breaks the tail layout.

Second application, same day: gl_func_00069B94 (post1b, 98.66 -> EXACT 41/41) -- the wrap that had cracked the layout with that rotated single-copy `while` still carried the `$v1` key / `$v0` next residual; rewriting it as explicit pre-loop advance + tail `next = next[1]` advance closed all 10 words. (1) **Assigning a whole local-array element promotes it.** One `args[0] = args[1];` in one case made uopt treat args[0]
as a register-cached scalar for the WHOLE function: every `(u8)args[0]` read became `lw` + `andi 0xff` (two andi when
read twice) instead of the target's `lbu 99(sp)`. Copying through a 1-word struct view
(`*(W *)&args[0] = *(W *)&args[1]`) keeps the element memory-resident (`lw t1,100(sp); sw t1,96(sp)` then `lbu`).
(2) **One reused byte variable.** The target held the opcode and every per-case `(u8)args[0]` in ONE s-reg; a single
`u8 op` assigned in each case reproduced it (separate `x`/`op` names coloured s0 instead of s2 and shifted o/sub/cmd).
(3) **Named call-arg temp flips the delay-slot fill:** `f(q, (u8)args[0])` emits `or a0,s0; jal; lbu a1` but
`y = args[0]; f(q, y);` emits `lbu a1; jal; or a0,s0` (the target's order) -- y colours a1 directly.
(4) **Array declared LAST** sits at the BOTTOM of the local area: target args[] at sp+96 with nothing above it was
reachable only that way here (other names' homes then sit above it; frame 0xB8 vs 0x88 is the leftover).
(5) A `for (i = 0; i < n; i++) args[i] = ...` pull loop (not a hand-written `p < end` pointer loop) produced the
target's double `andi 0xff` count truncation and the dead `or v0,zero,zero` (i's exit value) after the loop.
(6) Status bits written as 1-bit bitfields (`o->stop`, `cmd->paused`; cf. #one-bit-bitfield-test-dead-srl-phantom-25bfc)
re-phased the t-register sequence of the whole function (+0.5). (7) Re-fetching into the short-lived `r` in the
0x50/0x60 cases (`r = fetch(sub); tbl[n][r + 0xD4] = ...`) kept `n` in s5; with the call inline uopt re-derived n
as `r & 0xF` after the call and dragged `r` into s0. Open: r colours v0 (target copies it to a0 in the slti delay
slot); B5/C8 `op = args[0]` still lw+andi.

**gl_func_0002C7A4 (same unit, NM 80.3 -> 96.7, run 65):** the sibling VM tick took the same levers (bitfield status
bits, plain `for` cleanup sweep, `r = fetch()` in the case that uses the homed byte `n`). Two new ones:

loop entry); the target materialises `lui at,0x42fe; mtc1 at` at EVERY site. Spelling one of them `(f32)127` keeps
them separate candidates and nothing is hoisted (all-same `127.0f` cost -4.1). Check this whenever the build saves an

(9) **`r &= 0xFF;` before the second-level split**: the target's low path reads `v1 = r & 0xFF` (computed once for the
`>= 0xC0` test and reused for `& 0xF0` / `& 0xF`); writing `(r & 0xFF)` in each test kept the original v0 and moved the

`andi a1,s0,0xff`; a `u8 op` drops it and spills op across the inner call.

**gl_func_00030AF4 (same unit, NM 84.8 -> 91.5, run 66) -- switch-shape levers:**
(10) **A switch whose real labels are sparse compiles to a compare LADDER, not a table.** Target switch2 is a
`sltiu 12` jump table with bodies only for 0/9/10/11; with just those four labels IDO 7.1 emitted `beqz/beq` chains.
Adding the absent labels explicitly (`case 1: case 2: ... case 8: break;`) restores the table (+2.3). Count the
target's sltiu bound vs your label count whenever the build has a ladder where the target has `jr`.
(11) **`case 3: default:` on one body.** A small switch whose dispatch is `beqz; beq 1; beq 2; beq 3 -> X; b X` (the
explicit compare AND the fall-out both land on the same address) is a ladder switch with case 3 merged into default.
An if/else-if chain gives a different ladder (and homes maybe-uninit locals assigned in the arms, cf. 28C6C);
a 2-label `switch (sub) { case 0: ...; case 1: ...; }` also reproduced a `beqz; beq 1; b end` tail that if/else did not.
(12) **Homed-arg single load:** `D_s = sub; if (sub == 2)` reloads the homed K&R arg twice; the assignment
expression `if ((D_s = sub) == 2)` loads it once (target `lw t5,60(sp); sw t5,D_s; bne t5,2`).

A block-local `s32 *cp = &G` DOES hold one `lui/addiu a2` base for the load, stores and `lbu 3(a2)` (+1.1).

**gl_func_0002B09C (same unit, NM 74.0 -> 87.8, run 66):** this unit's jump tables live in the same bootup.uso
section 7 as the base unit's: `lw tN,IMM(at)` table = RoData word at `IMM + 4`, case address = value - 0x1466C
(game_libs shim) - function start (see MATCHING_WORKFLOW #game-libs-rodata-literals-and-tables-76f0). The table
showed a 3-arm numerator/denominator select (cases 1,3,5 / 2,4 / default) where the old wrap had a 2-arm guess.
Also: `xor t3,v0,tOld` with `lw tOld,76(a2)` AFTER the `jal` = the old-field read is written after the call
(`r = f(); old = o->p; o->p = r; t3 = (r == old)`); a pre-call read becomes a spilled local.

**gl_func_00025504 (same unit, NM 65.6 -> 93.6, run 66):** an old header blamed "IDO rematerialises the
0xFFFFFF mask 7x, not forceable from C" -- that is exactly the bitfield-extract tell
(#bitfield-extract-and-with-at-macro-258cc). Typing word0 as the 258C0 `{pad:4, sh:2, pad:2, msk:24}` struct

## 64388: the stack frame is a DECL-ORDER map -- every declared scalar owns a home slot; carrier struct copies; `if (1)` blocks set 3-component FP colouring (gl_func_00064388 NM 79.13 -> 97.30, 2026-10-14 agent-g) <a name="decl-order-frame-map-carrier-copy-64388"></a>

Target frame 0xB0 with Vec3 locals at 164/148/108/96/68/48 and unexplained 4..24-byte gaps between them; the old wrap
(0x98) put all scalars after the structs. In IDO 7.1 -O2 locals are laid out top-down in declaration order; here EVERY
declared scalar took a 4-byte home even though it lives in a register (unused `f32 pad[n]` / unused ints always take
slots, cf. 4F0C8). CAVEAT: this is not universal -- in sibling gl_func_000690A8 (same unit) the register-only scalars
(x/y/z/m/s/p) took NO slot (frame 0x30 = f32 v[3] + the loop counter's home only). Probe per function: add/remove one
used scalar decl and watch the frame/offsets. When it holds, count the gap words between consecutive structs and
declare that many of your real scalars there:
`Vec3 m; f32 len; f32 g[3]; f32 spd; f32 ax,ay,az,bx,by,bz; Vec3 t; Vec3 d; f32 c0,c1,c2,one; Vec3 e; Vec3 *pv,*qv;
Vec3 h;` reproduced every offset (m 164, len 160, g 148, spd 144, six scalars 120..143, t 108, d 96, four 80..95, e 68,
pv/qv 60..67, h 48) and the CSE temp of `arg0 + 0x1C` (spilled across two calls) lands at 40 only when the scalar count
is exact -- one extra declared pointer moves it to 36. Reusing an already-declared pointer for a late base (`qv = arg0 +
0x10` after the calls) instead of a new `pw` keeps the count.

Other levers in the same function:
- `lw/sw` word copy `d -> sp108 -> e` with the second leg interleaved (`lw t1,0(v0)` before the third store) = an explicit
  carrier struct: `t = d; e = t;` (same `t` reused for the second `t = h; m = t;`).
- Pointers `pv = arg0 + 4; qv = arg0 + 0x28;` written BEFORE the `if (len < K)` test stay materialized (`addiu v0,a0,4`)
  instead of folding into offsets (26AA4 rule); the late base in its own statement before an `if (1) {}` block likewise.
- `x * 1.0f` folds; `if (1) { one = 1.0f; } else { one = arg3; }` keeps `lui at,0x3f80; mtc1; mul.s`.
- Named results `bx = pv->x - qv->x; ...; d.z = bz; d.y = by; d.x = bx;` wrapped in `if (1) { ... }` gave the target
  colouring x f0 / y f2 / z f12 (without the block: z f2 / y f12 / x f14). Same for the scale block, which also frees v0
  so the carrier address reuses it. Using DIFFERENT named triples for the two blocks (bx.. for the sub, ax.. for the
  scale) matters; sharing one triple reverses the scale colouring.
- With the frame right, the param stayed in a0 before the first call and in s0 after it with NO separate local copy
  (the 6612C `self = a0; a0 = 0;` trick was unnecessary here and actually spilled `self` to the stack).
Open residuals (~2.7%): `len` colours f0 (target f2); the six sub loads issue pair-wise (target: all pv loads z,y,x then all
qv loads) -- named-load spellings spill one value or change the frame; g[] copy temps f8/f16 swapped; mtc1 one slot early.

Sibling gl_func_000690A8 (same session, NM 63.13 -> 85.28): an m2c graft with three `volatile f32` stack temps re-decoded
as `f32 v[3]` (an array stays memory-resident: the cvt/sw/lw round trips) + two inline column-vector transforms.
`count * sizeof(Vec3s)` keeps the alloc size in shift form (`sll 2; subu; sll 1`) -- a plain `count * 6` CSEs its 6
with the loop's `idx * 6` and turns into `multu`. A loop-1 `for (i = 0; ...)` plus `for (i = 0; ...)` again for loop 2
reproduces the target's `or t0,zero,zero` spilled across both calls with loop 2's offsets initialized as constants.

## 697C4: float-literal preheader hoist, materialised element pointer for `+=`, copy-before-guard amp (gl_func_000697C4 NM 62.85 -> 92.35, 2026-10-14 agent-g) <a name="float-literal-preheader-hoist-elem-ptr-697c4"></a>

- **Float literal vs D-variable.** Target: `lui at,0` sits ABOVE the loop guard (`beqzl v0,...`) and `lwc1 f18,0x2244(at)`
  sits in the guarded preheader, value loop-invariant in f18. Every spelling as a variable -- `*(f32*)(D + 0x2244)`, a
  pad-struct alias `D_x.v`, `extern const`, a plain `extern f32` -- only hoists the ADDRESS (`lui a2; addiu a2`) and
  keeps the `lwc1` inside the loop (stores in the loop may alias). A local `k = ...` before the `for` loads it above the
  guard. A float LITERAL (`w *= 0.01f`) reproduces the shape exactly: the D+0x2244 word is a game_libs `.rodata` literal.
  The NM reloc goes against `.rodata` (bytes differ only in %lo), so this is fine for an NM wrap; an exact would need
  the literal pool placed at that offset.
- **`w *= K` vs `s = w * K`.** A separate `s` lets uopt sink the mul to its first use and costs an extra FP reg (here
  that pushed a value into callee-saved f20 -> sdc1 + frame growth). Overwriting `w` pins the mul up front (`mul.s
  f0,f0,f18` right after the branch), matching the target.
- **Materialised element pointer for read-modify-write.** Target: `addu v0,t3,a1; lh t4,2(v0); addiu v0,v0,2; ... sh
  t9,0(v0)` (the scheduler moved the load above the addiu and folded the 2). `dst[i].y += d`, `dst[i].y = dst[i].y + d`
  and `((s16*)dst)[i*3+1] += d` all fold the offset into BOTH lh and sh. `p = &dst[i].y; *p = *p + d;` (also `p =
  (s16*)&dst[i] + 1; *p += d`) keeps p as a value and gives the target shape.
- **Copy + half before the inner guard.** `lw v1,0x94(s0); beqz v1; or t0,v1,zero` then the `/2` sequence on v1 BEFORE
  `beqz count`: `if (self->f94 != 0) { amp = self->f94; half = self->f94 / 2; for (...) }`. `amp = f; if (amp) { half =
  amp / 2;` sinks half into the loop preheader (after the count guard) and colours amp a3.
- Three separate RNG temps (`r`, `r2`, `r3`) instead of one reused `r` moved amp/half/seed-pointer onto the target's
  t0/t1/a2 (one reused r splits webs differently). Two-word stack iterator: `Nd *it[2]` (array = stays on the stack;
  see #homed-array-vs-struct-scalarize-padarrays-411c / #volatile-iterator-struct-stack-homed-walk-6337C) and the
  walk as `it[1] = head; while ((it[0] = it[1], it[0] ? (it[1] = it[0]->next, it[0]->data) : 0) != 0) call(it[0]->data, ...)`.
- Frame: `s32 pad[2]; f32 v[4];` reproduces 0x48 with v at sp+48 and it at sp+40 (v[3] put v at +52).
- Residual: expression t-reg numbering (t4.. vs t6.. from the first insn), loop-2 r/element colours, the 3x3 row-1
  schedule (where the `m[8]` load and the `v[0]` spill fall), and the list loop's second advance loading it[1] into v0
  instead of t9 (A/B/C/D/E advance spellings, `d` vs no `d`, void call alias: all identical or worse).
- **Same session, gl_func_00065148 99.55 -> EXACT 66/66:** the three row results r0..r2 were named and stored after the
  last row, but the accumulators rotated (build r0 f16 / r1 f18 / r2 f14; target f14/f16/f18). Wrapping ONLY the three
  late stores in `if (1) { ... }` fixed the colouring; wrapping the row defs (or defs + stores) is worse. Try the
  `if (1)` block on the store group first whenever named FP results rotate by one register.

## 2B94: struct assignment through the hoisted call-arg register; IDO's `a + b + c` reassociation; literal and triple spellings (gl_func_00002B94 NM 82.99 -> 99.50, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="struct-assign-through-arg-reg-reassoc-2b94"></a>

- **`addiu a2,sp,168` early, then `lw t2,404(s0); sw t2,0(a2); lw t1,408(s0); sw t1,4(a2); ...`** (t2/t1 alternating)
  before a call that takes `&local` = `local = obj->quad;` (a 16-byte struct ASSIGNMENT, then `f(..., &local, ...)`).
  IDO's block copy addresses the destination through the already-materialized argument register. Four scalar
  stores, a held pointer, or a loop all fold back to `sw N(sp)`; the old wrap called this unreachable.
- **Reassociation:** IDO -O2 rewrote `p->a + p->b + p->c` (left-assoc) as `(c + a) + b`: loads issue c, a, b and
  the first addu pairs c with a. To get the target's `(a + b) + c` with loads a, b, c, write `p->b + p->c + p->a`.
  With a fourth constant term (`+ x` where x folds to -19) the same holds for the first three. Same lever for a
  two-term sum feeding a store: `e[6] + e[0]` gave the target's `addu t3,t1(e0),t2(e6)`.
- **`lui at,0; lwc1 fN,0xCB8(at)`** with consecutive offsets in a game_libs function = `.rodata` float literals
  (here k/255 colour fractions, 0x3F48C8C9 = `0.78431374f`); read them from bootup.uso section 7 at imm + 4
  (see docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#game-libs-rodata-literals-and-tables-76f0).
- A `255.0f * G` multiply where G was spelled `*(f32 *)&D_00000000` came out `mul.s f, G, 255` with G loaded first;
  a separate `extern f32` for G gives the target `255` first. Shared `D_00000000` bases CSE across the function and
  change operand order.
- **Full if/else triples:** target sets `s1 = A; t0 = -19; v0 = 2` before the branch and `s1 = B; t0 = -19; v0 = -16`
  in the taken arm (the -19 repeated). That is `if (c) { s = B; x = -19; y = -16; } else { s = A; x = -19; y = 2; }`;
  defaults-then-override const-propagates the repeated -19 away.
- **FP temps:** named `f12 = p->1E4; f2 = p->1EC; d = (f32)i - (f32)j;` coloured d=f2 / 1EC=f0; reading the fields
  inline in each of the four expressions (and inlining `d`) gave the target d=f0 / 1EC=f2 / f12 / f14.
- **Frame:** in this function unused declarations DO take slots (removing three dead decls shrank the frame by 8),
  so the target map (spB8 184, spA8 168, four ints 152..164, gap 148, x 144, y 140, gap 132..139, f32[4] at 116,
  40 bytes below) is rebuilt with dummy `s32` decls in the gaps plus a 10-word pad array.
**SOLVED -> EXACT 361/361 (agent-g run 60, 2026-10-15).** The reloaded `obj->0x1F0` head value colours a0 when the
SAME variable is re-assigned from memory right before the next call and passed as its first argument
(`h = self->unk1F0; ...head uses of h...; spA8 = self->e[14].q; h = self->unk1F0; f(h, ...)`): the struct copy kills
the load so the reload survives, and the shared variable picks up the call-argument a0 precolour for the head web
too. The pointer/s16 pair then went v1/v0 (target v0/v1); the fix was which DECLARATION carries them: two otherwise-dead
homed decls, the s16 one declared between sp98 and sp90 and the pointer one between sp8C and sp84 (any other
variable - existing live vars, fresh decls, the flag var - gave v1/v0, t-temps, or shifted every t-reg by one).
Lesson: when two short-lived locals colour swapped v0/v1, sweep the (s16-var x pointer-var) grid over the
function's existing dead decls before anything else -- a 20-cell standalone grid found it in one compile round.
Landing: the four `.rodata` literal `%lo` words cannot come from an in-unit compile, so the function is an IDO 7.1
-O2 REPLACE_FUNC_BODY donor (game_libs_o2_2B94.c) with the donor-local `.rodata` reloc renamed `gl_func_00002B94_rodata`
and pinned to 0xCB8 (the 6F684 float-literal recipe; host keeps a placeholder body). game_libs.c's expected/ needs no
refresh (its 2B94 slice is the INCLUDE_ASM words; the four diffs are reloc-offset words).

## 3430: float-literal merging, call-block s-reg promotion, `!=` loop bounds (gl_func_00003430 NM 77.93 -> 95.79, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="literal-merge-call-block-sreg-3430"></a>

- **Identical float literals merge.** The target reloads `step` into caller-saved `$f2` from four separate `.rodata`
  words (0xCC8/0xCEC/0xCF0/0xCF4, all 0x3DCCCCCD) after each call. Writing `step = 0.1f;` at all four sites lets uopt
  see a single constant value: it hoists one `lwc1` before the loop into `$f24` (callee-saved, extra sdc1/ldc1) and drops
  the per-case reloads. Different literal values (`0.2f`) or forms (`1.0f / 10.0f`, `0.1`, `(float)0.1`) stay separate
  but still land in a callee-saved register; separate `extern f32` loads reproduce the target's `$f2` reloads. For an
  NM wrap use the externs; an exact would need the literal pool rebuilt at the right offsets anyway.
- **A variable referenced in a basic block that contains a call is treated as crossing it.** One `s32 t` reused for
  case 7's counter (passed as the call's a2) and for the post-call `x->74 + 16` went to `$s0`, dragging every case's `t`
  with it. A separate variable for the counter (colours a2 via the call-argument precolour) put `t` back in v1.
- **`for (i = 0; i != 8; i++)`** with a 4-byte stride emits the target's `addiu s3,s3,4; li at,32; bne s3,at` (and the
  parallel `addiu s4,s4,4` cursor). `i < 8` emits `slti/bnez`. A second loop with no calls needs its OWN index variable;
  reusing the first loop's `i` keeps the web in s-regs.
- **`lui a1,1; addiu a1,a1,-0x3318`** for an address argument = `(char *)&D_00000000 + 0xCCE8` (the REL addend sits in
  the instruction pair); a dedicated extern symbol leaves `lui 0 / addiu 0`.
- Float `x = x + y` came out with y loaded first; writing `y + x` gave the target's load order (same reversal as the
  integer sums in #struct-assign-through-arg-reg-reassoc-2b94).
- **Load/adjust/store counters: write them ON THE FIELD, no local (run 60: 95.90 -> 97.52; same lever made
  gl_func_00007344 EXACT).** Target `lw v0,0x78(s0); slti at,v0,255; beqz; addiu t1,v0,32; slti at,t1,256; bnez;
  sw t1,0x78(s0)` (adjusted value in a ugen t-temp, copied back with `or aN,t1` when it feeds a call) is
  `if (FW(s0,0x78) < 0xFF) { FW(s0,0x78) += 0x20; if (FW(s0,0x78) >= 0x100) FW(s0,0x78) = 0xFF; }` - uopt forwards
  the stored values. A `t = FW(..); t += 0x20; FW(..) = t;` local is a uopt variable: it colours v1/v0 and every later
  t-temp in the function shifts by one (that was most of this function's residual). Same for `x -= 1; if (x < 0)`
  decrements, table counters `((s32 *)(o + 0x8C))[j] += 1`, and a value both clamped and passed (`f(.., FW(s0,0x98))`
  = the target's `lw a2; addiu t6,a2,-50; sw t6; or a2,t6`). `*p = FW(s0,0x98) + *p` (not `*p + ...`) for the
  target's load order of a `*p += x` through a loaded pointer.
- Remaining 3430 residual = prologue only: the target materializes the hoisted 1.0f/10.625f loop constants inside the
  save sequence and loads `step` last; uopt always places the hoisted constants right after the `step =` load
  (moving the EC store, for-init, named constant locals, decl order: no change).


## Free-slot scan: IV-constant loop bound, inline test + in-if slot assignment, one-expression RMW pointer (gl_func_00003B1C / gl_func_00003C0C EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g run 61) <a name="free-slot-scan-iv-bound-inline-test-3b1c"></a>

Family: `a0` owner with eight slot pointers at +0x2C; scan for the first slot whose 0x94 state is 0,
claim + initialize it, return it. Target head: `li a1,32; move v0,zero; move v1,a0; L: lw a0,44(v1);
addiu v0,v0,4; lw t6,148(a0); bnez t6,next` and, at the found point, `move s0,a0` in a branch delay.
An old wrap (71.4) declared two caps here; both were C shape:

1. **The 32 bound vs a stored 32.** With `do { ... off += 4; } while (off != 32)` the bound shares one
   constant web with `slot->unk9C = 32` (a single `li` reused for the store, bound colours a0).
   `for (i = 0; i != 8; i++)` over a typed `GlSlot *slots[8]` member gives the identical IV-rewritten
   loop (`off += 4; bne off,32`) but the 32 is now a compiler IV constant: its own `li a1,32`, and the
   store gets a fresh `li t8,32`.
2. **Slot in a0 during the scan, s0 after.** `slot = o->slots[i]; if (slot->unk94 == 0)` colours
   `slot` into s0 for the whole loop. `if (o->slots[i]->unk94 == 0) { slot = o->slots[i]; ...`
   keeps the scan load an unnamed CSE temp in a0 and produces the target's `or s0,a0` copy.
3. The seven field stores after the first call schedule like the target in exactly one source order
   (78, A0, 98, B0, 80, 84, A8 for 3B1C); IDO does not keep source order, so permute the block
   (7! is small; a 6-order probe found it).

Same run, sibling 3C0C (donor, because of a 0.1f .rodata literal): the target reloads `entry->slot`
before every store after the first call (write `p->slot->f` each time), and the RMW
`lw t1,20(v0); addiu v0,v0,20; sw t2,0(v0)` comes only from ONE pointer expression
`q = (s32 *)(*(char **)(G + 0x44) + 0x14); *q += a1;`. A named intermediate for the chain
(`g = ...; q = (s32 *)(g + 0x14);`) or `((s32 *)g)[5] += a1` folds the 0x14 into the sw.

| decl list (standalone word diff vs target) | diffs |
|---|---|
| `char *n; char *lst;` | 2 (frame imm) |
| `char pad[16]; char *n; char *lst;` | **0** |
| `volatile int pad[4]; char *n; char *lst;` | 0 |
| `volatile int p1, p2, p3, p4; char *n; char *lst;` | 0 |
| `char *n; char *lst; char pad[16];` / `volatile char pad[16]` / `volatile int pad[4]` after | 2 (elided) |

## Array-typed list iterator, member-assigned by-value key, spelled-twice call args (gl_func_000029F8 bare -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g run 63) <a name="array-iterator-struct-key-29f8"></a>

Target shape: `sw t0,176(sp); beqz t0; sw t0,172(sp); lw t2,4(t0); sw t2,176(sp); lw v0,0(t0)` before the loop, the same advance at the bottom with t3/t4, and `lw t4,172(sp); lw v0,0(t4)` re-reading `cur->data` at the loop top -- an iterator `{cur, next}` that lives in the FRAME.

- **A local `struct {Node *cur, *next;}` is promoted to registers by IDO -O2**, even when every access goes through `GlIter *ip = &it` or a `(void)&it`. Declaring it as an ARRAY `GlNode *it[2]` keeps both words in memory with exactly the target's store-forwarding (within a block) and the loop-top reload (across the back edge).
- The advance must test the NEXT slot after the copy and step through it: `((it[0] = it[1], it[1] != 0) ? (it[1] = it[1]->next, it[0]->data) : 0)`. The semantically identical `it[0] != 0 ? (it[1] = it[0]->next, ...)` matches everywhere except the loop-bottom node register (v1 instead of t3); `(it[0] = it[1]) ? ...` and `!= 0 ?` with mixed slots fall apart (42-54 of 103).
- 4-byte struct passed by value with a frame copy (`lw a1,-0x3334(lui 1); sw a1,212(sp); sw a1,4(sp)`): `key.v = *(s32 *)(D + 0xCCCC); f(x, key);`. Struct-assigning the key (`key = *(Key *)(D + off)`) materializes the address (`addiu t8`) and copies through it; passing `*(Key *)(D + off)` directly drops the frame copy.
- `f(D, X, Y, X, Y, c)` with X/Y variables put X in a3 and copied it to a1; spelling the full sum at both sites (`a + b + x, ..., a + b + x, ...`) lets CSE merge them and the result lands in a1 with `or a3,a1`. The summand order is reversed relative to the load order (`FW(0x74) + FW(0x44) + x` loads 0x44 first).
- Frame/slot positions came from unreferenced `char pad[N]` arrays between the declared locals (see #unreferenced-array-first-decl-frame-pad-33228); char-array sizes round in 8-byte steps, so sweep the pad sizes in a loop rather than by hand.
- `q * scale` and `scale * q` both emitted `mul.s fd, q, scale`; `q * (t = scale)` gives the target's `mul.s fd, scale, q` (#feedback-ido-fp-commutative-operand-order-assignment-lever).


## Nested-`!=` goto ladder emits a SOURCE-ORDER beq chain with bodies in label order (gl_func_00052144 99.40 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="nested-ne-goto-ladder-source-order-chain-52144"></a>

Shape: a float-returning state dispatcher whose target asm is a `beq key,K,arm` chain in a NON-ascending order (0x120, 0x110, 0x308, 0x408, 0x508, 0x608, 0x304), four `li $f0; b epilogue` arms in that same order, then a default call block reached by a `b` after the last test. A plain `switch` emits the same shape but always sorts the compares ascending (0x110 first, 10 word diffs); an `==`-else chain inverts to bne + inline arms; a flat goto ladder keeps the order but IDO folds the last `beq; b def` pair into `bne` + a duplicated arm.

What matches (45/45, first try once the shape was known):

```c
if (state != 0x120) {
    if (state != 0x110) {
        if (state != 0x308 && state != 0x408 && state != 0x508 && state != 0x608) {
            if (state != 0x304) {
                goto def;
            }
            goto half;
        }
        goto one;
    }
    goto two;
}
return 4.0f;
two:  return 2.0f;
one:  return 1.0f;
half: return 0.5f;
def:  call(...); return 0.0f;
```

- Every `!=` test of the nest becomes `beq key,K,<else-target>` in source order; `&&` of `!=` gives one beq per term to the shared arm.
- The arm bodies are laid out in TEXTUAL order. With `return K;` as the else-arms of the nest they come out innermost-first (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0: reversed). Turning every arm into a `goto` and writing the labels after the outermost fall-through puts them in whatever order you write them.
- The innermost `if (... != last) goto def;` plus `goto half;` keeps the `beq last,half` + `b def` pair that the flat goto ladder loses.

Lesson: when a switch's only residual is compare ORDER, the source was not a switch. See also MATCHING_WORKFLOW's dispatcher-form table ("nested-`!=` -> full beq-to-body chain in source order").


## A folded `& 0xFF` before a byte store burns one ugen ring slot with zero instructions (game_libs_func_00042F4C 99.39 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="folded-byte-mask-burns-ring-slot-42f4c"></a>

Shape: a leaf quantiser with six `t = v * 128.0f; *(s8 *)(o + k) = (s8)(s32)(t < 127.0f ? t : 127.0f);` sites. Schedule, FP registers and instruction count were all exact; only the int temp of each `trunc.w.s; mfc1 tN; nop; sb tN` differed: target t8, t1, t4, t7, t0, t3 (one slot skipped before every site), build t7, t9, t1, t3, t5, t7. The old wrap had probed named/block/register temps, ghost `+0`/`|0`/`>>0` ops, `(u8)`, address casts, loops and pointer walks and called it a genuine ring cap.

EXACT: `*(s8 *)(o + k) = (s8)((s32)(t < f127 ? t : f127) & 0xFF);` at every site. The `& 0xFF` is redundant under the byte store, so no `andi` is emitted, but the mask expression is still numbered in the ring before the store's operand. One mask = one skipped slot per site, which also moves the first site from t7 to t8.

Probe results for the same site (ring of the six mfc1s):
- `(s8)(s32)x` -> t7 t9 t1 t3 t5 t7 (stride 2, the cap)
- `(s8)((s32)x & 0xFF)` -> t8 t1 t4 t7 t0 t3 (stride 3, EXACT)
- `(s8)(s16)(s32)x` -> t9 t3 t7 ... (stride 4: each extra narrowing cast burns a slot too)
- `(u8)(s32)x`, `(s32)x | 0`, `(s32)(f32)x` -> unchanged (folded before numbering)
- `(s8)(u32)x` -> a real unsigned-convert sequence (much larger)
- 8-bit bitfield stores -> the ternary is evaluated twice, worse

Rule: when a byte/halfword store's temps sit N ring slots past the natural numbering with no other diff, add N redundant masks or narrowing casts on the stored value (`& 0xFF`, `(s16)`), then count the stride. This is the store-side case of #subsumed-mask-single-ring-slot-burn-2a55c-2a740-cracked-2026-07-03 (subsumed masks on byte-ranged LOADS, 2A55C/2A740/27C48); here the value comes from `trunc.w.s` and the store does the narrowing. Partial transfer: game_libs_func_000430D8 (two-arm trunc->sb quantiser) 45 -> 13 word diffs with `& 0xFF` on the skip-test load plus `& 0xFF` on the first store; the remaining slot sits before the iterator's `cur->next` load and no fold found for it yet.

Reassigning the PARAM in the `||` fallback (`(arg0 != 0) || (arg0 = alloc(0x2FC), arg0 != 0)`) moves `or s0,a0` above `sw ra` like the target (with the separate local it sits in the bnez delay slot); the remaining schedule diff (arg1 reload + `lui a1` below the swc1 run) was statement order: store `+0x1C0 = arg1` BEFORE the four zero-float stores. The same arg0-as-self spelling took the TWO-level twin gl_func_000001CC (83.0 -> EXACT): with a separate `self` local the frame is 0x40 (one more named home) and `or s0,a0` sits in the bnez delay slot; with arg0 reassigned the frame is the target's 0x38, and declaring the sub pointer BEFORE `f32 d255 = 255.0f` moves its spill from +0x30 to +0x34. Comma literals `(0, 250.0f) / (0, 255.0f)` do keep the division at run time at -O2 with no d255 local.

## Runtime `div.s` by a constant without a named divisor: store-forward, then `/=` in place (gl_func_00000400 97.17 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="store-forwarded-float-div-no-divisor-home-0400"></a>

Target: `lui at,0x437f; mtc1 at,$f0` once, then `div.s` of 250/235/100/0 (each `lui/mtc1` immediates) by `$f0`, stored to four consecutive colour fields. The literal `250.0f / 255.0f` is folded by cfe into an `lwc1` from the rodata pool (so are every cast spelling: `(float)250 / 255`, `250.0f / (float)255`, `(float)(250.0/255.0)`). The usual fix (used by gl_func_000001CC) is a named `f32 d255 = 255.0f;` -- uopt const-propagates it but never folds a float divide.

The catch: **every named local gets a stack home, even one that is fully const-propagated and never loaded**. In 1CC that unused home is part of the target frame (0x38 = sub home + d255 home + two CSE call-arg temps). gl_func_00000400 has one more nesting level (sub2), and its target frame is ALSO 0x38 with four slots all used by spills (sub at +0x34, sub2 at +0x30, temps at +0x2C/+0x28) -- no room for a d255 home. Moving d255 into a block scope, `register`, late assignment, or a disjoint-scope block that ends before sub2's does not remove or share the home; a reassigned float PARAM drops the home but is stored to the caller's arg slot at entry (`sw a2,64(sp)`).

Fix: no divisor variable at all. Store the raw colour to the fields, then divide in place:

```c
*(f32 *)(o + 0xC4) = 250.0f;  *(f32 *)(o + 0xC8) = 235.0f;
*(f32 *)(o + 0xCC) = 100.0f;  *(f32 *)(o + 0xD0) = 0.0f;
*(f32 *)(o + 0xC4) /= 255.0f; *(f32 *)(o + 0xC8) /= 255.0f;
*(f32 *)(o + 0xCC) /= 255.0f; *(f32 *)(o + 0xD0) /= 255.0f;
```

cfe sees a memory operand (cannot fold); uopt forwards the stored constants, still emits the runtime `div.s`, and deletes the dead first stores. The interleaved spelling (`= 250.0f; /= 255.0f;` per field) and `D0 = 255.0f; C4 = 250.0f / D0; ...; D0 = 0.0f / D0;` produce the same bytes. Rule of thumb: count the target's frame slots vs your named locals + spill temps; if there is no unused slot, a const divisor in the source was not a named local.


Family sweep (same run): gl_func_00000FD0 (96.75 NM) went EXACT with the 1CC two-level shape verbatim (its frame HAS the unused d255 home), and gl_func_000005EC took the 0400 store-then-`/=` fix verbatim. Still-open siblings to try both spellings on: gl_func_00000A8C (95.9), gl_func_00003138 (96.9), and gl_func_000032B0 -- decide by counting the target frame's unused slots first.

Follow-up (agent-g, same day): gl_func_00000A8C (95.9) and gl_func_00003138 (96.9) both went EXACT with the 1CC "arg0 IS self" shape, NOT the store-then-`/=` fix: A8C's 0x28 frame has exactly one unused slot (sp+0x20, the d255 home; sub spills to sp+0x24), and 3138's named d255 never costs a slot at all (its frame is saves-only). In both, the only residual of the old wraps was a separate `self = arg0` / `obj = a0` local, which schedules `or sN,a0,zero` into the `bnez a0` delay slot instead of hoisting it before `sw ra`. Diagnostic: if the ONLY diff is that one `or sN,a0` sitting in the branch delay slot, delete the self copy and reassign arg0 in the `||` alloc fallback (`if (arg0 != 0 || (arg0 = alloc(N), arg0 != 0))`). gl_func_000032B0 is a separate case: its f4/f6/f8 constants live in the stolen-prologue predecessor game_libs_func_00003298 (cap).

## Commutative FP adds spelled reversed + one fewer named local close a "web-rank swap" (gl_func_0005DBB0 99.01 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="commutative-fp-add-reversed-operands-spill-home-5dbb0"></a>

The NM wrap was 116/141 words with a `while (0) { tr = m11 + m00; }` "colouring lever", and the residual was described as one `add.s` operand pick, an "else-path rowj/rowk web-rank swap" (t1/t2, sll t4/t5, six post-call `addu` pairs) and three cross-call spill homes 4 bytes low -- "rows/cols are provably CSE temps, rank not source-steerable".

All of it was source spelling:
- Every commutative float add was emitted with its operands in the opposite order from the target. Writing the source operands reversed fixed each one: `tr = m[2][2] + (m[1][1] + m[0][0])`, `m[i][i] - (m[k][k] + m[j][j])`, `(m[j][i] + m[i][j]) * t`, `(m[k][i] + m[i][k]) * t`. The `m[k][k] + m[j][j]` swap ALSO fixed the rowj/rowk CSE numbering (sll t4/t5, t1/t2, the lwc1 order and two spill slots), because the CSE row temps are numbered in the order their first use is evaluated. The `while (0)` lever was no longer needed once the operands were in the right order.
- The last 6 words were three spill homes (`sw a3/v0/v1, 0x38/0x3C/0x40` vs target `0x3C/0x40/0x44`) with the frame already exact. A declaration-order sweep found `tr, t, s` moves the homes but grows the frame by 8 (f64 alignment). Dropping the `f32 t` local and reusing `tr` for `0.5 / s` frees one 4-byte home, which puts the spill temps at the target's slots with the 0x60 frame unchanged.

Rule: on an FP routine whose residual is "operand pick" plus a coupled CSE-temp rank swap, swap the operands of each commutative `+`/`*` in the source before anything else (same family as #or-operand-reversal-tring-8468). If only spill homes are off by 4 with the frame exact, look for a named local that can be merged into a dead one; every named local keeps a home even when it lives in a register.

Partial transfer of the same session's ring work: game_libs_func_000430D8 went 13 -> 4 word diffs (standalone) with `(Link_430D8 *)(int)(p)->next` in the first iterator expression (the forwarded-load int cast burns exactly one slot, the slot before `cur->next`) and the first store's `& 0xFF` removed (that mask burns two slots here, not one). Left: the third arm-1 store wants one more slot (t8 -> t9) without moving the following iterator load, and arm 2's `idx * 16` gets t9 where the target has t8. Every `& 0xFF` / narrowing cast on a store in this function moves its register by two, and bitfield/struct/s8/u8 store spellings move it by zero.

## A "two-web colour permutation" across a call = an extra call ARG + a void callee (gl_func_0003FF44 98.29 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="call-arg-precolour-void-alias-3ff44"></a>

Target block: `lw a1,0x10(s0); lw v0,0x10(t7); sw a1,0x28(sp); addiu a0,v0,16; jal; sw v0,0x2C(sp)`, then both reloaded and used (`node->0x14 = n`). The NM had `node` and `n` as locals with `call(n + 0x10)`; build coloured them (v1, a1) against the target's (a1, v0), and a dozen probes (decl order, same-name reuse, nameless spellings, K&R extra param) were logged as an allocator cap.

Two facts in the target asm give the source: `node` is in **a1** at the call, i.e. it is the call's second argument (`call(n + 0x10, node)`; an arg register precolours the web that feeds it), and `n` lives in **v0** across the call, which IDO only does when the jal does not define v0, i.e. the callee returns void. successor follows the test, the conditional branch goes to the C `goto` target and the unconditional `b` to the other one.
`if (sel != 3) goto dflt; goto c3;` gives `beq c3; b dflt` (the 38830 rule applied to a non-terminal chain). That alone left
the c3 beq's delay slot holding an `lw a0,28(sp)` reload; reading arg1 once into a block-scope `int a = ia1;` used by both
the c4 and c3 calls makes the hoisted load common and moves `lui a1` into the delay slot: 0 diffs.

Same function: the first call's `lw a2,40(a0)` (count loaded straight into a2, then `addiu t7,a2,1; sw`) was a third call
arg, `n = p[10]; p[10] = n + 1; cb(a1, a2, n);` -- see [3D8A8](#extra-call-arg-and-test-member-before-naming-3d8a8).

## Entry `sw a1,home; lbu a1,home+3` + a delay-slot spill = a narrow param passed to the first call (gl_func_0002BA38 92.6 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="narrow-param-as-call-arg-entry-lbu-spill-2ba38"></a>

Target (29w, frame 0x20): `sw a1,0x24(sp); lbu a1,0x27(sp)` at entry, `lbu a0,7(a0); jal; sw a1,0x18(sp)`, then

scored 92.6 with frame 0x18: every spelling with a1 unused before the call (ANSI or K&R `unsigned char a1`, `int a1` +
`(unsigned char)` cast, a `b = (u8)a1` local) rematerialises the narrow value from the home (`lbu v0,0x1F(sp)` at the end)
and never gives it its own slot. Passing a1 as the call's SECOND argument narrows it at entry (it is needed in a1 for the
jal), and since it is live across the call it is spilled to a fresh temp slot -- the target. `a1 += 2; return a1;` on the
ANSI `unsigned char` param gives the `addiu a0 / andi v0` tail (K&R `unsigned char a1;` is equally exact).
`scripts/call-shape-scan.py` flags this class as `nm=jal/0 tgt=jal/01`.

## GfxRing DL builder that caches the builder pointer and re-reads it per packet (gui_uso_func_000016A4 / 0000055C 78 -> 98, gui_func_00002DE0 72 -> 77.5; 2026-10-15 agent-g)

Shape: `b = (*(D+0x254))->0x158` is stored to a cache (a module GLOBAL in 16A4 -- gui.uso
TextReloc shows two distinct syms, the D+0x254 import and the cache -- or a struct field
`a0->0x24` in 055C), then every packet re-reads the cache ONCE (`lw v0,0(t0)` / `lw v0,0x24(a0)`)
and uses that value for both GfxRing derefs, while packet 1 runs on the just-loaded value in the
expression temp t7 (no reload). Levers:
- Global cache: `b = G = expr;` (assignment chain) keeps packet 1 on t7 and IDO holds `&G` in a
  temp across the function by itself -- no `char * volatile *` hack and no `char **dp` local
  (a dp local makes the held address a colouring candidate and scores worse). A decode that
  invented three extra "c1/c2/c3" globals for the re-reads was simply wrong (only one reloc).
- Field cache: the chain gives v0 for packet 1 here; write `a0->c = expr; b = a0->c;` instead --
  IDO forwards the store and packet 1 lands on t7.
- Register rotation: the target rotates ONE per-packet local across a1/a2/a3 (16A4: slot ptr)
  while the other stays fixed (i in a0). Whichever local you declare in a per-packet `{ }`
  block gets the rotation; the function-scope one stays fixed. Putting `slot` (the target's
  rotator) in the block makes the held address/ugen temps shift instead, so the best scores came
  from block-scoping `i`: 16A4 14 words off (98.6), 055C 28 off (98.3). Not cracked: getting
  slot to rotate with i fixed AND the held &G in t0.
- FP: `x / 2` with an INT literal keeps one held `2.0f` ($f16, lui 0x4000) feeding every div.s;
  a `two = 2.0f` local is const-propagated into the FIRST use as `mul.s` by 0.5f (lui 0x3f00),
  and `/ 2.0f` is mul by 0.5f everywhere (2DE0 +2.9).
GOTCHA hit during this work: `objdump expected/` vs `build/src/<unit>.c.o` for an NM-wrapped
function compares INCLUDE_ASM against itself (false "exact"). Diff `build/non_matching/...`.
Fast scorer: `objdiff-cli diff -1 expected/src/<u>.c.o -2 <candidate.o> -o - <func>` and read
`right.symbols[name==func].match_percent` (~20 ms, same number report.json uses).

## Hand-decoded "clamp ladder" display-list code is often a stock gbi.h macro: re-decode with the macro text (gui_func_0000329C 74.1 -> 85.3, 2026-10-15 agent-g)

Signs: the packet words are `0xE4......` (G_TEXRECT), then `0xB4000000` and `0xB3000000`
(RDPHALF_1/2), each guarded by `(s16)(v<<2) > 0 ? .. : 0` clamps; the X-side guard tests
`(s16)xl < 0` but the Y-side tests the RAW `yl < 0`; the B4 word is `(-a << 16) | (-b & 0xFFFF)`;
the dsdx/dtdy divide shows up inside both arms of the B4 if/else. That is
`gSPScisTextureRectangle(pkt, xl, yl, xh, yh, tile, s, t, dsdx, dtdy)` from gbi.h (copy it from
`references/oot/include/ultra64/gbi.h` or papermario's `PR/gbi.h`), with s = t = 0. Its asymmetric
`((yl) < 0)` is the "raw Y guard" that hand decodes had to special-case. Passing dsdx as an inline
expression (not a local set beforehand) gives the divide in both B4 arms: uopt's PRE moves the
B3-word use into the arm that skips it. `pkt` is evaluated once per packet, so a GfxRing bump
written as a `{ ... }` block per packet matches. `0xBB000001, 0x80008000` before it is gSPTexture.
In 329C this rewrite took the hand-written 14-local version from 74.1 to 85.3 with the same op
multiset. Frame: named locals keep decl-order homes (see
`#feedback-ido-frame-slot-home-assignment-rule`). The target's w@0x3C / h@0x38 meant six named
decls before them. Still open in 329C and 2DE0: the target keeps the ring ctx, switch value and
x-side MAX temps in callee-saved s0. Named-variable and statement-order spellings did not reproduce it.
Same rewrite on the f32-scale sibling gui_func_00002DE0 (x = x0 + (-(w/2))*sx, fw = w*sx): 77.5 -> 80.7.
On gui_func_00000F04 (the per-glyph string version) it gave only +1.5 (82.2 -> 83.6, not committed).
There the old decode was already close, and the leftover is colouring: the ring ctx and the x-side
MAX temps share one register in all four targets (s0 in 329C/2DE0, a1 in 3714, a3 in F04).
For 3714 the macro form scored lower than the old decode (80.8 vs 83.0).

## Rematerialized pointer local keeps an `addiu v0,a0,K` base; bitfield sets show as temp-name skips (gl_func_00028E94 93.1 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="remat-base-local-and-bitfield-temp-skips-28e94"></a>

Target (78w, frame 0x38): after the second jal it re-derives `addiu v0,a0,48` and stores `sb t8,3(v0)` / `sb t2,5(v0)`;
earlier it keeps `addiu v1,a0,176` in v1 (spilled at sp+0x1C across the second jal). The wrap computed `v0 = obj + 0x30`
right before the stores: uopt folds that into `sb ..,51(a0)` / `53(a0)` no matter the spelling (int-cast, `register`,
bitfield struct type, even `return v0`). Moving `b30 = obj + 0x30; xf = obj + 0xB0;` to the TOP of the function (above the
first call, b30 also used for the first `obj+0x30` store) makes the value live across the calls; uopt rematerializes it
from the reloaded a0 at its next use instead of spilling, and the rematerialized copy is a real base register. Same for xf
(the `addiu v1,a0,176` right after the first call's reloads).

Temp numbering: target `lbu t0,0(a1)` ... `ori t3,t0,1; sb; ori t4,t3,8; sb` against the wrap's `lbu t9; ori t1; ori t2`
-- one name skipped before the load and two between load and first ori. Spelling the two `|=` as 1-bit bitfield sets
(`d->active = 1; d->ready = 1;` in a big-endian `{x0:4, ready:1, x1:2, active:1, ...}` struct) emits the same
lbu/ori/sb but consumes the extra temp names; the whole function's temp naming then lined up. `(word << 13) < 0` on the
byte whose bit 0x04 was just set/cleared = one 1-bit bitfield read; `(b & ~0xE0) | ((v & 3) << 5)` = a 3-bit bitfield store.

Also: the scanner's `nm=jal/01 tgt=jal/012` at site 1 was the resolved sub-id passed as a 3rd arg (`3CF18(obj, d, id)`,
same callee/args as sibling gl_func_000289B0). The final +0x10 frame with v1 at 0x1C came from 12 bytes of unused local
(`char pad[12]`; three unused ints are equivalent; named copies of the sub-record pointer perturbed colouring instead).

## `px = x; px += mem;` puts the variable first in addu when `x + mem` will not (gui_func_00000D04 95.7 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g)

The last diff in D04 was `addu a1,s3,t9` (target, s3 = the x accumulator, t9 = a freshly loaded

(`tbl[k] + x`), adding parentheses, or moving the offset gave the same order. uopt canonicalises
the commutative add of a variable and a load. The same function's `x += tbl[k]` already emitted
`addu s3,s3,t6` with the variable first. Copying into a fresh local and then using `+=`
(`px = x; px += tbl[k]; f(..., px, ...)`) reproduces that and lands in a1 with no extra move.
`x - -tbl[k]` adds a negu (+1 insn). Other D04 levers, all from the old residual list:
- `lbu v0` + `move a0,v0` in the delay slot vs target `lbu a0; beql a0,at`: test the raw
  `*p != ' '` and call `f(*p)`. A named `c = *p` local is what puts the char in v0
  (compare `#extra-call-arg-and-test-member-before-naming-3d8a8`).
- Stack-arg schedule (`lw t0,0(v1); lw t1,4(v1)` together, then `sw t0,16; sw t1,20` before the jal):
  read glyph[0]/[1] into named locals next to the already-named glyph[2].
- A `0xBB000001/0x80008000` pair whose lui/ori/lw order is off: one source line
  (`#feedback-one-line-stores-fix-schedule-order`). `if ((unsigned)(i = 0) < f(a3))` moves the
  `move s8,zero` after the a3 arg copy.

## Param reassigned from a call result: one s-reg holds a0 then v0 (gl_func_000290C8 90.5 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="param-reassigned-from-call-result-290c8"></a>

Target (62w, frame 0x38): `or s0,a0` at entry, `addiu a0,s0,48` for the second lookup, then `or s0,v0` unconditionally in the
following `beqz v0` delay slot; `a0 + 0x20` lives in a stack slot (stored in the first jal's delay slot) for a later call. The
wrap used a separate `s0 = a0` local reassigned only under `if (v0)`, so IDO kept the original a0 in a2 and spilled it to its
home slot (+8 frame, an extra `or a2,a0`). call-shape-scan read that a2 as a third call arg at both sites (`nm=jal/012
tgt=jal/01`); it was the spilled a0 copy, not an argument. The fix is `a0 = lookup(a0 + 0x30, k);`, reassigning the param
itself, with `p20` holding `a0 + 0x20` for the later call. Slot and schedule details: `char *v1; int pad;` declared first puts
the v1 spill at sp+0x34 and makes the frame 0x38. Writing `p20 = a0 + 0x20` inside the first call's argument list, with the
key read into a block-scope `int k` just before, moves `or s0,a0; addiu a0,a0,32` after the `sw t7/t6` constant stores and
puts `sw a0,36(sp)` in the jal delay slot. Assigning `p20` at the top, or as its own statement, hoists the addiu above the
prologue stores.

Rule: when a target holds a param in an s-reg and later overwrites that same s-reg with a call result (no copy, no spill),
assign the result to the param.

## A beql into the middle of a case arm means the labels share the arm (gl_func_0002F934 84.5 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="beql-into-arm-shared-case-labels-2f934"></a>

Target dispatch: `beqz a0,c0; li at,1; beq a0,at,c1 (delay: move a1,zero); li at,2; beql a0,at,c1+4 (delay: lui a0,0x600);
b end`. The c1 arm starts `lui a0,0x600; jal; ori a0,a0,0x700`. The beql jumps to c1's `jal`, one word in, because the
delay slot already did the `lui`. The `move a1,zero` in the case-1 test's delay slot runs for mode 2 as well. So modes 1
and 2 run the same three calls. The old wrap read the arm after the beql as a separate `case 2:` with one call (the last
one); the code after the beql target only looked like a separate block because c1's second call immediately follows it.
`case 1: case 2:` over one body is 40/40.

Rule: when a beql target is not the start of a block in the arm layout, and the delay slot holds a copy of the
instruction just before the target, the branch enters that arm. The case label belongs to that arm.



## `volatile` param vs `&param` escape; dead-looking copy pairs = an extra call arg (gui 3B80 91.0 -> 96.2, 27A0 92.5 -> 96.5 NM; tail D288 probe, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="volatile-param-and-cse-arg-copies-3b80"></a>

Three source facts found with `scripts/call-shape-scan.py` on gui_uso (the scanner runs as-is on `gui_uso/gui_uso`):

1. **Memory-resident param without homing the tail params.** 3B80 keeps its x cursor `a1` in its home
   slot (`lw t1,124(sp); addu; sw t1,124(sp)` per iteration, `lw a1,124(sp)` at each call). The old wrap got
   that with a dead `if (0) { f(&a1); }` escape, but the escape also stored a3 to its home (`sw a3,140`)
   and pushed the cursor (reassigned a3) into a0. Declaring the parameter `volatile int a1` gives the same
   load/add/store shape, no `sw a3`, and frees the a-reg the cursor wanted (+4pp with the other fixes).
   Use it when the target homes exactly one param and reloads it around every use.
2. **Frame size from declaration order (no pad).** 3B80 was +8 (128 vs 120) with no visible extra slot.
   IDO gives every declared local a frame word top-down in declaration order, and keeps the frame down to
   the lowest slot used (see `#loop-promoted-constant-web-absorbs-outside-mul-258c0`). The target has the
   uninitialised-junk read at frame-4 (116) and the `frow` spill at 92, so exactly five plain locals must be
   declared between them; moving two declarations after `frow` gave 120 with no codegen change. The same
   move fixed 2BB0's frame (120 -> 112, `field58` sixth) but did not move its score.
3. **`move aN,aT` + `move v0,aT` after one load = the loaded value is also a call argument.** 27A0 loads
   `info = a0[4]` into a3, then copies it to v0 (used later as `info`) and to a1 (overwritten on the other
   path, so it looks dead). The a1 copy feeds the next jal: `a1 = a0[4]; tile = f(budget / h, a1);` makes the
   load a CSE temp copied to both the named var and the arg register, reproducing both copies. Passing a named
   pointer local instead puts that local in an s-reg (IDO allocates the whole variable once any use reaches
   the jal's block). In 27A0 the temp then took t0 instead of a3, which shifted the t-registers and cost 1pp
   by objdiff, so the wrap keeps the old form. The source shape is still the right one.
4. **A register still holding a pre-store pointer at a jal is the 3rd argument.** tail D288 holds
   `parent = self->0x44` in a2 from the first load to the jal, while arg 2 is computed from a
   reload of `self->0x44` (after the `parent->0x4C = next` store, which may alias). `f(child, *(char **)self[0x44/4] + 0xB4, parent)`
   with `parent` a named local declared after `child`, which keeps child's spill at 0x1C, cuts the residual from 12 words to 4. What
   remains is child coloured a3 throughout, where the target uses v1 before the call and reloads into a3 after it. Copies, `&saved`
   and dropping `o` do not split the web. Not committed, since only an EXACT would clear the +3pp bar.

Also from 3B80 and 27A0: when the target re-loads a loop-invariant field in the loop-test branch delay
slot (`lw s2,4(s5)` under `beqz`), write the re-read at the loop top (`s2 = a0[1];`). Holding it in one variable
had coloured width into s7 and shifted four other s-webs. When a last-iteration arm ends in `subu s0,s0,s1`
shared with the main arm, look for a `tile = s0;` (`or s1,s0`) at the top of that arm.

   load or the index, duplicated table reads, `switch`, separate `t = v & 3`, u16 return / u16 `v1`.
3. Baked `lui 0; lbu -176(v0)` with no expected reloc: `(D_2A014_table - 0xB0)[a1]` against the existing

## K&R u16 param narrowed in place only under `if (!a3)` (gl_func_0001EE78 83.5 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="knr-u16-not-test-inplace-narrow-1ee78"></a>

Target head: `sw a3,44(sp); andi a3,a3,0xffff; ... bnez a3`, later a use-site `andi t5,a3,0xffff`
in the emit arm, temp ring starting at t7. Old wrap (`if (a3 == 0)`) narrowed into v1 and lost the
v1 cursor of the second Gfx pair to it (83.5).

1. **Test spelling picks the narrowing register.** With a K&R `u16 a3`: `if (!a3)` -> in place in a3
   with the home store (what the target shows). `a3 == 0`, `a3 <= 0`, `a3 < 1`, `(int)a3`,
   `(unsigned short)a3`, `(a3 & 0xFFFF) == 0` -> `andi v1/t0,a3,0xffff` and the test branches on that
   temp. `if (a3)` with the arms swapped (or `a3 != 0`) also narrows in place, but lays the arms out
   wrong. ANSI `unsigned short a3` behaves the same as K&R here. `int a3; a3 &= 0xFFFF;` narrows in
   place but never stores the home.
2. **Use-site re-mask:** write the later use as `(a3 & 0xFFFF)`. A bare `a3` gives `or t7,t6,a3`.
3. **Ring at t7:** `(arg4 & 0xFFFF)` on the u16 stack arg (`lhu t7,50(sp)`) folds but burns t6
   (#subsumed-mask-single-ring-slot-burn-2a55c-2a740-cracked-2026-07-03).
4. **Scheduling:** type the cursor as an 8-byte `{int w0, w1;}` pair. Call arm
   `gl_ref_00031BC8(dl++, 0x3C0)` puts the `addiu s0,s0,8` in the jal delay. A `char *` with
   `q = dl; dl += 8;` puts it before the jal. The emit arm needs two DISTINCT cursors (`p = dl++` /
   `r = dl++`; reusing `p` loses v1). Put each pair's three statements on ONE line. Split across
   lines, the scheduler swaps the pair-1 `sw w1`/`sw w0` order and moves the pair-2 `or v1,s0` and
   final `addiu s0` (same-line class).

scores the renamed jal reloc at 99.56. The report and the raw `.text` slice are both exact.

The 3-arg call (`parent` as a3rd arg) is at 98.69 by diff. None of these split the web: a re-read `c2 =
parent->4C` before the unlink store (child goes v1, but c2 gets its own home slot, the a0 copy is hoisted
