The old wraps wrote `((p[4] & 0x100) == 0 || (p[4] & 0x200) != 0) && v[0x938/4]` and got a direct `beqz t6` on the andi, one cached load, and a cap label ("beql-chain scheduling"). Two independent C facts give the target shape:

1. `((p[4] & 0x100) != 0) == 0` -- the double comparison survives as `sltu` + `beqzl` on the 0/1 value (the `!` / `== 0` spellings fold to a branch on the andi result).
2. The second test reads the flag through a different type, `((unsigned int *)p)[4] & 0x200`; the type split defeats uopt's load CSE so the target's reload appears (same mechanism as #type-split-cse-and-dead-bump-6cf0).

Colouring: target p sits in an arg register (a0 after a call in F060, a1 in F13C). Assigning p into a dead param (`a0 = (int *)v[0x800/4];` in F060; an unused second param `int *a1` in F13C) gives exactly that register (the 7ACC dead-param lever). Remaining 3-word residual in both: `v` colours v0 where the target has v1; under NCC an edg-inlined member function with `this = v` produces v1 because the inline's return temp holds v0 (cfe has no equivalent found yet).

## A local shared by several switch cases rotates arg-register colours; split the case's own use (gl_func_0002FB74 97.0 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="per-case-local-split-rotation-2fb74"></a>

Target (post, 0x990, two jumptables, no s-regs): v (param a1) copied to a3, the ladder counter c in a2 (init in the
prologue delay), a level local in v1. The 97.0 wrap had v a2 / c v1 / level a3, everywhere. `call-shape-scan.py --spill`
flagged the c spill at a 2-arg call (a2 saved, unset), but c is a known 0 on that path, so passing it as a third arg
emitted `or a2,zero,zero`; passing it at a later call made c a2 and pushed v to its stack home. Neither was the fix.

The fix was a web split: the wrap used one `b` for four unrelated case-local values (case 2's 0/1 bank, case 36's
gate word and toggle, case 39's level, case 512's 0/1). Giving case 39 its own local restored all three colours
(diff 244 -> 136 lines, standalone). Then, one at a time:

| change | diff lines |
|---|---|
| `case 258: case 2:` share one arm (beql into the arm with `c = 28` in the delay; #beql-into-arm-shared-case-labels-2f934) | 130 |
| case 39's `n = gN` read into the `cmd` web (v0) after `b3 = 0;`; level steps `b3++; ... b3++;` (gives `or v1,t1` then `addiu v1,t1,1`, i.e. a copy of the constant-1 register plus 1, not a folded 2) | 154 (temps renumber until the next row) |
| case 34: `gH = 0; if (gG != 4)` inline. A named `n = gG;` before the store was a global web in v0; the target loads into t6 | 52 |
| case 36 toggle through `b` (`b = tgl; sel = b + 186; b ^= 1; tglw = b;`) | 48 |
| the `(0x1010300, 0)` call is `addiu a1,zero,0` = 0.0f to the `(int, float)` blank alias | 46 |
| case 17: `p = &chan;` moved INSIDE the `gD == 0` arm. One level up, IDO folded the address into `lbu a0,3(a0)`. Inside, it stays `lui v0; addiu v0,v0,0` (scheduled above the `bnez`, which loses its likely form), as the target has | 38 = relocs only |

Declaration order changed nothing here, and variable names do not matter (IDO renames by web). When several webs
rotate together, look for a local that the wrap reuses across unrelated cases before adding call arguments. The
`--spill` hit was real (c is spilled there), but it was not an extra argument.

Landing: 29CCC / 31334 donor recipe, two tables at `_rodata` +0 / +0x54 under one pin (0x1750); baked counter /
toggle words at 0x1C908 / 0x1C90C as per-site pinned names; baked jals 0x423A4 / 0x44B70 as `gl_ref_` pins.


**Opposite direction, same lever: reuse one local across disjoint live ranges (gl_func_0005B3E0, post0b, 77.7 -> EXACT
87/87, 2026-10-15 agent-c).** Heap free + coalesce. With fresh locals per job, the second merge's prev pointer took v0
(target v1) and the b spill sat at 24(sp) (target 28). Two reuses fixed both: the loop cursor `p` also holds the
next-block pointer of the first merge (one variable, many refs, so it is coloured first and gets v0), and the header
word `h` (u32) also holds the prev pointer of the second merge (`h = (u32) b->prev;`, so it gets v1). Dropping the extra
local moved the spill slot to 28. Giving the u32 header and the prev pointer one variable put both ranges in the same
register (v0 when that variable outranked n, v1 once n was folded into p), so here IDO coloured per variable, not per
web. The call-shape-scan `SPILL #0 a0` hit was the heap param's home store, and the first call is `(heap, blk)`.
`h + 1 + size` (not `size + h + 1` or `h + size + 1`) gave the target's `addu t3,v1,t2` operand order.

## game_libs is C++ too: gl_func_00062A2C EXACT under NCC, and the Vec3 class recipe (agent-g 2026-10-21, run 113) <a name="ncc-game-libs-vec3-62a2c"></a>

The game_uso NCC route (MATCHING_WORKFLOW #game-uso-ncc-cplusplus-donor-recipe) also applies to
game_libs_post0b. gl_func_00062A2C (camera/transform blend, 209 words, cfe capped at 210/209
words with FP colouring residuals) is byte-exact from src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_62A2C.cpp,
spliced over a placeholder with REPLACE_FUNC_BODY.

**Tells that a function is C++:**
- A Vec3 copied `addiu vN,sp,K; lw/sw x3 into (vN)` and then `lwc1/swc1` per field from the stack
  temp into the destination. That is an inline `operator=(V3 v)` with a BY-VALUE argument (the temp
  is the parameter), whose body stores the floats member by member.
- `lw v1,0x54(o); lw v0,0x28(v1); lw t9,0x54(v0); lh t1,0x50(v0); jalr t9; addu a0,t1,v1`: a virtual
  call with the cfront `{s16 delta; s16 index; fnptr}` vtable entry, vptr at +0x28
  (`struct L { char pad[0x28]; virtual ...; }`).

**The V3 recipe that matched (every item moved frame slots or registers):**
```cpp
inline float flerp(float a, const float &b, float t) { return (b - a) * t + a; }
struct V3 { float x, y, z;
    void set(const V3 &v) { x = v.x; y = v.y; z = v.z; }
    void operator=(V3 v) { set(v); }
    void lerp(const V3 &b, float t) { x = flerp(x, b.x, t); y = flerp(y, b.y, t); z = flerp(z, b.z, t); } };
```
- Writing the lerp per component directly (`x = (b.x - x) * t + x`) lets uopt hoist all three
  `a` loads (f0/f2/f12 live together). The inline scalar `flerp` keeps the components sequential:
  `a` in $f0, `t` in $f2, `b` in the ugen FP ring, which is the target's shape.
- The set() forwarder adds two inline locals per copy: the temps land 32 bytes apart
  (sp+100/68/36), which pins the frame (216).
- A member whose temp is lowest in the frame (declared after its inline locals) is a different
  class: `V3c &operator=(const V3c &v) { set(v); return *this; }` with `set(V3c v)` by value.
- `o->dst = o->cur;` as a plain record assignment: the implicit `Rec::operator=` calls the member
  operators. The getter's 24-byte output object (only its first V3 used) fills a 12-byte hole.

**edg frame/temp facts (all measured with `-Wo,-zdbug:1` isvar lists):**
- Every inline call's parameters and `this` are named frame locals (vregs). They take slots even
  when they are register-coloured. edg reuses an inline temp across statements in some cases
  (62A2C: one temp for all three copies of `o->dst = o->cur`).
- A temporary bound to a `const V3 &` parameter (`(a + b) / 2.0f` with `operator/(const V3 &, float)`)
  is a function-scope temp at the TOP of the frame. Each statement gets its own, and the LAST
  created is the highest. In gl_func_0005062C the target has the opposite order, which is still unsolved.
- `volatile` on a parameter has no effect under NCC (the param was still cached in an s-reg).
  Unreferenced locals (even with a declaration) are dropped and take no slot.
- `switch` is lowered by edg to a compare chain in SOURCE order ending `beq <last>; <delay from
  default>; b default; nop`, which is the shape cfe cannot produce (it sorts the case values,
  and a goto ladder gives `bne default; b last`). The switch expression gets a temp with a frame home.
- `V3(float, float, float)` constructor temporaries (`return V3(a.x + b.x, ...)`) colour their float
  arguments as FP candidates (f12/f0/f2) before the stores. Plain `V3 r; r.x = ...` does not.

**In progress:** gl_func_0005062C is now 4 words from exact, see #ncc-5062c-subdivider-run114;
src/game_libs/ncc_drafts/gl_func_000578B4.cpp (95.0), see #ncc-578b4-texture-loader. Other C++ candidates
by tell (scan for the stack-temp copy / lh+jalr): timproc_uso_b5 8FC8/4118/5BF0/5FC0/D14C,
gl_func_000076F0 (16 virtual calls), gl_func_00065494, titproc 116C.

## game_libs under NCC: gl_func_0005062C to 4 words, and edg stack-pool facts (agent-g 2026-10-21, run 114) <a name="ncc-5062c-subdivider-run114"></a>

src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_5062C.cpp (spliced into the NON_MATCHING object only, see
MATCHING_WORKFLOW #game-libs-ncc-nm-only-donor-run114) is instruction-identical to the target once
stack offsets are masked. The run-113 draft was 93.3. These changes got it there, in order of effect:

- **The V3 constructor forwards to an inline `set(float, float, float)`** (`V3(float a, float b, float c)
  { set(a, b, c); }`). Assigning the members in the ctor body gives a different FP colouring for every
  `operator+` / `operator/` temporary. With `set`, the target's x f12 / y f0 / z f2 (sums) and the
  matching divide order come out (93.8 -> 99.3 in one step). Try this first on any NCC function whose
  V3 temporaries have the right instructions but permuted FP registers.
- **Named sum locals with the implicit `operator=`**: `m01.assign((s1 = v0 + v1) / 2.0f);` with
  `V3 s1, ..., s6;` declared FIRST. Their slots (580, 568, ... 520) are the top-of-frame copies that the
  run-113 draft got in the opposite order from `const V3 &` binding temps. Same rule as
  #ncc-temp-order-named-assign-6fa8: named locals follow declaration order, binding temps never do.
- **abs as a macro**, `#define fab(f) ((f) < 0.0f ? -(f) : (f))`. An inline `float fab(float)` puts the
  result in f2 (target f12) and adds two pool slots above the first return slot. `float`, `const float &`
  and template versions all behave like the inline. Wrapping the macro in `inline float fid(float)` or
  using an inline `fneg()` for the minus is neutral.
- **`V3 &assign(V3 v) { set(v); return *this; }`** (reference return) instead of `void`: adds the two
  pool slots below the divide temporary (D1 -> A gap 3 -> 5).
- Declaring `float ax, ay, az;` before `int h0..h5` puts their three unused slots between n2 and h0.
- The dead `if (0) esc(&scale, ...)` address escape is not needed any more. uopt keeps the int params
  in their arg homes with this shape on its own.

**Residual (4 words):** the first statement's operator+ ctor temporary is at sp+340, target sp+336.
Pool-slot pattern from the top, as `slots (N free) ...`: ours `R1 (1) P1 (5) R2 (1) D1 (5) A`, target
`R1 (2) P1 (4) R2 (1) D1 (5) A` (R = inline return slot, P/D = operator+/operator/ ctor temps, A = assign's
by-value param). One pool slot is allocated before P1 in the target and after it here. These were all
neutral: operator+ as member / friend / static / 3-arg / by-pointer, operator/ as member, declaration
order of members and operators (240 permutations), body prefixes in operator+ (`(void)0;`, `if (0) {}`,
comma), a default 4th ctor argument, call-site spellings (`operator/(...)`, casts, extra parentheses,
braces), if-condition spellings. A named local inside operator+ moves the slot after P1 (wrong way).
Deriving V3 from a POD base `P3` and taking `operator/(const P3 &)` produces exactly the target pattern
for the operator+ part (`R1 (2) P1 (4)`) but drops the slot between R2 and D1 and 8 frame bytes. Making the
sums `P3` locals gives the full target pattern but changes the code (720 words). So the answer probably
involves a base class or conversion somewhere; not found yet.

**How to study edg's frame layout (tools in this run):**
- Mask stack offsets when scoring a variant (a cmpfn-style compare that rewrites `N(sp)` and
  `addiu rX,sp,N` to a placeholder). If the masked compare is exact, only the layout is left and every
  other variant can be ranked by slot pattern alone.
- Print the frame as used-slot blocks with free-slot counts between them (from all `N(sp)` and
  `addiu rX,sp,N` operands, an addiu base counting as 12 bytes) and compare against the target's.
- `-O2 -g3` gives the same code as `-O2` (two prologue insns swap) and its `.mdebug` names the named
  locals and the `__V<id>` class temporaries with their virtual-FP offsets. Inline return slots and
  scalar pool slots have no symbol. A 40-line ECOFF parser over the HDRR / SYMR tables is enough (local
  symbols are 12-byte `{iss, value, st:6 sc:5 .. index:20}` records; offsets are file-absolute).
- **The layout of a single statement can be reproduced in a 15-line micro file** (same classes, one
  statement, `use(&m)` afterwards). The micro file gave the same pattern as the full function, so
  each hypothesis costs about a second. The pool slots above the first return slot are present even for a
  zero-argument inline (`add()`), so they are not that call's parameters.
- -O0 shows the cfront constructor protocol for every stack object (`addiu s0,sp,K; bnez s0` then
  `alloc(12)`), with inline `this`/reference params in s0..s7 in pool order, so it shows which slot is
  which kind. It does not show what the slots are used for at -O2.

**Side probe, gui_func_00000148 (99.98, the glyph-grid "find-or-create" constructor):** it is a cfront
constructor. `GuiGlyphGrid148::GuiGlyphGrid148(char *, int, int, int, int)` with a class-scope
`operator new(unsigned n) { return gl_func_00000000(n); }`, called as `new`, compiles under NCC to the same 255
instructions, `if (this == 0) this = alloc(40)` protocol included. Using `this` directly and dropping `line` gives the
target's 128-byte frame. Seven spill homes stay 4 bytes low (68/72 -> 64/68) and one named home is off. 400 random
declaration orders reach at most 246/255. That is the same residual the cfe wrap documents, so NCC alone does not
solve it. Not wired.

## gl_func_000578B4 is the gbi texture loader (agent-g 2026-10-21, run 113) <a name="ncc-578b4-texture-loader"></a>

The 12-pass m2c transcription of this 9676-byte function was hiding a libultra texture loader:
```
gDPSetTextureLUT(G_TT_NONE); cms/cmt from flags 0x100/0x200/0x400 and 0x1000/0x2000/0x4000;
masks/maskt = log2 helper(tex->w / tex->h);
if (flags & 0x10) switch (fmt) {  /* sub-image: gDPLoadTextureTile, SetTileSize(0, 0, lrs-uls, lrt-ult) */
    RGBA32 0x120, RGBA16 0x110, IA8 0x408, I8 0x308, I4 0x304 (_4b), CI8 0x508 (gDPLoadTLUT_pal256 +
    gDPSetTextureLUT(G_TT_RGBA16) first); default: error(str); }
else switch (fmt) { gDPLoadMultiBlock(_4b)(timg, tmem, tex->rtile, ..., tex->shifts, tex->shiftt);
    CI8 reads the UNINITIALISED sub pointer (original bug) and falls through to default: error(str, fmt); }
```
- One frame slot per gbi command (`Gfx *_g` block local), so an arm is 7 slots (0x1C).
- The display-list pointer increments `count` before reloading `ctx->dl->buf`, so there is a sequence point
  between them. In C++ it is `Gfx *next() { return &dl->buf[dl->count++]; }`. In cfe, the only working form is
  the two-variable comma macro `(d = c->dl, n = d->count, d->count = n + 1, &c->dl->buf[n])`
  (game_libs_func_0005769C matches with it). A one-variable `(n = c->dl->count++, &c->dl->buf[n])`
  makes `n` a whole-function live range that takes $a2.
- Under cfe one of masks/maskt/cms/cmt always takes $ra. Under NCC with the goto ladder they stay in memory
  like the target. With a real `switch` (target-exact chain), cmt goes back into $ra. That is the open item.

## game_uso under NCC: inlined member returning a child pointer = the target's v1 colouring (F060 / F13C -> EXACT), and other edg facts from B274 / 7448 (2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="ncc-inline-member-child-v1-f060"></a>

**F060 and F13C (99.64 / 99.57 under cfe -> EXACT under NCC).** Both
open with the same block: `v = self->0xB4; p = v->0x800; if ((!(p->0x10 & 0x100)
|| (p->0x10 & 0x200)) && v->0x938) ...`. The target keeps `v` in **v1**. Written
inline, `v` colours v0 under both cfe and NCC (the cfe residual of
[#materialized-bool-flag-test-sltu-beqzl-f060](#materialized-bool-flag-test-sltu-beqzl-f060)).
The original C++ read the child through an inline member:

```cpp
struct V { int *child() { return AT(int *, this, 0x800); } };
...
a0 = AT(V *, s0, 0xB4)->child();
if ((((a0[4] & 0x100) != 0) == 0 || (((unsigned *)a0)[4] & 0x200))
    && I(AT(V *, s0, 0xB4), 0x938) != 0) { F360(s0); return; }
```

edg's inline return temp takes v0, so the 0xB4 pointer goes to v1. Both
functions matched on the first NCC compile with the same lines, and all relocs
match. The PMF arguments are passed as `AT(PM, &sym, off)` by value (10694
recipe). Landed as `.cpp` donors:
[MATCHING_WORKFLOW #game-uso-ncc-cplusplus-donor-recipe](MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#game-uso-ncc-cplusplus-donor-recipe).
**Lesson:** in game_uso, a v0-vs-v1 (or a-reg) colouring residual on a pointer
that is dereferenced once is worth re-trying with that dereference moved into an
inline member.

**How edg (NCC) treats addresses, found on B274 (cap ~88.5, same as cfe):**
- `(char *)(unsigned)&sym`, the cfe lever that keeps an address in an s-reg,
  is a no-op under edg: the cast disappears and every use rematerializes
  `lui/addiu`. `int s1 = (int)&sym;` (an integer-typed local, cast back at each
  use) does keep it in s1. The same goes for `(char *)(int)`, `(long long)`, a
  reference, `register`, and an inline `gp()`: all of them fold.
- `char *d = &sym + 0xA0;` followed by `d->0x30` folds to `sym+0xD0`. The
  target's `lui v0,%hi(sym+0xA0); addiu v0,v0,%lo(sym+0xA0); swc1 0x30(v0)`
  comes from `int d = (int)&sym + 0xA0;`. An inline member on the sub-object
  and a do-while(0) both still fold.
- The C++ virtual call `(*(V **)(s0 + 0xC4))->m2()`, with
  `struct V { char pad[40]; virtual void m0(); virtual void m1(); virtual void m2(); }`,
  emits the target's `lw v0,40(v1); lw t9,28(v0); lh t5,24(v0); jalr t9; addu a0,t5,v1`
  exactly. B274's remaining gap is the frame (80 vs 64; the 16 bytes come
  from the double CSE in the `*= 1.0 - (x - K) / K2` block) and prologue
  scheduling. NCC did not move the score.

**Inline accessors and base+K folding, found on 7448 (98.06 cfe -> 98.89 NCC, 29/36 words, length-exact, not landed):**
- Natural C++ (`P &PP(b,o)`, with `struct P { char pad[0x10]; float v; float get(); float &r(); void set(float); }`)
  reproduces 7448's whole `addiu rB,table,K` + `0x10(rB)` structure without
  any of the cfe `if (1) { t += K; }` anti-fold hacks. The condition is that
  the `this` must be a **load expression** (`PP(TAB(a0), 0x758).get()` with
  `TAB(a) = *(char **)(a + 0x30)`). A named-local `this` (`char *t = TAB(a0)`)
  folds to full offsets, which is the same rule as FD04 under cfe.
- An inline `get()` returns through an f0 temp. An inline `float &r()`, used
  as an rvalue or as an lvalue (`PP(..).r() = x * y`), keeps the value in the
  expression ring (f4/f6/f8/f10/f16/f18), as the target does. A `set(x)`
  `this` colours v0, while a `r() = ...` `this` colours a1.
- The residual is 7 words of register choice: the target colours the hoisted
  `a0+0x35C` base a3, block-3 base a1 and the final 4C8/498 bases a2/a1, and
  NCC gives a2/v0/v0/a1. The variants tried are r/get/set/copy/mul members in
  each statement (about 50 combinations).


## game_uso under NCC: reassign the float param in place; a class temporary whose ctor forwards to an inline set() (B750 72.8 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="ncc-ctor-forwarding-inline-set-frame-b750"></a>

game_uso_func_0000B750 (0x134) has a C++ virtual call at the end (`lw v0,40(s0); lw t9,28(v0); lh t1,24(v0); jalr t9; addu a0,t1,s0`
= `((V *)s0)->m2()` with three virtuals, as on B274). Three facts took it from 72.8 (cfe) to byte-identical under NCC:

1. **The scale factor is the parameter itself.** Target: `lwc1 f16,104(sp)` inside the `flags & 4` arm (for `arg4 * 400`) and again in the
   delay slot of the `flags & 8` test, then `mtc1 1.0,f16` on the other path. Writing `k = (flags & 8) ? arg4 : 1.0f` or
   `k = arg4; if (!(flags & 8)) k = 1.0f;` loads arg4 into a temp for the multiply and gives k another register. `if (!(flags & 8)) arg4 = 1.0f;`
   (then `* arg4` everywhere) re-loads the stack param from its home into its own register on each path, which is the target pattern, and
   removes one local slot.
2. **edg gives locals and inline-argument temps stack slots.** Under NCC every named local adds 4 bytes to the frame even when it
   lives in a register (two unused locals made the frame 8 bigger), and inlined calls' argument temps take slots below the
   locals. The target had frame 88 with the temporary at sp+64 and only two locals above it (f0, v). Dropping the `flags` and `dst` locals
   (`AT(int, a0, 0x1C)` re-read each time; `AT(float, (int)&sym + 0xA0, 0x30)` inline, which still emits `lui/addiu sym+0xA0`) fixed the
   locals area. The frame below the temporary then depends on how many inline params are live together.
3. **The 4-float temporary is `Q q(x, y, z, x10 * k)` where Q's constructor forwards to an inline `set()`:**
   ```cpp
   struct Q { float x, y, z, w;
       void set(float a, float b, float c, float d) { x = a; y = b; z = c; w = d; }
       Q(float a, float b, float c, float d) { set(a, b, c, d); } };
   ```
   The nested inline gives frame 88 / q at 64 and colours the values like the target: x f0, y f2, z f12, w f14 (the 0x10 load stays an
   expression temp in f4). Results of the other shapes:

| temporary shape | frame / &q | FP colours (y, z, w) | diff lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float buf[4]` + stores | 80, s-reg promotion of a0 | -- | 111 |
| `Q(a,b,c,d)` direct ctor | 80 / 56 | f12 f14 f16 | 70 |
| `Q(a,b,c,d,e)`, w = d * e in ctor | 88 / 64 | f12 f14, product in f4 | 64 |
| derived `Q : B3(a,b,c)` | 80 / 56 | (adds instructions) | 121 |
| ctor forwarding to inline `set(a,b,c,d)` | 88 / 64 | f2 f12 f14 | 0 (labels only) |

A ctor parameter that is a constant or unused (default `= 0` / `= 1.0f`) is folded away and does not add a slot.
**Lesson:** if an NCC candidate in game_uso has the right instructions but the frame is 8 or 16 too small and the stack object
sits lower than in the target, add inline nesting (ctor -> set) or remove named locals before you touch the expressions.

## Int-returning blank callee blocks a v0 colour across the call; use a void alias (gl_func_00037BEC 67.5 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="void-alias-frees-v0-across-call-37bec"></a>
Target (construct-and-enlist helper): `lw v0,16(t7); addiu a0,v0,16; jal 0; sw v0,28(sp); lw a1,24(sp); lw v0,28(sp)`. The
local `lst` is spilled around the third call and comes back in **v0**. The build put it in v1 every time.
- Cause: the callee was the shared `extern int gl_func_00000000();`. A call to an int-returning function DEFINES $v0, so
  uopt treats v0 as clobbered at that call even when the result is thrown away. A web that lives across the call cannot
  take v0. Declaring the callee `void` (a new blank alias, `extern void gl_func_00000000_37bec(void *, void *);`, pinned to

  Check which blank the call goes through before blaming the allocator.

  stored v0 into n (`or a1,v0,zero`). The target reloads (`lw a1,16(a2)`). Writing `lst = ...;` BEFORE `n = p->10;`
  gives the reload with no other change. (`volatile` on the 0xC store also gives the reload, but it is not needed.)
  Things that did NOT stop the forward: `if (1) {}` around the read or the store, int/char* type split, struct-typed
  field, array-index spelling, a merged local carrying the call2 result.

  and the &D base took a3 (target v1); calling the cb through the existing void blank `gl_func_00000000_void` fixed both.

## A spilled local stored to its home a second time = BB boundary before the later call (gl_func_0003E868 61.3 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="bb-break-respill-3e868"></a>

  not the cb's return. Read the reloads (`lw v1,60(sp)` from the slot written in the jal delay) before trusting a sketch.
- Frame layout came from unreferenced arrays in declaration order: `char *obj; char pad1[4]; int stk[2]; char pad2[0x14];` put obj
  at 0x3C, a dead word at 0x38, stk at 0x30 (see #unreferenced-array-first-decl-frame-pad-33228).

## game_uso under NCC: 1DDC homing as a Vec3 class -- all 382 instructions identical, only the frame layout left (2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="ncc-vec3-class-shape-1ddc"></a>

game_uso_func_00001DDC (cfe NM wrap 99.46, 1528 B) is C++ written against a small value class. Under NCC
the body below reproduces every one of the 382 instructions, all registers included (mnemonic diff
382/382). 241/382 raw words are exact; every remaining difference is a stack offset. The frame is 360,

`scratchpad .../agent-g79/best_1DDC.cpp` (copy it into the donor `.cpp` before continuing).

Shape facts, each confirmed by a probe that flipped the asm:

- **The `Tri3i` word-copy hops are edg temporaries.** `Vec3 operator*(float s) const { return Vec3(x*s, y*s, z*s); }`
  makes `r` (the inline's object) -> return temp (word copy) -> the next temp (word copy). That is the cfe
  wrap's `st_* / hopA / hopB` chain.
- **`operator=` takes its argument BY VALUE**: `Vec3 &operator=(Vec3 v) { x = v.x; y = v.y; z = v.z; return *this; }`.
  The by-value parameter comes from the same pool as the second return temp. That is why the target's
  single-op `acc = ...` copies through sp+196, the slot the two-op branch uses for its second return. With
  `const Vec3 &` every assignment gets a fresh binding temp. `+=` / `-=` stay `const Vec3 &` (fresh
  binding temps at the top of the block: the 023D4 result copy and the final subtract source).
- **Plain-member copies use a separate `set(const Vec3 &)`**: key 3's two stores and `ref` are float
  copies with no temp. Writing them with the by-value `operator=` adds a word copy.
- **Constructor forwards to `set(a, b, c)`** (as in B750). This gives the scale stages' FP colouring
  (x f12, y f2, z f14) and moved the mnemonic diff from 227 to 375.
- **`Vec3 diff(self.x - ref.x, 0.0f, self.z - ref.z);`** constructed in place. The arguments become uopt
  variables (f0 / f14 zero / f16), so the squares use registers. Member stores reload them.
- **`a0->0x14` is a 4-byte class with a constructor** (`struct Ptr { Body *p; Ptr(Body *b) { p = b; } Body *operator->() const { return p; } };`).
  `Ptr out(a0->body);` gives the memory-resident output pointer (`sw t6,368(sp)` right after the load,
  then reloaded after the float stores). A plain pointer stays in a register, and a struct copy-init goes
  through `addiu tN,sp,K`. The 072EE8 argument must be `out->c30` (through `operator->`). That holds v0,
  so the shared temp base is v1, as in the target. `(char *)out.p + 0x30` gives `lw a0; addiu a0,a0,48`.
- **Matrix translation through an inline that returns `Vec3 &`**:
  `Vec3 &Mtx::getPos(Vec3 &v) const { v.x = m[3][0]; v.y = m[3][1]; v.z = m[3][2]; return v; }` called as

- **Block structure and declaration order set the frame.** Sibling blocks never overlay. Inside a block,
  the first-declared local is highest, and nested-block locals sit below the parent's. Fresh binding temps
  come first, in REVERSE order of appearance. The target puts key 3's locals at the top, so the body is
  `if (key == 0) return; if (key == 3) { Vec3 m; Ptr out(..); ... } else { Vec3 ref; Vec3 self; Ptr out(..); Vec3 acc; ... }`
  with no named `key` (a named `key` takes the -4 slot). Use `-g3` and parse `.mdebug` local symbols to
  read edg's slot assignment by name (the frame layout is the same as at -g0). Unused named locals get no slot.

**Residual (frame only):** (1) the two top-of-block binding temps are swapped: the target has the 023D4
copy at -44 and the subtract source at -56, but "later appearance = higher" gives the opposite. (2) The
first (horizontal) pass needs 8 more bytes of compiler temps in three places: before the short branch's

The vertical pass needs none, because it reuses the pool. Probes that did not supply them: friend /

Next step: find the edg construct that adds two 4-byte temps per horizontal-pass scale stage.

**Same residual in game_uso_func_00006FA8 (cfe 76.5).** With the 1DDC class (`operator-` by value,

## game_uso under NCC: the "bnez on a stack address + alloc(0xC)" block is edg's derived-class constructor protocol; Vec3 value class (6A30 93.2 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-g) <a name="ncc-derived-ctor-protocol-6a30"></a>

game_uso_func_00006A30 (cfe 93.2) matched 176/176 under NCC with the Vec3 class from
[#ncc-vec3-class-shape-1ddc](#ncc-vec3-class-shape-1ddc). The class has by-value `operator*`, the
constructor forwards to `set`, and `+=` takes `const Vec3 &`. Facts:

- **The alloc-fallback block on a local is a constructor.** Tell: `addiu a3,sp,K; or v1,a3; bnez a3,L; ...
  jal alloc(12); beqz v0,skip; or v1,v0; L: stores through v1`. The cfe wrap faked it with
  `dst = &pt; if (dst == 0) dst = alloc(0xC)`. It is edg 2.19's cfront-style protocol
  (`if (this == 0) this = operator new(sizeof)`), and edg emits it for a **derived** class constructor:
  `struct XZ : Vec3 { XZ(const Vec3 &v) : Vec3(v.x, 0.0f, v.z) {} };` then `XZ pt(s0->w->at);`.
  The stores go through `this` (v1) only with the base initialiser. A body-assigned derived
  constructor (`{ x = v.x; z = v.z; y = 0.0f; }`) keeps the call but stores straight to &pt. Plain
  (non-derived) Vec3 temporaries in 1DDC have no check at all.
- **Reloc name of the allocation.** The protocol calls global `operator new` (`__nw__FUi`). The USO imports
  it as `game_uso_func_055750`. Give the base class an inline
  `void *operator new(unsigned n) { return game_uso_func_055750(n); }` (with
  `extern "C" void *game_uso_func_055750(unsigned);`). The bytes stay the same, and the jal reloc then names
  the import the expected object uses. A class-specific `operator new` on the derived class itself is
  ignored by the protocol.
- **No named copy of a reloaded pointer, so PRE shapes the join.** The target loads `self->0x30` in each
  branch of an if/else and the shared tail uses it. Write `s0->w->...` everywhere with no named `w`.
  uopt's partial-redundancy elimination places the load in each arm. A function-scope `W *w` assigned in
  both arms adds an `or v0,v1` copy. The `0x6F8` accessor has to be called on the load expression
  (`s0->w->lim.getMax()`) to keep the unfolded `addiu v0,v1,0x6F8; lwc1 16(v0)`.
- **Frame slack is bought with named locals in the tail.** Every used named local gets a slot even when
  it lives in a register, and nested-block locals sit below everything else. The frame was 176 (target
  184) until each timer arm declared `W *w = s0->w;` (two slots, no code change). A named int in the
  else arm also reaches 184 but colours v0.
- Declaration order `va, r1, v94, rv, pt, yaw` (r1 before v94, although v94 is written first) gives the
  homes. Read them by name from `-g3` `.mdebug` local symbols.
- **Sibling game_uso_func_000071E0 (cfe 83.6) -> EXACT, same classes.** Three new facts:
  (1) A counter written through an **inline member taking the incremented value** (`s0->tick(s0->f54 + 1)`,
  with `tick(int c) { f54 = c; if (c >= 30) { f64 = 0; f54 = 0; } }`) colours the value a1, as the target
  has it. A named `int c` gets v0, and `++s0->f54 >= 30` gets a1 but loses the slots. (2) The inline call's
  argument temps are function-level allocations. They take the two TOP frame slots, and a later inline
  parameter of the same type (the XZ constructor's `const Vec3 &`) reuses the top one as its spill home
  (target `sw a1,168(sp)` in a 176 frame). So the stage after `if (state != 3) return;` has to be a nested
  `{ }` block, or its binding temp takes the top. (3) **Nested-block named locals go after every temp of
  the parent.** `{ float k = 6.0f; float fr = -yaw * k; s0->f3C = fr; }` adds the 8 missing bytes at the
  bottom with no code change. The same `fr` without the braces lands among the named homes and shifts every

## Goto-chain dispatch order + one-line store pair for the as1 schedule (gl_func_00035440 71.2 -> EXACT, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440"></a>

Target (post0b, 0x160, frame 0x70): dispatch on `o->4` comparing 1, then 0, then 2, with the three bodies
out of line after a `b end`, in the order 1, 0, 2.

1. **Not a switch.** A `switch` with cases written 1, 0, 2 emits the compares ascending (0, 1, 2) and gives
   the selector a hidden frame slot at the bottom of the frame (frame grew 0x70 -> 0x78 at the target's
   local total). A goto chain `if (k == 1) goto L1; if (k == 0) goto L0; if (k != 2) goto end; goto L2;`
   gives the target order. The last test needs the inverted skip + goto, or it folds into `bne` with the
   body inline (#feedback-ido-split-last-eq-test-to-suppress-bnel).
2. **Frame.** With the named `k` declared right after `r`, the slots are r 0x6C (also r's cross-call spill
   home), k 0x68, then the case block's 44-byte message struct, buf[24], tmp. Without `k`, or with a switch,
   a compiler slot appears and the frame is 8 bytes too big.
3. **One-line store pair.** In the block after `cb(buf, &tmp, 1)`, the target loads the global counter
   first (`lui t4; lw t4`) and then reloads a1 from its home (`lw t3,116(sp)`), stores the counter, and puts
   the a1 store in the jal delay slot. t3 < t4 means `s.a1 = a1` comes BEFORE `s.cfg = G` in the source
   (registers follow statement order; all 120 orders of the five stores were tried). On separate lines
   as1 issues the a1 reload between the lui and the lw, and the counter store goes in the delay slot.
   `s.a1 = a1; s.cfg = G;` on one line gives the target schedule, all else unchanged. A standalone
   reduction showed the same flip from the line break alone. Same lever as the as1 tie-break entry for
   func_00005F34 (search "COLLAPSING statements onto a SINGLE source line"); here the tell was "registers
   right, schedule of a load pair swapped". The permuter (158k iterations) did not find it.

## game_uso under NCC: C48C is a cfront out-of-line constructor; D9CC's NCC residual (2026-10-15 agent-g, both still NON_MATCHING) <a name="game-uso-c48c-cfront-ctor-d9cc-ncc"></a>

**C48C (0xD78, cfe 99.74).** The cfe wrap emulates each of the 32 stages with a manual
`obj = s1 + K; if (s1 == -K) obj = alloc(0x18)`. That shape is what edg (IDO 7.1 NCC, cfront ABI) emits
for an *inlined constructor of a member subobject*: `if (this == 0) this = T::operator new(sizeof(T))`
with `this = &list->m_k`. The likely original is `Obj::Obj(int a1, int a2) : Super(a1) { b4 = a2; D458(this); }`
with a `List` member at +0x13C (its own `this == 0 -> alloc(0x308)`), whose base `Hdr` (8 bytes,
`alloc(8)`) and 32 members (`FParam`/`IParam`, 0x18 each) are built in List's mem-initializer list.
What reproduces under NCC (scratch probes, standalone compile):
- A class-scope `static void *operator new(unsigned n) { return game_uso_func_055750(n); }` in each class
  gives the `jal 055750` with the member size. Do not put it in an empty base: edg gives an empty base
  4 bytes (no EBO), so every size and offset grows by 4.
- The per-stage `lw G; sw G,slot; lw 0(&slot); sw 0(s2)` then `lw a2,0(s2)` is the by-value `Name`
  argument: a temporary built by `Name(int)` from the global, copied into the INLINE ctor's by-value
  parameter. That parameter has one shared slot (s2) for every expansion. A named `t = u` local
  (cfe-style) puts t at the top of the frame, not at sp+44.
- Floats that IDO loads from .rodata (`lui at; lwc1 0x1EC(at)`, named game_uso_D_807FF820 in the
  expected relocs) cannot be literals in a donor, because the reloc would point into the donor's
  .rodata. A `const float &` ctor parameter bound to the existing alias extern keeps the load late,
  inside the `if`. Literal floats/ints substituted into the inline stay late on their own.
Still open: (1) `Obj::Obj` is a mangled symbol (`__ct__3ObjFiT1`). REPLACE_FUNC_BODY matches by name,
so it would need a donor-side `objcopy --redefine-sym` (or a donor-symbol option in the splice
script), and Super's out-of-line ctor would need the same rename to `import_0010D33C`. An inline
Super adds its own `this == 0` alloc(0x2C). (2) Frame 208 vs 200: the temps go ascending from sp+72
with the shared param slot at 52, where the target has temps descending from 192 and the param at 44.
The extern "C" free-function emulation (stage inlines) reached 779/862 words with only the sp offsets
wrong.

orders mul.s operands the other way from cfe). The three volatile-load compares written
`FF(arg0, 0x304) * vol` (the volatile still has to stay). The (f) "andi/or coalesced into a1" cap:
drop both named temps and write `if (FW(arg0,0x108) != 0) { FW(arg0,0x108) = (FW(arg0,0x108) & 0xFFFF) | 0x60000; call(arg0, FW(arg0,0x108), ..); }`

## Param split into a caller-saved copy + spills to its own home; FP colour order from a pointer copy; the unstolen range-check delay slot (gl_func_000396FC 59.2 -> NM 98.7, 2026-10-15 agent-c) <a name="param-split-spill-home-396fc"></a>

(UOPT REGALLOC rule 5: split when `adjsave * span <= best`, where `best` for a fresh callee-saved reg includes
`firstUseCost` = movcost * BBs / 4). Two ways to tip it, both verified: remove one post-call use of the param
(scoring tool only), or add basic blocks: `gl_func(a1, b); if (1) {} gl_func(a0 + 0x30, b);` in the three
call-pair cases split `self` exactly as the target. With none it colours s0 again; one `if (1) {}` after the
call in case 114 did not split it; dropping one of the three still splits in the final body.

(even 10 dense cases) to a `li at,K; beq` chain. A function with a `sltiu/jr` jumptable is therefore cfe C.

local): the rot and scale groups load all their shorts before any store, so the products are named locals

chain per element with nops. The target colours products f0/f2/f12/f18 and the constants k2 f14 / k1 f16; the
build gave k2 f12 / k1 f14 / third product f16. No renaming of x/y/z/w (all 576 group permutations) moved it.
The permuter found the lever: a pointer copy `s2 = s;` after the rot products, with the pos and scale reads
going through `s2`. It reorders the FP colouring AND adds the target's two extra spill words below the
locals (the call-spilled `self + 0x30` moved from 24(sp) to 32(sp), frame unchanged once two pads went).
1/32767 is a literal of this function (rodata right after the jumptable, +0x18); 0.01f at +0x1A10 belongs to

## Run-time float constant products = per-statement float locals (gl_func_00042778 15.7 -> NM 77.0, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="runtime-float-const-products-42778"></a>

Target: `lui at,0x4200; mtc1 at,f0; lui at,0x4000; mtc1 at,f2; mul.s f4,f0,f2; mul.s f6,f0,f2; trunc.w.s` x2 for
`a0[0] = a0[1] = (int)(32 * 2)`, and `32 * 4 + dot * 32 * 2` with every constant materialised and multiplied in
each of two statements. Literal spellings fold in cfe (`32.0f * 4.0f` -> 128.0 `lui 0x4300`; `x * 2.0f` -> `add.s
x,x`). Float locals `w = 32.0f; four = 4.0f; two = 2.0f;` keep the multiplies (uopt propagates the constants but
does not fold FP), but one set of assignments is CSE'd across the statements (one product computed once and
spilled to the frame). Re-assigning the locals before the second statement (`w = 32.0f; two = 2.0f;`) gives
each statement its own products: the else arm became word-exact. Still open in the main arm: the target computes
`32 * 4` before the dot product, and the second statement's `* two` still became `add.s` + spill.


## Vec3 squared length into a float callee: named x/y/z temps fix FP load colours and add order (gl_func_0005BD80 77.2 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="vec3-sqlen-named-temps-5bd80"></a>

Target (16 words): `lwc1 f0,0(a0); lwc1 f2,4(a0); lwc1 f14,8(a0); mul f4=f0*f0; nop; mul f6=f2*f2; add f8=f4+f6; mul f10=f14*f14; jal; add.s f12,f8,f10`.
The old NM used the K&R `gl_func_00000000(...)` blank, which promotes to double (cvt.d.s + a0/a1 move) -- swap to a prototyped `extern float gl_func_00000000_5bd80(float);` pinned at 0 in undefined_syms_auto.txt.
With that, `return f(a0[0]*a0[0] + a0[1]*a0[1] + a0[2]*a0[2]);` still misses: loads come out f2/f14/f0 and the final add is `add.s f12,f10,f8`. Writing `float x = a0[0], y = a0[1], z = a0[2]; return f(x*x + y*y + z*z);` gives the target colours and operand order word for word. (Reassociating as `z*z + (x*x+y*y)` swaps the add operands back -- wrong.) Try named load temps first on any small FP-expression leaf whose loads are coloured in the wrong order.
Same lever, 4-arg variant (gl_func_0005DB58 NM 71.8 -> EXACT, same day): the "K&R float call to gl_func_00000000 is unmatchable" cap is NOT a cap once the callee goes through prototyped per-site blank aliases pinned at 0 -- a `(float)->float` alias keeps the direct `jal` with f12/f0, and a `void (int, int, float, int)` alias makes O32 pass the float in a2 via `mfc1 a2,f0`. Any older NM comment citing #feedback-ido-knr-float-call as the gate should be re-tried with typed aliases.
Third member (game_libs_func_0005DB00 NM 49.4 -> EXACT): a leading `mtc1 a2,$f14` is just a plain `float` third parameter after two ints (O32 gives it the a2 slot) -- no `*(float*)&a2` bit-cast. A `(int, int, float, float)` alias passes a spilled float result via `lw a2,slot(sp)` and a live one via `mfc1 a3,$f0`; the spill slot follows decl order (`float r1, r2, q;` -> r1 at sp+0x24).

<a id="mtx-vec3-inline-cse-reversed-rows-5c8cc"></a>
### Matrix x Vec3 in place: inline CSE input reads + reversed row spelling + store order (game_libs_func_0005C8CC, EXACT)

Target (31 words, leaf): `lwc1 f2,0(a0); lwc1 f4,0(a1); lwc1 f12,4(a0); ... mul.s f6,f4,f2 ... add.s f0,f4,f6 ...`
with the three input components in f2/f12/f14, the row-0 sum in **f0**, rows 1/2 in f16/f18, and
`swc1 f0,0(a0); swc1 f16,4(a0)` late in the block. Long documented as "~34%, FP-reg-allocation cap,
permuter does not converge". Three independent levers, found by standalone probing:

1. **No named x/y/z.** `float x = v[0], y = v[1], z = v[2];` colours the inputs f0/f2/f12 and pushes the
   row-0 sum to f14. Reading `v[0]`, `v[1]`, `v[2]` inline in every row (stores go to named a/b/c so
   CSE keeps the three loads) gives exactly f2/f12/f14 + f0 for the sum. This is the OPPOSITE of
   [5BD80](#vec3-sqlen-named-temps-5bd80), where named temps were the fix -- probe both spellings.
2. **Rows spelled reversed:** `a = m[2]*v[2] + (m[1]*v[1] + v[0]*m[0]);`. The forward spelling
   `m[0]*v[0] + m[1]*v[1] + m[2]*v[2]` emits both add.s with swapped fs/ft (IDO emits `a + b` as
   `add.s d,b,a` here, cf. [5DBB0](#commutative-fp-add-reversed-operands-spill-home-5dbb0)); the
   x-term needs the vector written FIRST (`v[0]*m[0]`) to get `mul.s f6,f4(m),f2(v)`, while the y/z
   terms want `m[k]*v[k]`.
3. **Store order is TU-context dependent:** in a standalone one-function compile, source
   `v[0]=a; v[1]=b; v[2]=c;` schedules `swc1 v[1]` before `swc1 v[0]` and only `v[2],v[1],v[0]` /
   `v[1],v[0],v[2]` match -- but in-tree (post0b) the natural `v[0],v[1],v[2]` (also `0,2,1` and
   `2,0,1`) is the one that matches and the standalone winner is 2 words off. The as1 store
   schedule of independent swc1s is not stable across TUs: settle store order IN-TREE
   (cf. [standalone false cap](MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md)). Declaration order of a/b/c and x/y/z had no effect.

## game_uso under NCC: edg temp order -- binding temps are always "first-evaluated lowest"; first-appearing-higher = named locals assigned in-expression via the implicit operator=; `Vec3 &set()` adds frame (2026-10-16 agent-g) <a name="ncc-temp-order-named-assign-6fa8"></a>

Follow-up to [#ncc-vec3-class-shape-1ddc](#ncc-vec3-class-shape-1ddc), where 1DDC and 6FA8 both had
all instructions right but "two top-of-block temps in swapped order" plus missing frame bytes.

**Rule (standalone probes, `-g3` .mdebug + the `addiu rN,sp,K` slot sequence).** edg puts a block's
fresh binding temps first, declared in REVERSE creation order, so the temp that is evaluated FIRST
always sits LOWEST. None of these changed that: swapped `<` / `>` operands (they swap evaluation
too), `!(x >= y)`, `?:`, `&&` chains, an inline `lt(float, float)`, an inline taking both `const Vec3 &`,
a member `lt(const Vec3 &)`, member / friend `operator<`, an extra full-expression earlier in the block
(edg does NOT reuse binding temps across statements in one block), nested `{}` around the compare,
friend / out-of-class / `const`-returning / named-return `operator-`, `const Vec3 &` reference
binding, a user copy constructor (it elides the copies: wrong code) or destructor (wrong code).
A temp bound inside an inline function body (`dsq(Vec3 v)` by value) moves to that inline's nested
block, which is laid out at the BOTTOM of the frame.

**What gives "first-appearing higher": named locals.** Named locals follow declaration order
(first declared = highest) and sit after the block's temps. Initialising them in separate statements
(`Vec3 da = ...; Vec3 db = ...;`) breaks the code: the inline return temp is then shared between the
two statements (one IDO return slot, copy base a1). Assigning them INSIDE the one full-expression keeps
both return slots: `Vec3 d, e; if ((d = a->pos - s0->w->pos).lenSq() < (e = b->pos - s0->w->pos).lenSq())`.
This needs the IMPLICIT (trivial) `operator=`: edg then copies the return slot straight into d
(r -> ret -> d, the target's two word-copy hops). A user `operator=(Vec3)` adds a by-value
parameter hop, and `operator=(const Vec3 &)` adds a binding temp. 6FA8: mnemonics 127/127,
d and e in target order.

**`Vec3 &set(float, float, float)` (returning `*this`) instead of `void set`** adds 8 bytes of
compiler slots per class-temp stage, with no code change. It moved 6FA8's frame from 184 to 192 and
put r1 / ret1 / ret2 at the target offsets (123/127 words). It moved 1DDC's frame from 360 to 376
(241 -> 249/382 words). `Vec3 *` / `int` returns do nothing. `const Vec3 &` does the same as `Vec3 &`.
Inline ctor shape matters too: a body that assigns the members directly (no `set`) adds 4 more bytes
per stage but changes FP colouring.

**Residuals (not landed):**
- 6FA8: **SOLVED, EXACT (2026-10-16 agent-g, `src/game_uso/game_uso_ncc_6FA8.cpp`).** The
  `Vec3 &set()` trick was the wrong lever here. Its return temp lives in the ctor inline's nested
  block, and nested inline blocks are laid out at the BOTTOM of the frame. That is the 4-byte slot that
  ended up below r2 (r2 at 56 vs 52). Fix: `void set`, then add the 8 bytes between the stages
  instead. A named local inside the FIRST stage's inline only (`Vec3 to(const Vec3 &v) const
  { const Vec3 &u = *this; return Vec3(u.x - v.x, ...); }`, used as `(d = a->pos.to(w))`) lands
  between ret2 and r1. The same local in BOTH stages adds 8 at the bottom instead (wrong). The
  second stage's inline shape does not matter: a 6x6 grid of stage-1 x stage-2 bodies showed the
  layout depends only on stage 1. The named 4-byte slot above d is `Vec3 &w = s0->w->pos;`,
  used by the first subtraction only (an unused `Obj *c;` gets no slot, and float named locals get
  none either). **General tool:** to move 4/8 bytes of edg temps between stages, put a named local in
  one stage's inline body, and keep inline-ctor return temps (`Vec3 &set`) out when they would land at
  the bottom.
- 1DDC (`/home/danjs/decomp-drafts/best_1DDC_r80.cpp`, mn 382/382, frame 376 vs 384): the top-of-block
  pair is the 023D4 binding temp and the final `a0->vel -= diff * sel` source. **Swap fixed:** declare a
  named `Vec3 t2;` FIRST in the else block and write `a0->vel -= (t2 = diff * sel);` with the implicit
  `operator=`. The by-value hop that `acc` and `vel` need moves to a named member
  `Vec3 &assign(Vec3 v)` (`acc.assign(diff * ...)`, `a0->vel.assign(diff * speed)`). Code stays identical,
  the 023D4 temp is at -44, and t2 is at -56, as in the target. Keeping the by-value `operator=` for t2
  costs the pool hop (mn 380). Removing it for everything breaks `acc` (mn 339). Still open: 8 bytes.
  Every slot from 0xB8 down to the pool sits 8 bytes too high in absolute terms (172/184/156/104/92/68/80/56
  against target 164/176/148/96/84/60/72/48). `diff.set(0,1,0)`, `Vec3 diff; diff.set(...)`, `ref = vA0`
  and `Vec3 diff = Vec3(...)` did not fix it.

**game_uso_func_0000591C (spine, 1093 words) under NCC (first port, 2026-10-16 agent-g; draft
`/home/danjs/decomp-drafts/best_591C_r80.cpp`, mnemonics 1056/1093, frame 496 vs 464).** The head is
6A30's (`Vec3 va = s0->w->pos; va += s0->w->vel * k;`, the same r / ret 348 / bind slots). The four
"alloc-fallback" sites per chain are the XZ derived-ctor protocol: `XZ pa(helper->pos);` and a two-argument
`XZ(const Vec3 &a, const Vec3 &b) : Vec3(a.x - b.x, 0.0f, a.z - b.z)` returned by value through an
inline `flat()` (diff -> ret 348 -> named delta). Transform dispatch: the target copies the
hidden-pointer return slot (348) into a PER-CASE temp (276 / 264), then into the shared by-value
`operator=` parameter (252), then field by field into `tr`. That extra hop is
`tr = (const Vec3 &)game_uso_func_00007C1C(...);` (a plain `tr = f()` skips it; `Vec3 r = f(); tr = r;`
also gives the hop, with a different layout). The first nine function-level homes match the target

between tr and ow gives ow -72 / hit -76 / pt -88. Still open: a 4-byte name at -92 and at -104; `vsel`/`t0`
belong right under the ret slot (-120/-124, before the operator* inline `r` at -136). Chain locals in

<a id="addr-taken-param-home-reload-t6-51714"></a>
### Param homed then reloaded once into t6 = address-taken param read via pointer-to-param (gl_func_00051714, EXACT)

Target entry: `addiu sp,-0x30; sw a0,0x30(sp); lw t6,0x30(sp); ...` then every field read off `t6`
(4x `lwc1 fN,k(t6)` -> cvt.d.s -> K&R double args to the blank). Documented for months as "K&R home
spill+reload cap, C-unreproducible without varargs". It is just an address-taken param:

```c
void gl_func_00051714(float *a0) {
    float **pp = &a0;
    gl_func_00000000(fmt, (double)(*pp)[0], (double)(*pp)[1], (double)(*pp)[2], (double)(*pp)[3]);
}
```

`&a0` forces the home store; the four `*pp` loads have no intervening store so they CSE into one
expression temp, which IDO puts in **t6** (temps start at t6). Variants that miss:
`float * volatile a0` + `float *p = a0;` gives the same spill/reload but `p` is a coloured local (v0);
`volatile a0` read inline reloads a0 four times; `*(float **)&a0` / `*&a0` fold away (no home).
Second instance gl_func_000602A8 (80.0 -> EXACT, "three stacked caps" all C): same `int **pp = &a0;`
home/reload, `&D_00000000 + K` for the `lui/addiu` string (not a literal address -> `ori`), and an
**INT literal divisor** `x / 1024` to keep `div.s` by 1024.0f where `/ 1024.0f` and a
`float k = 1024.0f` local both fold to `mul.s` by 1/1024 when the quotient feeds a call arg directly
(`float k = (float)1024` also works -- the D9E4 int-cast lever).

Generalises: any "param stored to its home at entry and immediately reloaded into a t-reg" with no
call in between is a `&param` escape (cf. the volatile-param lever in
[3B80](#volatile-param-and-cse-arg-copies-3b80), which keeps the param memory-resident per use).

<a id="placeholder-symbol-cse-cap-79a4"></a>
## Placeholder symbols can fake a CSE cap: real reloc names + a separate symbol for the un-reloc'd `lui at` (timproc_uso_b5_func_000079A4 98.32 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

The wrap had been labelled a "permanent 98.32% cap": IDO CSE'd the fade-step load base one instruction
shorter than the target. The wrap read three things through `&D_00000000`: the 0x34 mode gate, the
0x1D0 fade step, and the 0xA4 slot table. Because they were one symbol, IDO built one shared `a2` base.
The target's `expected/` reloc table (`mips-linux-gnu-objdump -dr`) has `import_80020098` for the gate
(the `a2` base, also passed to 011E00), `import_8002013C` for the slot table, and NO reloc on the fade
step's `lui at; lwc1 f4,0x1D0(at)`. Fix: gate = `*(int *)(&import_80020098 + 0x34)`, table =
`((int *)(&import_8002013C + 0xA4))[slot]`, and keep the fade step on `&D_00000000 + 0x1D0`, a
DIFFERENT symbol from the gate, so it is not CSE'd. The raw bytes are the same, because the lo16 is
baked either way. The tail was the exact sibling `timproc_uso_b5_func_000080F4`'s call sequence, copied
as written. The 2026-05-28 note "splitting one base shatters the shared CSE web" was measured with
every other reference still on the placeholder. Once the other references carry their real names,
only the fade step needs to stay separate.

Last word: `slot = *(int *)(scr + 0x3E0 + idx * 4)` / `FW(scr + idx * 4, 0x3E0)` emit
`addu t4,t3,s0`. The array form `((int *)(scr + 0x3E0))[idx]` gives the target's `addu t4,s0,t3`.

**Second instance, timproc_uso_b5_func_0000283C (98.68 -> EXACT, 206 words).** The residual was two
schedule tells, not colouring:
1. `or s1,a0,zero` at entry, right after `sw s1`, with `sw a3,home` in the `bnez a0` delay slot. The build
   instead put the `or` in the delay slot. The alloc-or-reuse self pointer is the PARAM itself
   (`if (arg0 != 0 || (arg0 = alloc(0x20)) != 0) ... return arg0;`). A `var_s1 = arg0;` copy makes the
   move part of the if's block, so the scheduler drops it into the delay slot. Dropping the named copy
   also removes its frame slot. An unused `volatile s32 pad;` in its declaration position puts the slot
   back (an unused plain `s32 *spare;` works too).
2. Four `0.0f` stores to `p+0xDC` came out in the target order +8, +0, +4, +C only when all four
   statements were on ONE source line (`+0xC`, `+8`, `+4`, `+0` order). None of the 24 orders on separate
   lines matched. This is the as1 same-line lever ([#same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440](#same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440)).
De-aliasing to real names also exposed a CSE hazard. The target relocs the second child's vtable store
to the same `import_80086288` as the first. In C, the same symbol gets CSE'd across three calls (a spill
plus 8 bytes of frame). So that one site keeps a different zero symbol (`D_00000000_a`), and only its
reloc name differs from the target.

**FP corollary (timproc_uso_b5_func_00001DB0, NM, 6 -> 3 diffs, not landed):** two reloc'd doubles at
`D_807FF0D8 + 0xB8` and `D_807FF0E0 + 0xC0` (unpaired HI16, lo baked). `extern char D_807FF0D8,
D_807FF0E0;` with `*(f64 *)(&D_807FF0D8 + 0xB8)` gives the target's `ldc1 f16,184(at)` / `192(at)`
displacements (separate f64 externs give 0). The operand order of `mul.d` / `add.d` is NOT fixed: it
follows the whole expression's shape. `B * x + C` emits `mul.d (B, x)` and `add.d (C, prod)` as in the
target, `C + B * x` reverses both, and `x * B + C` reverses only the mul. The next statement's
`41.0f + 5.0f * f54` ignores its own operand order completely (all 16 combinations tested), but its
`mtc1`/`lwc1` f-register pick changes with the PREVIOUS statement's shape. Still open: `mul.s` and
`add.s` operand order in that statement (draft `/home/danjs/decomp-drafts/b5_1DB0_ldc1fix_3diff.c.txt`).

<a id="assign-in-call-arg-spill-before-copy-0478"></a>
## Spill-vs-copy order before a call follows where the copy is written: `f(slot, node = r)` (timproc_uso_b5_func_00000478 97.89 -> EXACT, 18B4 98.72 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

**0478.** Target, after `r = 8FC8(...)` returns: `addiu a0,s1,16; sw v0,80(sp)` (r's home), `sw a0,52(sp)`
(the `slot` local's home), `or s0,v0,zero` (the register `node` copy), then `jal 07ACE0; or a1,v0,zero`.
The wrap wrote `slot = arg0 + 0x10; node = r; 07ACE0(slot, r);` and got the `or s0,v0` BEFORE the
`sw a0,52(sp)`. Statement order, a one-line join, an if(1) barrier and decl swaps did not change it, and
the wrap had been labelled an allocator cap. The fix is to write the copy inside the call:

```c
slot = (int *)((char *)arg0 + 0x10);
07ACE0(slot, node = (int *)r);     /* [sw a0,slot][move s0,v0], a1 still from v0 */
```

`07ACE0(slot = ..., node = r)` (both assignments in the argument list) gives the same bytes. Moving
`node = r` after the call costs a reload and two words. When a register copy and an earlier
statement's home store are swapped right before a call, try the assignment inside the argument list.

**18B4 (same file, alloc-or-reuse ctor).** Two tells: (1) `or s0,a0,zero` at entry, before `or s1,a2` and
the `bnez a0` (whose delay slot is `sw a3,home`). The build put the `or` in the delay slot. Fix: use the
param itself as self (`if (arg0 != 0 || (arg0 = alloc(0x58)) != 0)`), no named copy, as in 283C
([#placeholder-symbol-cse-cap-79a4](#placeholder-symbol-cse-cap-79a4)). (2) The shared `arg0 + 0x10`
local took 72(sp) instead of 76(sp) while a `volatile s32 pad;` stood in for the removed copy's slot. With
NO pad it lands at 76. So the copy's frame slot is not always one to keep: check the slot offsets after
dropping it before adding a pad. All callees and globals were also de-aliased to their reloc names.

**024C (same file, 42-word vtable dispatch, labelled "NATURAL CEILING 96.43").** `p = a0->0x48; fn =
*(p + p->0x7C * 0x28 + 0x90); if (!fn) return; save p, a0 to globals; reload; fn();`. Target colours p in
v0, the reloaded param in v1, the 0x28 stride in a0, with ring temps t6..t9. Three levers, all needed:
1. Leave idx/fn UNNAMED (named ones take a0/a1 instead of ring temps).
2. `((Ent *)((char *)p + 0x90))[p[0x7C / 4]].fn` with `typedef struct { void (*fn)(void); char pad[0x24]; }
   Ent;` gives the target's base-first `addu t8,v0,t7`. The plain `p + idx * 0x28 + 0x90` gives
   `addu t8,t7,v0`. (A `char[0x28]` typedef did NOT flip it in arcproc 1170, so the struct with a typed
   member is what counts.) CONFIRMED on arcproc_uso_func_00001170 (99.38 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16): even
   with a MULTU-scaled stride (`li v1,40` CSE'd across both uses, `multu t6,v1; mflo t7`), the
   struct form `((Ent *)((char *)p + 0x90))[p[0x7C / 4]].fn` gives `addu t8,v0,t7` with NO named
   stride; seven flat spellings (array-of-char subscript, (int) base, +0x90 placement, comma) all
   stay mul-first. The old "multu-scaled addu stays mul-first in ugen" verdict was wrong.
3. The preceding call's return is dead, but the callee was declared `extern int f();`, so v0 stayed
   reserved and every colour shifted by one (v1/a0/a1). Declaring it `extern void f();` (every caller in
   the TU ignored the return) frees v0, the same effect as the 27BC void-alias lever, but with the real
   reloc name kept.

**0778 (same file, 605-word flat bulk registration, labelled "ugen coloring + as1 tie cap" at 97.48).**
76 calls `f(&tbl + K, packed_id)` with ids built from `n = arg0->0x50` and a global `g`. The 127-word
residual was all spelling, three rules:
1. Constant multiplies: `n*3`, `n*9`, `g*12` give IDO's in-place expansion (`sll t9,t8,2; subu t9,t9,t8`,
   `addu at,a1,zero; sll; addu`). The wrap's `n*4 - n` / `(g*4-g)*4` gave fresh temps and was 2 words short.
2. For `A | B` / `A + B` with two non-trivial subtrees, the build evaluated the RIGHT subtree first
   (it got the lowest ring temps and became the rs). Where the build's first-loaded value was the
   wrong one, swapping the C operands fixed every temp in that call (82 words over three groups).
3. A big constant held in a callee-saved register across calls 2-4 (`lui s1,7` CSE) stayed the rt of
   the `or` in every spelling (`0x70000 | x`, `x | (7<<16)`, a named `k`, `k << 16`, unsigned). The
   commutative assignment lever pins it as rs: `x | (k = 0x70000)` -> `or a1,s1,t8`
   (`(k = 0x70000) | x` does NOT). See [the assignment lever](#feedback-ido-fp-commutative-operand-order-assignment-lever).

**6394 (same file, NM 97.12; draft at 98.50 in /home/danjs/decomp-drafts/, not landed).** Two
address-folding tells, both fixed by how the base pointer is written (verified standalone):
1. Target `lui t4,%hi(D); addiu t4,t4,0x160` then `addu t5,scaled,t4` (the +0x160 stays in the base
   addiu). Every inline spelling (`&D + 0x160 + i*0x18`, `(E18 *)(&D + 0x160) + i`, struct
   `{pad[0x160]; E18 e[];}`, `&tbl[i]`, a goto barrier) folds it into the index:
   `addiu t7,scaled,0x160; addu v0,t7,lda(D)`. A NAMED base local does not fold:
   `b = &D + 0x160; return b + i * 0x18;`.
2. Target `lui a0; addiu a0,a0,0x130` (the call argument) then `lw t1,16(a0)` (a field read through that
   same register). With `tp = &D + 0x130` (initialised, assigned in the call, if(1), goto) IDO folds
   the field read to `lw t6,0x140(sym)`. Two statements `tp = &D; tp += 0x130;` keep the register base.
Each NEW named local here also cost an 8-byte frame slot (72 -> 80); reusing a dead existing local
kept the frame. Residual: the ugen temp ring is two slots behind the target from the table access
onward (target `sll t9` then t2/t3/t4, build t0/t1/t2); no phantom-alloc spelling found yet.

<a id="vec3-sub-mul-fp-candidates-bb-boundary-37938"></a>
### Single-use Vec3 arithmetic in the FP candidate pool needs BB boundaries (gl_func_00037938, NM 93.7)

Target: `sub.s f0 / f2 / f12` for `d = b - a` and `mul.s f2 / f12 / f14` for `sc = c2 * k` (k in f0),
each result stored once into a Vec3 local that is then struct-copied. Writing the results straight into
the struct (`d.x = b.x - a.x`) or into named floats with the store right after both give ring temps
(f4..f18): uopt forward-substitutes a single-use named float into its only use. What works:

```c
dx = b.x - a.x; dy = b.y - a.y; dz = b.z - a.z;
do {} while (0);                 /* BB boundary: dx..dz now cross blocks -> candidates */
pd->x = dx; pd->y = dy; pd->z = dz;   /* Vec3 *pd = &d; a plain d.x store still lets uopt
                                        re-derive b.x - a.x from the (unchanged) memory operands */
do {} while (0);                 /* second boundary: without it dx..dz share a block with k
                                    (per-BB interference) and take f2/f12/f14 instead of f0/f2/f12 */
```

The mul needs only the first boundary (its operand `k` is already a candidate). The named floats and `pd`
each get a home at their DECL POSITION, so they replace bytes of any pad arrays that were standing in for
the target's frame holes (#scalar-homes-are-the-holes-3cbb4). Related: a 3-member copy written on ONE
line in x,y,z order gives the descending f18/f16/f10 ring the target used for `arg.z..x = c4.z..x`.

<a id="iterator-entry-ring-skips-register-base-41edc"></a>
### Iterator entry-block ring skips track a register-variable base (gl_func_00041EDC, NM 97.6)

The exact 39EE4 walker (`next = head[0]; cur = next; node = cur ? (next = cur[1], cur[0]) : 0;`) burns
two ugen ring slots in its entry block (head t6, skip t7, cur[1] t8, skip t9, body cur t0). In
probes the skips appear only when the head load's base is a REGISTER variable: param a0, a value
returned in v0, or a coloured local (`s = self` -> v0). A base that is a temp (a call-spilled param
reloaded `lw t6,home`, `*sp` through `&self`, a global load) gives a dense ring with no skips. 41EDC's
target has the `lw t6,home` reload AND the skips (plus the entry result in v1), and no spelling got
both: separate entry var, comma-condition while, for/if/goto entries, pointer-form and typed iterator
structs, casts, volatile/register self, while(0) anchors in every order, and if(0) demotion were all
byte-identical. When a sibling's ring is +1/+2 everywhere after the head load, this is the class.

<a id="float-param-int-reg-mtc1-capture-reuse-5ce68"></a>
### Float param in an int arg register: reuse the param, do not copy it (gl_func_0005CE68, NM 96.6)

Slerp `void f(float *q1, float *q2, float t, int spin)`: O32 passes t in a2. Target captures it with
`mtc1 a2,f14` near the top, keeps it in f14 on the no-call path, and on the call path spills
`swc1 f14,home(a2)` in a jal delay slot and reloads it after. The m2c lift's `var_f14 = arg2;` copy
(the copy is then re-assigned as scale1) made uopt home the PARAM instead: `sw a2,home` at entry,
`lwc1` at every use, and frame 0x68 vs 0x48 because of the extra named temps. Writing the reassignment
into the parameter itself (`t = sin(t * theta) / sinom; if (flip) t = -t;`) gives the target's capture
and spill exactly. Same pass: m2c's 19 named temps -> 11 real names gave the 0x48 frame (named-local
count governs frame size), and q1[0] / q2[0] must be NAMED locals re-read after the calls so they colour
f16/f18 -- inline (unnamed) they become one CSE temp spilled to its own home.

<a id="lui-count-placeholder-sweep-44de4"></a>
## game_libs placeholder sweep by `lui` count; gl_func_00044DE4 90.4 -> EXACT (2026-10-16 agent-c)

game_libs `expected/` objects are raw `.word` dumps, so `objdump -r` shows almost no relocs and the
[#placeholder-symbol-cse-cap-79a4](#placeholder-symbol-cse-cap-79a4) check cannot be read off the reloc
table. Use the `lui` count instead: for every 85-99.9% wrap, count `lui` in `expected/` vs
`build/non_matching/` per function. If the target has MORE, the C merges several symbols (or writes
literal addresses). The 2026-10-16 scan of post/post0b found 34240 (7 vs 3), 34458 (4/3), 437C0 (20/19),
44DE4 (5/3) and 53C04 (6/4, same insn count).

gl_func_00044DE4 (62 words, teardown/reset). The m2c wrap had `*(int*)0 = 0x1FEB4; *(int*)0 = x;`, which
gives `lui t6,1; ori` and `sw t6,0(zero)`. The target has `lui t6,2; addiu t6,-332; lui at,0; sw t6,0(at)`
and a second `lui at,0; sw t8,0(at)`. Five levers took it to exact:
1. Two DISTINCT scalar base-0 externs (`D_44DE4_tag`, `D_44DE4_val`, pinned to 0) give one `lui at` per
   store. Sharing one symbol would CSE the base, see [#shared-at-absolute-store-cap-66a50](#shared-at-absolute-store-cap-66a50).
   Address constants are `(char *)&D_00000000 + 0x1FEB4` (the `lui 2; addiu -X` carry form). The
   callee is the blank `gl_func_00000000` because the target jal words are baked `jal 0`.
2. The early self uses read `a0` in the build and `s2` in the target. `volatile` on the FIRST self store
   (`*(volatile int *)(self + 0x244) = 0;`) fixes it ([#volatile-first-store-pins-param-sreg-copy-66c74](#volatile-first-store-pins-param-sreg-copy-66c74)).
3. Handler-table reads written as `((int *)(FW(self,0x240) + 0x198))[FW(self,0x204)]` give the target
   `lw idx` before `lw base` and `addu base,idx*4`.
4. Target loop: `or s1,zero,zero; blez; or s0,s2,zero` (counter s1, cursor init in the delay slot). Any
   hand-written cursor (`p = self; ... p += 4`) gives the cursor whichever of s0/s1 matches its
   assignment order, and that same order puts it either before the branch or in the delay slot, never the
   target's combination. No cursor at all, `for (i = 0; i < n; i++) e = ((char **)(self + 0x148))[i];`,
   lets IDO strength-reduce its own cursor and gives exactly the target shape.
5. `q = FW(self, 0x22C); FW(q, 0xC) = 0;` (named) loads into `v0` instead of a ring temp, and the later
   `lh t8` becomes the target's `lh t7`.

**Second instance, gl_func_00034458 (86.2 -> EXACT, 60 words).** The wrap read the list head and the
vtable record through the same `&D_00000000 + 0`, so IDO CSE'd one base. The target loads the head into
`s0` at entry and hoists the record address into `s4` (`lui s4,0; addiu s4,0`): 4 luis vs 3. Two distinct
base-0 externs (`D_34458_head`, `D_34458_obj`) plus carry-form template addresses gave every word except
the out-param homes (+8). `volatile int pad;` declared first, then `int outB, outA;`, puts them at the
target's sp+0x50/0x54. Side effect to expect: the NEXT function's objdiff % can drop slightly when the
wrap's NM size changes, because the old NM object counted a trailing alignment nop in its symbol size
(34548 75.1 -> 73.8 with identical code words).

**Third instance, gl_func_00034240 (post, 87.4 -> EXACT, 104 words): 7 target luis vs 3.** One
`&D_00000000` stood in for five symbols. Split into distinct base-0 externs: the record pointer `D_34240_G`
(address hoisted to s4), two cb args `D_34240_X` / `D_34240_Y` (fresh `lui a0; addiu a0` each), and the
poll arg `D_34240_P`. Use ONE symbol for P in both poll loops: the target rematerializes `lui s3; addiu s3`
per loop in the same register, and two symbols moved the second web to s2. **Folding fact:** the config
table read as `(char *)&D_00000000 + 0x1E21C` makes IDO fold the loop pre-test into `lui t0,2; lw t0,-7652(t0)`.
This did not change with a multi-def `if (1)`, a volatile pre-test, a while/goto loop, an index form, or an
int-cast address. A ZERO-OFFSET symbol pinned at the real address (`extern char D_0001E21C;` with
`D_0001E21C = 0x0001E21C;`) keeps the target's `lui s2; addiu s2; lw t0,0(s2)`. In the `.o` only that
HI16/LO16 pair differs from `expected/` (the pinned-symbol class, as gl_ref_* / D_0001B710). The ROM is identical.
Other levers in this function: drop the unused param (`(void)a2` homed a0); declare `d[0x80]` and
`saved34` before the named pointers (each registerized named local takes a ghost home); write
`gl_func_00000000(dp = d, -1)`; and put an empty `if (D_34240_G) {}` right after the first store. Without
that empty `if`, `addiu s1,sp,64` schedules up next to `sw s1`.

**Fourth instance, gl_func_00053C04 (post0b, 92.15 -> EXACT, 336 words, same insn count): 6 target luis vs
4.** The face->vertex table, the vertex count and the remap table shared one `&D_00000000`. Three base-0
externs fixed it: `s16 D_53C04_tbl[]` (address hoisted to s6), a SCALAR `u32 D_53C04_n` (the target re-reads it
with `lui a0; lw a0,0(a0)` before the loop and again in the loop, because the divide stores may alias it)
and `u16 D_53C04_map[]`. The lui fix alone gave +0.3 points. The rest came from levers that each change
the whole function:
1. **Frame homes count named locals, including block-scoped ones.** The target had counts[] at sp+112 and
   the struct carrier at sp+76. Getting there took exactly 10 scalars declared between the f32[3] arrays and
   counts[], and 6 after it. Unused locals (`j1..j3` holding the index-call results) still take a home.
   Reusing one named pointer for several loops (`v` for the zero loop, `n` for the copy loop) frees homes.
   Each change also re-colours registers.
2. **A named pointer cannot take `$a0` in the BB that sets up the next call's `$a0` argument.** Named
   `p1..p3 = arg1 + iN * 6` coloured a3/v1/a1/a2. Inline `((s16 *)(arg1 + (u32)i1 * 6))[k]` temps get the
   target's a2/v1/a0/a1.
3. **FP cross product:** IDO evaluates the second product of `A*B - C*D` with its factors swapped. Write
   it as `(b2-a2)*(c1-b1) ... - ((c1 - b1) * (b2 - a2))` to get the target's order. All 40 FP words matched
   after this.
4. **Dead `if (v) {}` sets the s-reg order** ([#dead-empty-if-priority-boost-placement-is-everything-a7b4-d418-cracked-2026-07-03](#dead-empty-if-priority-boost-placement-is-everything-a7b4-d418-cracked-2026-07-03)).
   Target i2/i3/i1 = s3/s4/s5. `if (i2) {}` then `if (i3) {}`, placed after the third block's
   `v = ...; n = ...;`, gave that order. As a side effect the three `&counts[iN]` addresses colour a1/a2 and
   hoist next to the first block, as in the target. Put earlier in the loop body (right after the defs), the
   same `if`s re-colour the whole loop wrongly.
5. A loop-invariant zero inside the `if`: `if (n) { off = 0; do ... }` puts `lw n` before `or s0,zero,zero`
   and `lui s6` (table) in the beqz delay slot. `off = 0;` before the `if` gives the opposite order.
6. **as1 tie, blocks 2 and 3:** the target loads `lw 0x54` before `lw 0x58`. Writing `v = ...; n = ...;` on
   ONE source line fixes it ([#same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440](#same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440)).
   Swapping the two statements instead renumbers the temps.
7. Copy loop: `((Vec3 *)FW(arg0, 0x58))[*m]` gives a base-first `addu`, and a separate dst pointer (`n`, not
   `v`) gets the target's a0/v1 split.
**Fifth instance, gl_func_0002DE24 (post, 76.07 -> EXACT, 30 words): 8 target luis vs 7.** Two global
stores (`+0`, `+0xC`) and the last call's global arg shared `&D_00000000`, CSE'd into `lui v1; addiu v1`.
Three base-0 externs fixed it. The entry `sw a0,24(sp); lbu t6,27(sp)` (and `lbu a0,27(sp)` after the
first call) is an `unsigned char` parameter whose address is taken (`unsigned char *p = &a0; ... (void)p;`).
A plain `unsigned char` parameter, prototyped or K&R, gives `andi a2,a0,0xff` and a 32-byte frame.
**More instances (2026-10-16 agent-c, all EXACT):** bootup_uso `func_000034E8` (6 vs 3): three source
floats read through one `&func_000003F8 + K` base were CSE'd into a held register. Three scalar `f32` globals
pinned at 0x538/0x53C/0x540 each get their own `lui at; lwc1`. The Vec4 destination is the zero-offset
`D_00000030`, which keeps its address in v0 with 0/4/8/C displacements. post0b `gl_func_00038360`
(+6): the m2c wrap passed a literal `0` where every serializer call takes the stream object
`&D_00000000` (`lui a0,0; addiu a0,0`). Declaring the innermost ctor pointer first moved the spill homes
by 4 bytes. bootup_uso `func_00002DA4` (12 vs 7, a jumptable donor splice): see
docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#bootup-uso-jumptable-donor-2da4. A store `G = f()` followed at once by a read of
`G` needs two symbols, because one symbol forwards v0.
bootup_uso `func_000087A4` (86.3 -> EXACT, 11 vs 9): the documented "three bare `lui r,0`, two hoisted
above the bnez" cap is three base-0 externs (read, OR-store, +4/+0 store pair). Which luis IDO hoists
above the branch depends on block shape: with no marker it hoisted the store pair's `lui v0; addiu v0`;
an empty `if (1) {}` right after `W = R | 8;` gave the target `lui t8; lui at; bnez; lui v0` (delay slot).
The same function's "K&R float arg promotes to double" cap is a prototyped alias of the blank
(`void f(char *, char *, int, float, float)`): the 4th float rides in a3 as bits, the 5th is `swc1 ,0x10(sp)`.
Frame: every extra named pointer local took a ghost home; inlining the `desc` local and declaring
`int kind; int pad[5];` put kind at the target sp+0x44 with frame 0x50.
bootup_uso `func_00002F90` (75.4 -> EXACT, 13 vs 9): the "func_000003F8 float-pool base held in a2"

plus the RMW bases and the link block (a2), one for the third child, the node and the alloc (s0). A void
