Scan tool: `scripts/call-shape-scan.py UNIT --lui` lists functions whose target has more luis (it also
prints insn counts, nm/tgt).

<a id="stack-ctor-u32-null-test-437c0"></a>
## IDO cfe folds `&local != 0`; `(u32)o != 0` keeps the stack-object alloc-or-reuse test (gl_func_000437C0 89.47 -> 99.87 NM, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

Tell: `addiu a1,sp,K; bnez a1,L; nop; jal alloc; addiu a0,zero,SIZE; beqz v0,skip; or a1,v0,zero`. This is
the constructor protocol run on a stack object (see [#ncc-derived-ctor-protocol-6a30](#ncc-derived-ctor-protocol-6a30)
for the NCC version). In cfe C, `o = (char *)&obj; if (o != 0 || (o = alloc(0x60)) != 0)` folds the test
and drops the alloc branch. `(o = &obj) != 0` and `&obj.f[0]` fold too. `if ((u32)o != 0 || (o = alloc(0x60)) != 0)`
keeps the exact shape. The member tests (`p = o + 0x34; if (p != 0 || ...)` giving `addiu at,zero,-52; bne a1,at`)
do not fold, so they need no cast. With a cast they lose two words.

Other levers in the same function:
- The arm-selector value `self->0x38` reuses the entry-check variable `st`. With a separate variable (or
  inline reads), `st` and `ok` swap v0 and v1 at entry. A dead `if (st) {}`, `while (0)` anchors,
  signature types, and an unnamed `ok` all failed to fix this.
- Calls whose result is unused go through the void alias `gl_func_00000000_void`. After an int-returning
  call, the next value goes to v1 instead of v0. This is the Index entry "Extern RETURN TYPE is a $v0-coloring
  lever" (timproc_uso_b5 0058).
- The 0x0/0x244/0x248 global table needs its own symbol. While it shared `D_00000000` with the 0x254
  reloads, the hoisted base took v1 and the arg1 reload took v0 (target: the reverse). That is the same
  placeholder-CSE effect as the lui-count sweep, even with an equal `lui` count.
- Per-command display-list writes: `{ char *_g; x = self->0x68; _g = (char *)x->dl->n++; _g = x->dl->buf
  + (s32)_g * 8; ... }`. Reusing `_g` for the index orders the `n` store before the base reload (target
  `lw 12(v1)` twice) without adding a home. Each such block-local gets its own spill home (60..40).
- Still open: the two member pointers colour v1, and the target colours them a2.
- Follow-up 2026-10-17 (agent-c, NEGATIVE, 7 words left): uoptlist has p and q as separate constrained LRs coloured v1
  after o (a1); nothing coloured earlier holds v1 across the arm, so v1 is free. No change from: one variable for p and q,
  reusing g or x for them (19 / 43 words), `register`, function-scope decls (frame shifts, 18), dead `if (arg1) {}` in
  the arm. Extending `ok` past the arm with a dead `if (ok) {}` costs a word. The target's v1 blocker is unidentified;
  the member tests may be a C++ member-constructor protocol (see #ncc-derived-ctor-protocol-6a30).

<a id="named-locals-reserve-ring-regs-6394"></a>
### Temp ring offset across the whole function = two named locals coloured into t0/t1 (timproc_uso_b5_func_00006394 -> EXACT)

**Symptom.** Size, schedule and frame exact; 60+ differing words, all register numbers, from one
point onward the build's temps are a constant number of ring slots behind the target (build
`lui t0 / addu t0,t0,t9 / lw t0,0(t0)` where the target has `t2`). Index, idx-temp, clamp and
operand-order spellings were all invariant (98.50 draft).

**Diagnosis.** Count uses of each t-reg in the target (`grep -o` over the no-alias disassembly).
In 6394 `t0` and `t1` appeared only 4 times each, all in the two template blocks
(`lw t1,16(a0); lh t0,32(t1); mtc1 t0,$f4`); every other temp skipped them. uopt-coloured
candidates keep their register for the whole function, and ugen's ring
(t6..t9,t0..t5) skips registers that candidates hold. So the target had two variables there:
the template row pointer and the template width. The width is live across the `x / 2` rounding
branch (`bgez`), so it spans more than one basic block.

**Fix.**
```c
s32 tmpl_w; char *tmpl_row;
tmpl_w = 0;                    /* dead entry init: makes tmpl_w the earlier variable */
...
tmpl_row = (char *)FW(tp, 0x10); tmpl_w = *(s16 *)(tmpl_row + 0x20);
import_0024F34C(tp, (s32)(((w / 2) + 0xA0) - (tmpl_w * 0.25f)), sp44, 2);
```
Naming both took the function from 62 to 6 differing words (row t0 / width t1, swapped). Both
live ranges are unconstrained, so they colour in first-occurrence (bitpos) order with the lowest
free register (see the uopt regalloc algorithm entry). A dead `tmpl_w = 0;` at function entry
emits nothing but makes tmpl_w occur first: width -> t0, row -> t1, exact. Declaration order, a
`s16` type, statement order inside the block, an empty `if (tmpl_w) {}` and a dead `while (0)`
were all wrong here (the last two added blocks and changed the frame).
Merging the width into an existing later variable (`temp_v0_3`) also gave it t0, but moved that
variable's later use from v0 to t0 (1 word off).

**General rule.** If a t-reg appears only in one short block of the target and the build's ring is
offset by the same count everywhere else, look for that many named locals in that block. Only one
named local here shifts the ring by one slot, not two.

<a id="same-line-registration-schedule-23e4"></a>
### Alloc-cascade sibling port + same-line call/test/store join (timproc_uso_b3_func_000023E4 -> EXACT)

The b3 ctor was a 96.32 wrap with "spill slots off by 4, entry delay fill, v0/a3 renumber"
listed as caps. Its sibling `arcproc_uso_func_0000251C` was already exact. Copying that body's
shape fixed all of those at once: the short-circuit alloc head, one `a3` web shared by
level-2 / vtable / registration nodes, `if (1) {}` before the dispatch base, and the unused
`volatile int pad`. Only b3's own statements were kept (0x60/0x64/0x68 stores, seven packed
ids, the 0x17D7 gate, the 4-arg final call). **Check the exact siblings of a capped
ctor before believing its cap list.**

The gate then needed two more changes.
1. The target reads D+388 and D+400 through a base CSE'd into `v0` (`lui v0; addiu v0,v0,0`).
   The 0x17D7 word comes from a separate `lui t1; lw t1,0(t1)`. So the 0x17D7 global needs its own
   extern. D+388, D+400 and the final call's D+400 must share one symbol: three uses keep the
   CSE, and the use after the call is re-materialized (`lui a0`). With only two uses on that
   symbol, uopt folded each into its own `lui`.
2. A 2-word as1 reorder was left: the build had `lw a0,44(sp)` (reload of the spilled `arg0+16`)
   before the base's `addiu v0`, and the target had the reverse. It needed
   `gl_func_00000000(arg0 + 16, a3); if (*(int *)(a3 + 0x14) != 0) { ... } *(int *)(a3 + 0x14) = (int)arg0;`
   on ONE line. Joining only the test + store, only the store + the gate, or only the call +
   the test did not help. A named `&D` local, array spellings, `if (1) {}` and a distinct base
   symbol had no effect. A 7-minute permuter run (import.py through the root `.venv` python,
   which has toml) found the join. See the as1 line-number tie-break entry above.

**Second hit (titproc_uso_func_00001E9C 99.18 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g).** A 2-word pair swap
after a call (`addiu t6,%lo(import_00073B18)` vs the `lw v1,56(sp)` spill reload) had survived
named temps, `if (1) {}`, goto labels and volatile-store probes and was filed as an "as1 pair-order
cap". Putting the call and the next store on one line fixed it on the first build:
`titproc_uso_func_04C678(fourth, D + 0x514); fourth[0x28 / 4] = (int)&import_00073B18;`.
**Any 2-word adjacent swap right after a call that was filed as an as1 tie-break cap: try joining
the call with the next statement on one line first.**

<a id="offset-in-addiu-separate-global-0c14"></a>
### Offset in the addiu, not the lw = a separate global at base+K (mgrproc_uso_func_00000C14 -> EXACT)

**Symptom.** The target reads a global pointer with `lui v1,%hi; addiu v1,v1,0x30; lw a0,0(v1)`,
with `v1` kept for several reloads. `*(int **)((char *)&import_80263D60 + 0x30)` gives
`addiu v1,v1,0; lw a0,0x30(v1)` (K folded into each lw). The older wrap used
`pp = &sym; if (1) { pp += 0xC; }` per region. That put 0x30 in the addiu, but the `if (1)` blocks
moved `sw ra` between the lui and the addiu and delayed one state reload past two stores
(4 words, filed as an "if(1) scheduling cap").

**Fix.** The pointer is its own variable at base+0x30. Declare `extern int *import_80263D60_30;`,
write natural C (`import_000A5A1C(import_80263D60_30); import_80263D60_30[0x504 / 4] = 0; ...`),
and append `import_80263D60_30 = 0x00000030;` to `undefined_syms_auto.txt` (on its own line; put
any comment on a separate line, because `bake-data-relocs.py` cannot parse a trailing `/* */` and
fails with "no value for symbol"). IDO emits the same held-address shape with addiu immediate 0
plus a LO16 reloc; the Yay0 block rule bakes 0x30 into it, so `make verify-blocks` matches the
ROM. The raw `.o` slice differs from expected/ only in those addiu immediates (pinned-symbol
exception class). The natural form also fixed the schedule: both as1 swaps disappeared.

**Recognition.** expected/ has a HI16 for the import but no LO16, and the addiu immediate is a small
non-zero K. The sibling `mgrproc_uso_func_00000B5C` (same state slot, 8-word residual,
86.96) went EXACT with the same symbol and no other change.

<a id="alloc-guard-vec3-temps-first-8cd8"></a>
## Alloc-guard Vec3 writes: compute components into temps before storing (game_uso 8CD8 71.26 -> 81.42, agent-g 2026-10-16)

The pattern is `p = 0; if (1) { p = &local; } if (p != NULL || (p = alloc(12)) != NULL) { p->x = ...; p->y = 0.0f; p->z = ...; }`.
The TARGET does all of the component loads (and subs) first and only then the three `swc1` to p. That is
the inlined C++ `Vec3(x, y, z)` constructor shape: its arguments are evaluated before the members are written.
If you write the stores component by component, IDO must keep each later load below the earlier store
through `p`, because the store may alias the load source, so it emits `lwc1/sub.s/swc1` per component.

Fix: put the non-constant components into temps first (`tz = q[2]; tx = q[0]; p->y = 0.0f; p->z = tz; p->x = tx;`).
Leave the constant inline. Making `ty = 0.0f` a temp scores the same.

- Declare the temps ONCE at function scope, in place of existing `volatile` ghost-home pads, and reuse them
  in every block. 8CD8 used padA0/padA1 -> `f32 tx, tz`. A block-scope `f32 t = ...;` gets its own stack
  home in IDO: 14 blocks grew the frame 528 -> 640 and scored worse.
- Apply it with a regex over every guard block in the function. In 8CD8 that was 14 blocks for +10.2 points
  in one step.
- Also works on the 7C1C fanout (#fresh-vec3-fanout-intcast-q-7c1c): 14 blocks, 75.76 -> 79.99. Its new
  `f32 tx, tz;` was added after the existing decls (no pads; the frame already differs, and objdiff fuzzy
  ignores sp offsets). Writing the temps in STORE order (79.99) beat x-then-z order (79.96). 591C, the
  same family, has not been tried yet.



<a id="float-matrix-decl-vs-assign-order-5be20"></a>
## 16-float matrix spill homes: decl order vs assignment order vs pointer-decl position (gl_func_0005BE20 99.42 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

gl_func_0005BE20 (4x4 adjugate, 16 calls to a 9-float 3x3 det helper) loads all 16 matrix elements
once into float locals. Six are colored into $f20-$f30; ten spill. The old NM matched every
instruction except the swc1/lwc1 stack offsets and the frame (-160 vs -168). Three separate knobs fixed it:

1. **Slot ladder = declaration order.** Each float local gets a home in decl order from the top of the
   frame down, and a local colored to a register still uses up its home. So the gaps in the target's
   ladder belong to the register-colored elements. Here the target's homes walk the matrix COLUMN-wise:
   `float m0, m4, m8, m12; float m1, m5, m9, m13; ...` (m0 @0xA4, m4 @0xA0, m8 @0x9C, m12 = gap
   0x98, m1 = gap 0x94, m5 @0x90 ...). Keep the decls separate from the assignments
   (see #frame-slot-topdown-decl-solver-40070). Using initializers in transposed order also
   reorders the loads and the coloring.
2. **Load schedule = assignment order, reversed within each run.** `m4=M[4]; m5; m6; m7;` loads
   M7,M6,M5. `m4; m7; m6; m5;` loads M5,M6,M7. The target's M5,M7,M6 needs `m4; m6; m7; m5;`.
   Changing the load order did not move any slot.
3. **Pointer locals declared before the floats add 8 frame bytes.** `float *M = arg0, *O = arg1;`
   declared first gave -176 with every slot already right. Declaring the two pointers AFTER the 16
   floats gives -168. Both pointers stay in a0/s0, but their decl position still sizes the frame.

Before declaring an FP-heavy spill-offset diff an allocator cap, map each slot to its variable and
read the gaps as register-colored locals in decl order. Here the old note said "spill-slot numbering
over the all-live set, not source-controllable".

<a id="prologue-move-param-vs-copy-62368"></a>
## Prologue `move sN,aK` placement: parameter vs local copy (gl_func_00062368 / gl_func_00061A0C -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

Both functions had the right instructions in the wrong order. A `move sN,aK` sat at the wrong point among
the prologue's `sw sX` saves, and the old notes called it a "prologue save-scheduling cap". It was
not a cap. Where the move lands depends on how the C names the value:

- The PARAMETER is itself the live variable (reassigned, or used as the loop counter): IDO puts the
  move early, inside the save sequence.
- A local initialized from the parameter (`int *s2 = a0;`): IDO puts the move after the saves, or
  in the first branch's delay slot.

62368 (get-or-alloc array init): the target has `move s2,a0` right after `move s0,a1`. Dropping
`s2 = a0` and reassigning the param (`if (s2 == 0) s2 = alloc(8)`) made it exact. The if form and
the `&&` form both work. 61A0C (hex dump): the target puts `move s4,a2` early and `move s1,a1` after
the saves. Making ONLY the count a parameter (`unsigned int s4` as the param, with `char *s1 = a1;`
kept as a copy) made it exact. Reassigning both params moved `move s1,a1` too early (9 diffs).

So for each mismatched move, try the parameter spelling and the copy spelling separately.
gl_func_00062E80 (constructor, 80.6 -> EXACT) needed the same param fix plus one decode fix: a field
store sitting in the final `jal`'s delay slot runs BEFORE the call, so write it before the call in C.
gl_func_00060D40 (75.5 -> EXACT) is the same constructor shape. An alloc-fail `return 0` adds
`b` + `move v0,zero` (+3 insns); `goto end` to the shared `return s0` removes them. Also the
field-store order in C has to match the target's store order.
gl_func_000628EC (NM 89.5 -> 98.63): the same param reassign fixed the prologue and dropped the copy's
home (grow the volatile pad by 8 to keep the frame). Moving a plain store ahead of a `|=` RMW in C fixed
the t-ring. The only residual is the 0.0/1.0 FP constant pair landing in f2/f0 instead of f0/f2, and
literal spellings, named locals and while(0) boosts do not change it.
gl_func_00041148 (post0b, 96.03 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-c): the deferred `move s1,a0` in a
debug allocator (`unsigned int s1 = arg0; if (arg1) s1 += arg1;`). Renaming the param to `s1` and
deleting the copy put the move first in the prologue; nothing else changed.

<a id="dead-pad-first-plus-spill-decl-order-7c74"></a>
## Empty slot under the spill slots: dead `char pad[4]` first AND spill-order decls (bootup func_00007C74 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

probed the two levers SEPARATELY:

- link-before-ret decl order alone keeps frame 0x20 (`link 0x1C, ret 0x18`).

scalar frame has one empty word BELOW the spill slots, try every decl permutation WITH a dead pad first,
not just the pad on its own.

**Same session, gl_func_00040CAC (post0b, 93.09 -> EXACT).** The old note said the target "copies the Vec3

**Negative, bootup func_00007204:** a 4-byte struct passed by value (`S a2`, homed at 0x38 and copied to a

**Not committed either, gl_func_0003E0F0 (post0b, 90.52 -> 93.40, short of the +3 bar):** the v1 block is a

where the q copy is the `or a0,v1` in the bnez delay). Function-level `char pad[20]; f32 vec3[3];` gives the

<a id="addu-operand-order-pointer-vs-int-add-28a68"></a>
## Opposite `addu` operand orders for the same pair: pointer add vs int add (gl_func_00028A68, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

Target loop body: `lw v0,base; addu t7,s0,v0; addu t8,v0,s0; sw t7,8(t8)` (record self-pointer
`rec->w8 = rec`). Writing `rec` once (or `base + off` twice) gives a single CSE'd `addu`. Writing it as
two different spellings keeps two adds, and the spelling picks the operand order:
- pointer add with a register-resident local, `(int)(off + base)`, keeps the written order (`s0,v0`);
- int add, `(int)base + off` or `off + (int)base`, always comes out base-first (`v0,s0`).
So the value is `(int)(off + base)` and the address is `*(int *)((int)base + off + 8)`.

Limit: when the base is an inline reload (`off + *(char **)(G + 0x2CFC)`), the load is evaluated
first in every spelling we tried (`off + X`, `X + off`, `&X[off]`, int casts, struct-array `&recs[i]`),
so the order is `t1,s0`. Reloading into a reassigned named local gives `s0,v0` but colours it v0 instead
of the ring temp t1. That word is the 28A68 residual (99.76).

<a id="signed-shift-bit-test-one-temp-5703c"></a>
## Single-bit tests: signed shift = one temp, unsigned shift-pair = two (game_libs_func_0005703C -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

A geometry-mode decoder tests six bits of one word with `sll tN,v1,K; bgez tN`. The old wrap wrote
each test as `((unsigned int)v1 << K) >> 31`. IDO folds that to the same `sll; bgez`, but the
folded `srl` still burns a temp number, so the build used every OTHER $t register (t9, t8, t0, t2,
t4, t6) where the target counts up one at a time (t6, t8, t7, t9, t0, t1, t2). Writing the tests as
`(v1 << K) < 0` fixed the whole ring. This is the same "count the skipped $tN" tell as
#one-bit-bitfield-test-dead-srl-phantom-25bfc, in the other direction: no gaps means no phantom.
The same function's second display-list append needed its own record-pointer local (`arr2`) to
land in a3 instead of reusing a2.

<a id="unsorted-dispatch-if-goto-plus-switch-54aec"></a>
## Unsorted beq dispatch chain = `if (v == K) goto` + a goto switch (gl_func_00054AEC -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

The target tests 0x72 first, then 0x68 and 0x69, as a chain of `beq` (argument moves in the delay
slots) followed by `b default`, and the bodies come after the chain in R/H/I/default order. Facts
from the probes (IDO 7.1 and 5.3 behave the same):

- A `switch` always emits its compares in ascending case order, whatever order the cases are written
  in, and the last compare is inverted into a `bnel` that falls into its body.
- An `if / else if` chain inverts every test into `bne` with the body falling through.
- A plain goto chain (`if (v == K) goto L;` three times, then `goto D;`) inverts the LAST test into
  `bne D; b L`. A one-case switch does the same.
- A switch with two or more goto cases and no fallthrough body emits `beq; beq; b default`.

So: `if (v == 0x72) goto R; switch (v) { case 0x68: goto H; case 0x69: goto I; } goto D;` with
the labelled bodies written in the target's order. Two switches (`switch (v) { case 0x72: goto R; }`
then the 2-case one with `default: goto D`) emit the same code. The bounded table read in case 'i'
reuses the switch variable `v` so it lands in v0, where a fresh temp took t2.
The same layout with a ONE-case second stage (gl_func_00052994, `beq 12 -> C; beql 1 -> ONE; b D`,
86.9 -> EXACT): the goto chain, a nested `if (v != 12)`, a one-case switch, and a duplicate `case 12`
all give `bne D; b ONE`. Writing the second test INVERTED gives the target's beq/beql:
`if (v == 12) goto C; if (v != 1) goto D; goto ONE;`. IDO inverts the inverted test back, and as1
fills the likely delay with ONE's first load. 52994 also needed the `if (1) { q = (int *)((char *)q
+ 0x18); }` base materialization from #game-uso-w4-lever-trio-2026-07-03 in both RMW arms (target
`addiu v0,a0,24; lw 0(v0)` where the build folded to `24(a0)`), and the dispatch variable reused
for the two loaded values (`(v0 = obj[1]) != 0`, `(v0 = obj[0x13]) != 8`) so they land in v0.

<a id="volatile-flag-object-fresh-t-60dc4"></a>
## Flag tests re-loaded every time = pointer to volatile (gl_func_00060DC4 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

A cascade `if (f->flags & 4) call(); if (f->flags & 8) call(); ...` where the target re-loads
`lw tN,16(v0)` into a NEW $t before every test, including tests with no call in between, and fills
the `beqzl` delay slots with the next test's load. The build kept the word in $v1 and tested it
with successive `andi`s. Declaring the flag object `volatile int *v0` (re-assigned from
`self->0x34` after each call as before) gives every load, the fresh temps, and the likely-branch
preloads. The function's first call was `jal; nop` with no argument setup and a0 still holding the
entry `self` (copied to s1). An explicit `self` argument emits `or a0,s1`, so the call is
`func()` with no arguments: K&R, and the callee just reads a0.

<a id="ixa-defeats-licm-xor-test-beq-order-52bbc"></a>
## 2-D array index keeps `row * 8` in the loop; `^ flag` flips the beq operands (gl_func_00052BBC -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

A leaf scans three u16 vertex indices of two directory rows per iteration. The old wrap was called a
"LICM-placement + eviction-order cap". Every flat spelling of `p68 + row * 8 + t0 + 2` (multi-def,
self-assign, `+= 0`, phantom `t0 * 0`, an array-IXA typedef, IDO 5.3) had `row1 * 8` / `row2 * 8`
hoisted to the preheader. The target recomputes them in the loop. Three changes fixed it:

1. Index the directory as a real 2-D array with the loop counter as the inner subscript:
   `((unsigned short (*)[4])a0[0x68 / 4])[row1][i + 1]`, with `i` running 0..2 (strength-reduced
   to the target's `t0 += 2`). The IXA keeps the `sll` in the loop, and the row2 -> s0 eviction
   follows from that. The index local has to be `int` (as `unsigned short` it took a3 and a second
   s-reg).
2. `v1 = -1; m[2] = m[3] = 0x7530;`: the target's `li t6; li t7; ...; sh t7,lo; sh t6,hi`. Two
   separate statements on one line give the same result, the same-line form of
   #same-line-registration-schedule-23e4.
3. The tests: `(m[0] >= m[2]) != flagX` always emits `beq a3,t4` (flag first) in either operand
   order, and `==`/else and `&&` spellings do too. Writing the condition as `(m[0] >= m[2]) ^ flagX`
   (or `- flagX`) emits `beq t4,a3` with the compare result first, and that fixes the later $t ring.

<a id="goto-skip-param-reload-5ad54"></a>
## Param reloaded twice around a `beqz` = goto-skip test; m2c comma-temps cost frame slots (gl_func_0005AD54 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

A 0x210 constructor (six list-head sub-ctors, a nested 4-byte cell, then `arg0[2] = arg2;
if (arg2) arg0[0] = alloc(arg2 * 8 + 8);`). The m2c-style wrap scored 97.27 with two faults:

1. **Frame 0x50 vs 0x20.** The wrap spelled each arm `(var != 0) || (sp1C = var, t = alloc(n,
   var), v = t, t != 0)`. The comma temps (and a stray extra `var` arg) each kept a stack home.

Callee `gl_func_00034458` is in this unit, so the C calls the blank alias
`gl_func_00034458_5AD54` (= 0) to keep the ROM's `jal 0` words.

<a id="hidden-arg-register-base-a88"></a>
## Address temp colored into an UNUSED-looking arg register = it IS a call argument (h2hproc_uso_func_00000A88 99.66 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

The wrap had 69/73 words exact. The residual four words were a paired-table load group:
target `lui a2,0; addiu a2,a2,0; lw v0,368(a2); lw v1,372(a2); or a0,s0,zero; sltu ...` then
`jal gl; addu a1,v0,at` (a two-argument call as written). Every spelling put the base in a0
(the first free arg register after v0/v1): signedness, typed void calls, struct/array/pointer
bases, comma/ternary forms, IDO 5.3 and 7.1, and 1,347 permuter trials.

The register was the clue. a2 is never otherwise written before that call, and IDO colors an
expression temp into a specific argument register when the value is passed in that register.
The call takes a third argument, and it is the table base itself:

```c
min = A88_diffpair[0x170 / 4];
tmp = A88_diffpair[0x174 / 4];
if ((unsigned)tmp < min) min = (unsigned)tmp;
gl_func_00000000(s0, min + 0x26000F, A88_diffpair);   /* a2 = &table, also the lw base */
```

uopt CSEs the `&A88_diffpair` argument with the load base, so it materializes once, straight
into a2, and the `lw`s use it. Nothing marks the argument in the asm: no separate `move a2`
appears. **Rule: when a lui/addiu base temp sits in aN while lower arg registers are free and
the next call "only" takes fewer args, try passing that base as argument N.** It works for K&R
callees (`gl_func_00000000()`), where extra arguments cost nothing in the prototype.

<a id="if1-bbs-uncolor-shared-name-4244"></a>
## One name for every unit + `if (1) {}` BBs = the "shared 0x38 spill slot"; hoisted-address .loc join (gl_func_00004244 2413/2479 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

gl_func_00004244 is a 9916-byte initializer with 32 unrolled units. Each unit does `p = base + off;
if (p != 0 || (p = alloc(0x24)) != 0) { ctor(p, ...); p->... = ...; }`. In the target, units 2..32
all save p with `sw a0,0x38(sp)` before the ctor call and reload it with `lw a0,0x38(sp)` after.
The old notes called this a cap ("anonymous spilltemp region sharing, named homes never repack").
It is not a cap, and the slot is a named home:

- **Distinct names never share a home.** One name per unit, or block-scoped names, gives one slot
  per name. The old wrap paired units onto 14 names and got 14 slots (0x90..0xC0).
- **One name covering every unit gets colored to s3** once it spans about 26 units. On this
  function, 22 units sharing a name stayed uncolored and 26 colored s3. An uncolored name has a
  memory home and ugen caches it in a0 inside each BB, which is exactly the target's sw/lw pair.
- **An empty `if (1) {}` right after the ctor call adds a BB without adding code.** That lowers the
  name's priority, so it stays uncolored across all 31 units. Here 18 to 30 of the units needed the
  `if (1) {}`. Adding all 31, or adding one anywhere in unit 1, swapped the s1/s2 coloring of
  `&sp78` / `&sp54`. A goto/label pair instead of `if (1) {}` is folded and does nothing.
- **The home offset follows declaration order.** Declared last, the name lands at 0x38 under the
  six declared-but-colored scalars. The unused old names (`var_a0_4..30`) have to stay declared:
  deleting them moves the frame map (1802/2479 words).

Same function, separate fix: the prologue's `move s0,a0` hoist (6 words) was the param-vs-copy
lever (#prologue-move-param-vs-copy-62368). Drop `var_s0 = arg0`, reassign `arg0` from the alloc,
and keep `char *var_s0;` declared, unused, so the frame doesn't move.

The last 2 words: `li at,-8` (unit 1's null test) and `addiu s2,sp,84` (the hoisted `&sp54`)
came out in swapped order. All 120 orders of unit 1's five pre-test statements, single same-line
joins, four test spellings, and `if (1) {}` at every unit-1 line left it unchanged. The `cc -S`
listing shows why. uopt hoists the colored address CSEs (`addu $17,sp,120; addu $18,sp,84`) to the
top of unit 1's BB, and they inherit the `.loc` of the LAST statement before that BB (the previous
if-arm's `*(var_v1 + 4) = 0;`). as1 schedules `li at,-8` (`.loc` of the `if` line) ahead of
`addiu s2` only when both carry the SAME line. So the fix is to join everything from that
`*(var_v1 + 4) = 0;` through unit 1's `if (...) {` onto ONE source line. Joining any shorter range
does nothing. Reading the hoisted instructions' `.loc` in `cc -S` tells you which lines to join.

The same recipe made gl_func_00001C54 exact (16 struct-by-value ctor stages, "sibling-scope
slot-sharing cap", 85% -> EXACT). Its per-block `{ char *m; struct SB1C54 t; ... }` pairs became ONE
function-scope `char *m; struct SB1C54 t;` declared last (homes 0x88/0x84), with `if (1) {}` after
all 16 ctor calls. Without the `if (1)`s the shared `&t` is CSE'd into an s-reg (the memcpy-form
copy the old note saw), and with 8 of them the result is still wrong (s1 = &t). All 16 make both m and `&t`
plain homes. The last 2 words were a lui pair, fixed by a same-line join
(`u15.v = G; srcC0[2] = F;`).

General rule: when a cap note says "target shares one spill slot across N disjoint webs", try ONE
name declared at the right decl position and then tune the name's priority with empty BBs. Don't
assume the slot is an anonymous temploc.

<a id="m2c-graft-frame-collapse-90cc"></a>
## Collapsing an m2c graft's frame: slot gaps tell you how many locals the original had (bootup func_000090CC 94.23 -> 95.26 NM, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

The 2106-insn constructor wrap had a 0x2D8 frame against the target's 0x178, so every sp-relative
word was off. Two IDO facts explain it. First, every declared local gets a frame word, top-down in
declaration order. That includes locals that live in registers and locals that are never used.
Second, a spilled named local is stored in its own slot. Use them as a recipe:

1. **Histogram the sp offsets** in the target and the build (`sw/lw/lwc1 ...,N(sp)` use counts). m2c
   names stack locals by target offset (`sp108`, `sp80`), which anchors the map.
2. **High-use target slots are spill homes of real variables.** Target 264 (24 uses) and 128 (56 uses)
   were the per-cascade element pointers. m2c had split them into 41 `var_a0_N` copies, each with its
   own slot. Renaming each `var_a0_N` to the `spXX` it was copied into (and deleting the copy)
   restores the single home. A 2-use slot at the very top (372) was the flag variable (`sp174 =
   var_t2`), and a 2-use slot near the bottom (88) was the loop counter (`sp58 = var_a1`). Make
   `sp174` / `sp58` the variables themselves. While they stay separate, the build spills the copy
   source into an extra slot at the bottom.
3. **Gaps between the used target slots are register-only locals.** Count them (here 4 above sp144,
   3 below sp118 with var_a2's 8-use home on top, 2 between sp8C and sp80, 5 above wpos, 5 below
   sp58). Reorder the declarations so the remaining temps fill exactly those gaps. Delete unused
   decls, hoist block-scoped temps (block scopes do NOT share slots), and merge temps only when
   their live ranges are provably disjoint. A merge that "helped" by overwriting a live value
   (var_t1 into var_t2) was wrong code; read every merge.

After this every sp word matched (1210 -> 1490 exact words), but objdiff's fuzzy % moved only about
+0.4 for it. objdiff gives an arg-mismatch most of an instruction's credit, so the score is driven
by insert/delete/replace. The other +0.6 came from structural fixes: self as the reassigned param
(`move s2,a0` inside the saves, #prologue-move-param-vs-copy-62368) and per-site symbols for the
lui/addiu-addressed rgb tables.

**Same pass on gl_func_0002E354 (70.78 -> 73.94, 2026-10-16 agent-c).** Merging every disjoint
same-type temp at once LOWERED the score (68.6), because each merge changes a uopt candidate's
live range and therefore its colour. Merging greedily, one pair at a time, and keeping a merge
only when the objdiff score does not drop gave +1.2. Disjointness was checked by line interval,
which is only safe with no loops or backward gotos, and the first occurrence has to be a plain
assignment. The bigger gains were two call decodes. A vararg `f(float, ...)` call with two extra
invented args double-promoted a float into a2/a3, where the target passes 3 args. And a
`lw a3,120(sp)` feeding a call is a single float passed in an INTEGER register, which only a
prototyped `(s32, s32, s32, f32, ...)` callee does. The K&R spelling emits `cvt.d.s` + `sdc1
16(sp)` and pushes the later args to 24/28(sp). Check every `cvt.d.s` before a jal against the
target.

<a id="same-line-store-pair-and-scratch-decl-order-c48c"></a>
## Store-pair order by same-line join + scratch-struct decl order (game_uso_func_0000C48C 99.7 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-g)

game_uso_func_0000C48C (3448 B) is a 32-stage constructor of the same family as
gl_func_00004244 and timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118. Each stage looks like
`u.v = G; t = u; obj = s1 + off; if (s1 != -off || (obj = alloc(0x18)) != 0) { ctor(obj, s1, t, 1);
obj[0xC/4] = tmpl; obj[0x10/4] = K; obj[0x14/4] = 0; }`. Two residual classes, both
source-steerable:

1. **`sw K,16(a0)` before `sw tmpl,12(a0)`.** The C writes 0xC first, and the target emits the
   0x10 store first, in every stage with an integer 0x10 field (12 of them). Put the two
   statements on ONE source line: `obj[0xC / 4] = tmpl; obj[0x10 / 4] = K;`. as1 then
   schedules the li-constant store first. This is the same as1 line tie-break as the 4244 lui
   pairs and the C3E8 brace-return. timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118 has the same shape:
   `FW(p, 0xC) = ...; FW(p, 0x10) = K;` joined on 13 stages gave +26 words there.
2. **Frame map.** The target has the per-stage scratch slots at the top (0xC0 downward) and the
   shared struct `t` (held in s2 as `&t`) at the bottom, 0x2C. Block-scoped `struct { int v; } u;`
   in each stage put the scratch slots BELOW the function-scope `t`. Declaring them as
   function-scope `u1..u32` BEFORE `t` flips that. The remaining offsets came from declaration
   position. One pointer (`s1`) declared above `u1` puts u1 at frame-8. `v1, obj` plus a
   `volatile int pd[3]` between `u32` and `t` reproduce the target's 5-word gap and the 0xC8
   frame. Probe the layout by watching `addiu sp`, the first stage's `addiu tN,sp,X`, and
   `addiu s2,sp,Y` while you move the declarations.

**kernel func_80000D2C (frame 0x98 vs 0x90).** The best C (draft

<a id="gbi-loader-dispatch-order-578b4"></a>
## GBI texture loader dispatch order, MIN shape, and reassociated OR chains (gl_func_000578B4, agent-g 2026-10-16)

**gl_func_000578B4 (post0b, 9676 B, NM 96.37).** The function is two copies of a
gDPLoadTextureBlock/Tile-style builder (FD SetTextureImage, F5 SetTile, E6 LoadSync,
F4/F3 LoadTile/LoadBlock, E7 PipeSync, F5 SetTile, F2 SetTileSize) selected by the
format code at `arg1+0x24`. Findings:

1. **Dispatch order.** Both target ladders test `0x120, 0x110, 0x408, 0x308, 0x304,
   0x508`, which is the source order of the arms. A `switch` always tests in ascending
   order (the build had `0x110, 0x120, 0x304, ...`). Per
   [#unsorted-dispatch-if-goto-plus-switch-54aec](#unsorted-dispatch-if-goto-plus-switch-54aec):
   `if (v == 0x120) goto A; if (v == 0x110) goto B; if (v == 0x408) goto C;
   if (v == 0x308) goto D; switch (v) { case 0x304: goto E; case 0x508: goto F;
   default: goto G; }` with the labelled arm bodies in that order. Both ladders then
   match (the second ends `beql 0x508` with the arm's first word in the delay slot).
   The fuzzy score barely moves (+0.02): the arm bodies already lined up.
2. **MIN for the LoadBlock lrs.** The target has `beqz at,L; nop; b L; or t1,a0,zero`.
   Both branches go to the same label, so this is an if/else whose else arm
   (`t1 = 0x7FF`) was hoisted out. `if (x < 0x7FF) { t = x; }` with no else emits only
   `beqz; nop; or`. A ternary or an explicit else reproduces the target, but t0/t1 then
   swap in every arm (the pkt pointer has to take t0 and spill to its m2c `spF0` home
   while the MAX result takes t0). Net 95.93, so the change was not kept.
3. **SetTile word 1.** m2c wrote `(... | maskt) + (shiftt << 10)) | cms | masks) + shifts`.
   The target uses `or` at every step, in field order. Writing `|` everywhere (or
   `_SHIFTL` with u32 casts) lets uopt reassociate the chain and move `shifts` up front,
   which costs about 3 points. `+` keeps the textual order with the wrong opcode. How the
   original kept an all-`|` chain in source order is still unknown.
4. The recurring arm residual is a t0/t1 swap: the target puts the call-crossing first
   pkt in t1 and the next pkt in t0. The build does the reverse.

Drafts: `/home/danjs/decomp-drafts/gl_func_000578B4_96.39_ifgoto_ladder.patch`,
`..._95.93_ladder_min_ternary.patch`.

**timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118 (99.02 draft), more negatives.** In case 0 the target
loads `arg0` once into v0, so the arg0 split piece is coloured there. None of these
changed that piece: a block-scoped `char *p = arg0`, `register` or `int *` copies,
copies into existing pointer locals (temp_v0/spA8/temp_t0/sp74/sp28), an index temp
read first, the D-store first, chained float stores, int zero stores, a label or
`if (1)` around the call or body, and a `u32` index. Every copy is copy-propagated
back to arg0. A new block-scoped local still costs +8 frame. Block 1 (0.5 materialized
before 1.0, with 1.0 still in f0) did not respond to dead `0.5f`/`1.0f` stores
(function top or just before the block), chaining either constant, moving the 0.5 or
0.0 group, or `0.45f * 1.0f`. Spelling the block-1 1.0 as `1`/`1.0`/`(f32)1.0`
detaches it from the shared 1.0 web, so the next stage loses its pre-`beqz` 1.0 load.
Joining the arg-field stores on one line (0x3BC/0x41C/0x3C8/0x3B8) left the
`sw a1,968` order unchanged.

<a id="if1-keeps-goto-target-out-of-line-d900"></a>
## `if (1) {}` in a goto target keeps the `beq`; sparse unsorted dispatch = source-order if-goto chain (bootup func_0000D900 57.1 -> 87.0 NM, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

Probe (IDO 7.1 -O2): `if (v == 7) goto c7; if (v == 6) goto c6; <default>; goto end; c7: a[1] = 26;
a[0] = 25; t = k | 1; goto end; c6: ...`. IDO emits `bne v,7 -> X; <c7 body inline>; b end; X: ...`,
whatever the source order of the labelled blocks and whatever spelling of the test (switch with one
case, `if (v != 7) goto n7; goto c7;`, `else if`). It inverts the test and pulls the target block
inline whenever that block is a single call-free basic block. Two things stop it:

- a call inside the target block (the block is then two BBs), or
- an empty `if (1) {}` anywhere in the target block (`c7: if (1) {} a[1] = 26; ...`).

Either way the test stays `beq v,7 -> c7` with the body out of line, in source order. In
func_000090CC this gave the target's `beq t3,7; beq t3,6; <default inline>; c7; c6` dispatch (the
earlier notes called it a switch-order cap). It is worth trying before concluding a compare chain
is a switch.

func_0000D900 is the bigger case. The target tests 20, 9, 6, 1000, 1001, 1003, 1002, 1004, 1005, 1006,
1007 (unsorted, sparse) with every body out of line and default last. The m2c switch built a
1000..1007 jump table instead (build `sltiu; jr t6`, target `jr` only for the return). Written as
`if (v == 0x14) goto c14; ... if (v == 0x3EE) goto c3ED; if (v != 0x3EF) goto cdef; goto c3ED;`
(last test inverted as in #unsorted-dispatch-if-goto-plus-switch-54aec), with `if (1) {}` in the two
one-store bodies (`A54 = 4`, `A54 = 5`), the chain, the delay-slot constant loads and the body order
all line up. The same pass fixed calls that take one argument where m2c had added `a1 = self`,
replaced 0x8B38-style literals with data aliases of func_00008AEC / func_00008B44 + K, and
replaced word-cast copies carrying an `(f32)` conversion with Vec3 struct copies (target
base-register lw/sw pairs). Together these were +30 points.

<a id="const-candidate-vs-reused-local-90cc"></a>
## Constant candidate in s0 vs a reused local (bootup func_000090CC, 2026-10-16 agent-c)

The target materializes `li s0,2` at the first use on each path (`bne a3,s0` for `arg1 == 2`, later
`beql s0,t7` for `D->0x34 == 2` and `sh s0,0x88E(s2)`) and keeps it in s0 across a `jal`. That is a
uopt constant candidate: three register-operand uses of the same constant, live across a call. The
build kept every use as `li at,2` / `li t6,2` because a named local took s0 first. The m2c graft
reused `var_t1` (the dispatch flag word, a short t-register value in the target) for
`d44.f28 + 0x70` after the draw calls. One variable is one candidate, so the late call-crossing
use pulled the whole web into s0. Splitting the late use into another declared-but-otherwise-unused
local frees s0. The constant 2 then colours s0 exactly as in the target. arg1 still lost its
register in that probe, so the split is not in the committed wrap, but the mechanism is general:
when the target holds a small constant in an s-register, look for a local whose web is joined
across calls by an unrelated later reuse.


## Comma constant on the RIGHT; literal spelling splits a shared FP constant (game_libs_func_0001F6A8 95.56 -> EXACT, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="comma-right-operand-literal-spelling-split-1f6a8"></a>

Target: a 256-entry f32 table fill, every entry `(D->0x2054 * 256) / divisor`, with `mul.s d,$f0,$fK` (the 256.0 in f0 first) twelve times,
then loop 2 `60 + x * 4` with 4.0 in f12 and 60.0 in f2, and loop 3 `480 + x * 60` re-materialising 60.0 into f12 and putting 480.0 in f2.

- Operand rank (#comma-constant-const-first-mul-5d754): `256.0f * K`, `K * 256.0f`, `(f32)256 * K`, a `f32 c = 256.0f` local, even a float
  PARAM `c * K` all emit load-first. `(0, 256.0f) * K` ALSO stays load-first; only `K * (0, 256.0f)` (comma expression as the right operand)
  gives const-first. Try both sides.
- One literal text = one constant candidate for the whole function. With `60.0f` in both loops, uopt keeps 60.0 in f2 from loop 2 into loop 3
  and gives 480.0 f12 (8 f2/f12 diffs per unrolled body). Writing loop 2 as `(f32)60 + ...` (or loop 3 as `* (f32)60`) makes two
  candidates: loop 3 re-materialises 60.0 and every register matched. Note the doc rule that `1.0f` spellings "all unify" was about one
  straight-line block; across loops the split works.

Boundary: the `.s` started with three all-zero pad words (entry 0x1F6B4); same recipe as 295BC (all-zero SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE on the
NM-wrapped INCLUDE_ASM predecessor gl_func_0001F3C8 in both builds + `elf-symtab-edit.py` on expected/). The INCLUDE_ASM predecessor works
as a host: the suffix lands after its asm block in the real build and after its C in the NM build (its NM % dips 0.2 for the longer symbol).


## Struct-by-value arg, `z + (y + x)` dot order, inline payload pointer shifts the t-ring (bootup func_0000D900 87.02 -> 99.08, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="struct-by-value-arg-dot-order-ring-d900"></a>

- Tell for a by-value struct argument: `lw a1,0(tN); sw a1,0x8C(sp); jal; sw a1,4(sp)` -- the callee arg is also stored into the
  OUTGOING arg area at 4(sp). m2c writes it as an int temp. Declare `typedef struct { s32 w; } S4;` and pass the struct to the K&R
  callee. `sp8C = *sp84` (whole-struct copy) emits `addiu v0,sp,0x8C; sw a1,0(v0)`; `sp8C.w = sp84->w` emits the target's direct
  `sw a1,0x8C(sp)`.
- A 3-term dot product written `x*a + y*b + z*c` evaluates z first (R-first rule, #2-term FP sums). The target `(x+y)+z` with x's loads
  first came from `z + (y + x)`; assigning it to a named f32 temp first gives the f0 result the target uses. Both dot products in
  the function needed the same spelling.
- Frame map: with Vec3 locals in the frame, EVERY declared local (scalars included, even register-allocated ones) gets a slot, top-down
  in declaration order. Gaps in the target frame are unused locals: two 12-byte gaps were unused Vec3s, and a 4-byte gap between
  two struct locals was a scalar declared between them. Merging m2c's duplicate pointer temp (temp_t1 == temp_v0_2) removed one slot.
- One case block read its payload pointer into a named local (target used a t-register for it). Reading it inline
  (`*(Vec3 *)(*(s32 *)(arg1 + 4) + 0xE0)`) moved every t-register in the function (dispatch constants included) up by one to the
  target ring. 160 -> 48 diffs from that one change.
- `v.x *= 4.0f` (in place on the struct copy) vs a named product: the named product took f2/f12 and pushed the 4.0/0.0 constants
  out of f0/f2.
Residual (34 words): a `s = clamp(s, 0, 50)` ternary colours s in f0 and 0.0 in f2 with the copy at the join; the target copies at
the entry (t in f0) and keeps 0.0 in f12. Ternary, if/else, copy-first, `register`, `if (1) {}` and comma spellings all colour the same.

## Copy-then-bump stores, goto loops against re-unrolling, stride variable (bootup func_000077D0 0 -> 99.75, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="copy-then-bump-store-goto-loop-stride-var-77d0"></a>

Glyph blitter: three modes, each a 32 x 16 loop of four u16 copies. The m2c body (s32 types, hand-copied unroll) scored 0.

- Store shape `or v0,a1,zero; addiu a1,a1,2; sh tN,0(v0)` (and `or v1,a0,zero; lhu tN,0(v1); addiu a0,a0,2` for a
  source pointer) comes from an explicit copy: `t = dst; dst++; *t = v;`. Every `*dst++ = v` spelling (cast lvalue,
  `dst[k]`) is strength-reduced to one `addiu a1,a1,8` and `sh -8/-6/-4/-2(a1)`.
- `for` / `do` loops with that body are unrolled x4 by IDO (16 stores per trip). Write the loops with labels:
  `j = 0; l0: ...; j += 4; if (j != 0x40) goto l0;`. When such a loop is the then-arm of an if/else, IDO inverts
  it (`beq exit; b top` with the first insn duplicated in the delay slot); `if (j == 0x40) goto next; goto l0;`
  with `next:` after the else restores the bottom `bne`.
- `tbl + c * 0x140` folds to `multu c,640`. The target `multu c,t1(320); sll 1` needs `stride = 0x140;` as a
  variable. `g = tbl; g += c * stride;` emits `addu v1,tbl,off` (target order); `tbl + c * stride` emits off first.
- Mode test order 0, 2, 1 with every body out of line: `if (mode == 0) goto m0; if (mode == 2) goto m2;
  if (mode != 1) return; goto m1;` (a switch tests 0, 1, 2).
- The call in the mode-1 loop: target keeps the loop bounds 64/32 in s0/s1 and spills dst (own home, `sw a1,76(sp)`
  in the bnel delay) and the counter (`sw a3,32(sp)`) around the call. `if (1) {}` before the loop and after the
  call gave that split; without them dst/counter/64.0f took s-regs and f20.
- Separate counters per loop (a fresh var for the else-arm zero loop, for the mode-2 outer loop and for the mode-1
  inner loop) each moved the score; the target reuses registers across modes, not variables.
- No address-taken locals, yet the frame tracked the declaration list (an unused local moved the call spill slot
  by 4); `s32 pad[5]` first gives frame 0x48 with the spill at 32(sp).
Residual (8 words): tbl and the stride swap t0/t1. Statement order, `while (0)`, `register`, a loaded (non-constant)
stride, stride set per branch: no change.

**EXACT 2026-10-17 (agent-c).** uoptlist: the 320 constant candidate and tbl are both constrained; the constant had the
higher adjsave and took t0. A dead `if (tbl) {}` as the FIRST statement of the mode-0 outer `do` loop (zero emission)
adds loop-frequency-weighted refs to tbl, so tbl colours first and takes t0. The same `if` before the mode dispatch
(outside any loop) changed nothing; inside the mode-0 copy loop tail or before `g += 0x280` in mode 2 it also worked.
Lesson: when a pointer loses a t-reg to a CONSTANT candidate, boost the pointer inside a loop it is live through.
Unwrap gotcha: the default (non-NM) build failed the ROM cmp after the C was exact in the NM build, because the
float-returning callee prototype `extern float func_411c_rf(void);` sat inside ANOTHER function's `#ifdef NON_MATCHING`
block. Without it the default build sees an implicit `int` callee (`mtc1 v0` + `cvt.s.w`, function grows 8 bytes and
everything after shifts). Before unwrapping, grep every extern the body uses and make sure its declaration is outside
any NM block.


## The D900 Vec3-copy kit on a sibling + pointer assigned before the if (bootup func_0000B520 36.9 -> 99.34, 2026-10-16 agent-c) <a name="d900-kit-b520"></a>

Sibling of func_0000D900 (scaled direction vector -> v50 -> v5C -> v74 struct copies -> added to the velocity). The
#struct-by-value-arg-dot-order-ring-d900 recipe applied directly: named products (f0/f12/f14), Vec3 copies instead of m2c's
int structs with casts, decl-order frame (an unused Vec3 between v74 and v5C, `s32 pad[3]` below v50), and the K&R call
without the stale f12/f14 "args" m2c read.
- The target forms `q = arg0 + 0x3C8` in the delay slot of the last branch before the join AND on the fall-through path, then
  reads `0/4/8(v0)`. Writing `q = arg0 + 0x3C8;` at its use folds into `lwc1 968(a1)`; assigning it at the top of the
  function (before the ifs) gives the target placement.
- `if (p->flags & 4) ...; if (p->flags & 8) ...` with only an `add.s` between: the target loads the word twice (`beqzl ...;
  lw t0,16(v0)` in the delay slot and again on the other path). A `*(volatile int *)` read for the second test does that.
- A limit read once into a named f32 and used in `lim < d` / `d < -lim` coloured lim/d f0/f12 swapped; reading the extern
  at both uses (IDO CSEs it into one `lwc1`) gave the target colours.
Residual: `s = 0.0f; s += 10.0f;` colours the 0.0 constant f2 and s f0 (target the reverse), as in D900's clamp.

**EXACT 2026-10-17 (agent-c).** The target uses ONE variable for the step magnitude `s` and the later target value
`t = self->0x768` (both f2 in the target). With `s` folded into `t` (`t = 0.0f; t += 10.0f; ... px = q[0] * t;`), the
merged variable's priority/interference changes so the 0.0 constant takes f0 and the variable f2: the f0/f2 swap was
gone in one edit (the now-unused `s` declaration stays to keep the frame). A second residual, the v5C copy base in v1
(target v0, the register q just used), went away with `if (1) {}` right before the `v50.x = px; ...` stores: the
block split ends q's live unit before the copy base starts, so they share v0.
Tell for the merge: two values of the same type in the target hold the SAME register in disjoint stretches of the
function and nothing forces it. Try one variable for both before any priority lever.
Pool reads: `lui at,%hi(func_00008124+0x48); lwc1 %lo(...)(at)` in the target. bootup_uso is LINKED, so ROM bytes
carry the resolved address (lui 1 / lo 0x816C), not the bare addend. Pin each scalar extern to the real address with a
linker expression in undefined_syms_auto.txt (`bu_b520_k48 = func_00008124 + 0x48;`); a pin to the bare addend
(`= 0x48`) fails cmp. objdiff scores the pinned function 100. undefined_syms_auto.txt is NOT a make dependency of the

the target stores and reloads (66 -> 78). The 3-term dot products and the length sum as `z + (y + x)` -> 91.6

## post0b decoder / emitter kit: default-arg selector, shared cursor/value var, struct-copy ring burns, volatile param, OR-chain order (agent-g 2026-10-16) <a name="post0b-decoder-kit-51ad8"></a>

From gl_func_00051AD8 (12-case jumptable decoder, NM 0 -> 99.15, standalone 240/240 words but one delay slot),
game_libs_func_0005721C (fog emitter, 0 -> 95.9), gl_func_000510F0 (30.3 -> EXACT) and gl_func_000561A8 (36.9 -> EXACT):

- **Switch selector in the default call.** `switch (s->op) { ... default: f(msg, op); }` with `op = s->op` as a plain
  statement (or `switch (op)`) makes uopt spill the selector (`sw t6,28(sp)` in the bound-check `beqz` delay, reload in the
  default). The direct arg wants the a1 colour, which the incoming s param still holds at the def. Writing the
  assignment INSIDE the call, `f(msg, op = s->op)`, keeps the selector in v0 and puts `or a1,v0` in the jal delay
  (a separate `op = s->op;` statement before the call also avoids the spill, but as1 then steals `or a1,v0` into the
  `beqz` delay).
- **One variable for cursor and value.** The target kept the stream cursor in a1 in most arms and in v0 only where the
  read value took a1. That happens when ONE pointer variable is both the cursor (`q = s->cur; s->cur = q + 1; x = *q;`)
  and, in the arms that keep the value, the value itself (`p = s->cur; s->cur = p + 1; q = (s32 *)*p;`). The value web
  passed as a call's 2nd arg in one arm gives the whole variable an a1 preference. A greedy per-arm search over
  (cursor, value) names got 80 -> 90.
- **Struct copies re-phase the temp ring.** `out->m = *(Pair *)(r + 1)` instead of two field stores fixed a t1/t9 order;
  a 1-word struct field copied by struct assignment burns the t5 ring slot (next load lands in t6, as in the target).
  A byte spilled across a call to a WORD-ALIGNED slot (`sb v0,40(sp)`) is a `u8 hi[1]` array; a `u8` scalar sits at
  slot+3.
- **Unused locals take frame slots at -O2** (pointer and scalar locals too), so the decl list sets the frame and
  every spill slot. Adding or deleting an unused declaration shifts everything by 4/8.
- **`volatile` parameter = reload from the home slot.** 510F0 passes its 2nd param to the call with `lw a0,220(sp)`
  instead of `or a0,a1`. Plain, `char *`, K&R and `(&arg0)[1]` spellings all give the move; `volatile s32 arg1` gives
  the home reload and the function goes EXACT.
- **Pointer-add deref for base-first addu.** `(o->tri + idx)->a` numbers the uv/pos base t6 and emits `addu v0,base,idx`;
  `o->tri[idx].a` and char arithmetic give index-first. One `char *q` for all six corner pointers keeps idx*8 in v1.
- **OR-chain evaluation order.** IDO evaluates the LAST operand of `a | b | c | d` first, then a, b, c. To load
  c[0..3] in order (fog colour), write `c1 | c2 | c3 | c0`.
- **Unsorted lookup chain with a trailing default call** (561A8): an if-goto chain with shared labels for paired keys;
  for the default block to sit AFTER every return label, write the last test as `if (m != 9) goto dflt; goto c9;`.
- **Open residuals.** 51AD8: as1 steals the default arm's first `lui a0` into the bound-check `beqz` delay (rule 2,
  exclusive target); the target keeps `sll t6` there, as if the default block had a second predecessor. Default
  position, gotos, wrappers, callee prototypes, -g3 and IDO 5.3 don't change it. A switch with a HOLE (one value
  mapped to default) does keep `sll`, but this table has no hole. 5721C: the target materializes 255.0f at
  function entry; a named/register k, block boundaries and literal spellings don't move it.

## 4x4 matrix family = the natural triple loop (gl_func_0005E288 + four siblings EXACT, agent-g 2026-10-17) <a name="matrix-triple-loop-family-5e288"></a>

The post0b matrix region (0x5E288..0x5EF00) is written as plain `f32 m[4][4]` triple loops. Earlier NM bodies
re-created IDO's output with pointer walkers and manual unrolling (65-72%); the natural form is exact once these
are set:

- `for (i..4) for (j..4) { r[i][j] = 0.0f; for (k..4) r[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j]; }`. IDO unrolls the inner sum
  (by 4, or pipelines a 3-trip loop) and turns the indexes into pointer compares.
- Which shape the column loop takes depends on what the sources are. If a source is a pointer PARAMETER, the
  column loop comes out software-pipelined: a `beql`/`bnel` rotation, with the row element loads repeated every
  iteration. If both sources are LOCAL arrays, uopt hoists the row loads (`lwc1 f0,0(a0)`, `f2,4(a0)`, ...) out
  of the column loop and rotates it. A target with per-iteration row loads and NO rotation is a local product read
  through a pointer alias: `d = Y; ... T[i][j] += d[i][k] * Z[k][j];`. One alias on either source is enough.
- Frame: every declared scalar gets its own 4-byte home in declaration order, even when it lives in a register or
  is never used (block-scoped declarations get separate homes, so they make it worse). Gaps between the matrices
  are therefore index or pad declarations. In 5E288 the 16 bytes between r1 and T are `s32 i, j, k, m;`, and the
  words below the last matrix are `d, a, e` (`e` unused, but it puts the spill temp at sp+76). Three of the
  siblings need 2-3 unused `s32 padN;` below R. A 3x3 product (5E718) still declares its result as `f32 r[4][4]`.
- Making the param live in a callee-saved register: with `void f(f32 (*a)[4])` it was homed and reloaded. A
  local copy `a = arg0;` colours s1 in 5E288 and s0 in 5EB4C. In 5E944 the copy `b = a` is what gives the target's
  caller-saved `or a3,a0` plus `sw a3,HOME(sp)` across the call. 5ED54 reads `a[axis]` before its first call and
  gets s0 without a copy.
- The index letters chosen for each loop move the colouring. The IV-eliminated `j` of the 5E288 product kept a
  live range in a2 that emits nothing, which pushed the row pointers to a3/t0. Loop 1 written rows i / cols k /
  sum j, and loop 3 written rows i / cols m / sum k, gave a2/a3. A search over the 3-letter permutations per loop
  found it in one pass.
- `angle / 2` (an int literal) keeps `div.s` by a materialised 2.0. `angle / 2.0f` folds to `* 0.5f`.
- An int table read in a counted loop (`tbl[m]`, m = 1..n-1) is strength-reduced to `&tbl[1]` plus a spilled end
  pointer only when `tbl` is a separate extern array (pinned in undefined_syms_auto.txt). Spelled as
  `((s32 *)((char *)&D_00000000 + K))[m]`, the offset folds into the `lw` immediate instead.
- Rotation-family callees take `(f32 (*)[4], s32 or Vec3 *, f32)`. They go through typed blank aliases pinned at 0
  (`gl_func_00000000_5e944` etc.), which give `mfc1 a2,$f6`. The K&R blank would promote the float to double.

Diagnostics that worked. `-Wo,-zdbug:6` still prints the coloring trace before uopt dies on the `wrapper_ecvt`
assertion, which this toolchain hits because the ecvt patch is not applied: "LR assigned (constrained) N", with
1=v0 2=v1 3=a0 4=a1 5=a2 6=a3 7=t0 and 14..21=s0..s7. `-Wo,-zdbug:1` or `:5` prints the itab, where
`{..} N isvar M 3 -OFF` maps LR N to the local whose home is at frame top minus OFF, and `P` marks a parameter.
Together they showed that a2 held the dead `j`.

Same pass, straight-line FP neighbours (all EXACT from the textbook formula, replacing m2c temp soups):
- gl_func_0005D9EC (axis-angle matrix, 63.1 -> 100): write `t = 1 - c; m[0][1] = t * x * y + s * z; ...` with x/y/z
  loaded into locals and let uopt find the CSEs (it homes t, t*x*z and s*y in frame temps on its own). The only lever
  was declaration order (`f32 t, x, y, z;`, so x is homed at sp+24).
- gl_func_0005D908 (70.2 -> 100): IDO loads the textually SECOND operand of `a * b` first. The target's src-first
  `lwc1` and `mul.s src, out` came from `out[i] = out[i] * src[j]`. A `src[j] * out[i]` spelling swaps every FP
  register. Its frame needed two unused `s32` declared above the `child` pointer.
- gl_func_0005D628 (77.0 -> 100): when the target loads both inputs ahead of two `div.s` and stores the quotients
  late, compute them into named locals first (`nx = -q->y / len; ny = q->x / len; a->x = nx; a->y = ny;`). Writing
  the stores directly re-loads after each store, because IDO assumes the store can alias. The later in-place `neg.s
  f12,f12` reuses the same locals (`nx = -a->x; ... a->x = nx;`). Writing `a->x = -a->x` picks fresh temps instead.

### as1: the bound-check delay fill is liveness through the jumptable (51AD8 open residual, measured)

`sltiu at,t,N; beqz at,DEFAULT` gets the default block's first insn stolen into its delay (rule 2) only if that
insn's destination is dead on the fall-through. For the fall-through, as1 follows the `.rdata` table: if ANY arm
reads the register before writing it, the steal is blocked and as1 fills the slot from the fall-through instead
(`sll t,t,2`, the target shape). Test: a 5-case switch whose arms store through `G[]`, with only the LAST arm
using the `o` param in a0. That one arm keeps `sll` in the delay; with no arm reading a0, `lui a0` is stolen. A
`goto` into the default from an arm also keeps `sll`, because the default is then shared. The 51AD8 target's arms
never read a0 or a1 before writing them in the final code, so whatever made a0 look live there is not visible in
the shipped bytes. Ruled out (each measured): return type, K&R definition, a block-local copy of `out` in arms
210/208, varargs or undefined-argument `.livereg` (every jal in the target sets a0 first), -O3, -g1/-g2, -mips1,
`-Wb,-O1`. Note that `cc -S` output re-assembled through as0/as1 is NOT faithful: the text form drops the binasm
reorg information. So probe as1 only through C.


## post0b dispatcher kit II: address-taken iterator, two-symbol global RMW, union field, jumptable holes (agent-c 2026-10-17) <a name="post0b-dispatcher-kit-2-40304"></a>

From four 0% post0b functions decoded to NM in one run (gl_func_00040304 99.82, gl_func_00040640 99.88,
gl_func_0003FC58 85.1, gl_func_000415A4 76.4; the first two are 8 and 5 words from exact, register colouring only).

- **Iterator kept in memory.** 40640 walks a list with a {cur, next} pair at 224/228(sp): the iterator body uses the
  just-loaded value from a temp (`sw t6,224; lw t7,4(t6); lw v0,0(t6)`) but every loop BB reloads `cur` from the
  stack. `volatile` on the pair gives the reloads but also reloads inside the iterator, and a `volatile` ARRAY promotes
  its base address to an s-register. Plain locals become register candidates. Address-taken scalars give exactly the
  target: forwarding inside one BB, reload across BBs. Use a dead `while (0) { LNode **pp; pp = &itc; pp = &itn; }`
  (zero emission) and write the step as `((itc = itn) != 0 ? (itn = itc->next, itc->data) : 0)`.
- **Global read-modify-write.** `G |= 4` (or `G = G | 4`) in one BB emits `lui v0; addiu v0; lw 0(v0); ...; sw 0(v0)`.
  The target's `lui t6; lw t6,0(t6); ...; lui at; sw t7,0(at)` comes back when the load and the store name DIFFERENT
  symbols (`W = R | 4`, both pinned to the same address; reloc-blind in game_libs) or when a call sits between them.
- **Float view of an int field.** `*(float *)&msg.p12` takes the address of the stack struct, and `&msg` then becomes a
  register candidate for the whole function (`addiu v1,sp,224` at entry, every `msg.x` read becomes `x(v1)`, the
  struct copy loop starts from v1). An `union { int i; float f; } p12;` member reads `lwc1 f6,236(sp)` directly.
- **Jumptable switches in post0b.** Default-mapped holes inside the table range (40304: 0x70/0x71) need explicit
  `case 0x70: case 0x71: default:` labels so the table is formed (4 real cases is below the 5-label threshold), and the
  hole keeps `sll` in the bound-check `beqz` delay (see #post0b-decoder-kit-51ad8). 40640's table starts at index 0
  with entry 0 = the tail and an extra `beqz` before the `sltiu`: `if (state != 0) { switch (state) { case 0: break;
  ... } }`. Rodata layout for the donor route: a memory-loaded float constant (never hoisted above stores, unlike a
  literal) is an extern pinned to its own RoData address; 40304's 0.01f sits BEFORE its table and 1/32767 after it.
- **Selector in a1.** 3FC58's compare chain tests `a1`; the default arm is `printf(fmt, msg.type)`, so the selector
  inherits the call-argument colour. Pass it in the default call.
- **Dead-$v0 poison again** (#dead-v0-poison-is-per-bb-split-the-defs-683d4): 40640's switch selector (v0, read after
  the head call) and its `o = global; o->vt->fn(...)` arms (o v1 / vtable v0) needed `if (1) {}` after the call and
  after `o = global`. 415A4: one `if (1) {}` after the first call made `self` reject to its 56(sp) home (the target
  reloads it per use); a second right before the first use gave the reload v0.
- **Dead `while (0)` FP anchors** order unconstrained FP candidates (40304: `while (0) { a = 0; b = 0; kt = 0;
  d = kt * K; }` moved a/b/kt to f0/f2/f12 like the target). The literal constant candidate always coloured LAST
  (f18) whatever the anchors; the target has it in f14.
- **Open:** (1) 3FC58: IDO places the call-free `case 7` / `case 8` blocks (AND / OR through a pointer) right after
  the compare chain with an inverted `bne`, whatever their source position or chain/switch grouping; the target keeps
  them in source order. (2) 40640: target colours the loop's first and third node loads a1 and the middle one v1;
  every variable split / bitpos anchor / dead-if boost probed gives v1/a1 swapped or all v1. (3) 415A4: the record
  block stores +0x28 twice (1030, then the separately ori'd value) through `lui at` while the other fields go through
  a v1 base; one symbol through a pointer + direct access merges into v1, two symbols reorder the stores.

## post0b quaternion/matrix textbook kit II (agent-g 2026-10-17) <a name="post0b-quat-matrix-textbook-kit-2"></a>

Five more post0b math functions went EXACT (0x5C000..0x5F000): gl_func_0005C284 (0 -> 100, 4x4 determinant),
5CE68 (96.8, slerp with spins), 5CCF4 (64.5, rotate vector by quaternion), 5DDE4 (56.4, quaternion -> matrix),
5EF00 (82.9, axis-align rotation matrix). In every case the old body was an m2c temp soup, and the fix was to write
the textbook formula and then apply one or two of the levers below.

- **Write the textbook source, not the m2c temps.** 5CE68 is Morrison's slerp from Graphics Gems III (`beta`,
  `theta`, `sin_t`, `cos_t`, `phi`, `bflip`, the float param `alpha` reused as the second scale). With NO
  x/y/z/w locals (a->x is read in the dot and again in the blend), uopt's CSE temps take exactly the frame homes the
  old body could not reach. 5DDE4 is Shoemake's Qt_ToMatrix (GG IV; the matrix -> quaternion half sits just above
  it). 5CCF4 is q * (v, 0) * conj(q) written as two Hamilton products with the v.w = 0 terms dropped (IDO does not
  fold `x * 0.0f`, so the source must leave them out). 5EF00 stores its 3x3 block column by column; that is the
  compute order, and the scattered store order is as1's.
- **`(f32)var` no-op cast = operand-order lever.** In a commutative FP op, cfe evaluates a plain float VARIABLE leaf
  after a deref (`v->x`), a negated deref, or an int->float conversion, whichever side it is written on: `c * -v->x`
  and `-v->x * c` both emit `mul.s fd, (-x), c`. When the target has the variable first (fs = var), write
  `(f32)c * -v->x` (`c + 0.0f` also works). Used 1x in 5EF00, 5x in 5CE68 (`(f32)beta * a->x`, `(f32)theta + ...`),
  1x in 5CCF4 (`(f32)tx * q->w`).
- **Constant rank.** `*(f32 *)((char *)&D_00000000 + 0x2040) * (f32)spin` evaluates the cast-deref constant first and
  rotates the whole FP temp ring by one register. A pinned extern (`extern f32 D_5CE68_pi;` with
  `D_5CE68_pi = 0x00002040;` in undefined_syms_auto.txt) ranks below the conversion, as in the target. The baked
  `lui at,0; lwc1 0x2040(at)` bytes are identical after the link.
- **One source line per matrix row (5C284).** The 16 element loads `m0 = M[0]; ...` were one statement per line;
  the target loads m7 before m6 (and m11 before m10) but colours m6 f0 / m7 f2. Every per-line assignment order
  gave either the load order or the colours, never both (a 120-variant pair-swap search found nothing, and the permuter
  only produced sp-offset false positives). Putting each row's four loads on ONE line (`m4 = M[4]; m5 = M[5]; m6 =
  M[6]; m7 = M[7];`) gives both. Same family as the same-line levers elsewhere in this file: the line number
  matters to uopt's ordering.
- **Copy temp declared LAST re-colours one web (5DDE4).** The target homes yz (frame 0x58) where the textbook source
  kept yz in a register (frame 0x50) and materialised 1.0f early. `t = q->y * s; ys = t;` (permuter find) fixes the
  colouring. The permuter declared `t` mid-list, which shifted xx..yz down 4, and its score ignores sp offsets, so it
  reported 0. Declaring `t` LAST puts its unused home on the target's empty slot (sp+32). Always raw-diff a permuter
  "0".
- **Homes are still declaration order** (5BE20 rule): 5C284 needs `float *M` declared FIRST (its unused home is the top
  word) and the column-wise m0, m4, m8, m12, m1, ... decl list; named cofactor temps a/b/c follow.

Tooling note: `scripts/disasm-func.py` printed a different function's code for gl_func_0005CCF4 and 0005DDE4 (frame
0x90/0x98 where the real functions have 0x38/0x58). Read targets from `expected/src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`
(`objdump -d --disassemble=FN`) or the `.s` file, not from disasm-func, for post0b.

## post0b cfront-inline kit III: iterator step form, Vec3 temporaries, param reloads, arg cursor (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 104) <a name="post0b-cfront-inline-kit-3"></a>

Several post0b functions are C++ (cfront) with inline member functions expanded in place. The shapes below
took 0%/stub wraps to 87-99% in one pass each.

**Inlined {cur,next} list iterator** (gl_func_00041A9C 0 -> 99.25, game_libs_func_0003DA14 0 -> 94.0,
gl_func_00049B3C). Target tell: `lw tA,K(list); sw tA,4(sp); beqz tA; sw tA,0(sp); lw tB,4(tA); sw tB,4(sp);
b join; lw v0,0(tA)` then a loop whose step repeats the same shape. Spelling:

```c
typedef struct L { char *data; struct L *next; } L;
typedef struct { L *cur; L *next; } I;
I it;
if (1) { I *q = &it; }            /* block-scoped, at function start: memory-resident, no extra code */
it.next = list;
while (((it.cur = it.next) != 0 ? (it.next = it.cur->next, it.cur->data) : 0) != 0) {
    use(it.cur->data);            /* body re-reads through it.cur, like the target */
}
```

- The address-taken iterator also pulled every OTHER candidate in 41A9C out of the s-regs. The target had
  an all-spill frame (no s-saves), and the build went from 3 s-regs to 0 (78 -> 98).
- An `if`/`v = 0` statement form of the step puts the result in an s-reg. The ternary keeps it in v0.
- When the target's init instance and loop-step instance use DIFFERENT temps (49B3C: init result in v0,
  step result in a0; list init in a1, step in v0), write the next-expression twice:
  `v = NEXT; while (v) { ...; v = NEXT; }`. One `while (NEXT)` gives one shared temp. In 49B3C that
  change and direct vtable fields together were worth 92.9 -> 95.3.
- The declaration placement of the iterator decides the frame slot. Function scope with the `if (1)`
  trick at the top matched 41A9C's layout. Declaring it in an inner block put it at the frame bottom.

**cfront `new` of a local object** (49B3C): `p = &local; if (p == 0) p = alloc(12); if (p) {...}` folds the
dead alloc away. Use `if ((unsigned)p == 0) { p = alloc(12); if (p == 0) goto skip; }` (see
#unsigned-cast-defeats-addr-nonnull-fold-5165c). Write the member stores through one named
`arr = (A *)(self + 132)` so `self + 132` is computed once, as in the target.

**Vec3 operator temporaries** (gl_func_0003B01C 18.2 -> 96.3). Target: six lwc1 (b.xyz, then a.zyx), three
sub.s, three swc1 to a temp, two whole-struct `lw/sw` copies to further temps, then a final copy done as
`lwc1/swc1`. Spelling: `dx = pb->x - pa->x; dy = ...; dz = ...; t.x = dx; t.y = dy; t.z = dz;`
(a ctor), then `t2 = t; t3 = t2;` as struct assignments, then `n.x = t3.x; n.y = t3.y; n.z = t3.z;`. The
final field-wise copy is what gives float loads/stores; a struct assignment there gives `lw/sw`
(53 -> 82). The ctor form for the subtraction is worth a further 82 -> 96.

**Stack params reloaded every iteration** (gl_func_00036A48 79.5 -> 87.8). Target: `lw t9,192(sp)` (the
arr param) and `lw t5,196(sp)` (n) inside the loop, with a byte offset in s0 instead of a walking pointer.
`if (1) { Vec3 **q = &arr; int *qq = &n; }` makes both params memory-resident. Same trick on a struct
local (`&v`) keeps otherwise-dead field stores (`swc1` of a result copy).

**Argument cursor, store before load** (gl_func_0004E96C 73.9 -> 99.5). Target per switch arm:
`lw v0,4(a1); addiu t,v0,4; sw t,4(a1); lw x,0(v0)`. `*c->args++` loads first and stores after.
`(p = c->args, c->args = p + 1, *p)` stores first, as in the target.

**float [0,1] -> 8-bit channel** (game_libs_func_00046DC0, game_libs_func_0004771C EXACT): the
`cfc1/ctc1` rounding-mode block with `lui at,0x4f00` around each `mul.s` by 255.0 is `(unsigned int)(c * 255.0f)`,
stored to u8 or u16 fields.

Open in this kit: 36A48's target copies the sret result from v0 into a separate temp before use (3 words
the build lacks). 3DA14's target re-reads `it.next` after storing `it.cur` in the step (the build forwards
it). 41A9C's loop uses t8/t9 where the build has v1/t7 (one extra temp in the target's first instance).

## post0b math kit III (agent-g 2026-10-17, run 103) <a name="post0b-math-kit-3-run103"></a>

Five more post0b math functions went EXACT, all from rewriting old NM bodies as the textbook routine:
game_libs_func_0005F534 (29.7, guPerspectiveF without the identity fill), 0005D474 (27.7, rotate a
quaternion by axis-angle), gl_func_0005EAA4 (59.0, Euler rotate x/y/z), game_libs_func_00062D70 (43.2,
s16 record to float unpack), game_libs_func_0005FC64 (0, 4x4 load from a float stream). Levers:

- **Unfolded multiply by 1.0 or 0.0.** cfe folds `1.0f * s`, `s * 1.0f`, `t = s; t *= 1.0f`, and even a
  float local set to 1.0f (uopt const-props it and folds the multiply). `s * (f32)1` survives, which gives
  the target's `lui at,0x3f80; mtc1; mul.s` (5D134). The same works for zero: `v *= (f32)0` keeps
  `mtc1 zero; mul.s`, while `v *= 0.0f` becomes a plain zero store (game_uso 8CD8).
- **Int literal divisor.** `x / 2` keeps `div.s` by a held 2.0; a float variable `two = 2.0f` is
  const-propagated and the first use turns into `* 0.5f` (8CD8; see also #matrix-triple-loop-family-5e288).
- **Colour a loaded constant last.** 62D70 loads a scale from RoData and multiplies four converted
  shorts by it. The target colours x, y, z, w f0/f2/f12/f14 and the scale f16; every spelling of the scale
  (pinned extern, cast-deref, pointer, named local, operand order) coloured it f2. A dead
  `while (0) { x = 0; y = 0; z = 0; w = 0; }` before the load gives x..w the earlier candidates. The "FP
  software-pipeline cap" in the old comment was only this colouring.
- **Call result order for a quotient.** guPerspectiveF's `cos(h) / sin(h)` as one expression divides
  first-call / second-call. The target divides second / first, which is `s = sin(h); cot = cos(h) / s;`.
  Declaration order `float cot, s;` then put the arg spill at sp+28.
- **The "bc1tl ceiling" was a K&R call.** 5EAA4 calls rotate(m, axis, angle, 0) three times. Through a
  prototyped `(f32 (*)[4], s32, f32, s32)` blank alias the body matched on the first compile, bc1tl and
  delay-slot reloads included.
- **Line layout again (5FC64).** `for (i..4) for (j..4) { p = a1++; a0[i][j] = *p; }` matches only with
  both `for` headers on one source line. On separate lines the final `a1 += 4` and row `+= 16` swap. The
  standalone compile matched with separate lines too, so confirm in the tree.
- **Frame homes for unused scalars (5D474).** The 0x50 frame needed seven scalar homes between the
  quaternion and the arg-spill temp: h, c, x, y, z plus two unused. Named products assigned on one line
  (`x = axis[0] * s; y = ...; z = ...;`) gave the loads-first order.

Open: 5C548 and 5D134 (quaternion axis helpers) home-store a0 and move q to another register in the
target (5C548) or keep it in a0 with &q[i]/&q[k] in a2/a1 (5D134); every spelling here either spills q to
its home or moves it. 5F0B8 (axis-angle matrix, 74.7) keeps the 0.0f store constant in callee-saved
$f22 and divides x first. 54144 (triangle centroid, 99.8) wants `addu v0,verts,idx*6`; every C spelling
of the vertex address emits the index product first.

Jumptables: IDO 7.1 and 5.3, at -O1 and -O2, lower a switch with 4 case labels (with or without default)
to a compare chain; 5 labels give a table. func_80001ADC's target dispatches 4 relocation types through a
4-entry table (`addiu t6,type,-1; sltiu at,t6,4`), so its source shape is still unknown.



## post0b kit IV: same-line load order, colour-by-variable, block temps take homes (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 105) <a name="post0b-kit-iv-run105"></a>

- **Two global loads in source order need ONE source line.** game_libs_func_00048184 (99.57 -> EXACT):
  `x0 = W / 2 - 64; y0 = H / 2 - 64;` on two lines issued `lw W` before `lw H`; written on one line,
  IDO issued `lw H` first, as the target does. This is the load-side twin of
  [#feedback-one-line-stores-fix-schedule-order](#feedback-one-line-stores-fix-schedule-order). In the same function an array subscript
  (`tbl[idx]`) instead of `*(T *)(base + idx * 4 + K)` gave the base chain the lower t-reg.
- **Registers follow variable identity, not role.** gl_func_0004E96C (99.55 -> EXACT, jumptable donor): two switch
  arms had the stream cursor in v1 and the loaded word in v0, the other arms had the opposite. Holding the cursor
  in the `int v` local that the float arms use for their trunc.w.s result, and the word in the `int *p` local
  the other arms use as their cursor, matched it: `v = (int)a1->args; a1->args = (int *)v + 1; p = *(int **)v;`.
  Separate locals, decl reorders and a reused pointer local all kept v0/v1 the other way round.
- **Block-local pointer temps reserve frame homes.** gl_func_00041A9C: two `if (1) { int *t = G; f(.., t[2], t[0]); }`
  blocks made the frame 8 too large (each t took a 4-byte home). Inlining `G[2], G[0]` fixed the frame, but the base
  then coloured v1 rather than v0, and every way of keeping a fresh variable cost the 8 bytes back. Still open.
- **One local reused for a later sub-object = one spill slot.** gl_func_00032E18: the target spilled the first
  sub-object pointer and the later `self + 0x110` pointer to the same slot (92), so the source reused one local. Two
  locals gave two slots.
- **m2c `s32 *` arithmetic scales offsets x4.** The old 32E18 body had `var + 0x2C` on `s32 *` locals (built `+176`
  where the target has `+44`) and an int temp for a float struct field. Retype the locals to `char *` before tuning.
- **Frame sculpting order.** Read the target's sp offsets first: decl order top-down places aggregates (49B3C: `ai`
  first plus a 12-byte pad struct; 4E244: one-int arrays between the iterator structs plus `int u[3]` below), and
  unused `int pad;` scalars are dropped but unused arrays/structs keep their space.
- **Float 0 in a GPR arg.** gl_func_00049B3C's `addiu a3,zero,0` was a `0.0f` arg to a prototyped
  `(char *, char *, char *, float, float, int)` callee (see [#feedback-ido-knr-float-call](#feedback-ido-knr-float-call)).

## post0b kit IV (agent-g 2026-10-17, run 104) <a name="post0b-kit-4-run104"></a>

Nine post0b exacts (gl_func_000550CC, game_libs_func_00054144, gl_func_000628EC, gl_func_00061C9C,
gl_func_000622D8, gl_func_0006264C, gl_func_00062540, gl_func_0006275C, gl_func_0005FF14) and NM gains on
5C548 (92.7 -> 99.18), 5D134 (71.2 -> 76.8), 61B30 (41.6 -> 65.9), 60AD0 (75.9 -> 82.0).

- **Float-as-int copy scan.** `scripts/float-copy-scan.py` (1080 repo) counts lw/sw/lwc1/swc1 per NM function in
  build/non_matching vs expected/ and pairs them by non-$sp field offset (`offm` column). `dir 1` = the C copies a
  float through an int lvalue (retype to f32); `dir -1` = the C uses f32 where the original moved raw words. A pair
  count with `offm 0` is usually a spill/regalloc coincidence (5F984, AC20), not a float copy. After run 103 the
  remaining genuine hits in agent-g units were few; 550CC was the big one.
- **Struct assignment is the int-word copy.** 550CC: `v = *(V3 *)(self + 0xDC)` and `v = *p` emit lw/sw word blocks
  even with f32 members; the field-wise `p->x = v.x` moves emit lwc1/swc1. Spell whole-vector moves as struct
  assignment and per-field moves as field copies, and pass raw tail args as `*(s32 *)` (lw, no lwc1).
- **Row-typed array gives a base-first addu.** 54144 `&verts[idx]` (6-byte struct) emits `addu v0,idx*6,verts` in
  every flat spelling (struct IXA, ptr+idx, char/u32 arithmetic, commuted, comma/cast index). Declaring the field
  `s16 (*verts)[3]` and taking the ROW `s16 *v = m->verts[idx]` (array-to-pointer decay of a row IXA) emits
  `addu v0,verts,idx*6`. Same family as the `typedef int Row[10]` rule in
  [#addu-operand-order-is-ucode-shape-not-allocator--array-ixa-emits-base-first-flat-ptr-arith-emits-deeper-operand-first-timproc-twins-cracked](#addu-operand-order-is-ucode-shape-not-allocator--array-ixa-emits-base-first-flat-ptr-arith-emits-deeper-operand-first-timproc-twins-cracked).
- **FP constant pair colours = constrained priority, flipped by a dead `if (0)` store.** 628EC stores 0.0f x12 and
  1.0f x8; the target puts 0.0 in f0 and 1.0 in f2, ours the reverse. In uoptlist the two constants are
  CONSTRAINED candidates coloured in priority order (the first coloured gets f2). One dead
  `if (0) { *(f32 *)(self + 0xF4) = 1.0f; }` just before the first 0.0f store swaps them. `while (0)` boosts,
  named locals, casts and double literals had no effect (run 102 probes).
