- **Memory-homed param vs register param.** The target `sw a0,0(sp); ... or a2,a0,zero` (5C548) = a param that is
  memory-resident (home store) and loaded once into a register copy at entry (the load forwards to a move). Spell it
  as `f32 *q = q0; if (0) { f(&q0); }`. The OPPOSITE problem (5D134: our build homed q and copied it to a1, the target
  keeps q in a0) was fixed by a dead `while (0) { q = &q[i]; }` reassignment of the param. In both, dead `while (0)`
  appearances placed before the copy set uopt's first-appearance colour order (5C548: i*4 v0, j v1, k a0, q a2).
- **`/ (f32)1024` keeps div.s.** IDO strength-reduces `x / 1024.0f` to `x * 2^-10` (`lui 0x3a80; mul.s`). The
  int-literal cast `/ (f32)1024` is not folded and gives `lui 0x4480; div.s`, the same cfe rule as `(f32)1 * s`.
  `(float)(u32)x` produces IDO's `cvt.s.w; bgez; add.s 2^32` pair itself, so don't hand-write the raw < 0 branch.
- **va_start tell.** A function homing all four arg regs and passing `(sp + FRAME + 7) & ~3` to a callee is a
  varargs wrapper: the value is `((int)&fmt + sizeof(fmt) + 3) & ~3` (61B30). Its held base needed the int-cast
  unfold (`int bi = (int)arr; base = (char *)bi;`) or every store folds to a lui-at macro.
- **Undefined symbol makes ld SEGFAULT.** In this toolchain `mips-linux-gnu-ld` prints `ld: ` and segfaults (no
  "undefined reference" text) when an unwrapped function references a symbol missing from undefined_syms_auto.txt
  (6264C's `D_sym_6264C`, which was harmless while the function was NM-only). Check every extern of a function you
  unwrap; `rm build/tenshoe.elf` after editing undefined_syms_auto.txt.
- **Baked jals to the stream readers.** 622D8/6275C called 0x7644C/0x76488 (`0C01D913`/`0C01D922`): use the existing
  `gl_ref_0007644C` / `gl_ref_00076488` pins with a plain extern call. The old fn-ptr casts gave lui/ori/jalr AND had
  the wrong address (0x764C4).
- **Store-then-call.** A flush `sb zero,0(tN)` in the delay of a `jal` runs BEFORE the call: write the store first
  (60AD0, also the 61C9C/6264C decodes where the old C had the order reversed).
- **One-shot `objdiff-cli diff` needs `-c functionRelocDiffs=none`** to agree with report.json on reloc'd USO
  functions; without it every jal/%hi/%lo against the blank expected words shows DIFF_ARG_MISMATCH even on exacts.


## post0b/post kit V: by-value structs, escaping locals, constructors (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 106) <a name="post0b-kit-v-run106"></a>

Twelve exacts and ~12 NM gains came from a handful of recurring source shapes. Older notes had listed them as caps.

**Struct parameters passed BY VALUE.** IDO homes a struct parameter at entry (`sw aN,home(sp)`) and reads its members back
from the home. That gives these tells:
- `lh tX,46(sp)` / `lb a1,67(sp)` in a frame of 40/48 = a member at +2/+3 of a by-value struct (or a `char`
  parameter passed on the stack). gl_func_0001CFDC / 0001D0AC (8-byte spec, `lh 46/50`), 0001D870 (12-byte), 000476DC
  (two 4-byte `{short hi, lo}` structs, the call takes `.lo`), 00042684 (colour in `.lo`).
- All of a1..a3 homed while one of them is never read as an int = that one is a struct. Its register is then free and
  gets reused (gl_func_0003D16C puts `o` in a2).
- `sw a1,4(sp)` in the function's OWN outgoing-arg area before a jal = passing a by-value struct on to the callee
  (gl_func_0003EB3C; the old body faked it with `volatile int *p = &a1`).
- A member read reloads from the home at each use (`lh t5,54(sp)` again before the call); a named local copy of the member
  does not.

**Struct RETURN.** An epilogue that copies a 12-byte local out word by word (`addiu t7,sp,36; lw t9,0(t7); lw t6,48(sp);
sw t9,0(t6) ...`) and then does `lw v0,48(sp)` is `Vec3 f(...)` with a hidden a0 return buffer (gl_func_0003695C). The
float-copy scan reports this as "int copy of floats". The build stores the fields with `swc1` through a `float *out`
parameter. Retyping the fields does not help; change the signature.

**Dead store of a loaded pointer** (`lw t6,20(a0); sw t6,68(sp)` with no reload): the local is address-taken, or it is a
member of a local struct whose other member escapes to a call. `struct { Vec3 v; char pad[12]; int p; } s;` with `&s.v`
passed reproduces it (gl_func_0003783C, 98.4). An unused `int **pp = &o;` does the same for a lone pointer
(gl_func_000372D4, 98.1). Both need the frame sized with pads afterwards.

**Alloc-or-given constructor.** `if (o == 0) { o = alloc(N); if (o == 0) goto out; } ... out: return o;`. Then match the
store ORDER to the target's sw sequence: IDO keeps program order for stores through the same base. 36E74 (0x28, 0x4C=a2,
floats, 0x00, 0x3C), 3E238, 39A04 (the 1.0f store before the next call), 3D16C (permute the last four stores). Placement-
constructed sub-objects: `p = (S *)(o + K); if (p != 0 || (p = alloc(4)) != 0) p->w = 0;` gives the `addiu at,zero,-K;
bne o,at` guard.

**Typed record view fixes multi-index `addu` order.** `rec + attr*0x64 + sub*0x14 + 0x50` in byte arithmetic emits
`addu t1,t0,v0` (index first). `&rec->grp[rec->attr].ent[sub]` through `typedef struct { char p[0x1B]; u8 attr; ...;
Grp grp[2]; ... } Rec;` emits `addu t1,v0,t0`, and also fixed 1D870's "colouring" residual. Declare `e` before `rec`
when the target spills `e` higher.

**`if (1) { p += 6; }` keeps a held base address.** `a0[6] &= ~2` folds the offset into the `lw/sw`. A pointer advanced
inside `if(1)` keeps the target's `addiu v0,a0,24; lw 0(v0); ... sw 0(v0)` (gl_func_0003E238). A bitfield gives
`lbu/sb` instead, and so do volatile and an int-cast pointer.

**Per-access externs.** In gl_func_0002F288 a counter at D+0x1C740 is loaded, stored and re-stored with three separate
`lui`. Only three distinct externs (one per access) stop uopt from CSEing a held base (`lui a1,2; addiu a1,-32768;
lw 18240(a1)`). Large offsets on an INDEXED access split as `lui 1; ori 0x8000` + `%lo(+0x4330)`. The target's folded
`lui at,2; lw -15568(at)` is a separate (file-static) array symbol: `extern float D_x[]; D_x[idx]`.

**Single-condition idioms.** `if ((r = o->type) == 1) return f(); return 0;` gives `lw v0` + `bnel v0,at` with `v0 = 0`
in the delay (3593C). A vtable call spelled inline, `(*(int (**)(int))(*(char **)&D + 0x5C))(x)`, calls through t9.
A named `f` pointer local puts it in v1.

**Baked in-unit jals in game_libs_post.** `jal 31fb0` / `jal 3204c` (words 0x0C00C7EC / 0x0C00C813) are absolute in-unit
targets. Pin them as `gl_ref_00031FB0 = 0x00031FB0;` in undefined_syms_auto.txt; ROM cmp passes. 1D870's note that
its callee was game_libs_func_0003443C was wrong (same word as 1CFDC).

**Also:** gl_func_00047E00 (4x4 matrix multiply) needs the inner `for (k)` loop written out. IDO unrolls it but keeps
the `0 + x` reload; four explicit terms fold the zero (96.6).


## post0b/bootup kit VI: unsorted compare chains, by-value ctor args, objdiff jal blind spot (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 107) <a name="nested-ne-goto-chain-35648"></a>

**Unsorted equality chain = nested-!= goto chain.** IDO emits a switch's compares in ascending case order, and puts
the case bodies after the chain in source order. So a target whose chain tests 1, 0, 2 (`beq v0,at(1) -> A; beqz v0
-> B; beq v0,at(2) -> C; b end`) is not a switch. The flat goto ladder (`if (k == 1) goto A; if (k == 0) goto B; if
(k == 2) goto C; goto end;`) gets the order right but turns the last test into `bne k,2,end` + `b C`. This nesting
keeps all three `beq`s and the trailing `b end`:

```c
if (k != 1) {
    if (k != 0) {
        if (k != 2) {
        } else goto C;
    } else goto B;
} else goto A;
goto end;
```

Cracked gl_func_00035648 / 00035370 (EXACT) and bootup func_00007D04 (58 -> 96). gl_func_000356FC needed only the
flat ladder with `if (k != 2) goto end; goto L2;` (see #feedback-ido-split-last-eq-test-to-suppress-bnel) plus the
items below. gl_func_0004D688's six-way chain (0x65, 0x66, 0x64, 0x67, 0x68, 0x6C) took the flat ladder (67 -> 73).
`scripts/byvalue-struct-scan.py --chains` lists every non-exact function whose target chain on one register is not
ascending.

- **Unsigned selector.** With `int k`, the compare constant 1 is shared with a later `a1 == 1` and CSE'd into v1
  (`addiu v1,zero,1` once). The target materializes `addiu at,zero,1` at each test. `unsigned k` (or a
  `switch ((unsigned)x)`) keeps the constants apart, because 1u and 1 are different constants to uopt.
- **Dead shared return block.** gl_func_000356FC ends `... beqz zero,epi; sw (kind-2 store); or v0,zero,zero; epi:`,
  with the `or` unreachable. It survives only when `end: return 0;` has TWO goto predecessors (kind 1 and the
  default). Each predecessor steals the `or` into its delay slot and branches past it. With one predecessor, or with
  `return 0;` written in each arm, the block is deleted.
- **Post-increment compares the old value.** `slti at,v1,31` on the value loaded before `addiu t7,v1,1; sw t7` =
  `t = *p; *p = t + 1; if (t >= 31) ...`. `if ((*p)++ >= 31)` materializes a slti/xori boolean. Reuse the dispatch
  variable for `t` when the target keeps both in the same register (7D04).

**objdiff blind spot: in-TU jal targets.** `objdiff-cli diff -c functionRelocDiffs=none` and report.json scored
gl_func_00035370 at 100 while it called the in-TU `gl_func_00034458` (`jal 0x34458`, word 0x0C00D116) where the
target has the placeholder `jal 0`. Only `make` (ROM cmp) caught it. Before you promote a function, check its callees:
an old NM body that names a real in-TU function where the target calls a placeholder will always score 100.

**By-value 4-byte ctor args in bootup constructors** (func_000055A0 51.9 -> 87.6). The tell is
`lui t4,0; lw t4,0(t4); sw t4,148(sp); jal alloc; sw t4,124(sp)`, then `lw t5,124(sp); sw t5,92(sp)` and
`lw a1,92(sp); ...; jal ctor; sw a1,4(sp)`. That is: a zero-page struct word goes into a per-object temp, then into
two inline-parameter copies (p1/p2, the same slots for every object), and is passed by value. What made it work:
- Copy through the int member (`p1.w = v0.w`). A struct assignment between locals copies through `addiu`-addressed
  temps.
- Pass the comma form `f(0, (t.w = G, t), ...)` when the target stores the temp and passes it in one go
  (`sw a1,372(sp); jal; sw a1,4(sp)`).
- Escape the per-object temps (`if (1) { S4 *q = &v0, ...; }`). Their stores are dead (only the copies are read),
  but the target keeps them.
- Give every reloc-blind zero-page reference its own extern. With `DI(0)`-style macros over one `&D_00000000`, uopt
  CSEs the base into an s-reg and deletes the dead first store of `DI(0) = DI(0) | 8; ...; DI(0) = 0;`. The target
  keeps both, because they were different symbols before relocation.
- Merge flag temporaries that the target keeps in one register (s0) into one C variable.
- Spell constants the target rematerializes per use as `(f32)0`. A repeated `0.0f` that is live across calls is
  hoisted into callee-saved $f20 (`sdc1 $f20` in the prologue).
- `func(obj + 0x5C, ...)` after the in-place sub-object construction passes the field address, not the possibly
  allocated pointer.

**Token passed by value through an aligned local** (gl_func_0003E9C8 70.7 -> 99.6). The target loads the token with
`lwl/lwr` (align-1 source), stores it with `swl/swr` into a stack local, and later reads it with `lw a1,68(sp)` and
`sw a1,4(sp)`. Type the local as an aligned `struct { int w; }` and copy into it through an align-1 view:
`*(Tag *)&key = *(Tag *)src`. Pass a per-call copy (`k1.w = key.w; f(a0, k1)`). Still open: the target gives the two
copies 8-byte slots at 56/48 (frame 0x48). Every named copy, block-scoped or comma-form, packs at 4 (0x40).

**cfront row transform** (gl_func_000432BC 61.8 -> 96.6). `x = m[8]*vz + (m[0]*vx + m[4]*vy)` gives the target's
`add.s f14,f6(sum),f8(product)`. The natural `m[0]*vx + m[4]*vy + m[8]*vz` swaps the operands of the second add.s.
Keep field accesses o-relative and use the `dst = o + 0xF0` pointer only for the calls.

**Correction to kit V:** gl_func_00047E00's 96.6 is the build WITH the inner `for (k)` loop. Four explicit terms
score 65.9 (re-measured this run). The residual is register choice only (t0/t3/a3 for the row pointer, end and the 16
bound, against the build's a3/t2/a1).


## post0b/post1b kit VII: rolled loops, shared-variable colours, baked in-unit jals (agent-g 2026-10-17, run 105) <a name="post0b-kit-vii-run105"></a>

Twelve exacts (game_libs_func_0005C548, gl_func_00060370, 00051694, 00055FB4, 0005BAF4, 0005B070, 0005B23C, 000521F8,
00051520, 00052AE8 in post0b; gl_func_00066484, 0006A420 in post1b) and NM gains on 533EC (11.7 -> 96.1), 5B90C (45.5
-> 96.5), 600A4 (38.2 -> 95.4), 62194 (36.2 -> 95.7), 5534C / 558A0 (-> 97), 51ED8 (24.3 -> 95.0), 54D04 (0 -> 66.1),
51F5C (81.9 -> 95.4), 50444 (53.1 -> 84.5), 60AD0 (82.0 -> 92.95), post1b 66264 (17.7 -> 93.8). Nearly all were m2c
soups or wrong decodes; the typed rewrite did most of the work. Levers that were new:

- **Rolled vs unrolled counted loop.** IDO -O2 unrolls a small counted loop (by 2 or 4) unless the counter is
  initialised IN the `for` header. gl_func_000533EC (3-iteration colour average) stayed rolled with
  `for (i = 0; i != 3; i++)`; an `i = 0;` statement before the loop, a do-while, or a variable bound `n = 3` all
  unrolled it (the old note called this a cap). Dividing by `i` after the loop reuses the loop-bound register (div by
  a register plus the break traps, as in the target). In gl_func_00050444 even the header form unrolled; only a
  `volatile` start parameter (the target reloads it from its home after a call anyway) kept it rolled.
- **Colours follow variables (again).** gl_func_00051520 keeps the stream pointer, the lookup result and a later arm
  pointer all in v0: write ONE local `v` for all three. Its first web still took v1 until a dead
  `while (0) { v = 0; p = 0; }` was placed right after the first call. In 5C548 a second dead loop AFTER the
  `q = q0` copy (`while (0) { v = &v[j]; v = &v[k]; }`) moved two address webs ahead of a third. The placement of the
  dead loop matters as much as its contents.
- **Typed list param = `beq` operand order.** With a `char *` heap param and a cast in `p != (Blk *)h`, IDO put the
  head register first; typing the param as the node type (`Blk *h`, no cast) gave the target's `beq v1,a0`
  (5B070; also 5B90C's list walk).
- **Comma-form store for an unrolled copy-then-store.** The target's fill loop did `or v1,v0; sb a0,0(v1); addiu
  v0,1` in every unrolled copy. `*c++ = v`, `p8 = c; c = p8 + 1; *p8 = v` and friends scheduled the increment above
  the first sb; `*(p8 = c, c = p8 + 1, p8) = 0xFF` matched (5B070, reused unchanged in 5B23C).
- **Store order steers load scheduling.** In the split-block path, writing `r->hdr = b->hdr - n - 1` BEFORE
  `r->magic = 0x87654321` let IDO hoist the `b->hdr` load above the magic store, as in the target.
- **Baked in-unit jals hide in expected.** objdump of the expected .o shows `jal 6f620` / `jal 7e970` where a blank
  import would show `jal 0`: the call is baked to an in-unit address, and the build must call a pinned
  `gl_ref_000XXXXX` (5B070 / 5B23C -> gl_ref_0006F620; 6A420 -> new gl_ref_0007E970). Calling the visually similar
  in-file function (62F08) scores 100 in objdiff but fails the ROM cmp.
- **beql with an unreachable copy of its delay load is not a cap.** It is IDO's normal branch-likely fill when the
  TAKEN side is the long block. gl_func_00066484 had the arms the wrong way round: `if (a != b) f(); else {...}`.
- **No named locals for spilled sub-object addresses** (521F8): `o + 48` / `o + 52` written as expressions are CSE'd
  and spilled to the target's slots; named `p`/`q` added frame homes. Default values copied by STRUCT assignment from
  a global show as `lui/addiu base; lw 0(base)` (a plain int global folds the %lo into the lw).
- **libultra -O1 functions in post1b** (homed pointer reloaded around every field access, unfilled delay slots): put
  the libreultra C in an -O1 donor and splice it with `REPLACE_FUNC_BODY`, exactly as for 6A304 (gl_func_0006A420 =
  osSpTaskLoad, first compile). An -O1 donor does NOT help when the target has filled delay slots (66AF0: the magic
  constant is re-materialised per compare, but -O1 leaves the slots empty).
- Smaller: a trailing alignment word after an exact body = all-zero `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` (55FB4); a named
  `m = e->mask` in the loop test flipped `and` operands (55FB4); by-value struct parameter (kit V) for the
  `{int **pp; int w; ...}` command walkers 5534C / 558A0, where `s.w &= 0xFFFF` keeps the preceding `s.w = w` store
  that `s.w = w & 0xFFFF` lets uopt delete.

Open: 51F5C wants the 100/101/0 compare order with the case-0 block after case 101; the kit VI nested-!= chain inverted
the last test into `bnez` here. 5AFD4's `(n + 0xFF000000) - 1` with the constant held in a register is still folded to
`+ 0xFEFFFFFF` by every spelling tried (incl. `(0xFF << 24)`, reordered terms). 5534C/558A0/600A4/5B90C residuals are
single colour or as1-delay choices.


## game_libs_post/bootup kit IX: unroll factor = body size, pool scalars, float param reuse (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 109) <a name="kit-ix-unroll-body-size-run109"></a>

**The unroll factor follows the size of the loop body before optimisation.** gl_func_00024378's copy loop (five
statements, each re-reading two pointer fields of the area global) is x4-unrolled with an `andi 3` remainder loop in the
target. The NM body read the fields through a local `B = gl_d_24378 + (int)&proxy` (a proxy-extern trick to keep the
base held). It unrolled x2 with a peeled single remainder. Typed views (`((Dst *)FW(B, 0x2030))[i].b2 = ...`, 0x14-byte
struct) did not unroll at all. Naming the global at every access, `SB(FW(gl_d_24378, 0x2030) + i * 0x14, 2) = ...`,
gave the x4 shape. uopt still CSEs `&gl_d_24378` into s0 for the whole function, so the held base did not need the
local. 69.5 -> 95.4. When the target unrolls more than the build, shrink the per-iteration source (drop base locals,
casts through typed arrays). When it unrolls less, grow it (the de-hoisting lever) or block it with a dead bound
reload.

- **Dead bound reload keeps loops rolled (confirms W33).** gl_func_0001DCB4's three classify loops are rolled in the
  target with an s32 counter and `slt at,s1,a0; bnez` (no `i != n` conversion). With `for (i = 0; i < n; i++,
  p += 0x20) { n = *(int *)(D + 0x2070); ... }` all three come out rolled with the target's bodies and no s8
  narrowing. It was not kept: the rewrite dropped enough `&D` uses that uopt stopped holding `&D` in an s-register,
  and that cost more than the loops gained. If the bound also feeds an address (`n * a3`), hoist that product into
  its own variable first, or the reload makes the multiply loop-variant.
- **Area global, store order.** In the same function each switch arm writes the float field before the int field
  (`lwc1; li; sw; b; swc1`), and a short read back through a just-stored pointer field (`*(s16 *)FW(g, 0x201C)`) gives
  the target's load after the four pointer stores.

**bootup RoData pool, continued (kit VIII).**
- Use per-address scalar externs whenever a function reads two or more pool slots. The run-108 rule (array symbol
  CSEs the base) held in all three cases tried: func_000055A0's `CF(K)` macro (`&func_0000057C + K`) became six scalars
  `D_bu_ro_598..5AC` (87.6 -> 92.5), func_00000610's two f64 reads became `D_bu_ro_d058/d060` (93.2 -> 97.5),
  func_0000C234's `D_bu_ro_pool[0x944 / 4]` pair hoisted `lui a3; addiu a3` and the scalars D_00000940/44/48 did not.
- An absolute `*(f32 *)0xC` in an NM body (func_000003F8, build `lwc1 f8,12(zero)`) was the pool slot
  func_00000044 + 0xC = 0x50. Grep NM bodies for small literal float addresses as well as `&func_ + K`.
- Scan used: for every bootup NM function, count target lwc1/ldc1 lines with `%lo(func_...)` against build lines
  with any `%lo(`. A target count above the build count marks a pool read still spelled through a register base.

**Float colours from param reuse (func_00000610 97.5 -> 99.9).** The target loads arg5 into f2 and writes the scaled
value back into f2; the clamp result and the later fabs(arg4) result share f0. Writing `arg5 = (f32)((f64)arg5 /
D_bu_ro_d058);` (no new temp) and using ONE `f32` local for both results gave that. Separate temps put the scaled value
in f0 and the results in f2. `arg2 / 4.0f` compiles to `* 0.25f`; `arg2 / (f32)4` keeps the target's div.s (the kit IV
`/ (f32)1024` rule).

**Other decode tells.**
- m2c `if (p->b5 == 1) { }` followed by an unconditional `p->b5 = n;` is a conditional store: target `lbu v0; ...;
  bne one,v0; sh (delay); sb`. gl_func_0001E134.
- A switch whose case blocks sit in an order different from the case values (1E134's 0, 3, 1 at 1b24/1b34/1b44 with
  case 1 falling into the default code) needs the cases written in that order with `goto` to the shared label.
  m2c put cases 3 and 1 at the end of the switch, jumping back.
- Baked absolute addresses read with `lui at,2; lwc1 -0x38c8(at)` at each access (no reloc): one scalar extern per
  access site. One symbol per address still got its base held (`lui; addiu v0`) when used twice in a block; a literal
  `*(f32 *)0x1C738` gave `lui 1; ori` (worse). gl_func_0002E354.
- An int chain `x == 1 || x == 2 || x == 3` whose 1 must not CSE with a later `== 1` test: compare `(u32)x` (kit VI
  unsigned-selector rule). A `switch` CSEs the constant just the same.
- gl_func_00026214 is the audio manager's frame handler (libultra `__amHandleFrameMsg` shape): `samplesLeft =
  osAiGetLength() >> 2`, `frameSamples = 16 + ((frameSize - samplesLeft + 0x80) & ~0xF)` clamped, then an OSTask
  fill with ucode_boot/ucode/ucode_data symbol addresses and `ucode_data_size = ((u64 *)end - (u64 *)start) * 8 - 1`.
  The 0x214C table is s16. 67.3 -> 79.1.

**Dead ends this run.** 24378's last diff is a dead `or a0,zero,zero` (an eliminated loop-counter init) that the target
keeps live into the first call, shifting every t-register by one; indexed, pointer and comma-for forms of the u64 clear
loop either unroll it or drop the init. 1E134's var_t4/var_t5 are memory-homed in the build (sw at each def) and in
registers in the target, spilled around calls; deleting the m2c `spC8 = var_t4` copy statements costs 1.4.
The `if (1) goto end;` lever (kit VIII agent-g) did not change C234's flat goto ladder.

## bootup/post0b kit VIII: RoData pool data symbol, named float locals, copy-slot pads (agent-c 2026-10-17, run 108) <a name="bootup-ro-pool-data-symbol-cce0"></a>

**bootup FP literals through a data symbol.** Every bootup_uso FP literal load is `lui at,0; lwc1 OFF(at)` against
the module's RoData section base (USO reloc symIdx 1, see
N64_FORENSICS.md#bootup-uso-fp-literal-pool-folded-into-func-0000098C). The old NM spelling
`*(f32 *)((char *)&func_00000940 + 0x1C)` names a FUNCTION, so IDO materializes its address
(`lui t6; addiu t6,t6,0; lwc1 0x1C(t6)`, one extra insn per site and an extra t-ring temp). A data symbol folds the
offset into the `%lo`:

```c
extern float D_bu_ro_pool[];     /* undefined_syms: D_bu_ro_pool = 0x00000000; (RoData base) */
extern double D_bu_ro_dpool[];   /* same base, f64 view */
... D_bu_ro_pool[0x95C / 4] ...  /* index = the RoData pool offset */
```

- Index by the FULL pool offset. func_0000CCE0's expected .o shows `lwc1 $f4,28(at)` (addend 0x1C against the
  splat function symbol), but the ROM word holds `0x095C`. Pinning the base at 0 with index 0x1C failed the ROM cmp;
  0x95C passed (CCE0 EXACT).
- Two references through the same array symbol can CSE the base into a register (`lui v1; addiu v1; ldc1 88(v1)`,
  func_00000610 93.2 -> 90.5). Keep per-address scalar externs (the existing `D_00000868 ...` list) where the target
  re-emits `lui at` per load.
- A store to the same section (`D_bu_ro_pool[0x2A0 / 4] = 1.0f`, 7328) takes the same base.
- Measured: E270 69.8 -> 99.8 (now only the documented spill-slot swap), D94 59.7 -> 70.9, 2C94 55.9 -> 61.4, 43D4,
  411C, 7328, C234, CAE8 +1 to 3. Call arguments that are text addresses (`&func_00008A40 + 0x20` passed to the
  allocator) take the same fix with a char-array view (`D_BF8C_8A40 + 0x20` gives `lui a0; addiu a0,a0,32`).
- CCE0's last diff was one store: write `f(cont, e0 = g(...))` so the spill of e0 schedules after the a0 copy.

**Named float locals colour f0/f2.** gl_func_0003783C (EXACT): the target keeps 0.0 in f2 and the loaded y in f0.
Plain stores (`s.v.y = *(f32 *)(a0 + 0x2C); s.v.z = 0.0f;`) use the f4+ temp ring. Named `float y, z;` locals give
the f0/f2 pair. The dead `sw t6,68(sp)` + frame 0x48 come from the pointer living in a memory struct beside the Vec3
(`struct { Vec3 v; char pad[12]; int p; } s;`) plus `int pad[3]`.

**Volatile pads between by-value copies.** gl_func_0003E9C8 puts the token at 68, o1 at 64 and the two by-value copies
k1/k2 at 56/48 (8-byte steps, frame 0x48). Declaration order `key; o1; volatile int pad1; k1; volatile int pad2; k2;`
reproduces it (99.58 -> 99.81). Residual: the last copy temp is t3 vs target t4. Several near-misses this run
(3E9C8, 372D4, 1DA7C, 4247C, BF8C's first if-arm FP ring) differ only by the t-/f-ring sitting one or two slots later
in the target, i.e. the original consumed temps that left no instruction. No spelling tried moves the ring.

**BF8C dispatch (88.3 -> 99.4).** Unsorted switch 0x63/0x61/0x62 = the kit VI nested-!= goto chain with the default
body innermost. `*(s32 *)(o + 0x990) = (f64)x < -0.75;` gives the target's `or t6,zero,zero; bc1fl; sw t6` boolean.
A flag stored, followed by an unrelated copy and then tested in the same register is one comma condition:
`if ((o->9CC = (w & 0x400) != 0, o->9F8 = o->490, o->9CC) != 0)`. Separate statements re-load or recolour it.

**Dead ends this run.** func_0000D900's clamp (copy-first `s = t;` + if/else-if) gets the target structure but the
three FP webs come out as a 3-cycle (t f0 / k f2 / s f12 vs target f2 / f12 / f0); 99.08 stays. func_000031C0 keeps
every value on the stack with no s-regs at -O2, so it is not a -O1 file (`-O1` reloads after each store). func_00007D04
stays rolled with the agent-g for-header form as well. gl_func_0003800C's last call has no `a0` setup in the target
(`f(?, n)`); uninitialised locals get a stack home instead.

## kit IX: void callees, cfront nested ctors with reused locals, `/ 2`, two-case switch gates (agent-g 2026-10-18, run 107) <a name="kit-ix-run107"></a>

Two exacts (timproc_uso_b5_func_00006C00, mgrproc_uso_func_00000E04) and NM gains on mgrproc 1824 (90.8 -> 98.4),
arcproc 125C (90.1 -> 99.1) and timproc_b5 CEB4 (92.4 -> 94.4, boundary move).

- **A discarded `int` return blocks v0.** 6C00 calls `func_00F954(...)` as a statement. Declared `extern int`, the
  call leaves a dead v0 def and uopt coloured the next two values (a global base and a loaded table base) a0/v1
  instead of the target's v1/v0. Declaring it `extern void` was the whole fix. Not universal: the same change did
  nothing on mgrproc 1824 (import_00096228) or E04 (04C678). Only change the extern when no caller in the TU uses
  the result (a conflicting later `extern int` redeclaration is a hard cfe error).
- **Operand order inside one expression picks t-reg ring positions per term.** 6C00's row-4 OR of two indexed loads
  needed the first term written base-first (`*(char **)(b + 0x40) + idx * 4`) and the second index-first; every
  other row stays index-first.
- **cfront nested inlined base constructors (E04).** A 4-level `if (o == 0) { o = alloc(n); if (!o) goto Lvt; }`
  goto ladder becomes nested `o2 = o1; if (o2 || (o2 = alloc(80))) { o3 = o2; if (o3 || (o3 = alloc(44)))
  {...; o3->vptr = vt3;} o2->vptr = vt2; } o1->vptr = vt1; member_ctor(o1 + 80);` -- note the 1704-level
  vptr store comes BEFORE the member call. A failed outermost alloc returns 0 (`return obj`).
- **The 07ACE0 list link tests the CHILD it was given, not its return value**: `link(obj + 16, child); if
  (child->0x14) child->4 = 1; child->0x14 = obj;`. Target tell: the second argument is spilled (`sw a1,K(sp)`)
  across the jal and reloaded into the register that the following `lw tN,20(aX)` uses. Bodies that read the
  return value (`rec = link(...)`) are a decode bug.
- **Reused pointer locals give the home map.** E04's frame 0x40 holds only three named homes (60/56/52) plus a
  compiler temp at 44: the source reuses o1 for every linked child and o2 for a later 224-byte alloc (that is why
  o2 is memory-homed). Folding the object pointer into the parameter (`obj`) and dropping the float-zero, count and
  vtable locals removed the extra homes; the 0x7C8 count is read through the field itself.
- **Store-before-call then re-read.** `obj->0x6A8 = a3` sits in the jal delay slot before 119C and the field is
  re-read after the call: write the store before the call, never forward the parameter.
- **One source line flips a scheduling tie.** E04's last two-word residual (an o1 spill reload vs a vptr lui/addiu)
  was found by the permuter as `do { ... } while (0)` all on one line; the `do/while` is irrelevant -- writing the
  44-byte ctor's `if (...) { call; store; }` on ONE line is enough. IDO's scheduler is line-sensitive (same lever
  as gui_uso_func_00001794).
- **`bgez x; sra y,x,1 (delay); addiu at,x,1; sra y,at,1` is signed `x / 2`.** arcproc 125C had it decoded as a
  `sum < 0` if/else with `>> 1`; `span = 0xA0 - (a + b + 4) / 2` made the body size-exact.
- **A two-case gate with the bodies after the compares is a `switch`.** mgrproc 1824's `beqz v0,L0; li at,1; beq
  v0,at,L1; b end` = `switch (s0->0x7D4) { case 0: ... case 1: ... }`; switch on the field expression, not on a
  named local (a local takes v-regs). Case 3's counter is stored unconditionally before the `>= 16` wrap, spelled
  through the field so the re-read forwards the stored t-reg.
- **Boundary move (CEB4).** Two words (`lui at,0x3F80; mtc1 at,f2`) hoisted above CEB4's prologue lived in the
  predecessor's `_pad.s`. Moved into CEB4's `.s` head (size 0x1A4 -> 0x1AC, label unreferenced, ROM unchanged),
  dropped the sidecar and its GLOBAL_ASM line, refreshed expected/ from the ROM-exact build.
- **Measure with objdiff before you keep a variant.** game_uso 41C0: a declaration-order home map (one leading pad)
  plus moving the template copy into the ctor body cut raw diff lines 146 -> 66, but objdiff fell 94.2 -> 91.0
  (insertion misalignment). Reverted.
- Permuter on this machine: run `import.py` / `permuter.py` with `/home/danjs/code/decomp/.venv/bin/python`
  (tools/build-venv has no `toml`).

Open: timproc_b5 8C44 (s0/s1 counter vs pointer swap; a `for (i < n + 1)` gets the s-regs right but keeps the
slt), CEB4 block 1 (target keeps an empty then-arm as `bc1f; nop; b skip` with the init stores hoisted above the
test -- no spelling reproduced it), C98C (t1/t2 on a spilled reload), 38B0/396C (store order vs volatile temps),
1824 (outer switch value v1 vs v0; jtbl displacement cap), 125C (pb/hb colour v0/v1 swapped).

## kit VIII: `if (1) goto` body order, int-typed address CSE, inlined member constructors (agent-g 2026-10-17, run 106) <a name="kit-viii-run106"></a>

Two exacts (gl_func_0005231C, timproc_uso_b5_func_00008688) and NM gains on gl_func_00055470 (44.9 -> 93.7), game_uso
41C0 (61.3 -> 94.2), 3018 (56.0 -> 93.1), 18FC (50.9 -> 91.2), E5C8 (76.9 -> 91.4), timproc_b5 6C00 (17.2 -> 98.9),
8C44 (22.9 -> 98.4), CEB4 (12.9 -> 92.4), 8AFC (38.7 -> 85.9), gui 329C/2DE0 (+1.3/+0.9).

- **`if (1) goto end;` keeps goto-chain bodies in text order.** With the kit-VI nested-!= chain and labelled bodies
  that each end in a plain `goto end;`, uopt lays the bodies out innermost-first (E5C8) or pulls the last body up under
  an inverted `bne dflt` at the end of the chain (5231C, 51F5C-style). Writing `if (1) goto end;` as the last statement
  of every body (or only of the body that gets hoisted, for 5231C) keeps each body where the source puts it. The old
  55470 note ("goto-body order is textual-order-invariant") came from plain gotos; with the `if (1)` form the same
  source went from 44.9 to 93.7. The lever did nothing on functions whose gotos are not chain-body exits (500EC,
  61478, 591C, 117C were unchanged), and it did not move 51F5C's case-0 block (a loop-continue target).
- **Switch or chain?** 5231C's old body was a `switch`, which IDO turned into a jumptable; the target is an unsorted
  `beq` chain (3,13,14,15,22,23,17,24). `byvalue-struct-scan.py --chains` misses chains that include a `beqz` or start
  after a `beqzl` on a different value (E5C8's chain runs on a3->0x12C, not on the 0xE8 field the old body switched
  on), so read the target chain register before trusting a decoded switch.
- **int-typed address arguments get CSE'd.** timproc_b5 func_00004068's colour parameter was typed `int`, so every
  caller passed `(int)v`. uopt treats that int-typed `sp+0x40` as an ordinary expression, CSEs it across the three calls
  and spills it (`sw a3,32(sp)` / reload). Typing the parameter `f32 *` and passing `v` gives the target's
  `addiu a3,sp,64` before each call (CEB4 75 -> 92; C310 90.5 -> 90.9 for free).
- **"Dead sentinel stages" in cfront constructors are inlined member constructors.** The game_uso 41C0 family
  (`if ((int)obj == -8) { obj2 = alloc(0x18); ... }`) is `o = obj + 8; if (o || (o = alloc(0x18))) { ctor(o, obj, prm,
  1); o->vptr = ...; }`: the compare against -8 is `obj + 8 == 0`, a failed alloc skips only that member (the old
  bodies' `goto end` was wrong), and the 8-byte base sub-object is the same shape with its result discarded. The
  template word is a by-value 4-byte struct (kit VI): one escaped temp per stage (`t1.w = tmpl->w`, kept with
  `if (1) { T *q = &t1; q = &t2; ... }`) copied into ONE shared inline parameter `prm.w = tN.w`, passed by value
  (`sw a2,8(sp)` in the jal delay). Stage 1 of 18FC/3018 also takes three by-value Vec3 params (struct assignments,
  addiu-addressed word copies) and copies one through a temp into the member.
- **Every named local takes a home in declaration order** (first declared = highest address), even locals that live
  in registers. Unused int pads in the declaration list rebuild a target's home map (18FC: all homes match with 8
  pads). A pad that crosses an 8-byte boundary moves everything below it by 8, so tune one word at a time.
- **One variable for the loaded word and the field pointer.** In 5231C's 0x34 arms the target loads the command word
  into v0, tests it, and loads `o + 0x34` into v0 in the branch delay slot: write `q = (s32 *)*p; if (q) { q = (s32 *)(o
  + 0x34); ... }`. A separate `w` for the 0x30 arms gives their a0. `do { *q |= 2; } while (0);` keeps the
  `addiu v0,a3,48` base unfolded.
- **Bottom-test shapes.** `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` with a call in the body kept `slt; bnez` (8C44 wanted `blez` guard
  + `bne`: a guarded `if (n > 0) { i = 0; do {...} while (i != n); }`). E5C8 wanted `sltu` where the plain unsigned
  `for` collapsed to `bne`: re-reading the count from memory in the condition (`v1 < *(u32 *)&D`) keeps the compare.
- **cfront virtual calls** (8688 EXACT): `o = get(scr); vt = *(char **)(o + 0x28); ((void (*)(char *))*(int *)(vt +
  0x6C))(*(s16 *)(vt + 0x68) + o);` -- entries are {s16 delta, fptr}. The old structural body had read them as a
  vtable on `scr`.
- Smaller: game_uso E5C8's `EAF4(a3, (v0 & 0x20) != 0 ? ...)` is unconditional with `g && (v0 & 0x40)` (sltu, beqz,
  sltu); a final `x &= 6; if (t >= 21) {...}` with the then-store in the branch delay means the `&=` is unconditional;
  gui 329C's descending 0x408/0x120/0x110 compare chain is the nested-!= chain too, with one variable for the ring
  context and the switch value (the target's s0).

Open: 51F5C (case-0 block after case 101 inside a loop; `if (1)` endings do not move it); 51448 (target keeps the
inlined link() parameter `n = o` separate from `o` and spills it across the call; uopt copy-propagates every spelling
tried, incl. block scope, field re-reads and dead `while (0)`); 18FC/3018 constant stores (target stores in source
order reusing f0 for 0/-1000/1000).


## post0b kit X: verbatim gbi macros, per-arm s16 casts, home maps, folded zero compares (agent-c 2026-10-20, run 110) <a name="post0b-kit-x-run110"></a>

Six post0b NM bodies (four were m2c soups) were re-decoded from the expected-object asm: gl_func_000493AC 72.4 -> 86.9,
0004BAF4 71.3 -> 90.2, 0003BE1C 73.4 -> 76.3, 0003B9C0 67.0 -> 72.3, 0003B2EC 60.5 -> 85.2, 0003A58C 66.4 -> 68.3.

- **libultra gbi macros, expanded as written.** 4BAF4's E4/B4/B3 sequence with nested sign tests and `>> 7` products is
  `gSPScisTextureRectangle` (copy it from references/oot/include/ultra64/gbi.h). Written out verbatim (MAX/MIN ternaries,
  `(s16)` casts, `(yl) < 0` without a cast in the t term, `_SHIFTL` masks) the whole clamp ladder matched on the first
  compile. dsdx/dtdy were `(u16)(s32)(1024.0f / scale)`: `(u16)` straight from a float goes through the FCSR unsigned
  dance, the `(s32)` gives `trunc.w.s` + `andi 0xffff` as in the target.
- **cfront inline display-list appends.** When the target loads `ctx = G->254->158` BEFORE the call that produces the
  DL word and allocates the slot after it, the append is an inline function (arguments first, then the body), not a
  macro with `_g = pkt` first. Write `ctx = ...; r = f(...); g = NEXT(ctx); g->w0 = ..; g->w1 = r;`. The pool slot is
  `n = p->n; p->n = n + 1; &ctx->gfx->buf[n]` with `ctx->gfx` re-read after the count store.
- **MAX/MIN with sll/sra after every lh.** 3BE1C's three-way min/max re-casts each loaded s16 (`sll v1,a2,16; sra`).
  That happens when the operands are int variables and each arm of the ternary is cast:
  `#define MAXS(a, b) ((a) > (b) ? (s16)(a) : (s16)(b))` with `int ia = va[k], ...; hi = MAXS(MAXS(ia, ib), ic);`.
  Casting the whole ternary, or s16 operands, drops the shifts.
- **Home map from declaration order** (kit VIII rule, applied wholesale). 3BE1C's 0xF0 frame has 33 named homes: 10 words
  above the Vec3 `q`, 13 between `q` and the memory-resident cell pair `s32 c[2]`, 10 below. Moving ten former block-scope
  locals to function scope between `q` and `c` put every slot on the target's offset. 3B2EC: the escaped Vec3 declared
  FIRST lands at the top (sp+140 of 0x98). Locals declared inside blocks are laid out after all function-scope ones.
- **By-value Vec3 parameter scaled in place.** 3BE1C's `p.x *= K[0]` writes back to the caller's stack slot (sp+256): the
  signature ends `..., V3 p)` (kit V). Without `if (1) { V3 *pp = &p; }` the members are promoted into f20/f22.
- **Folded zero compare.** 3A58C: `disc = r*r - (len2 - dot*dot); if (disc < 0.0f)` compiled to `c.lt.s rr, x` (uopt
  rewrites `a - b < 0` as `a < b`). The target subtracts, spills disc across the next call and compares against
  `mtc1 zero`. Escaping disc (`if (1) { float *pd = &disc; }`) gives the target form; `(f32)0` and `0.0f > disc` do not,
  `0.0` (double) does but emits c.lt.d.
- **One symbol for a table's start and end.** 3B2EC walks the {1,2,0} next-vertex table from `&D` to `&D + 6`. With both
  spelled through the same symbol IDO turns the walk into an offset counter (`addiu ...,-6`). Separate symbols for the
  loop bound and the post-loop `nx != end` test kept the pointer walk (+3).
- **`i * 12` as multu.** In 3B2EC the record offset compiled to `multu i, 12` with the 12 held in an s-reg. The target
  shifts (`sll 2; subu; sll 2`); `off = ((i << 2) - i) << 2` reproduced it and freed the register. In 3BE1C the plain
  product already shifted, so check the target before reaching for this.
- **Literal eps gates.** 3B9C0's two double eps compares were memory externs in the old body. The target hoists the
  in-loop one into callee-saved f24 before the loop, which IDO only does for a literal constant (a memory load is not
  hoisted past the loop's dist[]/out[] stores). Use double literals (exact rodata values unchecked in the NM body).
- **Inlined Array iterator (493AC).** cfront `ArrayIterator it = arr.iterator();` = a placement-constructed temp at one
  slot (`if (1) { q = &t1; } if (q || (q = alloc(12))) {...}`), copied by value into a return temp, then into `it`
  (`tmp = t1; it = tmp;`; the chained `it = tmp = t1` is worse). The constructor's `q->last = q->arr->count - 1` reads
  through the just-stored field (forwarded to the register), where a separate `a` local folds to `self+0x90`.
  Per-access aliases for the 0x1C4 flags word stop `&D` being held in a register. One shared temp for the target's s2
  webs (loop-1 element, vtable pointer, ctx pointer) moved them to the right register class.

Open, same class in four functions: the target rematerializes a constant or a local's address after each call (`lui
at,0x437f; mtc1` in 454C4, `addiu v0,sp,236` in 3A58C, `addiu a0,sp,224` and the constant 1 in 493AC, the post-loop table end
address in 3B2EC), where our build holds it in a callee-saved register and spills something else. Per-expression block
temps did remove the &tmp hold in 3A58C, but each temp then takes its own frame slot. IDO 5.3 makes the same choice as
7.1 here (standalone check on 3A58C), so this is not a compiler-version difference.

## HOLD vs REMATERIALISE across a call: firstUseCost (0.25 x BB count) against the call-crossing cost; emission-free `if (1) { }` BB adders flip it (agent-c 2026-10-20, run 111) <a name="hold-vs-remat-firstusecost-run111"></a>

Closes the open problem from #post0b-kit-x-run110 (the target reloads `lui at,0x437f; mtc1` / `addiu v0,sp,236` / a param
from its home after each call where our build holds the value in s0..s8 or f20+).

**The rule (uoptreg2.c `globalcolor` + `cupcosts`, verified by probes).** For each live range uopt prices every register:
- caller-saved register (v0..t9 / f0,f2,f12..f18): `cupcosts` = the sum of `movcost x freq` (movcost 1, freq = 10^(loopdepth-1))
  over the call crossings inside the LR: +freq for each LR block whose first predecessor ends in a call (the post-call reload), and
  another +freq for a call block that is itself a live unit of the LR (the value is USED in the block that ends with the jal).
  A value that is only live THROUGH the call block costs freq once; a value used in it costs 2 x freq.
- callee-saved register (s0..s8 / f20..f30): 0 if that register is already in `usedeeregs` (an earlier, non-interfering LR took
  it), otherwise `firstUseCost = movcostused * curstaticno * 0.25`, clamped to [4, 60], where curstaticno = the number of basic
  blocks in the function.
- the caller-saved scan runs first and the compare is strict `<`, so a tie goes to the caller-saved register (= reload after
  the call). If the best cost is >= adjsave x span, the LR is split instead (that is how params end up in their home slot).
So a constant used once per region in a small function (F = 4) is held in f20 if it crosses one loop call (cost 10), and is
rematerialised in a big function (F >= 10). Probe: the 454C4 standalone flips 255.0f from f22 to f2/f0 between 39 and 41 blocks
(F 9.75 -> 10.25 against a crossing cost of 10).

**Two constants, one loop (454C4).** The target has 255.0f in f0 (reloaded after the in-loop jal) and 120.0f in f20 in the same
loop. That needs `X(255) <= F < X(120)`: the 120.0f uses must sit in the call block (cost 20) and the 255.0f uses in an earlier
block (cost 10). Moving the DL-append `do {` up so it starts before the three `* 120.0f` stores does that (the do-label ends
the 255 block), and two `if (1) { }` before the list walk lift F to >= 10. Result: f0/reload + f20, f22 save gone, exactly the
target's FP allocation (the function is still 61.7: its frame and named-local homes are the bigger problem).

**The lever: emission-free BB adders.** `if (1) { }`, `do { } while (0);`, `while (0) { }`, `for (;;) { break; }` and
`goto L; L: ;` each leave 1-2 extra blocks in the flow graph and emit nothing, which raises firstUseCost. A bare label does
not. Placement:
- where you put them changes scheduling: the blocks are label boundaries for as1, so adders at the top of 3A58C cut the
  prologue/first-block interleave (68.3 -> 66.9); the same four before the call-free tail (`pt = a + step`) gave 75.1.
  Run `autosweep.py`-style sweeps (anchor x k) and keep the best; the end of the function / before `return` is usually safe.
- the flip is per LR, at different k: 3A58C dropped s1 (&tmp) at k = 5 and s0 (param b) together with f20 (param r) at
  k = 7. A dead `if (r) { }` (the dead-if priority boost) kept r colourable in f20 while b fell to its home slot at k = 6..7.
- removing callee-saved saves shrinks the frame (8 per FP pair, 4 per s-reg plus alignment); put the difference back with a
  `volatile int pad[N]` at the decl position that restores the target's offsets (kit VIII home rule).
- does not help when every s-reg is already in use (493AC: s0..s8 saved, so a reused s-reg costs 0 and no BB count flips
  it) or when the hold is inside a loop with several crossings (3BE1C's s8 needed > 40 adders and broke other things).
- the inverse (target holds MORE than we do, e.g. 3B9C0's f24) needs fewer blocks or a use moved into the call block.

**Diagnosing.** `-Wo,-zdbug:5` prints each LR with its live units (`- live bb - N loads stores reg`), the reaching-only blocks
(`- live bb (default)`), `adjsave`, forbidden set and loopdepth per node; `-zdbug:6` gives the colour order. Count blocks from
the `flow graph` list at the top of the dump. On this machine the shared IDO's uopt still has the ecvt assert, so the dump
dies part-way; build a private copy instead of touching tools/: clone decompals/ido-static-recomp into the scratchpad,
implement `wrapper_ecvt`/`wrapper_fcvt` in libc_impl.c (call host ecvt/fcvt, copy the string into a wrapper_malloc buffer,
write decpt/sign through MEM_S32), `make -C tools/rabbitizer static CC=gcc CXX=g++`, `make VERSION=7.1 RELEASE=1
build/7.1/out/uopt`, then copy the project's out/ directory and drop the new uopt in (codegen verified identical).

**Applied (run 111, same session).** Scan for the class first: compare the prologue save set of target vs NM build for every
NM function (`scripts/disasm-func.py fn` vs `--nm`) and keep the ones where the BUILD saves more s-regs / f20+ than the target.
Then sweep `if (1) { }` x k (1, 2, 4, 8) at every top-level statement of the function, compiling the whole preprocessed TU
(asm_processor + cc on the unit takes ~1 s, so 100 variants are cheap) and scoring register-exact against the target; verify the
best 1-2 placements in-tree with objdiff. Results:

| function | before | after | what else it needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| gl_func_00038108 (60 w) | 51.0 | EXACT | `p` folded into the a2 home; a distinct symbol for the 4th report arg (else copied from a0); `if (1) { r = o->0x28; }` for r v0 / o-reload v1 |
| bootup func_00006254 (88 w) | 67.3 | EXACT | cfront ctor shape (below); comma-expression call arg for the z[] store schedule |
| bootup func_000074E8 | 56.5 | 92.1 | adders (73.7), then the cfront ctor shape with no early returns, data symbols for %lo-folded globals (a function symbol + offset is NOT folded into the load), `if (1) { char **pa = &a0; }` so every a0->0x40 is re-read, a dead local reused for the tail stores |
| bootup func_0000E800 | 55.1 | 87.8 | adders (69.4), then decl order under a pad for the out-param homes, zero inits after the first call, root = &D (not a load), store through a data symbol |
| bootup func_00003D3C | 50.7 | 57.8 | float args through a typed placeholder prototype (target stores them with swc1, a K&R call promotes to double) |
| bootup func_000043D4 | 56.4 | 62.0 | one adder |
| gl_func_00040974 | 90.6 | 91.7 | adders only |
| 0004FBA4, 00040E90, 0000E124 | | +1.1 / +0.2 / +0.6 | not kept (4FBA4's adders also cost 61478 -0.6 through the shared NM object) |

**cfront constructor shape (6254).** `bnez a0,L; jal new(0xDC); beqz v0,END; or s0,v0` then `bnez s0,L2; or a2,s0; jal
new(0xB4); beqz v0,SKIP; or a2,v0` is `if (this || (this = new(0xDC))) { s = this; if (s || (s = new(0xB4))) { base body }
derived body } return this;` written on the PARAMETER (a `char *o = a0` copy takes a home and moves the `or s0,a0` copy past
the arg stores). A member sub-object at +0x2C whose ctor is inlined twice shows as `addiu at,zero,-44; bne a2,at` (= this+44
!= 0) then a second `bnez`: `c = s + 0x2C; if (c || (c = new(4))) { c2 = c; if (c2 || (c2 = new(4))) *c2 = 0; }` with a
separate inner `this` (one variable leaves the store on v1 instead of a0).

**Comma-expression argument moves the arg setup between stores.** 6254's `addiu a1,sp,52; swc1 z0; addiu a0,a2,48; swc1 z1;
jal; swc1 z2` came from `z[0] = 0.0f; f(s + 0x30, (z[1] = 0.0f, z[2] = 0.0f, z));` -- three statements put the a0 setup
last (into the delay slot). The comma temp costs one frame word; take it out of a pad.


## kit XI: twin ports, one reused local, cast-literal divisors (agent-g 2026-10-20, run 109) <a name="kit-xi-run109"></a>

Four exacts (timproc_uso_b3_func_000019CC, timproc_uso_b3_func_00000E60, arcproc_uso_func_00000FA8,
arcproc_uso_func_00001D18) and timproc_uso_b5_func_00001460 93.68 -> 99.98.

- **Sweep result for the 0x6A8 family.** Tells scripted over the target words (`bnez rObj,+N; ...; jal; li a0,SIZE` = cfront
  `if (o || (o = alloc(N)))`; `sw at,4(rX)` + `sw rObj,0x14(rX)` = the record-link block). NOTE: USO .s files mix `.word`
  lines with symbolic `jal sym` lines, so parse the hex out of the `/* off vram WORD */` comment, not only `.word`. Every
  0x6A8 allocator in agent-g's units is already exact; eddproc and n64proc are 100% exact. Remaining ctor/link-tell NMs:
  timproc_b5 D14C/D550/D884/DF14/8FC8 (the 0x2B8 group), gui 0148, titproc 05DC.
- **Port the exact twin first.** b3 0E60 (97.5, "natural ceiling") went exact by copying timproc_b1 0EE8's C: `base = &D`
  re-assigned right after the 0x6A8 load, the count stored to 0x6B0 and READ BACK as the for-init (store-forward), the
  switch discriminant reused as the counter, and the call argument mult-first with no table local. arcproc 0FA8 (90.9) is
  the same machine: its documented "list held in v0 across the call" cap was the call's return value
  (`r = f(...); if (a0->6B0 != r->1C) break;`). Its case 1 also needed BOTH discarded-return calls void (the set-up call and
  the link call; either alone kept the spilled `buf` in v1), all locals at function scope declared BEFORE the initialised
  `i`/`s1` (frame 48), and `((int *)v0)[v0[1] + 4]` for `addu t1,v0,t0`.
- **One reused local (E04 rule) beats the 3-arg trick.** b3 19CC's two link blocks used `o` and `sub`; the target shares
  o's slot for both, and the 0x18/0x64 pointer mutations (`if (1) { o = o + 0x18; }`) are the same variable too. Then o's
  use as the 3rd argument of the sub-create call colours the whole web a2, and the old "pass q as a dead 3rd argument"
  hack is not needed. arcproc 1D18 is its twin: there a `tv = *(int *)(sub + 0x18)` pre-load local shifted the t-ring for
  the rest of the function; `*(int *)sub = *(int *)sub & ~4` through the mutated pointer fixed 20 of 26 lines.
- **Stack-argument store order.** 1D18's `0x4C = arg4` (arg4 from sp+88) had to be written BEFORE `0xB8 = arg3` so ugen
  loads it first (t7, ahead of the `li 255` for 0xD0); the scheduler still sinks the store to the target's position.
- **Flag RMW through the object pointer.** b5 1460's target `lw s0,56(s1); lw t6,196(s0); addiu s0,s0,196; ori; sw t7,0(s0)`
  is `o = *(char **)(a0 + 0x38); o += 0xC4; *(int *)o |= 0x40;` (same s0 for object and flag address).
- **Two registers for one constant: `num / (float)255`.** Target `lui at,0x437f; mtc1 at,$f4; mtc1 at,$f6; div.s $f0,$f4,$f6`.
  `255.0f / denom`, `num / denom`, `(float)n / denom` all CSE to one register; a float VARIABLE over a CAST LITERAL keeps two
  (the `(float)K` cast-literal has its own web, cf. #kit-x-run108 `(float)0`). Fixing it also fixed the float ring of a
  later block. The sp+36 float in that function was not the 062880 return (both returns are discarded): it is the white
  itself, spilled across the calls and reused as widget C's alpha; four `if (1) {}` adders
  (#hold-vs-remat-firstusecost-run111) moved it from f20 to the stack. Open: the `a0 + 0x10` spill lands at 40 vs the
  target's 32; a 1560-permutation decl sweep, an unnamed temp, and adder count/placement never put it below the float.
- **Negative: the `255.0f * x` FP register swap** (target `mtc1 at,$f4` for the constant, `lwc1 $f6` for x; we get the
  reverse) in arcproc 125C, mgrproc 1C90, mgrproc 2E3C, titproc 1710. Invariant across `x * 255.0f`, `(float)255 * x`,
  `x * (float)255`, int `255`, a float var `k`, `k * (float)x`, `(k = 255.0f) * x`, `255.0f * (pr = x)` and all 2^3
  site-orderings in 1C90; `255.0 * x` goes double. The int t-ring is also one register behind the target after the
  same expression in 125C/1C90, so the missing piece probably consumes a temp in the original.
- **Negative: gl_func_000525F0** (v1 vs v0 reload): an inline-param copy block, the cfront `||` lazy-init, the combined
  assignment and a fresh `n` local are all byte-neutral (adds to the 12 spellings documented in the source).

## kit X: void-callee scan, the 0x6A8 constructor family, per-site BB splits (agent-g 2026-10-20, run 108) <a name="kit-x-run108"></a>

Five exacts (mgrproc_uso_func_00001614, game_libs_func_00001818, timproc_uso_b3_func_00000994, titproc_uso_func_00000C54,
arcproc_uso_func_00000A3C) and small NM gains (arcproc 125C 99.13 -> 99.56, mgrproc 1C90 99.17 -> 99.52, 1824 98.42 -> 98.52).

- **`scripts/void-callee-scan.py`** (1080 repo) aligns target vs NM build per function, finds jal sites where the target
  writes v0 after the call without reading the return, our build does not read it either, and the following register
  diffs are +1 shifts on the caller-saved ring (v0>v1, tN>tN+1). `--owner g|c`, `--all-calls` for the loose list.
  Strict hits are often false (t-ring rotations, misaligned repeated blocks); the loose `v0>v1` list found the real wins.
- **Every discarded-return call in front of the web.** mgrproc 1614's hdr web followed two discarded calls
  (import_007FE4E8, undeclared = K&R int, then 07ACE0). Declaring 07ACE0 void alone (an old probe) and
  import_007FE4E8 void alone were both neutral; both void together = EXACT.
- **The 0x6A8 constructor family is one skeleton.** b3 0994 (96.8), titproc C54 (94.0) and arcproc A3C (87.9, noted as a
  "global regalloc + frame cap") all went exact on the mgrproc E04 shape: `if (obj || (obj = alloc(N))) { o1 = obj; if
  (o1 || (o1 = alloc(0x6A8))) { o2 = o1; if (o2 || (o2 = alloc(0x50))) { o3 = o2; if (o3 || (o3 = alloc(0x2C))) {...}
  o2->28 = ..; } o1->28 = ..; f(o1 + 0x50); } ... } return obj;`, then ONE reused local `o1` for every object pointer
  re-read through a field (`o1 = obj->6A8; link(obj + 16, o1); if (o1->14) o1->4 = 1; o1->14 = obj;`). The
  `(obj->6A8, obj, 0x568, ...)` registration call is void (alias `gl_func_00000000_994v` / `_A3Cv` = 0): its dead int
  return otherwise pushes the vtable base w from v0 to v1. NM-only `D_xxx` externs need `= 0` pins before unwrapping.
  timproc_b1 097C (agent-c's unit) is the same family.
- **Smaller tells from that family.** An if/else block storing through `obj->6A8` wants the field re-read into o1 in each
  arm (a3 arm loads). Store order of two adjacent field stores before a jal decides which one lands in the delay slot
  (A3C: 0x6A8 before 0x6B8). `x * 30` reproduces IDO's own `sll; subu; sll` on ONE temp; the hand-expanded
  `((x << 4) - x) * 2` takes three. An `int`-typed mirror store `*(int *)G = *(int *)(root + 0x50)` re-reads through a
  fresh temp and rotates every later t-reg by one; `*(void **)G = *(void **)(root + 0x50)` does not. A missing call
  argument (`0139B0(x)` vs `(x, 1, 0)`) shows up as a beqz-vs-beqzl difference in the following finalizer.
- **Which base IDO holds in s0.** Six `f(o, (*(int *)&W + 3) << 16 | k, -1, &T)` calls: with W = a distinct symbol and
  T = `&D_00000000`, the target's `lw a1,0(s0)` (W base in s0) + rematerialized `lui/addiu a3` (T) came out; with the
  roles reversed IDO held T in s0 and re-loaded W through lui. A local `p = &W` is copy-propagated away.
- **Pointer v1 / value v0 for `p = obj->X; h = *(short *)(p + 0x20);`.** Seen in game_libs 1818, arcproc 125C, mgrproc
  1C90. An empty `if (1) {}` between the two defs gives it (the per-BB dead-v0 rule, #dead-v0-poison-is-per-bb-split-the-defs-683d4),
  but only when the pair is not shared across sites: 125C/1C90 reused `pb/hb` (`q/w`) at three call sites, which made
  them one web, and the split did nothing until each site got its own names. `do { h = ...; } while (0);` did not work
  where `if (1) {}` did.
- **1818's last two words**: store the field first, then the m home, and test the LOCAL (`if (n >= 12)`; the else-if
  keeps the field re-read). Spelling the call argument `m[0] + o->0x44` put m's load first (t5).

Open: mgrproc 1824 (the outer two-case switch keeps `li at,1` hoisted above the beqz in every spelling tried -- switch,
default arm, goto chain, nested if; the jtbl at RoData +0x5B8 also needs the module's earlier RoData in front of it in the
built .rodata, see #game-uso-rodata-relayout-late-rodata); 125C/1C90 FP pair (`mtc1 255` vs field load register swap,
operand order is normalised); game_uso 7C1C (13 insns short; its frame is 80 bytes small after the run-103 member-wise
copies -- pads at the documented gaps overshoot by 56 because the trailing scalars p/q/node/k/metric/thresh/tx/tz take
homes at the bottom; objdiff ignores frame offsets, so this does not move the score).

## kit XII (agent-c 2026-10-20, run 112): spilled plain local vs volatile, `(void)&x` no-op, sign-test bit tests, per-site void and adder sweeps <a name="kit-xii-agent-c-run112"></a>

**1. A spilled plain local, not `T * volatile`, for the memory-resident web in a cfront constructor (timproc_uso_b1_func_0000097C EXACT, 94.96 -> 100).**
The b1 twin of timproc_b3 0994 keeps its level-2 object pointer in a stack home
(`sw a3,48(sp)` in the bnez delay, `lw a0,48(sp)` / `lw t9,48(sp)` after the joins),
which earlier passes read as `char * volatile o2`. Ported to the b3 0994 / mgrproc E04
skeleton (nested `oN = oN-1; if (oN-1 || (oN = alloc(n)))` inlined base ctors, void
registration alias, one reused local o1), the volatile spelling put the `obj + 16` home 4
bytes low (0x20 vs 0x24) and the whole t-ring started one register late (t6 vs t7: volatile
spends an extra temp); a separate named alloc temp on top of it added two more frame words. The
plain `char *o2;` is spilled around the calls into exactly that home, and inside a block
uopt still uses the just-stored register value (the 0xE0 guard tests v0 and passes v0 in the
jal delay, `or a0,v0,zero`), which volatile can never do. Tell: a "memory variable" that is
also forwarded from its register within a block is a spill home, not volatile.

**2. `(void)&x;` is a no-op in IDO cfe.** It does not make `x` address-taken (097C stays
exact with it removed; it was inert on game_libs 41820, 372D4 and bootup E270). A real
address-taken local needs a live use of the address, e.g. `T **p = &x;` (gl_func_000372D4's
`int **po = &o;` is what homes `o` at 0x1C there).

**3. Bit tests: the sign-test spelling, and inline re-reads for ring temps (h2hproc_uso_func_000017A0 EXACT, 95.66 -> 100).**
The target tested bit 16 of `parent->0x4F0` as `sll t7,t6,15; bgez t7` and every later
temp was one ring register ahead of ours. `(((u32)x << 15) >> 31)` is folded to the same
sign test but its dead `srl` temp is still numbered, so the whole t-ring shifts +1; write
`(x << 15) < 0`. Same function: `v->0x94`, held by the target in ring temp t4 across two
tests, must be re-read inline (`if (v[0x94/4] == 0) ... else if (v[0x94/4] != 0)`); a
named `p148` becomes a v1 candidate. The remaining shift was the void-callee case
(#feedback-ido-void-callee-kills-dead-v0-def): all 14 discarded-return gl calls go through a
void alias.

**4. Sweep the void-callee lever per call site, and try pairs.** `scripts/void-callee-scan.py --owner X`
flags functions; finishing them is mechanical: rewrite ONE statement-level call of the blank
callee (`gl_func_00000000`, `func_00000000`, `gl_func_00034458`, a local alias) to a
distinct `extern void NAME_XXXXv();`, rebuild only the NM .o, disassemble target and build
(`scripts/disasm-func.py F` / `--nm`) and score; repeat for every site, then for "all" and
leave-one-out. Results this run: gl_func_00037AF0 EXACT (only the registration call),
gl_func_0004C300 EXACT (only the `if (G240 == 0) cb(&D + 0x20138)` call: the else-arm temp
moves v1 -> v0 and its `lui v0` hoists into the beqz delay, the documented "4 word" residual),
gl_func_000201B8 gained only with sites 3 AND 4 voided together (each alone: no change), bootup
CFA0 only with all 19. Skip call sites that are casts or assignments (`(T *)f(...)`, `x = f()`):
the void alias does not compile there. Unwrapping needs `NAME_XXXXv = 0x00000000;` plus any
NM-only data aliases in undefined_syms_auto.txt, then `rm build/tenshoe.elf`.

**5. Sweep `if (1) {}` adder positions automatically.** Inserting one adder after each
statement end of the NM body (one NM .o rebuild per position, about 1.5 s for post0b) found
gl_func_000372D4 98.10 -> 99.66 (adder right after `p = o->F4 + 0x30;`, restoring the
`addiu v1,v1,48` rebase between the stores) and gl_func_000432BC 96.61 -> 97.59 (after the
first `it.next = *(D + 0x18C);`). The same sweep was flat on 3E9C8, 4247C, 4EE44, 437C0,
1DA7C, bootup E270, 0610, BF8C and D900: their residuals are not hold-vs-reload.

**Open residuals noted this run.** gl_func_0003800C: the last call `o->0x20 = gl(o, n)` has
no a0 setup at all in the target (a0 still holds o from the previous `gl(o, 0)` as far as
the code goes), so the original's first argument was probably an undefined value; an
uninitialised local gets a home and a reload instead. gl_func_00039E24: the target
materialises `&D_b` into a2 and copies it to a0 for the call (one CSE candidate shared with
the post-call `lwc1 0x128(a2)` loads); ours builds a0 directly. gl_func_0003E9C8: each
by-value key copy spends a temp (no copies: t1, two named copies: t3, target: t4).

## kit XIII (agent-c 2026-10-20, run 113): split-OR ring burn, list-head block burn, delay-slot result decode, cross-function NM scoring, lever-sweep.py <a name="kit-xiii-agent-c-run113"></a>

**Split OR constant burns one ugen ring slot (bootup func_00003B78 EXACT).** After the
3734/38C0 levers (void alias for the reg call, merged $s0 web, array-typed config base, four
volatile ghost pads) the only residual was every temp from the flag chain onward numbered one
ring slot early (`lbu t7 / ori t8 / or t9 / or t0` vs target `t8/t9/t0/t1`). Spelling the
flag constant `(c | 1 | 0x8000) | 0x10000 | 0x40000` instead of `(c | 0x8001) | ...` gives
identical instructions but the folded intermediate consumes one ring register, and the
whole function matched. `(c | 0x8000 | 1)` and `((c | 1) | 0x8000)` also work;
`c | 0x8001 | 0x50000` and `| (0x10000 | 0x40000)` do not. Same family as the
`(unsigned char)` switch-selector burn (#uchar-switch-selector-ring-burn-jumptable-donor-44b78):
a constant the front end folds late still costs a ring slot.

**`if (1) {}` after the list-head load burns two ring slots (game_libs_func_000430D8 EXACT).**
The 2026-09-09 NM was 107/107 by mnemonic with 45 words off by t-register only (target two
slots later). `scripts/lever-sweep.py --blocks` found that one emission-free block right after
`p->next = <list head>;` closes it. Why exactly two slots is not understood; the sweep is the
way to find these.

**A `sw v0,X(s0)` in the delay slot of the NEXT jal stores the FIRST call's result
(gl_func_0004DDF8 EXACT).** The old decode read `call(n); o->2C = o->30 = call(n);`; the
target is `o->2C = call(n); o->30 = call(n);` -- the delay-slot store runs before the second
call. The wrong decode also pushed the shared `a1*4` CSE spill from 0x24 to 0x20, which looked
like an allocator cap.

**NM-build objdiff scores move for functions you did not touch.** In game_libs_post0b,
gl_func_0004D688 read 74.61, 75.03, 75.19, 72.50 or 72.92 depending on which `if (1) {}`
adders sat in OTHER functions (3B01C, 40070, 42938, 46050 ...), while its NM .o text and
relocations stayed byte-identical (`objdump -dr` over the symbol, diffed). Blank lines change
nothing. So it is an objdiff scoring artifact of the shared NM object, not codegen. Practical
rule: after applying several lever wins to one unit, rebuild that unit's NM .o and compare the
SUM of fuzzy bytes over the unit, not per-function deltas; drop a hunk only if its removal
raises the sum; and before chasing a "regression" in an untouched function, diff its
`objdump -dr` first.

**`scripts/lever-sweep.py --void / --blocks`** (committed run 113) runs the two cheap levers
on any NM function in-tree: it edits the real source, rebuilds only that unit's
build/non_matching .o (with the post0b text clip disabled so shrinking variants still build),
scores with `objdiff-cli diff -c functionRelocDiffs=none` (the report's number), always
restores the source, and prints or writes (`--patch-dir`) the best variant as a git-apply
patch. `--from-report 90 --units a,b` batches; unrelated units can run in parallel from
copies of the worktree (tar the tree minus episodes/.git into scratch). Run-113 batch over
130 NM functions >= 90%: 35 functions gained (+37.4 fuzzy points, every applied win an
`if (1) {}`), one exact (430D8); on the five big partials it added +2.6 (bootup 6808), +2.4
(46050), +0.8 (42938), +0.2 (E68). The void
mode skips function-like macros (`DISPATCH_X(...)` would otherwise be renamed) and callees
already declared void, and copies the callee's prototype params into the alias so float
promotion does not change.

**Every declared local homes a frame word -- including block-scoped ones in sibling
blocks; byte-typed locals pack.** gl_func_000454C4 (frame 0xB8 vs target 0x58): four unused
`int` declarations add 16 bytes, two sibling blocks `{int a;} {int b;}` add 8 (no slot
sharing), eight `u8` locals add 8. So the original had about eight declared words in total
(two of them the memory-homed `{cur,next}` iterator at 0x3C/0x40), and the gbi-style
display-list appends cannot each have had a block-local pointer. Rewriting with eight
declarations reaches frame 0x58, but the expression forms needed to drop the other names
cost more than the frame gains (60.5 vs 61.7), so the NM was left as is.

**gl_func_0003B1AC is not a boundary twin of game_libs_func_0003B1A8; it is the same
function (open).** twin-finder scored 3B1AC <- 3B1A8 at 0.994 because 3B1A8's .s IS 3B1AC's
.s plus the head word: the function really starts at 0x3B1A8 with `lw v1,0x8C(a0)` hoisted
above `addiu sp`, and the report credits 3B1A8 (324 B) at 100 through the folded INCLUDE_ASM
while 3B1AC (320 B) reads 0. But gl_func_000276E4 jals 0x3B1AC directly (baked `0x0C00EC6B`),
skipping the v1 load, so a C body for 3B1A8 alone leaves the mid-function entry for 276E4 to
resolve (an absolute undefined_syms pin) and needs the expected/ symbols re-bounded. The body
is a matrix-apply loop: `p = e->v` (word copy), `q[3]` float array (so the stores survive)
filled from p, x/y/z temps of `m[0..2] * q + m[4..6] * q + m[8..10] * q + m[12..14]`, written
back to q, then `v->x += q[0]` etc. Best probe 42 diff lines of 162 (frame 0x48 and every
slot exact with `float q[3]; int pad2[2]; V3 p; int pad1[2];`); the residual is the operand
order of the final `+ m[12]` / `+ m[14]` adds and a forwarded q[0] (target reloads it).
Probe C in scratch only; nothing committed.

## -O1 frame slots follow declaration order, `register` locals included (agent-g 2026-10-20, run 112) <a name="ido-o1-decl-order-register-ghost-run112"></a>

At -O1 every non-register local is memory-resident. Locals are laid out top-down in declaration order, and a `register` local also
reserves a 4-byte slot at its declaration position, even though it lives in an s-register and nothing is ever stored there. The kernel
rmon pair func_80008E98 / func_80008FF4 (filed as "allocator slot-ordering caps") matched once the declarations were
`register s32 *msg = arg0; <reply struct>; void *ctx; s64 *src; register s32 i;`. With `register i` second, every memory slot sits 4
bytes lower, and an extra pad grows the frame instead of shifting the slots. Same mechanism as the -O0 rule
(#ido-o0-decl-order-slot-lever-register-reserve-plain-home-alias). Details and the other run-112 kernel fixes:
docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#kernel-plain-loops-run112.

## kit XIV (agent-c 2026-10-20, run 114): display-list append, RMW aliases, array-vs-struct homing, gbi macro clones, baked game_libs callees <a name="kit-xiv-agent-c-run114"></a>

1. **Display-list append = comma temp.** Targets that append through a `{Gfx *buf; int count;}` header show `lw dl; lw n,4(dl); addiu; sw 4(dl); lw dl` (the header is RE-READ after the count store) then `lw buf,0(dl)`. `&m->dl->buf[m->dl->count++]` makes IDO load buf BEFORE the store (one header load, wrong order). The source shape is `#define NEXT(m) (_n = (m)->dl->count++, &(m)->dl->buf[_n])` with a function-scope `int _n`, used as the `pkt` of real gbi.h-style macros (`{ Gfx *_g = (Gfx *)(pkt); _g->w0 = ...; _g->w1 = ...; }`). bootup func_00000E68 57.9 -> 85.1 from this alone; also gl_func_00046FA8 (fill-rect + pipesync, 70.9 -> 98.7) and bootup 1A44 (gSPMatrix, 28 -> 91). For a plain cursor (`gfx++`) use `{ G *_g = gfx++; ... }` per packet, not `p[0..7]` + `p += 8` (1D200 53 -> 89, 1D944/1D9E0 76 -> 97).
2. **Write the real gbi.h macro, not its expansion.** E68's sub-display-lists are `gDPLoadTextureTile` in the 2.0J form (SetTileSize `0, 0, (lrs-uls)<<2, (lrt-ult)<<2`, `line = ((lrs-uls+1)*TILE_BYTES+7)>>3`) with `uls = j*64, lrs = uls + 63`. IDO's reassociation of those expressions is what makes the target's odd shapes: a hoisted `63` stored to a spill slot and re-shifted every iteration, `subu t6,t1,t1; addiu t7,t6,31` for `(lrt-ult)`, and a held `71` that is shifted (`>>3 & 0x1ff << 9`) inside the loop. Hand-folded constants never reproduce them. Reference text: references/libreultra/include/2.0I/PR/gbi.h (F3DEX branch). The cull/vertex words tell F3DEX apart from F3D (`vstart*2`, `(n<<10)|(16n-1)`).
3. **Global read-modify-write: one zero alias per access site.** Standalone-verified: IDO -O2 ALWAYS materializes `lui/addiu base` into a register for `X |= k` / `X = X | k` on one global within a basic block (scalar, array or struct member, volatile or not, `if (1) {}` between load and store). A target that shows the folded `lui t9,0; lw t9,4(t9)` ... `lui at,0; sw t0,4(at)` pair was compiled with DIFFERENT symbols for the load and the store (USO imports resolve both to the same zero). The same holds across sites: if the RMW bases are held in s-regs in your build but not in the target, give every access site its own alias. bootup 6808: per-site aliases freed s4/s5 for the target's held globals (89.8 -> 91.4). The alias names need `= 0` lines in undefined_syms only if the body is promoted.
4. **Identities first.** For bootup/game_libs bodies, recover every `lui/addiu 0` / `jal 0` target before decoding: bootup.uso TextReloc (scripts/uso-reloc-symbolize.py walk_dir + build_relocmap at module 0xD9FE28) joined with scripts/emu-symdump/bootup_uso.symnames.json, and for game_libs baked jals `callee = (target << 2) - 0x1466C` (gl_func_0001DCB4's "K&R 0003443C emits" were gl_func_0001DA7C / 0001E134 / 0001D3E0 / 0001DB88 / 0001D4B0, whose short params explain the per-site sll/sra 16). Knowing which `lui 0` pairs are the SAME symbol decides which s-regs IDO can hold.
5. **f32 array vs 3-float struct.** A local `struct {f32 x,y,z;}` filled field by field and read back is scalarised into f-registers. A local `f32 n[3]` stays in memory, which gives the target's `swc1 f4,48(sp); lwc1 f4,48(sp)` store-then-reload per element, reloads `obj->ptr` before every element (the store might alias), and the right frame. bootup func_000003F8 80.2 -> 98.7 from the array alone. The vec that IS struct-copied (`d = *pos`) stays a struct.
6. **cfront constructor shapes** (bootup 31C0, 12E00, game_libs 4E600 EXACT, 4FBA4, 41D40): (a) the object is the PARAMETER (`if (a0 == 0) { a0 = alloc(N); if (!a0) goto end; }`); (b) the inlined base ctor re-tests `this` (dead second alloc), so write `t = obj; if (t == 0) { t = alloc(M); if (!t) goto skip; }`; (c) each member sub-object is one `m = this + OFF; if (m == 0) { m = alloc(sz); if (!m) goto next; }` (folded to `this == -OFF`) plus, for members with a base class, an inner `p = m; if (p == 0) {...}`; (d) a stack object constructed in place needs `p = 0; if (1) { p = &local; }` or the `this == 0` test folds away (41D40 77.8 -> 91.3); (e) vtable calls are `(*(fn *)(vt + 0x24))(obj + *(s16 *)(vt + 0x20), ...)`.
7. **FP centring terms.** `10.0f / 2.0f` folds in cfe and `x / 2.0f` becomes `x * 0.5f`. The target's runtime `div.s` by a materialized 2.0 comes from f32 locals divided by a CAST literal: `cw = 10.0f; ... cw / (f32)2` (bootup_uso_tail4 12E00).
8. **Many-BB functions keep everything homed.** Two emission-free `if (1) { }` before `return` took bootup 31C0 from s0/s1 locals to the target's all-in-frame form (74.3 -> 88.5; see #hold-vs-remat-firstusecost-run111). It saturates at 2.
9. **Measuring:** `objdiff-cli diff -u UNIT -o x.json FUNC` (a per-function match_percent in about 50 ms) counts every reloc-vs-baked operand as a mismatch. `objdiff-cli report generate` is lenient. A function at 99.27 in diff can be 100 in the report with byte-identical text (4E600: only relocs to zero-valued D_00000000/gl_func_00000000 differed; promoted, `cmp` clean). Use diff for A/B probes and the report for the verdict. Before promoting, check for a jumptable: gl_func_00023914 reaches 100 in the report but its C table lands in the unit's discarded .rodata (ld segfault), so it stays NON_MATCHING.
10. **Edits shift other functions' scores in the same TU.** This confirms kit XIII and adds that the NM symbol SIZES of untouched functions change too: post0b 61478 (agent-g) went 0x290 -> 0x2a0 and 88.9 -> 86.5, and 4D688 72.9 -> 74.2, with zero edits to either. Report the unit sum and flag the other owner.

## kit XV (agent-c 2026-10-21, run 115): reloc-table builder chains, addend-pinned aliases, local loop bounds, nested dot products, label refs, C++ in bootup <a name="kit-xv-agent-c-run115"></a>

1. **Builder chains (bootup 3D3C/3F00/43D4/411C, all EXACT from 58-89%).** Recover every callee and data base from the bootup.uso TextReloc first (`uso-reloc-symbolize.py` walk_dir/build_relocmap at 0xD9FE28 + emu-symdump names). The shapes that then fell out: (a) the two `new X(flag)` results go through ONE temp `t` (`t = alloc(0x80); if (t) ctor(t, 1); o1 = t; t = alloc(0x80); ...`), which is why the target keeps the second object in the s-reg and the first in the frame; (b) results that the target re-reads from the frame are an ARRAY (`char *o[2]`, `char *r[2]`): an array local is never scalarised, a scalar is promoted to an s-reg; (c) the cross link `r0->0x908 = r1; r1->0x908 = r0;` plus the first link call is a block with two temps `{ char *a = r[0], *b = r[1]; ...; link(..., a, o1); }` (a lands in a3, the call's 4th arg, with no reload); (d) the camera reads are inline per argument (a `cfg` local hoists the load) but the local must stay declared (it holds a frame word); (e) when the shared temp's priority beats a long-lived result, give the later roles (b3, f1) their own variables and, if still one colour off, an `if (1) { }` right after the copies (3F00 s2/s3 swap).
2. **Asm operands carry the real addend.** The reloc table names the import (`import_0005C108`) but the `.s` spells `%lo(func_00000008 + 0x2C)`: the ROM word is 0x34, not 0x2C, and the alias must be pinned at 0x34 (7EC8 failed `cmp` with a 0x2C pin while rawcmp showed "symbol names only"). Always grep the `%hi/%lo` operands of the target `.s` and pin each alias at symbol+K (seen: 0x34, 0x3C, 0x90, 0x294, 0x4F0, 0x54C, 0x8ABC, 0xA0, 0xE8, 0x128, 0x240, 0x254). Zero-valued imports take per-site aliases; an RMW on one import needs separate load/store aliases (kit XIV 3).
3. **A LOCAL loop bound keeps `slt`.** `do { ... } while (++k < 5)` is LFTR'd to `bne k, s4` even though 5 is held in s4; `n = 5; ... while (k < n)` keeps the target's `slt at,s3,s4; bnez`. Assign `n` right before the counter init (139B0). Zero inits written in the for-init AFTER an early return are still hoisted above the `beq` together with the next constant (that hoist is the target's shape; writing them before the test is not).
4. **Global float read once before a loop with calls:** `sc = D_00000C64;` in the preheader puts it in f24 (a global read inside the loop is reloaded after every call; a rodata literal has the wrong reloc).
5. **Dot products with the running sum as `add.s fs`:** write `z*nz + (y*ny + x*nx)` (last term first, inner pair reversed), then pin the first product's operand order with an assignment lever on the right factor: `nx * (t = d.x)` (3F8 99.5 -> 100 together with the f18 literal colour it fixed; 4F704 both sums). A float-array threshold `((float *)(a0 + 0x98))[a1]` gives `addu t1,a0,t0` (byte-offset spelling gives the reversed addu).
6. **Distinct aliases change alias analysis.** IDO proves two different extern symbols never overlap and hoists loads over stores; the target (one symbol, two base registers) keeps every reload after the store (76F4 residual). If the target re-loads after each store, look for both pointers being the same symbol.
7. **Named int for a tested field** (`on = a0->0x3C; if (on)`) gets a v-reg candidate where the inline test uses the t-ring (D94). A `^=` RMW followed by `if (word & 8)` re-reads nothing (the xor result is reused), matching a target with no named flag (E124).
8. **Asm `.L` labels referenced from OTHER functions.** func_00007328 / 000083D0 / 00006808 used `%hi/%lo(.L00007F90)`-style data addresses that are labels inside func_00007EC8's asm. Once 7EC8 is C the labels vanish and `mips-linux-gnu-ld` SEGFAULTS (no message). `objcopy -R .mdebug` on the object and re-running the link prints the real error (`undefined reference to .L00007F90`). Fix: repoint those operands to pinned `D_00007F90`-style symbols (same ROM bytes). Before promoting, `grep -rn "L0000<range>" asm/` for the function's address range.
9. **Trailing alignment nops.** A target symbol size that includes trailing `nop`s (13B20: 0x150 for 0x144 of code) needs an all-zero `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` on the build object and `NON_MATCHING_SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` on the NM object, or the report stays at 96% and the ROM shifts.
10. **bootup has C++ too.** Tells: (a) CAE8's Vec3 copies go `addiu v0,sp,36; lw/sw x3; lwc1/swc1 per field` into a temp BELOW every declared local (cfe cannot put a local there; 99.9 in C); (b) 485C's two vectors are stored from f12/f2/f0 with the homed arg reloaded into a2: under NCC `struct V3 { V3(float a, float b, float c) { set(a, b, c); } void set(float, float, float); }` reproduces every register (47/47 words, only the two vector slots differ: target b1 64 / b2 32, NCC gives 68/52 or 56/68 - the open temp-order item of #ncc-game-libs-vec3-62a2c); (c) 7328's list search keeps the iterator `{cur, next}` in the frame and copies the key through pointers held in s0/s1: an inline `Ent::is(Key k)` taking the key BY VALUE reproduces the copy; `first()` must not be `e = 0; if (cur) ...` (edg/uopt puts e in an s-reg).
11. **Makefile default goal.** Since the 62A2C donor rule, the first rule in the Makefile is `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o: $(DONOR)`; a bare `make` builds only that object. Use `make RUN_CC_CHECK=0 -j8 all` (a stale ROM then passes `cmp`).
