12. **Small-function spellings that closed 14010/14598/144F4.** (a) A byte walk the target addresses as `lbu v0,0xE4(s0)` with `s0 = a0 + i` is `(a0 + i)[0xE4]`, not `s[i]` off a hoisted `s = a0 + 0xE4`; read the byte inline at every use (`(u8)(a0 + i)[0xE4]` three times) - a named `unsigned char c` lands in v1 where the CSE'd inline read lands in v0. `for (i = 0; i < strlen(p); i++)` re-evaluates the call each trip like the target. (b) A float field loaded inside the first test as an assignment-expression, `if ((spd = o->f) < 16.0f)`, schedules the `mtc1` of the constant before the `lwc1`; a separate `spd = o->f;` statement does the opposite.

## game_uso 3AC0 under NCC: the shared staging slot is an inline-ctor parameter pool slot; edg new-expression and parameter-temp rules (agent-g 2026-10-21, run 115) <a name="ncc-3ac0-new-expr-param-pool"></a>

game_uso_func_00003AC0 (1044 B, cfe NM 99.97, capped by the "12 stagings through one slot" problem in
[#feedback-ido-struct-copy-staging-ptr-flip-ghost-slot](#feedback-ido-struct-copy-staging-ptr-flip-ghost-slot))
is twelve `arg0->add(new Item(name_k), -1)` statements. Under NCC this body is instruction-identical to the
target (261/261 with stack offsets masked; scratch `g115/3ac0/z5.cpp`, `v2.cpp`, `s1.cpp`):

```cpp
struct P { int v; };
typedef P Name;
struct Q { P p; Q(const P &x) { p.v = x.v; } };            // trivial copy ctor
extern "C" void game_uso_func_051E64(void *, P, int, int);  // base ctor, P by value
struct Item { char pad[0x28]; void *vt; char pad2[0x58 - 0x2C];
    Item(Q q) { game_uso_func_051E64(this, q.p, 0, 0); vt = &game_uso_D_807FEAA8; } };
#define NM(k) (*(Name *)(game_uso_D_807FEC70 + 0x680 + 4 * (k)))
... game_uso_func_052F70(arg0, new Item(NM(k)), -1); ...   // x12
```

What each piece does (all measured on this function):
- **`new T(arg)` with an inline cfront ctor and NO class-scope operator new** compiles to one
  `jal operator new(sizeof)`, `beqz v0` over the body, then the inlined ctor: the target's alloc / skip /
  init / vptr shape. A class-scope `operator new` forwarding to the import made edg emit the cfront
  `this == 0` re-test inside the ctor (a second alloc). The global operator new reloc is `__nw__FUi`; it
  needs the usual alias for a real donor.
- **The argument is evaluated into the inline ctor's parameter before operator new is called.** That is the
  target's `sw t6,36(sp)` in the alloc's delay slot.
- **Parameter slot classes.** A parameter of class type with a trivial copy ctor (Q above, or a POD) gets one
  pool slot reused by every expansion and allocated after the named locals, so it is the bottom slot
  (sp+36): the target's shared staging slot. A parameter whose class has a user copy ctor gets a fresh temp
  per call at the top of the frame (ascending). A POD parameter filled by struct copy is reused too, but 12
  struct copies into one variable turn every copy pointer-based (`addiu s1,sp,K` + lw/sw 0(s1)), the same
  >= 9 rule as cfe.
- **Passing to the out-of-line base ctor.** A class with a user copy ctor is passed by address (cfront ABI,
  `addiu a1,sp,K`); a POD/trivial class is passed by value (`lw a1,36(sp)` + the `sw a1,4(sp)` arg home).
  `*(P *)&n` on an `int` parameter loses the store to the parameter slot (the read is not seen as a use).
- **Open: the frame.** The target has twelve 4-byte slots at sp+108..64, first block highest, and frame
  112. Every form tried that reads the global name (`NM(k)`, an `extern Name names[]` element, `NM(k).v`,
  `d = NM(k)` with named locals) adds one ascending top temp per statement (first block lowest). Named
  function-scope locals do come out descending (first highest), but then the temp is extra (273 words).
  So the twelve target slots are named locals filled without that temp. **Closest form (n1.cpp):** declare
  each one in the OUTER function block right before its statement, `Q q0(NM(0)); add(arg0, new Item(q0), -1);
  Q q1(NM(1)); ...`. Outer-block locals are allocated at function entry in declaration order, so q0..q11 come
  out contiguous and descending (first highest) and the shared parameter slot stays the bottom slot
  (sp+36), all 261 instructions identical. Left: the target has six unused pool slots between q11 and the
  parameter (sp+40..60), this source two, so every q is 16 low and the frame is 96 vs 112. Extra int
  parameters (constant args), inline `set()` layers in Q's ctor, an inline vptr setter, a named `Item *`
  and `const P &get()` did not add slots in the right place (the last moves the parameter up instead).
  Block-scoped `{ Q q(...); ... }` allocates on demand and puts the parameter right under q0. Tried before
  that: Q(int) with `d.v` (v0 candidate), Q(P) by value, member init, user operator=, references,
  pointers, comma, block-scoped `Name n = NM(k)`.

**gl_func_0005062C (run 115):** deriving V3 from a POD `P3` and declaring `operator+(const P3 &, const P3 &)`
moves the first operator+ ctor temporary to the target's sp+336: 688/689 words. The return slot is the
last word (sp+348, target sp+356): the base-class conversions allocate their two pool slots before the
return slot, the target after it. operator+ as a member of V3 or P3, a const return, a sum ctor,
explicit `operator+(...)`, and reference/pointer locals inside operator+ were all no better.

## timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118 run 115: arg-store order before the jal (agent-g 2026-10-21) <a name="b5-4118-run115-arg-store-order"></a>

**timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118 (run 115, NM 98.34 -> 99.14, landed as NM).** The 99.02 literal/pad draft
plus one source change: store `FW(arg0, 0x3B8) = arg4;` BEFORE `FW(arg0, 0x3C8) = arg6;`. With the
original order as1 fills the `lw t4,940(sp)` load delay with the arg6 store (`sw a1,968(a0)` moves up one);
the target keeps it in front of the jal. 4118 is cfe, not NCC: its tail switch is a jumptable and edg
always lowers `switch` to a compare chain. Still open: block 1 materializes 1.0 before 0.5 (colours are
already right), and switch case 0 gets an arg0 split piece in v0 (target) where ours reloads per use.
Neither responded to same-line joins, `if (1) {}` after the call, case-body order, or the natural
`switch (FW(arg0, 0x3C8))` (that one turns into a beq chain plus a frame slot for the switch value).

## game_uso cfront-lowered constructors: 3AC0 (NCC, dead named locals), 3018 + 18FC (plain cfe, struct-copy stage temps + BB-split constants), 41C0 partial (agent-g 2026-10-21, run 116) <a name="cfront-ctor-stage-struct-copy-3018"></a>

**The model.** The game_uso alloc-cascade constructors look like cfront output compiled by cfe: every
per-stage temporary is a NAMED local declared at the top of the function (so they come out descending,
first stage highest), inline-function parameters are shared locals (one slot per name, the "pool"), and
the `this == 0 -> alloc` protocol is explicit. IDO 7.1 NCC (edg) allocates its temporaries ASCENDING
(measured: mem-init conversion temps, Vec3 argument temps, default-argument temps, `const &`-bound temps,
inline/out-of-line ctors, -O0..-O3: always ascending; only named locals and inline-function named locals
descend). So a function whose target has several descending per-stage temps is usually easier in plain
cfe with named locals (C48C, 3018, 18FC) than under NCC.

**3AC0 (1044 B, NCC donor) -- the 4 missing frame slots were dead named locals.** The run-115 draft
(`Q q_k(NM(k)); add(arg0, new Item(q_k), -1);` x12) matched all 261 instructions with frame 96 vs 112.
Adding `int z0, z1, z2, z3; z0 = 0; z1 = 0; z2 = 0; z3 = 0;` AFTER the twelve statements gives four
4-byte homes between q11 and the shared parameter slot: frame 112, byte-exact (kit XVI fact 6 applies to
outer-block declarations placed last too). Landing notes: the donor calls the global operator new, so the
Makefile rule renames it after NCC (`$(OBJCOPY) --redefine-sym __nw__FUi=game_uso_func_055750`, a symbol
name only) so the imported reloc names the expected import; and the old `.s` carried 3ED4's `.late_rodata`
word (pi at RoData +0x90), so the placeholder body returns `3.14159274f` to keep it -- without it
verify-blocks showed `lo16=4` on four later `%lo` sites.

**3018 (1164 B, 93.1 -> EXACT) and 18FC (1076 B, 91.2 -> EXACT), plain C.** Three source changes to the
run-106 cfe bodies:
1. Stage template copy: `T.w = G; prm = T;` (STRUCT copy) instead of `prm.w = T.w;`. With the member copy
   uopt loads the word into v0 and stores the shared `prm` first; with the struct copy the load stays in a
   t-reg and the per-stage slot store comes first, the shared store in the bne delay slot (both targets).
2. Frame: `s0` is the parameter itself (a `char *s0 = (char *)a0;` copy costs a top-of-frame home), then
   re-fit the int pads (3018: drop g8 and g7; 18FC: drop g8, g0[3], one int after o1). Watch the
   first-stage `addiu tN,sp,X` and the `sw a0,K(sp)` this-spill slots while moving pads.
3. The stage-1 FP constants: the target materializes 0 / -1000 / 1000 (18FC: 0 / 64 / -1000 / 1000) into
   `$f0` one after another, each followed by its three stores. In cfe all three got different registers and
   as1 regrouped the stores. Two things were needed together: put `if (1) {}` between the vector
   initializations (a basic-block split, otherwise the constants' live ranges overlap), AND spell the zero
   vector with int zeros (`hi.x = 0;`). With `0.0f` the zero is one CSE candidate with the stage
   `*(f32 *)(o + 0x10) = 0.0f` stores and stays live (it took $f12/$f2). Any one of these two alone did
   nothing; statement order, same-line joins, pointer-based stores and shared float locals were no-ops.
The NCC draft of 3018 (Big::Big() with M1/M member classes, out-of-line NodeBase ctor, Name(int)
conversion) reached the same instruction stream except the frame (ascending temps) and the same FP
constant schedule.

**41C0 (536 B, 94.2 -> 132/134 words, NM).** Same stage fix plus: the `new Outer` result lives in a temp
`x` that is reused for `a0->node` in the tail (target: both at sp+64, memory-resident, so `x` is escaped);
`p1 = x;` in the tail (v1, spill home 68); one `void *q` escape pointer for t1..t3 and x (separate escape
pointers each cost a bottom slot); the condition re-loads `a0->0x40` while the argument uses the earlier
load (3A28's trick: that is what put the node in v0). Left: the node store `sw v0,64` belongs in the
07ACE0 jal delay slot with the p1 spill before it; here they are swapped (tried: store before/after/inside
the call, same-line joins, p1 placement, escaping p1).

## timproc_b5 panel ctors (32C8, 2B74) on the 3018 recipe; the struct-copy count switch; 97EC as an NCC donor (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 117) <a name="struct-copy-count-pointer-switch-2b74"></a>

**Porting the 3018 recipe** ([#cfront-ctor-stage-struct-copy-3018](#cfront-ctor-stage-struct-copy-3018)) to
timproc_uso_b5 32C8 (370 words, 92.6 -> 366/370 words) and 2B74 (469 words, 95.9 -> 450/469), both NM:
- Per-stage `uK.v = NAME; nm = uK;` (struct copy) and the 3018 `if (1) { T *q = &u0; q = &u1; ... }` escape
  instead of the old dead `if (0) call(&u0, ...)` escape. With the dead call every copy went pointer-based.
- Rows whose target order is `lui tA; addiu tA,vt; addiu tB,K; sw tB,16(a0); sw tA,12(a0)` want the vtable
  store written FIRST (`FW(c,0xC) = vt, FW(c,0x10) = K, FW(c,0x14) = 0`): source order picks the register
  numbering, as1 still emits the 0x10 store first.
- One function-scope `c` for all 0x18 children (target's shared home), separate `cA` / `cB` for the 0x20
  vec children; block-scoped `register char *c` per stage gives one home per block.
- Frame: the int pads move between "above c" and the bottom; a `f32` named local can add 8 bytes of frame
  (rounding), so re-check `addiu sp` after every new float local.

**The struct-copy count switch (2B74).** With 12 stage struct copies `nm = uK;` into the same `nm`, uopt
stops addressing nm directly and holds `&nm` in a callee-saved register for every copy and every by-value
argument read (`addiu s1,sp,172` up front, `sw t0,0(s1)` / `lw a2,0(s1)` at every stage, frame and saved
regs change). With 11 copies everything is direct, byte-for-byte like the target. The target has 12 stages
plus two more copies into nm, so its source did not have 14 plain struct copies. A form that gives the
target's words for a stage without counting: `uK = *(struct T *)((char *)&G + off); nm.v = uK.v;` (struct
copy from the global INTO the stage temp, member copy into the carrier: `lui tN; lw tN; sw tN,uK; sw tN,nm`).
The member form `uK.v = NAME; nm.v = uK.v;` is NOT equivalent (v0 and the nm store first). In the two vec
blocks the target reloads the stage temp (`lw t8,232(sp); sw t8,172(sp)` after the cp copies): that is
`uK = *(T *)&G;` before the vectors and `nm.v = uK.v;` after the cp copies. 32C8 has only 10 copies and
never hits the switch.

**Vec-child values (2B74).** The target loads both vec constants and materialises the zero before any
store (`lwc1 $f2; lwc1 $f12; mtc1 zero,$f0`, then the nine stores). Writing `vA.x = L; vA.y = L; ...`
gives the 3018 shape (one `$f0` reused per vector). Assigning named floats like cfront inline-ctor
parameters, `f = L11C; g = L120; h = 0;` then the stores, and in the second child
`(c = alloc(0x20)), (f = L124), (h = 0), (g = L128), (c != 0)` / after the 04A188 call `f = L12C; g = L130;
h = 0;`, reproduces all of it except the colour of g vs the zero (target zero=$f0, g=$f12; here
swapped, insensitive to declaration order, assignment order and int / float zero spelling). 32C8's
residual is the same kind: l134 takes $f0 instead of $f2.

**97EC as an NCC donor (71.9 -> 99.14, NM-only splice).** `XZ a(w->vel); XZ b(w->other->vel);
XZ e((a - b) * k); XZ f(w->other->pos - w->pos);` with the 6A30 classes (`XZ : Vec3`, inline class
operator new to the import, `XZ operator-(const XZ &) const { return XZ(x - v.x, z - v.z); }`) gives
every word except: (1) two edg temporaries of the e statement swap homes, and (2) the FP colouring that
follows. The target's `swc1 m2,32(sp)` ... `lwc1 m2,32(sp)` spill plus the DUPLICATED f.x / f.z loads in
the dot/cross tail come from an ESCAPED |e|^2 local (`float m2 = ...; float *pm = &m2; t = dot / *pm;`):
the store to an address-taken local kills the CSE of the earlier f loads. What we measured on edg temp
placement (`-g3` + scratchpad mdebug.py): temporaries are hoisted to the top of the enclosing block as
`__V<address>` locals in REVERSE creation order, before the block's named locals; for
`XZ e((a - b) * k)` the materialised `(a - b)` always lands above the `* k` result bound to the ctor
parameter. The target has them the other way round. No spelling tried flips that: free or member
operators, `.scaled()`, copy-init, `const Vec3 &r = ...`, member-init temporaries, preceding dummy
functions. A named `XZ d = a - b;` puts B above d but costs the B chain its private middle slot. A named
`Vec3 dp;` (assigned) fixes the C chain's position.

## kit XVI (agent-c 2026-10-21, run 116): bootup_uso is C++ -- five NCC donors; edg block-scope slots, same-line schedules, virtual-call colouring, dead-store frame slots <a name="kit-xvi-agent-c-run-116"></a>

bootup_uso takes IDO 7.1 NCC (`.cpp`) donors exactly like game_uso / game_libs
([MATCHING_WORKFLOW #game-uso-ncc-cplusplus-donor-recipe](MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#game-uso-ncc-cplusplus-donor-recipe)):
`REPLACE_FUNC_BODY += func_X=$(DONOR)` on `build/src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso.c.o` (+ the NM object) over a
placeholder C body. bootup_uso is not Yay0-packed, so `cmp tenshoe.z64 baserom.z64` is the byte gate and
verify-blocks is unaffected. Blank (USO-relocated) refs keep using pinned aliases in undefined_syms; a
callee or datum whose expected reloc names a real bootup symbol (`func_00000080 + 0x20`,
`func_0000023C + 4`, `func_00000008 + 0x20`) can be referenced by that name directly (`extern "C" char
func_00000080[];`) and the reloc then matches the expected object's name. Landed this run: CAE8 (99.94),
485C (94.1), CFA0 (99.03), E740 (26.4), E800 (87.8), all instruction-exact.

**Tells, in order of reliability:** a real virtual call (`lw vX,0x28(o); lw t9,K+4(vX); lh tN,K(vX);
jalr t9; addu a0,tN,o` -- vptr at +0x28, slot (K-8)/8); a Vec3 copied through a stack temp then per field;
the cfront `this == 0` alloc protocol; a cfe NM whose only residual is frame slots, a v-reg swap around a
hand-written dispatch, or hacks like `volatile` locals / `if (1) {}` that a C++ inline would explain.
The CAE8..E800 region (rider state object) is all C++; so are the alloc cascades (B1B4, 90CC) and
h2hproc's 0620 (an out-of-line cfront ctor).

Facts measured this run:

1. **Block-scope named locals are allocated when the block opens, after the pool slots of earlier
   inline calls** (485C). `V3 b1(...); f(&b1); { V3 b2(...); f(&b2); }` puts b2 at sp+0x20 under five pool
   slots; the same b2 at function scope sits right under b1 (sp+0x34). Use an inner block to push a named
   local below the inline temps; function-scope names are homed top-down in declaration order first.
2. **One source line = one as1 scheduling unit.** 485C: b2's constructor and the call on one line
   (`V3 b2(...); f(STR, &b2);`) put the a0 `%lo` before the x store; on two lines the store went first.
   E800: `f(&g4); *(void **)(func_00000008 + 0x20) = &v;` on one line gives the target's
   `addiu t6; lui v1; lui at; sw t6; addiu v1`. Same mechanism as cfe's same-line pairs
   (#same-line-store-pair-schedule-35440), and it works under NCC too.
3. **A hand-written vtable dispatch costs colours; a real virtual call is free.** CFA0's cfe NM (54 words
   off) had `o`/`vt` locals for three dispatches; `(*(VO **)(st + off))->f()` with
   `struct VO { char pad[0x28]; virtual void v0(); virtual void v1(); virtual void f(); }` gave the
   target's v1/v0 pair at every site.
4. **edg operand order.** Compares come out reversed relative to cfe for the same `beq` (CFA0:
   `st->0x8DC == CTX` loads CTX first). Every `a * b` product of two memory loads also loads in the
   opposite order (BF8C: swapping all products fixed 23 words at once). Port a cfe body, then flip compares
   and products before anything else.
5. **Colour a post-call reload a0 by first defining the variable as the call argument** (CFA0):
   `r = probe(ctx = CTX, ...); ... ctx = CTX; changed = (ctx->0x98 < out) || ...` -- the context pointer
   web is constrained to a0 by its first def, so the post-call reload lands in a0 (v1 otherwise).
6. **Frame slots under edg are bought with named locals, even dead ones.** Every referenced named local
   gets a 4-byte slot whether or not it is register-allocated; an unreferenced one is dropped. CFA0's three
   missing slots came back with `dst = 0; o = 0; vt = 0;` (dead stores, no code). CAE8: `int mode = g;
   switch (mode)` and two named destination pointers took the frame from 64 to 80 without code change.
   E800: a named `root` declared first moves z/x/y from 44/40/36 to the target's 40/36/32. Conversely
   B1B4 lost its extra 16 bytes by dropping named `t`/`n`/`buf` (and a block-scoped `n` sits below the
   spill homes). Check with `-g3` `.mdebug` names (a 40-line parser of the local SYMR table is enough).
7. **Copy loops: step the source pointer per element.** E740 (26.4 under cfe with a hand x4 body):
   `for (x = 0; x < 64; x++) { *dst++ = *src; src += 4; } src += 0x540;` lets IDO unroll x4 into the
   target's 0/8/16/24 offsets with one `addiu v1,v1,32`.
8. **Splices drop INCLUDE_ASM padding.** E740's `.s` carried three file-end pad nops (E7F4..E800); the
   donor body is 0xB4, so everything after shifted until `func_0000E740=0x0,0x0,0x0` went into both
   SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE lines (all-zero pad, legal). A Makefile variable change does not rebuild the object:
   rm the `.o` files.
9. **cfront chains (h2hproc 0620, B1B4).** The 0xF0 "Thing" built after the cascade is `new Thing` with a
   POLYMORPHIC out-of-line base (`struct R1 { char pad[0x28]; R1(); virtual void r0(); }; struct Thing :
   R1 { char t[0xC4]; Thing() {} virtual void r0(); };`): the base ctor call comes first, then the
   derived vptr at +0x28. A non-polymorphic base puts the vptr after Thing's own data (+0xEC), and an
   intermediate polymorphic class adds a second `this == 0` alloc. The class-scope operator-new rule is
   agent-g's (#ncc-3ac0-new-expr-param-pool): use the global operator new (`__nw__FUi`, alias 0).

**Open (all scratch in `c116/`):** B1B4 is one 4-word colour off under NCC (the table counter reads into
v0, target a1; block-scope/register/unsigned/inline-helper/param-reuse spellings all v0). 41EDC and 7328
share a `{cur, nxt}` list iterator whose loop-bottom `next()` colours the nxt temp v0 (target t7 + a
pre-zeroed v0 result); the entry copy matches. 437C0 (stack `Derived obj` with the 0x60 Base of B1B4)
keeps the Derived `this` as a separate first pool slot, so the protocol var lands at sp+68 and colours a2
(target sp+72, a1). D900's clamp and BF8C's if/else FP ring give the same residual under NCC as under cfe.
h2hproc 0620 reaches the target structure (cfront chain, polymorphic Thing) but colours the level-2 `this`
s0 where the target spills it through a shared home. 48AEC (game_libs, iterator with protocol + Mtx/Gfx
inline appends) is 511/519 words structurally; it needs the iterator class to derive from a base for the
`this == 0` check and an `inline void pushMtx(void *src)` for the two matrix arms.

## kit XVII (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 117): registry add(), the list iterator, smart-pointer homes, NCC switch/temp facts <a name="kit-xvii-agent-c-run-117"></a>

Seven NCC (`.cpp`) donors landed: bootup func_0000B1B4 and func_00007328, game_libs_post0b gl_func_000372D4,
gl_func_00038964, gl_func_0003D48C, gl_func_00038598 and gl_func_00038728 (post0b below 0x50000 takes donors
exactly like 62A2C; re-probe the post0b NM clip after every post0b splice, it moved 0x2e7a4 -> 0x2e7e4).

1. **An inline method's expression temp can colour an argument register.** B1B4's last four words were a
   table counter read into v0 (target a1). The table and its count share one symbol (`func_00000148`:
   five slots + count at +0x14), so it is a registry object with an inline
   `void add(Base *b) { if (n >= 5) error(); Base *o = b; tbl[n++] = o; }`. The `tbl[n++]` expression temp
   lands in a1; a named `int k = n` lands in v0 (every spelling of the cfe and earlier NCC ports). The dead
   `Base *o = b` copy is what buys the edg frame slot that moves the later v1 spill from 28 to 24.
2. **The `{cur, nxt}` list iterator (38964, 3D48C, 7328; 41EDC open).** A stack pair at sp+N/N+4 walked
   with a pre-zeroed v0 result and the nxt load in a t-temp at the loop bottom is
   `struct Iter { Link *cur, *nxt; Iter(Link *h) { nxt = h; } T *next() { return (cur = nxt) ? (nxt = nxt->next, cur->obj) : 0; } T *get() { return cur->obj; } };`.
   Advancing through `cur->next` gives the same top copy but the bottom copy colours the nxt load v0 and
   zeroes v0 in the else arm (11-21 words off). The owner pointer kept in its incoming home (`sw a0,32(sp);
   lw a1,32(sp)`) comes for free. 7328 also needed `matches(Msg m)` taking the message BY VALUE (the copy
   through a hoisted `addiu s1,sp,52`).
   **Finding more:** the iterator's signature is `beqz tX; sw tX,N(sp); lw tY,4(tX); sw tY,N+4(sp); beqz zero;
   lw v0/v1,0(tX)`. post0b 0x34890..0x49B3C carries about twenty of them (34890, 3863C, 38DC0, 39094, 393B8,
   3D2C8, 3DA14, 3DBEC, 3DDC0, 3DE48, 3E1B0, 40974, 40E90, 41A9C, 432BC, 478FC, 47F9C, 49B3C; 40640 has a
   jumptable so it is cfe). 38598 and 38728 matched on the first port. Also: an object call whose `this` is
   loaded into a1 and copied to a0 (`lw a1,12(a0); jal; or a0,a1`) is an inline `Sub::lock() { f(this); }`
   (38728); a plain `f(o->sub)` loads straight into a0.
   **Open in the family (v0/v1 class):** 41EDC and 3D2C8 colour the first next() result v1 and the get()
   object v0 in the target (we get v0 / v1); 3863C puts the vptr in a2 (target v0); 3DDC0/3E1B0 compare the
   v1 copy of the result (we compare v0); 3DE48/3DA14 keep the result in v0 and the loop object in a copied
   a0 (we colour the result a0 directly; their Manhattan sum also needs `z + (x + y)` under edg).
3. **A dead store of a loaded pointer to a frame slot (`lw t6,20(a0); sw t6,28(sp)`, never reloaded) is a
   one-pointer smart-pointer aggregate local**: `struct Ptr { O *o; O *operator->() { return o; } }; Ptr p;
   p.o = s->att; p->node->...` (372D4). An aggregate local lives in memory, so the initialising store
   stays; cfe needed `int **po = &o`.
4. **An x store at base+K before `addiu base,base,K2` and the y/z stores at small offsets after it** is an
   inline member setter on a sub-object (`Sub::setPos(const V3 &v) { pos = v; }` with this = p+0x30).
5. **NCC never emits a jumptable** (IDO 7.1 NCC at -O2 lowers every switch to a beq chain, even 8 dense
   cases). A function whose target has a jumptable is cfe C, whatever its by-value Vec3 temps say
   (40304/40640 are C).
6. **NCC lays temporaries out ascending; edg's mem-initializer temps come out in REVERSE order** (three
   `Key(D)` conversion temps in one ctor: D1 at the lowest slot). Constructor-shaped bootup functions whose
   per-member temps descend (8124: key temps 64 then 60; 90CC: sp144, sp140, ...) are therefore cfe C that
   emulates cfront output, not NCC (agent-g reached the same verdict on game_uso 3018/18FC, see
   #cfront-ctor-stage-struct-copy-3018). 8124 under NCC is 2 words off: everything else, including the
   Kid::attachTo(this-checked) tail and two Leaf named locals for the frame, matches.
7. **Frame slots under edg, more measurements.** A function-scope named local declared after a loop is
   still homed with the function-scope names, above every block-scope local; moving it into its own block
   drops it below (7328 `mode`). Inline function parameters do not get slots; inline by-value class
   parameters do (the copy). A named local in an inline called twice adds two slots (8124's Leaf).
8. **Asm `.L` refs into a function you replace** (repeat of kit XV #8, hit again on 7328): 27E8, 31C0 and
   2DA4 pointed `%hi/%lo(.L00007350 / 7398 / 7490 / 73EC)` into 7328; repoint them to pinned `D_` symbols
   before the link (ld segfaults silently otherwise). `grep -rn "\.L0000<range>" asm/` first.
9. **Splice hazard: the last function's plain SUFFIX_BYTES skip.** Splicing B1B4 shifted trailing .text
   zeros behind bootup's last function, so the plain `SUFFIX_BYTES func_0000F1B4=...` skip path fired and
   the ROM came up 4 bytes short; F1B4 moved to SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE.

## kit XVIII (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 118): first() for the iterator entry call, inline members on the iterated object, frame slots from dead block locals <a name="kit-xviii-agent-c-run-118"></a>

Ten post0b list-iterator functions landed as IDO 7.1 NCC (`.cpp`) donors (REPLACE_FUNC_BODY, recipe as in
kit XVII): game_libs_func_0003DBEC, game_libs_func_0003DDC0, gl_func_0003E1B0, gl_func_00041EDC,
gl_func_0003D2C8, gl_func_00047F9C, gl_func_000478FC, gl_func_00040E90, gl_func_00040974 (matched on the
first port of the 393B8 matrix loop + 40E90 record copy, frame fixed with dead named ints) and
gl_func_0003863C (first() also moves the vptr after the second get() into v0).

1. **The entry next() through an inline `first() { return next(); }`.** With one `next()` used at the top
   and the bottom of the loop, edg reuses one pool temp for both calls, so at the loop head the loop variable
   equals that temp on every path and uopt copy-propagates every early use onto it: the compare reads v0
   instead of the v1 copy (3DBEC/3DDC0/3E1B0), or the body reads v0 where the target reads s0 (40E90), or the
   object pointer colours one register off (41EDC, 3D2C8). Routing the first call through a nested inline
   allocates a second return temp while next()'s is still live, the loop variable becomes a phi of two
   temps, and the target's `beqz v0; or v1/s0,v0` copy shape comes out. The tell is the top expansion: an
   explicit else arm (`beqz tN,L; ...; b L2; lw v0,0(tN); L: or v0,zero,zero`) where the bottom copy
   pre-zeroes. Cost: one more edg temp slot (frame +4/+8). It is not universal: 478FC (a non-leaf whose
   body keeps a `Flags &` pointer in v0) matches with plain next() and coalesces everything into s0 with
   first(); 432BC and 393B8 reach "instructions exact, frame +8" / "s0-s1 swap" either way (open).
2. **An inline member on the iterated object fixes the get()/vptr colours.** 41EDC's body
   `if (it.get()->flags & 4) it.get()->update();` coloured the object a1; the target's v0 object / v1 vptr
   comes from `it.get()->tick()` with `void tick() { if (flags & 4) update(); }` in the node class.
3. **Declare non-allocating callees `void`.** `extern "C" void *gl_func_00000000(...)` for every call makes
   uopt treat v0 as defined by each call; a later CSE'd base (41A9C's `&D_t1` pair) then avoids v0. Use a
   separate pointer-returning declaration (or an inline `operator new`) only for the allocating calls.
4. **Dead block-scope ints buy the bottom frame slots** (47F9C, 40E90): `{ int z0, z1; z0 = 0; z1 = 0; }` at
   the end of the loop body adds slots below the by-value V3 temp without code; function-scope dead locals
   (kit XVI #6) go above it instead.
5. **A body-scope reference to a flag sub-object** (`Flags &f = o->fl; ... f.set(2); ... f.clr(2);`) is what
   leaves the target's `addiu v0,s0,196` pointer in both arms (478FC); the same inline setters on
   `o->fl` fold to `196(s0)`.
6. **edg evaluates the three owner resets in reverse**: `ow->sel = 0; ow->cnt = 0; ow->any = 0;` stores any,
   cnt, sel (478FC).
7. **A large baked data address** (`lui s2,0x2; addiu s2,s2,-1680` hoisted, then `lw t0,0(s2)`) needs a
   symbol pinned at that address (`gl_d_0001F970 = 0x0001F970;` in undefined_syms); `*(int *)(D_00000000 +
   0x1F970)` makes uopt split the hoisted address into base 0x18000 + offset 0x7970, and a literal
   `(int *)0x1F970` gives `lui/ori`. objdiff scores the pinned-symbol reloc as a match.
8. **Callee names in donors must be the blank import** (`gl_func_00000000`), never the NM C's
   `gl_func_00034458` placeholder: the donor reloc then resolves to 0x34458 and the ROM differs at the jal
   (caught by the ROM cmp, not by the .o compare).
9. **Jumptable + C++ tells together = cfront output compiled by cfe.** 39094 has the iterator-ctor-before-lock,
   inline lock() and seven virtual calls, but a 9-way jumptable; NCC never emits one (re-measured at
   -O1/-O2/-O3 with dense 0..8 cases), so such functions stay cfe C.

**Open (scratch in `c118/w/`):** 41A9C (3 words: the D41 new-expression temp and the first next() share an
edg pool slot, a2 vs v0; first() gives v1); 432BC (instructions exact with first(), frame 112 vs 104: an
inline `set(float, float, float)` costs 8 bytes of pool slots); 393B8 / 38DC0 (matrix-multiply loop: the
hoisted constant 16 takes s0 before the loop variable, while 40974's target has exactly that order; with
first() the temps coalesce into s0); 3DE48 / 3DA14 (3 words: `add.s` operand order of the
Manhattan sum; also 3DE48's .s ends with 3DF5C's stolen `lw t6,16(a0)`, a boundary fix); 49B3C (array
iterator is a DERIVED class built through the cfront protocol on a stack temp, two by-value copies; colour
and frame residuals); 437C0 (stack Derived: Base `this` pool slot 4 low); 90CC (bootup, 422 diff words:
the tail colours, see its NM comment).


## kit XIX (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 119): NCC -O0 for bootup's -O0 islands, if/return next(), .mdebug frame maps <a name="kit-xix-agent-c-run-119"></a>

1. **bootup's -O0 islands are C++ too: compile the NM C body with NCC -O0.** The cfe -O0
   "return-value dead-double-b" gap ([#feedback-ido-o0-return-value-dead-double-b](#feedback-ido-o0-return-value-dead-double-b):
   a second dead `b epi; nop` before the epilogue after a `return` arm, from cfe's closing-brace
   marker) does not exist under edg: the same body built with `NCC -O0` is the shipped code. Eight
   exacts on the first try (func_00011E00/11ED4/11FA8, F81C, 11B5C, FC28/FD4C/FEE8), each a byte-
   identical recompile of the existing cfe NM body. Recipe: the body goes into a self-contained
   `extern "C" { ... }` .cpp (K&R `f()` externs become `f(...)`, `(*)()` casts become `(*)(...)`;
   scratch `mkdonor.py` in c119 does it), Makefile `$(DONOR): OPT_FLAGS := -O0` on the donor object,
   `REPLACE_FUNC_BODY += fn=$(DONOR)` on both trees of the unit, placeholder `{ return 0; }`, and the
   unit's TRUNCATE_TEXT copied to `NON_MATCHING_TRUNCATE_TEXT` (the NM tree no longer has the extra
   pairs either). One donor .cpp can serve several functions of a unit. Scan for more: compile every
   -O0 unit's NM TU as C++ and compare per function (`o0scan.py`). Other agents' -O0 units with the
   same gap (game_libs_mid, game_libs_o0_949C, mgrproc_uso_o0_19C, game_uso) are worth the same test
   if those segments are C++.
2. **An if/return `next()` gives each call its own return value.** `T *next() { if ((cur = nxt) != 0)
   { nxt = nxt->next; return cur->obj; } return 0; }` instead of the `?:` form: the loop variable is no
   longer copy-propagated onto the shared edg temp, so the target's `beqz v0; or s0,v0` comes out
   without first()'s extra pool slot (kit XVIII #1 cost +8 frame). gl_func_000432BC: first() gave
   instructions-exact at frame 112; if/return gives frame 104, exact. The top expansion still
   pre-zeroes v0 (`or v0,zero,zero; beqz tN; ...; lw v0,0(tN)`), same as the ?: form.
3. **Rebuild a cfe frame map from `.mdebug`, then add or delete named locals.** A `-g3` compile of the NM
   TU plus a .mdebug SYMR dump (c118/tools/mdebug.py) gives every name's offset; diff that against the
   target's sp offsets (compare relative to the frame top). In func_00006808 (frame 240, nine s-regs)
   cfe gave even unreferenced named locals a slot, in declaration order from the top, with block-scope
   locals below all function-scope ones, so two dummy declarations above e4, one before va/vb, op moved
   above v4C and no block-scope temps made every offset match the target. This is not universal: small
   functions whose named locals all live in registers get no slots (game_libs_func_0003D54C's cfe NM has
   six named locals in an 8-byte frame), so measure before relying on it. Under edg (kit XVI #6)
   referenced named locals get slots and unreferenced ones are dropped.
4. **`(T *)(int)&sym` keeps a global's address in an s-register.** `p = &g; *p = x;` is folded back to
   `lui at; sw x,%lo(g)(at)` by uopt; through an int cast the pointer stays a variable, held in a
   callee-saved register like the target's `lui s5; addiu s5; ...; sw t,0(s5)` (6808's post-loop
   D_776C/D_1EBDC pair). It costs registers elsewhere (6808: frame +8), so it is a lever to try, not a
   fix.
5. **The dead `if (v) {}` priority lever works under NCC too** (cf. #dead-empty-if-priority-boost-placement-is-everything-a7b4-d418-cracked-2026-07-03).
   gl_func_00038DC0 and gl_func_000393B8 (kit XVIII's "s0/s1 swap": the hoisted constant 16 of the matrix
   loop took s0 before the loop variable): `if (n) {}` as the first statement of the j loop adds
   loop-weighted refs to n, which then outranks the constant and takes s0. With first() + an if/return
   next() for the frame (38DC0), or the if/return next() plus one dead `int e0; e0 = 0;` beside src
   (393B8, the 40974 slot trick), both are exact. Placement matters: after the call, before the loop
   or at the end of the body did nothing; inside the innermost statement broke the unroll.
6. **Unconstrained candidates are coloured in first-occurrence (bitpos) order, so declare the loop
   variable early.** In game_libs_func_0003DB38 the regalloc dump (`ra.sh`/`ran.sh` with the
   diagnostic compiler copy) listed every candidate as `assigned (unconstrained)`: no priority lever can
   help there. The target's loop variable takes v0 and the next() temp a0; a dead `Node *n = 0;` before
   `for (n = it.first(); n; n = it.next())` makes n occur first and gives exactly that.
7. **An ABS inside a sum must be a macro, not an inline function, under edg.** game_libs_func_0003DE48
   and game_libs_func_0003DA14 sum `|dx| + |dy| + |dz|`. With `inline float adiff(a, b)` every one of
   the 12 operand orders and associations came out wrong: edg materialises inline-call results in a
   non-source order (`(x + y) + z` evaluated y, z, x) and the final add operands flip. With
   `#define adiff(a, b) ((a) < (b) ? -((a) - (b)) : ((a) - (b)))` the plain ?: expressions evaluate left
   to right and `x + y + z` is the target's x, y, x+y, z, (x+y)+z. 3DA14 also reads the position through
   `V3 *q = &n->pos` (the target's `addiu a1,a0,48` repeated in both ABS arms).
8. **IDO NCC accepts cfront's assignment to `this`** (`warning(3442): assignment to "this"
   (anachronism)`), and `new T(...)` on such a class calls no operator new: the constructor allocates.
   That is the literal cfront protocol `if (this || (this = alloc(sizeof(T), heap))) { ... }`, the shape of
   gl_func_00034890's three-level constructor chain whose protocol allocations all pass the heap
   argument. The ordering of the base-class calls relative to the assignment is not solved yet (scratch
   c119/w/34890).
9. **Boundary fix with a renamed successor** (game_libs_func_0003DE48 / gl_func_0003DF58): the
   predecessor's .s carried the successor's first word (`lw t6,16(a0)`), so 3DE48's real body is 68
   words and the successor starts at 0x3DF58. Move the word, rename the successor's .s/glabel/C, and
   adjust the expected/ object in place instead of running the whole-tree baseline refresh: shrink the
   predecessor symbol (and its `.NON_MATCHING` alias) by 4 and rename/re-base the successor pair
   (`scripts/rename-elf-symbol.py`, then a 20-line st_value/st_size editor, scratch `symedit.py`). ROM
   bytes are unchanged; the report then scores the 68-word body.

10. **Kit XX's source-order operands, refined: pointer + int is normalized pointer-first.** gl_func_00028A68
    (post) needed `addu t7,s0,v0` (off + base, the stored value) next to `addu t8,v0,s0` (base + off, the
    store address). `(int)(off + base)` still emits base first because edg canonicalizes pointer
    arithmetic; writing the value as an int sum `off + (int)base` and the address as a pointer sum
    `base + off + 8` gives both orders, and the two sums are then different expressions, so uopt keeps
    both addus (an int/int pair is CSE'd into one). The call argument `(char *)(off + *(int *)G)` is the
    same trick. Donor callees must stay the blank import (the `gl_func_0001CA10` name in the NM C baked
    0x1CA10 into the jal and the ROM cmp failed).

**Open (scratch in `c119/w/`):** 41A9C (the first next() shares the D41/E41 new-expression pool temp, so

## kit XX (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 118): NCC keeps source operand order; NCC -O0 for the -O0 extra-branch group; loop-IV lui order <a name="kit-xx-agent-g-run-118"></a>

1. **edg (NCC) does NOT canonicalize commutative operands; cfe does.** Standalone
   proof (IDO 7.1 -O2, same body): `*q = 41.0f + 5.0f * p[0x15]` -> cfe
   `mul.s f8,f4(field),f6(5.0); add.s f16,f8(prod),f10(41)` (constant always
   rt), NCC `mul.s f8,f4(5.0),f6(field); add.s f16,f10(41),f8(prod)` (source
   order). Same for `C0 + B8 * (double)(1.0f - *r)`: NCC gives the exact
   `mul.d f18,f16(B8),f10(cvt); add.d f6,f4(C0),f18` with the same register
   numbers as cfe, only rs/rt swapped. Integers too: `j + p[i]` -> NCC
   `addu v0,a2,t8`, cfe `addu v0,t8,a2`; `p + i*24 + 16` -> NCC base-first.
   IDO 5.3 cfe canonicalizes like 7.1 cfe (not a version difference).
   **So in any C++ unit (game_uso, timproc b1/b3/b5, mgrproc, arcproc, game_libs,
   bootup) a residual that is ONLY "operands of mul/add/addu reversed vs target"
   is the compiler front end, not the allocator: compile the same body with NCC
   and spell the operands in the target's rs,rt order.** timproc_b5 1DB0 went
   99.55 -> EXACT with the cfe NM body unchanged. A quick finder: diff every
   NM function and count `-`/`+` line pairs that are the same op with rs/rt
   swapped (agent-g run 118 scan: post0b 28A68 (1 line), 35E64, 3B01C are agent-c
   units with only that residue). Not universal: in 2B74/32C8/BBDC/C98C/1460 the
   residue is something else and NCC is worse (bodies tuned for cfe).
2. **NCC -O0 clears the "-O0 extra-branch" group outside bootup too** (kit XIX #1
   was bootup): game_libs_mid 8FFC/9100/8E48, game_libs_o0_949C 959C, mgrproc
   _o0_19C 700/A14, arcproc_o0 B4/12C all became EXACT from their cfe NM bodies.
   Donor rule: `$(DONOR): OPT_FLAGS := -O0` on the `.cpp.o` (the generic NCC
   rule passes `$(OPT_FLAGS)`). edg -O0 spelling differences vs cfe:
   - evaluation order is SOURCE order: `if (a0[2] == a0[1] + 1)` loads a0[2]
     first; write the side the target evaluates first on the left
     (`a0[1] + 1 == a0[2]`);
   - compound assignment through a pointer (`*p -= 1`, `p[1] += 1`) makes edg
     take the lvalue address into a fresh register (an extra s-reg + save);
     spell it `*p = *p - 1`;
   - K&R definitions must become prototypes; implicit-int returns `int f(...)`
     without a return statement are accepted.
   - NCC drops stores to an unused local array that cfe keeps (arcproc 125C's
     `ones[4]`): a unit whose target keeps such dead stores is cfe, not C++.
3. **The 9204/92F4 "s-reg promotion cap" was the 8FFC shape:** a plain `int obj`
   (home slot, sw v0 / lw s1 / return-from-home) + `register` base/o/tmp
   aliases + a base-0 alias symbol for the `&D + 8` read. Re-decoding the
   siblings on that shape and compiling with NCC -O0 = 60/60, 58/58.
4. **Placeholder hygiene for donor splices:** (a) if the old `.s` carried
   `.rdata`/`.late_rodata`, the placeholder must re-emit those bytes in order
   (1DB0: 14 state-name strings then its two doubles -- string literals and
   double constants in a dummy body; verify the host `.rodata` size); (b) do
   NOT keep INCLUDE_ASM as the host: replace-function-body then skips ("already
   matches donor") and the asm-processor `.NON_MATCHING` symbol makes objdiff
   report the function with no fuzzy (unmatched); (c) a donor that is 4 bytes
   short of the `.s` size where the `.s` ended with a nop = the alignment pad:
   re-add it with `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE := fn=0x00000000` (+ the
   `NON_MATCHING_` twin) -- all-zero pad, legal (959C).
5. **Loop IV materialization order (func_800009EC, last 2 words).** Two loop
   pointers whose `lui`s scheduled in the wrong order were cracked by changing
   which one is an induction variable: the second pointer is NOT a stepped
   variable but `&D_80013112 + i * 0x9C` in the call (uopt strength-reduces it
   into an IV created after `mod`'s), and the init is the comma for-init
   `for (mod = base, i = 0; i != 0x87; mod++, i++)` (a separate `mod = base;`
   statement, or `i++, mod++`, swaps the two `addiu` or moves the step into
   the bne delay slot). 240 statement orders of the stepped form had been inert.
6. **Regalloc dump caveat for FP constants:** `-zdbug:6` colours expression
   candidates (`uilod` loads used twice) and creates constant candidates after
   the itab (index > itab size); 32C8/2B74's residue is a constant zero coloured
   after the loaded floats (target: before). Moving the zero vector first makes
   it span both loads (gets $f12); `while(0)` boosts and int/float zero
   spellings did not reorder it. Open.

## kit XXI (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 119): the camera-homing V3 family under NCC; D9CC memory re-read; sweep results <a name="kit-xxi-agent-g-run-119"></a>

1. **The run-118 levers are exhausted in agent-g's units.** A scripted pass over every non-exact
   function (expected vs NM object, difflib on relocation-stripped disassembly, residue split into
   rs/rt-swapped commutative pairs, inserted `b`/`nop` groups, and everything else) found no
   function whose residue is only operand swaps and no -O0 unit with leftover extra branches.
   timproc_b5 BDEC has 8 swap pairs, but under NCC its `(float)255 / denom` (the cfe cast-literal
   CSE break, kit XI) folds back to `div.s f2,f20,f20`: edg folds the cast in the front end, and
   `255.0f`, `(float)255.0`, `(float)(int)255` and `(float)0xFF` all do the same. BDEC stays cfe.
2. **game_uso D9CC under NCC: re-read the field through memory.** The cfe body compiles under NCC
   to the same 17-word residue (two branch-likely sites plus the "andi temp coalesced into a1" t-ring
   cascade). Two edg spellings fix the cascade:
   `FW(arg0, 0x108) = (FW(arg0, 0x108) & 0xFFFF) | 0x60000; call(arg0, FW(arg0, 0x108), ...)` (no
   value local), and `if (FW(arg0, 0x108) != 0)` with no `temp_v0_4` local. That leaves 4 words:
   at the 3-way join before the `500.0f` test, the target keeps `beqz t8; nop` and `bc1f; nop`, and
   only the first gate uses `bc1fl` with the `lui` duplicated. Both compilers convert all three.
   These were neutral: nested ifs, `!= 0`, an `if (1) {}` adder, `goto` ladders, an else-chain
   instead of the goto, and a macro abs. In NCC, write the three `vol * FF(arg0, K)` products
   field-first (`FF(arg0, K) * vol`).
3. **game_uso 1DDC / 24BC / 28C0 / 2CC8 are NCC V3-class code (the "no s-reg -O2" shape).** Frame
   with only ra saved, the a0 param spilled around calls, and pointer locals homed and reloaded:
   NCC -O2 produces this on its own. The cfe bodies needed arrays and volatiles to fake it.
   Recipe (src/game_uso/game_uso_ncc_28C0.cpp, 250/250 words, frame and every temp home right):
   - V3 has a set-forwarding ctor, `operator+=`/`-=` returning `V3 &`, `void operator*=(float)`
     (the reference-returning `*=` shifts the else-arm block homes up by one slot), and
     `operator-` returning `V3(x - v.x, ...)`. That gives the target's ctor temp -> return slot ->
     named copy chain (120 -> 140 -> 172).
   - 023D4 returns V3 **by value**. The cfront ABI passes the hidden return pointer in a0 (that is
     the `addiu a0,sp,140`), and the int-copy into `r` is `r = f(src);` with `V3 r;` declared at
     the top.
   - The out/tgt pointer homes (sw at entry, reloaded in later blocks, never in s-regs) come from a
     local aggregate with an inline ctor: `struct Ctx { Body *tgt; Out *out; Ctx(Self *s) {...} };
     Ctx c(a0);`. The inline ctor takes `&c`. A plain pointer local gets s0. A struct without a
     ctor gets scalarized. A dead `if (0) touch(&out)` gives the right code but costs frame.
   - `matrix.getPos(v)` is an inline on the M4 sub-object at +0x70. That gives the odd
     `lwc1 160(v0); addiu v0,v0,112; lwc1 52(v0)` load pattern.
   - Pool slots: a named `float f = len * k;` with component `*=` puts the product in f0 (the
     target's register), and a dead `int zz; zz = 0;` at the start of the else block adds the pool
     slot that block's homes need.
   - Locate remaining layout errors with a role-aligned offset map: align the target and the build
     with stack offsets masked, then print target-offset -> build-offset pairs. One shifted group
     shows up as a constant delta.
   **Residual (28C0, 98.1):** `operator-`'s three results colour x f12 / y f0 / z f2, where the
   target has f0/f2/f12. The regalloc dump shows uopt colouring the ctor's first float param after
   the others and giving it colour 26. The out/tgt reloads use t-regs or a0, where the target
   splits the live range into v1. Not solved: ctor body assignment, mem-init, named locals inside
   `operator-`, a non-member operator.
4. **Other negatives:**
   - gl 5062C: a 60-combination ctor/operator sweep did not fix the return slot.
   - game_uso 97EC: a non-member `operator*` / `operator-` does not swap the two binding temps.
   - game_uso 41C0 under NCC has the same jal-delay store order as cfe.
   - gl 671E4: the `or a3,a0` copy is a real 4th call argument (`f(a0 + 0x11B0, &g, 1, a0)`); the
     store still schedules through a0, not a3.
   - gl 61B30 under NCC emits the target's `or a3,sp,zero; addiu a3,a3,47; and` va_start form
     natively, but the base-store sinking is unchanged.

## kit XXII (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 120): decode errors behind masked diffs, edg static initializers, permuter-as-colour-fixer, store + compound shift <a name="kit-xxii-agent-c-run-120"></a>

Fifteen exacts (58.86 -> 59.39 % code). NCC donors: gl_func_00043654, gl_func_00041A9C,
game_libs_func_0002F720, game_libs_func_0004E37C, gl_func_0004E584, h2hproc_uso_func_00001204.
In-unit cfe C: gl_func_000233E4, game_libs_func_0001D944, game_libs_func_0001D9E0, gl_func_00027D00,
gl_func_00047E00, gl_func_00025AC8, gl_func_000231B4, gl_func_00021D84, bootup func_000074E8.

1. **Diff tools that normalise branch targets (`L`) and jal targets hide decode errors.** Six of
   this run's "caps" were wrong C that only a branch-offset-aware diff exposed:
   - gl_func_000233E4 ("branch-likely cap"): the `bnez v0` skips BOTH calls; the NM ran the handler
     unconditionally.
   - h2hproc_uso_func_00001204: each clamp is NESTED inside its step (`if (a < 0xFF) { a += 16; if
     (a >= 0x100) a = 0x2D0; }`); both target branches skip to the shared tail.
   - gl_func_000231B4 and gl_func_00021D84: one path has NO return statement. The target jumps past
     the `or v0,zero,zero` straight to the epilogue, so the caller sees the last callee's v0. A K&R
     `int` function that falls off its end reproduces it (`if (!r) return 0; ...stores...; }`).
   - bootup func_000074E8: the final call takes no argument (the target only stores `p->0x48 = 0` in
     its delay slot; a0 is whatever the previous call left).
   - gl_func_00025AC8 ("USO-reloc cap") and 231B4: the callee is a baked USO jal; a
     `gl_ref_XXXXX = 0xXXXXX` pin in undefined_syms is the whole fix. The reverse trap: an NM body
     calling a real function name (`gl_func_00034458`) bakes that address where the target has jal 0.
   Compare branch offsets relative to the function's FIRST label. bootup's expected objects carry
   `alabel D_XXXX` symbols inside functions (and print their reloc tables out of place), so
   last-label-relative offsets are wrong there. Scratch `rdiff.py --raw --pins` keeps branch offsets
   and jal targets and applies undefined_syms pins to reloc'd HI16/LO16/26 fields. `clscan.py` ranks
   every near-miss by its non-jal, non-branch residue; branch-only and jal-only rows are the cheap
   ones.
2. **A no-argument function that runs the cfront `this == 0` protocol on a GLOBAL address is edg's
   static initializer (`__sti__<hash>`) for a global object** (gl_func_0004E584, 87.9 -> exact). Tell:
   `lui a1,%hi(G); addiu a1; or v1,a1; bnez a1` at the top, an alloc of the object's size when the
   address is 0, then member constructors with their own protocols. The donor is the class
   definitions plus `G obj;`; a dedicated Makefile rule renames the hashed symbol
   (`$(OBJCOPY) --redefine-sym $$($(CROSS)nm $@ | awk '/ T __sti__/{print $$3}')=gl_func_X $@`, after the
   3AC0 operator-new precedent). The object's relocs import as UND and resolve through the existing
   pin. The prologue tie (`or v1,a1` above `sw ra`) needed the declaration's `;` on its own line (as1
   ties the sti code to the declaration's last line). `stiscan.py` found no other non-exact one in
   agent-c's units.
3. **The permuter fixes single-colour residues** on NCC donors and on cfe bodies. Re-check every
   output with the branch/jal-aware diff, because its score includes reloc noise (on bootup it is
   useless). Finds this run, kept as plain C:
   - 43654 (NCC): a dead `if (!sp34) {}` between the two stores of a DL append (pointer v1 -> a1).
   - 1D944/1D9E0 (cfe): the second param is an `unsigned short` K&R param (its promoted home store is
     the target's `sw a1,4(sp)`), and `a1++; a1--;` ON ONE LINE before the second command burns the
     ring slot the target spends there (`a1 += 0`, `a1 = a1` or separate lines do not).
   - 27D00: the nibble clear is a double mask `(f60 & 0xFFFF & ~0xF) | 1`.
   - 25AC8: n1 declared after acc/i; the first loop tests a block-scope copy of the call result.
   - 21D84: the slot address recomputed per store (CSE'd) instead of a named slot pointer groups the
     three home reloads before the stores.
   - 47E00: copied row base `b = a`, `(n = m)[k][j]`, `if (1) {}` before the j loop, then
     `perm8.py` permuted the declaration list until out sat at sp+64 with m homed right above it.
   Setup: `extract.py unit fn out.c` builds a standalone cfe file (pulls declarations for undefined
   identifiers from the unit); `pc.sh` / `round.sh` / `runperm.sh` wire cfe / NCC permuter dirs (NCC:
   compile.sh wraps the C in `extern "C"` and turns K&R `()` externs into `(...)`); `declperm.py --cfe`
   moves each declaration to each position. Never `pkill -f permuter` (or pgrep it) in a command whose
   own text contains the pattern; it kills the calling shell. Use a script file.
4. **`p[k] = v; p[k] <<= 4;` keeps both stores** (game_libs_func_0002F720): the RMW is
   store-forwarded, the first store survives DSE and the shift reads the register. A plain double store
   is DSE'd; the cfe NM's `if (1) { p[k] = v; }` split kept it but coloured the temp v1. With edg's
   source-order `fl * K` and the late 0xE store it is exact under NCC.
5. **Re-used kit idioms:** registry `add()` (kit XVII #1) on game_libs_func_0004E37C, exact on the
   first port; if/return next() (kit XIX #2) on 41A9C, whose blank USO data refs must stay DISTINCT
   symbols pinned at 0 (one shared symbol is CSE'd into s0); a void alias for discarded calls (kit
   XVIII #3) on h2h 1204; same-line call + store (kit XVI #2) on 74E8.
6. **Makefile hazard (game_libs_post):** the 29CCC line assigns `REPLACE_FUNC_BODY :=` for
   game_libs_post.c.o, so a donor block placed before it is silently dropped (the ROM comes out short at
   the function and every later jal shifts). New post donor blocks go after the 28A68 block.
7. **bootup data bases in pins:** func_000074E8's `D_74e8_g/h` reads (`lw t6,0x2C(t6)` / `lw t0,0x44(t0)`)
   resolve to 0x34 / 0x134 in the ROM: the expected relocs are against func_00000008 / func_000000F0,
   so the pins are 0x8 / 0xF0, not 0.
8. **NCC sweep (scan2.py):** compiling each NM body as C++ with the unit's other declarations (other
   definitions dropped, K&R definitions converted) over all of agent-c's units: NCC beat cfe on raw
   words only where the body already used C++ idioms, and cfe-tuned bodies mostly got worse. The wins
   came from recognising idioms (registry, iterator, sti) and from fixing decodes, not from recompiling.

**Open (scratch in `c120/w/`):** 454C4 (ours holds 255.0f in f22 and 0x03000000 in s5; the target
rematerialises both inside the loop and keeps only 120.0f in f20; the loop's flags test also loads
twice in the target. No spelling or flag found yet); 4EE44 (src base temp v0 vs a1); 35B1C / 3E9C8 /
4247C / 3800C (one schedule or ring word each, permuter nothing); 437C0 (Base `this` pool slot 68 vs
72); 3E0F0 (`sw a0,76` in the jal delay); 3638 (bootup: arg-home store vs `addiu a0` in the first
jal's delay; every line placement tried); 470E4 x3 (cfe: ring +2 in the packet tail); 46FA8 (NCC
permuter got ctx to v1, dl/n still swapped); 34A78 (two byte stores share one `lui at` in the target:
4 words); 346F0 (re-decoded 42 -> 96.9: the target ends the unrolled copy on the src pointer, LFTR);
