## kit XXIII (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 120): literal constants, unlinked-block immediates, iterator reuse, edg temp pools <a name="kit-xxiii-agent-g-run-120"></a>

1. **A float/double LITERAL is a reg-alloc-prep constant candidate; a data-symbol read is not.** game_uso
   func_00000000 (cubic B-spline basis, cfe NM 66.7) is natural C++ with the 1/6 written as
   `(1.0f / 6.0f)`: the constant candidate is created during reg-alloc prep, after every variable, so it
   is coloured last (`$f16`, after omt/t2/t3 in f0/f2/f14) while its `lui at; lwc1` is still scheduled
   first. Read through a symbol (`float D = *(float *)&D_00000000` or a global) it is an ordinary
   candidate coloured at its first occurrence (`$f0`); a global re-read after each `out[]` store.
   When the target loads an FP constant early but colours it after the computed values, write a literal.
   (Under cfe the same swap made timproc_b5 32C8 worse: literals coloured f0/f2/f4 in creation order, so
   this is not a cfe lever.)
2. **The game_uso block is extracted from the .o WITHOUT a link** (`objcopy --only-section=.text`, no
   bake-data-relocs.py; mgrproc and timproc blocks do bake). A relocated word therefore ships its raw
   addend: a donor literal's %lo is its offset in the donor's own .rodata, and a `<fn>_rodata` pin in
   undefined_syms_auto.txt never reaches the block bytes (verify-blocks reports `lo16=N` while the ROM cmp
   still passes -- verify-blocks is the gate). 0000 works because its literal is the unit's rodata item 0.
   For other offsets read the constants through DISTINCT zero-valued externs with the offset in the addend,
   `*(float *)(&D_43D8_fmin + 0x94)`: each gets its own `lui at` with the %lo folded (one shared symbol
   gives a `lui/addiu` base register). Either way the host placeholder must re-emit the .rodata words the
   INCLUDE_ASM .s carried (`.late_rodata`) so the unit's rodata layout is unchanged (compare
   `objcopy -j .rodata` before/after; a smaller trailing .text pad is harmless).
3. **The 3DB38 `{cur, nxt}` stack iterator is in game_uso too.** game_uso 43D8 (69.8, "dual sp-slot
   cursor not C-reproducible, a1 promoted to $s0" under cfe) is a for loop over
   `Iter it(o->head); for (n = it.first(); n; n = it.next())` with the +/-FLT_MAX seeds: 60/60 words, the
   two sp slots, the nxt reload in the skip-test delay slot and every colour. Finder: in the target, a
   `sw rX,N(sp)` followed within three instructions by `sw rX,N-4(sp)` (nxt = head; cur = nxt). The gui
   unit has it (2DE0, 329C, 27A0, 3B80), so gui is C++ as well.
4. **edg pools inline-function temporaries by type, and a pooled FP temp inherits every use's register
   preference.** In 28C0 `sqrtf(d.lenSq())` put lenSq()'s result in the same edg temp as operator-'s first
   V3 ctor argument; that candidate then wanted `$f12` (the call argument) and the x/y/z difference triple
   came out f12/f0/f2 instead of f0/f2/f12. Writing the sum out in the call fixed the triple and the probe
   constants (85 -> 76 words). Check the dump for one `-NNvreg` var serving unrelated expressions.
5. **A block's edg temporaries are laid out before its named locals.** 28C0's else-arm probe ctor temp sat
   4 bytes high under a dead `int zz`; moving the arm's body into a nested block below the `int zz; zz = 0;`
   put the int slot above the temp (76 -> 72, every stack offset now right).
6. **Under edg a global's address stays in an s-register only through a named int copy.**
   `int gi = (int)&sym; Glob *g = (Glob *)gi;` holds it (game_uso B274's `lui s1; addiu s1`); a plain
   pointer, `(Glob *)(int)&sym`, `register` or `*const` are folded back into lui/%lo per use (kit XIX #4's
   int cast is a cfe lever). Same trick for a display object reached through an inline member
   (`((Dst *)di)->setPos(p)` with `int di = (int)&sym + 0xA0` gives `lui/addiu v0,+160; swc1 48(v0)`).
   cfront vtables: a vptr at +0x28 needs the virtuals in a base class with only padding before them, and
   the call through entry +0x18 is the class's third virtual. Cost seen: float->double arithmetic on
   cast-pointer reads adds 8-byte edg temporaries (B274 frame 88 vs 64, still open).
7. **Why the camera-homing out/tgt reloads colour v0/v1 in the target (28C0, 24BC): they are split
   pieces of a "-ve save" candidate.** From the uopt source (c111/ido/src/uopt): a non-vreg var (struct
   member or address-taken) can be a candidate, but every call kills it (`clkilled`: `!vreg`), so each
   live unit after a call pays a reload and a store-back (`needreglod`/`needregsave` via `prehascup`/ppin)
   and the whole range is "-ve save"; `split` then colours only the dense pieces (`compute_save`). Our
   Ctx members are not candidates at all: a pointer member used only as a load base forms no live range
   (tiny test: it appears only once passed as a value), and the Ctx ctor's `this` stores make it
   indirectly accessed. Plain pointer locals get `$s0` (positive save); `indiracc` is only set where code
   motion inserts an indirect access (uopttrep func_00478FA0). In 24BC an `Out::setGoal()/setPos()`
   inline pair reproduces the target's one-reload-per-group structure (t-reg instead of v0). Not cracked.
8. **5062C's last word is edg temp ORDER inside the first midpoint statement.** Target frame:
   [2 phantom][ret 356][2 phantom][ctor temp 336]. `operator+(const P3 &, const P3 &)` with V3 arguments
   gives [4 phantom][ret][ctor] (the base conversions come before the result temp); any V3-typed parameter
   gives [2][ret][1][ctor] (ret right, ctor 4 high). Neutral: member vs non-member, extra or default
   parameters, pointer parameters, nested inline helpers (they add copies), casts at the call site, a
   comma-first temp in the body (lands after the ctor temp: the ctor temp is allocated before its arguments
   are evaluated), a named local in the body (unique per inlining, frame grows).
9. **game_uso 7448 is inline accessors on sub-objects** (`AT(tab, 0x758)->get()` with
   `float get() const`, `set(float)`): 14 words on the first compile. Residual: the target keeps the get
   `this` in v0, the set `this` (blocks 2-4) in a1, &q in a3 and the 4C8 get `this` in a2, i.e. four
   separate pooled temps; ours merges them. D9CC under NCC with field-first products is 4 words (the
   branch-likely pair; double literals colour the same as data reads).

## kit XXIV (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 121): raw-diff decode sweep, one frame word per declared local, temps vs named locals, NCC switch results, struct copies <a name="kit-xxiv-agent-c-run-121"></a>

Four exacts (gl_func_0004A6E8, game_libs_func_0004406C in-unit cfe; bootup func_00007288 in-unit cfe;
bootup func_00000A9C NCC donor) and decode fixes on 445AC, 3E9C8, 35B1C, 4BAF4/39E24, 34EB4 and 7D04.
`scripts/rdiff.py` (MATCHING_WORKFLOW#rdiff-raw-pins-run121) is now in the project.

1. **Sweep method.** Run `rdiff.py --raw --pins` over every NM wrap in the band, then count each opcode in
   ours minus target (sp-relative loads/stores counted apart). Zero mnemonic difference with only
   register changes = colouring; zero with a different order = schedule; anything else, or a different
   constant, frame size or jal target, is a decode candidate. Of 128 agent-c wraps at 85-99.99, 52 had a
   zero multiset; most decode errors were in the small nonzero group.
2. **cfe reserves a frame word for every declared local, used or not.** Compile the extracted function with
   `-g3` and read `.mdebug`: `local 5 -4 root / -8 v / -12 a3 / -16 k` for 7D04, while its spills used
   other slots. A frame 8 bytes too large with identical slot usage therefore means one or two named
   locals too many. Fixes:
   - 7D04: keep only a3 (its spill home lands at 36) and k; the root/v pointers become expressions.
   - 1D4B0: the DL pointer reuses the `dl` parameter (parameters do not count) and the index is read
     inline. This fixes the frame but drops the (short) sign-extension of the signed-char index; objdiff
     scored the size change 99.90 -> 96.10, so it was reverted.
   - 4A6E8: block-scope the g pointer; `dst` declared before `i` then puts dst's home where the target has it.

   The rule is not exact: on 445AC, dropping one of five locals left the frame unchanged, so rounding and
   temp slots matter too. Under-sized frames point the other way: 36A48 (+40), 3E0F0 (+24), 41D40 (+40)
   and the open 42938 (+40) probably need extra declared locals or temporaries. 36A48 passes and returns
   Vec3 by value, which points to NCC temporaries. None of these was tested.
3. **m2c int temps declared as named locals colour v0/v1.** The target keeps them as t-ring temps
   (4406C, 89.3 -> exact). The two int fields were `s32 a10 = FW(arg0, 0x10)` locals (v0/v1). The target
   loads them into t6/t0 and converts each into the SAME float `d` the float lines use
   (`d = (f32)FW(arg0, 0x10); FW(arg0, 0x10) = (s32)(((f32)FW(arg1, 0x10) - d) * t + d);`).
   Tell: our `lw v0/v1/aN` against the target's `lw tN` at the same index. 40 wraps show it, most of them
   large.
4. **A dead `addiu rX,rX,K` after a load from rX is an assignment to a named local.** cfe keeps the
   assignment even though nothing reads it:
   - 7D04's `lw t6,4(v0); addiu v0,v0,4` is `v = *(int **)(root + 0x84) + 1; f(..(*v)..)`, and splitting
     one variable into two webs (`k = s0->0x40; k = k->0x84 + 4`) gives the v1/v0 pair.
   - 46BC4's `addiu v1,v1,256` is `child = o->0x254 + 0x100; if (child[1] & 2)`.
5. **A constant return through a register means a switch that assigns one result variable, under NCC**
   (A9C, 97.8 -> exact). The tell is `addiu v1,zero,8` hoisted into the 'n' compare's delay slot, then
   `jr ra; or v0,v1`. edg lowers the switch to a compare chain in case order (NCC never emits a
   jumptable; the same switch under cfe becomes one).
6. **t8/t7-alternating `lw`/`sw` pairs are an IDO struct copy** (7288, 95.8 -> exact): `*(Q16 *)(d + 0xDC) =
   src;`. The held source base comes from the asm operand `%lo(func_0000027C + 0x18)`, so the alias is
   pinned at 0x294 (kit XV #2). The flags RMW goes through the advanced pointer (`q = base->0x254 + 0x78;
   *q |= 4;`). rdiff shows `addiu t6,t6,660` against the expected `24` (its reloc targets
   func_0000027C), but the ROM bytes are equal.
7. **Constants and pins the raw diff exposed:**
   - 3E9C8: `lui 0x2` + negative lo is 0x1F34C, not 0x2F34C (every offset was 0x10000 high).
   - 35B1C: an unpinned `gl_ref_0001E6B0`.
   - 4BAF4 and 39E24: a camera block the ROM holds as the base `lui 0 / addiu 0xA0` with fields at +0x30.
     Pin the alias at 0xA0 and drop the 0xA0 pad from the struct, otherwise IDO folds 0xD0 into every
     field offset.
   - 34EB4: the flags test needs its own zero alias, because one shared `&D_00000000` was CSE'd into s3
     with `base`.
   - 445AC: the first ctor stores the NEW 32-byte object into `a3->0x18` before the init call (the NM
     reassigned a3), and the nested base-ctor alloc(20) goes to v1 only.
8. **Permuter on bootup is useless** (confirming kit XXII #3). The 7D04 base score was 8200 of reloc
   noise. The "better" outputs inserted `goto end;` at the top and removed real code; re-scored with the
   raw diff, all of them were worse than the base.

**Open:**
- 3800C: the last call gets no a0. An uninitialised int or float first argument gets a stack home and a
  reload, `register` too.
- 34890 / 8124 / 1438C: cfront ctor protocols whose inner `this == 0` tests survive in the target, so they
  are C++ (NCC). A first C++ draft of 34890 was worse than the cfe NM.
- 46BC4: the dead child temp is reproduced; the state-flag pointer is recomputed per arm in the target.
- 35E64: V3 temporaries under NCC. Each trivial `V3()` emits the `this == 0` protocol, so the point local
  must not be default-constructed.
- 1D17C: the target keeps every gbi `p++` step in its own register (a0, a2 = a0+8, t0 = a2+8,
  v0 = t0+8). cfe and NCC fold them.
- 240A0: the colour of the early `return h` (v0 raw, a1/v1 copy) is not a decode error. A bare `return;`
  makes the jump target right but the code longer.
- 4AFB4, 4EE44, 4CDB0, 437C0, 40640: pure colouring.

## kit XXV (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 121): nested-if labels, gui DL emitters, gbi.h texture macros, pad-word boundaries <a name="kit-xxv-agent-g-run-121"></a>

Eight exacts (59.44 -> ~60.1 % code): game_uso D9CC (2096 B); gui 1A5C, 1CA8, 06B8, 1EF4 (DL colour
emitters), 413C, 4354, 3F18 (texture-tile loaders). Every one came from recognising the original
shape; none from colour tuning.

1. **A branch-likely residue at a join can be label structure, not as1 (game_uso D9CC, 4 words ->
   exact).** The raw diff (`rdiff.py --raw --pins`) showed the target's plain `beqz t8; nop` and
   `bc1f; nop` branching to L20c while our branch-likely forms went to L210 (= L20c + 4, the stolen
   `lui`). The masked diffs only showed "beqz vs beqzl". Cause: the first gate was ONE `&&` in the
   NM body; in the original it is two NESTED ifs (`if (x > 30.0f) { if (mask & 0x1F0) {`), and the
   early `goto` lands after BOTH closing braces. The mask test and the 0x22C test then branch to the
   inner if's end label, which is directly followed by the outer end label, so as1 has no
   instruction to steal and keeps the nop; the first gate's target starts with the 500.0f `lui` and
   becomes `bc1fl` with the lui duplicated. Rule: when a branch keeps a nop where a sibling branch to
   the same address was likely-filled, look for an empty label (a closing brace) between them.
   Kit XXI #2's "nested ifs neutral" probe nested the wrong pair. The host placeholder re-emits the
   .s's three .rodata doubles (`*(volatile double *)a0 = 0.8;` etc.; compare `objcopy -j .rodata`).
2. **gui display-list colour emitters are inline-member C++ (1A5C/1CA8 92 -> exact, 06B8 90 ->
   exact, 1EF4 91 -> exact on the first compile).** Recipe (src/gui_uso/gui_uso_ncc_1A5C.cpp):
   - `struct Ctx { ...; DL *dl; Gfx *next() { int n = dl->n++; return &dl->buf[n]; } };` and
     `Gfx *p = CTX->next(); p->w0 = ..; p->w1 = ..;` per command. The context, list and index are
     edg's pooled inline temps (v0/v1/a0 in every append); each named slot pointer is its own
     candidate (a3, t0, ...).
   - The context global read as `*(Ctx **)&D_00000000` per append: its address becomes a uopt
     constant candidate coloured after the variables (the target's `lui t1/t3; addiu` held base).
     A named `int gi = (int)&D` (kit XXIII #6) colours it first (v0) and shifts everything.
   - Every colour channel is `(u32)(c * 255.0f) & 0xFF` BEFORE its shift, red included. Under
     `<< 24` the mask is redundant and folded away, but only after the t-ring has spent a register on
     it: without it every later temp of the float -> u32 sequence is one ring slot early (the old
     "colour cascade" of the whole family). This is just gbi.h's `_SHIFTL(r, 24, 8)`.
   - The first parameter is an unused `this`-like pointer: edg still stores it to its home
     (`sw a0,0(sp)` with no frame), even when declared `int`.
   - 06B8's context is `w->ctx` (a0+0x24); 1EF4 has three appends (combine, env, prim).
   **Not cracked (same family):** 17DC and 2334 (combine, `a1 & 0xFF` env alpha, prim colour + a3
   alpha): every word but the third slot pointer's colour (target t2, ours v1 -- it reuses the list
   temp's register) and the resulting one-slot ring shift (192 raw words). Tried: real gbi.h
   DPRGBColor/SetPrimColor macros, block-scope slot pointers, set() members, separate next2(),
   `(unsigned char)` alpha, dead `while (0)` anchors (edg emits code for them: +4 words). 08C0
   (combine x2 + prim colour from a memory `float col[4]` of 1.0f): 3 words left, the third slot
   pointer again (target v1, ours a0); `col` must be declared FIRST (frame 16, col at 0, any
   earlier named local grows the frame) and kept in memory through a pointer copy
   (`float *c = col;`), and the four 1.0f stores on separate lines. Permuter 15 min (C form with a
   `static inline` next(), see scratch g121/perm08c0) found nothing real: its lenient score
   counted reordered stores as near-equal.
3. **gui texture-tile loaders are the stock gbi.h macros (413C 85.8, 4354 85.7, 3F18 83.9 ->
   exact).** SETTIMG / load SETTILE (tile 7) / LOADSYNC / LOADTILE / PIPESYNC / render SETTILE /
   SETTILESIZE at origin 0, `tmem = tile << 8`, maskt 8, masks 8 or 9: write it with the verbatim
   libreultra 2.0I macro bodies (src/gui_uso/gui_ncc_gbi.h: `_SHIFTL`, `gSetImage`, `gDPSetTile`,
   `gDPLoadTileGeneric`, `gDPNoParam`) and `c->next()` as the packet, and pass the corners as macro
   TEXT (`#define LRS (uls + w - 1)`): IDO reassociates the expanded `(uls + w - 1) - uls + 1` into
   the target's `a3 = uls + w; t0 = a3 - uls` and `a3 - 1` forms, which a named `lrs` local or the
   open-coded cfe reconstruction (85 %) never reproduces. Twins differ only in fmt/siz/masks
   (RGBA16, IA8, RGBA32). Look for more gbi.h macro users wherever an NM body open-codes
   `0xF5`/`0xF4`/`0xFD` words.
4. **Leading zero words inside a function symbol are the predecessor's pad (gui 3F18).** Its .s
   began with three zero words before the real entry (`sw a3,12(sp)` at 0x3F24); the donor is 134
   words and the splice made the ROM 12 bytes short. Boundary fix (ROM-neutral, separate commit):
   drop the words from the .s (`nonmatching ..., 0x218`), add them as
   `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE := ... gui_func_00003B80=0x00000000,0x00000000,0x00000000` (APPEND to the
   unit's existing `:=` line, + the NON_MATCHING mirror), and edit expected/gui_uso.c.o in place
   (3B80 and its .NON_MATCHING alias size +12; 3F18 and alias value +12, size -12; scratch
   symedit.py, one exact name per call). Check `nm -S expected/...` size against the donor's word
   count BEFORE wiring any splice.
5. **uopt regalloc facts read this run (c111/ido/src/uopt/uoptreg2.c):** unconstrained live ranges
   are coloured in bitpos order; each picks the lowest-cost register, and on ties (leaf functions:
   `allcallersave`) the FIRST register in class order that an earlier range already took
   (`regstaken`). Interference is `intfering()` = intersection of `livebbs`, but in the gui
   emitters a param register is shared with a later slot pointer inside one uopt basic block, so in
   practice ranges are finer than a whole block; do not reason from "one BB, all interfere".
   Address constants of globals and float literals enter in reg-alloc prep with the highest bitpos
   (coloured last), which is why they land in the first free t-register after the variables.
6. **game_uso 7448 (14 -> 11 raw words, not exact).** The target has four distinct int temps (gets'
   `this` v0, sets' `this` a1, the 4C8 get's `this` a2, &q a3); a named `P *d, *s` pair for the
   last statement gives a1/a2 there, but the earlier sets then share v0. 40 spelling variants
   (types, references, named locals, member vs cast access, field 0x36C direct) in scratch
   g121/gen74*.py; none separates all four.
7. **Raw-diff sweep tooling note:** the scratch rdiff attached ALL printed relocs of a big object to
   the function's first instruction (objdump prints them up front with `--disassemble=fn`), giving a
   spurious one-word diff at index 0 (`addiu 0`, `lw 0`) on game_uso / post0b; scripts/rdiff.py
   (agent-c run 121) attaches by offset.

## kit XXVI (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 122): expression pointers for temp spills, operand rank on one ->, dead li from & ~0xF, decode errors behind pins <a name="kit-xxvi-agent-c-run-122"></a>

Nine exacts (59.53 -> 61.13 % code on the rebased tip; seven of them report-moving): gl_func_0001DA7C,
gl_func_0003190C, gl_func_00023760, gl_func_0001D200, game_libs_func_0001D4B0, gl_func_0002D7D0
(game_libs_post, in-unit cfe), game_libs_func_0004247C, gl_func_0004D0B4 (post0b), gl_func_00023914
(post, IDO -O2 jumptable donor). Scratch tooling: `c122/tools/rdiffn.py` = scripts/rdiff.py that also
resolves jal relocs to `gl_func_000XXXXX` / `game_libs_func_000XXXXX` names at their encoded address
(game_libs links at VRAM 0); without it, every call to a real in-module function shows as `jal 0`
and real wrong-callee errors (a placeholder name like gl_func_0001CA10 used for a blank import) hide
among them.

1. **A pointer that the target spills across a call into a TEMP slot is an expression, not a named
   local.** cfe reserves a frame word for a named local and still spills it to a separate temp slot,
   so the frame comes out 8 bytes large and every slot shifts. Writing the record pointer as a macro
   expression (`#define e (&TAB[a1])`, or `(char *)&D + a2 * 0x158` inline at each use) lets IDO CSE
   it into one temp whose spill lands where the target's does:
   - game_libs_func_0001D4B0 (frame 0x30 -> 0x28, the open item from kit XXIV #2): record pointer as
     a macro, `int k = e->k` kept in the if-block for the `(short)` narrowing.
   - gl_func_0001D200: same for `rec`, plus the dl parameter reused as the cursor (one fewer word).
   Check: the target's spill offset is BELOW the named-local area (sp+32 with locals at 52..60).
2. **One typed member read flips the addu operand order.** `rec + *(u8 *)(rec + 0x1B) * 100` and
   `w2 + *(short *)(e + 0x10)` emit `addu t,rX,rY` with the cast-deref first whatever the textual
   order (kit #99's rank). Spelling the single read as `((struct { char p[0x1B]; u8 b; } *)rec)->b`
   restored the target's operand order in 1D200 (kit #99 needed two levels in its case; here one
   anonymous-struct level was enough). Swapping the source operands changed nothing.
3. **`(x + 0xF) & ~0xF` stored into a short** emits `addiu at,zero,-16` and then `andi 0xfff0`
   (the and is narrowed by the store, the `li at` stays dead). A target with a dead `li at,-16`
   wants `& ~0xF` / `& -16`; `& 0xFFF0` drops the word (1D200, 1 word length difference).
4. **A redundant `& 0xFFFF` on an `unsigned short` field burns exactly one t-ring slot** (no
   emission) -- 1DA7C was t9-vs-t1 everywhere after its calls; same lever as kit XIX's 1D3E0 `& 0xFFFF`
   and kit XXV's `& 0xFF`. Probe it first on any uniform +1 ring phase after a u16 load.
5. **`int` function with no return statement**: v0 is treated as live at the exit, so a guard that
   branches to the epilogue cannot take the `lui v0` (next block) into its delay slot and as1 emits
   `beqzl ...; lw ra` instead (3190C's last guard). `void` gives `beqz; lui v0` (1 word short).
6. **Decode errors the raw diff exposed (all were "colouring" or "reloc" notes before):**
   - 23914 called the in-file 23B44 / 23B98; the target's jals go to 0x381B0 / 0x38204 (gl_ref_ pins).
     240A0's NM still calls `gl_func_0001CA10` where the target has a blank import (jal 0): a real
     name links to its address, so that placeholder must become gl_func_00000000 before any exact.
   - 3190C: the guard query is a baked jal (0x45F04) and each else arm's second command is
     0x0602x000 (the NM had x004).
   - 23760: the busy path returns the 381B0 result (spilled over the acquire call), not acquire's.
     Slots: the return-holder copy declared first (sp+52), the type byte assigned to `ok` (v0), the
     37F80 result reusing the copy (no extra word).
   - 2D7D0: three leading stores of 8 to three blank USO refs (`lui at; sw v0,0(at)` x3) were simply
     missing; three distinct zero aliases (one symbol would be DSE'd).
   - 4247C (permuter, re-verified): the 5th argument as a named int read before the call and the
     global re-read at each use = two more ring slots.
7. **report.json scores reloc-only residues as 100.** 23914 (jumptable %lo) and 4D0B4 (a leading
   zero word in its INCLUDE) were "exact" in the report while still INCLUDE_ASM in the ROM. Promote them:
   23914 via the 29CCC donor recipe (`game_libs_o2_23914.c`, `gl_func_00023914_rodata = 0xEA0`; keep the
   donor's C_FILES filter-out on its own `C_FILES := $(filter-out ...,$(C_FILES))` line -- the shared
   filter-out line conflicts on every rebase); 4D0B4: the zero word at 0x4D0B0 is gl_func_0004D084's
   all-zero SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE pad, with `gl_func_0004D084=0x2c` added to the post0b clip line so the NM
   symbol keeps its size. Both change the post0b NM text size: re-probe the clip.
8. **post0b iteration hazard:** a post0b NM edit that changes a function's length makes the NM build
   fail at the clip (`.text 0x... smaller than requested`). Build with
   `NON_MATCHING_TEXT_CLIP_KEEP_ALIGN=` on the command line to diff, but that also drops the
   551E0/55B10/4D084 symbol resizes; delete the NM object afterwards, or the next refresh-report shows
   the sentinels "lost".
9. **Dead named-local defs are colour candidates.** 445AC (permuter hint): `v = D_glob_e` as an
   argument (v dead afterwards) re-phased the t-ring after it (12 -> 6 words), but v takes v1 where the
   target has a t7 temp, and the base of the following `*(int *)((int)&D_alias + 0x1C) = a3` (int cast:
   IDO then materialises lui/addiu instead of folding) colours t8/t7 where the target has v0 -- the target
   looks like the same burn with the base as the candidate. Frame: dropping the `s0 = a0` copy AND the
   `g` base pointer together fixed 0x60 -> 0x58 (either alone did not).

**Open (scratch in `c122/w/`):**
- 3E0F0 / bootup 8124 / bootup 7204: NCC cfront-protocol constructors whose new-expression result is
  a SEPARATE web from the ctor's `this` (7204: `or a1,a2` copy before the call; 3E0F0/8124: the result

- 1438C: NCC draft with every instruction right; the two Val temporaries are laid out 56/60 (target

- 1DA7C-style ring burns did nothing for 2A258 (pure schedule: sh 0x14/0x10 ten slots early),

## kit XXVII (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 122): declared-local frame gaps, BB-split literal candidates, double-literal "data variables", same-line stores, edg dispatch order <a name="kit-xxvii-agent-g-run-122"></a>

Three exacts (gl 64588 2148 B, gl 675A4 1048 B, gl 546E8 812 B) and one NM step (gl 578B4 raw 1822 -> 1799).

1. **A frame that is too SMALL by N words, with every used offset shifted by a constant, is N unused
   declared locals (gl 64588, 95.64 -> exact).** cfe gives every declared local its own frame word, used
   or not (kit XXIV #2), in declaration order (first declared = highest). The target's 336-byte frame had
   84 bytes more than ours and a block of homes below `t`/`m` that ours did not have. Method: histogram
   every `N(sp)` and `addiu rX,sp,N` operand in both objects (scratch `spo.sh`), find the constant shift
   per region, and insert unused `int gN;` locals where the target has gaps. Here: one word above u1,
   three above m/t, seven between t and the box-1 slot pointer, three between `set[]` and `tmp`, four
   between `tmp` and the box-2 slot pointer, four below. The two box slots each have their OWN slot
   pointer (`mb1` home 148, `mb2` home 56), not the shared `m` of the 13 simple slots. After the frame
   matched, every sp offset was exact on the first build.
2. **Literal candidates in one straight-line block all interfere; `if (1) {}` splits them (gl 64588).**
   uopt interference is per BB (`livebbs`), so the -1000/0/1000 (box 1) and 1.0/-10/10/0 (box 2)
   constants of one block got f0/f12/f2 where the target reuses f0 for each group in turn. An
   `if (1) {}` after each constant group makes a BB boundary: the ranges stop overlapping and every group
   colours f0, with the next `mtc1` scheduled after the previous group's stores, as in the target.
   Box 2's 1.0 has only two uses, and as `1.0f` uopt rematerialised it per use (two `mtc1`, f16/f18).
   Written as the double literal `1.0` (or int `1`), it becomes a candidate (one `mtc1`, f0) and the
   function is exact. Rule: when a float constant is materialised once per use in ours but once in the
   target, try the double or int spelling of the same literal.
3. **A "data variable" read through `&D + off` in game_libs can be a double literal (gl 675A4, 8 words
   -> exact).** The NM read the stick dead-zone through `extern struct { char pad[0x2200]; f64 v; }`
   into a named `f64 temp_f14`, which uopt colours with the variables (first, f12), swapping it with
   the 0.0f literal (target zero f12, threshold f14). bootup.uso RoData (module 0xD9FE28, section type 7
   at ROM 0xD9FE40) holds 0x3FC999999999999A = 0.2 at +0x2200. **The section data starts with one
   marker word, so offset X is at ROM 0xD9FE44 + X** (10000.0f at +0x1C78 and the 3430 jumptable at
   +0xCCC confirm it). As the literal `0.2`, the threshold is a constant candidate coloured after the
   zero: exact. Landed as an IDO 7.1 -O2 donor (game_libs_o2_675A4.c, the 3C0C recipe) so the .rodata
   reloc is renamed `gl_func_000675A4_rodata` and pinned to 0x2200. Two traps hit while wiring it:
   - Do NOT list a REPLACE_FUNC_BODY donor as a Make prerequisite of the host. Target-specific variables
     propagate to prerequisites, so the donor gets the host's whole REPLACE_FUNC_BODY list (dozens of
     "symbol not found"). The recipe already runs `$(MAKE) $$donor`.
   - `rdiff --pins` does not catch a call to a real in-module function (`gl_func_00062F64`): it links to
     its address (`jal 0x62F64`) where the ROM has a blank `jal 0`. ROM cmp caught it (6 bytes); use
     gl_func_00000000 for blank imports.
   Negative: the same "literal, not data" idea on timproc_b5 32C8/2B74 (zero wants f0 before the
   +0x134/+0x120 loads) does not change their colouring, as literals or as data, in any statement order.
4. **A two-word as1 order residue fell to the same-line rule (gl 546E8, 99.01 -> exact; permuter, about
   2 min).** The rematerialised `mtc1 zero,$f2` after the `s1 + 0x30` call was scheduled before the
   0x28 vtable store; the target has the store first. Writing the call, the closing brace of its `if`
   and the store on ONE source line (`gl_func_00000000(s1 + 0x30, &zv); } FW(self, 0x28) = ...;`) gives
   the target order. The call and the store on one line without the brace, or the store and the next
   statement on one line, do not. Standalone permuter setup that worked: base.c = the function plus its
   decls, compile.sh = cfe -O2, target.s = the expected words as `.word` (reloc noise is a constant
   offset on the score).
5. **game_libs dispatch compare chains are edg source order (gl 578B4).** Both texture-format dispatches
   compare 0x120, 0x110, 0x408, 0x308, 0x304, 0x508 in that order, which a cfe `switch` (sorted) cannot
   give. A goto ladder in source order works if the last test is written `if (x != 0x508) goto def;
   goto arm;`, so uopt keeps the target's `beq arm; b default` tail (`== 0x508 -> arm; goto def` gets
   inverted). The two leading calls are baked `jal 0x6A750` words (pin
   `game_libs_func_00062F08_578B4`). Raw 1822 -> 1799; the rest is the NCC-vs-cfe colouring of an
   m2c transcription (see the run-113 NCC draft).
6. **Not moved (all re-verified with `rdiff --raw --pins`):**
   - game_uso 591C: the "five gates" are case 0 of the first `switch (self->0x74)`: the target branches
     to a `b join; or v0,v1` block (switch temp copied at the join), ours goes straight to the join. The
     target keeps a second register (v0) for the selector, copies it at every join, and stores
     `vsel = 1` from v1. No cfe or NCC spelling tried keeps the copy: `v0 = vsel; switch (v0)` in either
     or both switches, `self->0x74` re-reads, and `v0 = vsel;` at the end of each case all produce the
     same code. 558 raw words of colouring remain.
   - gl 76F0: no decode error. difflib alignment made the case blocks look reordered, but the block
     order is identical (compare the `lh ..,N(v0)` vtable offsets in order). Still capped by the
     4-entry jumptables (cfe tables only from 5 labels, NCC never) and the same switch-temp copy as 591C.
   - gl 5062C (1 word): typing the six vector parameters as the POD base `P3` (the `nrm`/`vtx`
     prototypes taking `P3 *`) moves the first operator+ return slot to the target's sp+356, but the
     ctor temporary moves 4 high (`[2][ret][1][ctor]`, the target is `[2][ret][2][ctor]`). Sweeping all
     64 operator+ parameter-type pairs and all 64 P3/V3 parameter mixes: best is still 1 word.
   - gui 17DC/2334/08C0/055C: no shared fix. Verbatim gbi.h `gDPSetEnvColor` / `gDPSetPrimColor` /
     `gDPSetColor` macros (block-scoped `_g`), an inline `W::prim()` member for 08C0's third append (it
     brings its own pooled temps and shifts the whole ring), and declaration placement all leave the
     third slot pointer's colour (17DC: ours v1, target t2; 08C0: ours a0, target v1). 055C under NCC
     has a different defect: each packet's constant `lui` is allocated before the dl temp dies (ours a
     fresh t-reg, the target reuses the dl temp register).
   - gui 148: all homes from 120 down are exact. The frame is 136 vs 128 because the target has exactly
     ONE declared local above `col` (ours has three: sum, maxw, row). Block-scoping `row` in either loop
     or reusing `col` for the fill loop moves other homes. The run-114 note (reuse a1 for maxw, drop
     `line`) is still the closest.
   - timproc_b5 32C8 (5 words) / 2B74 (25): see #3. gl 3430 (15 words, the prologue places the step load
     and the hoisted 1.0f/10.625f before the saves): a permuter run (same setup as #4, 10k iterations,
     about 8 minutes) found nothing real below its base score. Its four 0.1f step literals (RoData +0xCC8/+0xCEC/+0xCF0/+0xCF4) do
     merge into one candidate as `0.1f`, `0.1` or `(f32)0.1`.

## kit XXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 123): RoData literal sweep, inline-member arg webs, cfe frame accounting <a name="kit-xxviii-agent-c-run-123"></a>

Two exacts (bootup func_0000E270 via an IDO 7.1 -O2 literal donor, func_00007204 via an NCC donor) and
four NM steps (45178 27 -> 5, 240A0 20 -> 10, E2D0 55 -> 19, 8124 40 -> 31 raw words, `rdiff --raw --pins`).

1. **Which loads are literals: read the USO TextReloc table, not the values.** game_libs and bootup_uso
   are both bootup.uso's Text (ROM 0xDD0A6C + offset); its TextReloc section (ROM 0xE620EC, 0x2D894
   bytes, entries `[(symIdx << 4) | kind, text offset, flag]`, kind 2 = LO16, 3 = HI16) gives every
   relocated load's target symbol, and symIdx 1 is the RoData section (data at ROM 0xD9FE44 + offset).
   Scanning every agent-c NM wrap for `lwc1/ldc1` whose LO16 targets symIdx 1 (scratch
   `c123/litscan.py`) found only 36 functions: the FP-heavy colouring group of run 121 (437C0, 4CDB0,
   46FA8, 470E4, 4AFB4, ...) loads NO RoData constants at all (their FP comes from object fields and
   `lui`-built immediates), so the literal lever cannot touch them.
2. **Results of the literal swap** (in-tree NM, literal for the data read, nothing else changed):
   - E270 (99.83 -> exact): pi at +0x998. The old "f0/a1 spill-slot swap cap" was the named
     `float ratio` local; written as `3.14159265f / arg1` inline in both calls, IDO CSEs the quotient into
     one temp and the frame drops 0x28 -> 0x20. Donor `bootup_uso_o2_E270.c`, `func_0000E270_rodata = 0x998`
     (host = the same C; the splice discards the in-unit .rodata).
   - 45178: the -32700/32700/32700 clamp bounds as literals colour lo f12 / hi f14 like the target
     (27 -> 14). Exact still needs a donor with `gl_func_00045178_rodata = 0x1B60`.
   - E2D0: the f64 at +0x9A0 is 0.1 (no colour change by itself; see #5 for the real fixes).
   - No change: D900 (0.1/0.2; residue is the clamp copy), BF8C (0.1f/0.1; ring phase is in an earlier
     if-arm), 610 (5000.0/0.3; frame), 3C43C, 36F0C, 1304C (+-3 words, far from exact).
   - A function's literals must be contiguous and in donor emission order for ONE `_rodata` pin:
     396FC's 0.01 sits at +0x1A10, before its jumptable (+0x1A64) and 1/32767 (+0x1A7C), so it needs a
     second symbol or is a shared constant.
3. **Inline member as the hand-off keeps the new-expression result a separate web** (7204, 5 words ->
   exact under NCC). `new Pair(a1, p)` then `func(a0 + 0x2C, o)` always coalesced o into the call's a1;
   the target keeps it in the ctor's register (a2) and copies it at the call. Writing the hand-off as an
   inline member of the list, `struct L { void add(Pair *n) { func(this, n); } }; ((L *)(a0 + 0x2C))->add(o);`,
   gives the parameter n its own web: 33/33. Line breaks matter here too: the same body on one source
   line moved the prologue `addiu a0,zero,8` (7 words).
4. **3E0F0 / 8124: the returned object pointer is spilled to the first declared local's home (-4)**, not
   kept in s0 with the ctor's this. Under NCC, a memory-resident pointer reproduces the store/reload:
   `inline Obj *link(Obj *&q, Obj *n, char *a) { gl_func_00000000(q = n, *(int *)(a + 0x40)); return q; }`
   + `Obj *p; return link(p, new Obj, arg0);` puts the `sw` in the jal delay slot and `lw v0,76(sp)` at
   the end (8 words: frame 72 vs 80, stores s0 not the a0 copy, W4 member this a1 vs a0). A plain named
   copy, `Base *`, references without the assignment inside the call, `volatile`, and a by-value holder
   struct (7 words, wrong store timing) do not. 8124 under cfe: frame 88 -> 80 by declaring the result
   pointer first (its spill home sp+76) and dropping the second sub-object pointer (31 words left).
5. **cfe frame accounting seen this run:**
   - A `switch` costs one frame temp word (610: `switch` + 4 named locals = 0x38, either alone 0x30);
     its five sparse cases still compile to a compare chain. An if/goto ladder does not keep the target's
     out-of-line case layout (uopt re-sinks the bodies). Kit XXIX says a 5+ case compare chain is NCC,
     but 610 under NCC is far worse (param homes, 114 words); unresolved.
   - Unused arrays size the frame only from a threshold (E2D0: `int pad[8]` moved everything to the
     target's 112, pad[4..7] did not), so fit pads by measuring, not by counting words.
   - E2D0: `dot` and the clamp result `s` are ONE variable (f0 across the normalise call, spilled to its
     own home at sp+68 = one unused word below `s`), and `dot *= k` keeps dot as the first `mul.s`
     operand where `dot = dot * k` / `k * dot` both flip it. The normalise call takes only `&v[0]`, yet
     arg3 stays live in a3 (spilled to its home around both calls): `if (arg3) {}` after the call
     reproduces exactly that.
6. **45178: an index read into its own named int before the store** (permuter hint, cleaned):
   `t = FW(p, 0xC); n3 = FW(FW(p, 0xC), 4); i = n3; FW(t, 4) = i + 1;` gives the target's list v0 /
   index v1 / packet a3 in the second vertex slot, while the first slot wants `i = FW(FW(p, 0x3C), 4)++;`
   (with `++` in both slots the ring burns one t-register). The frame stays 104 only with `lo` turned
   into the inline literal (one declared word fewer). Left: the packet pointer spills to its home (40)
   where the target uses the temp area (36), i.e. the original pointer is an unnamed temp; written as a
   register expression (`(int *)((char *)q + i * 8)` twice) it does go to 36 but recolours (22).
7. **240A0:** the `gl_func_0001CA10` placeholder is a blank import (jal 0) in the ROM; the two fixed thunks
   are `gl_ref_000381B0` / `gl_ref_00038204`. Raw 20 -> 10: the jumptable %lo (donor pin 0xEB4) and the
   case-0/3 return-value colouring are left (four more spellings of the case-0 store tried, all 10+).

**Open:** 45178 (5: spill slot), 3E0F0 (NCC 8, cfe 11), 240A0 (10), E2D0 (19: z-first dot sum is cfe's

## kit XXIX (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 123): NCC fingerprints in cfe NM wraps, m2c frame/operand fixes, donor .late_rodata, sweep results <a name="kit-xxix-agent-g-run-123"></a>

Five exacts (gl 53560 1228 B, gl 55470 1072 B, gl 56974 928 B, gl 56D14 736 B, game_uso 57D8 324 B; 61.13 -> 61.69 %).
Four of them came from one observation: these cfe NM wraps were C++.

1. **Fingerprints of a C++ (NCC) function hiding behind a cfe NM wrap.** Sweep the target of every NM wrap for
   (a) a compare chain `addiu at,zero,K; beq rX,at,..` of three or more cases with NO `jr` jumptable in the
   function (cfe sorts the cases and tables any switch of 5+ labels; edg lowers `switch` to a chain in CASE
   order and never emits a table), or (b) a virtual call in edg's order `lw t9,N+4(vt); lh tK,N(vt); jalr t9;
   addu a0,tK,obj` (delay slot filled; cfe's hand-written `(*(fn*)(vt+N+4))(obj + *(short*)(vt+N))` gives
   `lh; addu; lw t9; jalr; nop`). Any hit is worth a first NCC compile before more cfe tuning. Results:
   - **gl 55470 (93.72 -> exact)**, the command-stream opcode dispatcher (src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_55470.cpp):
     `switch (s->cmd)` with the cases in target chain order (1014, 1012, 1015, ... `case 113:` falling into
     `default:`, then `case 1018` last); `int next() { return cmd = *(*cp)++; }`; flag ops as inline Flags
     members on the D block (this = a0, arg = a1); 1017/1003 pass the 76-byte stream struct by value; the
     default arm is a REAL virtual call (`struct Obj : ObjPad { virtual m1()..m7(int *); }`, 40-byte base so
     the vptr is at +0x28, entry +0x38 = 7th virtual). Last three words: the 1012 test is `s->next();
     if (!(s->f18 & s->cmd))` (the `and` operands come out in target order only with the statement form; both
     source orders of `f18 & next()` give the same, wrong, order), the {cmd, cur} pair is a function-scope
     class object declared after a dead `Two pt;` (frame 0x130), filled by an inline `set()` through a block
     `int c = s->cmd;` and followed by `if (1) {}`.
   - **gl 56974 (93.86) / 56D14 (96.41) -> exact** on the first compile (one TU, game_libs_ncc_56974.cpp):
     `switch (k)` with `int k = m->w1 & 0xF00;`, each arm one SETCOMBINE through `G *next() { int n =
     dl->n++; return &dl->buf[n]; }`. The 56D14 NM's long lever list (if-goto ladder, `if (1) {}` arms,
     `long long` stores) was all imitation of edg's chain.
   - **game_uso 57D8 (82.51 -> exact)**: the 8-way value selector that cfe always jumptables is one switch;
     the `addiu v0,a1,0x758; swc1 0x10(v0)` store is an inline `Val::set()` whose `this` is
     `AT(char *, a0, 0x30) + 0x758` (re-read, not the cached `sub`), and reading the state pointer through
     `a0->0x30` too makes the `== 2` constant colour v0.
   - Not exact yet (drafts in this run's scratch, best raw words): gl 61478 printf panic (39; the target
     keeps the switch value in v0 and copies it to a1 for the per-char calls -- `int c` fixes the frame, no
     spelling of c / the switch found that keeps both registers), game_uso E5C8 (47; EAF4 call args fixed by
     reading `a0->0xB4->0xA58` three times; open: count address candidate a1 vs a2, the `&4` test keeps a
     plain `beqz; nop` in the target where ours goes likely), gl 68DD4 (23; homes fixed with `One x1; int t;
     Thing *a; One x2; int r;` -- one-word class objects as frame pads -- open: one reused local `x` must
     take t0 for the 0xC object / second clear base / vptr), timproc_b5 5BF0 (72; real virtuals v16/v12
     fix the call shape; the 255 numerator merges with the 255.0f divisor under edg in every spelling tried),
     mgrproc 23FC (93; `255.0f * f` operand order fixes the four alpha sites under NCC).
   - Not C++: titproc 116C and timproc_b5 D884/DF14 have real jumptables; gl D288 / 51ED8 and timproc_b5 D14C
     use the cfe virtual-call order.
2. **NCC drops unused scalar locals (no frame word) but keeps an unused class object.** To pad an NCC
   frame use `struct One { int a; One() {} };` (one word) or a two-word class; `int pad[2]` / `volatile int`
   pads vanish.
3. **An m2c transcription with a frame N words short is N unused declared words (gl 53560, 97.49 ->
   exact).** All used homes were right and the frame was 64 bytes short: `s32 pad[16];` declared FIRST
   (above sp4C) fixed it (cfe keeps an unused array's words). The same function also had:
   - the second product of each cross-product row in the wrong source order: IDO emits `multu` with the
     operands swapped relative to the source, so write `(c - b) * (b - a)` where the target multiplies
     `(b - a)` by `(c - b)`; the same for the block's float sums (`v1[k] + v0[k]`);
   - a `ori` immediate that is a symbol (`&D + 0x2103C`);
   - the manual `if (n < 0) f += 4294967296.0f` that is IDO's own u32 -> float conversion of a `u32` count;
   - a branch landing 4 bytes late: the second loop's `var_s7 = 0; var_s2 = 0;` belong INSIDE the loop's
     `if (count != 0)` guard. With them outside, the join's `var_s7 = 0` is partially redundant and uopt sinks
     it into the loop exit; inside, uopt hoists them above the branch (dead on the bypass path) and keeps the
     join store.
   - every call is a blank import: in-unit `gl_func_00034458` calls link to `jal 0x34458` (ROM cmp caught
     10 words that rdiff --pins could not see), so use gl_func_00000000.
4. **A donor host placeholder must keep the INCLUDE_ASM .s's `.late_rodata`.** game_uso 57D8.s carried 24
   words of 44F4's float pool (RoData +0x9C); with an empty placeholder the unit's .rodata lost them and seven
   later `lwc1 %lo` fields moved by 0x60 (verify-blocks `lo16=7`, ROM cmp still passed). Re-emitting them from
   C does not work for lui-only floats (`-10000.0f` is `lui`, no pool entry), `static const` arrays go to the
   START of .rodata, and auto aggregates become immediate stores. What works: move the block verbatim to the
   end of the next INCLUDE_ASM .s in text order (here 591C.s) and compare `objcopy -j .rodata` before/after.
5. **Literal-recovery sweep (scratch litsweep.py: target lwc1/ldc1 through a lui base -> value at ROM
   0xD9FE44 + off).** Only six of my game_libs wraps at >= 90 still read FP values through data symbols (64388,
   693A4, 697C4, 15FC, 3430, 2840); none moved: 64388's 1e-5/455.0 and 693A4's 0.01 as literals leave the
   colouring unchanged; 15FC's colour pool is n/255 (193, 123, 246, 9, 155, 119) + 0.18 and is byte-identical
   as literals or externs (its residue is the 100-constant v0/v1 tie). timproc_b5 32C8: the zero there is a
   uopt constant candidate; it only interferes with the l134 load when both are in one BB, and then it colours
   f12 (coloured last) instead of the target's f0 (6 placements of the zero group and `if (1)` tried).
6. **Frame-size sweep (scratch frames.py)** listed 22 wraps in my units with a frame delta; 53560 was the
   only clean decode win. gl 59E80 (the GBI state setter, permuter body at 94 %) rewritten with gbi-style
   blocks (`n = dl->n++; _g = &dl->buf[n]`) matches the load order and frame, but the t-ring phase depends on
   how many uopt candidates sit in t-registers (target: per-packet `_g` in v0/v1/a0/t0/t1, constants 3 and
   0xFFFD reusing t0/t1 late); block-scoped `n`/`_g` put the ring one register late, function-scope ones fix
   the ring but give one `_g` register. Not cracked.
7. **The switch-value copy register (591C / 76F0 / 61478):** under NCC the 61478 target's `beq v0,at; or
   a1,v0,zero` pattern (switch value in v0, the per-case argument copy in a1) did not appear with `int c`,
   `char c`, a separate `k = c`, `switch (c = *fmt++)`, or `register`. 76F0 has real jumptables (cfe).

3. **The by-value array index iterator (gl 4E244 exact).** `{Arr *a; int idx; int last}`, 12 bytes, built by
   `new`-protocol code on a stack address (`addiu v1,sp,60; bnez v1; ...; jal new; li a0,12`), copied twice
   (construct -> return temp -> `it`), stepped by `idx < last ? &a->data[++idx] : 0`, body re-reads
   `a->data[idx]`. What it takes under NCC:
   - edg emits cfront's `this == 0 -> new(12)` protocol only when the fields live in a BASE class whose ctor
     runs from the derived ctor (`struct IBase { ...; IBase(Arr *) }; struct AIter : IBase { AIter(Arr *arr)
     : IBase(arr) {} }`); a ctor on the class itself, out-of-line or not, never shows it;
   - `inline AIter Arr::iter() { Arr *self = this; if (0) { self = this; } return AIter(self); }`: the
     return-by-value gives the two copy ladders, the named `self` is the target's 4-byte slot between the
     return temp and the constructed object, and the dead assignment recolours the construction block
