## kit XXXII (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 125): ctor forwarding to set() moves edg temps, 1304C / D900 / h2h 1360 under NCC, block-scalar frame order <a name="kit-xxxii-agent-c-run-125"></a>

One exact (bootup 4948, 1704 B; ROM cmp clean) and three NCC NM donors that took cfe NM wraps to
99.6-99.9 %. Scratch for this run: `c125/d4948`, `d1304C`, `dD900`, `dH1360`, `dH620`, `d35B1C`,
`d3800C`, `d49B3C`, `d41D40`, `d4B0A8`.

1. **bootup 4948 EXACT: forward the Vec3 ctor to an inline `set()`.** Run 124's donor was
   instruction-identical except that the divisor-call result of
   `r = ff(ang) * e->a / ff(ang)` went to the edg float temp at sp+236 where the target has sp+232.
   Probes showed the temp is edg's own (it disappears when the expression is split, and inline
   wrappers with a float parameter such as `idf(ff(ang))` or `pick(dummy, ff(ang))` move it to 232),
   but every probe that moved the slot also swapped the shared x/y ctor temps to f2/f14. What fixed
   both:
   ```
   struct Vec3 { float x, y, z; Vec3() {}
       void set(float a, float b, float c) { x = a; y = b; z = c; }
       Vec3(float a, float b, float c) { set(a, b, c); } };
   ```
   with NO dead statement in the ctor and NO declared `E16 *ep` (use `#define e (&tbl[idx])`).
   Pattern: if an NCC float-temp slot is one word off and the colours of shared inline-parameter
   temps flip whenever you move it, change how the ctor reaches its fields (a forwarding inline
   member) before you change the expression. The trailing zero word is an all-zero
   SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE word; the float import, tables and constants are zero pins.
2. **NCC frame accounting (D900, 1304C, h2h 1360, -g3 layouts).** Homes are assigned top-down in
   this order: function-scope declarations in declaration order (scalars AND class objects), then
   every block-scope SCALAR of the whole function, even in later case arms (D900's `int r` in the last
   case lands above the case-20 temps), then edg temps and block-scope class objects in creation
   order. Consequences:
   - a temp created early (a float->double compare temp, an inline function's parameter or return
     temp) sits above later inline-expansion locals such as an `operator*`'s `r` and its return
     temp; declaration tricks cannot move it below them (D900 open item, 16 bytes);
   - unused block scalars still take a word (1304C/D900: drop or add one to hit the frame);
   - `-O2 -g3` NCC compiles keep the same layout and name the locals in `.mdebug`
     (`c124/tools/mdebug.py`): the fastest way to read an NCC frame. Unnamed gaps are temps.
3. **bootup 1304C (93.78 -> 99.63, NM donor `bootup_uso_ncc_1304C.cpp`).** Shape- and frame-exact
   (`rdiff --noreg` 0, frame 96). What it took:
   - declarations `int x, y, i, j; float up, dn; float k; float lf, rt; int count;` (k at sp+68,
     frame 96: kit XXXI rule);
   - `if (f->timer != 0) f->timer--; if (f->timer == 0)`: the target's `addiu t6,v0,-1; sw; or v0,t6`
     needs a fresh decrement temp; the run-124 `t = f->timer = t - 1` shifted the whole t-ring by one
     (about 400 raw words came from that one statement);
   - centre cell through `i` (uopt strength-reduces 4*i into its own IV), texel through
     `j = i` copied at the top of the x loop, `i++` at the END of the body: the target's early
     `addiu a3,a3,1` + `or t1,a3` copy;
   - `for (count = 0, y = 0; ...)`, `for (x = 0, i = y * 32; ...)` for the init order, and a named
     result in the inline `next()` (`Gfx *g = &dl->buf[n]; return g;`) for the hoisted DL constants.
   Left (42 raw words): the per-packet `_g` pointers rotate a1 a2 a3 a1 a2 t0 a1 | a1 a2 a3 a1 a2 a1
   ... in the target and strictly a1 a2 a3 here, which shifts the hoisted constants (t5/t0 vs ra/t2).
   Not moved by: a single `Gfx *g` for all packets (all a0), nested macro blocks for
   gDPLoadTextureBlock / gSPTextureRectangle, `if (!flag)`, `Ctx &`, `Ctx *const`, next() spellings.
4. **bootup D900 is C++ (99.08 -> 99.92, NM donor `bootup_uso_ncc_D900.cpp`).** The dispatcher is the
   edg case-order compare chain (20, 9, 6, 1000, 1001, 1003, 1002, 1004, 1005..1007, default): a
   plain `switch` in that case order. Ten raw words left from cfe's 34:
   - clamp = `inline float clampf(float v, float lo, float hi) { if (v < lo) return lo; if (v > hi)
     return hi; return v; }` assigned to a NAMED `k`, then `d = p->pos * k;`: the target's entry
     copy `mov.s f0,f2`, 0.0 and 50.0 sharing f12, and the f0/f2/f14 product temps with the
     `mov.s f12,f2` copy of k (a ternary clamp, or the clamp inside the operator call, misses);
   - the Vec3 ctor-forwards-to-`set()` recipe from #1 again; dot products in natural
     `a*x + b*y + c*z` order (cfe needed `z + (y + x)`); a named `Data *p` held across the stores
     (without it `ev->data` is reloaded once).
   Left: the operator temps sit 16 bytes low (#2), case 6 keeps 0.0 in f12 (target f2; chained
   `x = y = z = 0.0f`, a named zero and `0` vs `0.0f` do not move it), and `bu_d900_k990` needs a
   pin at 0x990.
5. **h2h 1360 is C++ (94.49 -> 99.76, NM donor `h2hproc_uso_ncc_1360.cpp`).** The edg-order virtual
   call at the top is the tell. What it took:
   - blink gates `if (((ctx->f6B8 == 0) ? counter : 16) & 0x10)`: one pooled ?: temp in v0, shared
     with the vtable load at the top;
   - the colour as an `unsigned char c` with `if (v != 1) c = 115; else c = 0;`: an int `c` is
     coalesced into a3, while the char keeps the target's `or a3,v0` argument copy;
   - `v = ...; if (...) ...; gl(buf, fmt, v, c);` on ONE source line: as1 then puts
     `addiu a0,sp,56` before `lw a2,0(t7)` (the kit XXXIII per-line schedule);
   - one `Item *it` for the four sub-items (its uopt spill is the target's sp+32) with inline
     `reset()` / `move()` members.
   Left (6 words): in `it->move(self->a.font->w + 68, ...)` the target keeps the font pointer in v1
   and the width in v0; here the pointer is a t-ring temp and the width goes to v1 (through `r` or
   `v`). A 5th declared scalar grows the frame by 8; a `Font::width()` accessor gets v1 for the
   pointer but adds two unpooled temps (frame +8) and re-colours the top of the function.
6. **Out-of-line ctor drafts (mangled donor symbol; `c125/nccr.sh` compiles, renames the single
   `T` symbol with objcopy and diffs).**
   - gl 35B1C: `Node::Node(List *, Key, int)` with a 4-byte `Key` passed by value; the frame comes
     from an inline `int &Key::r()` used as `kr.r() == t.r()` (reference return temps; `get()`
     returns by value and colours wrong) plus a `Key &kr = k` alias. 77/77 words, 5 diffs: the vptr
     store `sw t6,12(s4)` before `addiu v1,s4,4; addiu at,-4` (target after), the same residue as the
     cfe NM. Source lines (all on one line, inline ctor out of class, ctor-init forms) and class shape
     (virtual first, base split) do not move it.
   - gl 3800C: 63/63 with `h = reg(id)` except that the target passes id in a1 with a0 untouched.
     Not an uninitialized int/float local (homed and loaded), not an empty or 4-byte struct by value
     (byte/word copy), not a struct return (a0 = return slot), not a dead store, not an inline
     wrapper with an unused parameter.
   - gl 4B0A8 (588 B) is also an out-of-line ctor: base ctor out of line `Base(name)` with the vptr
     at +0x28 in the BASE (so the derived vptr store follows the base call), by-value `P2` copy of a
     const table, four calls, the 4E244 iterator over `src->arr`, `gSPDisplayList` through an inline
     `next()`. First draft 166 raw words: one s-register too many (the construct-block this copy in
     s0) and the target frame is 168 with ~20 dead words below the iterator.
   - h2h 620 (716 B): four protocol levels (new 1724 / 1704 / 80 / 44) = Obj : N1704 : N80 : Node44
     with Node44 : Base0 whose ctor is out of line, a member at +0x50 with an out-of-line ctor, the
     list `attach()` inline (owner/flag) used three times, `new Holder` whose base ctor is out of
     line, virtual slot 11. Draft 178 vs 177 words: the N80 `this` temp is memory-resident at sp+48
     in the target (reload every use, also the `new Holder` result), coloured a3 here, and the target
     frame has two more temp words (56 vs 48).
7. **Iterator siblings of 4E244.** gl 49B3C: `Self::iter() { Arr *self = &arr; return AIter(self); }`
   called as `self->iter()` with `for`/`while` either way puts `it` at 116 and the ret/construct temps
   at 100/88 (target 92/80) for 31 raw words (from 40); `AIter(&arr)` direct in `Self::iter()` gives
   92/80 but frame 128 with li at 36 (target 40), 38 words. gl 41D40: the target holds `&G` in s2
   across the arg0 call and a pooled Arr pointer in s1; named `Arr **g`, `Arr *&g`, dead redefinitions
   and an inline `Reg::run()` member all fold the address back into `lui; lw %lo` (69 words).
8. **Gate notes.** The 1304C / D900 / 1360 donors change NM-object sizes in bootup_uso_tail4 (+8)
   and h2hproc (+8); the post0b clip (0x2e84c) is untouched. Purge
   `build/non_matching/src/{bootup_uso/bootup_uso,bootup_uso/bootup_uso_tail4,h2hproc_uso/h2hproc_uso}.c.o`
   and the new `*_ncc_*.cpp.o` (4948, 1304C, D900, 1360) before a gate.

## kit XXXIII (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 125): pooled scratch = call argument, per-line as1 schedule, NCC frame = declared scalars, cfront vs edg new <a name="kit-xxxiii-agent-g-run-125"></a>

Three exacts (gui 27A0 1040 B, 3B80 932 B, 0148 1044 B; 61.85 -> 62.25 %), all NCC donors spliced into
gui_uso.c.o (src/gui_uso/gui_uso_ncc_{27A0,3B80,0148}.cpp).

1. **gui 27A0 (run-124 draft at 4 words -> exact): the pooled int scratch is also the strip helper's 2nd
   argument.** The run-124 draft reused the `a1` PARAMETER as the scratch with `int x = a1;`, which put the
   `or s8,a1` copy after the `sw a2` home store. Correct shape: x IS the parameter, and a separate `int t`
   holds the width/height reads, the context pointer (`((Ctx *)(t = (int)CTX))->next()`), the switch value
   (`switch (t = self->spr->mode)`) AND the sprite passed as the second argument of the first call
   (`t = (int)self->spr; tile = gl(budget / h, (Spr *)t);`). That last use gives t a preference for a1, uopt
   colours it a1 before x, and x (colour s8) is copied at entry with the other parameter moves. Every
   earlier variant (named local, inline width(), `register`, `if (0) &x`) left t in v1 because nothing tied
   it to a1. Rule: when a pooled temp's colour is an argument register, look for a call where the same
   value is passed in that register and route it through the temp.
2. **gui 3B80 (10 words -> exact): as1 schedules per source line.** In all three case arms the target is
   `lui; addiu; li budget; b; sw fn` and ours put the `li` in the delay slot. Statement order, types, an
   inline helper returning budget, `fn` through a pointer / reference: no change (uopt emits `li` first in
   every spelling, the -S output shows it). Writing `case 0: budget = 4096;` on one line and
   `fn = (RFn)&D_3B80_f0; break;` on the NEXT line gives the target order (the same line-boundary effect as
   kit XXVII #4). Both on one line, or `fn` first, or `break;` alone on a line do not.
3. **gui 0148 (cfe NM 99.98, 255/261 -> exact): an NCC frame is one word per declared scalar.** Under NCC
   the cfe body compiled with nosp-0 but the same frame 136 vs 128. NCC drops never-referenced scalars and
   ignores `register`; the frame is (declared referenced scalars) words plus the anonymous spill area right
   below them. Thirteen locals put the gw/gh spills at sp+68/64 (target 72/68), so the target has TWELVE:
   - remove `line` (index `(px + y * a2)[x]`), then drop one more. Param reuse is the only removal that
     keeps the colouring: the width sum lives in the dead `a1` parameter (dead after `a0->pixels = a1`;
     declare it `int a1`, cast at the store) -- the target's s5 holds a1 then the sum;
   - that leaves a1/sum in s6 and maxw in s5 (rank swap). A 10-minute permuter run on the NCC source
     (compile.sh wraps the C in `extern "C" {}` and calls NCC; target.s = the expected words as `.word`)
     found a dead `if (maxw) {}` after the fill loop: it extends maxw's live range, lowers its priority,
     and the webs swap to the target colours. Declaration order of the register-only scalars is irrelevant
     (150 random orders all scored the same).
4. **gui 329C / 2DE0 (not exact, best NCC 106 / ~166 raw words; drafts g125/gui/x2.cpp, d1.cpp).**
   - The target's pooled temp in s0 (next() `this`, the switch value, the first MAX temp) needs a CALL
     inside its live range: write the three case arms as an inline member `CTX->load(tex, w, h)` that calls
     the loader with `this` -- the inline `this` temp is defined in each arm, the pooled variable's range now
     contains the call blocks, and uopt gives it s0 (`lw s0,36(t2)` mode load, as the target).
   - Frame: six used scalars above w/h (`Spr *s; int tile = 0; int x, y; float fw, fh;` then `int w, h;`);
     `int tile = 0` passed as the macro's tile argument is the sixth (an unused scalar is dropped).
   - Left: every t-register is one lower than the target from the first packet on (target keeps t2 busy:
     its spr register is the same variable as the second MAX temp), and the s16 `x << 2` / int `y << 2`
     of gSPScisTextureRectangle are computed one basic block later than the target (target: in the block
     that defines x / y). Named xl/yl ints, short xl, `x * 4`, float fx/fy staging, `self->sp()` accessors,
     `Spr::info(int &w, int &h)` (makes w/h address-taken: w/h memory homes stay right but self gets homed)
     all fail. 2DE0 (f32-scale sibling) shows the identical two defects under the same source.
5. **gl 65494 NCC draft (g125/gl/b1.cpp, raw 233 / nosp 115; cfe NM 78 %).** What already matches:
   - `V3` with `set()`, `V3 &operator=(V3 v)` and `operator+=(V3 v)` BY VALUE (a const-ref version loses
     the param hop: each assignment is ret temp -> param temp word copy -> float stores), `operator-` /
     `operator*` as `return V3(...)` through the set()-forwarding ctor (x f0, z f12, y f2 as the target);
   - the hit struct must not hold a V3 with a user default ctor (its implicit ctor runs the `this == 0 ->
     new(12)` protocol); keep a POD `P3 n` and assign `n = (V3 &)hit.n`;
   - `sumN` accumulates component-wise (no param copy), `sumP += o->prev * -d` through operator+=; zero the
     sums z, y, x; prototype the callees (400.0f must not promote to double).
   Open: the second word copy of each param hop is re-read from memory in the target (ours forwards
   registers), the param temps are distinct per site in the target (each `addiu tN,sp,K` local) where ours
   pools them and LICM-hoists the address into s6/s7 (one s-reg too many, count spilled), two zero
   registers in the target (f24 outer, f22 for n's components), frame offsets (n -84, hit -144).
6. **timproc_b5 is cfront output compiled by cfe, not NCC.** `new Panel` in D550 is `v0 = alloc(712);
   if (v0) { base check: if (this == 0) this = alloc(696) ... }` with NO most-derived check: the cfront
   protocol (`new T` calls the ctor with this = 0 and the ctor allocates). NCC's edg (`p = operator
   new(sizeof); if (p) T::T(p)`) emits an extra check for the most-derived class. So keep the ||-alloc-
   fallback C reconstructions there (and switches get real jumptables, as 4118 has).
7. **timproc_b5 4118 NM 86 -> 76 raw words:** `if (1) {}` between the 0.5f and 1.0f groups of the first
   quad-constant block orders the constants as the target. Open, all in the 8-case tail: in case 0 the
   target reloads `this` from its arg home ONCE into v0 for four accesses, while case 1 (and ours
   everywhere) reloads per access; copies into existing or new locals are copy-propagated away and change
   nothing; the t-register ring of the later cases follows from it. The function's .rodata offsets in the
   NM tree are 132 bytes low only because NM-tree predecessors drop their literal pools; the matching tree
   would place them through the INCLUDE_ASM .late_rodata order.
8. **Landing hazard (seen this run):** a donor referencing a symbol that is missing from
   undefined_syms_auto.txt made mips-linux-gnu-ld SEGFAULT (not an undefined-reference error). Define every
   donor-only blank alias (here D_27A0_fn*, D_3B80_f*) as `= 0x00000000;`.


## kit XXXIV (agent-c 2026-10-22, run 126): DL pointer rotation = block placement (1304C), NCC fill-rect emitter, reused-variable coalescing, decode fixes <a name="kit-xxxiv-agent-c-run-126"></a>

Four exacts (bootup 1304C 2264 B, gl 46FA8 316 B, bootup 7D04 332 B, gl 45CB0 368 B; ROM cmp clean after each)
and one NM decode fix. Scratch: `c126/` (`d1304C`, `d46FA8`, `d4A7C4`, `d7D04`, `dD900`, `dH1360`, `d49B3C`, `d4CDB0`,
`d43BEC`, `d470E4`), tools in `c126/tools/`.

1. **bootup 1304C EXACT: the packet-pointer rotation is uopt block placement (kit XXXV).** The run-125 NCC
   donor was shape- and frame-exact with 42 raw words left, all in the 28-packet display-list tail: the
   target's per-packet `_g` pointers go a1 a2 a3 a1 a2 t0 a1 | a1 a2 a3 a1 a2 a1 a2 a3 ... where ours was a
   strict a1 a2 a3 ring. A `-Wo,-varref,N` sweep (diagnostic only) moved it only a little (42 -> 37 at N 18/19),
   so the boundaries had to be PLACED. `c126/tools/pksearch.py` inserts a statement after any subset of packet
   lines (one line per `G2(c->next(), w0, w1)` macro) and scores all subsets in parallel (NCC compiles in
   ~0.1 s; K=4 over 29 positions = 27 841 jobs in 3 minutes):
   - empty `if (1) {}` between packets: best 15 words (after packets 12, 23, 25);
   - on top of that, packet 26 through `nextb()` (`int n = dl->n++; if (1) {} Gfx *g = &dl->buf[n]; return g;`,
     the boundary between the index bump and the slot address): 6 words;
   - on top of that, packets 3 and 18 through `G2B` (`{ Gfx *_g = pkt; if (1) {} _g->w0 = ..; _g->w1 = ..; }`,
     the boundary after the slot pointer, before its stores): 0 words.
   So three kinds of cut were needed: between commands, inside next(), and inside the command macro. The t0
   choices in the target are the slot pointers whose live range starts in one block and ends in the next.
   Search the three kinds in stages (each stage keeps the previous best); a flat search over all of them is too
   big. `SUB:old=>new` mode of pksearch swaps a spelling per packet instead of inserting a line.
2. **gl 46FA8 EXACT: a post0b fill-rect emitter is C++.** gDPFillRectangle + gDPPipeSync after up to three
   pre-dispatch calls, else an out-call. Tells: the inline next() append (lw dl; lw n; addiu; sw; reload dl),
   and all four register params homed at entry and RELOADED from their homes (edg keeps x/y/w/h memory
   resident here; cfe never did). First NCC compile was 79/79 words with 15 colour diffs. Then:
   - `Ctx *g; Gfx *p = (g = a0->mgr->ctx)->next();` makes the context the pooled next() `this` (v1, as in
     the target) for both appends; a named `Ctx *g = ...; g->next()` coloured a0, and two separate
     `a0->mgr->ctx->next()` expressions got the first append right but recomputed the context;
   - `-varref` sweep: exact minus one slot register at N = 21 (needed: one fewer counted load before the
     cut), so the fix is a load-saving spelling, not an empty if;
   - the spelling product (`c126/tools/variants.py`, all combinations of a few alternatives per site) found
     it at the default limit: `Gfx *next() { int n = dl->n++; Gfx *g = &dl->buf[n]; return g; }` (named
     result) puts the second append's list / index / slot in a2 / v0 / a3. Note this is the OPPOSITE of kit
     XXXV's `return &dl->buf[dl->n++]`: which spelling saves the load depends on the function, so put
     several next() spellings in the product.
   Placeholder host + REPLACE_FUNC_BODY in both trees; the post0b NM clip moved 0x2e84c -> 0x2e854 (62F08 NM
   offset 0x2e804; the clip rule still holds).
2b. **gl 45CB0 EXACT: light record fill + light packets, C++.** Two inline next() pools on the context
   (display list +0xC, 0x48-byte light records +0x2C), unused first parameter homed at entry. The first NCC
   compile had the right shape (92/92 words) once the three packets used per-command slot pointers (the
   context then stays in a1 and is reloaded from its home after the call, as in the target; one reused
   `Gfx *p` coloured it s0). The colour bytes' registers (target r/g/b = a0/t1/t2) were block placement:
   `-varref` 40 helped (the target cuts LATER), so the twelve `l->c[k] = r` stores became three chained
   stores through one pointer (`{ unsigned char *q = l->c; q[0xC] = q[8] = q[4] = q[0] = r; ... }`: one r
   load and one l load instead of four each, same code), and two empty `if (1) {}` (after the b conversion,
   after the first packet; nccif K=2) placed the rest. Frame 64 = two dummy scalars `int k1, k2; k1 = 0;
   k2 = 0;` (the dead stores vanish, the words stay; unused declarations without the stores are dropped).
   Recipe for next()-tell functions in agent-c units: NCC draft with per-command slot pointers, then
   `-varref` sweep, then load-saving spellings (chained stores, named next() result), then nccif K<=2, then
   dummy scalars for the frame.
3. **bootup 7D04 EXACT (cfe): a reused variable coalesced two values.** The run-107 NM was 5 words off:
   `k = s0->0x40; k = k->0x84; ...` reused `k` for the object and its list, so both took v1; the target holds
   the list in v0. Giving the list its own `int *l` (and `l = *(int **)(k + 0x84) + 1` for the second call,
   which also gives the unrolled loop's dead `addiu v0,v0,4`) is exact. The root table pin is
   `D_7D04_root = 0x23C` (= func_0000023C; the ROM holds `lw 0x254`, an intra-module USO reloc is RESOLVED in
   the ROM bytes) -- a zero pin linked but failed the ROM cmp. Check the ROM word before choosing a pin value.
4. **gl 4A7C4 decode fix (NM raw 16 -> 2).** The flag test is not an early return: its `bnez` lands on the
   final `jal` (with `or a0,a1` in the delay), so the push is an if-block and the callback runs on both
   paths. `rdiff --raw` shows it as a branch target off by 8 (L78 vs L70); read raw branch targets before
   blaming colours. With an empty `if (1) {}` after the slot store the string address is no longer hoisted
   above the compare and idx colours a0. Left: the carrier spills to the second parameter's home (sp+36)
   where the target uses the first (sp+32); a 1-param form with a local index colours the index v1 again.
5. **NCC frame forensics.** `-O2 -g3` + `c124/tools/mdebug.py` prints every named local's vfp offset
   (`c126/tools/fr.sh FILE FUNC` = frame + locals + raw diff in one line). Reference-binding temps appear
   as `__V<number>` (e.g. an iterator construct temp, const-ref parameters), plain value temps stay unnamed.
   - gl 49B3C (now frame-exact, colours left, 56 raw words in the draft vs 60 in-tree, not landed): the target
     has `it` at -12, an unused 12-byte block at -24, the return temp at -36 and the construct temp at -48;
     that is `AIter Self::iter() { return AIter(&arr); }` (no `this` temp: self is a parameter), a dead
     12-byte class object declared right after `it` (`Pad12 dead;`, a class with a ctor so NCC keeps it), and
     `cur()` as `a->data[idx]` without the operator[] reference temp (puts the list iterator at -88).
     Colours: the target's pooled scratch is a1 (construct `this`, idx+1, vptr), ours v1; an inline S(o)
     address helper made the construct use a1 but added a function-level temp above `it`.
   - bootup D900: removing the block `int r` (reuse a function-scope slot) and writing the clamp as if/else
     puts the operator temps at the target's -72, but the clamp's inline temps (2 words) sit above the
     operator temps in every spelling (value / const-ref / ?: / local-r / void-ref clamp); the target has them
     below. 10 raw words, unchanged.
6. **Did not move.** h2h 1360 (4 words with a `Font *r` named pointer: the width loads straight into a1,
   the target loads it into the pooled v0 first; every accessor / inline / named-width form that gives v0
   recolours the whole pool), 4CDB0 under NCC (14, cfe NM stays 5), 43BEC under NCC (self spilled to its
   home instead of s0), the 470E4 colour twins under NCC (colour bytes register-promoted, target keeps
   them in sp+4..7 homes), 4EE44 (reusing a loop variable for the base load does nothing). NCC drafts left in
   scratch: gl 45E20 (30 raw words: the loop index / accumulator s-registers swapped, and the target keeps a
   redundant second `lo = 1984` that both front ends fold), gl 4B2F4 (77: the pooled next() temps go to
   s-registers across the pack call), gl 44CE8 (12, all frame: `&pool.buf[n++]` costs two edg temp words
   and the record pointer spills to a fresh slot instead of its home, frame 48 vs 32 in every spelling),
   bootup 1A44 (89: the target evaluates the matrix-slot argument before the float conversions).
7. **cfe sweeps over the agent-c units.** `c126/tools/usweep.py UNIT...` recompiles the processed NM-tree
   `.c` (build/non_matching/src/UNIT.c, plain `cc`, no make) at several `-varref` limits and scores every
   non-exact function; `c126/tools/cfeif.py UNIT FN K` is the in-tree empty-if search on the same file
   (non-destructive, parallel; whole post0b compiles in 0.4 s). Over post0b (< 0x50000), bootup_uso*,
   game_libs_post, h2hproc and timproc_b1: no function becomes exact at any limit (largest movers 5F0B8 is
   agent-g's, 54E78 agent-g's; mine: 42778 66 -> 55, h2h C18 89 -> 72); empty-if K=2 on 42 small post0b
   residuals found only 4A7C4 and 46FA8 (15 -> 12). The cfe near-miss band in these units is not block
   placement; NCC conversions of next()-tell functions are the better lead (tellscan: 4B2F4, 45E20, 45CB0,
   488A0, 483BC, 1A44 untried).
8. **Gate notes.** Purge `build/{,non_matching/}src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso_tail4.c.o`,
   `build/{,non_matching/}src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`
   and every `*_ncc_*.cpp.o` (new: `game_libs_ncc_46FA8.cpp.o`, `game_libs_ncc_45CB0.cpp.o`). New pins:
   `D_7D04_root = 0x23C`, `func_7D04_randf = 0`. post0b NM clip 0x2e84c -> 0x2e854 (62F08 NM offset 0x2e804).

## kit XXXV (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 126): uopt's 20-variable-load block limit, empty-if layout search, gui DL emitters <a name="kit-xxxv-agent-g-run-126"></a>

Six exacts: gui 08C0 664 B, 17DC 640 B, 2334 640 B, 055C 348 B, 16A4 240 B (NCC donors), and gl 5721C 856 B (cfe,
post0b). That is +3388 B. Also timproc_b5 4118 NM raw 76 -> 72. All of them came from one finding: uopt ends a
straight-line basic block after a fixed number of variable loads, and because interference is decided per block,
where that boundary falls picks the colours.

1. **uopt ends a basic block after 20 counted variable loads** (uopt source `uoptinput.c` ~181:
   `endblock = varrefs >= curvarreflimit`, checked at every statement boundary where the ucode stack is empty;
   `varreflimit` is 20 by default, `uoptinit.c` ~720). There is no label, but the result is a real graph node
   for everything after it: live ranges, `livebbs`, interference (`intfering()` = intersection of `livebbs`).
   Which loads count:
   - a load counts when the variable was not assigned earlier in the same block, when that assignment cannot be
     forwarded, or when the assigned value contains an `ilod`, was killed by a store, or is a big tree;
   - a load is free (forwarded, not counted) when the in-block assignment is a constant, an address, another
     variable, or a single-use expression without loads. `veqv` (memory-overlapping) variables never count.
   So the first block of a long DL emitter ends after about two appends. Every web defined before the boundary
   and still live after it interferes with everything in both blocks. A web that starts after it interferes only
   with the second block. This is the "slot pointer comes out one register off" residual of the whole gui
   family (kits XXV / XXVII / XXXI): it was never a colouring tie, it was the boundary.
2. **Diagnostic: sweep the limit.** `-Wo,-varref,N` sets the limit. This is for diagnosis only, never in a
   build: it is a toolchain flag change that alters codegen. Compile the draft at N in {12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32,
   1000}. If some N other than 20 makes it exact or much closer, the residual is block placement. The sign
   tells the direction: if larger N helps, the target has fewer counted loads before the boundary (remove some);
   if smaller N helps, it has more. Scratch tools: `g126/vr.sh` (NCC draft), `g126/g57/vc.sh` (cfe file),
   `g126/vs/sweep.py` (every NM function of whole units, NM-tree .c recompiled per N), `g126/vs/dsweep.py` (every
   old NCC draft under the scratch tree). Results:
   - gui 17DC: exact at N >= 23. Needed: three fewer counted loads before the third slot pointer's definition.
   - gl 5721C (cfe): 15 words at 20, 2 at N >= 22. Needed: fewer loads before the colour block.
   - unit sweep (187 NM functions in agent-g units): only 5721C moved to near-exact. Partial movers: gl 54E78
     121 -> 92 (N 32), 5F0B8 100 -> 81 (N 28), 697C4 222 -> 202, timproc_b5 5BF0 80 -> 74 (N >= 24). gui 329C
     draft (g125 w0.cpp) went 106 -> 88 at N 12, but the pooled-temp colour (s0 vs t2) stays. Kernel, titproc,
     mgrproc, arcproc and b3 did not move (labels everywhere, or IDO 5.3).
3. **Spellings that remove counted loads without changing code:**
   - `Gfx *next() { return &dl->buf[dl->n++]; }` instead of `int n = dl->n++; return &dl->buf[n];`: same
     code, one fewer pooled copy read per append.
   - `p->set(w0, w1)` (an inline `Gfx::set(unsigned a, unsigned b) { w0 = a; w1 = b; }`) instead of `p->w0 =
     ..; p->w1 = ..;`. Reads of set()'s `this` forward to p and are free; the two p loads are gone.
   - cfe 5721C: `d = max - min;` read twice instead of `(max - min)` at both divides. d's single-use, load-free
     value is forwarded, so its reads are free, and the parameter loads are counted once.
   17DC / 2334 = n1 next() + set() for the first two packets (`src/gui_uso/gui_uso_ncc_17DC.cpp`). 08C0 = the
   same recipe. A first exact used an empty if inside a second next(); the recipe version replaced it.
   5721C also needed `arr[0] = ..; arr[1] = ..;` on ONE line (as1 per-line scheduling, kit XXXIII #2).
4. **Empty-if layout search (055C, 16A4).** When the target needs boundaries that no load count gives, place
   them: an empty `if (1) {}` after a statement, or inside an inline member (`Gfx *nextb() { int n = dl->n++;
   if (1) {} return &dl->buf[n]; }` puts the boundary between the index bump and the slot address). Search
   all placements by brute force: 055C (six appends) took 2048 variants (next / nextb per packet x empty if
   after each packet) and found exactly one exact layout. 16A4 took 256 variants. The search is mechanical and
   fast for NCC drafts (`g126/ifs/nccif.py FILE FUNC UNIT K`: every 1..K-subset of statement positions,
   parallel). For in-tree cfe bodies it is `g126/ifs/ifsearch.py UNIT FUNC K` (it rewrites the unit source
   and restores it; never run it while editing that unit). The cfe batch over 28 small-residual NM wraps
   (single positions) found nothing: those residuals are not block placement. Caveat: an explicit label
   boundary that a live PARAMETER crosses can home the parameters (`sw a1..a3` at entry). 17DC with an empty
   if before the first append went 192 -> 116 for that reason. The varref route (#3) has no labels.
5. **Reading the boundary.** `-Wo,-zdbug:2` with the dump toolchain (`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump`, ecvt
   fixed) prints `flow graph` nodes and per-node `expoccur` / `antlocs` / `avlocs` bit lists. Map the bits
   through the itab (`-Wo,-zdbug:6`, `isvar` lines carry the frame offset of each variable) to see which
   statement starts the second node. `-zdbug:6` then shows the colouring order. The tie rule (kit XXXI #5,
   uoptreg2.c): the first register in class order that is free over the whole live range and already
   `regstaken`. So a web that does not share a block with the pooled dl temp takes v1. One that shares a block
   with p1 / p2 takes the next free a-/t-register.
6. **timproc_b5 4118 (76 -> 72): case 0 reads the index first** into the dead `temp_t0` (a new local grows the
   frame), so the `lw 952` is hoisted as in the target. The rest of case 0 is LR splitting: `-zdbug:6` on the
   NM tree shows arg0 split into 0 / 1213 / 1215 (uncoloured, -ve save), 1216 -> a0, 1217 -> a2, 1226 / 1244
   uncoloured. The target has one more coloured piece (case 0 -> v0, one reload for four uses). The function
   does not react to `-varref` (cfe output full of labels). Not cracked.
7. **game_uso 0B3C has a 4-entry jumptable** (`sltiu 4; jr`, table at game_uso_D_807FF970+0x50) on
   `s->26C` with cases 0..3. Probes: cfe tables a switch only from 5 case labels (4 cases, with or without
   default, chain); IDO 5.3 cfe the same; NCC never tables (8 cases still chain). With `case 4:` the range is 5
   (`sltiu 5`). No front end tried makes this table, so the switch shape is open. The NM is also 16 bytes of
   frame high and uses different low slots (target 48..96, ours from 100). Raw 797, shape (--noreg --nosp) 37.
   Fixes known but not landed: `one` rematerialised as `li 1`, `q = bv + 0x70` kept unfolded in a register.
   7C1C was not attempted beyond the sweep.
8. **gui 2BB0 is the 27A0 strip blitter with a fixed tile of 32** (NCC draft `g126/g2b/d2.cpp`, raw 64 vs
   cfe NM 57, not landed). Matching: pooled `t` for ctx / spr / tex (the target's s2 web), `w` reused as sx, two
   dummy scalars (`int k1, k2; k1 = 0; k2 = 0;`) for the frame of 112. Open: self is homed at entry in ours
   (the target keeps it in a0 and spills it just before the loop), the target's dead `or v0,v1` copy in the
   > 32 arm, s-register permutation (rem s1 / h s0 / t s2 in the target).
9. **Batch and sweep notes.** The cfe empty-if batch (28 wraps, single positions) moved only gl 51ED8: 10 -> 5
   words with one empty if after `p = ap;`. That is not landed (post0b clip churn for an NM). The 329C draft
   with the macros expanded (`gcc -E -P`) gets the same 88 words with one empty if right after the rectangle
   macro's `_g =` line, which is the boundary the N = 12 sweep found. Gate hazard: `make -n -B` on a unit
   object (my sweep's way of reading compile commands) re-ran sub-makes and rebuilt four NM-tree objects
   (post1b2c, post1c, post2b_c, post2b_d) stale. The report then lost 16 exacts until those objects were
   deleted and rebuilt. Read compile lines from a plain `make -n` on a deleted object, or hard-code them.

## kit XXXVI (agent-c 2026-10-23, run 127): game_libs_post big list, blockcut-search traps, 90CC is cfront C <a name="kit-xxxvi-agent-c-run-127"></a>

No exacts this run. NM improvements: gl 25504 106 -> 76 raw, gl 49B3C 60 -> 32 (run-126 NCC draft spliced into
the NM object only), gl 2C7A4 219 -> 206 and gl 250C8 85 -> 82 (one block cut each). Scratch: `c127/` (`d25504`,
`d26790`, `d26D64`, `d24378`, `d4EE44`, `d437C0`, `dD900`, `d90cc`), tools `c127/tools/fx.py` (replace one function
in the NM-tree processed `.c`, compile out of tree with cfe, raw-diff), `cfeif2.py` (cfeif on any full source),
`survey.py` (raw diffwords of every non-exact function in the agent-c units).

1. **gl 25504 (106 -> 76, `--noreg` 2).** Three source facts the old body missed:
   - frame 88 -> 104 by declaration order alone: `sum, i, cur, e, sh, idx, ret` (ret 7th puts cur's home at sp+92
     as the target; no dummies needed);
   - the first loop is a plain indexed `for (i = 0; i < GW(0x1030); i++) sum += (tab[i]->msk + 15) & -16;` through
     its own table symbol. IV elimination leaves the dead init `or s5,zero,zero` in the target twice (before this
     loop and again as the second loop's init); the hand-written pointer loop dropped it, and the bound re-read from
     the global keeps the loop rolled (no x4 unroll);
   - `gl(e->key, cur, e->msk, (s32)e->sh)` in the else arm: with plain `e->sh` the CSE temp coalesced into a3 and as1
     stole a `lui` into a `bnel`; the cast makes the argument a separate value, the temp stays v1 and the target's
     `bne v1,at; or a3,v1` delay copy appears. (`(u8)` gives an `andi`, `(s8)` a shift pair.) The `if (1) {}` after
     `sh = e->sh;` had to go (the arg2[4] load then becomes a t-temp first operand: `bne t9,v1`).
   Left: the t-ring runs one register low from the first loop on (the target spends t0 and t1 before the word load;
   no cast, mask, `x++; x--;` or block cut reproduces the extra slot), the first loop's sum / -16 colours are swapped
   (a1 / v1 in the target), and the main loop's slot address is v0 here, a t-temp there.
2. **24378: the same dead IV init.** The target's `or a0,zero,zero` at the top (live into the first call's a0) is
   most likely the init of the u64 clear loop's index after IV elimination, not an argument. Every indexed spelling
   tried unrolls x4 there (the target does not); not solved. A block cut inside the unrolled byte loop "improves" raw
   words 323 -> 263 only because the function shrinks to 290 words: **reject any raw-word gain that changes the
   function length.**
3. **blockcut-search trap: cuts between `}` and `else`.** The tool inserts `if (1) {}` at every statement end,
   including right after the closing brace of an if-arm, which turns `} else {` into `} if (1) {} else {` and
   re-binds the else to the empty if (the else body becomes dead code). Three of this run's best "layouts" were that:
   2119C 146 -> 108, 2B5F4 197 -> 175, and the second cut of 250C8. Check every proposed position against the source
   before landing (or exclude positions followed by `else`). The valid single cuts landed: 250C8 after
   `gl(sub, field18 & 0xff);`, 2C7A4 after the opcode fetch `r = gl_func_0003F010(sub);`. `-Wo,-varref` sweeps leave
   all eleven big-list functions unchanged (labels everywhere).
4. **bootup 90CC is cfront-style C (cfe), not edg.** An NCC prefix draft (Named base with vptr at +0x28, member Sub
   at +0x3EC, FloatParam members) shows edg's out-of-line ctor homing `this` and reloading it, and inlining the base
   ctor with its own this==0 check. The target keeps self in s2 from a single top-level `if (self == 0 && !(self =
   alloc(2700))) return 0`, calls the base ctor out of line (`func(this, &D_8730)`), then expands each member ctor
   with the alloc protocol on the MEMBER address (`if (this + 0x3EC == 0) alloc(0x154)`, failure skips to the next
   member). The param members are 0x18-byte objects: out-of-line base ctor `(this, owner, Key by value, 1)` (`sw
   a2,8(sp)` home), vptr +0xC, float +0x10, int +0x14; each site copies its Key into its own temp (sp+324, 320, ...)
   and then into one shared parameter temp (sp+260): cfront temporaries. The second member group (+0x540) passes the
   key through a pointer to a stack temp held in s1. The in-tree cfe body already has this shape; its 553 raw words
   include local-symbol addend diffs (`func_00008744 + 4` vs `&D + 0x8748`) that link to the same address, and the
   reloc-masked count is 421. Next step there is colour/schedule work on the cfe body, not a rewrite.
5. **Probes that did not move:** 26790 (64): the target keeps the `&D` constant candidate in ONE register (a3) in
   every case including through the 0xF3 loop (`lw 8304(a3)` / `lw 11516(a3)`, IV `addu v1,a1,t1` offset first);
   ours folds the 0xF3 loads to `lui; lw %lo` and colours the candidate a2 elsewhere. `g` through F5/F6, a struct-array
   alias, `i * 208 + base` (int or pointer), `&arr[i]`, a PRE-style memory bound all left it. 26D64 (93): loop-head
   spellings (2-D queue index, `<< 3`, idx after the test, break + tail store) do not stop uopt sinking the `sll`.
   4EE44 (2): the src base load colours v0 vs a1 in every spelling (float** + 45, int, unsigned, reused counters).
   437C0: dead `if (arg1) {}` anywhere and reusing x/g/arg1 for the sub-object pointers fail (PR #10 matched it with
   one `s32 var_a2` for both sub-objects among ~25 m2c-named locals: `src/match_imports/gl_func_000437C0.c`).
   D900 (now exact via PR #10): our NCC frame hunt was the wrong front end. The import is cfe C with an explicit
   goto dispatch chain, `int pad[2]` / `int pad[7]` frame pads and staged struct copies (`scaled -> stage -> impulse`):
   `src/match_imports/func_0000D900.c`. Read the PR #10 imports before resuming any of their siblings.

## kit XXXVII (agent-g 2026-10-22, run 127): block-cut sweep with scripts/blockcut-search.py, K&R va_alist, declared-local frames <a name="kit-xxxvii-agent-g-run-127"></a>

Three exacts (gl 51ED8 132 B, gl B958 276 B, timproc_b5 8C44 244 B = +652 B, 63.34 -> 63.43 %) and
timproc_b5 6E08 NM raw 81 -> 23. All came out of one systematic sweep with a new reusable tool.

1. **scripts/blockcut-search.py** (usage in docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#blockcut-search-run127):
   places emission-free `if (1) {}` cuts at every 1..K-subset of statement positions of ONE
   function, compiles each variant out of tree in parallel and scores rdiff --raw --pins. cfe wraps
   build in PROMOTE mode (only that wrap compiled as C, the matching-build asm-processor pipeline,
   so a 0 is directly landable); NCC donors / drafts via `--file`; `--swap 'X=>Y'` adds spelling
   alternatives (the header too); `--also NAME` cuts inside an inline member; `--varref` is the
   kit XXXV diagnostic. It never runs make (the run-126 `make -n -B` trap) and never edits src/.
2. **Positions after `{` matter.** The run-126 cfe batch cut only after `;` and `}`. gl B958's
   (IDO-unrolled word-compare loop) exact layout is ONE cut directly after `for (...) {`: it moves the
   `or a0,a2` copy into the first `beq` delay slot, a "delay-slot swap" that 30 spellings had not
   moved. timproc_b5 8C44 (guarded do-while scan) needs two cuts, after `cnt = n + 1;` and after
   `i = 0;` (k = 2, 231 variants): they decide the i/p/n colours (s1/s0/v0).
3. **K&R varargs.h form for cfe varargs functions (gl 51ED8).** `void f(char *a0, int a1, ...)`
   with `&a1` for the va pointer stores a1 TWICE (the varargs save AND an address-taken param home;
   the target stores it once, in the a1/a2/a3 save group). Writing the function as
   `void f(a0, va_alist) char *a0; int va_alist;` (the varargs.h convention: cfe recognises the
   name and saves a1..a3) and using `&va_alist` / `va_alist` in the body gives the single save.
   Renaming a plain K&R param without `va_alist` drops the a2/a3 saves. Plus one cut after `p = ap;`.
   Other cfe varargs bodies in agent-g units (61478, 61B30) did not move with it (their residuals
   are colour / schedule).
4. **timproc_b5 m2c bodies: one frame word per DECLARED local.** 6E08 had 11 m2c temps (frame 88 vs
   56). The target frame holds exactly four declared words (old1 52, two unused, old2 40), so the
   body was rewritten with `old1, i, cur, old2` (decl order = slot order), the slot as an array
   index `((s32 *)(arg0 + 0x3D0))[i]` (s0-first addu; `(int)arg0 + i * 4 + 0x3D0` gives the reverse
   operand order), the counter bump evaluated after the item call (`(i += 1, 0x2A4)` inside the
   offset; a separate `i += 1;` lands in a `bgezl` delay slot), and the one cut after the first
   capture (81 -> 40 alone: it keeps old1 spilled instead of in s2). LEFT (23 words): the slot RMW
   (target `addiu v0,v0,976; sw 0(v0)`, a pointer temp in v0; a named pointer gives v1 and reversed
   addu operands, the field form folds the offset) and block 2's `i = 0` after the first call.
5. **Sweep table** (raw --pins words; NM tree before; "cut" = best blockcut-search result, k = 2 for
   raw <= 16 else k = 1, greedy k = 3..5 for the movers):

   | function | bytes | raw before | best after | exact? |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | gl 5062C (NCC NM donor) | 2756 | 1 | 1 | no (edg return-slot order; 15 class / ctor variants again) |
   | timproc_b5 2B74 | 1876 | 25 | 25 | no (flat) |
   | timproc_b5 32C8 | 1480 | 5 | 5 | no (flat; 30 vF8 / vEC / zero / cut orders) |

   | gui 2BB0 (cfe / NCC d2) | 560 | 57 / 64 | 41 / 57 | no |

6. **Negatives worth not repeating:** gl 5062C with P3-typed parameters: `V3 *` / `const P3 &`

## kit XXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 128): rewrites from scratch, block-pointer RMW, void accumulators, variable-reuse colours <a name="kit-xxxix-agent-g-run-128"></a>

One exact (timproc_b5 6E08, 624 B, 63.43 -> 63.51 %) and eight NM rewrites. Scratch: `g128/` (`6e`, `75`, `bb`, `7c`,
`2b`, `5f`, `117`, `1460`, `32`); tools `g128/try.py` (swap one wrap body, promote-compile, score), `g128/par.py` /
`parn.py` (score many wrap bodies in parallel through blockcut-search `--file`, `NMT=1` = NM-tree file for units whose
promote build fails), `g128/parf.py` (standalone NCC drafts), `g128/sbs.sh` / `dis.sh` (side by side / relocs),
`g128/fr.sh` (NCC `-g3` local offsets), `g128/ep.py` (episode writer).

1. **timproc_b5 6E08 EXACT (run-127 NM 23 raw): a slot read-modify-write through a block pointer built in two
   steps.** Target: `addu v0,s0,t1; lw t2,976(v0); addiu v0,v0,976; addiu t3,t2,-1; sw t3,0(v0)` -- the load folds
   the offset, the store goes through a pointer that is incremented AFTER the load. `SLOT(i)--`, `*&SLOT(i) -= 1` and
   every one-expression pointer (`&SLOT(i)`, `(s32 *)(a + 0x3D0) + i`, `&((s32 *)a)[i + 244]`, named index) give
   `sw 976(v1)` or reversed addu operands. `{ s32 *p = (s32 *)(arg0 + 0x3D0); p += FW(arg0, 0x3C4); *p -= 1; }` is the
   target (23 -> 2). Scan for the tell with `g128/scan_rmw.py` (`lw rX,K(rB)` / `addiu rB,rB,K` / `sw .,0(rB)`):
   117C, B154, b3 1C68, arcproc 1F54, gl 3430 / 68DD4 have it; in 117C the spelling was already right (its residual is
   b kept in s0 where the target spills a1 to the a0 home).
2. **A block-scoped loop counter keeps `i = 0` after a call (6E08 2 -> 0).** Two identical loops shared `s32 i`; in
   the second the `or s1,zero,zero` was hoisted above the preceding call (no cut, no statement order, `for (i = 0; 0;)`,
   comma forms moved it). Declaring the second loop's counter in its own block (`{ s32 j; ... }`) puts it after the
   call as in the first loop. Keep the top-level `i` declared even if the first loop could also be block-scoped: removing
   it moved the frame words (k1.c, 2 words).
3. **game_uso 7538 rewritten (611 -> 18 raw, same 344 words).** It was a long-long state machine with stubbed arms.
   - It is VOID. v0 is the event-bit word (stored to `out->0x40`), v1 a local `moving` flag (the final out pointer
     reload reuses v1). With an `int` or `long long` return the regalloc dump shows the word as
     `assigned (constrained) 2` = v1 even with nothing else in the function: uopt keeps the return register away from
     the variable that feeds it. Callers ignore the value; the 6A30 NCC donor already declared it void. The exact
     caller 6CF0 needed an explicit `void game_uso_func_00007538();` (its implicit int declaration conflicts); 6CF0 stays
     byte-identical.
   - Dispatch = if / else-if chain of event arms writing `0x6C = m | BIT`; one empty if after the 0x10 arm's if / else
     joins it before the merge reload (the run-127 tool found it); the 0x20 arm writes the `% 9` before the `= 60`.
   - The 0x80 window is `t < 8 || (t >= p + 8 && t < p + 16) || t >= p + p + 16` (short-circuit = the target's three
     compares and the second 0x4DC reload), the limit a nested ternary (inner result in a3, `or a2,a3`).
   - `m = t - 1` written AFTER the 0x100 range chain folds into `t == 1` (`addiu at,zero,1; bne`); written BEFORE the
     chain (another basic block) it stays `addiu a1,a2,-1 ... bnez a1` (84 -> 55). The fold is block-local.
   - The table lookup needs an empty if right after `float *tp = (float *)((char *)&D + 0x638);` or the addend folds
     into the `lwc1` offset instead of the `lui/addiu`.
   - a-register colours by variable reuse (55 -> 18): uopt colours a VARIABLE (one live range for all its webs, numbered
     by first appearance) and unconstrained ranges in number order, each taking the first free register. The target's
     colours are explained by three reused variables: `arg` (a3) also holds the 0x20 / 0x80 arm counters, `n` (a2) is
     the 0x50 counter at entry, the 0x100 countdown value and the 0x4DC period (`n = FW(a0, 0x4DC)` in the window test
     and at the top of the frame body), `m` (a1) is the mask, the decremented counters and `m = n + n`. LEFT (18): the
     two table pointers and the lim tail; every spelling that assigns `m = t + 1` there shifts the whole t-ring of the
     function (217 words), so some candidate then lands in a t register.

## kit XL (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 129): the game_uso camera family as NCC donors, Ctx accessors, POD returns <a name="kit-xl-agent-g-run-129"></a>

Two exacts, both IDO 7.1 NCC (C++) donors spliced into both game_uso trees with REPLACE_FUNC_BODY:
game_uso 2CC8 (768 B, written from scratch, cfe NM was 190 raw) and game_uso 24BC (600 B, run-119 NM donor at
118 raw finished). 63.51 -> 63.69 %. Scratch: `g129/2c`, `g129/24`, `g129/28` (tools `run.sh` = score many donors
in parallel through blockcut-search `--file`, `fr.sh` = frame + slot probe, `../../g128/fr.sh FILE FUNC` = NCC `-g3`
local offsets).

1. **2CC8 / 24BC / 28C0 / 1DDC / BB8C are one C++ family.** All take `Self *a0`, keep `a0->out` (and for 2CC8 / 28C0
   `a0->src->body`) in a two-pointer aggregate `struct Ctx { Body *tgt; Out *out; Ctx(Self *s) { out = s->out; tgt =
   s->src->body; } };` (the target stores both at entry, out above tgt), use `M4::getPos(V3 &)` (the `lwc1 160(rB);
   addiu rB,rB,112; 52(rB)` this-adjust shape comes out by itself under NCC) and `M4::rotate(V3 &)`. Tell for the
   family: the entry `sw t6,top-4(sp)` / `sw t8,top-8(sp)` pair plus a `lw v0,top-4(sp)` reload before each group of
   three float stores.
2. **Ctx accessor = the target's v0 / v1 reloads.** `c.out->setG(q)` reloads `c.out` into a ugen t-register (t9, t0,
   ...) and every later t-register in the function shifts by one. With `Out *getOut() const { return out; }` and
   `Body *getTgt() const { return tgt; }` the call result is an edg temporary and ugen gives it v0 (2CC8: 105 -> 0
   with both accessors; one accessor 31 / 43). The uopt dump shows these temporaries are NOT uopt candidates (only key,
   a2 and one v1 piece are coloured), so the v0 / v1 choice is ugen's. In 24BC the tail needed
   `Out *o = c.getOut(); o->setG(q); o = c.getOut(); o->setP(q);` (accessor plus named pointer); plain
   `c.getOut()->setG(q)` flipped getPos's `this` from v1 to v0.
3. **A POD return keeps the word copy, a by-value operator= makes the float-store chain.** 2CC8 has both shapes in
   one arm: `r = f()` is ret temp (sp+140) -> r (sp+192) as `lw/sw`, while `d = *vel / k` is ret temp -> param temp
   (sp+84, `lw/sw`) -> d (sp+168, `swc1` interleaved with the subtraction). With one class both go the same way. The
   answer was `P3 game_uso_func_000023D4(Src *)` (POD `struct P3 { float x, y, z; }`, `V3::operator+=(const P3 &)`)
   and `void V3::operator=(V3 v)`. `V3 v = V3(0, 0, +-1000)` keeps the ctor temp -> v word copy (`V3 v(...)` builds in
   place and loses it; `v = V3(...)` with the by-value operator= adds a param temp).
4. **Frame rules seen here (edg, `-g3` offsets from the virtual frame top).** Function-scope named locals get slots in
   declaration order from the top, then each block's temporaries, then its named locals; a nested block's locals land
   below the enclosing block's temporaries (24BC tail `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); ... }` moved o below the 023D4 return
   temp, sp+52 -> sp+60 as the target). A named `int key = a0->key;` costs a slot and leaves a 4-byte hole before the
   next V3 (24BC m at top-24 instead of top-20); comparing `a0->key` twice gives the same single load without the slot.
   The run-120 28C0 trick (dead `int zz; zz = 0;` plus a nested block per arm) gave 2CC8's frame 216 directly; in 24BC
   the dead int sits between the key-3 arm's two store groups.
5. **One cut for a caller-saved reload between two calls (24BC 7 -> 0).** The target reloads a2 after the first call
   and re-saves it before the second; ours kept it in the home across both. `scripts/blockcut-search.py --file ...
   --k 2 --also getOut --also setG` found single cuts after `r = f();`, `q += r;` or `n.set(...)`: a block boundary
   there makes uopt place the reload / store pair at the block edges.
6. **28C0 (72 -> 68 scratch, not landed).** Same family, but the target puts the out / tgt reloads in v1 (getPos's
   this in v0). Accessors turn our t-register loads into v0 (same raw count), a dead `if (key) {}` moves key to v1
   (77), nested `o` blocks / no named key shift the slots (160+). The v0 / v1 choice is ugen's and depends on what else
   is live; not found.
7. **Did not move (block-cut searches, all promote / NM-tree scored with `rdiff --raw --pins`).**
   - game_uso 7538 (18): `--k 2` over all 146 positions (10.7k variants) and the deletion swap: flat. The a1 / a2 swap
     is colouring priority: the 0x44 load candidate (one CSE expression over every arm) is coloured before `arg + 1`;
     unsigned / volatile / short reads, `n` / `m` reuse for lim or the table pointer, `++arg`: flat or 57+ (any reuse
     of n or m in the 0x80 arm renumbers the t-ring, ~220).
   - gl 5F0B8 (34): k = 3 cuts with deletion: no gain. A named zero assigned anywhere before the products is
     constant-propagated and only adds a frame word (47). The target materialises 0.0f and 1.0f at the top of the
     divide block (uopt loads constant candidates at the block entry), so the target has no boundary between the
     divides and `mf[3][0] = 0`; our cuts are what took it from 100 to 34. Open.
   - gui 2BB0 (34): k = 3 cuts with deletion, a4 reused as the loop divisor (34, the s1 = a4 copy is still coalesced).
   - timproc_b5 D550 (38): k = 2 cuts with deletion (NM tree): flat.
   - game_uso BB8C (66): explicit pointer bumps for getPos (`p += 0x70`, `M4 *mm = &s->mtx`, float pointer, P3 copy):
     70-206. The `addiu v0,v0,112` is emitted in ours too but scheduled after the loads with folded offsets.
   - game_uso 7C1C: not attempted this run (the family above paid better).
8. **Next:** 1DDC (1528 B, cfe 36 raw) is the same family: a block-scoped Ctx per arm (sp+368 / sp+300), getPos,
   `self += f()` with a P3 return (ret temp sp+252 -> binding temp sp+340), `acc = diff * e` through the by-value
   operator= (ret temp -> pooled param temp sp+196 -> float stores), `V3 t = diff * e; acc = t * k` in the else arms,
   `a0->vel = diff * speed` (vel is a V3 member at 0x2C), `a0->vel -= diff * sel` (binding temp sp+328). Draft
   `g129/1d/d3.cpp` (no named key, dead `int zz` in the key-3 arm, diff written as `diff.y = 0; diff.z = ...;
   diff.x = ...;`) has every slot down to sel (top-120) and the whole key-3 arm right; the temporaries below differ
   (ours top-156 / -200..., target ret pool at top-132, then -164 / -188 / -208 ...; frame 336 vs 384): 275 raw, not
   landed. 28C0 needs the v1 rule.
9. **Table (raw `--raw --pins` words).**

    callers 2FC8 / 2714 compiled against; both stay byte-identical). verify-blocks: game_uso block OK. Purge
    `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_uso/game_uso.c.o` and every `*_ncc_*.cpp.o`. post0b untouched (clip 0x2e834).

## kit XLI (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 130): game_uso 1DDC as an NCC donor, chained products, temp order <a name="kit-xli-agent-g-run-130"></a>

No exact this run. Everything went into game_uso 1DDC (1528 B), the last big member of the camera family (kit XL).
The NCC draft went from 275 raw words (373/382 insns, frame 336) to full length, the same instruction shape and every
integer register matching. The remaining gaps are the frame (392 vs 384, slots off by 4-8 below `sel`) and the FP
colouring. Scratch: `g130/1d/best_x2.cpp`. Tools: `g130/cmp.sh FILE FUNC [rdiff flags]` (NCC -O2 + rdiff),
`g130/ps.py OBJ FUNC [x]` (positional compare: total / sp-only / other), `g130/nsp.py` (non-sp diff count),
`g130/run2.sh FUNC "flags" files...` (parallel score). Raw `--raw --pins` word counts swing by 100+ on one frame shift
when the frame is wrong, so score shape with `--nosp --noreg`, then registers with nsp.py, then the frame with `../g128/fr.sh`.

1. **Write chained products as one expression, not through a named temporary (shape 28 -> 16, +6 insns).**
   The target's else arms are `acc = diff * (mag - speed) * a0->k1;`. That gives ctor temp -> ret slot (-132) -> a
   word copy into a `this` temp (-208) for the second `operator*`, then a NEW ret / param pair (-188 / -268), because
   the first ret slot stays busy until the end of the full-expression. `V3 t = diff * (...); acc = t * k1;` frees the
   ret slot at the `;` and reuses the pair, so the second hop is missing and the copies get interleaved.
2. **Block cut for forwarded values (shape 16 -> 4).** After `self += game_uso_func_000023D4(a0);` the target reloads
   self.x / self.z from memory. Put `if (1) {}` there, then write the statements in the order
   `speed = a0->spd; diff.y = 0; diff.z = self.z - ref.z; diff.x = self.x - ref.x;` (I swept all 24 orders with and
   without the cut; only the syzx / szxy / szyx orders with the cut reach 4). The length is then 382/382.
3. **Use the accessor through a nested named pointer at every site (fixes the v0 / v1 swap and the t-ring).**
   `game_uso_func_072EE8(c.getOut()->acc, &acc)` put the accessor result in v1 and the param-temp pointer
   (`addiu vX,sp,196`) in v0. The target has the opposite. `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); game_uso_func_072EE8(o->acc, &acc); }`
   swaps them. Then `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); ref.x = o->px; ... }` for the ref load removes the one-register t-ring
   shift (ours t1/t9/t0, target t0/t8/t9). Every integer register now matches; `c.out->px` or `c.getOut()->px` does
   not do this. Cost: each nested `o` is a frame slot (frame 376 -> 392).
4. **edg frame-order facts (NCC `-g3` locals).**
   - Inside one scope, the temporaries get addresses with the LAST-CREATED one highest. Ours has the
     `vel -= diff * sel` binding at top-44 and the `self += P3` binding at top-56; the target has them swapped. Things
     that did not swap them: a by-value `operator+=(P3)` or `operator-=(V3)` (moves the temp into the nested area), P3
     declared after V3, a V3 return or a P3 -> V3 conversion ctor, a named `P3 r` in the function, else or ref scope, and
     the no-else `return` shape. In the no-else shape the function-scope temporaries go to the very top, ABOVE the key-3
     block's locals.
   - The ctor's inline `set(a, b, c)` layer adds 8 bytes to the frame (no set: 328, with set: 336). A
     `const float &s` operator* gives frame 384 but spills real float temps (shape 44). `V3 r; r.x = ...` and
     `r.set(...)` change the code (251+).
   - Target slots (top = 384): binding P3 -44, binding vel -56, ref -68 ... sel -120, ret -132, arm-1 ctor -164,
     param -188, this-copy -208, ctor -220, ctor -236, param2 -268, vel ctor -288, -300, this-copy2 -312, -324, -336,
     vel-= ctor -348. best_x2 matches -164 / -208 / -220 / -236 / -268. Ret and param are 8 deeper (the ref-block
     `o` is allocated before them). Everything from the vel ctor down is off by 4 (the first 072EE8 block's `o`).
     Next step: find a v0-giving accessor spelling that takes no slot, or put that slot before -132 without moving ret.
5. **FP colouring still open.** In each arm the target puts x in f12, y in f2 and z in f14; ours puts x in f2 and y
   in f12. The diff computation keeps diff.x in f0 and diff.z in f16. Spellings of the operator* / ctor / set
   (return V3(...), friend, reversed set order) did not change either.
6. **Not attempted:** 28C0 / BB8C / 7538 / 7C1C / the family scan (the time went into 1DDC). 1DDC's register fix
   (#3) is the same v0 / v1 question as 28C0 (kit XL #6): try the nested `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); ... }` per use
   there first.
7. **Table (raw `--raw --pins` words).**

    | function | bytes | before | after | how |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | game_uso 1DDC (NCC scratch) | 1528 | 275 (373 insns) | 382/382 insns, shape 4, non-sp 85 | not landed (cfe NM stays at 36) |

8. **Gate / landing notes.** No source change was committed. Tree = origin/main 6f39c903e.

## kit XLII (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 131): one node type, a named pointer in the dead slot, the pooled temporary owns v0 <a name="kit-xlii-agent-g-run-131"></a>

No exact this run. game_uso 28C0 (1000 B) NM donor went 72 -> 4 raw (`--raw --pins`), committed on agent-g
(`src/game_uso/game_uso_ncc_28C0.cpp`, NM tree only). Scratch: `g131/28` (generators `gen*.py`, best `best.cpp`),
`g131/1d` (1DDC), helpers `g131/lst.sh OBJ FUNC` (numbered listing) and `g131/dump.sh FILE FUNC` (NCC `-Wo,-zdbug:6`
through the dump toolchain, prints the per-function itab + colouring; the dir name is printed last).

1. **Out and Body are the same class.** In the camera family `out->px/py/pz` sit at 0xA0..0xA8, which is exactly
   `mtx.m[3][0..2]` of the M4 at 0x70 that Body has. Declaring one `struct Node { char pad[0x30]; char acc[0x30];
   float gx, gy, gz; char pad6c[4]; M4 mtx; }` for `Self::out`, `Self::obj` and `Src::body` lets one named pointer
   hold both the output node and the target node.
2. **The dead `int zz; zz = 0;` slot (kit XL #4) was a named pointer.** In 28C0's else arm, replacing it with
   `Node *o;` and writing `o = c.getOut(); p.x = o->mtx.m[3][0]; ...` for the head load and
   `o = c.getTgt(); o->mtx.rotate(v);` for the rotate keeps the frame (232) and every slot. uopt colours `o` v1
   (the target's `lw v1,228(sp)` hoisted into the `bne` delay slot, and `lw v1,224(sp)` as the rotate base). The bnel +
   duplicated load disappears by itself once the head value is v1: as1 only fills a plain `bne` delay slot from the
   target block when the register is dead on the fall-through.
3. **Who gets v0: the pooled edg temporary vs a named pointer.** `-zdbug:6` on 28C0: the edg pooled temporary (every
   accessor return and the inline getPos `this`, frame -68 here) and the named `o` are both coloured, in priority
   order. When `o` has two sites (head + rotate) the pooled temp is coloured first and takes v0, `o` takes v1
   (target). Give `o` a third site (either 072EE8 argument) and `o` is coloured first: o = v0, pooled = v1, 29-31 raw.
   A nested `{ Node *o2 = ...; }`, a second named pointer, an inline `Node::add(V3 *)` wrapper, `c.out->acc`
   direct, declaration position (function scope at 3 spots / else scope) and block cuts (`--k 2`, 1830 variants) all
   stay at 4 or flip. RESIDUAL 4 words: both `lw v1,228(sp); addiu a0,v1,48` (072EE8 args) come out as the pooled
   temp in v0.
4. **Accessor spelling sweep (28C0, 1944 + 5000 + 2500 variants through `run2.sh`).** The per-use nested
   `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); ... }` that fixed 1DDC moved the key-1 arm's t-ring into place (72 -> 38) but in the else
   arm costs a slot (frame +8). `c.getOut()->getP(p)` (inline `Out::getP`) 26. Named pointer in the dead slot 12,
   function-scope `Out *o` for the key-1 072EE8 as well 10, Node type 4.
5. **1DDC (scratch only).** One named `Out *o;` declared after `sel` in the else scope, used at all three sites
   (`o = c.getOut(); ...`), instead of three nested blocks: frame 392 -> 384 (target), raw 187 -> 117
   (`g131/1d/v/v_8ooo.cpp`); keeping the ref load and the second 072EE8 as nested blocks with `o` declared too gives 115
   (`v_8non.cpp`). Non-sp diffs unchanged at 85: the FP colouring

## kit XLIV (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 133): lessons from PR #10 <a name="kit-xliv-agent-g-run-133"></a>

PR #10 (txemaleon, merge 9a0de6a21) landed 91 exact functions as plain IDO 7.1 cfe C, one function per file in
`src/match_imports/<fn>.c` with a context header (`src/match_imports/context_*.h`, `include/match_imports/common.h`).
Each file builds with `$(CC) -c $(CFLAGS) -O2 $(MIPSISET)`, is linked by GNU ld with
`scripts/match-origins-<fn>.ld` (.text at the function's offset, every extern = 0), gets its relocation symbols renamed
by `scripts/bind-native-relocations.py` + `scripts/match-bindings-<fn>.json`, and is spliced with
`private REPLACE_FUNC_BODY` (both trees, separate `-nm` ld / json). Several were our documented dead ends:
timproc_b5 1460 (3 raw), gui 2BB0 (34), game_uso 7538 (18), game_uso 28C0 (4, "C++ only, NCC donor"), gl 3800C (99.3 %).

1. **The separate TU is not the lever.** The flags are the host's (-O2 -mips2 -32 -G 0, same cfe), and asm-processor
   does not touch C bodies. What the private TU buys is freedom in DECLARATIONS: each callee gets its own prototype,
   and the function's own parameter gets a real struct type, without colliding with the host file's placeholders.
   Every one of the five diffs below is a source difference that would compile the same way in the host TU if the
   declarations allowed it.
2. **Per-callee prototypes (gl 3800C, 28C0).** Our 3800C stalled on "the last call never sets a0; n is in a1". The PR
   declares `extern int gl_3800C_get(void);` -- the call has NO arguments; the counter just happens to be coloured a1.
   Our shared `gl_func_00000000` K&R placeholder forced every call site to pass something. 28C0 declares
   `float game_uso_func_070238(float)` and `Vec3 *game_uso_28C0_rotate(Vec3 *, ...)`: prototyped float arguments
   are not promoted to double (no cvt.d.s / mfc1 pair) and a pointer-returning helper followed by a by-value struct
   copy (`dcopy = *rotate(scratch, src);`) gives the target's word copy. **Rule: when a residual sits at a call
   boundary (arg register, cvt, return register), suspect the callee's prototype before the regalloc.**
3. **One-element arrays and volatile unions force memory homes (1460, 28C0).** 1460's last residual was "the arg0+0x10
   spill lands at 40, target 32" -- the PR writes the white value into `float retA[1]` (retA[0] = white after the
   062880 call, read back for widget C's alpha) and `volatile int pad[4]`. An array local is never a uopt candidate,
   so it gets a fixed frame slot by declaration order and stops competing with the spilled pointer. 28C0 uses
   `GameUsoVectorOutput *out_home[1]`, `float mag[1]`, `union { Vec3 value; volatile Vec3 reload; } v2` (writes via
   `.value`, reads via `.reload` = forced reload exactly where the target re-loads) and explicit `s32 pad1[2]`,
   `pad2[2]`, `pad3[4]` between the Vec3 locals to set every slot offset. That reproduced what we had attributed to
   edg's pooled temporaries (kits XL-XLIII): **28C0 is C, not C++.** Before declaring a function "NCC only", try
   array-of-1 homes + volatile-union reloads + pad arrays in cfe.
4. **Per-arm reloads and dead statements re-rank uopt candidates (7538).** Our 18-word residual was an a1/a2 swap of
   the table pointers and lim tail. The PR (m2c-shaped: one temp per value, `temp_a1_2` ...) differs in: the mask is
   re-read INSIDE each event arm (`if (1) { active_mask = arg0->field_6C; }`, one arm uses
   `*(volatile int *)((char *)arg0 + 0x6C)`) instead of once after the chain; a dead
   `while (0) { temp_a1_5 = temp_a2 + temp_a2; }` at the top of the 0x80 arm (first appearance of the variable --
   uopt colours in first-appearance order, kit XXXIX, and a dead loop body still counts in cfe's numbering);
   `if (1) { table_pair += arg0->field_58 * 8; }` after the base; `if (1) { temp_a2 = arg0->field_44; }`; the clamp
   through an explicit `f64 temp_f0`. Literal `0.0f` instead of our shared `float zero` variable.
5. **Comma copies keep an `or` copy uncoalesced (gui 2BB0).** Our residual: "target keeps lw s6 + or s1,s6 (rem a
   copy)". The PR: `scratch = ((Info *)(metadata_copy = info, info = 0, metadata_copy))->field_08` -- copy into a
   second variable and kill the first, so the copy survives; `short raw_height; int height = raw_height;` (sign-extend
   once into an int web); `unsigned int step_x, step_y`; a block-scoped `int last_step_x`; trailing `if (src_x) {}`.
6. **Other recurring PR idioms** (grep `src/match_imports`): `do { stmt; } while (0);` around single statements
   (28C0 prologue: changes block structure without code), `if (a0) { }` empty conditionals on a live pointer,
   `f = (0, mag2) * k` comma to break a CSE, and m2c-style temps kept verbatim (`temp_a1_2`, `temp_a1_3` ...: one
   variable per value instead of reusing a named one).
7. **Workflow to reuse the mechanism** (legal: compiled C, relocation symbols only renamed). Copy one existing set:
   `src/match_imports/<fn>.c`, the four Makefile stanzas (compile x2, link x2, bind x2, REPLACE_FUNC_BODY x2 +
   prerequisite lines), `scripts/match-origins-<fn>{,-nm}.ld`, `scripts/match-bindings-<fn>{,-nm}.json`. Check
   `scripts/bind-native-relocations.py` for what the json must contain (`raw_sha256` is checked).
8. **Applied this run (scratch `g133/`; `g133/sc.sh file.c FUNC [unit]` = standalone cfe compile + `rdiff --raw --pins`).**
   - **The standalone TU really is neutral:** the in-tree 1DDC NM body pasted into a file that only includes
     `context_game_uso.h` scores the same 36 raw words as in-tree.
   - **gl 62194 22 -> 10 raw (committed, length 65 = target, clip unchanged).** The array-of-1 home `unsigned int n[1]`
     for the stride * a3 product + a block-scoped `char *p` (computed before `n[0] = ...`) gives the target's
     a2-product-first order with a 3-argument call (our old 4-argument trick cost +8 frame), and dropping the named
     self->8 local gives frame 40. LEFT: self->8 CSE temp v1 (target t0); in the target the else product is a uopt
     candidate in v1 that outranks it. Named / block / function-scope product variables and k = 2 cuts are flat.
   - **1DDC key-3 arm (36, flat).** Target `lw t6,20(a0)` = the first out pointer is a ugen-local temp (t6), and the
     non-3 arm's `lw t7` follows from ugen's register rotation (t6 already used in program order); ours makes it a
     uopt candidate (v0) under every spelling tried (separate block variable, outh[0]-only reads, store order, comma
     forms: 36 / 47 / 78 / 137-385). Untested next idea: rewrite 1DDC from the PR's 28C0 source (the same homing
     body), not from our NM.
   - **timproc_b5 32C8 (5, flat):** zero literal / l134 spellings (0.0f, chained, `vF8.z = vF8.x`, scoped zero, comma
     zero, cut before) all 5-107.

## kit XLV (agent-c 2026-10-23, run 128): blockcut-search rules, PR #10 spellings and lever A on agent-c units <a name="kit-xlv-agent-c-run-128"></a>

**Tool fix (committed on agent-c).** scripts/blockcut-search.py now (1) never offers a cut
position whose next token is `else` (after `}` or after a `;` of an unbraced then-arm), and
(2) parses rdiff's `len ours vs target`: a variant of a different length prints
`N LEN!ours/target`, ranks below every same-length variant and never prints as `improve`;
a base with the wrong length triggers a warning. `--selftest` checks both rules without
compiling. Doc: docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#blockcut-search-run127.

**Standalone TU vs in-unit.** For every probe below, a scratch TU that includes
src/match_imports/context_<unit>.h and the function alone scored exactly what the
in-unit promote build scores (4EE44 2 / 2, 6204 2 / 2). So the PR's separate TU is plumbing;
the C is what has to change (agrees with kit XLIV).

**Lever A (per-callee prototypes) is flat on integer-only callees.**
- gl 4EE44 (2 raw, `lw a1,112(s0)` vs our v0 for the loop-init `*(o+0x70)` reload):
  distinct prototyped names for all three `gl_func_00000000` calls, no change. Also flat:
  decl order of `src / r / result / c,k` (all 2), `src` built in the `for` init, `int`-typed
  base, `&((float *)p)[45]`. Worse: a named `p` for the 0x70 pointer before the call (17),
  an unused int (7: frame), a pointer-stepped row (24), `x = x + y` instead of `+=` (96).
- bootup CA0 (17 raw: box base v1 / h a0 / -h a1 in the target, ours v0 / v1 / a0):
  `void *alloc(unsigned)` + `void base(char *, char *)` or `char *` returns: 17.
  Box block spellings (named `short *b`, inline `-h`, short `h`, stepped `b += 8`) all 17;
  varref sweep flat 12..1000 (not a block-placement residual). Some candidate live across
  the box block holds v0 in the target; nothing in the decoded statement list does.
- bootup 6204 / E9FC (`lui a0` before `sw ra`): 24 combinations of callee prototype
  (K&R int, `void(void *)`, `void(char *)`, `int(void *)`, `void(int)`, varargs) x data
  declaration (`char`, `int`, `char[]`, static array): every one 2. Not a declaration effect.
- h2hproc 620 (46 raw): the 3800C spelling (sequential `if (p == 0) { p = alloc(); if (p == 0)
  goto X; }` chain with fallthrough labels instead of nested `||`) is 55 and one word long;
  dropping the `volatile` on `r` is also +1 word. The nested-`||` form stays best.
- gl 49B3C (32 raw, NCC NM donor): the cfe "condition-in-while" idea (loop rotation
  duplicates the condition so the first and later iterator results get separate temps, as
  the target's v0 / a0 and a1 / v0 show) is what the NCC `while (it.next())` already
  does; in cfe it is 73-85 and changes the length. Stays NCC.

**Lever A candidates left untested (next run):** a grep of agent-c NM bodies for placeholder
calls with float arguments finds bootup lines ~3844 (`z[1] = 0.0f` comma arg), ~7915 (float
index expression), ~8167 (`func_cce0(0, st, 2, 140.0f, ..., -350.0f)` = double promotion
candidate) and timproc_b1 1340 (~673, `(int)(f * 255.0f)` arg). The game_libs_post hit
(33BE4 `gl_d_33be4_28f`) is a data symbol, not a float. These are the functions where
per-callee prototypes can change argument setup; the five probed above are integer-only.

## kit XLVI (agent-g 2026-10-23, run 134): lever-A sweep (negative), trailing `if (p) {}` exact, store-then-read homes <a name="kit-xlvi-agent-g-run-134"></a>

Scratch: `g134/` in the session scratchpad (`sc.sh file.c FUNC unit` = standalone cfe -O2 + `rdiff --raw --pins`,
`nc.sh` = same with NCC, `var.py` = apply old/new blocks from stdin and score, `tail_if.py` / `tail_if_tree.py` =
lever-E sweeps, standalone and in-tree).

1. **EXACT game_libs_func_00003298 (game_libs.c, 5 raw -> 0, episode logged).** The last 5 words were the 0xFF
   constant in v0 (target v1). In the target the loop's `color = child + 0x64` pointer (the `addiu v0,v0,100` at the
   loop bottom) is still LIVE after the loop, so v0 is busy when the tail stores need a register for 0xFF. Fix:
   declare `color` at function scope and end the function with an empty `if (color) {}` (PR #10 idiom #6, kit XLIV:
   "trailing empty conditional on a live pointer"). Zero instructions, it only extends the live range.
   **Lever E: when a constant or late temp takes v0 where the target uses v1 (or any "one register too low"
   colour at the END of a function), look for a value the target keeps alive to the end (a dead-looking `addiu` /
   pointer bump in the last loop) and add `if (x) {}` before the closing brace.** A returned value (`return color;`)
   is NOT the same: it adds `or v0,...` and keeps the constant in v1's competitor.
   Sweep of lever E (`if (v) {}` before the final brace, every declared local/param, in-tree NM build): 525F0, 62194,
   67D50, 32C8, 1DDC, 51F5C, 8000235C, 80000598, 80009474, 5AFD4, 66EEC, arcproc 125C, 558A0, 3430, 61B30, 5534C,
   68DD4 and the list in item 6: no other win (flat or worse). 5F0B8: `if (xy) {}` restores the 113-word length
   (callee-saved f22 appears) but scores 121 raw -- the FP pressure moves without landing.
2. **Lever A sweep (per-callee prototypes) on agent-g's partial functions: NEGATIVE.** Scripted over every partial
   function in agent-g ownership (90 with an NM body; 28 call `gl_func_00000000` directly): counted, from
   `rdiff --raw --pins`, ours-minus-target `cvt.d.s`/`cvt.s.d` rows (float promotion), `mfc1`/`mtc1` rows, rows that
   write a0-a3 (phantom / missing argument set-up) and sign/zero-extension rows (`sll/sra 16|24`, `andi 0xff|0xffff`,
   return-value casts). Result: **zero promotion rows anywhere** (the float callees already have typed externs), no
   extension rows at a call boundary (gui F04 +7 is float->short packing, not a call), and every a0-a3 delta is a
   colouring/schedule difference inside an otherwise identical call sequence (spot-checked 67D50, 68DD4, 5AFD4,
   51AD8, 61B30, 558A0, 5534C; 51AD8's prototyped callee was already probed in run 105). Same conclusion as agent-c's
   kit XLV for its units: the K&R placeholder is not what holds these residuals.
3. **game_uso 1DDC 36 -> 13 raw (committed).** Rewritten towards PR #10's 28C0 shapes:
   - key-3 arm: `outh[0] = (char *)a0[0x14 / 4]; out = outh[0];` (store the one-element home FIRST, then read it)
     makes the forwarded value a ugen temp (`lw t6,20(a0); sw t6,368(sp)`, stores through t6) exactly as 28C0's
     `out_home[0] = a0->field_14; ... mode_out = out_home[0];`. Our old `out = ...; outh[0] = out;` made `out` a uopt
     candidate (v0). Alone this fixes the arm but shifts the t-ring by one for the rest (137 raw).
   - the t-ring comes back with a block-scoped copy of the non-3 home for the ref_v reads:
     `{ char *mo = out_home[0]; ref_v.x = *(float *)(mo + 0xA0); ... }` (36 -> 25). Reading `out_home[0]` directly in
     each load costs a hidden ugen temp between the home load and the dcopy word copy.
   - FP: the pass-1 else-arm excess in its own variable (`yd_unused`, f0 like the then-arm), the three later
     z-products in `y_excess_unused` instead of `mag` (keeps mag's f16 web short; the FIRST then-arm z product must
     stay `mag` or the function changes length), the final commit Y in `fx` (25 -> 13).
   - LEFT (13): the zero constant (target f14 in both passes) against fy (the 0x7C load in pass 1 = target f2, the
     commit-1 Y = target f12). Every zero spelling (`(float)0` / `0.0f` / via any variable / do-while(0) group /
     `diff.y = speed * 0.0f`) is either constant-propagated to the same candidate or changes length; a dead
     `while (0) { v = v + v; }` (lever C) at the top or before `speed` is neutral for every float variable; a 625-way
     brute force of fy's four roles over {fx, fy, fz, y_excess_unused, yd_unused} floors at 13.
