## kit LXXII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 147): one-word struct copies advance the t-ring, 526D0 ctor donor, 533EC constant divisor <a name="kit-lxxii-agent-g-run-147"></a>

Scratch: `g147/` in the session scratchpad. `g147/fd.sh UNIT FUNC` prints the positional diff of the in-tree NM build
against `expected/`; `g147/tdis.sh OBJ FUNC OUT` dumps one function as `x: insn` lines (the format `g145/cmp.sh` and
the `run.py` loops read); `g147/uv.py` is the run-146 whole-unit variant loop (scratch copies only).

1. **EXACT gl_func_000526D0 (post0b, 584 B, NCC copy-constructor donor).** Run 146 had all 146 words from an edg ctor
   with every t-register from the 0x18 copy on one step behind the target, plus frame 56 vs 72. The register lag:
   **the member at 0x18 is a one-word struct** (`Flags m18;`, same type as the 0x30 flags). The memberwise copy of a
   one-word struct allocates a temp pair and stores the second register, so it advances the ring by one where a plain
   `int` copy does not. (51AD8's NM notes found the same thing for its 0x58 word.) **Lever:** a copy block whose
   t-registers are all one behind the target from a given word on -> make that word a one-member struct. The frame:
   `struct Base : Blk6` (the derived-to-base conversion in the implicit `operator=`: +8) and the copy in an inline member
   that does its own null test, `void copy(const Obj *o) { if (o) { int save = m1C; *this = *o; m30.v |= 0x10; m1C = save; } }`
   called as `copy(src)` (+8 = 72). With the test outside the inline (`if (src) copy(*src)`), `&m30` is no longer CSEd
   into v0. Probes that did not move the frame: user `operator=` on Base / Blk6 / Sub / Flags, inline wrappers around
   the register / finish calls or the `Sub()` body, reference parameters, `this->operator=`.
   Landing: `src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_526D0.cpp`, REPLACE_FUNC_BODY into both post0b objects. The donor recipe renames
   symbols with objcopy (names only, as for 4E584): `__ct__3ObjFPvT1P3Obj` -> `gl_func_000526D0`, the base ctor and
   `__vtbl__3Obj` -> zero aliases. The callees are extern "C" `gl_func_00000000_526d0_*`; all five zero aliases are in
   undefined_syms_auto.txt. The C side is an empty placeholder.
2. **EXACT gl_func_000533EC (post0b, 372 B, cfe).** The run-105 body divided by the loop counter (`r / i`) to get a
   register divisor. The target **divides by the literal 3**: uopt keeps the constant 3 in a register (t1) for the loop
   bound and all three divisors, so ugen emits `div` with trap checks as if the divisor were a variable. Then:
   - a cursor copy `p = tri;` indexed as `p[i + 1]` gives the target's `t0 -> a0` copy before the loop;
   - writing the tri address index-first, `idxTab[arg1] * 8 + base`, fixes the t-ring phase of the whole body (19 -> 1);
   - the last word was the commutative `addu` order of the colour entry. `colorTab + k`, `k + colorTab`, `&colorTab[k]`,
     casts, shifts, decl orders and a Col struct all give the same order. **Re-reading the table from the object,
     index first**, `p[i + 1] * 4 + *(u8 **)(arg0 + 0x50)`, puts the table first (the load is CSEd with colorTab, which
     uopt holds in t2). **Lever:** for a one-word commutative operand-order residual where source order is inert, spell
     the invariant operand as the memory re-read it was loaded from.
   The NM build grew by one word (92 -> 93), so the post0b NM clip moves 0x2e88c -> 0x2e890 (62F08 NM offset 0x2e840).
3. **timproc_b5 32C8 is an edg composite constructor (NCC draft, not landed).** `g147/t32/d.cpp`, `f.cpp`, `i.cpp`: a
   `Panel` ctor with member objects `Hdr h` (no virtuals: a table pointer and 0), six `TextRow`, two `VecRow`, two
   `ValRow`, all derived from `RowBase { int a, b, c; RowBase(void *, Name, int); virtual void f(); }`. RowBase's
   out-of-line ctor is func_04A188. The vptr sits at 0xC because edg puts it after the members of the class that
   declares the virtual. This reproduces the 0x288-word text-row prefix except for stack offsets. Two facts about
   edg/IDO slot order: **edg temporaries for mem-initializer arguments take ASCENDING slots** (first temporary lowest),
   while **locals of an inline function expansion and named locals take DESCENDING slots** (first highest). The
   target's per-row name stash (292, 288, ...) is descending, and a shared inline parameter slot (164) holds the value
   that is loaded into a2. An inline maker `Name mk(char *s) { Name n; n.v = s; return n; }` or `operator Name()` gives
   the descending per-row slot but also adds a shared return-value slot (three stores per row instead of two). The
   target's VecRow temporaries are descending too (V3 zero 260, b 248, c 236, then the name 232), while this NCC
   allocates every temporary in ascending order: mem-initializer temporaries, several temporaries inside one
   mem-initializer, and call-argument temporaries in a plain function (`g147/t32/tt5.cpp`, `tt6.cpp`). Making the
   Panel ctor inline under an out-of-line derived ctor did not change this either. So the target's slots are not
   these edg temporaries, and the cfe body (99.93, f0/f2 colouring only) stays the route for 32C8.
4. **Negative / open:**
   - gl 51448: the target's inline `setParent` spills `this` and `p` separately while o stays in s0. Base-class
     setParent (implicit or explicit casts), a reload of o from the stored fields, reference parameters, a static inline
     with `Obj *&`, `else o = 0`, and `init()` returning `this` are all copy-propagated or add code. `o = new Obj;` with a GLOBAL inline `operator new` (cfront protocol: no re-check) and an inline `Obj()` over an out-of-line `Base(name, 0, 0, 0)` gives the whole head (52 words, the same 23-word setParent residual). With a class-member `operator new`, edg re-checks `this == 0` and allocates again. timproc_b5 DF14 constructs the same 0x16C class the same way, and its own `new Panel` result is likewise spilled apart from s0 (r at sp+92). It is the next place to look for the separate-web spelling.
   - gl 68DD4 (cfe 98.71): separate v / pp / q per stream read makes it worse (pp v0 / q t1 / v v1 in the target's first

   - gl 15FC as a real C++ ctor (`Obj : Base`, vptr at 0x28 like 526D0, `M2C` member, body stores): same 103 words with
     the same `li 100` v0/v1 tie; inline setter / reference / chained / float spellings are inert.
   - gl 525F0: the reload register after the call (target v0) does not change with chained / stored-then-reloaded /
     copy-variable spellings.
   - arcproc 125C: ten spellings of the `seq[2] == seq[1] + 1` compare leave the extra t-ring slot. Under NCC standalone,
     the dead `ones[4]` stores disappear (frame 96), so cfe stays.
   - timproc_b5 CEB4: the first block's true arm must survive as an empty basic block (the target keeps `b join` with

5. **Library sweep:** run 146 already checked the kernel and the game_libs tail. game_libs.c (0x0-0x1D000), post0b
   >= 0x50000, post1b and the proc USOs remaining NM functions are game C / C++ (object constructors, animation, display

6. **Gate:** rebased onto d276acf28. ROM byte-identical after purging game_libs_post / game_libs_post0b / game_uso and

## kit LXXVI (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 149): the jumptable rule read out of cfe -- a 4-entry table is not reachable from C <a name="kit-lxxvi-agent-g-run-149"></a>

The "4-entry jump table" cap (76F0 switch2/switch4, game_uso 0B3C, titproc 116C, game_uso 8CD8, kernel func_80001ADC,
~8-10 KB) was re-opened from the compiler itself rather than by probing. Result: **negative, now proven from the
binary.** No stock compiler we have (IDO 7.1 cfe, IDO 5.3 cfe, IDO 7.1 NCC/edgcpfe) can emit a jump table with fewer
than 5 entries, so the target `sltiu at,x,4` tables came from a different compiler build. Keep the phantom
`case 4: break;` (1 word + the table base words) as the best NM shape and do not grind these again.

1. **Who decides: the front end, not uopt or ugen.** `cc -O2 -j t.c` keeps the ucode. A 4-case switch's ucode is
   `lod / ldc / equ / fjp` runs (opcode bytes 0x52 0x49 0x23 0x26), a 5-case one is one `xjp` (opcode 0x8c, the
   140th entry of uopt's `uopcode_enum_values`) followed by `clab` and the `ujp` table. uopt only passes `xjp`
   through (`uoptinput.c` reads `lbound`/`hbound`, `uoptemit.c` ~5000 writes them back unchanged; the only
   rewrite is a constant selector), and ugen lowers it 1:1 to `sltiu (hbound-lbound+1)` + table. So the rule lives
   in cfe (`/usr/lib/cfe`, MIPS binary; the recompiled C is `tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/cfe.c`).
2. **The rule (cfe.c `func_465d90`, the Switch_stmt code generator, recompiled-C lines ~161880-162857):** case
   labels are kept in a list sorted by value (source order does not matter -- checked). One pass groups them into
   clusters: the next label joins the current cluster if `value <= previous + 25` (the literal `0x19`, a signed or
   unsigned 64-bit compare by selector type), and the cluster's label count goes up by one. When a cluster closes
   (and for the last cluster), `if (count < 5)` (`at = a1 < 0x5`) splits it back into single labels, each of which
   becomes an `equ`/`fjp` test; a cluster of 5 or more whose last value has a zero high word and a low word below
   0xFFFFFFFF stays a table. `func_465654` then does a binary search over the clusters and calls `func_46508c`
   (the only `xjp` writer, `t3 = 0x8c`) for each table cluster with `lbound` = the first label and `hbound` = the
   last label. `default:` is not in the list. Both constants are hard-coded; no `-W` option reaches them.
3. **Consequences, all confirmed by compiling:** a table needs at least 5 distinct labels inside one cluster, and
   its range is first..last label, so a table always has at least 5 entries. Duplicate labels are rejected
   (`case 3: case 3U:`, `case (char)259:`, `case 0x100000003LL:` all give "Duplicate case label"). An outlier label
   extends the table if it is within 25 of the previous one (`case 0..3, 28` gives `sltiu 29`; `-26` splits);
   `case -1` with an int, char or long long selector gives a 5-entry table with a bias; with an unsigned selector it
   splits. IDO 5.3 behaves the same at -O0/-O1/-O2.
4. **NCC never emits `xjp`**: edgcpfe writes ucode itself (`NCC -v`: edgcpfe -> uopt -> ugen, no cfe), and 4-, 16-
   and 40-case dense switches at -O0 and -O2 all come out as compare chains. So a C++ unit with a jump table was
   not built by our edgcpfe either (consistent with the earlier "a jumptable function is cfe C" note).
5. **What this means for the cap list:** the target tables are 4 entries (`sltiu 4`), i.e. 4 labels in one table.
   That needs a front end whose threshold is 4 (the old pcc rule was `n >= 4`), not any C spelling. The phantom
   5th label stays the best shape; the residual is the `sltiu` word plus the table base words.

**titproc 5DC (NM 94.38 -> 98.87, 356/356 words, frame 104):** three levers from one function, then a colour cap.
(a) An address used as a call argument at five sites, which the target holds in s8 from the prologue (`lui s8;
addiu s8,s8,16`), is the address CONSTANT `(char *)&sym + 0x10`, not `d + 0x10` from the int base variable: the
constant becomes its own loop-invariant candidate; `d + 0x10` is rematerialised per case (`addiu s4,s1,16`, +3 words).
(b) A flag store `done = 1` written before the first call of a case is turned into a copy of uopt's hoisted
constant-1 register (`or s6,s7`); written after the call it fills the jal delay as `addiu s6,zero,1` like the target.
(c) cfe gives every declared, referenced local a frame home, so the frame and the uopt spill slot follow the NUMBER of
locals: merging the per-case block locals into one function-scope `t` (its rr / r1 / flag / result / av webs) took
the frame 160 -> 104 and put the mask spill at the target's sp+68. (d) `mask + x` with a load chain x always emits
`addu a1,x,mask`; the 2-D index `(int)&((char (*)[2])mask)[0][x]` gives the target's base-first order.
Left: d (an `ucvt` constant candidate) colours s1 and t s0 (target the other way). coloring-solve shows t's M-variable
LR and every per-web split outrank d; decl order, `if (1) {}` after every statement, `register`, `unsigned`,
dead `while (0)` uses of d (nested, x10), `if (d) {}` (folded), web swaps between r and t, a1 reuse, removing the av / 01EFC8 webs from t: no flip; permuter 14 min (41.9k iterations) never beat the base score.

**titproc 116C decode gap (not kept):** case 2 of the NM body is missing a call -- the target runs
`titproc_uso_func_012150(&import_00020098)` between the `(5)` call and the `s0->0x60` call, and the 0x154 flag clear
is an advance-then-store (`lhu 4(v0); addiu v0,v0,4; ... sh 0(v0)` = `reg = *(char **)(D + 0x154) + 4;
*(u16 *)reg &= 0xFFF7;`). Adding both brings the build from 284 to 288 of 290 words, but the report fuzzy falls
94.13 -> 93.24 (the shared `_116c_v` call alias), so the tree keeps the old body; it stays a 4-entry-table cap anyway.
Left after that: case 3's `lw t9,0(v0); addiu t1,zero,720` placement, a `beqz` vs `beqzl` join, and the two
per-site `lui at` stores to D+0xA8 / D+0x84 (the build CSEs one `&D` base).

**Also probed this run (no gain, see below for where the residuals stand):** 97EC (edg temporaries of
`XZ e((a - b) * s->k)` homed 204/192 vs target 192/204: non-member / friend / reversed `operator*`, non-member
`XZ::operator-`, copy-init, reference-bound and explicit `.operator*` spellings all keep the order); 68DD4 (all 7
per-read splits of pp / q / v and 36 read1 x read2 spellings, including `*(*pp)++`, `(*pp)++`, `q++` with
`q[-1]`, are worse than the shared-variable 19-word body); timproc b5 32C8 (all orders of the uE8 / vF8 / vEC /
`if (1) {}` / zero block, `0.0f`, chained or copied zeros, `vF8.z = vF8.x`: l134 still takes $f0); 64388 (a dead
third parameter or a const-reference parameter on `operator-`, `operator/=` or `operator*` does not move the

## kit LXXVII (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 144): control-flow spelling flips s-register pairs; unsigned compare splits a shared constant; volatile flag picks the copy as base (five exacts, 3.4 KB) <a name="kit-lxxvii-agent-c-run-144"></a>

Scratch: `c144/` in the session scratchpad (`exg.sh SRC FUNC OUT "prefix"` = NM body of any unit as a standalone .c;
`fz.sh` / `fu.sh` objdiff per function; `rp.sh FUNC...` = `make non_matching_objects` + `objdiff-cli report generate`
into a scratch json + print the report fuzzy -- the report is the gate number, `objdiff-cli diff` on an in-tree .o
scores reloc-baked exacts at ~99.7 and is NOT the gate; `ep.sh` = log-exact-episode wrapper).

1. **`continue` vs if-block is a register-colouring lever.** Two OoT-shaped loops whose only residual was a swapped
   s-register pair (loop index vs its strength-reduced `*20` / `*4` cursor, or a pointer param copy vs the cursor)
   matched by re-spelling the control flow, not the declarations:
   - gl_func_000221D8 (DiscardSampleCacheEntry, 99.24 -> 100): OoT's single `if ((id1 match) || (id2 match) || id == 0)
     { ... }` written as `if (!(...)) { continue; } { ... }` moves fontId / fontId*20 from s4 / s5 to the target s5 / s4.
     (The only other 0-diff form in a 80-variant `if (x) {}` sweep was an empty test on the *uninitialised* fontId --
     illegal; the continue spelling is the legal equivalent of extending fontId's live range.)
   - gl_func_00023BDC (RelocateFont, 98.88 -> 100): the reverse -- OoT's two `continue`s in the drum loop written as
     nested if-blocks move fontDataStartAddr / index from s3 / s2 to s2 / s3. 273 if-split variants (run 143) and every
     declaration / initialiser order had not moved it.
   Recipe: enumerate {continue, nested-if} for every early-out in every loop (2^k variants, standalone in parallel).
2. **Comparing one of two equal constants unsigned splits the CSE** (gl_func_00022464, DiscardSampleCaches, 90.76 ->
   100): `((u32)sampleBankId1 != 0xFF) || (sampleBankId2 != 0xFF)` gives the target's two fresh `li at,255`; with both
   signed (or both unsigned) uopt hoists one 255 into t0 at the loop head and every later t-register shifts by one.
   That shift is also why objdiff scored the 130 = 130-word form **0.0**: its diff aligned the shifted body as 89
   insert/delete pairs (rdiff showed 49 words). An objdiff 0.0 on a same-length body = alignment collapse, not a
   symbol / section problem. Same entry: a non-matching cache entry **breaks** out of the entry loop (target `bnezl`
   to the font-loop tail), not just skips it.
3. **A volatile 1-bit flag makes the load go through the per-iteration copy** (gl_func_0001DCB4, synthesis update,
   98.61 -> 100): `volatile u32 enabled : 1;` (OoT / SM64-EU declare the note-sub flags `vu8`) turns
   `lw t7,0(v1); or v0,v1` into the target's `or v0,v1; lw t7,0(v0)`. No effect on 201B8's / 221D8's flags (checked).
4. **Delay-slot order through a pointer bump** (gl_func_00032E18, 98.36 -> 100): target schedules `x store, a0 =
   o+0x30, y, z (jal delay)`; every store permutation and a comma argument either kept `a0` in the delay or moved the
   homes (+8 frame). `zv.x = 0; o += 0x30; zv.y = 0; zv.z = 0; f(o, &zv);` matches (o is dead afterwards).
   The promotion needed a `gl_32e18_blank = 0` alias: `gl_func_0001CA10` is no longer defined (renamed
   game_libs_func_0001C9E4), and the unpinned symbol made the linker segfault silently -- always full-link.
5. **Function-scoped if-split sweep over full-TU scratch copies** (`c144/fsweep.py SRC FUNC PREFIX v1,v2` writes
   whole-file variants with `if (v) {}` before each statement of FUNC only -- c142's ifsweep.py runs to the end of the
   file when given a full TU; `c144/fct.sh` = asm-processor preprocess + cc + rdiff, ~0.3-1 s per game_libs_post
   variant, `c144/frs.sh` = 6-way parallel). Full-TU compiles reproduce in-tree lengths that extracted bodies miss
   (2D374: 170 both ways; 4D468 / 488A0 still diverge from in-tree under fct -- check the base first). Found
   gl_func_000250C8 97.68 -> 98.08 (`if (asyncLoad) {}` after the RelocateFontAndPreloadSamples call) and
   game_libs_func_0004B2F4 98.15 -> 98.23 (`if (ctx) {}` before the second packet). Watch for statement lines that
   are an unbraced loop body: an insertion there changes semantics (those variants come out far shorter). 2D374's only
   winners (53 -> 32 words) were tests on the *uninitialised* st / v at the first timer block -- illegal; the
   initialised spellings (`v = D_2D37C_mode; if (v == 1)`) are worse.
6. **NM gain**: gl_func_000201B8 97.73 -> 97.86 -- the `int a = st0` copy reversed the `bne` operands of the `== 3`
   tests; comparing the u8 st0 directly gives `bne v0(3),t5`; `a` stays declared unused (its home keeps the frame).
   Left: `v = 1` copies the held 1 (t1, from the mode switch) where the target re-materialises `addiu v0,1`; a store
   of 1 then re-read of `sub->cur` at the tail (OoT's `side = nextSide` shape), 1U / unsigned v / unsigned cur,
   volatile flags: none move it.
7. **Negatives.** 250C8 (OoT FinishAsyncLoad inlined: a block-level `retMsg` copy gives the target's `or v0,a1` and
   the fontId temp at sp+36 but is 152 vs 150 words; ID-before-status hoisting and the send reusing the first load
   in a1 are not reproduced), 4EE44 (src expression spellings, if inversions), 445AC (`v =` removal fixes t7 but the
   store base takes t8 not v0), 49DBC (target leaves 12 bytes unused *between* sp50 and sp38 with the same frame;
   unused scalars / larger array / pads grow the frame), 4B2F4 (162-variant slot-increment grid, best 98.06 with more
   diff words), 4D468 (ternary / shared merge var), 488A0, 2D374, 307A8. post0b standalone compiles diverge from
   in-tree (TU-context prototypes): use in-tree `make build/non_matching/...post0b.c.o` (22 s) for post0b work.

## kit LXXVIII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 150): as1 schedules inside source-line groups; real C++ constructors <a name="kit-lxxviii-agent-g-run-150"></a>

**1. as1 reorders only within one `.loc` group.** `cc -S` (or `NCC -S`) stops before as1 and prints the ugen
text, with a `.loc 2 <line>` before each source line's code. Feeding that `.s` back through
`cc -c -O2 x.s` reproduces the object for plain functions, so edits to the `.s` show what as1 does with a
given input. Deleting every `.loc` let as1 regroup all the stores of bootup func_00000CA0's vertex table
(all `-h` stores first); with the `.loc` lines it moved stores only inside one line. The C rule that follows:
*statements on one source line form one scheduling group, statements on separate lines keep their order.*
In 0CA0 the last corner was `box[3].set(h, nh, h);` (one line): as1 issued `sh a1,0x32` before
`sh a0,0x30`. Writing it as three statements on three lines (`box[3].x = h;` / `box[3].y = nh;` /
`box[3].z = h;`) gave the target order. Line breaks are ordinary formatting, not a `#line` trick. Try this
lever whenever the only residual is two independent instructions swapped inside one statement or between
two statements on the same line. It does NOT move a prologue `sw ra` (6204/E9FC: the `lui a0` / `sw ra` order
did not change with or without `.loc` lines), and the `.s` round trip does not reproduce functions with
jumptables or `div` macros exactly (51AD8, mgrproc 1824 came back longer), so check the base round trip first.

**2. A get-or-create head is a real C++ constructor.** `if (o == 0) { o = alloc(N); if (o == 0) goto end; }
base(o, &D); o->vt = &desc; ...; return o;` is edg's constructor protocol. Writing the class makes NCC emit
it: `D::D(int a1, int a2, int a3) : B(&D_000066A8) { ... }` with `B(char *)` declared out of line (an inline
base ctor adds its own `this == 0` test, the cascade shape seen in h2h 0620 / 90CC), the virtual declared in
B so the vptr lands at +0x28 after B's 0x28 bytes, and `inline void *operator new(unsigned n) { return
func_00000000(n); }`. This scheduled the vptr store and the member stores like the target, where the cfe body
(97.2) coloured `h` / `-h` v0/a0 instead of a0/a1. Rename the mangled names with objcopy (as for 526D0):
`__ct__1DFiN21` -> the function, `__ct__1BFPc` and `__vtbl__1D` -> blank aliases in undefined_syms. The
objdiff report shows 99.66 until the expected baseline is refreshed (reloc names); the ROM is byte-identical.
h2h 0620 rewritten as an L1 : L2 : L3 : L4 inline-ctor chain came out structurally right (177 vs 178 words)
but uopt memory-homes the wrong level (L2's `this`, target L3's) -- not finished (draft in the run-150 scratchpad, g150/h2.cpp).

**2b. bootup func_000031C0 is `new D` + a mode switch, and the C++ draft is 202/202 words.** The head is
edg's protocol for `new D` where `D : B` (0xB8 / 0xB4), `B : Base0` with `Base0(void *)` out of line and the
virtual declared in Base0 (vptr +0x28), member `M4 m` at +0x2C where `M4 : M0` and `M0() { a = 0; }` (the
target's TWO `this == 0` tests on +0x2C are the member check plus M0's own), then `fn_fin(this)` and
`pos = V3(0, 500, 0)` through an out-of-line set taking the stack temp. Case 1 is `new E(obj, a3v)` with
the base ctor out of line and `f158 = 0; f154 = a; f150 = f14c;` in the inline body; the other `fn(0, ...)`
calls are cfront out-of-line ctors and stay plain calls. Declaring `w, h, v, r2, r3, obj` in that order
(no `e`: `h = (char *)new E(obj, a3v);`, the target copies E's new-temp straight into h) gives the target's
slot order (w 140 ... obj 120, new-temps below), and `obj = new D; if (1) {}` fixes the obj/a3v v0/v1 swap in
the tail. With every sp offset masked, one v0/v1 swap is left (the reload of E's `this` after the base call).
Still open: the frame is 112, target 144. NCC drops unreferenced locals even when volatile, but a referenced
`int pd[8]; ... (void)pd;` takes slots (it costs no code) and gives frame 144 with w..obj at the target
offsets (34 positional diffs left); a named pad always lands with the named locals, above every edg temp,
wherever it is declared, so the target's holes BETWEEN temps (0x70, 0x54..0x64) are not reproduced. Uopt's
copy propagation also differs: the target reads the new-temp for the first use in each case (A1 / E's base
call) and obj for the rest, ours reads the temp for all of case 0 and obj for case 1, so E's new-temp shares
D's slot (target: separate, 104). The two literal-pool loads also need a donor `.rodata` pin like 2DA4. Draft:
run-150 scratchpad g150/bootup_31C0_ncc_draft.cpp. The cfe body is 93.57.

**3. A function-typed alias keeps loads after stores.** bootup func_000076F4 scales a vector at import+0xA0
by a triple at import+0x128. With two data arrays as1 knows the bases cannot alias and hoists the three scale
loads above the vector stores; reading the vector through `extern void bu_76f4_vf();` (`(char *)bu_76f4_vf +
0x30`) leaves each scale load after the previous store, as in the target (87.33 -> 99.07). Left: the
`lui v0` / `lui a2` order after the call. Round-trip tests showed the target order needs the G rematerialisation
`la $6` emitted after `la $2, vf` inside the line-12 group, not in the call's delay; no C spelling found yet.

**Negatives (this run).** 6204 / E9FC: NCC (unfilled `jr` delay reproduced), static-init `__sti__`, member
and unused-param forms -- `sw ra` always first. 24B8: one reused var for the 0x400 flag puts it in a t-reg,
not the target's s0 (90.75 / 93.1, reverted). 1A44: reading the DL word before NEXT moves nothing (reverted).
E2D0: dot-sum spellings (z-first, parenthesised, `+=`) never give the target `(x + y) + z` under cfe.
timproc_b5 4118 case 0 (target loads `this` once into v0 for four uses, ours reloads each use): a copy local
is propagated away, the alias call's return value is one word short.

## kit LXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 151): the line-layout sweep, and what source lines do NOT reorder <a name="kit-lxxix-agent-g-run-151"></a>

**1. The line sweep (kit LXXVIII #1 made systematic).** `g151/lsweep.py UNIT FUNC [rounds]` (session scratchpad)
copies the whole unit to scratch, generates every "join two adjacent simple statements onto one line" and "split a
multi-statement line" variant inside FUNC, compiles each through asm-processor + cfe -O2 (16 threads), scores with
objdiff fuzzy against `expected/`, and greedily keeps the best raising change per round (`JOINALL=1` also joins
control lines, case labels and braces; `SRC=` scores another copy). Run over every NM function >= 95 % in
bootup / h2hproc / timproc_b1 / timproc_b5 / mgrproc / post0b >= 0x50000 / post1b / game_libs.c (16 functions) and
about 35 more in the 75-95 band. **Only bootup 90CC gained at >= 95 %** (three store pairs joined). Confirmed in
report.json after the full NM build: 90CC 96.85 -> 97.15, bootup 55A0 93.93 -> 94.33, 6808 92.80 -> 92.81, 0E68 +0.01, gl 76F0 +0.005,
gui F04 91.24 -> 91.31, game_uso 591C +0.003, and gl 578B4 97.10 -> 97.20 from joining all 68 gbi
`FW(p, 0x0) = w0; FW(p, 0x4) = w1;` pairs (a gbi macro expands both command words on one source line, so that is
the natural layout for display-list code; no single pair split back helps). Most variants compile to identical
bytes: when the residual is a register colour or a uopt placement, line layout changes nothing.
**Score with the project build.** The bare scratch compile (asm-processor + cfe, no Makefile post-processing)
disagrees with the real `build/non_matching` object + objdiff project config for gui, timproc_b5 and game_uso
(scratch base 85.8 vs report 91.8 for gui 4568): its "gains" there (gui 4568 +1.95, 2DE0, 3714, b5 B368 / B624,
game_uso 7C1C +0.37) were zero or negative in report.json and were reverted. For bootup / h2hproc / game_libs.c /
post0b the two agreed. Re-measure every sweep result with `make build/non_matching/src/<unit>.c.o` and
`objdiff-cli diff -u src/<unit> <fn>` before committing.

**2. Where the line rule stops.**
- **Delay-slot filling crosses lines.** gl 51AD8 (the default arm's `lui a0,2` stolen into the bound-check
  `beqz` delay): the whole body written on ONE line still steals it.
- **Two instructions that both write `at` never swap**, whatever the lines: `li.s 1.0` (`lui at,0x3f80; mtc1`) and
  a global load (`lui at,%hi; lwc1 %lo(at)`) keep ugen order (WAW on `at`). timproc_b5 CEB4's blocks 2/3 (target
  loads D[0x398] before materialising 1.0) did not move with any join; the order is set by where uopt puts the
  constant, not by as1.
- **uopt puts rematerialised values right after the call** (inside the call's line group). In -S text, CEB4's
  `li.s $f2, 1.0` and bootup 76F4's rematerialised `la $6, G` both follow the `jal` in the call's group. Joining
  76F4's call line with the first scale line puts G and vf in one group, but as1 then issues G first
  (`lui a2; lui v0; addiu v0; addiu a2`, target `lui v0; lui a2; addiu a2; addiu v0`): 3 -> 6 words, reverted.
- **Loop-invariant constants go at the END of the preheader**, after the code of the statements before the loop
  (after the for-init moves). gl 3430's target issues 1.0 / 10.625 inside the save sequence and the step load
  after the 0xEC store. Putting the header, declarations, step load, EC store and `for` on one line puts them all
  in one group (16 -> 13 positional words) but the step load is still issued first, and fuzzy drops
  (97.41 -> 97.17): not kept. Reading the step global inside the loop instead makes uopt hoist its ADDRESS into s5.
- **`beq reg, imm` in the direct compile path is not what `cc -S` shows.** mgrproc 1824's outer two-case switch
  (target: `addiu t7; beqz v0; sw t7; addiu at,1; beq`, ours issues `addiu at,1` above the beqz): the -S + as1
  round trip gives the target order, the direct compile never does. Micro tests (switch {0,1}, default arm,
  if-cascades with returns, `if (x != 0) { if (x == 1) ... }`, IDO 5.3, -g3) all put `li at,1` above the first
  branch. So the -S lab (kit LXXVIII #1) is not evidence for `li at` placement around branches.

**3. h2hproc 0620 (cfe), two steps (report.json numbers below)**: the target loads `a3arg` before the 0x528 clear; writing
`p->0x6A8 = a3arg;` BEFORE `p->0x528 = 0;` (separate lines) gives that order and keeps its sw in the jal delay
(15 -> 13 words). Then (JOINALL sweep) **the level-4 get-or-create test and its body on ONE line** -- `if ((child != 0) || ((child = gl(0x2C)) != 0)) { gl(child, &D + 0x3C0); child->vt = &d0;` -- 95.72 -> 96.51 (objdiff -u 94.93 -> 95.72): edg expands an inline constructor into one source line, so the whole cascade level is one as1 group. Try this on every edg-shaped head written out over several lines (90CC, 31C0, 4118). Left: level-4 `child` is memory-homed in ours (target: a register, spilled only around the call),
one-slot shift of the p+16 temp (target 36, ours 32; removing / moving the `v0` local does not help), and the
0xF0 block's `or a0,v0` / `sw v0,48(sp)` order (`r = a3; gl(a3);` joined, `gl(r = a3)`, `gl(r)`: unchanged).

**4. NCC lift of my units (c134/ncc tools, P -> agent-g).** 53 NM functions in timproc_b5 / game_uso / gui /
titproc / mgrproc / arcproc / post1b / game_libs.c / post0b >= 0x50000; 28 compiled directly, 15 more after
fixer. **None beats its cfe body** (NCC fuzzy from a scratch objdiff, cfe from report.json -- treat
close pairs as ties): 4118 97.12 (cfe 99.14), 525F0 99.18 (= cfe, same v0/v1 word), CEB4 93.8
(97.1), BDEC 91.9 (95.6), 5F5F0 93.0 (98.8), game_uso B3C 91.1 (94.9), 7C1C 89.3 (92.2), titproc 116C 86.4
(94.1), gui 3714 85.3 (93.5), mgrproc 2B7C 93.9 (94.1), 59E80 93.9 (94.0).

**5. Negatives.** gl 525F0 as C++ (inline `attach(parent, n)`, member `X::attach`, inline get-or-create getter,
copy local in the getter): the finaliser reload stays v1 (target v0). bootup E2D0: 48 dot-sum spellings
(operand order inside each product, `(x+y)+z`, `x+(y+z)`, two statements, `- -z`, negated forms): add.s
operand order never flips. bootup 76F4: block / pointer / second-symbol spellings of the scale loop keep the
lui order; a function-typed second alias for the scale base gives the target's `lui v0; lui v1` order but moves
the base out of a2 (37 words). mgrproc 1824: `++` / `+=` / volatile / unsigned / cast switch values and
if-cascade rewrites all keep the hoisted `li at,1`.

## kit LXXX (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 152): m2c phi splits, by-value struct args, per-site symbols, subtract compares <a name="kit-lxxx-agent-g-run-152"></a>

**1. m2c splits one C variable into one name per definition, and both compilers pay for it.** m2c names a
variable after its register and definition (`var_f0`, `var_f0_2` ... `var_f0_5`, `temp_t0_27`). Under cfe every
named float gets a home slot even when it lives in a register (bootup B75C frame 224, target 120), and separate
variables get separate colours. Merging a family back into ONE variable is plain source (the defs never overlap;
check that no merged name is still live at the next def). `g152/famsweep.py SRC UNIT FUNC` (session
scratchpad) generates every whole-family merge (`FAMONLY=1`) plus every in-family pair merge, scores each with
the project build and ranks them. Results (keep a merge only if the body length does not move away from the target; post1b 65494's
`var_v0` -> `temp_v0` merge read 79.50 -> 81.97 at 335 vs 334 words and was dropped): B75C `var_f0*` + `var_f12*` 88.98 -> 89.48 (frame 224 -> 208);
gl 578B4 the six `var_t0*` dxt phis (one per gDPLoadTextureBlock expansion) 97.20 -> 97.72 (2411 -> 2421 of
2419 words). Merging the `temp_f2*` / `temp_f12*` families in B75C LOST fuzzy, and 90CC / 4118 gained
nothing, so sweep instead of merging blindly. cfe declaration order did not move a single home in B75C
(78 decl-move variants, all identical).

**2. Decode errors that m2c-lifted NCC donors carry (bootup C234 79.55 -> 85.17).**
- **`sw aN, 4*N(sp)` in a jal delay slot in the target only = a struct passed BY VALUE.** IDO copies a by-value
  struct argument into its outgoing arg slot as well as the register. C234's lookup call takes a 4-byte
  struct `{ s32 v; }` as arg 2: `sp8C.v = *(s32 *)(tbl + 0x38); f(D, sp8C, p, 0);` gives both target stores
  (`sw a1,140(sp)` = the local, `sw a1,4(sp)` = the arg slot). Copying the whole struct
  (`sp8C = *(S4 *)(tbl + 0x38)`) gives an addiu-pointer copy instead. `argscan.py` lists NM functions where the
  target and build disagree on arg-slot stores, frame size or `addiu rX,rX,0` counts.
- **A shared function-symbol base is CSE'd and spilled.** Five calls on `(char *)func_00008A7C + K` became one
  `lui/addiu` spilled to sp+52 and reloaded; the target issues `lui; addiu` at every call. Per-site symbols
  (`bu_c234_k0..k4`, blank / NM-only) give the target shape.
- **`lui; addiu r,r,0; lw K(r)` where the target has `lui; lw K(r)`:** the base was a FUNCTION symbol
  (`(char *)&func_00000008 + 0x2C`). Reading through a data symbol (`*(s32 *)(sym + 0x2C)`, `extern char sym[]`)
  folds the %lo.
- **Old-value counter tests:** `if ((p->n)++ >= 0x97)` gives the target `slti v1,151` on the OLD value; the
  m2c form (`t = p->n; p->n = t + 1; if (t >= 0x97)`) lets uopt compare the incremented value (`slti v1,152`).

**3. `x - 1 == 0` keeps a constant out of an s-register (timproc_b5 C310 91.46 -> 93.75).** With
`if (*(s32 *)(arg1 + 0x3BC) == 1)` inside the 5-trip loop, uopt hoisted the 1 into s8 for the whole loop (one
extra callee save, frame +8, every s-register renamed). `if (*(s32 *)(arg1 + 0x3BC) - 1 == 0)` compiles to the
same `bne` against a fresh `li at,1` and frees s8; the target materialises the 1 inside the loop (`li t0,1`
at the loop top, so this is not the full answer: left is t0 vs at). Moving `i = 0;` to just before the
loop's pointer setup gives the target's late `move s1,zero` (92.48 -> 93.75). The same trick on the 8FC8
`&= ~4` hoist (`li s1,-5`) has no spelling: `~4u`, `x = x & ~4`, a dead test all keep the hoist.

**4. Smaller results.** bootup 63B4 (NCC donor): `pad[1]` instead of `pad[3]` in the frame struct gives the
target frame 144 and A / B at the target offsets (q lands 8 high) 83.10 -> 83.21; pointer-form or member-function
transforms (so B reloads after A's stores, as the target does) all lose 7-14 points. timproc_b5 4118: reading the
case-0 table index inline instead of first gives 99.14 -> 99.17 but makes the body one word longer (1721, target
1718), so it was reverted; the target's single `lw v0` of the spilled arg0 for
four uses in case 0 (case 1 reloads per use) did not come from empty tests, one-line layout, a block copy
local (frame +8, still reloads), or reordered stores. C234's remaining frame gap is 28 dead bytes below the
named V3 locals (NCC slots that no instruction touches; `-S` shows no reference); moving `sp40` first lines
up spCC / spB4 / sp8C / sp7C with the target (85.10 -> 85.17).

**5. Gotcha: parallel sweeps must not share a backup file.** Two `try.sh` sweeps on different units both wrote
`orig.bak`; one restored the other unit's source over `bootup_uso.c`. Use `mktemp` per call (fixed in
`g152/try.sh`) and diff every touched source against HEAD before committing.

**Negatives.** gl 59E80 rewritten as a clean 20-command gbi macro emitter: 3 words short of the size-exact
permuter body and lower fuzzy (both macro forms). game_uso BB8C / 7C1C, b5 8FC8 / DF14, gui 2DE0, post1b 65494
reviewed: constructor heads and s-register / home-slot layouts, no structural decode error found.

## kit LXXXI (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 153): commutative operand-order sweep, lazy-register tail, prologue lui <a name="kit-lxxxi-agent-g-run-153"></a>

1. **Operand order is a free lever.** cfe and NCC keep the source order of commutative operands, and the order
   decides which value is loaded first (temp-ring register) and which register lands in `fs` / `ft` of
   add.s / mul.s / addu. It is not a fixed mirror: in bootup E2D0 the target dot product
   `f16 = v1.x*v0.x; f6 = v1.y*v0.y; f10 = v1.z*v0.z; (x + y) + z` came from
   `v[1].z * v[0].z + (v[1].y * v[0].y + v[0].x * v[1].x)` -- the sum shape is mirrored and only the first
   product is mirrored. Try all orders per expression (40 combos for a 3-term dot product cost seconds).
2. **`opswap.py` (scratchpad g153):** finds every ` * ` / ` + ` with space-delimited operands (for `+` the operand
   extends over `*` / `/` chains; skips operands after `-`, `/`, `%`), swaps one at a time on a scratch copy,
   compiles the whole TU the same way as the build (asm-processor pre-pass + cfe, or NCC for `_nm.cpp` donors) and
   keeps a swap only if the score improves; repeat until no change. Score with
   `objdiff-cli diff -1 expected/<unit>.o -2 scratch.o -o - <fn>` (`right.symbols[].match_percent`): a positional
   word-diff score picked swaps that LOWERED report.json fuzzy on three NCC donors (gui 329C, b5 396C, B624).
   Always confirm with scripts/refresh-report.sh and check the body length (5F0B8: every swap made the NM body one
   word shorter than an already-short body -- rejected; a length change also moves the post0b NM clip).
3. **kernel 1594 (95.98, negative):** the target's second loop keeps `c` (segment start) and `lim` in t6 / t7 and the
   other temps in t4 / t5 / t8 / t9 -- one ugen ring, even across the `beqz c` -- while every C spelling (named
   locals, re-reads, assignment expressions) has uopt colour them into v1 / a0 or reload after the aliasing store.
   IDO 5.3 -O2 gives the same body as 7.1; NCC is worse.
4. **525F0 / 51448 lazy-register tail (negative):** the shared `add(obj + 0x10, t); if (t->f14) t->f4 = 1;
   t->f14 = obj;` tail reloads the spilled obj into v0 in the target. NCC with the tail as an inline member of
   either class or a free inline, and the lazy head as an inline getter, keep the v1 reload (getter forms add 8
   bytes of frame).
5. **bootup 6204 / E9FC (negative):** `lui a0` scheduled before `sw ra` is not reproduced by IDO 7.1 or 5.3 at
   -O0..-O3, -g, -mips1/2/3, with or without -Wab,-r4300_mul, nor by NCC free / member / static / virtual
   functions; only a parameter (whose home store is an extra word) flips the order.
6. **Biggest single wins were matrix / dot-product bodies** (690A8 `x = m[4]*v[1] + m[8]*v[2] + m[12] + v[0]*m[0]`
   style, 5F984 rot-matrix rows, 3558 squared-length sums, b1 1340 integer width sum): run the sweep first on any NM
   body with vector arithmetic. Long greedy runs need a per-improvement checkpoint (the first 578B4 run hit its
   timeout and lost its swaps). verify-blocks needs the repo `.venv` on PATH (crunch64).

## kit LXXXII (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 146): the near-exact queue under the line / temp-merge / operand-order levers <a name="kit-lxxxii-agent-c-run-146"></a>

**Summary.** The three newest levers (kit LXXVIII line layout, kit LXXX m2c temp merges, kit LXXXI operand order) were
run over every agent-c near-exact (99.0-99.99 %). **None of them moved a single near-exact.** Their remaining words
are register colours, a home/temp slot, or an edg temp order, and none of those depend on line grouping, variable
families or operand order. The levers did pay on the lower band (60-93 %).

**1. Scoring harness (session scratchpad c146).** `sc.sh SRC UNIT FUNC` compiles any full copy of a unit exactly
like `build/non_matching` (asm-processor pre-pass, cfe -O2 with the unit's include dir, asm-processor post-process)
and prints objdiff `match_percent` / size of FUNC against `expected/src/<unit>.c.o`. It took about 2 s for
post0b and agreed with `objdiff-cli diff -u` for every unit tried (post0b, post, game_libs, game_uso, timproc_b5,
arcproc_tail1, titproc). `ncc.sh` is the same for NCC donors. `od.py UNIT FUNC [-1 a.o -2 b.o]` prints only the
differing rows. Use them with `xargs -P 16` for grids. Treat report.json as final: the report number weights relocs
differently from the scratch number. For example, 45178 is 99.985 in report.json and 99.70 in objdiff.

**2. All declared locals get homes in declaration order; a spilled CSE temp goes to the temp area below them
(gl_func_00045178).** The 104-byte frame is t 0x64, a 0x58, b 0x4c, q 0x48, i 0x44, p 0x40, n3 0x3c, m 0x38,
hi/v/r 0x34..0x2c, g 0x28 (top-down in declaration order, dead ones too). The target spills the gbi packet pointer at
**0x24**, below every home, so in the target it is a compiler temp and not a named `int *g`. Every frame-preserving
spelling of a named g (168 decl-order / pad positions, block scope, `register`) leaves it at its home or grows the
frame. A struct-typed list pointer reproduces the temp spill:
`typedef struct { int w0, w1; } G45178; G45178 *g; ... g = (G45178 *)FW(FW(p, 0xC), 0); g[i].w0 = 0x01030040;
g[i].w1 = gl_func_00000000(m);` (and `i = FW(FW(p, 0xC), 4);` without the n3 copy). `&g[i]` is CSE'd and spilled
at sp+0x24 as in the target, but the second slot's index / list / address registers then come out a3 / v1 / t0
(target v1 / t3 / a3): objdiff 99.70 -> 99.12, so the variant was **not kept**. Decl-order moves (122), line
sweeps, `if (x) {}` sweeps and index-copy variants did not change those colours. The remaining exact path:
fix those three colours, then add an IDO 7.1 donor for the three literal %lo (`gl_func_00045178_rodata` = 0x1B60).

**3. Negatives (each <= 15 min, all scored with sc.sh / ncc.sh):**

  (`const V3&` / `const P3&` / by-value params, `(P3 &)` / `(V3 &)` casts on either operand of `-` and `*`), all

## kit LXXXIII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 154): recognition survey, in-game sibling templates <a name="kit-lxxxiii-agent-g-run-154"></a>

**Part 1 -- library recognition survey (negative).** All 208 non-exact functions were fingerprinted (lui/ori 32-bit
constants, hardware addresses, call shape) and checked against references/ (libreultra, oot, papermario):
- kernel 0 %: bzero 2CD0, osWritebackDCache 2DF0, osInvalICache 4F50, osInvalDCache 5000, whole-dcache 9CE0 and the
  CP0 helpers are all handwritten libultra `.s` (cache / mtc0 ops). game_libs tail 0 %: exceptasm 6A09C / 6A5F0 /
  6AD68 / 6AD78, bzero 6B048, osWritebackDCache 6C400, __osProbeTLB 6D894, osInvalICache 6F254, osInvalDCache
  6F2D4, bcopy 70324, SetFpcCsr 71370, osMapTLBRdb 73258, osWritebackDCacheAll 74860 -- all handwritten, no C.
- No libm / libc / gu constants remain (no pi/180, 180/pi, 32767, guPerspective / guLookAt tables). 1e9 in gl 6126C
  is an in-house mini printf (calls the in-house itoa 34458); 0x12345678 / 0x87654321 / 0x1234000N are in-house
  allocator tags (4D468, 4D688, 5AFD4; agent-c 334E8 / 33BE4 / 33EB8); the GBI words (F3DEX 0x06 DL, 0xB6 / 0xB7
  geometry mode, 0xBA othermode, 0xE4 / 0xB3 / 0xB4 texrect, 0xE7 pipesync) mark in-house display-list builders
  (gui F04 / 2DE0 / 329C / 3714 / 4568, gl 4BAF4 / 4B620 / 578B4 / 59E80 / 5A2C4 / 46050 / 42938, bootup E68 / 1A44).
  Kernel 1594 / 18F0 / 1ADC are the in-house USO loader. Agent-c units (post 2D374..34000, titproc, arcproc) are
  in-house too. **The library vein is exhausted for the tracked non-exact set.**

**Part 2 -- the vein that is left: in-game copy-paste twins.** `scripts/sibling-scan.py` (committed) compares each
non-exact function's opcode sequence (primary opcode, SPECIAL funct, COP1 fmt + funct) with every `.s` body via
difflib and prints the best partners with their fuzzy. **An exact partner at ratio >= ~0.75 is a template; port its C
(or its NCC / match_imports donor) and adjust offsets.** Top hits this run and what happened:

| target | partner (exact) | ratio | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| timproc_b5 396C (188) | b5 38B0 (match_imports C) | 1.00 | EXACT: the 38B0 file with fields 0x184/0x188/0x18C |
| h2hproc 620 (708) | arcproc A3C / timproc_b1 097C | 0.81 | EXACT: A3C skeleton (see below) |
| gl 4CCB4 (240) | gl 3829C | 0.79 | EXACT: nested short-circuit alloc chain |
| gl 4D0E4 (108) | gl 62F08 | 0.77 | EXACT: store-run order + typed constant |
| gl 3E0F0 (192) | gl 37AF0 | 0.85 | NM 90.52 -> 93.88 (frame / homes exact) |
| b5 DF14 (1688) | b5 D884 (NM 95.5) | 0.97 | NM 82.73 -> 95.23 |
| gl 39E24 (192) | bootup 76F4 (NM 99.8) | 0.87 | NM 95.00 -> 99.79 (same code in two USOs) |
| gl 525F0, 488A0, 41D40, 4FBA4, 5AFD4, 51448 | 3E904, 483BC, 4E244, 4F85C, 635D8, 33228 | 0.67-0.76 | no gain (documented caps / C++ shapes) |

Recipes from the four exacts:
1. **396C: match_imports twin + placeholder prototype.** The frozen `src/match_imports/context_timproc_uso_b5.h`
   still declares 396C with the old `(char *, s32, char *, f32, f32)` placeholder, which conflicts with the typed
   twin signature. Do not edit the frozen context (its sha is recorded in scripts/match-imports.json): wrap the
   include, `#define timproc_uso_b5_func_0000396C timproc_uso_b5_func_0000396C_ctx_placeholder` / `#include` /
   `#undef`. Casting typed locals from the placeholder params instead changes codegen (48 vs 47 words). Wiring = the
   38B0 stanzas duplicated (compile x2, ld x2 with `.text 0x396c`, bind x2 with a new `raw_sha256` of the linked
   .text, REPLACE_FUNC_BODY x2 + prerequisites); `bind-native-relocations.py` needs `PYTHONPATH=scripts` if you
   compute the sha by importing replace-function-body.py.
2. **h2h 620 = arcproc A3C with fewer args.** The 96.5 % NM body (regalloc "cap" since 2026-06) fell at once to
   A3C's spelling: nested `if (x != 0 || (x = alloc(N)) != 0)` levels with ONE o1/o2/o3 chain, the registration call
   through a void alias (`gl_func_00000000_620v`, frees v0 for the vtable base), one reused `o1` for every re-read
   object pointer, the stream word through a distinct `D_h2h_620_r`, the table as `&D_00000000`. New symbols pinned at
   0. Lesson: before grinding a "cap", look for an exact twin in another overlay.
3. **4CCB4 = 3829C.** The old decode (three sequential allocs with gotos) was the wrong shape; the target is 3829C's
   nested short-circuit chain (o1 = alloc(0xC); v1 = o1 or alloc(8); r = v1 or alloc(4)), void return, o1 left in a2
   for the second call. Frame 40 = ONE leading `volatile int pad0` (the spill homes then land at 28 / 32). The
   target's `lui t7; lui t8; addiu t8; addiu t7` order for the two v1 stores comes only from writing both stores on
   **one source line** (as1 reorders within a line, kit LXXVIII); on two lines the addiu order is t7 first.
4. **4D0E4: typed constants are not CSE'd.** A leaf store run where the target materialises `1` twice
   (`addiu t6,zero,1` early, `addiu t3,zero,1` after the global load). (a) Put the global read store
   (`a0[0x48/4] = D_00000000`) BEFORE the 0xC00 / 1 stores in source -- the scheduler sinks it into the jr delay and
   the later constants land after the lw. (b) Write the second `1` as an unsigned constant through a u32 lvalue,
   `*(u32 *)&a0[0x64/4] = 1U;` -- uopt does not CSE equal constants of different type (same family as kit LXXVII's
   unsigned compare), so it gets its own register. `if (1) {}` / `(u8)1` / block scope all leave the CSE.

Negatives worth keeping:
- 3E0F0: 37AF0's `tmp` first + `volatile padA[4]` + `zero[3]` fix frame 80 and every home, but `tmp = o` is
  coalesced into o's s0, so the home store is `sw s0,76` (before the arg setup) instead of the target's
  `sw a0,76` in the jal delay; `char *tmp[1]`, `if (0) f(&tmp)`, comma forms all store s0.
- 51448: same class -- the target spills the copy `n` (a1 web) to 40 and `l` to 44; NCC with an inline
  `link(l, n)` gets the 40/44 homes for l but n stays s0 (90.7). Reading n back from the just-stored field is
  forwarded and coalesced (flat).
- 39E24 / 76F4 (identical code, 2 words each from exact, pins aside): the target emits `lui v0` (vector base) before
  the rematerialised G (`lui a2`) after the second call; early / block / pre-call vector locals are copy-propagated
  and every one-line grouping is flat or worse.
- 488A0 as an NCC port of the 483BC donor: 98.35 (cfe NM stays 99.06); 41D40 as an NCC port of 4E244's iterator
  classes: 87.7 (the target keeps &G in s2 across calls; references / volatile references do not reproduce it).
- 5AFD4: `(x >> 4) + 0xFF000000 - 1` folds to one constant under every cast / type split tried.

Survey candidates outside agent-g ownership (not edited): arcproc 16F4 (85.36) and timproc_b3 13B8 (80.36) are
opcode-identical (ratio 1.00) -- solve one, port to the other; arcproc 125C (99.78) has an exact twin in mgrproc 1C90
(0.87); timproc_b5 32C8 (99.93) vs b5 2B74 (0.75).

**Ownership note.** 4CCB4, 4D0E4, 39E24 and 3E0F0 sit in post0b below 0x50000 (agent-c's range). They were

## kit LXXXIV (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 155): colour-pairing levers, sibling scans exhausted <a name="kit-lxxxiv-agent-g-run-155"></a>

**1. gl 68DD4 EXACT: two levers together, neither alone.** The 85-word script-op handler sat at 98.71 with
"colours only" residuals: `x` t1 (target t0); read 1 `pp/q/v` = v1/t0/a2 (target v0/t1/v1); read 2 = v1/t0/a2
(target v1/v0/a2). Read the target's colours as *pairs of roles sharing one register*: v0 = {pp1, q2},
v1 = {v1, pp2}, t1 = q1, a2 = v2. uopt colours per C variable, so write the source with one local per
pair:
```c
A = *(int *)arg0;  q = *(int **)A;  *(int **)A = q + 1;  B = *q;  FW(arg0, 4) = B;  sp30 = (&D_00000000)[B];
B = *(int *)arg0;  A = *(int *)B;   *(int *)B = A + 4;   v = *(int *)A;  FW(arg0, 4) = v;
```
That alone gave the right *shape* but every value one register too high (A v1, B t0, q t2, x t1): the
leading `gl_func_00000000();` is a K&R int call whose discarded result keeps a dead v0 def (kit IX). With
the call through a void alias (`extern void gl_func_00000000_68dd4v(void);`, pinned 0 in
undefined_syms_auto.txt) the whole function is byte-exact, ROM cmp OK. Per-read split names (pp2/q2/v2),
splitting only v, renaming the 0xC object and decl reorders were all worse (90-98.6); the void alias on the
old spelling alone gave 97.59. **Recipe:** when the residual is a consistent register shift, (a) look for a
discarded call to an int-declared placeholder before the shifted code and route it through a void alias,
(b) group the target's registers into role pairs and give each pair one local.
- Same alias on gl 51448's discarded link call moves the obj reload into v0 as in the target (95.00 -> 95.56).
  Bootup 24B8 (four discarded placeholder calls) 94.87 -> 95.21; flat on 51AD8, 3430, 2840, 55A0, 5AFD4, B75C.
  It does NOT help 525F0 (the reload stays v1), BDEC, 2B7C (import_0024D108 / 083574 / D704) or E2D0
  (float / double / void return aliases for the normalize call: worse or flat).

**2. Sibling scans.** `scripts/sibling-scan.py --min 0.5 --size-tol 0.6 --exact-only` and a longest-common-
opcode-block scan (>= 40 ops vs every exact) over the agent-g units found no new whole-function template.
Block hits worth knowing: game_libs 5A2C4's 98-op colour-conversion block equals the u8 colour packs of
47B28 / 47394 / 470E4 (the template's `col[k] = f * 255.0f` with u8 col read back emits lbu reloads -- the
target keeps the converted values in registers and re-homes r at sp+0x20; 89.07 stays); bootup 90CC
shares 94 ops with gl 64588; gl 5F984 shares 70 with the 5E288 / 5EB4C / 5ED54 matrix family.
- 5F984 (NM donor, NCC): the siblings' **param copy** `f32 (*m)[4]; m = arg0;` (a copy of the param,
  coloured s0) 90.11 -> 92.35 and 179 -> 181 of 184 words; `volatile f32 q0;` above R and `volatile f32 q1;`
  below it give frame 0x100 = target: 92.46. Unused non-volatile pads and volatile arrays are dropped by NCC.
  Residual: len home 180 vs 176, v at 168 vs 160, and the rot block's register cycle through sp32/36 (the
  same ugen juggle as game_uso 3558's matrix block -- unsolved in both).
- Twin NM port: timproc_b3 13B8 is opcode-identical to arcproc 16F4 (offsets -0x50 / -0x38, flag 4 -> 2);
  16F4's C ported verbatim 80.36 -> 85.36; then `saved64 = temp_s1; saved60 = temp_s2;` copies before the
  strlen call (target spills both there) 85.41 on both twins. Arg1 now sits in s8 as in the target; the rest is
  an s1/s3/s4 permutation (buf vs region pointer vs arg2).

**3. Negatives (time-boxed, keep for the next pass).**
- b5 D884: a plain `extern volatile struct` / volatile scalars for the EE6C flag word fix the lw-after-sw
  order but materialise `lui+addiu` bases (CSE'd into v0, or per-site addiu); the target's shared `lui at`

## kit LXXXV (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 147): epilogue alignment after an infinite loop, original-unit donors, sibling ports <a name="kit-lxxxv-agent-c-run-147"></a>

**1. IDO aligns the unreachable epilogue after an infinite loop to a 32-byte boundary of the .text
section.** In a function whose loop never exits (`for (;;)` with no break/return), IDO emits the back
branch, then zero words (nops) up to the next 32-byte boundary of the whole .text section, then the
epilogue (`lw ra ... jr ra`). Test file (one unit, IDO 7.1 -O2): eight copies of
`void f(void) { for (;;) g(); }` put their epilogues at 0x20, 0x60, 0xA0, 0xE0, 0x120, and after a
non-looping function in between at 0x180, 0x1C0. The nop count therefore depends on where the function
sits in its translation unit, not on the C. Functions with ordinary returns are not affected.

Consequence: if splat cut the original unit at a different place than the original source file began,
the correct C gets the wrong number of nops (a 4-to-28-byte length error with every other word right).
**How to find the original unit start:** take the target's epilogue address E (the `lw ra` after the
zero words). The original unit starts at an address S with S = E (mod 32). Look for an earlier function
start with that residue. For gl_func_00034548: E = 0x34654, E mod 32 = 0x14. post0b starts at 0x34458
(residue 0x18, wrong); game_libs_func_000343F4 starts at 0x343F4 (residue 0x14). The exact 34EB4
(epilogue 0x35134) and the hang stub 3485C (epilogue 0x34874) have the same residue, so 343F4 starts
the original unit. splat had put 343F4 in game_libs_post.c and started post0b at 34458.

**Recipe (legal donor splice, no instruction forcing):** write an IDO 7.1 -O2 donor `.c` that is the
original unit's head: copy the real, already-exact C of every function from the unit start up to the
target, in order, then the target's C. Splice only the target(s) with REPLACE_FUNC_BODY. Check with
`objdump -t` that every leading function has its target size, so the offsets agree. Here
`src/game_libs/game_libs_o2_34548.c` = 343F4 (from game_libs_o2_343F4.c) + 34458 + 34548 + 34684 +
346F0 + 34810 + 3485C (all the in-between C copied from game_libs_post0b.c). It yields 34548 at 316
bytes (post0b layout gives 320) and 3485C at 32 bytes. 3485C used to be a bare INCLUDE_ASM whose
report entry had no fuzzy at all (objdiff gives `None` for it); it now has a C host
(`void f(int a0) { int *p = &a0; for (;;) {} }`, 0x28 bytes in post0b's layout, shrunk to 0x20 by the
splice) and scores 100.

**Makefile gotcha:** a `.c` donor listed as a prerequisite of its host inherits the host's
non-private target-specific variables (GNU make passes them to prerequisites). post0b's
`TRUNCATE_TEXT :=`, `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE :=` / `+=` and `REPLACE_FUNC_BODY :=` lines ran on the donor
object and failed (`KeyError: function gl_func_0004D084 not found`). All four are now `private`.
(The `.cpp` donor rule uses none of them, which is why the many NCC donors never hit this.)

**2. gl_func_00034548 decode (34458 sibling, scan ratio 0.63): 77.38 -> 98.73 in cfe, then 100 via
the donor.** The old body was the wrong shape. The real one:
- the loop is infinite; the poll result is stored to the global BEFORE the zero test
  (`if ((slot = poll()) == 0) continue;` puts the `sw v0,0(s1)` in the beqz delay) and the global is
  re-read after every later call;
- `&D_00000000 + 0x3BB34` split into a held base `0x38000` (`lui 4; addiu -0x8000`) plus a 15156
  offset on every access. A symbol pinned at the address (`D_34548_slot = 0x0003BB34;`, accessed as a
  plain `char *` global) gives the target's `lui s1,4; addiu s1,-0x44CC` and `lw 0(s1)`. Keep
  `&D_00000000 + K` for the values used as arguments (0x3BB18 in s2, the 0x1E424 / 0x1E438 templates);
- the vtable record is a distinct base-0 extern (`D_34548_obj`), as in 34458;
- frame 96 with homes 92 / 84 / 80: **declared register locals reserve home slots in declaration
  order**. `int sp5C; char *s0; int sp54, sp50;` gives sp5C 92, (s0's unused slot 88), sp54 84,
  sp50 80. A `volatile int pad` or an extra int instead grows the frame by 8, and the result temp
  `r5` must be declared after the out pair. `int out[2]` is not 8-aligned and changes nothing.

**3. Twin port between two non-exact functions: gl 334E8 <- gl 33BE4 (scan ratio 0.94): 68.85 -> 73.71.**
334E8 is 33BE4 with the source fixed to an 8-byte stack buffer filled by the first callback (template
0x1E280), length 8 and no flag gate. Copy 33BE4's body with fresh per-site aliases (gl_d_334e8_*, same
values), declare the buffer FIRST (target home sp+96) and share one result temp (avail = cur), which
gives frame 104. Length 636 -> 712 (target 708). Tried and not kept: `cpdst = base` (exact length 708,
71.31), distinct symbols for the two spin loops or no volatile (the spin addresses are hoisted into
s3 / s4), one struct symbol for all fields (the base is CSE'd into a register, 62.06). The same
spellings on 33BE4 itself score lower than its current 80.59, as does reusing `flags` as the temp for
the +0x28 loads.

**3b. gl 4E424 (distance-estimate leaf, float args): parameter registers ARE the variables.** The
target holds `x1 -= x0` in the a3 web (moved to f20), computes dy straight into y0's f14, writes the
smaller distance back into x0 (f12) and the result into the zero constant's f16, while the zero keeps
ONE `mtc1` for all three compares. A 168-variant grid over which name holds each role (dx: x1 / local;
dy: local / y0 / y1; dz: local / z0 / z1; a: local / x0; b: local / y0 / z0; c: local / zero) put
`x1 = x1 - x0; y0 = y1 - y0; dz = z1 - z0; ... x0 = min; b = max; zero = ...` on top: 90.98 (run-134
NCC NM donor, retired) -> 93.22, 51 -> 50 words (target 49). Reusing y1 / z1 (stack-passed params)
instead puts them in callee-saved f22 / f24 and grows the frame; writing to `zero` while its compares
are still ahead splits the constant into one `mtc1` per compare.

**3c. game_libs 307A8:** `c -= 1; D.cnt = c;` instead of `D.cnt = c - 1;` reuses the counter web
(target `addiu v0,v0,-1`): 93.31 -> 96.38. The rest is two `lui at` shared by stores / loads to
different fields (`sw zero,12(at); sw zero,8(at)`); one symbol for both fields gets CSE'd into
`lui; addiu` instead (91.35), and one source line does nothing.

**4. Negatives (all scored with the scratch scorers sc.sh / ncc.sh):**
- **timproc_b5 32C8 <- 2B74 donor (ratio 0.75):** the 2B74 NCC skeleton with 32C8's fields scores
  92.75; the current 32C8 C body compiled as C++ scores 96.46 at 1476 bytes (one word short: NCC does
  not re-materialise the zero `mtc1` on the alloc path before the join, cfe does). In cfe, a shared
  zero variable `h` (2B74's comma-expression trick), a reused `fa` for l134 / l13C, and moving the
  uE8 load or the v104 zeros around all stay at or below 99.49 scratch (99.93 report).
- **game_uso 1DDC policy fix:** `if (fz) {}` at entry tested an uninitialised local. Removed.
  `if (a0) {}`, `if (key) {}`, `if (*a0) {}`, `fz = 0` + test and `if (1) {}` all give the same 99.10.
- **gl 4CDB0 as an NCC donor with an inline `next()` (gui 55C's 1A5C recipe, ratio 0.57):** 1296
  variants (next / `if (1) {}` next / cached-dl next per packet x an empty if after each packet):
  best 95.49 scratch, below the cfe body (99.17 scratch, 99.64 report).
- **game_uso 97EC:** an XZ `operator*`, no XZ `operator-`, copy-init `XZ e = ...`, a named `d = a - b`,
  named-return operators: all flat or lower (99.15 best).
- **kit LXXXIV void-alias lever on agent-c near-exacts (every subset of the statement-level discarded
  calls routed through a void alias pinned at 0):** arcproc 125C (4096 subsets), gl 15FC (94), 40304 (32),
  445AC (512), 45178 (8), 4EE44 (8), 4AFB4 (4): every variant gives the same words as the base.
  timproc_b5 32C8 with all ten 04A188 calls void: 99.49 -> 99.36 scratch. The t-ring offsets in 125C and
  the v0 / v1 tie in 15FC do not come from a dead v0 def.
- **gl 34890 (90.35):** 720 declaration orders of a / p / nx / node / b / c (b and c at function
  scope) and the same body under NCC: flat (89.87 -> 89.90 at most). The target stores h (a1) to its
  spill home before EVERY alloc call and reloads it right after each; the build stores it once.
- **Sibling-scan noise:** for agent-c's units the exact partners below ratio ~0.65 were not twins
  (35B1C / 35C6C, 4AFB4 / 33A20, 44CE8 / 3D16C, 3D71C / gl 8A40 (-O0), 34890 / 3D2C8). 34548 / 34458
  at 0.63 was the exception: it shared the idioms (vtable slot +0x70, the trailing 7-arg print call),
  not the control flow.

Gate (agent-c branch, rebased on aca0b6e18): ROM cmp OK, verify-blocks 6/6, `make non_matching_objects`
0 errors, sentinels 100, no exact lost, 76.78 -> 76.83 % code; post0b NM clip 0x2e90c -> 0x2e91c (62F08

## kit LXXXVI (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 156): held results, NCC home grids, scratch void sweep <a name="kit-lxxxvi-agent-g-run-156"></a>

**1. gl 5F984 EXACT: an FP "register cycle through sp+32/36" is ugen spilling the INPUTS because the
outputs are held.** The target's rotate block (`v = rot^T * v` before the rotation call) did
`swc1 b,0x20(sp); swc1 d,0x24(sp); ... lwc1 ...` around every product, and kept the three results in
f0 / f12 / f14 until it stored them (y, x, z) just before the call. Our `v.x = ...; v.y = ...; v.z = ...;`
stored each result at once, so the inputs always had a free temp and nothing spilled (2-3 words short,
92.46). The cause is register pressure inside ugen, not uopt colouring: three live results + three live
inputs exceed the FP temp ring, and ugen spills to the temp area at sp+0x20.. (below every home). Recipe:
```c
f32 a = v.x, b = v.y, d = v.z;
c   = rot[0][0] * a + rot[1][0] * b + rot[2][0] * d;   /* c, h, len: locals already dead here */
h   = rot[0][1] * a + rot[1][1] * b + rot[2][1] * d;
len = rot[0][2] * a + rot[1][2] * b + rot[2][2] * d;
v.y = h;  v.x = c;  v.z = len;
```
- Use locals that are already dead at that point for the results. Under NCC every declared local takes a
  frame word (kit LXXXIV); three fresh `nx / ny / nz` grew the frame 0x100 -> 0x110 (93.30). Reusing c / h /
  len kept 0x100 and gave 93.41.
- Then grid the multiply operand order (512 cells, `rot * var` vs `var * rot` per product): **only the
  all-`rot[r][c] * var` cell reaches the target length (736)**, 99.93. The other 511 are 728-732 bytes.
- The remaining words were homes only. A 56-cell grid (pick any two scalars between `volatile q1` / `len` / `v`,
  the other six between `v` and `out`) put len at 0xB0, v at 0xA0 and out at 0x48. Almost every pair works,
  so the rule is "two words above v, six between v and out". Unused `f32 pad[2]` / `t[2]` are dropped by NCC.
- Wiring: the donor is now spliced into build/src and build/non_matching
  (`GAMELIBS_5F984_DONOR`, `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_5F984.cpp.o`). The NM donor `_nm.cpp` is retired.
  The placeholders `gl_func_00000000_sqrt5F984` / `_rot5F984` are pinned at 0. The post0b NM clip goes up by
  the donor growth (+12): 0x2e91c -> 0x2e928, = 62F08 NM offset 0x2e8d8 + 0x50. ROM cmp OK.
- **game_uso 3558 has the same juggle and the same cause.** Its matrix block also keeps the three
  `stage[]` results and the three `vb[]` sums in registers (f0 / f2 / f12 and f14 / f16 / f18) and stores
  them late. Writing the products into the dead `sc / k / mag` (m-first operand order) gives the target's
  spill pattern for the first block and moves the length toward the target (984 -> 996, target 1008), but
  the score drops (69.73 -> 67.51) because the `vb` adds are not held yet. Not kept. To finish it: hold
  `vb0..2 = vb[i] + x` in locals too, and store stage y, x, z and then vb in the target's order.

**1b. The same lever on the timproc_b5 "0xDC record" heads (AC20, B624, B154, B368) and elsewhere.**
All four functions start with `v = rec(+0xDC) - pool` (three subtractions against two pool statics). The
target loads all three pool words first, sharing one `lui at` per pool (`lwc1 0(at); lwc1 4(at)`), and
keeps the differences in f0 / f2 / f12 (or f2 / f12 / f14) before the three stores. So the "shared lui at"
residual noted in kit LX / run 143 was this same effect. as1 only shares the `lui at` between neighbouring
loads, and the held form is what makes the loads neighbours. Spellings that worked:
- cfe (AC20): dead f32 locals `ang = ...; var_f12 = ...; wrap = ...;` and then the stores. 91.58 -> 92.41, and
  the length becomes the target's (1336 -> 1332). The old `if (arg0) {}` keep-live is no longer needed.
- cfe (B154): `ang` plus two block locals `f32 hy, hz;`. Their homes are taken out of the volatile pad
  (`pad9C[4]` -> `[1]`): 83.08 -> 92.23.
- NCC (B624): three block locals `f32 hx = ..., hy = ..., hz = ...;` 89.84 -> 93.72, same length. NCC (B368):
  the same plus the kit-LX reference form for x / y: 89.58 -> 92.71, 174 -> 173 words (= target). On B624
  the reference form gives 94.78 but makes the body one word too short, so it was not kept.
- bootup 8BD4: the `nn = dir * negamt` triple through block locals, 83.95 -> 91.85. Holding the `imp`
  triple too (the target holds it as well) scores 91.80, so it is left as is.
- game_uso 3558: `side[1]`'s product held in the dead `k` before the three `side[]` stores: 69.73 -> 72.33.
- `g156/hold.py SRC UNIT FUNC [ncc]` is a greedy scratch sweep. It rewrites every `X.x / X.y / X.z` (or
  `[0..2]`, `.f0 / .f4 / .f8`) store triple into held block locals, keeps a change only when objdiff
  improves, and repeats. Over the 47 remaining agent-g cfe bodies it found only 3558 and 5F984 (whose
  .c NM body is now unused). Over the NCC NM donors it found bootup C234 (sp68 / sp40 scaled vectors,
  85.33 -> 89.85, same length); gui 3714 / 329C / 2DE0, 63B4, 2840, 5F5F0, BB8C and 7C1C stayed flat. A quick signal for where to look: the target has many more FP results in
  f0 / f2 / f12 / f14 (the non-temp registers) than the build. 7C1C has 54 vs 17, C234 11 vs 1,
  gl 63964 21 vs 0 and gl 65494 12 vs 4. These are the next candidates; hold.py found nothing in 63964 /
  65494 in store order x, y, z.
- `g156/hold6.py` is the same sweep, but it also tries all six store orders for each triple. gl 63964
  accepted five triples (d stored z, x, y; s1 y, x, z; r2 / s3 x, z, y; out x, y, z): 76.08 -> 77.49, same
  length. Nothing changed for 65494, B75C, 8BD4 or 3558. **The target's store order shows up directly
  in the expected asm (the swc1 order after the three FP ops), so read it off instead of searching.**

**2. Scratch-only sweeps (nothing written into src/).** `g156/sc.sh SRC UNIT FUNC` compiles a full copy
of a unit like build/non_matching (asm-processor, cfe, post-process). `ncc.sh` does the same for NCC donors.
Both score with `objdiff-cli diff -1 expected -2 scratch.o -c functionRelocDiffs=none` (agrees with
report.json when the function has no REPLACE_FUNC_BODY donor; for donor-spliced functions score the donor
file). `vsweep.py FUNC UNIT` reuses lever-sweep.py's site finder (`find_void_sites` / `callee_proto` /
`build_void_variant`) but compiles scratch copies. It tries each discarded call to a non-void callee as a
void alias, per callee, all, and pairs of improving sites.
- Void sweep over all 69 agent-g non-exact functions (2 min with `xargs -P 14`): the only gains were gl 5A2C4
  (+0.28, `func_00000000_5a2c4v`) and bootup E68 (+0.04, `func_00000000_e68v`). Both landed, pinned at 0.
  Everything else was flat or worse. The lever is used up in these units.
- Converse scan (`v0scan.py`): for every jal, compare "v0 read before redefinition" between expected and
  build. Only one function disagreed. timproc_b5 AC20 reads 071028's return value as the dot-product axis,
  but the target discards it and materialises `timproc_uso_b5_D_807FFBB0` (lui / addiu) after the call.
  Fixed: 91.07 -> 91.58. Length 1328 -> 1336 (target 1332). The decode fix adds the target's two address
  words; the remaining extra word is the gxy base CSE (a1, target shares `lui at`). Typing the pool as a
  struct or an f32 array does not change it.
- Infinite-loop epilogue alignment (kit LXXXV) does not apply here: no agent-g non-exact target has a zero
  run of 3+ words after an unconditional back branch.

**3. Negatives (each time-boxed).**
- timproc_b5 4118 (99.14, 6872 bytes, one region): in case 0 the target loads arg0 from its home ONCE (v0)
  and uses it for all three stores. Ours reloads before every store. All of these were flat: copies into
  every existing char* local (copy-propagated away), `register` param, block-local `p` (+8 frame, and
  still reloaded), table-store first, one-line layout, chained 0.0f stores, `if (temp_t0) {}`. This is an
  allocation-region decision (arg0 gets a register only inside case 0 in the target), not a spelling.
- bootup 76F4: two symbols at one address (call argument vs scale loads) to reorder `lui v0` / `lui a2`:
  93.7-94.3 (from 99.82). The rematerialisation is load-bearing.
- gl 525F0: a non-void return of obj (to force the v0 reload) adds `or v0,v1` (96.5).
- bootup E2D0: nine placements and spellings of the arg4 keep-live test (none, `!= 0.0f`, volatile read,
  operand swap). The current one stays best (99.54).
- gl 5F5F0 (NCC): 32 line layouts of the else arm and 54 x/y/z decl orders and positions are all flat
  (98.80). The xEye home store (a1) still follows the v[] stores.
- gl 2840 (NCC): dropping sp3C / sp38 / vx / vy for plain dx / dy (volatile or not, 12 decl placements):
  81.5. game_libs 65EE4 (-Olimit 1 donor): the two residual classes are `lui tN; ori a2,tN` vs
  `lui a2; ori a2,a2` for the data constant, and the a0 / a1 setup order of the base-arg calls. Literal /
  unsigned / `|` spellings, explicit-constant args, prototyped callees and line splits are all flat.
- arcproc 16F4 / b3 13B8: too many structural differences (83 rows) for a time box.

Gate (agent-g, rebased on 1f25600d8): ROM cmp OK, verify-blocks 6/6, `make non_matching_objects` 0 errors,

game_libs_post0b.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5.c.o`,
`build/{,non_matching/}src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_uso/game_uso.c.o`,
new donor `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_5F984.cpp.o`, retired `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_5F984_nm.cpp.o`,
changed NM donors `build/src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5_ncc_B624_nm.cpp.o` / `_ncc_B368_nm.cpp.o`,

## kit LXXXVII (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 148): alignment survey, original-file-start map, twin / NCC levers <a name="kit-lxxxvii-agent-c-run-148"></a>

**1. Alignment survey (whole ROM, negative).** Scanner (scratch only): for every function in every
objdiff unit, take the target words from `expected/` and the NM build words from `build/non_matching/`,
mask relocated fields (HI16/LO16 low halves, jal targets), drop every zero word, renumber branch offsets
into the stripped index space, and compare. **No non-exact function is a pure nop-count / nop-position
difference** -- the only hits were INCLUDE_ASM handwritten asm (fuzzy None, identical by construction).
Of the non-exact functions with a different zero-word count, all have real codegen differences
(stripped opcode ratio 0.04-0.88). Only one non-exact function has an infinite-loop pad in the build:
gl 4D688 (the NCC NM donor emits one pad word; the target has none because its epilogue 0x4DA14 is
already at the aligned residue) -- its 82 % is codegen, not layout. Nothing found in agent-g's range,
so no patches.

**2. Where the original units start (game_libs).** game_libs address A = bootup.uso text offset
A + 0x1466C, so:
- **unit starts are 16-byte aligned in bootup text = gl A with A mod 16 = 4.** Every pad-terminated
  function below ends at A mod 16 = 4, and 343F4 (kit LXXXV) and 42334 fit. A function start with
  A mod 16 != 4 (e.g. 34458, the old post0b start) cannot begin a unit.
- **every infinite-loop epilogue sits at A mod 32 = 0x14** (32-aligned in bootup text): 34548, 3485C,
  34EB4, 61478, 66A50, 66EEC, 6DD14, 7507C (kernel: 800056EC, 80005C50, 80007FC8, 800071C0 at
  residue 0, kernel text being 32-aligned). The unit holding such a function must start at a function
  with A mod 32 = 0x14, and the donor for it must start there too (kit LXXXV recipe). Cross-check: the
  units holding 61478 / 6DD14 / 7507C start right after pads at 0x61054 / 0x6DA74 / 0x74854, all
  residue 0x14.
- **Known unit ENDS** (zero words after the last `jr ra` delay slot, i.e. IDO's .text padding to 16;
  the next unit starts at the address given): 0x9674 (o0 949C), 0x1F6B4, 0x22674 (pad pseudo-fn
  2266C), 0x295C4, 0x2D374 (pad 2D36C, audio driver end), 0x35E64 (pad 35E5C), 0x3FF44 (3FC58's
  trailing word), 0x42334 (pad 4230C: 10 words = the next unit needs 32-byte alignment), 0x4DD14,
  0x56084, 0x5AFB4, 0x5FDC4, 0x60584, 0x61054, 0x67394, 0x67FE4, 0x69CC4, 0x69F54, 0x69F64, 0x6B0F4,
  0x6C714, 0x6CB84, 0x6CC14, 0x6CC64, 0x6DA74, 0x6EF64, 0x6F044, 0x6F254, 0x6F2D4, 0x6F384, 0x6F3B4,
  0x6F3E4, 0x6FBE4, 0x70034, 0x70324, 0x70854, 0x70C44, 0x70FA4, 0x73314, 0x743C4, 0x74844, 0x74854.
  Known start without a pad: 0x343F4. A unit that ends exactly on a 16-byte boundary leaves no pad,
  so the list is a subset. All loop functions are already exact, so this vein is closed unless a new
  loop function is decoded; use the map to pick the donor head.
- Note for exacts: a function whose target .s carries the unit's trailing pad (3FC58: 748 vs 744)
  needs an all-zero pad SUFFIX when it goes exact.

**3. arcproc 125C EXACT (99.78 -> 100): port the exact twin's match_imports C.** sibling-scan pairs
it with mgrproc 1C90 (0.87), whose exact body lives in `src/match_imports/mgrproc_uso_func_00001C90.c`
(a native port of the original source). Porting that C verbatim (125C has one threshold field 0x77C
and its own offsets) fixed the long-standing t-ring "cap" at once; after a 48-cell grid the only extra
steps were one more bottom `volatile int` pad and `(int)(field * (0, (float)255))` (operand order).
What the twin's C carries that the grind never found: the whole body inside `if (flag) { ... }` (no
early return), the field re-read at every use (no `progress` local), `while (0) { w = ...; }` before
the span block, ONE q / w pair reused in both tails, and the volatile pad frame map
(pt_a..pt_d / sp50[4] / pmid / sp48 / ... / pad_a..pad_d). **Before grinding a near-exact, check
whether its twin is exact through a match_imports file -- those carry the original's statement
shapes.**

**4. gl 44CE8 under NCC (91.28 -> 99.53, NM donor `src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_44CE8_nm.cpp`).**
Pool record alloc `&pool->e[pool->n++]` (50 x 12-byte records at +0x378, count +0x5D0). The target
folds the first count test to `lw 1488(a3)` but REMATERIALISES the pool base `addiu v0,a3,888` in the
bnezl likely slot and again after the overflow call; cfe either spills a named base or folds every
access to a3 offsets (every cfe spelling <= 91). Under NCC with `Pool *p = &o->pool` the shape is
right at once (98.6). edg frame cost: each edg temporary takes a frame slot -- `n++` +8, a separate
`int k` +8, an inline member call's `this` +8 -- so the target's 32-byte frame (r at 28, p at 24)
needs the old count carried in r itself (`r = (Rec *)p->n; p->n = (int)r + 1; r = &p->e[(int)r];`,
a role pair as in kit LXXXIV). Left: that count then colours a0 (r's argument register) instead of
v1; the expression-only capture `r = &p->e[p->n]; p->n += 1;` colours v1 but numbers the address temp
before the increment (t8 / t9 swap). A dead 4th parameter as the count is worse (frame 40).

**5. gl 3E0F0 (93.88 -> 99.90): read the argument word first.** `{ int x = *(int *)(arg0 + 0x40);
gl(tmp = o, x); }` with the volatile tmp moves the home store into the jal delay slot after the
argument setup (target order); `tmp = o; gl(tmp, ...)` stores before. Left: the delay-slot store
takes o's s0 where the target stores the a0 argument copy; copy locals, `arg0 = o`, `tmp = a = o`,
casts and an empty test after the call are flat or worse.

**6. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- gl 45178 (99.99, one spill slot 36 vs 40): `g` (the gbi packet pointer) spills to its home; the
  target uses the temp area. Moving g through every decl position, volatile / plain pads at every
  position (+8 frame), dropping `hi` for the literal: flat.
- gl 64388 (NCC donor, operator return slot 116 vs 108): member / by-value / named-result forms of
  operator- and operator*, and 2-word pads at every decl position: flat or worse.
- gl 4EE44 (base load v0 vs a1): void / float / pointer return for aEE44_a, `r = aEE44_a(...)`, src
  spellings, the base through c / k / r or a new local at any decl position: flat or worse.
- titproc 5DC is a PURE s0 / s1 swap of d and t (after renaming, only the save slots differ):
  `if (d) {}` at top / loop / case 10 / tail, decl reorder, char* d, case-0 t -> mask: flat or worse.
- gl 4AFB4 (offset reload t1 vs v0): 32 spellings (array / pointer / shift forms x empty tests x
  if(1)): flat. gl 3D71C (src/dst addiu order): data / function-typed / local symbols for src and

  flat. gl 40304 constant / result locals (kit LXXXVI style): worse.
- game_libs 307A8 (two `lui at` shared by stores / loads of adjacent fields): one extern symbol for
  each pair, one-line pairs and file-local `static` structs for the pairs (kit LX's shared-at trick)
  all CSE the base into a register (91-95 scratch vs 95.8). timproc_b5 32C8 with the kit LXXXVI
