## kit LXXXVIII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 157): C++ copy chains, NCC $f20 params, compound assignment, NCC zero CSE <a name="kit-lxxxviii-agent-g-run-157"></a>

**1. A "struct copy chain" in m2c output is a C++ return by value.** m2c shows
`sp68 = ...; sp7C = sp68; sp8C = sp7C;` (word copies through t6 / v0 / a0) for code like
`d = pos - pool;`. Under NCC the chain falls out of an inline helper that returns a NAMED
local of a non-POD type:
```c++
struct V { f32 x, y, z; V() {} };            /* the user ctor matters: POD V loses it */
static inline V relPos(const V &a) {
    f32 &x = sXY[0]; f32 &y = sXY[1];          /* kit LX reference form: one lui at per object */
    V r; f32 dx = a.x - x; f32 dy = a.y - y; f32 dz = a.z - sZ;   /* held results */
    r.x = dx; r.y = dy; r.z = dz;
    return r;                                  /* r -> return temp -> destination */
}
...
sp8C = relPos(*(V *) (arg0 + 0xDC));
```
- This also gives the target's `addiu v0,a0,0xdc` + `lwc1 0/4/8(v0)` for the reference argument.
  Plain locals, pointer locals, references, `return V(...)` (a ctor return evaluates the
  arguments right to left, z first) and `V r(dx, dy, dz)` all fold the offset into
  `lwc1 0xdc(s0)` instead. Declaring `V r;` AFTER dx / dy / dz also loses the base.
- Return temps are shared: every chain in a function reuses one return slot (B368's head
  and first scale both copy through sp+0x124). A chain that needs its own slot (B368's
  second scale, sp+0x4C) came from taking the factor by `const f32 &`: `scaled3(s240, o->f128)`.
  Nested calls (`w = va + n * va.y`) give two temps plus a parameter copy (gl 63964 shape).
- The inline helper's locals take frame words under NCC (6 words in 8BD4, 3 per helper);
  the targets have them too, but not always in the same place. Volatile scalars keep a
  word; unused arrays (volatile or not) are dropped.
- Decl scope decides home order: function-scope locals first (top), then the helper
  temps of statements at that scope, then inner-scope locals. Moving the if-arm locals
  into the arm put B624 / B368 homes in target order.
- Score-blind trap: moving homes changes WHICH instructions differ, not how many, until
  every home lines up. A greedy pad sweep sees nothing; compute the target layout
  (offsets from the frame top) and place pads by hand.

**2. The bootup 8BD4 "$f20 parameter" cap is cfe-only.** The cfe body spilled amt
to its arg home around each call (documented as a toolchain cap). Recompiled under NCC
the same body keeps amt in $f20 with `sdc1 / ldc1` like the target: 91.85 -> 92.28 at once,
96.67 with items 1 and 3, 96.83 (length 836 = target) with the skip set written as three
`skip = code == K;` statements behind `if (!skip)` (one sltiu + bnez per test; the `||` form
merges two branches). Wired as an NM-only donor, bootup_uso_ncc_8BD4_nm.cpp.
`f20scan.py` idea: compare `sdc1 $f2x` counts between expected and the NM build. In agent-g
units only 8BD4 (fixed), BB8C (target 4, build 5) and gl 5F0B8 differ; 5F0B8 under NCC
scores lower (90.0 vs 91.9).

**3. NCC compound assignment through a computed lvalue takes its address.**
`*(int *)(*(char **)(b + 0x170) + 0x938) += 1;` compiles under NCC to
`addiu v1,v1,0x938; lw; addiu; sw 0(v1)` (cfe: `lw 0x938(v1) / sw 0x938(v1)`). Write
`x = x + 1`. In 8BD4 this removed four words (848 -> 832) and gave +2.1. A scratch sweep
(`g157/cas/sweep.py`) that rewrites every memory `op=` per site found no other gain in
the agent-g NCC donors (few such sites).

**4. NCC keeps a float zero in one register across calls; cfe re-materialises it per block.**
B154 (identity quaternion + three axes + a zero-filled vec4 after the calls) and gl 63964 under
NCC put 0.0f in $f20 / $f22 (`mtc1 zero, fs0` once, sdc1 in the prologue). The targets
re-issue `mtc1 zero` in every block, which is cfe behaviour; `0.0f`, `(f32) 0`, `(f32) 0.0`,
`0`, `0L`, `0U`, chained stores and a 401-cell site grid are all identical under NCC
(edg folds them all into one constant). The same split shows in the 1.0f axis constant
(target f12 per block, NCC a temp). So these targets are cfront C compiled by cfe, and an
NCC lift tops out once the constants matter. NCC 63964 with inline operators and an
`f32 arg1` parameter (a float after an int argument goes in a1, so `sw a1` still matches)
scores 87.86 but at 1092 bytes (target 1120, the four missing `mtc1 zero` plus others), so
it was not kept.

**5. Notes.**
- B624 extra: the 0x144 countdown is `if (c) c -= 1; if (c == 0)` (target t5), and passing
  `arg0 + 0xF4` directly instead of the sp28 local shrinks the frame to the target's 0x98.
- C234: the same inline-helper rewrite of its two scale chains scores lower (89.85 -> 89.5).
- `__inline` works in IDO 7.1 cfe, but it leaves an 8-byte `jr ra; nop` out-of-line stub in
  .text, so it cannot be used in a unit that must stay ROM-exact.
- b5 4118 not retried (kit LXXXVI negative stands). game_uso 3558 as NCC with inline
  `operator-` / matrix helper: 55.7 (cfe 72.3); gui 2DE0 / 329C / 3714 have no copy chains;
  BB8C (NCC) has the same zero-CSE split as item 4.

## kit LXXXIX (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 149): separate increment statement, held triples in post0b / post <a name="kit-lxxxix-agent-c-run-149"></a>

**1. gl 44CE8 EXACT (99.53 -> 100): write the count increment as its own statement.** Run 148's NCC
donor (kit LXXXVII #4) carried the old pool count in r (`r = (Rec *)p->n; p->n = (int)r + 1;
r = &p->e[(int)r];`) to keep the 32-byte frame, and the count coloured a0 (r's argument register)
instead of the target's v1. Changing only the increment to `p->n++;` gives v1 and the exact bytes:
```c
r = (Rec *)p->n; p->n++;
r = &p->e[(int)r];
```
`p->n = (int)r + 1` makes the stored value an expression of r, so uopt merges the count's live range
with r's (a0); `p->n++` is a read-modify-write of the field that leaves the count as its own value.
`r = &p->e[(p->n = (int)r + 1) - 1]`, `p->n = 1 + (int)r` and `r = p->e + ...` stay at 99.53;
`&p->e[p->n++]` and a block `int k` are 99.07 / 99.02 (k costs a frame word under NCC). The donor is
now `src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_44CE8.cpp`, spliced into build/src and build/non_matching (old `_nm`
donor retired). The donor's NM size equals the old NM size, so the clip did not move.
- **The same shape in cfe (gl 454C4):** five of its six display-list slot allocations
  `i = *(s32 *)(dl + 4); *(s32 *)(dl + 4) = i + 1;` written as `*(s32 *)(dl + 4) += 1;` raise
  61.68 -> 62.61 and the length 2016 -> 2024 (target 2028). The header allocation stays as it was
  (changing it scores lower). `c149/incsweep.py SRC UNIT FUNC [ncc]` is a greedy scratch sweep over
  every `A = E; E = A + 1;` pair (`E++` / `A = E++` / `E += 1` / `++E`). Over all 72 non-exact
  functions in agent-c's range only 454C4 gained. In the gbi packet functions (4CDB0, 4B2F4, 488A0)
  every per-site combination is flat or worse (81-cell grid on 4B2F4, 27 cells on 488A0): their g / i
  colour swap is not this effect.

**2. Held FP results in post0b / post (kit LXXXVI lever).** The quick signal is still the count of FP
results in f0 / f2 / f12 / f14 (target vs build, `c149/fpsig.py`). It found two functions: 4F2DC (7 vs 0)
and 36694 (15 vs 3). Results:
- **game_libs 4F2DC 82.71 -> 88.56** (1052 -> 1060 bytes, target 1064). Only the `vec70 = vecEC +
  vec19C` sum triple is held. Holding vecA0 (the scaled ray) and the vecEC / vecE0 scale triples as
  well scores lower in every combination (8-cell subset grid: 82.7-86.2), and the store order of the held
  triple makes no difference. The block locals add 8 frame bytes; `pad60[4] -> [2]` takes them back (+0.17).
- **gl 37540 71.85 -> 75.93** (756 -> 760, target 764). The scaled `g.vB4 = r(+0x50..) * a` triple
  and the `g.saved = r(+0x60..)` copy are both held. vB4 alone scores 75.80 but shortens the body to 752
  (away from the target), so it was not kept on its own.
- **gl 33094 (NCC NM donor) 80.26 -> 84.65:** the `b = p->pos` copy in the `p != 0` arm loaded into three
  block locals and then stored. Holding the `a` copy as well drops the length (380) and the score
  (78.4); a 24-cell decl-order grid is flat.
- **gl 36694 (NCC NM donor) 82.80 -> 83.44:** four triples held (vAC x z y, v78 x z y, v3C y z x,
  v30 x y z). The target still has 15 results in f0 / f2 / f12 / f14 and compact cfe-like homes, so the
  NCC donor may not be the right compiler for it. Re-lifting it to cfe is the next thing to try.
- Sweeps: `c149/hold6.py` (agent-g's greedy, 6 store orders) is too slow under load for big units
  (25-minute timeouts on 12 post0b functions). `c149/single.py` (each `X.x / .y / .z` triple held
  independently, 8 compiles in parallel) and `c149/single2.py` (any run of 2-3 float assignments
  `L = R;`) are faster. Most agent-c bodies spell stores as `*(f32 *)(p + N)` / macros, so the triple
  regex finds 0-3 sites per function. **A held triple in post0b changes the NM body length, so the post0b
  clip has to be recomputed after every such edit:** build the NM object, then clip =
  `nm game_libs_func_00062F08` + 0x50. This run moved it 0x2e928 -> 0x2e930 -> 0x2e938 -> 0x2e93c, one
  Makefile comment per step.

**2b. gl 250C8 98.08 -> 99.85 (audio, OoT `AudioLoad_ProcessAsyncLoad` with `__BgCopyFinishProcess`
inlined): one retMsg web.** The target loads `asyncLoad->retMsg` into a1 in every case's branch-delay
slot, and that value goes to osSendMesg. Reading it once into `retMsg` for the switch selector and again
into the SAME variable before the status store does it:
```c
retMsg = asyncLoad->retMsg; if (1) {} switch ((s32)ASYNC_TBLTYPE(retMsg)) { ...cases read asyncLoad->retMsg... }
retMsg = asyncLoad->retMsg; if (1) {} asyncLoad->status = 0; osSendMesg(asyncLoad->retQueue, (void *)retMsg, 0);
```
OoT's separate `doneMsg` (97.65) or `retMsg` used inside the case bodies too (95.8 / 94.6) score lower.
Left: the first load colours v0 (target a1, then copied to v0), and fontId's home is 0x54 where the
target shares the temp slot 0x24 with the bytesRemaining spill. fontId written as a repeated
`ASYNC_ID(...)` expression scores lower (95.6-96.3).
- gl 201B8 (OoT AllocCached-style pool, 97.86): `sub->cur = v = 1;` respelled as `v = 1; sub->cur = v;`,
  `sub->cur = 1; v = 1;` or with a comma: flat or worse. The target rematerialises `li v0,1` where
  the build reuses the hoisted t1 = 1.

**2c. Store order read from the target (`c149/revscan.py`).** For each function, the scanner counts
same-base `swc1` triples within 8 instructions whose offsets go down (8, 4, 0: z-first) or up, in both
the target and the build. A difference means the source writes those stores in the other order.
- **gl 415A4 76.35 -> 84.34** (same length 448, target 452). The zeroed `v[4]` block has target stores
  0xC, 8, 4, 0 from `addiu v0` off the struct pointer. `if (1) { v = t->v30; }` (t = &D_415A4_t in
  v1) instead of `D_415A4_t.v30` gives 86.25 alone, but it lets the two a28 stores fold into v1 and
  shortens the body to 440. Sending those two stores through a second extern name (`D_415A4_tA`; NM
  only, the NM object is not linked) keeps the target's absolute `lui at` and the length: 84.34.
- **gl 3B01C 98.21 -> 98.32:** the target subtracts z, y, x and copies n z-first. Writing dz / dy / dx
  in that order and reversing both n copies (8 x 18 grid) gives the gain; the pa / pb load order is
  still different.
- Other hits (2D374, 4FD00, 36F0C, 37348, 3C43C) are register-colour residuals, not store order.

**3. NCC re-lift of cfe bodies (run-134 `ncctry.py`, re-run on the current bodies).** Of 51 cfe
functions, 22 compile without hand fixes, and **none scores higher under NCC** than its cfe body
(closest: 35B1C 97.16 vs 97.40, 39E24 99.31 vs 99.79, 2D374 94.54 vs 96.69, 4EE44 99.73 vs 99.94).
44CE8's jump from 91 to 99.5 under NCC was specific to the rematerialised pool base. This vein is
closed for agent-c's cfe bodies.

**4. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- gl 3E0F0 (99.90, one word: `sw a0,76(sp)` in the last jal delay, ours `sw s0`): `(char *)(tmp = o)`,
  `tmp = o + 0`, `(int)` casts, `register` copies, `tmp = q = o`, the store inside the second argument
  (`(tmp = o, x)`), `if (0) {}` after the call, split declaration: flat, or +8 frame / s0 kept.
- gl 39E24 (lui v0 / lui a2 order): `*=` written as `vf = g * vf` / `vf = vf * g` for one or all three
  products: flat or worse.
- gl 445AC (t7 vs v1 for D_glob_e, the D_445AC_b base register): dropping `v =`, moving it to
  D_glob_d, char* / array / named-pointer forms of the D_445AC_b store: flat or worse (99.18-99.73).
- game_libs 4CDB0 packet 3 with `(*(int *)(g + 4))++` in each of the macro forms (block / function
  scope, g first / i first, `i = (...)++`): 96.1-99.64, never above the current 99.64.

## kit XC (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 158): IDO output vs handwritten assembly <a name="kit-xc-agent-g-run-158"></a>

Run 158 classified the 48 zero-fuzzy functions (all INCLUDE_ASM) and moved
the handwritten ones to real `.s` source (see
docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#handwritten-assembly-sources). Codegen facts used
to tell the two apart:

- **IDO never emits the trapping forms** `addi`, `add`, `sub` for C
  arithmetic (it uses addiu/addu/subu), so any of them in a function is hard
  evidence of hand assembly (the boot entry stub, the Yay0 decoder,
  __osProbeTLB's `add v0,v0,t5`, the rdb byte-store loop).
- **CP0 hazard nops** (`mtc0 ...; nop; nop` before `jr ra`, the three nops
  after `mtc0 EntryHi` before `tlbp`) and **a lone `swl $zero,0(a0)`** (bzero's
  unaligned head) are reference-`.s` shapes; no C idiom produces them.
- **Not evidence on their own:** `jr ra; sqrt.s $f0,$f12` is what IDO emits
  for `sqrtf` (`__builtin_sqrtf`), and `lw v0,0(a0); lw t9,0(v0); jr ra;
  sw t9,0(a0)` is what IDO emits for a pop-queue helper. game_libs_func_0006E20C
  (2 pad words + sqrtf) stays in the C queue; game_libs_func_0006AD68 counts as
  handwritten only because it sits inside the exceptasm object and equals the
  assembled `__osPopThread`.
- **An `addiu sp,sp,-8` frame with no saves** (a `register` local frame at
  -O1/-O2) at the end of a k0/k1/eret symbol is compiled C that splat glued on:
  `__osDequeueThread` (thread.c) closed both func_800031F0 and
  game_libs_func_0006AD78. The kernel one is split off as func_80003BF0 and
  matches as the plain libultra C at -O1 (`move a2,a0; lw a3,0(a2)` scheduled
  ahead of `addiu sp,sp,-8` -- at -O1 -g3 the addiu comes first instead);
  in game_libs the same fix moved gl_func_0006AF0C 8 bytes earlier (the old
  14-insn fragment's fake a2/a3 parameters and -O1 -g3 levers were artefacts
  of the wrong boundary).
- Old-libultra `__osDisableInt` / `__osRestoreInt` (no __OSGlobalIntMask
  logic) are the libreultra interrupt.s forms, not OoT's.

## kit XCII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 159): zero-pad pseudo-functions, more handwritten routines, NCC operand order <a name="kit-xcii-agent-g-run-159"></a>

**1. Zero-pad pseudo-functions: fold into the predecessor, rebuild one unit's baseline.** A splat
symbol made only of zero words (fuzzy `None` in report.json, still counted in total_code) is the
alignment pad of the previous object or function. Five were retired: game_libs 67ABC (2 words after
67AA0), 74EDC (6 words at the head of post2b_f = the tail pad of the 74DB4 IDO 5.3 object, which
lives in another unit), 75260 (after 75254), 75264_pad (the 75264 unit's tail sidecar) and the two
pad words at the head of 6E20C (after 6E1A4). Recipe, per unit:
- `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE := <pred>=0x00000000,...` on `build/src/...` **and**
  `NON_MATCHING_SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` on `build/non_matching/...` (both trees, or objdiff sees a
  symbol-size mismatch). Remove the INCLUDE_ASM / GLOBAL_ASM pad line and `git rm` its `.s`.
- A pad that crosses a unit boundary moves the TRUNCATE values: 74DB4 0x128 -> 0x140 (the suffix
  grows the symbol; IDO's own .text padding is then truncated away), post2b_f 0x388 -> 0x370.
- Rebuild only that unit's expected/ object from the INCLUDE_ASM baseline: import
  `strip_decomp_in_file` / `func_map` from scripts/refresh-expected-baseline.py, strip the one
  source, `make RUN_CC_CHECK=0 EXPECTED_BASELINE=1 build/src/<unit>.c.o`, restore the source. Keep
  REPLACE_FUNC_BODY **active** (do not pass `REPLACE_FUNC_BODY=`): the tracked expected/ objects of
  post2b_f / 74DB4 / 75264 were byte-identical that way, post1b / post1b2c differed only at
  relocation offsets (checked with `objdump -r`), while the donor-less build differed in real
  words. Then compare the new baseline's .text with the real build (reloc-blind identical) and
  install. The rebuilt baseline carries `.NON_MATCHING` marker symbols for every stripped function
  (the old one had fewer); report.json was unchanged for every other function.
- Result: the pad bytes move into a 100 % symbol (+44 bytes matched), ROM byte-identical.
- Still open, agent-c's units: game_libs_func_0004230C (10 words), 35E5C, 2D36C, 2266C (2 each).
  35E5C's predecessor gl_func_00035DAC is now an exact NCC donor splice, so the "predecessor is an
  NM wrap" reason in its comment no longer holds. Tried here (ROM cmp OK with the suffix on 35DAC in
  both trees), but the one-unit baseline helper above does NOT work for post0b: with donors kept the
  rebuilt baseline drifts from the real build at 0x18c5c (right after gl_func_0004D084, whose pad
  suffix is a `private ... +=` line), 15678 non-reloc words. post0b needs its own documented
  baseline recipe (MATCHING_WORKFLOW: strip + `EXPECTED_BASELINE=1`, see the 5FDC4 row); reverted,
  left for agent-c.

**2. Handwritten routines with non-zero fuzzy.** Run 158 classified the zero-fuzzy functions; three
more had partial C scores and were still handwritten:
- game_libs 70324 = libultra bcopy (38.67 -> 100, 772 bytes). The identity (libc/bcopy.s, trapping
  `add`, interior `jr ra`, the `.weakext` double export) was already proven in its comment; the C
  body was a memmove for the NM path. `src/libultra/game_libs/bcopy.s` is written from the target
  disassembly the way the IRIX assembler emitted it: macro expansions (`blt` = `slt` + `bnez`,
  `and v0,a0,3` = `andi`) and the reorganizer's fills (branch-likely target copies such as
  `bnezl at, L; slti at,a2,16`) are spelled as the real instructions, labels follow the reference
  source. A script turned `objdump -M no-aliases` output into labelled source (`beqz zero` -> `b`,
  `sll zero,zero,0` -> `nop`, `$` register prefixes, delay slots indented).
- kernel func_80008054 (12.35 -> 100): one splat symbol with three entry points; the second entry
  `b`s into the first entry's wait loop, which no C function can do. Addresses are `li`
  expansions (`lui a0,0xA404; ori a0,a0,0x10` then a 0 offset) and the poll loops have nop delays.
- kernel func_80008030 (82.78 -> 100): its 9-word sibling. t0 as the first temp, `move v0,zero`
  plus an unfolded `ori v0,v0,1`, and a nop in the bnez delay; the probe battery in kernel_031b.c
  showed no IDO configuration emits that trio.
- game_libs 6E214 = sqrtf (gu/sqrtf.s, `jr ra; sqrt.s $f0,$f12`): IDO emits the same two words
  from `__builtin_sqrtf` (kit XC), so the decision rests on location: its own 16-byte aligned
  object in the libultra tail, byte-identical to the assembled reference.
- Search that found them: grep the comments of non-exact functions for "handwritten" / `.s`
  references, and scan the target words of every non-exact function for trapping add/sub/addi,
  CP0/cache/TLB, ctc1/cfc1 and k0/k1. The second scan now only hits `break` (division checks)
  and `cfc1/ctc1` (float-to-int conversions), i.e. compiled C. Nothing handwritten is left in the
  non-exact list.

**3. NCC gets bdec's commutative operand order (timproc_b5 BDEC).** The target emits
`mul.s ft1, fs0, ft0` (denom first) and `addu a2, s2, t8` (s2 first); cfe puts the named web second
whatever the source order. The same body under NCC puts both first, like the target, and the head
matches word for word, but edg folds the `(float)255` numerator into the register that already holds
255.0f (`div.s fv1, fs0, fs0`), so the CSE break that cfe allows is lost (92.27, 588 bytes vs 604).
Moving the denom declaration (5 positions), `register`, and late assignment are flat under cfe.

**4. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- timproc_b5 B624 / B368: the target keeps the axis 1.0f in f14 in all three rotate blocks; ours uses
  f14 only in the first (where it is used twice) and ring temps after. A shared `one` local (block or
  function scope), a static const, all 36 orders of the block-2/3 assignments and the 6 orders of
  block 1 are flat or worse.
- mgrproc 1824: target emits `li at,1` after the outer `beqz` (in the case-1 compare block), ours
  hoists it above. `default: break;`, a switch-value local, `+= 1` / `++` spellings, if/else-if and
  goto chains (the goto chain still hoists it) are all flat or worse.
- timproc_b5 CEB4: the then-arm of block 1 is truly empty in the target (`b join` with the join's
  `lw a1` in the delay). Dropping the pre-initialisation and storing 1.0f in the arm, or doing both,
  makes it worse (85.9 / 94.4); the D-load-before-1.0f order in blocks 2/3 does not follow the source.
- game_libs 525F0: a BB boundary between the call and the reload of obj (do-while, switch(0),
  goto label, `if (call) {}`, named result, while/break) does not change ugen's v1 choice.
- game_libs 51448: an NCC lift with the list link as an inline helper still coalesces n with o.
- game_libs 5AFD4: `x + 0xFF000000 - 1` folds to one constant in every spelling (decrement
  statement, pointer arithmetic, `- 1` first, `0xFF << 24`, `/ 16`, negative form) and with IDO 5.3.
- timproc_b5 4118: one-line, comma, chained and reordered case-0 stores, a block pointer and a
  trailing `if (1) {}` leave the per-store reloads; writing the table store last gives 99.17 but
  6884 bytes (target 6872, current 6880), so it was not kept.
- bootup E2D0: nine more arg4 spellings (no keep-live, `arg4 + 1.0f`, temp `k`, volatile read,
  `*&arg4`, early keep-live, address taken) are flat or worse.
- bootup 6204 / E9FC (`lui a0` before `sw ra`): NCC and the flag matrix (7.1 / 5.3 at -O1, -O2,
  -O2 -g3, -O3, -mips1) all give the cfe order.

## kit XCI (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 150): zero-pad symbols folded into predecessors, compound-assign and operand-order sweeps <a name="kit-xci-agent-c-run-150"></a>

**1. An all-zero pad symbol counts as an unmatched function; fold it into the exact predecessor.**
The four zero-only symbols in agent-c's range (game_libs_func_0002266C / 0002D36C, 2 words each,
game_libs_post; game_libs_func_00035E5C 2 words / 0004230C 10 words, game_libs_post0b) each sat
after an exact function. Recipe (64 bytes, 78.157 -> 78.166 % code, no length or layout change):
- delete the pad's `INCLUDE_ASM` line (leave a comment) and `git rm` its `.s`;
- append `PRED=0x00000000,...` (one word per pad word) to the unit's existing
  `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` and `NON_MATCHING_SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` lines (both builds, so the NM object
  length and the post0b clip do not move: 62F08 stays at 0x2e8ec, clip 0x2e93c);
- edit the tracked `expected/` object metadata-only with the new
  `scripts/elf-symtab-delete.py <in.o> <out.o> PAD:PRED ...` -- it deletes PAD (and
  PAD.NON_MATCHING) from `.symtab`, grows PRED by PAD's size, renumbers relocation symbol indices
  and `sh_info`, and refuses if a relocation references the deleted symbol. Check
  `objcopy --only-section=.text` and `objdump -r` are unchanged before installing.
  (`elf-symtab-edit.py` can only resize, and the expected objects of these units are raw-byte
  objects that a C-build copy cannot replace: their `.text` differs at every baked reloc.)
- `rm` both unit objects, `make` (ROM cmp), `make non_matching_objects`, refresh the report: the
  pad rows disappear and PRED stays 100 at the bigger size.
(agent-g run 159 / kit XCII folded the agent-g-range pads independently by rebuilding the one-unit INCLUDE_ASM baseline; the metadata-only symbol delete here avoids that rebuild, which diverged for post0b after 4D084.) Three more pads in agent-g's units were prepared the same way as patches, now superseded by run 159 (post1b 67ABC after
67AA0, post2b_f 75260 after 75254 -- the unit's last word, under TRUNCATE_TEXT 0x388 -- and
ido_75264's `_pad` GLOBAL_ASM sidecar after 75264). Not done: post2b_f 74EDC (6 words at the unit
START: the predecessor is in the previous unit, a cross-unit boundary move) and post1b2c 6E20C
(2 pad words + handwritten sqrtf).

**2. Compound assignment vs expanded form changes FP operand order and colouring.** `c150/casweep.py
SRC UNIT FUNC [ncc]` tries every `L = L op R;` as `L op= R;` and every `L op= R;` as
`L = L op R;`, one site at a time (8 compiles in parallel). Results over 71 non-exact functions:
- gl 3B01C 98.32 -> 98.63: `n.x = n.x * -r` emits `mul.s fd, -r, n.x`; `n.x *= -r` emits the
  target's `mul.s fd, n.x, -r` (all three products).
- gl 36F0C 87.07 -> 87.89: the opposite direction -- `w[1] = w[1] + x` instead of `w[1] += x`.
- 4FD00 76.16 -> 79.39: greedy over 12 `sum[k] += rec[k]` statements (expand sum[0] on all four
  lines and sum[2] on one); two further expansions reach 80.0 but shorten 972 -> 968 (target
  1004), so they were not kept.
- 4F2DC +0.04 (two of three `*=`), 2E354 +0.005 (`sp78 = sp78 * x`).
- 37540: `*=` on two lines scores 76.97 but shortens 760 -> 756 (target 764): not kept.
So the two spellings are not equivalent in cfe/uopt for floats: try both per site.

**3. Operand order of a single commutative operator (`c150/opswap.py`).** Swapping `A * B` /
`A + B` in a `L = A op B;` statement, one site at a time:
- gl 37540 75.93 -> 77.45: `b = K * F(v, 0)` (the scale constant first) plus `z = z + y`.
- 42938 69.60 -> 69.98: `h = two * 240.0f`.
- Tiny or none elsewhere (201B8 +0.004, 2E354 +0.005, NCC 36694 +0.03, not kept).
In 3B01C the operand swap alone (`-r * n.x`) is flat: only the compound form gave the order.

**4. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- gl 250C8 (99.85): fontId's spill shares the temp slot 0x24 in the target; IDO 7.1 -O3 with
  OoT's separate static `AudioLoad_FinishAsyncLoad` (inlined) scores 90.4 (still homes fontId);
  reusing one variable for bytesRemaining and fontId 97.7; ASYNC_ID(...) expressions in place of
  fontId 94.5-96.5.
- gl 45178 (99.99, g's spill 0x24 vs its home 0x28): every named / block-scoped / unnamed /
  padded spelling either keeps 0x28 or grows the frame (an unused int takes a home here).
- gl 4EE44 (a1 vs v0 for the loop base): src spellings, loop-var order, `+=` form: flat.
- gl 39E24 (lui order): a `static` vector gives the target's lui order but lets the scale loads
  hoist above the stores (85.5); a same-object static CSEs the base (63); alias externs worse.
- gl 64388 / game_uso 97EC (NCC return-slot / temp order): member operators, named-return
  helpers, `const float &` factors, explicit temporaries: flat or worse.
- 4D468 (NCC, a3 merge register): real `new (16) E` / out-of-line ctor / shared ternary
  variable: flat or worse.
- 3B01C as an NCC donor with a kit LXXXVIII `sub()` helper: 96.7 at once (chain and bases right,
  frame 0x80 vs 0xC0, pa base not hoisted); cfe stays higher.
- Held-results single-site sweeps (`single.py` / `single2.py`) on the 11 post0b functions that
  timed out in run 149: no gain.

game_libs/game_libs_post.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`. No new donors.

## kit XCIII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 160): parameter home stores, old-pointer walks, index loops, NCC value-class port <a name="kit-xciii-agent-g-run-160"></a>

**1. Parameter home stores tell you which parameters the original used.** IDO (cfe and NCC) stores a register
parameter to its home (`sw aN, frame+4N(sp)` in the prologue) when the parameter is (a) never used, (b) live
across a call, or (c) address-taken / an aggregate; a parameter used only between calls stays in its register.
Probe (`t4.c`): `int f(int a0, int a1, int a2) { return g(a2) + g(a1); }` homes a0 (unused) and a1 (live
across the first call), not a2. So compare the prologue home stores of target and build (`g160/homescan.py`
lists every non-exact function where the two sets differ):
- **Build homes a parameter the target does not, and the body has an empty test on it** (`if (arg0) {}` after
  calls): the test keeps the parameter live across the calls and forces the home + reload. gui 2DE0: the
  target reads `lw t0,16(a0)` straight off a0, never `sw a0,104(sp)`; moving the two empty tests to x0 (homed
  in the target anyway) gives 88.75 -> 89.83. It costs two words (300 -> 298 of 303); the two missing words
  are the target's s0 save / restore, the known ring-context residual of this family (329C / 3714 too).
  timproc_b5 8FC8 has the same symptom (a0 homed by its two `if (arg0) {}`), but substituting arg1 / arg2
  or dropping the tests scores lower (86.64 -> 86.63 at best): there the tests are load-bearing elsewhere.
- **The same test can be the cause of an extra caller-saved spill pair.** timproc_b3 13B8 and its twin arcproc
  16F4 (timer HUD, like b1 1340) ended with `draw(..., sp138); if (arg1) {}`: the test kept arg1 live across
  the tail calls and added a `sw tN,156(sp); jal; lw tN,156(sp)` pair the target does not have. Dropping it:
  85.41 -> 86.46 on both, 688 -> 684 of 680 bytes. A scratch sweep that removes each parameter empty test of
  every agent-g NM body (27 cfe sites, 10 NCC sites) found nothing else except one of the two `if (1) {}` in
  3558's getPos (72.58 -> 72.74).
- **Build homes an UNUSED parameter the target does not**: the original used it, typically reused as a local.
  gl 6126C (mini printf: `(char *buf, int arg1, FI val, int arg3, u8 *fmt)`): the target homes a2 / a3 (val is
  read from 72(sp) as int and float; a3 is stored and never read) but not a1. Reusing arg1 as the format
  character `c` removes the a1 store at the target length (83.47 -> 83.89). A union-with-double / 8-byte
  struct / f64 / long long val, ANSI `...` and K&R `va_alist` signatures all keep homing a1 (a K&R va_alist
  function homes every register from va_alist on, agent-g run 127, gl 51ED8).

**2. `q = p, p = q + 1, *q` is the target's post-increment through a copy.** When the target walks a pointer
held in an s-register as `or v0,s2,zero; lbu t9,0(v0); addiu s2,s2,1` (load through a COPY of the old pointer,
bump afterwards), `*p++` gives `lbu t9,0(s2); addiu s2,s2,1` (no copy). Writing the read as
`(q = p, p = q + 1, *q)` with a pointer local q reproduces the copy (probe `t3.c`). In 6126C the target uses the
copy form at all four reads, but only the first and the width-digit reads keep the body at the target length
(per-site sweep, 16 x 3 variants with `xargs -P 12`); all four give 85.11 at 500 vs 492 bytes. Also: the walk
is over the fmt PARAMETER itself (target `lw s2,80(sp)` and no copy into a second register), not a local
copy (83.02 -> 83.07).

**3. An index loop keeps the count live: the t-register "spill around every call" is the original loop
bound.** timproc_b1 1340 (timer HUD glyph loop): the target holds `count` in t1 and stores / reloads it at
sp+152 around every call inside the loop although the loop test uses `s1 != s4` (i*13 vs count*13). That is
`for (i = 0; i < count; i++) { ... buf[i] ... pos6 + i * 13 ... }`: uopt strength-reduces i*13 and buf+i and
rewrites the test (LFTR), but keeps the original count web alive in a caller-saved register. The m2c
pointer walk (`do { ... p++; xp += 13; i += 13; } while (i != bound)`) has no such web: 85.58 -> 85.69, 229 ->
233 of 238 words. A dead volatile pad was dropped to keep the frame at 336.
`g160/tspill.py` lists functions where target and build disagree on such `sw tN,K(sp); jal; lw tN,K(sp)`
pairs. mgrproc 23FC is the SAME glyph loop (target: i*13 counter t0 @56, bound t1 @48, count t2 @84, all
spilled around the call), but there the index form gives the count an s-register (s3, arg0 pushed to s4):
97.25 -> 92.53 at the same length, not kept. The count only stays in a t-register when no callee-saved
register is free for it.

**4. cfe C that emulates C++ -> an NCC value-class donor (game_uso 3558, 72.33 -> 72.58, 246 -> 251 of 252
words).** The cfe NM body had Tri3i word copies (`*(Tri3i *)buf = *(Tri3i *)(s0 + 0x68)`), pad arrays and
"marshalling chains". Rewritten as C++ (`game_uso_ncc_3558_nm.cpp`): `Vec3` with a BY-VALUE `operator=(Vec3 v)`
(word copy into the param temp at sp+140, then float stores), an `operator-` with a NAMED return (r at sp+104 ->
return temp -> binding temp sp+76 -> e, exactly the target's chain), an `M4::getPos(Vec3 &)` (gives the target's
`lwc1 160(v0); addiu v0,v0,112; lwc1 52/56(v0)` base adjust), and the rotated triple held in the dead mag / t /
k (kit LXXXVI) which brings back the sp+40/44 FP juggle. Notes: an unused `Vec3 pad1;` (non-POD, user ctor) DOES
keep a frame slot under NCC (unused float arrays do not); NCC const-propagated every zero spelling (literal,
double literal, named float, ctor temp) into per-site `mtc1`, so the target's single $f20 zero (sdc1 save)
is not reproduced; explicit `vb.x = vb.x + stage.x` statements (instead of the reference `operator+=`) lose
the juggle entirely (58.7), as does a member `rotate()` with its own locals (57.9).
**The else-branch `w *= 0` must be a DOUBLE literal under NCC too** (`w *= 0.0;` through `operator*=(float)`):
a float zero (`0.0f`, a named float) lets uopt fold the three products into plain zero stores, the double
literal keeps the target's three `mul.s fN,fN,zero-reg` (72.74 -> 75.62). The muls are verified target words but
the body overshoots (1004 -> 1024 of 1008 bytes; the extra words are in the d / e chain and the missing
$f20 hold), so the step is flagged. Double literals for the side / w.y zeros change nothing under NCC.

**5. cfe homes follow declaration order, but objdiff fuzzy ignores sp offsets.** bootup B75C (frame 208 vs
120): folding m2c families and inlining single-read temps shrinks the frame 208 -> 144 with IDENTICAL fuzzy,
and moving a declaration moves the homes (a f64 declared before sp60 pushes it 12 bytes down) again with
identical fuzzy. Frame / home work only pays when the function is otherwise exact. The m2c names
(`sp6C`, `sp60`, `sp28`, `sp1C`) are the target offsets, so the target layout is: sp6C, 2 words, sp60, sp5C,
sp58, sp54, 10 words, sp28, sp24, sp1C. The real gain in B75C: the second `0x974` statement reloads the field
(`swc1; lwc1 2420(a3)` back to back in the target): a volatile read there gives the reload, 90.26 -> 90.97,
520 -> 522 of 524 words.

**Negatives (time-boxed).**
- game_uso 7C1C: the cfe-in-C++ lift with `p = 0; if (1) { p = &X; }` constructs rewritten as a real
  `XZ(float, float) : Vec3(a, 0.0f, c)` constructor (edg `this == 0 -> operator new` protocol, 14 sites):
  92.25 -> 91.27, frame 872 vs target 944. The target materialises the `this` of the NEXT two constructs
  (`addiu a1,sp,320` / `addiu a2,sp,308`) before the current one and spills them around the alloc call; no
  spelling found. timproc_b5 8FC8's `blez` loop guards on a just-stored literal count remain (agent-h notes).
- gl 5AFD4: the `(diff >> 4) + 0xFF000000 - 1` fold survives 16 more spellings (parameter reuse `a2 =
  0xFF000000`, named int, `| ` instead of `+`, unsigned `-1U`, `+ 0xFFFFFFFF`, seven pointer-arithmetic forms).
- timproc_b5 DF14: the per-site df14_ee6c symbols let the scheduler hoist the flag loads above the stores
  (target: load after each store); one shared symbol or volatile stores score lower (92.9 / 94.0 vs 95.2).
- gui F04 / 329C / 3714: remaining rows are scheduling and the s0 ring-context colour.
- Old-pointer-copy scan (`g160/walkscan4.py`, any register): beyond 6126C the only hits are agent-c units:
  gl 3B2EC 88.94 -> 89.80 and 3BE1C 76.33 -> 77.02 (`while ((lq = lp, lp = lq + 1, i = *lq) != -1)`), gl 46050
  82.45 -> 82.88 (both string reads), all with the length moving toward the target; handed over as patches
  (post0b NM clip +0x10 / +0x8, together 0x2e93c -> 0x2e954). Gotcha: a Makefile-only clip change does not
  rebuild build/non_matching/.../game_libs_post0b.c.o -- delete that object (62F08 drops to 80 otherwise).
- Sibling scan rerun (`scripts/sibling-scan.py --min 0.6 --exact-only`): no new template for agent-g units;
  hits are agent-c post0b < 0x50000 (3E0F0, 41D40, 488A0, 4AFB4, 4EE44, 4FBA4) or already-known (51448, 525F0,
  5AFD4, 32C8).

Purge: `build/{,non_matching/}src/timproc_uso_b1/timproc_uso_b1.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_uso/game_uso.c.o`,
`build/{,non_matching/}src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/gui_uso/gui_uso.c.o`,
`build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`, `build/{,non_matching/}src/timproc_uso_b3/timproc_uso_b3.c.o`,
`build/{,non_matching/}src/arcproc_uso/arcproc_uso_tail1.c.o`; new NM donor `build/src/game_uso/game_uso_ncc_3558_nm.cpp.o`;
changed NM donor `build/src/gui_uso/gui_uso_ncc_2DE0_nm.cpp.o`.

## kit XCIV (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 151): else-arm constants, inline iterators, unsigned conversions <a name="kit-xciv-agent-c-run-151"></a>

**Summary.** Structural pass over agent-c's mid band (no regalloc sweeps). Ten NM gains confirmed in report.json, all
from decode/shape fixes read off the target; no exact. Scripts in the run-151 scratchpad (`side.py`, `frep.py`,
`b1scan.py`, `guardscan.py`) are described below so they can be rewritten in a minute.

**1. The else-arm constant: `b .+8` is a fingerprint.** IDO compiles

    x = K;  if (c) { ...; x = v; }          /* m2c / "pre-assign" form */
    if (c) { ...; x = v; } else { x = K; }   /* else-arm form */

differently. In the else-arm form uopt hoists `x = K` above the compare (often into the branch delay slot or just before
`slt`) and the then-arm ends with an unconditional `b join` whose target is the very next instruction after its delay
slot -- the word `0x10000001` (`beqz zero, .+8`). The pre-assign form falls through and has no such word. m2c always
prints the pre-assign form. So: count `0x10000001` per function in the expected object and in the NM build
(`b1scan.py`: objdump both `.text`s, split by symbol, compare counts); every extra one in the target marks an if/else to
restore. Hits this run:
- gl 4B620 / 48AEC / 41D40 / 454C4: the iterator advance `cur = 0; if (i < n) { i++; cur = &p[i]; }` is
  `if (i < n) { ...; cur = &p[i]; } else { cur = 0; }` (often only ONE of the two advance sites -- score each);
- gl 3BE1C / 3B2EC (twins): the grid cell index (`else cell = -1`) in one, the list pointer (`else list = 0`) in the
  other -- the twins take opposite picks;
- gl 493AC: the remap pick `j = i; if (tbl) j = tbl[i];` -> `if (tbl) j = tbl[i]; else j = i;` (+0.74);
- gl 2E354: the 8 / 0x40 pick. A ternary `v = c ? a : b` compiles like the pre-assign form here.
Not every hit pays: 4FD00's tail `ret` (target `b .+8; li v0,1`) and 33BE4's chunk clamp score lower or move the length
away from the target, so keep only scored gains (454C4's `n = cnt; if (cnt <= 0) n = 1;` gains +1.0 but leaves the
exact length; 3BE1C's s16 MAXS / MINS ternaries in every operand order, or as statements, are flat or worse).

**2. C++ inline iterator (cfront) kit** -- the post0b constructor family (4B620, 48AEC, 493AC, 41D40):
- the dead `this == 0 -> alloc(0xC)` guard of a stack-constructed iterator survives behind `p = 0; if (1) { p = &it; }`
  (kit LXIV (d)); the older `p = &it; if (0) { f(&p); }` spelling also keeps the guard but HOMES p (an extra
  `sw p,96(sp)` / reload in 48AEC, 2016 -> 2052 bytes once removed);
- the ctor reads `end` through the list pointer it just stored: `coll = self + 0x84; it->list = coll;
  it->end = ((s32 *)coll)[3] - 1;` (target `addiu v0,v0,132; ...; lw t3,12(v0)`), not `self->0x90`;
- each element read of one statement is a separate add: the target CSEs `i * 4` (held in one register) but re-adds
  `base + i*4` per read. Two reads with the SAME spelling CSE into one; write them with different spellings
  (`(*p)[i]` and `*(s32 *)((char *)*p + i * 4)`). 4B620 +3.6, 48AEC +2.9 (three reads per node, best = three spellings).
- copies of the by-value iterator: declaration order sets the stack order (41D40 target: ctor temp lowest, walked copy
  highest -> declare `c, b, a`).

**3. Unsigned conversions.** m2c spells `(f32)(u32)x` as `f = (f32)x; if (x < 0) f += 4294967296.0f;`. IDO compiles the
spelled-out form with a second `bgez` / `mov.s` pair; `(f32)(u32)x` gives the target's single `bgez; cvt.s.w; lui
0x4f80; add.s` (2E354: two sites, +2.9, 3724 -> 3692 bytes). Grep m2c-lifted bodies for `4294967296`.

**4. Small decode fixes read from the target.**
- negating an `s8` temp re-sign-extends (`negu; sll 24; sra 24`); the target's bare `negu` means an int temp (2E354).
- a 3-way pick whose target shows `bnel` + a dead duplicate of the default constant after the `b` is
  `if (a) v = A; else { v = DEF; if (b) v = B; }` (2E354).
- vtable this-adjust deltas are `s16` (`lh 0x60(vt)`), not words; a value re-read after a vcall in the target (no sp
  spill) must be re-read in C; `*(T *)0x254` absolute reads in old m2c bodies are `&D_00000000 + 0x254` (target
  `lui/addiu; lw 596(r)`) -- 469A8, +2.7, though its length moved away from the target (380 vs 384, target 412: the
  removed spill pair was wrong, the remaining gap is elsewhere).
- a context read through `&D_00000000 + K` shares a held `lui/addiu` base with every other `&D_00000000` use; when the
  target re-emits `lui; lw K(r)` give the read its own zero-pinned alias (493AC: `D_493AC_d`, +3.0 -- the shared base had
  pushed `&rec` and a constant 1 into s7 / s8).
- a `char *volatile` local that m2c-era decodes used to keep a pointer homed is re-read at EVERY use; when the target
  reads the home once and takes all fields off one register, copy it into a plain local first (36F0C: the 3x3 rotate,
  `m = sp84;` then nine `m->...` reads, +3.4, 984 -> 956 bytes, target 968).
- an `&D_00000000 + 0x254` fix that the report scores flat (43D38: report.json treats the absolute and the symbol form the
  same) is not kept: sc.sh-style scratch scores and report.json disagree on reloc-only changes, confirm in the report.

**5. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- sibling-scan at 0.6 (exact partners only): no new template in agent-c's range (41D40 / 4E244, 4FBA4 / 4F85C,
  488A0 / 483BC, 525F0 / 3E904 were all tried in kit LXXXIII).
- 2E354 switch-4 per-arm recomputes (`andi` in each arm in the target): 64 per-arm expression combos all give the same
  merged code at +8 bytes; the odd-case chain as a `switch` scores 88.79 but is 4 bytes over the target length.
- 30AF4 case-5 constants 13 / 14 / 16 held in registers: still const-propagated whatever the spelling.
- 46050: the char dispatch as a switch (outer or inner) loses 3.4.
- 4BAF4: the bounds test re-reads `0xB8` / `0xBC` per compare in the target but CSEs `0xC0` / `0xC4`; `int` / `s32` /
  `long` / array spellings of the re-read all compile identically.
- 454C4: the `elem` / `elem2` copy web (target keeps both), copy inside the loop body / block-local copy: flat; colour
  product operand order: flat (IDO canonicalises).
- 49B3C advance forms: flat.
- 4FBA4: the target keeps the outer `obj` in a2 with sp+48 spills around the four ctor calls and copies it to s0 for
  the loop; a separate `res = obj` web (also with `return obj`) is copy-coalesced back: flat.
- 3B6A0: `while (inside && (fp += 2, tp != end))` moves the increment into the `bne` slot as in the target and scores

- 4C5E4: `* (f32)2` -> `* 2.0f` (target mul.s by 2.0 where ours emits add.s x,x) scores lower.
- branch-likely count scan (`likely.py`, the same idea as `b1scan.py` for bnel/beql/bc1tl/...): the cell family

## kit XCV (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 152): loop-condition increments, post-increment appends, NCC re-lifts <a name="kit-xcv-agent-c-run-152"></a>

**Summary.** Structural pass over agent-c's mid band (post / post0b below 0x50000). Eleven NM gains confirmed in
report.json (table in the index entry); no exact, no exact lost. Every gain below was scored by rebuilding the NM unit
and running `objdiff-cli report generate`; the quick difflib scorer (instruction-string ratio) disagreed with the report
in both directions several times (493AC NCC: scratch "full" lower, report +1.6; 4B620 frame moves: scratch flat), so
only report numbers are quoted.

**1. Increment in the loop condition = the `bne` delay slot.** The cell family's edge walk ends in the target with

    beqz  ok, exit        ; nop
    bne   nx, end, top    ; addiu fv, fv, 2      <- the increment sits in the back-edge delay slot

while `do { ...; fv++; } while (ok && nx != end);` puts `fv++` in the `beqz` delay slot and closes the loop with a
`bnel` whose slot is a copy of the loop's first instruction. Writing the increment inside the condition,
`} while (ok && (fv++, nx != end));`, gives the target shape: 3B9C0 (NCC donor) 75.15 -> 76.55, 3BE1C (cfe)
76.69 -> 77.31, 3B6A0 (NCC donor, `fp += 2`) 70.94 -> 72.22 (kit XCIV had this one flat; re-measured here in the report
with a fresh donor .o, it pays). 3B2EC, whose walk ends in `break` instead of an `ok` flag
(`nx++; } while (fv++, nx != end)`): flat. Count branch-likely words per function (target vs NM build) to find these:
an extra `bnel` / `bnezl` back edge in the build is the tell.

**2. `list[n++] = v` vs `list[n] = v; n = n + 1;` with an s16 counter.** The target (4A890) copies the OLD counter
into a fresh register with its own `sll 16 / sra 16` before indexing, then increments and re-truncates the counter
separately. Only the post-increment spelling gives that; the split statement indexes with the counter itself. Under the
NCC donor this plus walking `arg2` itself (no `p` copy), no `cnt` copy around the overflow call and no parameter empty
tests took 4A890 from 81 to 86 of 88 words, 68.64 -> 86.41. An `int` counter with explicit `(s16)` casts compiles like
the split form.

**3. NCC re-lifts after decode changes.** The run-134 sweep (kit LVI) chose cfe or NCC per function on the bodies of
that day. Bodies that changed since can flip: 46050 (with item 5's then-arm fix) 84.31 cfe -> 86.48 NCC, and 493AC
90.60 -> 92.20 under NCC with no source change. NCC colours the 46050 DL-packet temps `_q` / `_n` v0 / a1 as the target
does (the residual the old comment blamed on cfe). Losers in the same report test (keep cfe): 41D40 92.99 -> 92.84,
3BE1C 77.31 -> 71.34, 3B2EC 89.45 -> 83.16, 412E8 88.11 -> 85.45, 41820 94.72 flat, 454C4 63.85 -> 63.78, 48AEC
88.11 -> 87.90, 2E354 much lower. Recipe that compiles most bodies: the NM preamble's typedefs and macros, every
`extern f();` turned into `extern f(...);` inside one `extern "C" {}` block, `extern "C"` on the definition,
function-pointer casts `(void (*)())` -> `(void (*)(...))`. Bodies with int <-> pointer assignments (36F0C, 469A8,
40070, 4B620) need casts first. Beware the `(...)` prototypes when float arguments are passed (default promotion to
double); prototype those callees exactly.

**4. In NCC, a cursor copy survives.** 46050's target reads each character through a copy (`or v1,s3; lbu a1,0(v1);
addiu s3,s3,1`). Under cfe the copy was propagated away (the old comment); under NCC `{ u8 *p = arg1; arg1 = p + 1;
ch = *p; }` keeps it, at both the entry read and the loop-bottom read: 86.48 -> 86.91, +2 words toward the target.

**5. Then-arm placement.** The target falls through into the display-list EMIT path and jumps out of line to the
measure call; the decode had `if (flag != 0) call; else EMIT;`. Writing `if (flag == 0) { EMIT } else call;` is the
target layout (cfe 82.45 -> 84.31, 4 bytes away from the target length, flagged; the NCC donor carries it).

**6. if/else orientation = which value is hoisted.** Kit XCIV's `b .+8` tell says an if/else exists; the target also says
which arm is the else: the else-arm value is the one hoisted above the compare. 454C4's clamp is `or v0,s2; bgtz s2,
join; ...; b .+8; li v0,1`, so the hoisted `cnt` is the else arm: `if (cnt <= 0) n = 1; else n = cnt;` 62.81 -> 63.85
(the reverse orientation 63.32). The pre-assign form also let uopt rewrite `cnt <= 0` as `cnt * 2 + 0x86 < 136` off a
held packet word, which spilled across a call. FLAG: 2028 -> 2020 bytes, away from the target length. The elem advance
of the same loop as if/else: 62.55 (lower, not kept). 334E8's chunk clamp `if (avail < rem) chunk = avail; else chunk =
rem;` 73.71 -> 73.14 (not kept); 3B2EC's cell index as if/else 89.45 -> 85.06 (not kept, as in kit XCIV).

**7. Per-arm truncation.** 2E354's switch 4 recomputes `andi a2,v0,0xff` in each arm. With every arm written as
`rv & 0xFF` uopt reuses one CSE'd value (`or a2,a1` copies); writing the arms through the `u8` copy of `rv`
(`var_t9 = var_v0_2;`, `var_v0_2 + 1`) gives the per-arm `andi`. With the odd-case chain as a real 4-way switch (target
`b .+8` case-1 arm) 88.24 -> 89.28 (FLAG: 3684 -> 3696 bytes, away from the target). The odd-case switch alone was +0.55
in kit XCIV and rejected for length; here the two together are kept and flagged.

**8. Read a field after the call when the target does.** 2E354 read `arg0->0` before the 1C290 call (m2c statement
order) and spilled it across the call (`swc1 f2,112(sp)` in the jal slot); the target loads it after the jal. Moving
the statement below the call: 89.28 -> 89.49, -2 words toward the target. Tell: a `sw` / `swc1` in a jal delay slot
reloaded right after the call in the build, absent in the target (a 10-line scan over both objects lists them).

**9. A DL macro's block-scope locals cost frame words per expansion.** 4B620's `DL_APPEND` was a `do {} while (0)` with
four block-scope locals, expanded 9 times: frame 264 (target 176). With all four at function scope the frame is 136;
`_dl` / `_h` at function scope and `_n` / `_cmd` block-local put `it3` at the target's sp+164 (frame 200): 94.41 ->
94.48. Declaring the three iterators in reverse order moves `it3` to the top of the locals (as in 41D40); scored flat.
The remaining 4B620 gap is the target's s4.

**10. One variable for two roles (469A8).** The target copies the first vcall's result into s0 (`or s0,v0`) and later
loads the second vtable into s0: one variable in the original. Reusing `temp_s0` for both: 67.64 -> 67.81, 380 -> 392
bytes toward 412. The held `self + 0x100` / `+ 0x78` pointers still fold into offsets.

**10b. Re-read an address-taken struct where the target reloads it (3B2EC).** p is memory-resident (`if (1) { V3B2 *pp
= &p; }`); after `p.x = x; p.z = z;` the target computes the grid cell from RELOADED copies (`lwc1 f8,140(sp)`,
`lwc1 f18,148(sp)`) while `p.x` in C forwards the stored register. `(&p)->x` still forwards; `((f32 *)&p)[2]` reloads.
Both reads as `((f32 *)&p)[0]` / `[2]`: 89.45 -> 91.56, 920 -> 928 bytes toward 940. The twin 3BE1C keeps p.x in a
register in the target (no reload) -- check the target before applying.

**11. Negatives.**
- 41D40: the loop as `if (r) do { ... } while (r2)` with separate first / in-loop result variables gives the target's
  two `b .+8` arms and non-s-register results but loses the s2-held string address: 92.99 -> 92.64 (404 bytes, away).
- 3B6A0 frame (target 128, NCC 64): `f32 pad[16]; pad[0] = 0;` (kit LVI) does not grow the frame of a LEAF function;
  neither does a volatile array or a referenced char array.
- 46050 dispatch as a switch: under NCC the switch is laid out exactly as the target (tests in source order 10, 9, 48,
  bodies out of line, `beql` for 48) but the case constants are immediates, where the target holds 48 / 9 / 10 and
  `&margin` in s7 / s6 / s5 / s8: 85.05 vs 86.48 for the if-chain. `goto` chains are re-linearised. `margin` as
  `register`, reference or inline symbol: identical code.
- 46050 NCC: `_e` at function scope is far worse (19.8 scratch); dropping `if (charw) {}` or either `if (1) {}`: lower.
- 307A8: one alias for the two zero stores (target shares one `lui at`) makes uopt hold the base (95.31); a chained
  `a = b = 0` likewise (95.43).
- 3D71C: a local for the copy destination, or a source-pointer local declared first: identical code (as1 order).
- 2E354: switch-1 value through the named `sp58` gives the target's home slot but scores flat; NCC lift much lower.
- 3B6A0 (NCC donor): the target homes all four argument registers and re-reads o / max / outd / outp from 128..140(sp);
  forcing homes with `if (1) { T *q = &param; }` escapes scores lower (o: 70.65, max: 69.51, all four lower still).
  Dropping either parameter empty test (`if (max) {}` 70.68, `if (pt) {}` 72.17) also loses.
- 3B9C0 without its two `if (self) {}` tests: 71.99. 4A890 with the `cnt` copy back (80.41) or without `sz` (86.36).
- 48AEC: a local for the held `&D_i + 0x3C8A0` 88.10; per-branch block-local packet variables (the target's two
  branches spill gctx / cmd / disp to different homes) +0.06 with the frame 32 bytes further from the target (not kept).
- 4E424: a new `dy` with `y0` reused for the larger value 87.51; 3BE1C list pointer as if/else 76.98 (on the new
  baseline); 4FD00 tail as if/else 78.0; 4B620 iterator order `it2, it, it3` and 469A8 bit-test order: flat.
- 30AF4 case-5 13 / 14 / 16 register constants and 48AEC's held `&D + 0x3C8A0` / spilled `gctx`: not attempted further.

`build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_493AC_nm.cpp.o`, changed donors `game_libs_ncc_4A890_nm.cpp.o`,

## kit XCVI (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 153): argument-register counts, NCC scalar homes, 578B4 frame + gbi layout <a name="kit-xcvi-agent-c-run-153"></a>

**Summary.** Big near-exact pass over gl 578B4 / 201B8 / 49DBC. One exact (gl_func_00049DBC, 1356 bytes, NCC donor;
78.30 -> 78.47 % code); NM gains 578B4 97.76 -> 98.27 and 201B8 97.86 -> 97.94 (report.json). All numbers below are
report.json or objdiff one-shot (`objdiff-cli diff -1 expected.o -2 build.o -o - SYM`, read `left.symbols[].match_percent`);
the one-shot form scores reloc-carrying donors < 100 even when the report says 100, so use it only for deltas.

**1. Count the argument registers the target sets (decode, both functions).** A call whose arm in the target loads only
a0/a1 takes TWO arguments, whatever m2c wrote:
- 49DBC tail: `beqz arg1, L; lui a2,0` then `lw a0; jal; addiu a1,sp,80` -- the lone `lui a2` (no `addiu`) is the
  else-arm's `&sym` hoisted into the beqz delay slot (harmless on the fall path because a2 is dead there), so the arg1
  path is `return f(arg2, &sp50);`. The NM body passed a third `&D` and kept a2 live.
- 578B4 switch-2 default: the target sets a0/a1 only; passing `var_a2` as arg 3 kept var_a2 live across the 34458 call in
  its home (`sw a2,276(sp)` + `lw a2,276(sp)` = the 2-word length excess). Two args: 2421 -> 2419 words = target.
K&R callees (gl_func_00034458 / gl_func_00000000) accept any count, so this is free to try. Tell: a call in the build
that loads one more aN than the target's, or a `lui` without its `addiu` in a delay slot.

**2. Two DISTINCT base-0 symbols when the target materialises the same address twice.** 49DBC's else call has
`lui a3; addiu a3` AND `lui a2 ... addiu a2` (in the jal delay): one `&D_00000000` for both makes uopt CSE a3 = a2
(`or a3,a2,zero`). New pins `gl_d_49dbc_t2` / `gl_d_49dbc_t3` (= 0).

**3. NCC: every named scalar local takes a frame home BELOW the arrays.** Under NCC the address-taken arrays/structs
are laid out top-down in declaration order from the frame top, and the named scalar locals (even ones that live in
registers: `temp_s1`, `temp_v0_2`, `temp_v1`, `base`) get homes underneath them. 49DBC's long-standing "sp38 at 68,
target 56" residual: removing all four named scalars (inline the expressions; edg CSEs them back) and widening the
colour scratch `u8 sp38[11]` -> `u8 sp38[24]` (the 24-byte gap up to sp50) lands sp38 at sp+0x38 with frame 0xB0. An
unused declared local does NOTHING under NCC (edg drops it) -- unlike cfe (kit XXVII). Also dropped the old
`if (arg2) {}` empty test: with the two-arg call it was the last length word.

**4. m2c spXXX names restore frame homes dropped by a phi merge (578B4).** Run 152 merged six var_t0 phis into one
variable (fuzzy up) but the frame shrank 496 -> 472, shifting every upper home by 24. Mapping (target slot, build slot)
pairs from aligned `N(sp)` operands (`slots.py`) showed which named homes were missing; the spXXX names say where:
4 pads between sp118 and spFC, 1 before spF0, 1 before sp50 (unused `s32` locals keep their homes in cfe). The four
switch-1 arm DL pointers must live in their OWN named homes across the 34458 call (`sp1A8 = ...; FW(sp1A8,0)=..;
FW(sp1A8,4)=call(..)` instead of a shared temp_t1_3 copied into a dead spXX), with sp1A8 declared right after
temp_t1_3 so it lands at sp+0x1A8. 97.73 -> 97.86.

**5. 578B4 gbi spelling levers (each greedy, per site).**
- Both LOADTILE `gDPSetTile` packets on ONE line, w0 then w1 (`FW(p,0)=0xF5000100; FW(p,4)=0x07000000;`): target
  `lui t7,0xf500; lui t6,0x700; ori; sw 0; sw 4`. Split lines (either order) or w1-first on one line do not give it.
- `(uls + width) - uls` with uls read twice (`FW(sp1DC,4) + lh) - FW(sp1DC,4)`) instead of through a variable (w /
  temp_a0_6): the target's `addu t, uls, width` operand order (10 of 12 sites kept). Operand swaps of the source `+`
  are inert here (cfe canonicalises var + load).
- s2_110's SetTile w1 was leaf-first; chain-first like its siblings fixes the scheduling (mnemonics) but leaves the
  final `or` leaf-first; `(u32)(u16)(lh & 0xF)` for the 0x2C leaf fixes that `or` at s2_110 and one more site (others
  regress: context-dependent, sweep it).
- Negatives: `(u32)` casts around the 2E term, gbi-faithful `_SHIFTL` spelling of the whole w1 (97.54), TILESIZE w1
  in gbi order `tile | lrs<<12 | lrt` (-0.3 to -1.7 per site), adjacent-statement join sweep over the first ~3/4 of the body (s1 arms through s2_408; 0 keeps),
  variable identity of temp_t1_7 in s1_508 (inert).
- More 578B4 negatives (late in the run): moving / joining `temp_t1_7 = FW(sp1DC, 0x0)` (inert); a final-`or` rewrite at
  the s2_120 SetTile w1 through a temp variable, plain `|`, `(s16)` / `(u8)` / `*(u16 *)` leaves (all lower); toggling
  chain/leaf order on each of the 10 SetTile w1 lines (all lower); `(u32)`-grouped TILESIZE w1 in either order (-1 to
  -2); `if (1) {}` after each switch-2 `temp_t2 = ...` (lower); all 24 orders of the temp_t2..t5 statements (inert --
  cfe CSEs them). 201B8: an `if (1) {}` after every statement (lower or inert) and void aliases on the three discarded
  calls (inert); `sub->cur = 0; v = 0;` respelled as a chain / reversed / via v (all 95.98, -1.8).

**6. 578B4 diff-region classification for whoever continues (98.27, 2419/2419 words, frame 496 = target).**
_SUPERSEDED by [kit XCVII](#kit-xcvii-agent-c-run-154): the function is C++; under NCC every item below except the s2_508 ra/t0 pair is fixed. Map kept for the cfe body only._
Structural: only two left -- 0x18e0-0x191c (s2_110 w1: the 2C `lh` scheduled one slot late + the last `or` order) and
0x1dcc (one `or` operand order). Everything else is register colour/ring:
- 12 `addu t,a0,tN` vs `addu t,tN,a0` / `or t,ra,tN` vs `or t,tN,ra` operand-order words in the switch-1 arms
  (0x1a4..0x1208): the TILESIZE w1 `0x07000000 | A | B` evaluates B first in the target; spelling changes so far move
  other code.
- t0/t1 web swaps at the head of s1_508 / s2_508 (0xe5c, 0x2158: temp_t1_7 = `lw t1,0(a2)` in the target, t0 in the
  build; a DL pointer takes the other) -- not variable identity.
- t6..t9 ring-parity cascades starting at each SetTile w1 final `or` whose operand order differs (0x136c, 0x1d30,
  0x2378): a flipped last `or` frees registers in the other order, and every following statement is renamed until the
  next flip. Fixing those three `or`s is the highest-value remaining item (~400 of the ~535 register words).
- `lw ra,504(sp)` vs `lw t0,504(sp)` (arg2 reloads) in s2 arms follow the same cascades.

**7. 201B8 (cfe).** The mode switch arms are `cfg = ..;` then `tbl = ..;` on SEPARATE lines (target `lui a3; lui t2;
addiu a3; b; addiu t2`; one line or tbl-first reorders the pairs), and both `r[0] + r[2]` sums are written `r[2] + r[0]`
(the load order mirrors). 97.86 -> 97.94. Negatives: v=1 (`sub->cur = v = 1`) still reuses the held t1 = 1 -- `v = 1;
sub->cur = v`, `1U`, char literal, `mode == 1U` (keeps t1, -0.6), `switch ((unsigned)mode)` (-2), v as s16/u16/u8/
unsigned (all worse); st0 ternary / single-assignment forms (-0.3 / flat); an NCC lift of the body is 90.2 (cfe it is).

**8. 5A2C4.** Held colour results (`cr = (u32)(fr * 255.0f)` ... then colv[] and the rgba pack from cr/cg/cb, plain or
chained assignment) compile byte-identical to the inline form -- cfe already CSEs them; the frame 0xD0 vs 0xC0 residual
is not a held-results case. 42938 not reached.

**Gate.** Full make ROM byte-identical, `make verify-blocks` 6/6 OK, `make non_matching_objects` 0 errors, no exact
lost vs origin/main 8b0b3e212, sentinels 551E0 / 55B10 / EBC8 / C5B0 / 62F08 at 100, 78.47 % code. post0b NM clip
0x2e9c4 -> 0x2e9bc (62F08 NM offset 0x2e96c). New pins: `gl_d_49dbc_t2`, `gl_d_49dbc_t3`, `gl_func_00000000_49DBCv`.

## kit XCVII (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 154): 578B4 under NCC -- source-order `|` chains, referenced-pad homes, packet-pointer identity <a name="kit-xcvii-agent-c-run-154"></a>

**Summary.** gl_func_000578B4 (9676 bytes, the gbi texture loader) was carried to 98.27 as a cfe body with dozens of
operand-order hacks. agent-g's run-113 note said it is C++; porting the CURRENT cfe body (not agent-g's macro draft)
to IDO 7.1 NCC took it to 99.95 one-shot / **99.9855 report.json** in about 25 minutes, with the same 2419 words. Wired as
an NM-only donor (`src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_578B4_nm.cpp`, `GAMELIBS_578B4_NM_DONOR`); 7 words left, so no exact.
Code % unchanged (78.47); no exact lost; ROM byte-identical; verify-blocks 6/6; post0b NM clip unchanged 0x2e9bc.

**1. Mechanical cfe -> NCC port recipe (works for any m2c-style body).**
- Header: the s8..f32 typedefs, the `FW` macro, an `extern "C" { ... }` block with every callee as `int f(...);` and the
  base-0 symbols, then `extern "C"` before the function line. Copy the body verbatim.
- edg rejects int -> pointer assignment (`ptr = FW(..)`, error 3611). A 20-line script that reads the error line and
  caret column and wraps the right-hand side in `(T)(...)` fixed all 192 sites in two passes (casts are codegen-inert).
- Frame: NCC drops locals that are never referenced but gives a frame home to every referenced one in declaration
  order (kit XCVI 3). The cfe body relies on unused pads/temps holding homes, so list every local referenced once
  (only its declaration) and reference it with one dead line after the declarations (`p = 0; temp_a2 = 0; ...`). That
  alone took the frame from 0x148 to the target 0x1F0 with every m2c `spXXX` at its own offset. Declared-but-unused
  `volatile` pads are dropped too (they need the line as well).
- Score raw first (here 91.5 before any spelling change, with frame and length right): the remaining diffs are the
  front-end-specific spellings the cfe passes tuned.

**2. edg evaluates a commutative `|` chain in SOURCE order.** cfe (kit 6/12 rotation notes) pulls the last complex
operand of a flat chain to the front, so the cfe body was spelled with operands rotated. Under NCC the same spelling
evaluates in the written order, so the fix is the gbi macro's natural order:
- SetTile w1 FLAT: `tile | cmt | maskt | (shiftt << 10) | cms | masks | shifts` -- no `(u32)` grouping, no `(u16)` leaf
  (the cfe "chain | leaf" final-`or` problem simply does not exist under edg). This one family took 98.5 -> 99.88.
- TILESIZE w1 `(tile << 24) | (lrs << 12) | lrt`; LoadTile w0 `(uls << 12) | 0xF4000000 | ult`, w1
  `0x07000000 | (lrs << 12) | lrt`; LoadBlock size `w * h` written `0x20 * 0x22` (multu operand order follows).
- A rotate-last-complex-to-front script plus a per-statement operand-permutation sweep (161 / 328 variants, 24
  parallel NCC builds, 35 s per sweep) got 91.5 -> 98.0; normalising each statement FAMILY to one spelling (the real
  source is one macro) beat the greedy sweep, which oscillates between arms.
- The cfe-only fixes (`(FW(..,4) + lh)` vs `(lh + FW(..,4))` for load order) still apply per site under NCC.
- The integer `x | (t = const)` operand pin (timproc lever) is INERT under NCC.

**3. Switch on the field, not a copied temp.** `switch (FW(arg1, 0x24)) { case ...: goto ...; default: goto ...; }`
(edg source-order compare chain) puts the scrutinee in t1 like the target; `temp_t1 = FW(..); if (temp_t1 == ..)`
ladder put it in v0. For switch 2 the temp spelling was already right.

**4. Variable identity still matters under NCC for multi-arm webs.** temp_t1_7 (the CI8 TLUT pointer) is shared by
the two CI8 arms; its register (t1 vs t0) in BOTH arms flipped when the two single-store packet pointers of the second
arm (`F0` LoadTLUT and `BA` SetOtherMode) became one variable (temp_t0_26 -> temp_t0_25, the dropped name kept by the
dead-reference line). Merging the first arm's four packet pointers instead wrecked the frame (93.3).

**5. Two-use constant ties.** In s1_508 the target holds 0x07000000 in t1 and rematerialises 0xF5480000 through `at`;
the port held 0xF5480000. Writing the LOADTILE SetTile w0 width as the arm's width local (`((temp_a0_6 + h) - temp_a0_6)`,
the form every other arm uses) instead of `FW(sp1DC, 4)` twice flips it (7 words). Assignment-expression pins of the
constant, packet-line joins and the |-permutation sweep were all inert.

**6. One-line layout can matter under NCC.** `temp_a0_6 = FW(var_a2, 0xC); temp_t0_27 = ((temp_a0_6 * FW(var_a2, 0x10)) + 1) >> 1) - 1;`
on ONE line loads 0x10 before 0xC like the target (two lines: 0xC first). But an adjacent-line join sweep over the
whole CI8 arm (80 variants) and an adjacent-statement swap sweep (80) were all inert or lower -- try it per site, it is
not a general rule.

**7. Remaining 578B4 residual (7 words, s2_508 = second CI8 arm).** The DL pointer that crosses the
gl_func_00034458 call (`sp50`, spilled at sp+0x50) is `ra` in the target and `t0` in the port; the next arg2 reload is
`lw t0,504(sp); andi ra,t0,0x1ff` in the target (`lw ra; andi ra,ra` here and in every other arm). Inert: variable
identity of sp50 (temp_t0_25 / temp_a0 / temp_v0_4 merges), tmem spellings (`(u32)`, `&=`, `0x1FF & arg2`, `511`,
copy through a local, assignment inside the w0), dropping `var_a2 = sp1DC`, `volatile` arg2, line joins of the packet,
and a non-volatile sp20 home for tmem (drops the dead `sw ra,32(sp)` and the frame -> lower). Also inert: moving the
tmem statement before / after the call (uopt sinks it), one tmem variable for every arm or sharing another arm's,
inline `(arg2 & 0x1FF)` everywhere (96.76), sp50 typed s32 / int * / u32 / void *, 1-3 call arguments, the s2_508 tail
(`sp34` / `if (0)` spellings), declaration-swap sweeps of temp_ra_8 / temp_t0_25 / temp_t1_7 / temp_a1 (115 each; homes
never read, coloring unchanged; swapping sp50 only moves its spill slot), and WHOLE-function adjacent-line join (630)
and adjacent-statement swap (630) sweeps, distance-2 (649) and distance-3 (633) statement swaps, a block-scoped `{ char *g50 = ...; }` packet pointer (frame +8, still t0),
and two variable-identity grids over the arm's packet pointers (F0 / BA / FD50 x 6 names = 216; the first four packets
x 3 names = 81), the volatile tmem store at each of 52 positions, the arm's DL-struct / count temps renamed to the
arm-1 `g` / `n`, the dxt block in the other arms' naming (temp_a0_6 = size, 99.92), and decl-swap sweeps of var_t0 /
temp_v0_6 / temp_t1 / temp_a0_6, a volatile `sp34` instead of the `if (0) { f(&sp34); }` home (reloads a1: lower),
tmem parameter typed u32 (inert), and reusing the BA packet pointer for any subset of the six post-call packets (63
variants, <= 94.35) -- no variant beat 99.95. Pattern worth knowing: in the target BOTH CI8 arms give the call-crossing
DL pointer `ra` and temp_t1_7 `t1`; every variant that moves temp_t1_7 to t0 also moves the s1_508 pointer off ra. The uopt coloring dump
(`-Wo,-zdbug:6`) aborts in `wrapper_ecvt` on this machine (the local libc_impl ecvt patch is not applied), so the
priority comparison is still unread.

**8. Negatives: the same mechanical NCC port on other game_libs near-exacts loses** -- they are cfe (C): gl 4EE44
99.73 (cfe 99.94), gl 445AC 98.08 (cfe 99.82), gl 40304 90.55 (cfe 99.82), gl 201B8 90.26 (cfe 97.94, matches kit
XCVI), 5A2C4 78.2 with 408/451 words (cfe 89.34; its pad arrays are dropped -- it would need the dead-reference line
AND a different body), gl 3D71C 95.0 (cfe 96.0; its src/dst addiu schedule is also inert to a held `src` / `dst`
block pointer and a one-line copy). Tell for a C++ body before porting: commutative-operand-order residuals that cfe spellings
cannot move, edg-style source-order compare chains, gbi macro packets. One port + score takes ~3 minutes.

**9. gl 250C8 (cfe 99.85) side probe.** The residual `sw a0,36(sp)` (target) vs the fontId home 84 means the target
spills fontId into the 0x24.. TEMP area, i.e. it is a uopt temp, not a named local. Inert or lower: fontId as the
inline `ASYNC_ID(asyncLoad->retMsg)` everywhere (95.1), `ASYNC_ID(retMsg)` / `ASYNC_STATUS(retMsg)` spellings (93-97),
and a block-scoped `u32 fontId;` in case 1 (cfe homes block locals at the BOTTOM of the local area, sp+44 here, and
grows the frame -- it never reaches the temp area; 99.27-99.31 vs 99.39 harness base).

**10. gl 51448 (95.56) side probe.** NCC port 95.07 = cfe (same 2-word-short shape: the target spills the copy `n`
of `o` to sp+40 and `l` to sp+44 across the void link call; here n stays coalesced with o in s0). Inert: n read back
from any of the three stores (`*(char **)(a0 + 0x28 / 0xC / 0x10)`, store-to-load forwarded), function-scope n at
three declaration positions. Swapping the 0xFFFF / vtable stores (the target stores +0x120 first) is lower (91.2).

**11. gl 35B1C (97.40) side probe.** Looks C++ (`o != 0 || (o = new)` + member placement-new test `o + 4 != 0`), but the
NCC port is 97.16 with the SAME residual (vtable `sw t6,12(s4)` scheduled before `addiu v1 / addiu at,-4` instead of
just before the bne); the store after `p =` is inert, after `q = p` / folded into the `if` condition is lower (94.1).

**Gate.** Full make ROM byte-identical, `make verify-blocks` 6/6 OK, `make non_matching_objects` 0 errors, no exact
lost vs origin/main 53953ff40, sentinels 551E0 / 55B10 / EBC8 / C5B0 / 62F08 at 100, 78.47 % code. post0b NM clip
unchanged 0x2e9bc (62F08 NM offset 0x2e96c). No new pinned symbols. Purge: `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`,
`build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post.c.o`, new donor `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_578B4_nm.cpp.o`.

## kit XCVIII (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 161): 4118 exact -- switch case placement, void callee pieces, break-line delay slots <a name="kit-xcviii-agent-g-run-161"></a>

**Summary.** One exact: timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118 (6872 bytes, the largest exact in timproc_b5; 78.47 -> 79.37 % code,
report.json). The run-115 99.14 body had two residual regions, both at the end: switch case 0 reloaded the homed arg0 per
access (target: one `lw v0,936(sp)` for four accesses) and the post-switch block's scheduling. Five source changes closed
them; all were found by small sweeps with `sc.sh` (2 s per compile). Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/g161/` (`sw4118.py`,
`w2.py`, `od.py` = objdiff one-shot diff printer, `sbs.py` side-by-side by offset).

**1. An empty case group placed FIRST blocks the register piece in a later case.** The switch had
`case 2: case 4: case 5: case 6: break;` as its first arm (m2c order). Moved below the last case, uopt gives arg0 a
register piece inside case 0 (one load, four uses) exactly as the target does; the rest of the function is unchanged
(6880 -> 6872 bytes = target). Placed after case 0 (fall-through), after case 1 or after case 3: identical to last.
`default: break;` instead of the empty labels changes the table (worse). Before this, 40+ case-0 shapes (copies, block
locals, statement orders, `if (1) {}`, labels, extra uses -- even 8 uses of arg0 in case 0 did not create a piece) were
inert: the piece decision was blocked by the empty arm, not by the case body. **Tell:** a later case whose body reloads a
spilled parameter per statement while the target loads it once into v0/a0 -- look for an empty case group at the top of
the switch.

**2. The piece takes v0 only after a VOID call.** With the case-0 call through the shared K&R `timproc_uso_b5_alias`
(int return) the piece took v1 / a0. Calling the real callee `timproc_uso_b5_func_00008D90` with its `void (int *, int)`
prototype (the target's reloc names it) gives v0. Same rule as kit "void-alias dead-$v0 exclusion": an int-returning
jal defines v0, so a piece starting at that call cannot use it.

**3. A named index temp is a uopt variable; the target's index is a ugen temp.** `temp_t0 = FW(arg0, 0x3B8); ...;
D[temp_t0] = 1;` colours temp_t0 v0 / v1; the target computes the index in t2. Writing the index inline in the final
statement (`((int *)(D + 0xB8))[FW(arg0, 0x3B8)] = 1;`) gives t2 and as1 still issues the index load right after the
base load.

**4. Post-switch store order by permutation.** The first five statements after the switch (0x414 = arg9, 0x3C0 = arg5,
the temp_f0 chain, 0x4B8, 0x4B4): all 120 orders compiled; `0x3C0 = arg5` FIRST is the only family with the target's
arg5 load before the 0x40C load and the 0.5f `lui a1` late. Line joins in that block were inert.

**5. A case's last statement and its `break` on ONE source line.** Last residual: case 0 ended `sw t1,184(at); b; lw
a2,936(sp)` (the reload for the a2 piece at the join filled the delay slot) where the target has `lw a2; b; sw t1`. The
reload is emitted at the end of the case BB, in the line group of the `break`; as1 only hoisted it above the store when
the store and the `break` share a line: `D[FW(arg0, 0x3B8)] = 1; break;`. Joining all case-0 statements on one line also
works; `break; case 1:` on one line does not. In -S output the whole flag block of another function (D884) was emitted in
source order and as1 still hoisted loads across `.loc` lines there (distinct symbols), so "line groups" are not a hard
barrier for every pair -- but for a spill reload vs a store they decided it here.

**6. Landing a cfe body that has a jumptable / literals in a USO unit (29CCC recipe, as 5FC0).** `src/timproc_uso_b5/
timproc_uso_b5_4118.c` = the unit's first 7 lines + the NM preamble + body verbatim; Makefile: add it to the C_FILES
filter-out list and `TIMB5_4118_DONOR` with `private REPLACE_FUNC_BODY +=` on both trees; pin
`timproc_uso_b5_func_00004118_rodata = 0x0000014C;` (the donor .rodata = 0.45f, 0.036f x3, 0.1f x5, then the 8-entry
table, identical in layout to RoData +0x14C..+0x18F). The unit keeps its INCLUDE_ASM + NM body (the NM object's rodata
layout stays as before). **Gotcha:** `make` was ROM-OK but `make verify-blocks` failed with `bake-data-relocs: no value
for symbol 'D_b5_4118_s01'`: bake-data-relocs.py does not parse `NAME = 0x0;  /* comment */`. The 31 per-site
`D_b5_4118_sNN` and the three `timproc_uso_b5_alias_pfN` pins had trailing comments (harmless while the function was NM);
moved to one comment line above each group. Check every symbol a new donor references:
`objdump -r donor.o` -> each must match `^NAME = 0x...;$` exactly.

**7. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- **b5 D884 / DF14 EE6C flag word** (target: `lui; lw 4(r)` per load, `lui at; sw 4(at)` per store, every load AFTER the
  previous store; ours hoists each load above the previous store): 1-bit bitfields (byte `lbu/sb` ops, 89.96); a plain
  `extern volatile s32` (base CSE'd `lui/addiu`, 94.10); per-site volatile casts with +4 or +0 and per-site `volatile s32`
  declarations (always `lui; addiu; lw 0(r)`, 89.2); one non-volatile symbol (forwarded, 91.8), with `if (1) {}` (91.9) or
  `do { } while (0)` around each statement (93.1); load and store of each statement through ONE per-statement symbol
  (target length 1680, base materialised, 91.9); function-typed symbols for loads, stores or both (89.2-94.4); all six
  statements on one line (95.56, +0.05, length off, not kept) or in pairs (flat). In the -S text ugen emits them in
  source order; the hoist is as1's (distinct symbols). The target needs the same symbol for load and store as1-side and no
  uopt forwarding -- not found.
- **bootup 76F4** (`lui v0` vf before `lui a2` G after the call): an early / in-block vf local with or without joining
  the call line (99.05 / 99.82 flat); a second, function-typed symbol for the scale base gives the target's lui order but
  colours it v1 and stops holding G in a2 (93.82).
- **mgrproc 1824** (`li at,1` of the outer switch hoisted above the counter increment): increment / switch line joins,
  `+= 1`, `++`, `if (1) {}`, `default` first / last, unsigned key: all 98.52; swapping the two case bodies 36.9.
- **titproc 5DC** under NCC (all callees `(...)` in one `extern "C"` block): 82.36 (cfe 98.87 stays).
- **4118 dead ends kept for the record:** the case-0 extra-use probe (5 / 6 / 8 arg0 stores: no piece) is what showed
  the body was not the gate.

**7b. Greedy single-line relocation inside runs of simple statements (`g161/rl.py UNIT FUNC`).** For every run of 3-14
consecutive same-indent simple statements, move each line to each other position (8 compiles in parallel), keep the best
same-length variant, continue with the next run. Check every kept move for a data dependency by hand (only independent
stores / loads / declarations were kept). Gains (report.json): b5 D884 95.51 -> 96.63 and DF14 95.23 -> 96.23 (the
`0x114 = arg8` store right after `0x110 = arg7`, `0x120` before `0x124`: as1 then issues the stack-argument loads like the
target), game_uso 0B3C 94.93 -> 94.94, 591C 94.15 -> 94.16, bootup 55A0 94.33 -> 94.35 (a declaration), B75C 91.05 ->
91.12. Flat: b5 CEB4, bootup E2D0, titproc 5DC, and a second pass over D884 / DF14 (all runs). Sibling sweeps of today's levers: the break-join (item 5) over 13 NM functions / 53
`stmt;\n break;` sites (85-100 band): no gain anywhere else; empty-case-group-last (item 1) on the only two other
switches that start with an empty group (b5 8FC8, bootup 6808): inert. bootup 90CC's 7 / 6 dispatch as an if-goto chain,
case order swap, unsigned key: all lower or flat (97.15). gl 3430's step load inlined into the loop (91.2), after the
0xEC store or in the `for` init (95.4): lower.
