## kit XCIX (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 155): coloring dump on NCC donors, live units, copy + kill <a name="kit-xcix-agent-c-run-155"></a>

**Summary.** The uopt dump now runs on the 578B4 NCC donor. Reading it showed how uopt actually decides interference
(live units, see 2), which explains the s2_508 ra/t0 pair but did not give a C spelling that reaches it. The same
dump then cracked three other near-exacts: gl_func_0003E0F0 (192 bytes, cfe, copy + kill, 4),
game_libs_func_0004CDB0 (332 bytes, cfe) and gl_func_000488A0 (448 bytes, NCC donor), both through the itab-bit
tie (6), plus gl_func_0004AFB4 (140 bytes, cfe) through a void blank alias (7). Code 79.37 -> 79.52 %. ROM
byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6, `make non_matching_objects` 0 errors, no exact lost vs origin/main a56e4b358,
sentinels at 100, post0b NM clip unchanged 0x2e9bc (no NM length change). New pins: `gl_func_00000000_4afb4v`,
`D_4AFB4_s` (both 0).
Purge: `build/{,non_matching/}src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`, retired NM donor
`build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_488A0_nm.cpp.o`, new donor `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_488A0.cpp.o`.

**1. Running the dump on an NCC (C++) donor.** The patched compiler (ecvt fix) is
`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/out/` and has both `cc` and `NCC`. It is for diagnosis only, never for building.
Run it in a scratch dir, because uopt writes `./uoptlist`:

    cd /tmp/claude-1000/<scratch> && /home/danjs/code/decomp/tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/out/NCC \
        -c -G 0 -non_shared -Wab,-r4300_mul -O2 -mips2 -32 -Wo,-zdbug:5 -o x.o <donor>.cpp

The .text it emits is identical to the build compiler's (checked on 578B4). How to read it:
- An LR number is the itab **bit** (`{idx|n}  bit  isvar M 4 -416` lines). For a variable, `M 4 -N` is its frame home
  at `sp + frame - N`. Under NCC every referenced local gets a home top-down in declaration order, and so do the unused
  `volatile` pads. So a 20-line script that walks the declarations turns bits into names (scratch `tools/c5.py`).
  Bits above the last itab entry are code-motion temps (hoisted constants such as `KBA000E02`, which colours t2 at
  function entry in 578B4) and split pieces.
- `-Wo,-zdbug:6` gives the coloring trace (`bit: piece assigned (constrained) R` / `not colored (-ve save)` / `split out`).
- `-Wo,-zdbug:5` gives, for each LR, `>>>active<<<{..} bit colour`, then `adjsave`, `forbidden: [...]`,
  `:::interfere with::: ...` and `- live bb - unit ...` lines. **Use this one.** It answers "why did X not get register R"
  directly: either a neighbour with R was coloured first (it is in the interfere list), or R was free and X simply
  took the lowest free register.
- Colour numbers: 1 v0, 2 v1, 3-6 a0-a3, 7-12 t0-t5, **13 ra**, 14.. s0... (t6-t9 are ugen's ring, never uopt colours).
- `-Wc,-d` (the ugen trace, stdout) also works through NCC.

**2. Live units: uopt's interference is unit-granular.** uopt cuts a long straight-line BB into extra flow-graph nodes
(label 0, one successor). Measured with synthetic functions: about **20 memory operations** per unit (each load or store
counts, the `p[i] = K` statement counts as 1, `p[i] = q[i] + K` as 2). Lines and statements do not matter.
- **A call ends a unit and resets the count.** The post-call unit always holds the result store plus the next ~20 ops.
- Two LRs that are both in a unit interfere even if their intervals inside it are disjoint. In the 578B4 dump no two LRs
  with the same colour ever share a unit. Example: arm 1's `sp118` (the call-crossing DL pointer) gets ra only because
  `temp_t0_17`, which is defined after `sp118`'s last use, sits in the same post-call unit and takes t0.
- **Zero-emission unit shifters.** Dead stores (`x = 0;`) and discarded loads (`(void)p[3];`) are removed before the
  count. But a load multiplied or masked away inside a live expression (`... + (FW(temp_v1, 0x400) & 0)`) is counted and
  then folded, with no instructions emitted. Each one moves every later unit boundary up by one op, up to the next call.
  Use distinct addresses: re-using an address that is really loaded makes a CSE temp (frame +32 in 578B4).
- **`if (1) { stmt; }`** starts a real new BB with zero code. Placed right after a call's result store, it removes every
  interference between the call-crossing pointer and the LRs defined after it.

**3. 578B4 s2_508 residual, fully explained (still 7 words).** The second CI8 arm's FD50 pointer `sp50` (bit 765, home
sp+0x50) lives in unit 146 (FD50 packet + call) and unit 147 (post-call). At its turn (adjsave 1.5) only t1
(`temp_t1_7`) and the a/v registers are forbidden, so it takes t0, the lowest free one. For the target's ra, t0 and t2..t5
must be forbidden while ra stays free. t2..t5 come from the `temp_t2..t5` expressions defined in unit 147. But the tmem
expression `arg2 & 0x1FF` (bit 553, ra in every arm, ra in the target too) is defined in unit 147 before them. So
sp50 = ra and tmem = ra cannot both hold with the current unit layout. Probes:
- 4 phantoms at the arm head pull the BA packet into unit 146, so `temp_t0_25` forbids t0. Then sp50 = **ra**, but tmem
  loses ra: it is split, frame +32, 96.46.
- Phantoms + `if (1)` barrier after the result store: sp50 = **t2** (99.938, only the t2/t3 pair differs).
- A grid of phantom counts at 10 positions, `if (1)` barriers at all 89 statements of the arm, `if (sp50) {}` dead uses at
  6 positions, `char * volatile sp50` / `&sp50` (both make sp50 uncoloured: ugen ring temps, home store first, lower),
  moving `temp_t2..t5` before the call (uopt sinks them) and `-Wo,-zmovc` (diagnostic): nothing beats 99.95.
- The target's `lw t0,504(sp); andi ra,t0,0x1ff` needs no lever of its own. When the destination ra is also the register
  of another live register variable (sp50) in the same ugen BB, ugen loads into a scratch register first. In this
  build ra is not taken, so it loads straight into ra.
So the original's statement or unit structure around this call differs from the port. Most likely candidates: per-macro
`_g` packet variables, or a different shape for the `dl->n++` header, giving different unit boundaries. Next step: model
the unit counts of a gbi-macro spelling of arm 2 (block `{ Gfx *_g = &dl->buf[dl->n++]; ... }` per packet) with
`c5.py` before scoring bytes.

**4. gl 3E0F0 EXACT: copy + kill.** The last word was the volatile `tmp` store in the final jal delay slot: target
`sw a0,76(sp)` (the argument copy), build `sw s0,76(sp)` (o's register). Fix:
`{ int x = *(int *)(arg0 + 0x40); p2 = (int *)o; o = 0; gl_func_00000000(tmp = (char *)p2, x); }`. With o dead at the
call, ugen stores the value that sits in a0. p2 (re-used function-scope local) then gets a frame home, so declare it
above `zero[]` and shrink the pad (`volatile int padA[3]; int *p2; float zero[3];`). Frame 80, zero[] at 48, tmp at 76.
A block-scoped copy `char *n = o; o = 0;` also fixes the register, but adds frame +8. Tell: a store in a delay slot
takes a long-lived s-register where the target uses the argument register that holds the same value. Kill the source
variable after copying it.

**5. Side diagnoses (no gain).**
- gl 45178 (99.985, 2 words + 3 literal pins): the target spills the second packet pointer at sp+36, which is the uopt
  temp area. An unnamed spelling (`((int *)(base + i*8))[0/1]`) does spill to 36, but only the shared `i*8` becomes the
  CSE temp; the base is reloaded after the call (91.8). A block-scoped / `register` / re-declared `g` stays at its home
  40, and an extra pad grows the frame. Open.
- gl 4EE44 (99.935, 2 words): the post-call `*(o+0x70)` reload is the `uilod` expression LR coloured v0 (the target
  uses a1). Inert: a void callee, `r = callee(...)`, a for-init comma, float-pointer spelling. A named `mm` and an
  assignment inside the argument are lower (7 words).
- gl 39E24 (99.79, the vf / G `lui` order after the second call): the target materialises the vector base (v0)
  before G (a2). In ours G comes first. Inert: `while (0)` / `if (0)` anchors on vf at the top, before or after the
  first call and before the first FP statement (a top anchor does move vf to bit 0 and gives it v0, but the order stays),
  and the `*=` operand order. Anchors after the last store are lower (27 words).

## kit C (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 162): diff-table decode fixes, BB-local FP constants, cfe scalar homes <a name="kit-c-agent-g-run-162"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts. One large NM gain: titproc_uso_func_0000116C 94.13 -> 98.96 (report.json, 1160 bytes, length
1136 -> 1160 = target). The coloring-only queue (b5 32C8, game_uso 1DDC, titproc 5DC) and five other near-exacts stayed
flat. Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/g162/` (`py/prc.py BASE.c UNIT FUNC VARIANTS.py` = parallel variant scorer over
`sc.sh`; `py/prn.py` the NCC twin; `py/spmap.py TARGET.o BUILD.o FUNC` = target->build stack-offset map from objdiff
rows; `py/pr.py` window printer).

**1. Read the structural rows first.** The 116C diff had 291 rows, nearly all ARG_MI, but its INSERT / DELETE / REPLAC
rows were four real decode errors, each worth more than any colouring lever:
- case 2: `lui a0,&D; addiu a0; lhu; addiu v0,v0,4; andi; jal 012150; sh t6,0(v0)` -- a missing call
  `012150(&D)` whose only visible trace was the `& 0xFFF7` store in its delay slot (the 1710 sibling's case 2 had the
  same block: `z = *(char **)(D + 0x154) + 4; *(short *)z = ... & 0xFFF7;` inside `if (1) {}`, then the call);
- branches to a different place: the target's `bnez a0, X` / `beqz v0, X` jump to the 0x40100 gate, ours to the
  epilogue -- the gate block was nested inside `if (av == 0) { if (gate512) { ... } }` but belongs at the END of the
  else arm (reached whenever av != 0 or the 512 gate fails);
- per-site `lui at; sw 168(at)` / `lui at; sw 132(at)` where ours materialised one `&D` base in v1: the two stores name
  DIFFERENT symbols (the reloc says import_00263D30 and import_00020098); spelling both through D_00000000 made uopt
  CSE the base;
- `lw t7,60(v1); addiu v0,v1,60; slti; beqz; nop; lw t9,0(v0)`: the clamp test reads `*(s0->0x64 + 0x3C)` afresh and
  the increment goes through `c`; with `if (*c < 255)` uopt CSEs the two loads (one word short, no nop).
Then two spellings: `vt = *(char **)(*(char **)(s0 + K) + 0x28); v1 = *(char **)(s0 + K);` (vtable first, object
named after it) flips every obj/vt pair to the target's v1 / v0 (97.22 -> 97.96, all 7 sites; mixed subsets lower);
`*(int *)(s0 + 0x74) * 30` at the case-1 else site (IDO's own `sll 4; subu; sll 1` keeps the load a t-temp and reuses
one register) 97.96 -> 98.96; the same `* 30` at the other three sites is lower (the const-40 web there still colours
a1, target v0). Left: the 4-entry table (`sltiu 4`, no cfe form -- keep the phantom `case 4`), const 40 a1 / v0, the
t-ring at the 0x70 counter sites. The vt-before-object spelling swept over 22 sites in nine units: no other gain.
**Rule:** in a 92-96 % function, list `grep INSERT|DELETE|REPLAC` of the objdiff one-shot before any register work;
a missing `jal` or a wrong branch target is a decode error, and fixing it toward target length can be followed by
colouring work on a correct body.

**2. FP constants are BB-local candidates; `if (1) {}` is not a block boundary.** b5 32C8 (l134 in f0, target f2 with
the zero in f0): with `if (1) {}` between every vec statement the colours do not move (l134 f0, l13C f2); with
`do { } while (0)` around groups they do (l13C f0 after a boundary, the zero f2 / f12 when it shares the block). The
zero is ONE candidate across the function (placed early it takes f12 everywhere, including the later rematerialised
`mtc1` sites). Never reached: zero f0 with l134 and l13C both f2. Sweeps (all recorded in g162/t32): 84 zero
interleavings, 600 + 2400 random orders x `if` / `do` partitions, 4096 order x partition configs with a register
fingerprint test (killed at the 20-min timeout with no hit in the completed part), dead `while (0)` zero uses
(no effect). The target needs the zero coloured BEFORE l134 while interfering with it; every source order colours
l134 first.

**3. 0B3C's frame: cfe homes every named scalar at the bottom.** `py/spmap.py` on game_uso 0B3C: target frame 336,
ours 352; the arrays / Vec3s keep the target order but the target has 2 words below v30 and 11 words of gaps between
arrays (1 between c3 and fresh, 3 between c1 and stage, 6 between stage and zv, 1 between zv and nseg); ours has 17
words below v30 (the 14 named scalars) and no gaps. Moving the scalar declarations between the arrays changes nothing
(scalars always go below the aggregates), and turning 11 scalars into 1-element arrays placed in the gaps drops the
fuzzy to 67-84 (the arrays are not scalarised). The target's 11 gap words are aggregates in the original (temporaries
or 1-word structs), and it has only two named scalars of its own -- the m2c scalars need a different decomposition.
nseg / ncur / nsub are also reversed (target nseg lowest).

**4. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- game_uso 1DDC: the uninitialised `if (fz) {}` lever replaced by a real parameter (`void f(int *a0, float fz)` +
  `if (fz) {}`): 98.70 (param move costs), with an int pad param 98.18; the illegal form still gives 99.93, not 100.
- titproc 5DC (d = s1 / t = s0, target swapped): zdbug shows the constant `(int)&import` (bit 2) coloured AFTER t
  (bit 18); t's webs moved into the dead parameter a1 per case (31 subsets x 3 modes) and the empty `case 10` first /
  last: flat or lower. **`if (t) {}` after the do-while gives 100.0 (1424 bytes, every word)** -- t then lives

  (case 1 sets done without touching t), so under the current policy it is not landed. Every legal way to define t

  fourth argument (97.75), `if (t) {}` at the end of each t-setting case instead (98.31 max, longer). Note the
  target itself reads s5v from its never-written home (`lw s5,92(sp)` in the prologue), so the original source did
  rely on uninitialised locals in this function. Policy call for the user, not a lever to use.
- game_uso 97EC (NCC, x in f2 vs target f12): 20 ctor / operator / set() spellings (by-value XZ ctor, init lists,
  free operator*, XZ operator*, delegating ctors, int zero): flat or lower.
- bootup E2D0 (arg4 colour): `if (arg4) {}` / `s = arg4` / `s = 1.0f + arg4` / `if (1) {}` at every statement
  (52 positions x 4): the original position stays best.
- mgrproc 2B7C (`held = a3 + 0x490` spilled, ours folds `held + 0x10`): IXA, int, earlier / later definitions all fold;
  `char *volatile held` gives the target home (sp+92) but hoists the addiu above the switch (90.40).
- gl 76F0 (the switch value is a v1 candidate copied to v0 in the target): temp / var_v0 / cast spellings flat.
- b5 AC20 (target per-site `lui at` for the gxy reads and a held `a0 + 0xDC`): a separate gy symbol 91.53 (lower).
- bootup 31C0 (target tests 0, 2, 1): if / else-if, swapped arms, `default` / phantom case: 65-92.
- bootup 6808 (address bases held in s4 / s5): dead `while (0)` uses, moving the gD / gE definitions: lower.
- bootup 24B8 (target keeps the s0 variable in a callee-saved register; its first web is the `& 0x400` temp of the
  first call's argument): `s0 = FW(v0, 0x10) & 0x400` named before / inside the call, `k` merged into s0 with the
  vtable in v1: flat or lower.
- bootup 55A0 (alloc-or-init `node` coloured a1 with an `or a0,a1` copy in the init call's delay; ours a0): `if (node
  == 0) {...} if (node != 0)`, assignment in the condition, empty-then form: flat or lower (the target copy is real).
**5. Late gains (relocation).** mgrproc 2B7C 94.07 -> 97.56: `a3 = *(char **)(arg0 + 0xD4);` moved ABOVE the four
`spA4..spB0 = 1.0f` volatile home stores (the target loads 0xD4 through a0 and copies a0 to s4 late; with the read
after the stores ours copies first and loads through s4 -- every later s-reg shifted). The 24 store orders alone are
flat. kit XCVIII `rl.py` sweep: b5 C310 93.75 -> 94.84 (`f32 sp60` declared first, `fb = ...` before `i = 0`),
bootup 31C0 +0.04 and b5 B154 +0.06 (one declaration each); flat on 2B7C (after the move), mgrproc 23FC, b5 AC20.
(gui 4568 and bootup 8BD4 score differently under `sc.sh` than in the report -- donors / flags -- so their sweep
results were not used.)

- mgrproc 2B7C `held`: a dead `if (0) f(&held);` escape or `char **hp = &held` gives the target's memory home (sp+92)
  and length, but uopt hoists the `addiu a3,0x490` above the switch dispatch (90.40 vs 94.07).
- titproc 116C after the fixes: the kit XCVIII relocation sweep (`rl.py`, 14 runs), the six case-0 store orders x
  both counter spellings, and dead `while (0)` boosts of the 40 constant: no gain (the 40 candidate, zdbug bit 206,
  is coloured last and gets a1).
- Scans that came up empty: target-only `jal` rows in 80-99 % functions (2 functions, both moved calls, not
  missing ones); target `lui at` count above ours (only 55A0, see above).

**6. Equal-adjsave ties colour in ITAB-BIT order; move a variable's bit earlier with a dead `while (0)` store.** In
`-Wo,-zdbug:5`, look for competing LRs with the SAME adjsave (common for straight-line packet code: 3.0 / 31.5).
Constrained LRs are picked by max adjsave, so a tie goes to the lower bit, which takes the lower register. The bit is
the variable's FIRST OCCURRENCE in ucode. A `while (0) { k = 0; }` at the top of the function survives into the itab
(the body is removed later, with no code) and gives k the earliest bit.
- **game_libs_func_0004CDB0 EXACT.** Packet 3's block index i and the CSE'd `obj->0xC` load were tied at 3.0. The load
  was first in ucode, so it took v1 (target: i = v1, g = a0). Fix: packet 3's index is a function-scope `k` with
  `while (0) { k = 0; }` at the top. That moved the load's packet-3 piece to a0, but the E9 packet then took a0 for its
  g, so the E9 packet uses the function-scope g (the v1 web of packets 1-2) and reads its index through it:
  `{ int i; unsigned int *p; g = GFX(obj); i = *(int *)(g + 4); ... }`. 78/83 -> 83/83.
- **gl_func_000488A0 EXACT (NCC donor promoted from NM-only).** ctx, n and the `ctx->dl` load were tied at 31.5, with ctx
  first (v0; target ctx = a0, dl = v0, n = v1). Fix: a named DL cursor `d` (`d = ctx->dl; n = d->count; d->count = n + 1;`
  keeping `g = &ctx->dl->base[n]` as the re-read) plus `while (0) { d = 0; n = 0; }`. That orders d, n, ctx -> v0, v1, a0.
  The last 2 words: c2 (`c2 = obj->ctx`) sat alone in the unit after the `if (obj) {}` BB split, so it took v0. Writing
  `c2 = obj->ctx;` BEFORE the `if (obj) {}` puts it in the header's unit (v0 / v1 / a0 / a1 taken) -> a2 like the
  target, and the emission order is unchanged.
- Not ties (no gain here): gl 3DF58 (best v0 adj 23 vs n a1 adj 10; the target swaps them, so it is a priority
  difference) and gl 525F0 (obj is not coloured; the reload register is ugen's temploc binding: `fin = obj; obj = 0;`
  moves it to a2, never to the target's v0).

**7. A void blank alias lets a call-crossing web keep v0 (gl 4AFB4 EXACT).** A call that returns int defines v0, so any
web live across it cannot be coloured v0. When the target spills a web before a call and restores it with `lw v0,..`
afterwards, and that call's result is unused, call it through a void-declared blank alias
(`extern void gl_func_00000000_4afb4v();`, pinned `= 0x00000000;` in undefined_syms_auto.txt). Here the `a3 << 3`
offset web then keeps v0 across the middle call (spill at 0x20 + `lw v0,32(sp)`). The old `if (a3) {}` hack is no longer
needed. It is the same mechanism as kit XCVIII's "a piece can only take v0 when the call it follows is VOID", but for a
spill/restore pair rather than a piece. Negatives: 525F0 (obj is not coloured, so ugen's reload binding does not care),
4EE44 (the post-call reload is a new LR; void callee inert). 5F5F0 (NCC, z f14 vs f18 + an a1 home-store order): dead
`while (0)` anchors on x / y / z / xLook / len / slen / ulen / d2 are all inert (12 variants).
gl 445AC (6 words): dropping the `v = D_glob_e` name puts that load in t7 like the target, but the `&D_445AC_b`
store base then goes to t8 instead of v0, which re-phases the ugen ring (12 words). Naming the base through v / v1 / an
assignment expression is no better. Not kept.
gl 36A48 (NCC): only the frame slots of the call-return temp (target 92 / 116) and the load order are left. Pad / declaration
sweeps and `r.x` / `dir.x` operand spellings did not beat the base.

## kit CI (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 156): spill-slot tells, live-range sharing across switch arms, as1 bound-check fill still open <a name="kit-ci-agent-c-run-156"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts and no NM changes (every probe below was flat or lower; the tree is origin/main ebc19497d,
79.52 % code, report.json). The run was a dump-driven pass over the post0b / post near-exacts. It produced several
diagnoses that narrow the remaining residuals; each item names the lever that would be needed. Scratch:
`/tmp/claude-1000/c156/` (`sc.sh` = full-unit cfe score in ~6 s, `var.py BASE UNIT FUNC VARIANTS.py` = parallel
replace-and-score, `ex.py SRC FUNC OUT.c` = standalone NM extract for the dump, `zd.sh SRC DIR [5|6]` = dump compile,
`nsc.sh X.cpp FUNC` = NCC donor score, `rl.py` = kit XCVIII relocation sweep pointed at agent-c).

**1. Whole-unit dump is cheap.** For game_libs_post.c (17k lines) the dump compiler finishes in under a second after
asm-processor's pre pass: `asm_processor.py -O2 unit.c > pre.c; zd.sh pre.c DIR 5`. Find a function's section with
`grep -n "global coloring of FUNC"`; the itab is between `COPY PROPAGATION OF FUNC` and that line. No need to
extract a standalone file unless the dump of one function is all you want.

**2. A spill at a temp-area slot means the spilled value is NOT a named variable.** cfe homes every referenced named
local in declaration order from the top of the frame (kit XCIX 1 for NCC; the same holds for cfe), and ugen saves a
caller-saved coloured VARIABLE around a call at that home. Expression live ranges (CSE'd expressions) and split pieces
are saved in the temp area below the homes. Corollary (measured in 250C8 and 45178): a named local assigned a PURE
expression over register variables (`fontId = ASYNC_ID(retMsg)` with retMsg a variable, `g + i * 8` with both
variables) is copy-propagated away, and the expression LR -- which may cross a call because it reads no memory --
is saved in the temp area; the same expression over a memory read (`ASYNC_ID(asyncLoad->retMsg)`) is killed by the
call, so the name keeps a real home. Measured on three functions:
- gl 45178 (99.985): the second packet pointer `g` is saved at its home sp+40; the target saves it at sp+36. Spelling
  the sum as an expression over two register variables (`g = base; ((int *)(g + i * 8))[0] = ...; [1] = call(m);`)
  makes `g + i*8` a call-crossing expression LR, and ugen saves it at sp+36 exactly like the target -- but the
  colours change (index a3 / base v1 / sum t0, target index v1 / base t3 / sum a3; 99.41). Anchors, `register`,
  block scope, a dead pad before g (frame +8), `if (g) {}` after the use (no split, home stays): none reaches both.
  Closest shape: index in its own variable (n3), base re-read inline, packet pointer as a block-scoped `_g`
  (`{ int *_g = (int *)((char *)FW(FW(p, 0xC), 0) + n3 * 8); _g[0] = 0x01030040; _g[1] = gl_func_00000000(m); }`)
  gives EVERY register of the target (index v1, base t3, pointer a3), but the block variable gets a home below the
  outer ones (sp+44 with the old `g` still declared, frame 112; sp+40 with it removed, frame 104 = base). The cfe
  frame keeps a fixed 40-byte bottom (args, s0 / ra, an 8-byte temp area at 32..39), so 68 bytes of homes always
  round the frame up to 112. The opposite trade: index n3 + base in its own variable + the sum as an expression
  (`((int *)(b + n3 * 8))[0/1]`) gives index v1, pointer a3 and the save at sp+36 like the target, but the base
  becomes an LR (a1, target a ugen temp t3) and the m reload sinks below the packet code (95.06). The target's sp+36 is inside that temp area: the original packet pointer is a split
  piece or an expression LR, never a named home. Measured frame rule: frame = round8(homes + 40) here.
  Also flat: the base as the slot-1 index variable i (99.52: base a3 / sum t0), a memory-resident base (`if (0)
  f(&g)` / `if (1) { char **gp = &g; }`: home store + reload, 97.2-97.4), and `#pragma no side effects` on a
  separate callee alias so the inline `FW(FW(p, 0xC), 0) + n3 * 8` could be CSE'd across the call (no effect: the
  base is still reloaded after the call, 556 bytes).
- gl 250C8 (99.85): `fontId` homed at +84 (decl slot 3), the target keeps it at +36 together with the bytesRemaining
  temp. A block-scoped fontId goes to the first slot below the outer homes (+44 / +40, never +36). So the target's
  fontId is an expression temp (the case-1 `ASYNC_ID(retMsg)` CSE across the SetFontLoadStatus call, computed from the
  v0 copy of the retMsg load); every spelling that makes it an expression (all arms through the retMsg variable, only
  case 1, OoT's doneMsg) changes the arm code and costs 4-12 bytes. Closest: OoT's own shape (every arm through the
  retMsg variable, a separate `doneMsg = asyncLoad->retMsg` at the end): fontId's temp lands at sp+36 and the
  dispatch head gets the target's `lw X,24(s0); ...; or v0,X` copy shape, but X is a0 (target a1, the osSendMesg
  argument register) and the dispatch delay slots then take `andi a1,v0,0xff` instead of `srl a0,v0,8` (95.83,
  608 bytes). Reusing pad / fontId / retMsg for doneMsg, a direct argument, `if (1) {}` / order sweeps (15
  variants): flat or lower; status-store-first gives the target length (600) but 92.77.
- gl 40304 (99.82): the `&self->m30` spill takes 32 instead of the target's 36. Bisection by deleting single
  statements of case 0x72 (diagnosis only): only removing `sp->z = c;` moves it to 36. Writing that store as
  `self->scl.z = c` gives 36 too, but the pos-copy loads are then hoisted (98.84). All 32 combinations of sp / self
  spellings for the three scale stores, the `y = *sp` copy and the call argument: none keeps both.

**3. One expression LR can span several switch arms.** In 40304 the zdbug:5 listing shows the `self + 0xC0` LR live in
bb1/bb2 (arm 0x6D) AND bb13-15 (case 0x72), one colour (a2) for both. Same-expression arms share an LR; keep this in
mind when a spill slot or colour in one arm moves after editing another arm. (It did not explain the 40304 slot:
changing arm 0x6D to a different field left 32.)

**4. Any loop construct changes the prologue of 4B2F4.** A `while (0) { x = 0; }` anchor ANYWHERE in
game_libs_func_0004B2F4 (top, inside the if body, after the matrix copy, inside `if (0)`), and even `do {} while (0);`,
grows the function by 8 bytes (frame 192 -> 184, s0 saved after the branch instead of before it). So the kit XCIX
itab-bit anchor is unusable here; dead stores and `if (0) { x = 0; }` are removed before the itab and do nothing.
Its three slot-pointer / slot-index ties (region 1: equal adjsave 3.0, pointer bit 59 before load bit 60) stay.

**5. 40304 FP residual is a priority gap, not a tie.** K = 1/32767 (constant LR, adjsave 1.5) must colour before c and d
(2.0 each) and after a, b, kt (2.0). Ties go by bit, but a constant's bit is after every variable, so only a lower c/d
adjsave (an LR covering two units / BBs with the same code) would do it. `if (1) {}` after d (one more BB) changes
scheduling (832 bytes); phantom loads (8..23 in the b statement) change length or nothing; anchors with extra K uses do
nothing (while (0) uses do not count toward adjsave); inlining c or d into the store adds code.

**6. 51AD8 / 396FC bound-check delay (as1, still open).** New negatives on top of the measured liveness rule (above, in
the 51AD8 section): line joins of the default with the last break / the switch line / its own break, `default` first
(964 bytes), `default: dflt:` label, `if (1) {}` at the default head, an explicit range check before the switch (with
and without `goto` into the default), the default as code after the switch, extra unused parameters (the prologue

79.52 -> 79.64 %. NM gains (report.json): kernel func_80001594 95.98 -> 96.62, game_uso 97EC 99.15 -> 99.97,
titproc 116C 98.96 -> 99.12, timproc_b5 B624 96.07 -> 96.10, timproc_b5 BDEC 95.65 -> 95.82. Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/g163/` (`py/zd.py
BASE.c VARIANTS.py NAME FUNC` = zdbug:5 per-LR summary for a cfe variant, bit / colour / adjsave / forbidden /
defining op; `py/spseq.py` = sequence of `addiu r,sp,N` for target and NCC variants, the quickest view of edg

**1. edg inline temporaries come from a per-type pool (gl 64388 EXACT).** The last 2 words of 64388 were the
shared operator return slot (`addiu v0,sp,116`, target 108). The uopt dump (`isvar M 4 -N` homes) showed
operator-'s reference parameters a / b homed at sp+112 / 108, BELOW the slot; the target has them above.
Rules measured on the donor:
- An inline function's parameter gets a temporary only when it is used more than once (a once-used parameter
  is substituted; `nrm(o->dir, o->len)` wrappers change nothing).
- Temporaries are freed at the end of the full expression and REUSED by later expressions of the same type
  (the `this` temp at sp+132 serves operator/= and assign).
- Named locals inside an inline body (`V3 &t = *this;`) are not pool temps: they go to the top of the frame
  (frame +8, everything else unchanged).
So the fix is to make an EARLIER statement allocate the two pointer temps: `void operator/=(float s) {
dv(*this, *this, s); }` with `inline void dv(P3 &d, const P3 &v, float s) { d.x = v.x / s; ... }` allocates d
and v (both multi-use) during `o->dir /= o->len`; operator- then reuses them for a / b and the return slot
lands at sp+108. Same code, 128/128 words. Tell: an NCC donor whose only residual is a temp / slot home a few
words off, with the target's home ABOVE yours: pre-allocate the missing temps in an earlier full expression
through an inline helper with multi-use reference parameters.
- Side use (b5 B624, NM): declaring an inline helper's locals apart from their assignments (`f32 dz; V r;
f32 dy; f32 dx;` then the references and the assignments) moved its return-slot temp r from sp+100 to the
target's sp+104 (12 of 72 order variants; +0.03).
- Declaration-bound temporaries (the temp bound to `XZ(const Vec3 &)` in `XZ e(expr);`) are PREPENDED to the
block's list: in 97EC, creation order e-bound, T1 (the materialised `a - b`), f-bound gives f-bound 204, T1
192, e-bound 180, then e 168 / f 156. The target has e-bound 204 / f-bound 180 (append order). Toy sweep
(`toy/run.py`): if / do-while(0) / for / while / switch / bare block bodies, copy-init, `X(expr)` casts,
`const V &` named temporaries, a helper returning X, free operators, by-value ctor parameter: all prepend
(by-value shares one temp). Open.

**2. On-field forwarding makes ugen temps that cross a branch; the forwarded load is a phantom LR.**

## kit CIII (agent-c 2026-10-24, run 157): cfront DL-append inlines, edg temp-home counting, volatile re-read tell <a name="kit-ciii-agent-c-run-157"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts. Four NM gains in game_libs_post0b by rewriting cfe bodies as NCC (C++) NM-only donors
(report.json): gl_func_0004B620 94.48 -> 98.82 (1236 bytes, length = target), gl_func_0004BAF4 91.78 -> 95.58
(1692 bytes, length 1676 -> 1692 = target; an intermediate cfe fix took it to 92.03 first) gl_func_0003E5E0
75.74 -> 91.78 (608 bytes, length 644 -> 604) and gl_func_00040070 95.03 -> 99.28 (564 bytes, length = target). Code % unchanged
(79.64, NM only). Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/c157/` (`ndo.sh X.cpp CTORSYM FUNC` = NCC compile + rename + objdiff
rows; `ndo2.sh X.cpp FUNC` same without rename; `run2.sh` / `run3.sh` / `run4.sh` = parallel variant scorers over a
base .cpp, `od.py` = row printer that tolerates objects without addresses).

**1. The tell for a cfront DL-append / constructor body (both functions).** The target puts the display-list
append temporaries (`dl`, `head`, `count`) in CALLEE-SAVED registers although no call happens inside the
append run, and one register serves unrelated values across the function (4B620: s0 = arg1, then the count of
appends 1-2, then the head of appends 3+, then the iterator's construct `this`, then `++idx`). Those are edg
POOL temporaries: one variable per type, reused by every later full expression, so the variable is live across
calls somewhere and uopt gives the whole thing an s-register. A cfe body can never reproduce that (its block
locals are separate variables). Rewrite the function as C++: 4B620 is `Obj::Obj(void *a1) : Base(a1)` (cfront
`this == 0 -> new(0xD8)` head, inline Base ctor with its own `new(0xCC)` fallback and external BB ctor, vptr
store at 0x28, `DL::add(hi, lo)` inline appends, the 4E244 by-value index iterator); the first NCC draft
already had the exact prologue (s0..s4, self in s4) that the cfe body was "capped" on.

**2. Count the edg temp homes to fix the frame.** Under NCC every referenced local, named or edg temp, gets a
home top-down in declaration order (kit XCIX 1). With the dump (`isvar M 4 -N`) list the homes of the draft and
compare with the target's known slots (iterator copies, spilled scalars). For 4B620 the target had 11 scalar
homes between the named iterator and the return temp, and 8 below the construct temp; the draft had 7 / 4.
Each inline construct adds a predictable count:
- a NAMED local inside an inline body (`Gfx *g = ...` in DL::add) is a new variable per expansion, homed where
  the expansion occurs (not pooled): this gave the target's per-append rotation of g (a0 / a1 / v0 / v1) and the
  8 lower homes;
- a parameter that is used once is substituted (no home); `if (0) { hi = lo = 0; }` in the inline keeps hi / lo
  as two pooled parameter temps (two homes for all expansions): frame and iterator slots then matched exactly
  (97.34 -> 98.82);
- a post-increment `head->count++` makes two pool temps (the base pointer and the old value);
- passing an argument through a second inline layer (`add(hi, lo) { gset(alloc(), hi, lo); }`) also creates
  parameter temps, plus one for the inner multi-use pointer.

**3. Value vs reference accessor decides which value is the pool temp.** In 4B620's loop the target holds the
ADDRESS `&data[idx]` in a pool register for the `&elem->m34` argument but the loaded VALUE for the
`elem->m64` reads. `Elem *cur()` for the m64 reads and `Elem *&ref()` for the `&ref()->m34` argument (96.09 ->
97.40); ref() for both is 93.6, a `a->data[idx]` spelling instead of `(*a)[idx]` 91-92. Also: IBase stores
`a` before `idx` in the target (`a = arr; idx = -1;`, +0.1).

**4. Volatile tell: a field re-loaded in every test while its neighbour stays CSE'd.** 4BAF4's viewport clip
`cx + hw < x || cy + hh < y || x < cx - hw || y < cy - hh`: the target loads cx / cy once (a2 / t0) but re-loads
hw / hh (0xB8 / 0xBC) into the SAME register (a3) in every test. Named temporaries, comma-assignments to one
variable, inline helpers with multi-use parameters and a Viewport member function all still let uopt CSE both
loads (cfe and NCC). Reading the two half-extents as `volatile int` reproduces it exactly (93.78 -> 95.41, two
rows of length back). Look for this shape -- one register reloaded per test with no intervening store -- before
spending time on CSE-breaking spellings.

**5. Per-site `lui` = a different symbol, again (4BAF4 cfe, 91.78 -> 92.03).** The `& 2` flag test read
`lui t7,0; lw t7,0x1C4(t7)` while the other &D reads share a held base; the flag word is its own blank USO data
symbol (new pin `D_4BAF4_flags = 0`). Same rule as kit C item 1.

**6. 4BAF4 as NCC: what moved and what did not.** Straight lift of the cfe body under NCC: 93.33; inline
`Ctx4B::next()` for the PKT macro: 93.78; volatile half-extents: 95.41; reading the context global directly (no
`gs` copy, kills an `or v0,v1`): 95.44; the 0xEE, 0xB3 and final 0x06 appends as `add(hi, lo)` with `s` / `r`
declared before `x`: frame 0xF0 and x..h homes at sp+0x80..0x74 exactly like the target, 95.58 (the first 0x06
append through add is lower). Residual: t-register colours shifted by one through the body (target self t3, iz
t5, spr t2), MAX / MIN merge copies in the scissor packets.

**6b. Nested alloc-or-given blocks with a static 8-byte copy are `new` of member-function callbacks (3E5E0).**
The cfe body had `node = alloc(0x10); if (node) { rec = node; if (rec || rec = alloc(0x10)) { key = rec; if (key ||
key = alloc(4)) *key = VT1; rec->obj = arg0; rec->pmf = *(8-byte static); } *node = VT2; }` three times. That is
`new Leaf(obj, pmf)` with: root `struct K { virtual void f(); }` (4 bytes, its vptr is VT1), `struct CB : K {
void *obj; PMF pmf; CB(void *o, const PMF &p) { obj = o; pmf = p; } }` with NO virtuals of its own (so its ctor
stores no vptr), and leaves `struct CB1 : CB { CB1(...) : CB(o, p) {} virtual void f(); }` whose (empty) ctor
stores VT2 last -- exactly the target order K vptr / obj / pmf / leaf vptr. Rules measured: a class-level
`operator new` adds one more protocol level (75.07); declaring the leaf as the class holding obj / pmf puts its
vptr BEFORE the members (66.41, edg sets the vptr after the bases and before members / body); the PMF parameter
by value goes through a stack temp, by const reference it is copied straight from the static. 75.74 -> 91.78.
Residual: the new result (an edg temp, s1 here) is a2 spilled to the temp area at sp+0x2C in the target, with
rec / key in s0 / s1; passing the new-expression directly as the call argument changes nothing.

**6c. 40070 as a C++ ctor: cfe 95.03 -> 99.28 (NM-only NCC donor, length 564 = target).** Shape: external
`BB(void *)` that ITSELF declares a virtual (only then does the vptr land at 0x28, after BB's 0x28 data bytes; a
first virtual in Base put it at 0xB0), `Base : BB` with a `W4 { M4 m; W4() {} }` member at 0x2C (the 4E584 nested
protocol) and a body `gl(this); zero();` where the zeroed `float z[3]` lives in a separate inline `zero()` (a
named local of the ctor body itself is declared BEFORE the member-protocol temps and lands two slots too high),
`Obj : Base` with a member at 0x104, and the Vec3 copies as `dc.set(b4)` / `f4.set(cc, d8)` with BY-VALUE V3
parameters (the target's int-word copy into a stack temp followed by float member stores: 79.65 -> 96.47).
Then the decisive one: the 0x104 member's element is a FLOAT zero (`struct M4f { float a; M4f() { a = 0.0f; } }`).
That use inside the member protocol keeps the FP zero constant's live range colourable across the protocol
calls, so uopt rematerialises `mtc1 zero` after every call there exactly like the target (three words); with an
int element the zero piece is uncoloured (adjsave -0.5 in the zdbug:5 listing) and materialised once at the
join (length 556). The 0x2C member must stay int (float there: 93.77). Residual: frame 0x50 vs 0x70 (four more
homes between z and the set() temp, more at the bottom) and the 0x104 element store (`sw zero` in the target,
`swc1 fv1` here); `set3(x, y, z)` helpers, a float-param member ctor and block-scoped z: flat.

**7. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- 4B0A8 as real C++ (ctor, inline DL::add, 4E244 iterator): 88.8 first draft; naming the DL / element / field
  temporaries of the loop body (`DL *d = m40; char *a1v = it.cur()->m6c; s32 a2v = ...`) gives the target's

## kit CIV (agent-g 2026-10-24, run 164): C++ `new` in cfe bodies, edg home allocation order, 31C0 NM port <a name="kit-civ-agent-g-run-164"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts. bootup func_000031C0 93.61 -> 99.61 (808 bytes) as an NCC NM-only donor
(`src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso_ncc_31C0_nm.cpp`, Makefile stanza after 8BD4's): every word but the sp offsets
matches (202/202), frame 112 vs the target's 144. Code % unchanged (79.64). Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/g164/`
(`c31/fr.sh BASE.cpp VARIANTS.py NAME` = NCC compile + target-to-build sp-offset map; `py/hm.py OBJ FUNC` = first
instruction per sp offset; `py/md.py OBJ` = .mdebug local symbols of a `-g3` compile (named locals only);
`toy/h.sh X.cpp` + `toy/dec.py` = dump-compiler homes per function and the decoded `ustr` itab, e.g.
`M-12=R2 M-16=M-12` = "home -12 gets the call result, home -16 copies it").

**1. Tell: object construction written as C.** 31C0's cfe body read `obj = alloc(0xB8); if (obj != 0) { p = obj;
if (p == 0) { p = alloc(0xB4); if (p == 0) goto post; } init(p, &D); p->vt = ...; member at +0x2C with two nested
this==0 tests; ... } post: obj2 = obj;` plus calls `f(0, ...)` that return the next object. That is:
- `obj = new Obj2;` with a GLOBAL inline `operator new(unsigned n) { return alloc(n); }`, Obj2 : Obj adding 4
  bytes (0xB8), Obj's ctor inline = out-of-line base `B(void *)`, vptr +0x28, member `M m` (M contains N, both with
  inline ctors -> the two protocol tests), body `fin(this); vec(pos, V3(0, 500, 0))`. Only the BASE ctor keeps its
  this==0 fallback (at sizeof(Obj) = 0xB4); the new-expression's own protocol is folded.
- toy (`toy/t1.cpp`): global operator new -> the result is the new-temp on both arms (`beqz v0` straight to the
  join, which copies the temp: the target's `lw t7,116; sw t7,120`). `new (4) Obj` (placement with an extra
  argument) or a class-specific operator new keep a this==0 retest with fallback alloc and give the null arm
  `obj = 0` (one more slot and a `b` / `sw zero`). An out-of-line ctor is called as `ctor(0, args)`.
- the `f(0, a3v, obj, 0.0f, 500.0f, -1500.0f, p4, &D)` calls are `new WA(a3v, obj, ...)` with out-of-line ctors
  (same bytes as the extern-C calls; rename `__ct__2WA...` with objcopy); case 1's
  `alloc(0x15C); if (e) { B2(e, obj, 0, 500, -1500); e->vt = &D_7120; ...}` is `new KB(obj, a3v)` with an inline
  ctor over the out-of-line base B2 (as `e = alloc` C it reloaded e into v0, target v1; as `new KB` exact).
- the tail `tail(parent + 0x10, n); if (n->owner) n->dirty = 1; n->owner = parent;` x2 is an inline `P::add`.
- the -1500.0f literals are two separate RoData words (+0x530 / +0x534); NCC also emits two pool entries.
Result: the 93.6 cfe body with pads / struct copies became a 202/202 C++ body with no tricks except one BB split.

**2. `if (1) {}` as a live-unit split for a v0 / v1 pair.** 31C0's tail copies `a3v->v[0..2]` to obj then to h:
the dump showed a3v's tail piece (6 loads, adjsave 5.0) coloured before obj's (2.5) -> a3v v0, target obj v0 /
a3v v1. `if (1) {}` after the first h copy (8 positions swept, two equal winners) gives the target's colours
(99.34 -> 99.69). Inline copy helpers, V3 operator= / set forms, macro add: no change.

**3. edg home allocation, measured (all with `toy/h.sh` + `dec.py`).**
- named locals first, top-down in declaration order (kit XCIX 1); then edg temps.
- `A *a; a = new A2;` (A2 derived from A): homes a, R, T, A-this, N-this. R is the derived-to-base CONVERSION
  temp (`M-8 = M-12`); with `A2 *a` or `void *a` it is absent. A second `new K(...)` later REUSES R's slot as its
  new-temp (pool reuse by type), which is why 31C0's KB new-temp sits above the Obj2 new-temp in the port.
- an inline ctor's parameters get homes only when their argument is not substitutable; `KB(void *o, char *a)`
  called with two function parameters homes both (`M-12 = P0, M-16 = P4`), called with a local and a parameter
  it homes none; `if (0) { o = 0; ... }` keeps them, but as POOL temps they land in freed slots of the same type
  (o in T's slot, a in Obj-this's slot) and float ones below the member-ctor homes.
- an inline-body temporary is homed when its inline LEVEL is expanded: `V3(0, 500, 0)` directly in Obj's ctor
  is homed right after Obj-this; moved into an inline `initPos()` called by the ctor it lands below the M / N
  this homes. A V3 temp of a statement in a `{ }` block at the end of the function is homed at the bottom.
- a V3 ctor that forwards to an inline `set(a, b, c)` adds two homes per construction.
31C0's target order below the named locals is T 116, X 112, Obj-this 108, KB-new-temp 104, five words, the
V3 temp 72-80, four words, the tail V3 temp 44-52. Not reproduced: `Obj2 *t` / `void *` / `Node *node` copies,
decl-init, cast / placement / explicit-lowering forms (explicit 90.3), Obj2 ctor bodies, a virtual in Obj2, KB
with `if (0)` kept parameters, `new KB` in an inline helper, `B2 *hb` conversions (all frame-only moves or
lower). Next step: count the target's slots against a breadth-first inline-expansion model (KB's temps come
before Obj's level-2 body temps in the target).

**3b. More home-order probes (toy `toy/gen.py`, `dec2.py` prints every itab op that touches each home).**
- Without the conversion temp (`A2 *a` / `void *a` / `(A *)(void *)new A2`) the later `new K` temp still finds a
  freed slot of the pool; with a NAMED `K *k` / `B *b` result variable the K new-temp gets a fresh slot, but above
  the A2 new-temp (named locals first, then temps). No spelling put a fresh new-temp BELOW the base ctor's `this`
  as 31C0's target has it (KB new-temp at sp+104 under Obj-this at sp+108).
- `new KB` behind one or two inline helper layers (`mkB`, `mkB2`) and every obj type (Obj *, void *, Obj2 *):
  frame unchanged (Obj2 * flips the body into s-registers, 78.8).
- PROGRESS on the first four homes: `void *objv; objv = new Obj2(a3v);` (no conversion temp R) with
  `Obj2(char *k) { if (0) { x = (int)k; x = (int)k; } }` (a kept ctor parameter, no code) gives
  objv -24, T -28, k -32, Obj-this -36 = the target's obj 120 / T 116 / X 112 / Obj-this 108 (frame 112 -> 112:
  the KB new-temp then reuses T's or k's freed slot). With `Obj2 *objv = new Obj2(a3v);` (declaration) T is NOT
  freed (decl-bound) but k is, and the KB new-temp takes k's slot. The target's KB new-temp at 104 is a FRESH slot
  right below Obj-this, so in the original neither T nor X was free when case 1 ran (both decl-bound or not
  pooled); not reproduced yet (mkB / mkB2 / mkB3 nesting does not change it).
- So the target's eight extra homes (1 + 5 + 2) are not explained by inline nesting, conversion temps or pool
  reuse in this edg; next idea is a different class shape for Obj2 / KB (members with inline ctors that emit no
  code) counted with `dec2.py` first.

**3c. b5 32C8 (cfe, 99.93) residual from the zdbug:5 dump.** The vF8 / vEC block is ONE flow-graph node of 12
memory ops (uE8 load + store, l134 load, 3 stores, l138 load, l13C / l140 loads, 3 stores; `if (1) {}` ends it).
l134 (bit 105, adjsave 3.0) and l13C (bit 116) are both uopt-coloured and interfere (same node), so l134 takes f0

**1. Copy + kill INSIDE the call argument (gl 51448).** 51448 is `o = new Obj; a0->28 = a0->C = a0->10 = o;

target stores o into n's HOME (`sw s0,40(sp)` before the call) and reloads n into a1 after it; the cfe body kept n
coalesced with o in s0 (a block-scoped `char *n = o;` is copy-propagated). Fix:
`gl_func_00000000_51448v(l + 0x10, (n = o, o = 0, n));` with function-scope `char *l; char *n; char *o; f32 k;` (that
declaration order is what gives frame 0x30 with n at 40 and the l spill at 44; 4 of 24 orders do). Statement forms
`n = o; o = 0; call(l + 0x10, n)` already fix the a1 reload (96.00) but schedule `or a1,s0` before the home store;
only the comma inside the argument gives the target's `sw s0,40(sp); or a1,s0`. This is kit XCIX 4 (copy + kill)
applied to a cfront inline-expansion argument. Tell: an inline helper's parameter that the target keeps in its own
home and reloads into the ARGUMENT register after the call, while ours stays in the source's s-register.

  first; every source order (720 permutations of the six init stores, 60 with the k load and 1.0 placed), comma /
  side-effect-in-address forms, a vt / ff local, `register`, a doubled vptr store (the first one is removed with its
  LDA), volatile on either store and typed-lvalue variants give either vt-first stores or 0xFFFF in t6. Open.

  at M-8) but edg sets the vptr before any ctor-body load, while the target loads k (D+0x1BB0) before the vptr store:

## kit CIX (agent-g 2026-10-25, run 167): pooled-temp LR merging re-ranks uopt colours (B154 + B624 exact) <a name="kit-cix-agent-g-run-167"></a>

**Summary.** Three exacts. timproc_uso_b5_func_0000BDEC (600 bytes, cfe 95.82 -> 100) as a new NCC donor
`src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5_ncc_BDEC.cpp` (Makefile `TIMB5_BDEC_DONOR`, no pins), and two timproc_b5 AC20-family
NCC donors promoted from NM-only:
timproc_uso_b5_func_0000B154 (532 bytes, 98.90 -> 100, `src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5_ncc_B154.cpp`, Makefile
`TIMB5_B154_DONOR`, pin `timproc_uso_b5_func_0000B154_bss`) and timproc_uso_b5_func_0000B624 (556 bytes, 99.92 -> 100,
`..._ncc_B624.cpp`, `TIMB5_B624_DONOR`, pin `timproc_uso_b5_func_0000B624_bss`). Code 79.94 -> 80.16 %. NM: mgrproc
2B7C 97.56 -> 97.68. Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/g167/` (`nccg.sh` / `ccg.sh SRC UNIT FUNC [KEEP.o]` = NCC / cfe compile
+ objdiff score, keep path now relative to the caller's cwd; `run.py` / `runc.py BASE VARIANTS UNIT FUNC` = parallel
variant scorers; `zdn.py` / `zdc.py SRC FUNC` = zdbug:5 LR dump for NCC / cfe; `dis.py OBJ FUNC`; for cfe, a whole-TU
copy with `#define NON_MATCHING 1` prepended compiles standalone in ~1 s and scores like the tree).

**1. The lever: a pooled temp that reuses a slot merges LRs.** edg allocates parameter temps of inline calls (and
other scalar temps) from a per-type pool; when an earlier temp is dead its slot is handed to the next request of the
same type. Both uses are then ONE ucode variable (`M 6 -56vreg` in the dump), so uopt builds one live range whose
adjsave is the sum of both. The colouring order (priority, then bit) changes with no extra frame home. Tell: a
two-colour swap between sibling temps (e.g. x / y differences in f0 / f2) whose dump shows equal adjsave (1.0 / 1.0,
coloured in bit order) -- give the one that must be coloured FIRST a later reuse.
- B624: the target head is x f2 / y f0 (B154's target is x f0 / y f2: the colours come from the REST of the function).
  `inline void one(Quat &q, f32 xa) { if (0) { xa = 0.0f; } V3 a(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f); q.rot(&a, xa); }` called as
  `one(o->q, o->f114)`: the `if (0)` keeps xa a real temp (without it the argument is substituted, 95.15), the temp
  reuses the slot of the head V3 ctor's first parameter (the x difference), the merged LR (adjsave 1.33) outranks y
  (1.0); the dump shows it coloured f2 with f0 forbidden (the merged range now reaches into block 1 and meets an f0 LR
  coloured before it), and y then takes f0. A named
  argument (`f32 ang = o->f114; one(o->q, ang)`) is copy-propagated: colours revert.
- B154: `o->sc.all(o->f118)` with `void all(f32 v) { f32 s = v; x = s; y = s; z = s; }` -- v reuses the x temp
  (adjsave 2 -> 4, x coloured first = f0 as in the target); the run-166 `while (0) { dx = 0.0f; }` anchor was only
  imitating that order and cost a misplaced home.

**2. Frame homes in this family (measured with `-g3` + `g164/py/md.py` and an all-sp-offsets listing).**
- B154: the named `s` inside `all()` is the word the target has between the third axis vector and the pooled
  `this` temp (inline-level named local, homed at the bottom of the if-block region).
- B624: target order a1 72, one word, a2 56, a3 44, this 40. With `one()` the first axis vector is one()'s inline
  local; the block-2 angle as a block-scoped `{ f32 ang = o->f110; V3 a(0,0,1); rot }` gives the word between a1 and a2;
  the block-3 angle as a named `f32 ang3;` declared at the IF level (before the `one()` call, assigned just before the
  third rotation) is homed above a1 instead of between a2 and a3 -> exact (shadowing `ang` at the if level also
  matches; the landed form uses ang3).
- B154 V4: `set(a, b, c, d) { w = d; x = a; y = b; z = c; }` -- the w store first makes the f120 load follow the sE8
  stores (ours hoisted it into f12; target f0).

**3. Dropping a superseded NM body needs a placeholder.** With the cfe NM bodies of AC20 / B154 / B368 / B624
removed, the non_matching tree compiled `INCLUDE_ASM`, which emits a `<func>.NON_MATCHING` marker symbol; the splice
then skipped (bytes equal) and the report scored all four donors 0 (lost exacts AC20 / B368). An empty
`#ifdef NON_MATCHING void f(char *arg0) { } #else INCLUDE_ASM #endif` gives the splice a body to replace (0x8 ->
donor size); the ROM tree is unchanged (`replace-body-skip`). Gate this with refresh-report, not only the ROM cmp.

**4. BDEC: the cfe operand-order cap is an edg tell; an inline int keeps a constant out of CSE.**
- The cfe body's residual (14 rows) was every `mul.s $f, $f20, field` / `addu a2, s2, field` with the named operand
  FIRST (cfe canonicalises; edg emits operands as written) plus the 192-web numbering. Compiled as C++ the order is
  right, but `(float)255 / denom` becomes `div.s $f2,$f20,$f20`: edg folds the cast, and uopt CSEs the 255.0 literal
  with denom's constant value. Under cfe the cast survives into ucode as a CVT that uopt folds after CSE.
- `inline int full() { return 255; }` and `a = (f32)full() / denom;` reproduces that: the inline call is not folded
  by edg, uopt folds the cvt late, and the target's fresh `lui 0x437f` numerator appears (92.27 -> 96.49). `255.0f`,
  `2.55e2f`, `(f32)(s32)255`, `(f32)0xFF`, `(f32)(255.0 / denom)`, int / short / unsigned char variables (the cvt then
  stays at runtime, 612 bytes) and an inline returning `255.0f` all fail.
- Then the natural structure: named `a` assigned in both arms of the dim test, `col[3] = a` at the top of EACH arm of
  the second test (the target's join reload / store; a single `col[3] = a` before the test leaves the store in the
  branch delay, 98.87), and the colour buffer declared first as `float col[5]` (frame 104; a leading `volatile float`
  pad matches too, not used). Declaration order of the other locals is free (24 / 120 permutations exact with the
  buffer first). Tell for the lever: a cfe NM body whose residual is commutative operand order plus a constant that
  the target materialises again although an equal-valued variable is live.
- The same 255-numerator note sits on b5 func_000010xx (line ~855, "the same float-const-CSE cap as BDEC") and C310;
  C310 under NCC with the lever is 93.74 (cfe 94.88) -- its other spellings were tuned for cfe.

**5. Other gains / negatives (time-boxed).**
- mgrproc 2B7C 97.56 -> 97.68: the case-3 tail re-reads `arg0->0xD4` into a3 (the target reuses a3; a separate h
  was v1). Left: `held = a3 + 0x490` (target: its own web in v0, spilled at its home sp+92) -- cfe folds held + 0x10
  into a3 + 0x4A0 in every spelling; an address-escape gives the length but a ugen temp; a C++ port (inline method on a
  member at 0x490, pooled this) also folds (90.6). s0 / s1 counter / string swap unchanged.
- B624 before the lever: V3 ctor parameter orders (a reversed-parameter ctor colours right but evaluates y first:
  load order wrong, 99.83), const-ref ctor parameters (+8-24 bytes), dot() operand / member / pointer spellings, rot()
  parameter keeps with named angles: none.
- CEB4: C++ `Col` class copies 560-664 bytes (target 428); the cfe body compiled by NCC folds the then-arm (94.04);
  goto / `||` / empty / `if (1) {}` then-arms fold (94.37); block 1 without the init (no PRE hoist, 85.9);
  `if (1) {}` after the grey loads leaves the 1.0 remat before the sel load.
- titproc 116C: the target's 4-entry jump table (`sltiu at,t6,4`) -- a 4-label switch compiles to a compare chain
  under both cfe and NCC (toy: 5 labels are needed for a table at -O2); the C keeps an empty `case 4:` (99.12).
- D884 / DF14 EE6C flag word: the target reloads the word after every store with a fresh `lui tN` (no base CSE, no
  store forwarding). A volatile scalar CSEs the base into a register (lui + addiu), same-symbol non-volatile accesses
  forward, u32-load / s32-store puns forward, per-site symbols let the scheduler hoist the loads, 1-bit bitfields emit
  byte ops. Open. (NCC compile of the cfe body: 74.15, the volatile pads behave differently.)
- 32C8 (cfe 99.93): `fa = 0; vF8; if (1) {} vEC; v104 = fa` gives the target's structure (l134 / l13C share one colour,
  the zero is a uopt LR) but the zero is coloured AFTER l134 (bit 274, a constant LR) -> f2 / f0 swapped (97.66);
  extra fa defs / uses / placements: identical output.
- 32C8 under NCC (g164 draft `d32c8b.cpp`, 96.82): the section-4 inline-int trick applied to the zero, `h =
  (f32)izero()` with `inline int izero() { return 0; }` at all three zero sites (the alloc-condition comma, the
  post-ctor reset and the v104 vector), restores the target's per-path `mtc1 zero` (99.87, 1480 bytes = target);
  left: the vF8 / vEC constant colours. Zero vector first + `if (1) {}` between the vF8 and vEC lines gives EVERY
  colour (zero f0, -2500 / 2500 sharing f2, rings f4 / f6: constant LRs are coloured in first-USE order) but then
  ugen emits the zero `mtc1` and the v104 stores before the vEC part (99.36-99.40); the zero's first use must stay
  first for its bit and its stores last for the schedule -- dead `while (0)` / `if (0)` uses, an early `h =` at the
  function top or block top: no effect (a folded constant has no variable to anchor). The cfe body stays (99.93).
- bootup 31C0: `if (0)` keeps on P::add / KB parameters: lower (97.2-99.1).
- Front-end checks (cfe body compiled by NCC, all lower, so these stay cfe): mgrproc 1824 (NCC turns the 5-case inner
  switch into a compare chain, 86.0; the target has the table), gl 3430 (82.1), bootup E2D0 (a Vec3 rewrite 78-79),
  titproc 116C (91.8); and a 4-label switch with an outlying fifth label (`case 1000`) is still a compare chain.
- b3 13B8 / arcproc 16F4 / b1 1340 (the "BUF lda web in s3" twins, cfe 86.46 / 85.69): the cfe body compiled as

## kit CXI (agent-g 2026-10-25, run 168): game_uso 1DDC as the 24BC sibling in C++, pointer-pool slots across arms, the block-temp order cap <a name="kit-cxi-agent-g-run-168"></a>

**Summary.** No exact. game_uso_func_00001DDC (1528 bytes, cfe NM 99.10) gets a new NM-only NCC donor
`src/game_uso/game_uso_ncc_1DDC_nm.cpp` (Makefile `GAMEUSO_1DDC_NM_DONOR`, non_matching object only): 99.77, length and frame
= target; left: v0 / v1 on the two transform pointers and the f23D4 return slot 8 bytes low (coupled to the ugen t-ring,
section 4). Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/g168/` (`rel.py OBJ FUNC` = frame-relative used-slot map of ours vs target, one row per 24
words: the fastest way to see which temp region is short; `spmap.py` = aligned target -> ours sp-offset table; `frs.sh` /
`regs.sh BASE VARIANTS` = per-variant score + frame + row distance / key colours; `mk.py BASE VARIANTS NAME OUT`).

**1. Recognising the family.** The cfe body (two `if (1) {}` scoped pointers, Tri3i word-copy hops, shared fx / fy / fz result
slots) was a C imitation of C++ copy chains. Tells that the function is a sibling of an exact C++ donor: the same Self field
offsets (out 0x14, obj 0x38, src 0x3C, key 0x40, spd 0x94, 0xAC / 0xDC / 0xF4 / 0x10C) as 24BC / 28C0 / 2CC8, the same
callees (000023D4 returning a struct through a0, 070238 sqrt, 071028 normalise, 072EE8 push), and the key-3 arm word for word
the 24BC key-3 arm. Start from the sibling's classes, not from the cfe body: the first draft from 24BC's `V3` / `M4` / `Ctx`
scored 99.43 where a fresh class design had plateaued at 90-97.

**2. What each target shape is.**
- `lw t6,20(a0); sw t6,368(sp)` then stores through t6, `lw v0,368(sp)` before the second group: `Ctx c(a0);` (a stack object
  holding a0->out) declared in the arm, and `Out *o = c.getOut(); ...; o = c.getOut(); ...` -- the re-read after the float
  stores is the object member, not a named pointer (a named `Out *` is coloured; `Out *const &o = getOut()` makes a
  block-level temporary ABOVE the named locals; an address-taken pointer via `getOut(Out *&)` is stored but forwarded).
- `lw v1,60(a0); lwc1 160(v1); addiu v1,v1,112; lwc1 52(v1); lwc1 56(v1)`: `M4::getPos(V3 &v) const { v.x = m[3][0]; ... }`
  on `a0->src->mtx` with Body `{ char pad[0x70]; M4 mtx; }` (the `this` adjust to the matrix is the addiu; a `Vec3 pos`
  member at 0xA0 gives `addiu v0,v0,160; 4 / 8(v0)` instead).
- ctor temp -> `addiu a3,sp,252` word copy -> second word copy -> float copies into acc: `acc = diff * k;` with
  `V3 operator*(float s) const { return V3(x * s, y * s, z * s); }` and a by-value `operator=(V3 v)`; the else arms'
  extra hop is the first product's result copied out of the pooled return slot before the second multiply.
- `self += f23D4(a0);` with a const-reference `operator+=`: the call result is copied (lw / sw) into a block-level temporary
  that is homed above the named locals; the same for `a0->vel -= diff * sel;`.
- `ref.set(c.getOut()->pos)` float copies, `diff.set(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f)`, the V3 ctor through `set(a, b, c)` (with member
  stores in the ctor the FP colours of the products are wrong, 90 -> 96.4).

**3. Frame lever: operator= forwarding to set(const V3 &).** With `V3 &operator=(V3 v) { x = v.x; y = v.y; z = v.z; return
*this; }` the frame was 368 (target 384) and every arm's temps sat 4-16 bytes high. `V3 &operator=(V3 v) { set(v); return
*this; }` (set taking `const V3 &`) adds the reference-parameter slot per expansion and gives frame 384 with all lower rows
equal (`rel.py` rows 3 / 4 identical) -> 99.75. A named float in operator* (`float k = s;`) or a named reference
(`const V3 &v = *this;`) adds 4 bytes per call (392); `if (0) { s = 0.0f; }` keeps s as a temp but it is coloured (no frame
change, length + 16).

**4. Pointer-pool slots are shared across the if / else arms.** getPos's `this`, set()'s reference parameter and getOut()'s
return value are pointer temps from one pool; a slot first used in the key-3 arm is reused in the other arm and becomes ONE uopt
variable (kit CIX), so the arms' register choices are coupled. Observed: every frame-correct variant colours the key-3 source /
non-3 object pointer and the operator= parameter address with opposite members of {v0, v1}; the target has v1 for both. A dead
named local in the key-3 arm (`int zz; zz = 0;`, the form in the landed 24BC donor) flips the key-3 / object pair to the
target's v1 but then the parameter address and the push-call `c.getOut()` swap (and the ugen t-ring is one slot ahead); reading
ref through `c.out->pos` instead of `c.getOut()` fixes the f23D4 return-slot position (-140 -> -132) but also advances the
t-ring by one. The shipped donor keeps the getOut() form (key colours swapped, return slot 8 bytes low, ring right).
Moving the key-3 stores to `o->goal.set(m)` (pointer pool first used in the key-3 arm) does not move the non-3 slots.

**5. Two homes above the named locals in creation order = two NAMED locals declared first (99.75 -> 99.77).** The target
has the f23D4 copy at sp+340 above the final `diff * sel` copy at 328, both above ref. As block-level reference-bound
temporaries (`self += f23D4(a0);` / `a0->vel -= diff * sel;` with const-ref operators) edg homes them newest-on-top: toy
(`toy/t.cpp`, `t2.cpp`, `t3.cpp`) -- `a += g(); *p -= a * 2;`, both through an extern `use2(const V3 &)`, mixed, a derived
result type, `V3(g())`, either statement nested in `if (k)` / `{ }` (the nested temp drops below the named locals), a by-value
`add(V3)` (deep parameter slot): every form puts the later temporary on top. They are named: `V3 r; V3 e;` declared FIRST in the
arm (above ref / self / c / acc), V3 with NO user operator= so `r = game_uso_func_000023D4(a0); self += r;` and
`e = diff * sel; a0->vel -= e;` are the target's lw / sw word copies out of the return slot, and the acc / vel chains that need
the by-value parameter hop go through `void put(V3 v) { set(v); }`. Same lesson as B368 (kit CVII: removing the user operator=
gave the word copies), here for the frame order. Tell: two copy-target homes above the named locals in the wrong order.
97EC (99.97) does NOT follow directly: named `Vec3 eb, fb` + `XZ e(eb)` scores 99.58 (the (a - b) temp stays a block
temporary above them, frame 264 vs 272); `XZ d = a - b;` named between them 98.87 (920 bytes).

**6. Negatives (time-boxed).**

- bootup 76F4 (99.82): the post-call `lui v0 / lui a2` order -- a function-typed G alias (93.8), a second G array (93.7), named

**1. edg pools 4-byte temps by SIZE, not by type -- the inline nesting decides which slot (uopt variable) a temp gets.**
zdbug:5 on 43D38 showed one frame slot (M -16) holding the main loop's `Ctx *` inline `this` AND the `Elem *` this of a
later inline Elem member, and in 43D38's final form an `int` row index and a `Ctx *` sharing slots. A pooled slot is ONE
uopt variable, so whatever lands in the same slot merges live ranges (kit CIX) -- and a temp's colour depends on which
LRs its slot also carries (a temp whose slot is live across the row loop is forbidden the loop's a0 IV and takes a1).
The free list hands out the lowest free slot in allocation order, so the knob is HOW MANY temps are allocated before the
one you care about in each statement:
- an implicit-`this` member call allocates no `this` temp when called on `this`; `clr(this)` on a member
  `void clr(Elem *e)` allocates TWO (implicit this + e), which is what moved the else NoOp's nested `Ctx *` temp from
  slot -12 (v1 / a2) onto the loop's a1 slot -- the last two rows of 43D38;
- a keep-free inline (`at2(int i) { return &dl->buf[i]; }`) called with a parameter temp does not copy it (no extra
  slot); the kept form (`if (0) { i = 0; }`) does. Moving the row loop from `kill(k) { at(rows[k]) }` (keep) to
  `kill(int k) { gDPNoOp(ctx6C->at2(k)); }` called as `kill(rows7C[k])` removed one int slot, which moved the branch
  packet's `_g` home from sp+0x18 to the target's sp+0x1C (named block locals are homed after the temps allocated
  before them);
- route a value through an inline member's int PARAMETER to make it the pooled int temp: `link(int i)` / `end(int i)`
  put the branch row and the end row in the target's a2 (the end row tested against -1 in place, no named `e`).
Order of discovery: 97.51 (at() keep) -> 99.01 (branch call through at(i), head via keep-free at2) -> 99.62 (end test
as `if (rows7C[GS->hi] != -1)`) -> 99.78 (link / end members) -> 99.85 / 99.87 (row loop as kill()) -> 99.89 (kill via
at2) -> 100 (clr(this)). Also: the donor's call must bind to `gl_func_00000000` (USO baked reloc: the target `jal 0`);
binding to the real address passed objdiff but failed the ROM cmp.

**1b. The same lever closes 4D468 (99.76 -> 100).** The residual was the `p ? p : 0` node ternary's result temp (ONE pooled
slot for both merge sites) in a2 where the target has a3. Binding the FIRST of the three `(k, *(int *)(w + 0x1C), id)`
calls through `inline void bind(int k, int h, int id) { if (0) { h = 0; } gl_func_00000000(k, h, id); }` gives the
handle a kept (non-propagated) pooled int temp that reuses the ternary's slot; the merged LR is live across that call's
a2 setup, so a2 is forbidden and the ternary result takes a3 at both sites. Binding all three calls (or two) makes the
merged LR heavy enough to outrank the owner and swaps s1 / s2 (98.80); binding any ONE of them is exact. A keep on a
constant argument (`call3(p, 0xB0000B70, 0x100)` with keeps) is inert: uopt propagates the constant before colouring.
New pins: `D_4D468_x / y / z / w / a2 = 0` (baked USO relocs) and `gl_func_0004D468_bss = 0x3CB00` (the static guard
pair; the splice renames the donor-local .bss reloc).

**1c. 3E5E0 (94.32 -> 99.36, length 600 -> 608 = target, frame = target).** kit CVII / CX noted that all three
new-expression results shared ONE pooled home (M-20) and so one s1 LR; the target keeps the first two as short a2 LRs
spilled around the ctor call. Moving the first two registrations into `inline void reg0(char *a) { if (0) { a = 0; }
gl(&k1, &k2 + off, new CB1(a, pmf), 0); }` / `reg1(...)` (kept parameter, the new-expression straight in the call, no
named `n`: a named one costs a frame word) splits them off the loop's slot. Residual (25 rows): their spill slot
(target sp+0x2C = top-0xC, i.e. the FIRST temp slot; ours sp+0x20, still the loop's slot) and the inner ctor this
(target s1, ours v1). Without the keep on `a` it collapses (94.26); x through a kept `call0(int)` moves the spill to
0x24, a block-scoped loop `node` shrinks the frame (0x30).

**2. Frame homes with zero code: unused `volatile int` locals in a BLOCK at the right nesting level (40070).** The
target's four words between the inline zero()'s z[] and the V3 by-value temp, and four below it: `zero(); { volatile int
p1, p2, p3, p4; }` inside the inline Base ctor and `{ volatile int q1, q2, q3, q4; }` after the last call of the Obj ctor.
Unused volatile ARRAYS are dropped entirely (no frame change); scalars at function top go to the frame top. 99.35 -> 99.57,
frame 0x50 -> 0x70 = target; the only row left is the 0x104 element store (kit CVI: the target's `sw zero` with the FP-zero
LR unsplit; int element / punned / union / inline float-param fill forms all split the LR or spill, 96.7-96.8).

**3. 48510 (`Strip::add`, 97.29 -> 98.71).** `int idx[3]` (the target's array ends exactly at the frame top, sp+0x6C with
frame 0x78; `idx[4]` puts it 4 lower) + a volatile pad for the frame; the count read and the append as inline

then one ring slot. Micro-test (`void S::f() { if (nv >= mx - 1) g(); }`): EVERY spelling (operand order, `!(<)`,
named limit, inline getters, volatile nv, `(mx - 1) * 1`, cfe C) loads nv into the first ring register -- the target
order comes from the surrounding code, not the expression.

**4. 4E00C (90.75 -> 93.81): a loop over an ARRAY MEMBER unrolls, a pointer loop does not.** The target's tail is two
sub-objects: 0x148 `{ int w[6]; }` (w[0], four words, w[5]) and 0x160 `{ int e[8]; int c; }` whose 8-word clear the target
unrolls x4 (`v1 += 4`, compare 8). `for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) p[i] = 0` through an `int *` stays rolled; the same loop on an
array member inside an inline `Blk2::clear()` unrolls exactly like the target, and the 4-trip loop on `w[]` (inline
`zero(int k) { for (; k < 5; k++) w[k] = 0; }` called with 1) unrolls too, and the spill slot of the earlier call
matches. Residual: the target keeps the 4-trip loop's IV (`li v1,1; sll t6,v1,2; addu v0,a0,t6` + ascending stores),
ours folds it (`addiu v0,a0,4`, descending stores); every loop / parameter / keep spelling folds (keep: 86.96).
Length 284 -> 292 (target 300), so the post0b NM clip moved 0x2e9fc -> 0x2ea04 (62F08 NM offset 0x2e9b4). Gotcha: a
donor length change in post0b silently drops game_libs_func_00062F08 to 90 in report.json until the clip follows it --
always re-check the 62F08 sentinel after ANY post0b NM length change, not only after deliberate clip edits. And after

## kit CXIII (agent-g 2026-10-25, run 169): timproc_b5 8FC8 is cfe (jumptable) yet an NCC C++ NM donor beats its cfe body; edg's pooled new-expression temps vs explicit protocols; E68 init-placement lever; BB8C empty-test removal <a name="kit-cxiii-agent-g-run-169"></a>

**Summary.** 0 exacts. NM (report.json): timproc_uso_b5_func_00008FC8 (6496 B) 86.64 -> 87.71 (new NM-only donor
`src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5_ncc_8FC8_nm.cpp`, Makefile `TIMB5_8FC8_NM_DONOR`, ctor symbol renamed),
bootup func_00000E68 (3036 B) 87.04 -> 88.82 (cfe body edit), game_uso_func_0000BB8C (1008 B) 92.65 -> 93.31
(policy fix: the banned trailing `if (k) {}` on an uninitialised `k` removed -- it was costing score, not buying it).
Scratch: `/tmp/claude-1000/g169/` -- `ncc.sh SRC [KEEP.o]` (NCC + rename + objdiff score for 8FC8), `nccx.sh SRC UNIT FUNC
[OLD=NEW]` (generic), `od.py OBJ [lo hi]` / `odx.py` (objdiff-ALIGNED view: per-50-insn buckets of equal / arg-mismatch /
insert-delete, or the mismatching rows of a range -- use this instead of difflib side-by-sides, which misalign on
register-only differences), `combo.py BASE PREFIX opt1.py ...` (scores EVERY subset of a list of (old, new) replacement
sets, 24 threads, ~16k variants in ~4 min), `mkopt.py A B OUT.py` (turn a hand edit into an option file), `mover.py SRC
LO HI CMD...` (move each simple assignment down to just before its next use / up after its previous one, score each),
`cfesw.sh` / `cfefile.sh` (same for an in-tree cfe NM body).

1. **8FC8 can never match under NCC.** Its tail `switch` on the u16 mode is a 5-entry jumptable (`sltiu at,t1,5; jr`),
   and edg lowers every switch to a source-order compare chain (kit XVII, re-confirmed with a 6-case toy). Like its
   exact sibling 4118 (kit run 161) it is cfe code compiled from cfront output. The NCC port is still worth having as a
   comparison object: the cfe body carries an extra callee-saved register (s0-s3 where the target uses s0-s2 + f20),
   and the C++ class version gets the right set (s0-s2) once the four 0x70 rows are real classes.
2. **What the port is made of** (all in the donor head comment): base `B` (out-of-line ctor 04C678, vptr +0x28, name
   +0xC, inline `add()` = 07ACE0 + `if (n->parent) n->flag = 1; n->parent = this`), Sub30 / Sub2C, the 0x2BC Panel over
   an 0x2B8 base with out-of-line member ctors 2B74 / 32C8 (edg sets the base vptr BEFORE the member ctors, as the
   target), WA / WB / WC over the out-of-line `B2(char *, f32, f32, f32)` (0546DC) with an inline W16C child whose vptr is
   an imported vtable, Kid (05D0E0 is a cfront `ctor(0, ...)` call = `new Kid(...)` with an out-of-line ctor), S70 rows
   with a virtual `add()` at vtable slot +0x58 (`lh 0x58` / `lw 0x5C` / `jalr` / `addu a0`). Decode facts found on the
   way: every `DF_xxx` / `DS_xxx` "extern" and the `import_80807FB8 + 0x23C/0x270`, `D_807FEE6C + 0x2B8`,
   `import_808000CC + 0x31C` loads are RoData LITERALS (expected .rodata: 0x23C/0x270/0x2B0-2B8 = 1e7f, 0x244 -1030f,
   0x248/0x24C -/+1.5457f, 0x250 -0.0251f, 0x254 0.28f, 0x258 0.764f, 0x25C 0.972f, 0x260 0.0377f, 0x264 1.936f, 0x268
   0.296f, 0x26C 0.496f, 0x294 -750f, 0x298 -1.5582f, 0x2A4 0.728f, 0x2A8 0.288f, 0x2EC 0.34f, 0x2F0 -375f, 0x2F4.. 375f,
   0x300.. 2.89f, 0x320 4.712389f). Under cfe the extern spelling emits the same code; under NCC an extern FLOAT's address
   is a loop-invariant candidate (hoisted into an s-reg in the 8-item loop) where a literal is rematerialised -- use
   literals in NCC donors. The W16C ctor stores the literal 1e7f three times (one load); a `const f32 &` parameter
   version homes the argument temps. The mode mask is `int tu` (`and s0,s0,-4`); a `u16` adds two `andi`.
3. **edg pools new-expression temporaries** (by size, kit CXII) into function-scope variables whose live ranges span
   most of the function and take s0 / s1 everywhere. The target colours each allocation site's temporary separately
   (cfront temps). Writing a site as an explicit `T *p = (T *)alloc(n); if (p) { base-init; vptr; ... }` (and the
   inline base protocol as `if (bp || (bp = (T *)alloc(n2)))`) removes that site's pooled temp: Sub2C 86.46 -> 86.62,
   first Panel -> 87.75. But it is a global trade: converting the other two Panels, the WA/WB/WC widgets, the S70 rows
   or Sub30 each LOWERS the total (86.1-86.8); the 14-toggle subset sweep (`c4`) peaks at 87.76 (+0.01, not kept).
4. **Negatives (8FC8):** `if (1) {}` anywhere in an edg function body is a no-op (folded by the front end; it only
   matters inside inline bodies); `do {} while (0);` / dead `{ int zz; zz = 0; }` sweeps +-0.1; `S70 *volatile a..d`
   gives the target's derived s0 / base s1 in the rows but costs reloads elsewhere (83.5); explicit `char *vt` vtable
   variable for the 17 virtual calls frees s0 for `tu` (target) but colours vt t0 (target s1, a call-crossing variable --
   in the target the same register carries the add() parameter across 07ACE0 in the panel links); routing those links
   through vt gives vt s0 and brings s3 back (87.18); V3 setPos chains written as explicit copies 84.8; `set(f64...)`
   for the zero triple 83.9.
5. **bootup E68 (cfe NM body) 87.04 -> 88.82: initialise a counter right before its only user.** `k = 0` (the arr[]
   index, used only in phase 2) sat before phase 1; moved to just before `m = E68_MGR; ult = 0;` its live range no
   longer spans the vertex loop, it outranks `buf` for the last callee-saved register, and `buf` is spilled to 0x1CC
   and reloaded like the target. General tell: the target spills a long-lived pointer that your build keeps in an
   s-reg while one of your counters is homed -> shorten the counter's span. (`mover.py` automates the search; on the
   7C1C NCC donor and the 8FC8 donor it found nothing above +0.02.)
6. **BB8C policy fix:** the run-128 trailing `if (k) {}` (k uninitialised on the early return) was removed; the score
   went UP (92.65 -> 93.31), so the documented f20/f22 swap it "fixed" was compensated elsewhere.
