## kit CXIV (agent-c 2026-10-25, run 162): near-exact cfe bodies ported to NCC C++ -- macro `_g` homes, call-argument stores, kept pointers, store-forwarded decrement <a name="kit-cxiv-agent-c-run-162"></a>

**Summary.** Five exacts, all by porting an in-tree cfe NM body (98.6-99.99, every one "documented cap") to an NCC C++
donor spliced over an empty placeholder in both post0b trees: gl_func_00045178 (540 B, 99.99), gl_func_000445AC (876 B,
99.82), gl_func_0003B01C (380 B, 98.63), gl_func_0003D71C (220 B, 96.00), gl_func_0005AFD4 (156 B, 91.77): 80.27 -> 80.56 %
code. NM: game_libs_func_0004B2F4 98.23 -> 98.37 (NCC NM-only donor). Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/c162/` (`nn.sh X.cpp FUNC
MANGLEPAT [ctx]`, per-function `rXXXXX.sh`, `install.py` = placeholder + Makefile block, `gate.sh`, `commit.sh`).
**General lesson: a cfe body at 98-99.99 whose residual is a spill slot / base register / constant fold / store order is
often C++ -- port it before grinding the cfe body.** Each port below took 5-15 minutes; several of these had 100+ prior
cfe variants logged as negatives.

**1. A spill BELOW every named local is a block-scoped macro local (45178).** The cfe body spilled the gSPMatrix packet
pointer at its named home (sp+0x28); the target spills it one slot lower (sp+0x24, the temp area). Under NCC the stock
`gDma1p` macro's `Gfx *_g` is a block-scoped named local, and kit CXII's rule (block locals are homed after the temps
allocated before them) puts it under the ONE pooled temp of the preceding `n3 = c->dl->count++` post-increment. Recipe:
function-top decls in the cfe order (t, a, b, q, i, c, n3, m, v, r: NCC homes every referenced named local in decl order);
`i = c->mh->count++; m = &c->mh->buf[i];` then `n3 = c->dl->count++; gDma1p(&c->dl->buf[n3], 1, call(m), 64, 3);`;
the upper clamp bound as a literal (a named `hi` costs a home and frame word); the w1 call int-returning
(`gl_func_00000000_i`), the others void (kit XCIX). Explicit `n = h->count; h->count = n + 1;` gives the right homes but
swaps v0 / v1; the post-increment gives the target's mh v0 / count v1. Literal .rodata reloc -> `gl_func_00045178_rodata`
pinned 0x1B60 (three literals at +0 / +4 / +8 -> USO RoData 0x1B60..0x1B68).

**2. A store written AS the call argument (445AC).** `gl(D_445AC_b.x1C = new A40, 0x64, 1)`: the holder base becomes a v0
variable (target `lui v0; addiu v0; sw a3, 28(v0)`) and no named pointer home is allocated (frame 0x60 -> 0x58 = target).
Every spelling with a named `A40 *p` (struct member, inline `set()`, `(int)&D + 0x1C`, kept holder parameter) either folds the
base into `sw a3, %lo(D+0x1C)(at)` or costs the home. Also: under NCC a varargs call evaluates its arguments in source order,
so the last vararg loads into t7 like the target (cfe needed `v = D_glob_e` = a coloured variable in v1).

**3. Kept named pointers and the itab-order anchor on an EXPRESSION (3B01C).** `n = *b - *a` with V3 `operator-` returning
`V3(...)` and a BY-VALUE `operator=` (kit CXI) reproduces the three copy hops; both position pointers as named pointers with
`if (0) { p = 0; }` stop uopt folding `other + 0x54` into the load offsets (target `addiu v0, a1, 84`). The two uadd
expressions then tie at adjsave 4.0 and colour in itab-bit order; a dead `while (0) { b = &other->pos; }` at the TOP puts the
other+0x54 expression first (v0) -- kit XCIX's anchor works for CSE expressions, not only variables. Frame 0xC0 from twelve
top-level `volatile int` pads + `volatile int q` before `r` + `{ volatile int z1, z2; }` at the end (kit CXII homes).

**4. Kept destination pointer orders two base addius (3D71C).** The cfe residual "as1 schedules the src addiu before the dst
addiu" disappears with `Blk *d = (Blk *)gl_3d71c_dA0; if (0) { d = 0; } *d = *(Blk *)(D + 0xE8);` (d's addiu v0 first, then
the source's t6); and edg keeps the written multiply operand order (`o->x * factor`: the factor loads first, `mul.s ft4, ft2,

body's three allocations (0x10 unconditional, then 0x10 if `b == 0`, then 4 if `c == 0`, each with a null skip, the

`this == 0 -> operator new(sizeof(T))` fallback with its own null skip (Base's 4-byte alloc, Mid's 0x10), the Base vptr,

assignments in the ctor bodies are ACCEPTED by NCC but lose the null skips (75).

(per-site greedy over `DL::add` spellings / free DL-first inlines), `grid418.py` / `grid418b.py` / `perm418.py`
(41820 grids), `grid8.py` (250C8 fontId site grid), `zd.sh X.cpp` (zdbug:5 candidate table).

**0. 41820 = `void Self::init()` under NCC (94.72 -> EXACT), in five steps from kit CXVI's 93.98 draft.**
(a) The attach block `gl(&m10, q); if (q->f14) q->f4 = 1; q->f14 = this;` as a member `link(Rec *q)` with a KEPT q
(`if (0) { q = 0; }`): q goes to its pooled home and is re-read after the call, `this` is re-read from the parameter
home, length 588 = target (97.57). The third attach (on `new O44`) wants the plain member (97.73). End-of-body block
volatiles for frame 0x40.
(b) **A member call on `this` allocates a pooled `this` temp even when the body never uses `this`** (zdbug:5 ucode:
`ustr M-16 <- P` right before each call; it vanishes when the call is removed). It took the slot the Arr new-temp had
just freed, so q sat one slot lower (0x2C vs the target's 0x30 = the Arr temp's slot, which also makes them ONE uopt
variable coloured a2). The fix is a FREE inline with q FIRST: `inline void lnk(Rec *q, Self *s) { if (0) { q = 0; }
gl(&s->m10, q); if (q->f14) q->f4 = 1; q->f14 = s; }` called `lnk(D_41820_f, this)` (97.73 -> 98.16). s-first, `SB *s`
or keeping s are worse / inert.
(c) A trailing dead `if (s) {}` in lnk (kit XLVI lever E) made the SECOND attach's this reload a coloured v0 (it was a
t-ring load, which also shifted the O44 tail's t-ring by one): 98.16 -> 98.81 local. `if (this) {}` at a call site or a
second `if (s) {}` collapses the function to 572 bytes (edg then knows this != 0 and folds a protocol).
(d) **The first attach's this reload needed v1 (ours v0): keep the call's RESULT alive.** `int r = gl(&s->m10, q); ...
if (r) {}` at the end of that attach's inline keeps v0 (the return register) live through the attach, so uopt colours
the reload v1 -- the last instruction difference. The extra pooled int temp moved the &m10 uopt spill from sp+0x1C to
0x18; dropping one of the two end-of-body volatiles put it back. objdiff then showed only relocation rows (98.91
local = reloc noise); report.json 100.
(e) Promotion: donor renamed without `_nm`, the NM-wrapped cfe body replaced by an empty placeholder, the Makefile rule
switched to both trees (`init__4SelfFv=game_libs_func_00041820`, `__ct__3B44FPc=gl_func_00000000_41820_base`,
`__vtbl__3O44=D_41820_h`), new pin `gl_func_00000000_41820v = 0x00000000` (the blank void callee was never pinned: the
cfe body was NM-only). ROM cmp byte-identical; replace-body imported 64 donor relocs.
Rules worth reusing: when a kept inline parameter lands one pooled slot off, look for a member call on `this` in the
same stretch (its hidden temp) and switch to a free inline with the kept parameter first; when one reload is v0 where
the target has v1, keep a call result live past it with `int r = call(...); ... if (r) {}`.

**0b. 37348's last 4 words (kit CXVI: the post-call 0.0 in f2, target f0) close with agent-g's kit CXIX lever.** The
second push vector's zeros written as `z3(v2, 0)` with `inline void z3(V3 &v, int z) { v.x = z; v.y = z; v.z = z; }`:
the int -> float conversion of the constant is folded after uopt's candidate selection, so these three stores get
their own local zero (`mtc1 zero, f0`) instead of joining the head's 0.0 candidate (whose LR is forbidden f0 by k).

## kit CXIX (agent-g 2026-10-25, run 173): a later reuse of an FP constant joins the earlier candidate's live range (32C8 under NCC 160 -> 2 words), uopt emits a constant candidate's li.s at its first use, 31C0's hidden slot is the new-expression result temp <a name="kit-cxix-agent-g-run-173"></a>

**Summary.** 0 exacts (80.88 % code). NM gains (report.json): gui F04 97.35 -> 97.44, gui 3714 95.41 -> 96.09 (item 5,
commit f5a57f4eb). The run went to the near-exact queue; most findings below are diagnoses and negatives so the next agent can skip them. Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/g173/`:
`cmp.py SRC FUNC ASM [cc|NCC|obj]` (kit CXVII's, now deletes its temp objects), `var.py BASE FUNC ASM 'old|||new&&&...'`,
`tdis.py ASM [lo hi]` (disassembles a raw-`.word` / reloc-annotated .s), `zdparse.py uoptlist [LR...]` (one line per
zdbug:5 candidate: LR, colour, expr, adjsave, forbidden, live BBs, interferences), grids in `p32/` (`vgrid / zgrid /
lgrid / ogrid / cgrid / hgrid / igrid / agrid / fgrid .py`, all write to `sw/` and delete their files).

**1. An FP constant reused LATER in the function joins the earlier uses' candidate, and the long LR gets split at a
call (timproc_b5 32C8 under NCC: 160 -> 8 words).** Kit CXVII found the NCC port of 32C8 165 words off with the 0.0
constant's LR "split at the cA-block call". zdbug:5 shows why: the two value children at the END of the function
(`*(f32 *)(c + 0x10) = 0.0f`) are the same constant expression as the v104 / vDC zeros, so the candidate's LR runs
from the vector block to the end (BBs 48..73), is constrained, and uopt splits it into f0 / f2 / uncoloured pieces --
the fallback-path `mtc1 zero,$f0` disappears and every later word shifts. The target emits those two stores with a
local `mtc1 zero,$f8` / `$f10` (ugen temps, not the candidate). Writing them through an int parameter,
`inline void setv(char *c, int v) { FW(c, 0x14) = 0; *(f32 *)(c + 0x10) = v; }` / `setv(c, 0);`, gives exactly that:
the int -> float conversion of the constant is folded AFTER candidate selection, so the store gets its own local zero
and the vector zero keeps one unsplit LR (8 words; `FW(c, 0x10) = 0` int stores prove the point at 368 words, an
inline `f32 fz(int v) { return v; }` call does the same as setv). Rule: when a constant candidate's LR is split or
mis-coloured, look for the SAME constant used far away (other blocks, the function tail) and route that use through
an int-typed inline parameter. In cfe C the equivalent (`*(f32 *)(c + 0x10) = FW(c, 0x14);`) is inert -- cfe's 32C8
body did not have the problem.

**2. 32C8 after that: 2 words, the same residual as kit CXVII's cfe literal form.** Best form: v104 / vF8 / vEC in
natural order on ONE source line, `if (1) {}` between vF8 and the uE8 name (`v104.x = 0; v104.y = 0; v104.z = 0;
vF8.x = -2500.0f; ... if (1) {} uE8.v = ...; vEC.x = 2500.0f; ...`). Left: `mtc1 zero,$f0` before the l13C (2500)
load (target after). What decides it: uopt emits a constant candidate's `li.s` at its FIRST USE inside the first BB of
its LR (moving the zero's first use after vEC.x moves the mtc1 to the target position) -- but then the zero LR no
longer covers vF8's statements, or (with no BB split) the -2500 / 2500 candidates live in the same BB as the zero
and take f2 / f12. The target needs: zero coloured f0 over vF8's region AND defined after the l13C load, with l134 /
l13C both ugen f2. Grids (all floor 2): 1536 line layouts, 870 single-line zero positions, 664 BB-split x chained
`a = b = k` / `z = x` forms, 432 h-variable forms (`h = fz(0)` as a non-constant variable: target order, colours swapped
-- the -2500 / 2500 candidates adj 1.0 outrank the zero's 0.5), 336 int-converted vector constants, 2B74-style named
f / g / h locals. Without any `if (1) {}` the function changes globally (391 words, an extra s1 save): the split is
structural under NCC, whatever the original construct was. Exact 2B74 sibling for comparison: its BB head emits
`lwc1 f2 (-1500)`, `lwc1 f12 (1500)`, then `mtc1 zero,$f0` -- the other candidates' loads first, the zero last.

**3. 31C0 (NCC NM donor, 9 words): the hidden 4-byte slot is the new-expression RESULT temp.** zdbug:5 program
order: `M-32 = alloc(0xB8)` (T), the inlined ctor chain on M-36 / -40 / -44, then `M-28 = M-32; M-24 (obj) = M-32`.

C++ member over the same data, and the first natural NCC draft scores 86-97 at the target length. All three were
first drafts plus 2-6 spelling probes (minutes each). The Mesh object used by 54264 / 500EC / 50444 / 4FD00 / 4A308:
+0x44 triangle count, +0x54 planes (12 B), +0x58 normals (V3), +0x60 positions (S3 = 3 x s16), +0x68 triangles (8 B:
s16, then u16 i[3]), +0x78 colour bytes.

**0. 54264 = `void Mesh::sample(V3 &p, V3 &n, int t)`, a uniform random point in a triangle (85.12 -> EXACT).**
`u = rnd(); v = rnd(); if (u + v > 1.0f) { u = 1 - u; v = 1 - v; }`, the three positions through an inline
`V3(const S3 &)` ctor (the `* 6` index stays a multu with the 6 in a register -- no `mult` variable needed), w = 1 - u
- v, p = a*w + b*u + c*v per component, then the normals copied in through a BY-VALUE `void set(V3 v)` (the target's
int-word copy into ONE temp at sp+0x24, then float copy-out; plain struct assignment drops the temp, 792 B) and n
blended the same way. First draft 86.5; set() 97.9 at the target length; three function-scope volatiles before `V3 a`
= frame 0x78 and every home (98.11). The last residual was p's reload in v0 (target a1), so as1 hoisted the 12 constant
into a1 instead of p and could not raise the &tmp addiu above the p stores. zdbug:5 showed p's coloured piece alone in
the basic block after c's ctor (inline CTORS end a basic block; non-ctor inline members do not) with nothing in v0 live
there. **Fix: name c's S3 pointer and keep it past the p stores** (`cs = &verts[...]; V3 c(*cs); ... p stores ...;
if (cs) {}`, cs declared in place of one volatile so the homes stay): p leaves v0 and the hoists happen (99.02). The
dead test's extra blocks flipped two colour priorities (t*8 / the 6, 12 constants / p: v1 <-> a1, and u / v: fv1 <->
fa0); **a second dead test `if (t) {}` right after it restores both** (99.86), and the fold order `u = 1 - u` first
closes the last two words. ROM: the two rnd() calls go to gl_func_00000000 (baked jal 0); no relocs in the target.
Rule: when a parameter's reload takes v0 where the target has its arg register and nothing interferes, keep a v0-coloured
value (a named pointer from the previous statement) live across that block with a trailing dead test; if the extra
blocks reshuffle other colours, a second dead test on an unrelated live value can shift the priorities back.

**1. 608A4 = `void TextWin::draw(int big)` (84.27 -> EXACT, first draft 86.94).** Optional big-font switch (cw = ch =
8), a by-address `Pt p(0, 0x408)` for the frame call, the right edge clipped to 290, the title call, then one text call
per visible row whose length exceeds the horizontal scroll (`for (i = top; i < top + vis; i++, yy += ch)`, the bound
re-read after each call). The global draw context (&D_00000000, held in s4) was set with plain member stores in the
draft (86.9); **through inline members `size(w, h) { cw = w; ch = h; }` / `pos(px, py) { x = px; y = py; }` it is
EXACT**: the parameters of the inline are the target's otherwise-unexplained s0 / v0 values computed before the store
pair. Calls bound to gl_func_00000000 for the ROM tree (a donor calling gl_func_00034458 links a real address).
Rule: a pair of stores whose values sit in an odd register (s0 with no call between) is an inline member's
parameters.

**2. 500EC = `int Mesh::paint(unsigned t)`, a triangle graph-colouring step (91.72 -> EXACT, first draft 92.66).** For
each other triangle i sharing a vertex position with t, if `adj(i, t)` (out-of-line, renamed to the blank jal 0) give i
a colour from a wrapping counter (new pin D_500EC_cnt = 0) when it has none, reject if an adjacent triangle already has
it, else copy it to t. The cfe body's two constant-6 carriers, hand-spelt `((x<<2)-x)<<1`, goto layout and
retry block all fall out of `for (k = 0; k < 3; k++)` + an S3 inline `int operator==` (its result is the target's
xor / sltiu v0 and its `this` binding the target's `or v1,a1` / `or a0,a1` copies). Steps: the vertex written
inline at each comparison instead of a named `S3 &v` (96.91, length = target: the named reference had removed the
per-comparison this copies), `col[j] == col[i]` in the conflict scan (96.97), and **the candidate on the LEFT of
`==`** (`pos[tris[i].i[n]] == pos[tris[t].i[k]]`): 99.93 = relocations only. Rule: for an inline comparison operator
the operand order decides which side is `this` (copied) and which loads first -- grid both sides before anything else.

**3. 50444 (NM, 86.72 -> 91.94, length 484 -> 488 = target).** `unsigned intern(int start, Mesh *m, float *pos,
float *uv, unsigned max)` with the same S3 (and S2) inline `int operator==`; the position key through an inline
`S3(float, float, float)` ctor gives the target's loads-first order (member-wise stores interleave), the uv key
member-wise (the target interleaves those), member-wise inline `operator=` for the appends (struct assignment gives
lwl/lwr), and **`int start`** (signed) -- an unsigned start was 4 bytes long (a copy of the reloaded start into the
loop register). Residual: pos stays a register candidate (target: memory home stored at entry, base reloaded into t7),

`if (0) gl(&pos)` (homes every parameter, frame 0x28), the loop on `start` itself (s-register), element-left
comparisons, `o.x == x` inside the operator.

**4. Negatives (time-boxed).**
- 4FD00 (Mesh edge-midpoint test, 79.5 cfe): a natural draft with S3 `operator+=` sums, `V3(const S3 &)`, by-value

- 415A4 (module init, 84.34 cfe): best NCC 87.87 but 440 B (cfe NM 448, target 452; away, not kept). Open: the target

  function to give the target's alloc / test / ctor-call shape (an out-of-line ctor moves the alloc inside the callee).
  `(g1 = this)->pC` materialises &g1 (C++ lvalue assignment); a separate `g1 = this;` puts this in s0.
- 4B2F4 (98.37): flags `| 2` written into a new temp in the target (`ori t5,a2,2`) while flags itself is an a2

  memory variable (90.5); keeps on flags lose. Not reached.
- 40070: `M4f() { a = 0; }` (int literal into the float member) and an int inline parameter both keep `swc1`; the int

- 41D40 / 4B0A8 (AIter next()): for / do-while / named-result next() spellings are identical or lower; the two loop

- 31A74 under NCC: 86.66 at 552 B (cfe 90.72 at 564); prototyped char arguments and dropping the named locals do not
  recover it. 4A890: a variable reused for the ids copy and the list base gives the target length (352) at 82.6; a

- 4F2DC (screen-point raycast picker, cfe 88.56) as `int Picker::pick(int x, int y, V3 &out)` with V3 operators

## kit CXXII (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 177): two more cfe bodies are C++ (3B2EC Obj::height, 36F0C FreeCam::update) and beat their capped cfe forms as NCC NM donors; inline members with REFERENCE parameters are the target's memory homes and per-statement reloads; edg will not inline a member that contains a loop <a name="kit-cxxii-agent-c-run-177"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts. Three NM gains in game_libs_post0b by porting cfe / C-lift bodies to natural NCC C++
(report.json): gl_func_0003B2EC 91.56 -> 95.62 (`game_libs_ncc_3B2EC_nm.cpp`, 952 B, target 948, cfe 936),
gl_func_00036F0C 91.26 -> 93.21 (`game_libs_ncc_36F0C_nm.cpp`, 972 B, target 968, cfe 956), gl_func_0003C43C
94.28 -> 96.08 (existing C-lift donor edited, 864 -> 868 B, target 872). Code % unchanged (81.29). Scoring loop
used: compile the draft with NCC into a scratch .o, objcopy the mangled member name to the gl symbol, then
`objdiff-cli diff -1 build/src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o -2 draft.o -o - <sym>` and read `match_percent`
from the JSON (matches report.json to ~0.05) -- about 1 s per probe, so a 20-probe port fits in 10 minutes.

**0. 3B2EC = `int Obj::height(int max, f32 *out, f32 x, f32 z)` (ground heights under (x, z), sibling of 3BE1C /
3B9C0).** The cfe body needed volatile pads, an escaped `Vec3 p`, a `c[2]` array and two loop-end symbols to reach
91.56. As C++: the grid lookup through inline Obj members `toCell(const V3 &p, int &cx, int &cz)` (two
statements `cx = (p.x - col->grid->x0) / col->grid->cw`), `cellOf(const V3 &p)` (bounds test, `cz * w + cx` or
-1) and `list(int cell)`. **The reference parameters ARE the target's memory homes**: p stored at sp+140 and
re-read with lwc1, cx / cz stored at sp+60 / 56, and `self->col` re-loaded from `this` before every grid access
(stores through an `int &` may alias). First draft 71.9 without the members, 86.7 with them. Then: the triangle
offset spelt `((i << 2) - i) << 2` (kit-run-110 rule still holds under NCC: plain `col->nrm[i]` is a multu by a
12 in an s-register; length 960 -> 948 = target, 90.65); ten unused function-scope `volatile int` scalars for the
0x98 frame (an unused volatile ARRAY is trimmed, no frame change); the face as an inline `Col::face(int i)` with
the remap pointer in a local (`s16 *r = remap; return r ? &faces[r[i]] : &faces[i];` -- one remap load plus the
target's `or v0,v1` this copy), **the face call BEFORE the verts load** (95.57 from 94.0: the target's verts load
sits between the this copy and the remap branch), the next-vertex table start through its own symbol (not
`&D_00000000`, which CSEs with the float-pool base held in an s-register), and the edge walk as a counted
`for (k = 0; k < 3; k++)` over `f->vi[k]` / `f->vi[next[k]]` (IDO LFTRs it into the target's two pointer walks
with the end constant hoisted into s0). Residual (952 B, +1 word): the post-loop `if (k != 3)` end constant
becomes a register COPY of the loop end (`or s6,s0` in the outer preheader) where the target rematerialises
`lui/addiu` at the test; with a pointer walk the same symbol for both ends CSEs into s0 and the freed s-register
goes to `max` (target keeps max in its arg home), two different symbols hoist the second into its own
s-register. Every k spelling tried (`unsigned k`, `k != 3` bound, `k < 3` post test = sltu, `if (k == 3) {..}`,
do-while, k at function scope, s16 / u8 k = 82-83) is identical or worse. Not reached.

**1. 36F0C = `void FreeCam::update()` (debug free camera).** Pad buttons 0x40 / 0x80 add / subtract 100.0 (a
double literal on the zero variable, as in the cfe decode), 0x400 reads the stick, the three-way |m| > K test
accelerates through `accel` (`int a = accel; int n = a + 1; if (a < 100) { accel = n; a = n; }` = the target's
`addiu t1` in the delay slot + `or v0,t1`), the move vector rotated by the camera matrix, 0x1000 turns yaw /
pitch, pitch clamped to +-89, the boom (0, 0, dist) rotated by pitch then yaw through two calls taking
`&w.y, &w.z` / `&w.x, &w.z`, added to the target-node position. Levers in order: `V3 v, w` as structs with an
inline `operator+=(const V3 &)` (72.6 -> 81.1: by-reference use keeps them in memory with the target's dead
zero stores); `Cam *volatile c = cam` + the 3x3 rotate as an inline `Cam::xform(V3 &o, f32 x, f32 y, f32 z)`
(85.8: the volatile gives the target's reload after every store, the inline's `this` reads it ONCE for the nine
matrix loads -- the cfe form needed a separate single read); the target-node position through `M &m =
c->tgt->m` (a sub-object reference = the target's `lwc1 96(v1); addiu v1,v1,48; lwc1 52(v1)` pattern, 87.9);
**`operator+=` written `x = x + o.x`** (88.8 -> 92.7: NCC keeps the written operand order, kit CXVII); homes
c 132 / v 116 / w 92 by declaring `Pad *p;` (assigned later) between c and v and the move scalars between v
and w (under NCC every scalar local gets a frame slot in declaration order, even when it lives in a register);
`pitch = pitch + -p->sy * 4.0f` (93.16). Residual: the target computes `&w.y` / `&w.z` into a1 / a2 at entry
(named pointer locals and references are rematerialised at the call instead) and colours the move scalars
f14 / f16 / f12 (ours one register up); the clamp result lands in f12 instead of f2. Init-order / decl-order
permutations of the move scalars are identical.

**2. 3C43C (C-lift NCC donor, 94.28 -> 96.08).** Two scheduling residuals from the run-134 lift fixed: the
limit constant read into a block-scope `{ float k = *(float *)(D + 0x1AB8); lim = k; }` (the target keeps the
constant in f16 and copies it into lim's f12 with `mov.s`, so the later -600 constant reuses f16), and
`float dd = 0.0f + dist[best];` written right after the f24 store (the target loads dist[best] and adds the zero
above the h10 halfword store; the stored-through-float hit record keeps a later read below it). Residual: 24
extra frame bytes below the two 0x28-byte staging records (target frame 0xE0, ours 0xF8). Measured: every
scalar local and every float `?:` (the ABS macro) costs one 4-byte NCC slot; moving the five scalars above the
arrays leaves 24 bytes at the bottom; the target's 0x28 spacing of the staging copies (sp+108 / sp+68) is NOT
two unused Hit locals (unused struct locals are trimmed). A real C++ draft (`Obj::nearest`, V3 `operator+=`,
by-value `set(V3)`) gets the target frame 0xE0 exactly but scores 89-94 (the by-value temp lands at sp+60).

**3. Rules.**
- An inline member taking `const V3 &` / `int &` of a caller local is how NCC code gets memory-homed locals and
  per-statement `this->member` reloads at -O2; reach for it before volatiles when a target re-reads a local it
  just stored.
- edg does not inline a function containing a loop (a member `int edges(...)` with the edge `for` stayed
  out of line, 276 B), so loops stay in the caller.
- Under NCC, order matters twice: the frame follows the declaration order of every scalar, and the first
  inline call's `this` copy / loads are scheduled where the call is written -- try moving one statement
  above its neighbour before anything else (3B2EC face-before-verts +1.6).
- Negative (time-boxed): 5F0B8 not tried as C++ (memory-homed xx / xy temporaries with store-then-reload pairs;
  needs a design), 30AF4 / 2E354 have jumptables (cfe only), 201B8 / 250C8 are in the audio range.

Gate (agent-c on cdf5045d5, not rebased by request): full make ROM byte-identical (cmp), verify-blocks 6/6,
`make non_matching_objects` 0 errors, no exact lost vs local origin/main, sentinels 551E0 / 55B10 / EBC8 / C5B0 /
62F08 at 100, 81.29 % code. post0b NM clip 0x2ea44 -> 0x2ea68 (3B2EC +16, 36F0C +16, 3C43C +4; 62F08 NM offset
0x2ea18). New pin `D_3B2EC_c = 0x00000000`. Purge: `build/non_matching/src/game_libs/game_libs_post0b.c.o`, new NM
donors `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_3B2EC_nm.cpp.o`, `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_36F0C_nm.cpp.o`,
changed NM donor `build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_3C43C_nm.cpp.o`.

## kit CXXIII (agent-g 2026-10-27, run 176): a frame-tuned cfe NM body ported to NCC mechanically (bootup 90CC) -- what edg changes and the fixes, in fuzzy order <a name="kit-cxxiii-agent-g-run-176"></a>

Target: `func_000090CC` (bootup_uso, 8424 bytes, the 2106-insn alloc-cascade constructor). The cfe body was at 97.15
(report) after a long frame-layout tuning pass (PASS-4 in its comment). Queue item: port to C++ under NCC.
Result: NM-only donor `src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso_ncc_90CC_nm.cpp` (Makefile `BOOTUP_90CC_NM_DONOR`, build/non_matching
only), 97.15 -> 98.50, 2106 words = target. Commits c27c71e4f .. 61665b025 on agent-g.

**0. Mechanical port recipe (20 minutes for 870 lines).** Copy the cfe externs + body into a .cpp, wrap the externs in
`extern "C" { }`, declare the blank callee `extern char *func_00000000(...);` (returning a pointer removes most casts; the
K&R `()` would mean "no arguments" in C++), make fn-typed blank bases `(...)`, and fix the C++ type errors by retyping
the *access* (`*(char **)(p + K) = ptr` instead of `*(s32 *)(p + K) = ptr`), never by adding conversions to the value.
First compile: 95.52 (below the cfe body), frame 0x170 instead of 0x178.

**1. edg drops unreferenced locals; cfe kept them.** The cfe body had two never-used filler locals (`temp_s1_8`,
`var_s0_3`) that only existed to occupy frame slots. edg removes an unreferenced variable entirely, so every local
below them moved up 8 bytes. `T x = 0;` (initialised, still never referenced: edg warns "declared and never referenced")
KEEPS the slot and emits no code. Better still, give the filler a real job later (item 5) so no unused local is left.

**2. A pointer do-while store loop unrolls under NCC.** `p = base + 24; do { p += 4; *(s32 *)(p - 4) = 0; } while (p != end);`
(3 words) was emitted rolled by cfe but unrolled 4x with a remainder loop by NCC (+13 words), for every pointer spelling
tried (`*p = 0; p += 4`, `while`, `((s32 *)p)[-1]`, different end symbols). An index loop
`for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) ((s32 *)(base + 24))[i] = 0;` stays rolled (-1 word vs target, but +fuzzy). `*q++ = 0` with an
`s32 *` local is also rolled but drags in an edg temp slot (frame shift) -- avoid.

**3. Constant folding: route literals through the kit CXIX int inline parameter.** `(f32)255 / inv` (inv = 255.0f) became
`div.s f, f0, f0` under NCC: edg folds the cast at parse time and uopt then shares inv's constant. `fi(255) / inv` with
`static inline f32 fi(int v) { return v; }` gives the target's separate `lui 0x437f; mtc1`. The same parameter route
fixed a shared `temp_f0 = 0.0f;` stored twice (edg propagated the literal into two `mtc1 zero` materialisations; target
one `mtc1 zero, f0`): `temp_f0 = fi(0);`.

**4. Global read-modify-write through a named local gives the in-place v-register shape.** Target
`lui v0; lw v0, %lo(g)(v0); lui at, 2; or v0, v0, at; sw v0` (destination = source register) is a candidate local, not
an expression: `t = g.f04; t |= 0x20000; g_st.f04 = t;`. Expression form and same-symbol form both scored lower.

**5. The m2c body's variable roles were wrong -- the biggest single gain (+0.48 then +0.33).**
- One m2c variable (`var_t1`) carried two unrelated live ranges: arg8's flag word (no call inside; target t1) and, 300
  lines later, a `g->ptr + 0x70` draw argument live across four vfn calls (target s1). Under one name uopt gave both s1,
  which spilled the 0x878 member pointer (target s1 too) to a new bottom slot. Writing the late value into the member
  pointer's variable (`temp_s1 = (char *)(... + 0x70)`) = target colouring: 97.25 -> 97.73.
- The flag word itself is the PARAMETER: target reloads `lw t1, 0x198(sp)` in every case arm and ors in place, i.e.
  `arg8 |= 1; ... arg8 &= ~4; store arg8`, not `t = arg8 | 1`. Keep the dead copy's slot with `s32 var_t1 = 0;`
  (item 1): 97.98 -> 98.31.
- Rule of thumb for any m2c-graft port: a variable assigned from a stack parameter and then only or-ed / and-ed is
  probably the parameter; a variable reused far away for an unrelated value should be split before chasing colours.

**6. Smaller levers that held (each kept only because report.json rose):** a per-site alias for the third identical
vtable store (`bu_90cc_vt548_b`; the shared address was hoisted into s0 across a call), the vtable store written before
the field store on the same line (edg evaluates the statements in the written order, allocation follows), a fn-typed
blank base for the second `D_0` read (separate `addiu` base register like the target, realigned the t-ring by one for
~40 lines), the scaled table write through `var_s0` from a base held in the filler local (folds `sym + 0x18` into the
loop-invariant base: `addu s0, a0, t; sw x, 0(s0)`), comparison operands swapped so the 0x4C read is on the left (target
loads the other operand first), the two case-arm halfword stores written in the opposite order (edg emitted them in
reverse source order), and the `&sp7C` holder assignment moved out of the cascade arm (cfe needed it inside; NCC
schedules it where the target has it).

**7. Diagnosis tool: edg's real frame layout.** Compile the donor with `NCC ... -O2 -g3` and read the .mdebug local
symbols (stLocal = 4, value relative to the virtual frame pointer; frame size + value = sp offset). This showed that
edg lays out user locals in declaration order exactly like cfe, and that the two words below the lowest user local are
edg/uopt temps with no symbol. In 90CC the target stores `arg0 + 0x808` at sp+0x40 (bottom, i.e. a temp slot), while
the port's `sp40` user variable sits two words higher; dropping the variable and recomputing `arg0 + 0x808` at the use
puts the store at 0x40 and realigns the t-ring, but changes four candidate colours (t3/t4, t0/t1 swaps) and the
`arg8 &= ~4` gets tail-duplicated (+2 words): net -0.45, not kept. The cfe `if (1) {}` between the two statements is the
only position where that dead block changes NCC output.

**Residual at 98.50 (by size):** the t-ring is one register behind the target from 0x41720 to 0x44C00 (target skips t6
right after the 0x808 cascade: the hoisted `addiu t6, zero, 25` of case 7 is allocated before the cascade's temps);
case-7 constant hoist and case-6 delay-slot fill; `lui s0, %hi(g); lw v0` for the four draw-argument globals (the
loaded pointer is a candidate in v0 with the dying s0 as the lui register; every spelling tried keeps `lui s1; lw s1`);
the dead `addiu s0, s0, 0xB4` the target keeps in a jal delay slot; `lw a3, 0x840 / lw a2, 0x8B8` argument load order;
the `&D_8880` address hoisted above `beqz` (target puts `lui a0` in the delay slot); wpos.y store scheduling.

**8. A dead pointer increment the target keeps (90CC 98.50 -> 98.52).** The target has `addiu s0, s0, 0xB4` in a jal

Obj::query()`, 1528 -> 1560 bytes, target 1568), game_libs_func_0005F0B8 91.73 -> 92.39 (cfe body, length

**1. 3BE1C = `int Obj::query(int max, f32 *dist, Tri **out, V3 p)` (vertical ray, sibling of 3B2EC / 3B9C0).**
Ported from the cfe body onto the 3B2EC donor's types and its inline `toCell(const V3 &, int &, int &)` /
`cellOf()` / `list()` members (the cell-index homes and per-statement self->col reloads came for free). In fuzzy
order: the K triple through its own symbol `D_3BE1C_128` (held base, `addiu v0,v0,0x128`; 74.8 -> 80.6), off
computed BEFORE the grp test (the target tests `tris + off`), the material call through a `Col *cc` copy of

`continue` (edg's `continue` in a `while ((i = *list++) != -1)` duplicates the loop test, +8 bytes), t->a / t->b
read before the 0x200 branch, the cfe edge do-while with `fv++` inside the condition, then:

  read through a COPY of the old pointer, and that copy took an s-register (`or s0,a2; lh t8,0(s0)`); the split
  form reads `lh t9,0(a2); addiu a2,a2,2` like the target.
- **De-naming single-use locals** (83.38 -> 87.55): `ia / ib / ic` (the dropped-axis vertex coordinates), `vt`,
  `qa / qb` and `sg` written as macros instead of named locals, and self->col held in a function-scope
  `Col *cc` (the target's s1). Every named scalar is an edg variable with its own frame home and a colour; with
  them gone the frame went 0x108 -> 0xF0 (= target) and the saves s0..s8 -> s0..s7 (= target). `n`, `a / b`,
  `d`, `ok` must stay named (de-naming them costs 1..4 points).
  Residual: the face pointer is not copied into s0 after the `face()` expansion, off spills to sp+76 (target
  sp+84), r is not copied into a0 after the 0x100 test, the first inner MAX of `MAXS(MAXS(ia, ib), ic)` is two
  arms (the target pre-assigns one arm before the branch; every MAXS / MINS spelling, cast placement and operand
  order is identical or worse), and the edge-loop schedule. A V3 `q` with `(&q.x)[k]` is identical to `f32 q[3]`

  (-0.8 / -3.7), but +0.9 on 3B6A0 (below), whose target keeps off in a frame home.

**2. 5F0B8 (guRotateF-family axis-angle matrix, cfe).** The target keeps the 0.0f store constant in callee-saved
f22 and c in f20 although no call follows: all ten caller-saved FP registers are taken by interfering live
ranges, so the constant's live range must begin early. Dropping the second `if (1) {}` (after the m[2][0] store)
and naming `ys = y * s;` / `xs = x * s;` just before their first use gives the target's fs0 = c / fs1 = 0.0f and
frame 0x80; declaring `xs, ys` BEFORE `zy, xz` moves the zy / xz homes to the target's sp+60 / sp+56 (cfe slots
are top-down in declaration order, but here the two named copies land below the unused xs / ys slots).
Residual: x*s is not memory-homed (the target stores it to sp+52 and reloads it twice; every placement of an
extra BB break or of the xs / ys definitions moved the zero constant back out of fs1), and the (1-c)*xy / z*s
products swap f8 / f10. Measured: `0.0f` instead of `0` for the zero stores costs 7 points (84.6), zero stores
first costs 17, a named zero variable is flat.

**3. Negatives (each probed, no gain).**
- 39E24 (cfe 99.79): under NCC a DATA symbol for the camera vector gives the target's `lui v0` (vector) before
  `lui a2` (G) and keeps the 0x30 / 0x34 member offsets in the loads when the vector is a struct object
  (`gl_39e24_vf.pos.x`), but uopt then hoists the three scale loads above the vector stores (distinct data
  symbols do not alias). The function-typed alias blocks the hoist but flips the lui order; G as a function
  alias blocks the hoist with the right lui order but is SPILLED across the call instead of rematerialised (a
  function address is a value, a data address is a constant); volatile G / a volatile cast / the vector inside G
  (same symbol, uopt still separates the offsets) / an int-cast address: all lose. The target's shape is as1
  keeping memory order across different base registers while uopt emitted source order -- not reachable from
  any NCC or cfe spelling tried.
- 4EE44 as NCC `Obj::draw()` (the m30 pointer local is required, 95.6 -> 99.76): identical residual to cfe (src
  load in v0, target a1); src spellings, decl order, loop operand order flat.
- 525F0 as NCC `Obj::add(Node *)` with inline get() / attach(): identical to cfe (v1 reload, target v0).
- 35B1C as an NCC constructor `Node::Node(List *, Key, int)` with an inline Member ctor (cfront this==0 alloc
  cascade reproduced, frame fixed by two volatiles at 97.16 = the cfe score): the vptr store stays right after
  its `addiu` (target two words later); out-of-class inline ctor placement and one-line layouts are inert.
- NCC lowers a dense 12-case switch to a beq chain too (51AD8 / 396FC stay cfe).
- 307A8 under NCC: one global object accessed through an inline member gives per-access `lui at` (no held base,
  the alias-per-site effect for free) but still one `lui at` per store of the zeroing pair (target shares one).
- 33EB8 under NCC holds the stream-object base in an s-register (target rematerialises per site).
- 4B0A8, 49B3C, 34890, 3DF58: member-vs-free, next() spellings, iterator form, declaration order: flat.
- 3B9C0 as NCC C++ (do-while edge walk, `*nx` split, de-named temporaries): 72.6 vs cfe 76.5, not kept.
- 3C43C / 36F0C / 3B2EC de-naming (row / k / n / h / vt): flat or worse; the lever is for functions whose
  frame is too LARGE with many single-use locals.

**4. Rules.**
- NCC: a named local that is used once is not free -- it is an edg variable with a home slot and a colour.
  When an NCC port's frame / s-register count exceeds the target's, de-name single-use locals (macros or
  inline expressions) before adding or removing volatiles.
- NCC: `*p++` (and `x = *p++` in a call argument) reads through a copy of the old pointer; split it into `*p`
  and `p++;` when the target reads straight off the walking register.
- NCC: a `continue` in a `while ((i = *p++) != -1)` loop duplicates the loop test; a nested `if` does not.

## kit CXXV (agent-g 2026-10-27, run 178): bootup 90CC 98.525 -> 98.829 -- read `NCC -S` (ugen output before as1) to tell uopt, ugen and as1 apart; the "one register behind" t-ring was a recomputed CSE temp, the hoisted `li 25` is as1, and structural fixes have to be landed in batches <a name="kit-cxxv-agent-g-run-178"></a>

Target: `func_000090CC` (bootup_uso, 8424 B, NCC NM donor `src/bootup_uso/bootup_uso_ncc_90CC_nm.cpp`). Start
98.525 (report.json), end 98.829. Every committed step raised report.json. objdiff "real" rows (diff rows left after
masking relocation names and immediates) went from 249 to 68.

**1. `NCC -S` is the missing diagnostic.** `tools/ido-static-recomp/build/7.1/out/NCC -S <same flags> -o x.s x.cpp`
writes ugen's assembly BEFORE as1 runs: macro `la` / `lw r, sym` / `li.s`, the `.livereg` masks and ugen's own
register choices (`$14` = t6), in ugen order. Diff two variants' `.s` files with the `.loc` and `#` lines filtered out
(`grep -v "^ #\|\.loc"`) to see which pass made a difference:
- uopt decides which variable gets which register and where constant / address candidates are loaded (`li $2, 7`).
- ugen decides the t-ring temps (`la $15, sym`) and the statement order.
- as1 is responsible for anything that appears in the `.s` but sits somewhere else in the `.o`. as1 expands `la` /
  `lw sym` and renames its scratch register to any dead register (the target's `lui s0, %hi(g); lw v0, %lo(g)(s0)` is
  as1 using a dying s0). It fills load and branch delay slots from a successor block, hoists a fall-through block's
  `la` above a `beqz`, and copies a short join block (`addiu at, -5; and t1, t1, at; b`) into a predecessor that
  branches to it.

**2. The "t-ring one register behind from 0x41720" (kit CXXIII residual) was a CSE temp, not the case-7 constant.**
The donor kept `sp40 = (s32 *)var_s0;`, a named local for `arg0 + 0x808` homed at sp+0x48. Fix: drop the variable and
write `arg0 + 0x808` again at its only use (the call about 150 lines later). uopt then makes a CSE temp and spills it.
In the `.s`, ugen materialises the temp through the ring (`addu $14, $18, 2056; sw $14, 64($sp); lw $16, 64($sp)`),
which moves the ring by one register for the rest of the function. as1 folds the copy into `addiu s0, s2, 0x808;
sw s0, 0x40(sp)`, the target's store at the target's temp slot. On its own this change scored LOWER (report 98.758 ->
98.719) because two as1 decisions changed elsewhere: a short join block got copied into a predecessor and two `la`
moved above branches. Together with item 3 it is +0.07. kit CXXIII item 7 tried the same drop without item 3 and
scored -0.45.

**3. The case-7 `addiu t6, zero, 25` above the switch is as1 filling a load delay slot from a successor block.**
uopt puts a constant candidate's `li` at the START of the first BB of its live range. The case constant 7 came out as
`li $2, 7` before `lw $24, 0($3)` because the BB started right after the `if (1) { fq += 6; }` body. So 7 interfered
with the `fq` pointer (fq -> v1, 7 -> v0), and as1 filled the `lw` delay slot with `li v0, 7`. The target has fq in
v0. The fix is a BB boundary right after the store: `fq = (s32 *)arg0; fq += 6; if (1) { *fq &= ~2; }`. uopt then
emits `li $2, 7` after the store and fq takes v0. `li v0, 7` can no longer move above `sw t9, 0(v0)`, so as1 fills the
delay slot with the next independent instruction it finds, the case-7 arm's `li t6, 25`. That is exactly the target's
shape. An EMPTY `if (1) {}` after a statement creates no BB; the statement has to be INSIDE the `if (1) { }` body.
- Tried and inert or worse: every type and int-parameter spelling of the 25; a block-scope or function-scope variable
  holding 25 (copy-propagated, and the function-scope one adds a frame slot); a dead store of 25 before the switch;
  ternaries; a shared case-6 / case-7 tail. `-Wo,-zcopy:0` with such a variable gives the target's shape, but only
  because nothing gets propagated. zdbug:5 joins the case 25 and the 25 at 0x9F48 into one negative-save LR
  (BB 226..293, three reload points), which turned out to be irrelevant.

**4. Structural fixes can lower objdiff fuzzy, so land them in batches.** objdiff chooses one alignment for the whole
function. Fixing a local insert/delete pair can make it pick a worse alignment elsewhere (replace pairs instead of
insert + delete), so a correct local fix can score lower. Two fixes each scored lower on their own:
- wpos.x/y/z stored together before the int fields (target: `lwc1 z` before the int stores, `swc1 z` scheduled after
  them).
- the 0x840 call argument read into `var_v1` before the call (`lw a1, 0x840` before `or a0, s2`).

Together they gave +0.22 (98.531 -> 98.748). Check each fix on its own region (rows.py), keep the ones that are right,
and score them together.

**5. Smaller levers kept, in order:**
- `((s32 *)bu_90cc_d148_18)[i] = 0` over a new symbol at the +0x18 address gives the target's `sw zero, -4(v0)` pointer
  loop (pin `bu_90cc_d148_18`).
- In the 5-argument call, read the 0x840 argument into a block local first (`lw a3, 0x840` before `lw a2, 0x8b8`).
- `for (sp58 = 0; sp58 != 0x23; sp58++)` instead of the while loop puts the `addiu at, 0x23` before the increment.
- Read the third draw-argument global into `temp_v0_51` instead of `var_v1` (v0, like the target).

**6. Residual at 98.829 (68 real rows):**
- arg2 and the &D_00000000 base swapped between t3 and t4 (uopt colouring order).
- as1 copies the `arg8 &= ~4` join block into the rgb30 arm.
- as1 hoists the d148 loop bases and `&D_8880` above their branches (the target puts the `lui` in the delay slot).
- `var_v1` in v1 instead of v0 in the gcfg read-modify-writes.

## kit CXXVI (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 179): automatic lever sweeps over every NM body of two units -- de-naming (once-assigned local -> macro), `volatile` per local, adjacent independent-statement swaps, each kept only when report.json rises and the length moves toward the target; the in-file cfe body can be scored in ~1 s by compiling a scratch copy of the whole .c <a name="kit-cxxvi-agent-c-run-179"></a>

**Summary.** No exacts (81.35 % code unchanged). Twenty-one NM functions of game_libs_post / game_libs_post0b raised
(table in item 5). The run turned the kit CXXIV levers into scripts and ran them over every NM body of the two units:
the NCC donors and the in-file cfe bodies alike.

**1. Scoring an in-file cfe NM body without touching src/.** Copy the whole unit to a scratch file, edit the copy and
run `python3 tools/asm-processor/asm_processor.py -O2 copy.c > copy_pp.c` (cwd = the project, so the `-I include`
paths resolve), then the project's `cc -c -G 0 -non_shared -Xcpluscomm -Wab,-r4300_mul -O2 -mips2 -32 -I include -I src
-DNON_MATCHING -o copy.o copy_pp.c`, then `objdiff-cli diff -1 build/src/game_libs/<unit>.c.o -2 copy.o -o - <fn>` and
read `match_percent`. Skip asm-processor's post-process step: only the C function is scored, and objdiff matches it by
symbol. A 28k-line unit takes well under a second per variant, so a 40-variant sweep of one function takes about a
minute. The numbers follow report.json closely (2D374: local 98.92 = report 99.59; the offset is constant).
Run parallel sweeps in separate work directories: two sweeps writing the same temp file names clobber each other.

**2. The three sweeps (scripts in the run's scratch area, easy to rewrite).**
- *De-naming*: for every local assigned exactly once by a whole-line `x = expr;` (or declared `T x = expr;`) that has
  other uses, replace the assignment with `#define x (expr)` (and `#undef x` after the function), drop the
  declaration, and score. Check every kept hit by hand: the macro re-evaluates `expr` at each use, so a call or a
  side effect in expr changes the semantics. Rewrite kept hits as plain source (the expression inline at each use).
- *Volatile*: prefix each local declaration with `volatile`, one at a time.
- *Adjacent swap*: swap each pair of adjacent single-statement lines at the same indentation. Keep a swap only when
  neither statement's left-hand side appears in the other one, and never swap two display-list packet emits (that
  changes the output). A greedy loop applies the best kept swap and sweeps again until nothing rises.
- Length rule: a candidate that changes the function length counts only when the new length is closer to the target.
  That rule threw out the biggest raw hits: 3BE1C de-naming `v1` / `ey` 88.6 -> 91.3 but 1560 -> 1544 bytes (target
  1568); 3B6A0 de-naming `ax` 74.5 -> 78.0 at +4 bytes away; 4D688 volatile `var_s4` at -4 bytes away.

**3. What each lever found.**
- De-naming (NCC and cfe): 4A308 `t2` (the entry+6 index, re-read at both uses) 94.47 -> 95.66; 2D374 the decrement
  `n = c - 1` written at the store, which also brings 680 -> 676 bytes = target (96.69 -> 98.22); 4F2DC
  `dists[i]` re-read three times; 4C5E4 the 0x148 pointer re-read; 6126C the format character tested inline;
  3B6A0 `a` / `lim`; 36F0C the accel copy (`n = accel + 1; if (accel < 100) accel = n; k = accel / 10.0f;`).
- Volatile: **469A8 `volatile s32 sp48` +6.3** (the run-151 note had already named a target "sp+72 home of the
  0x148 -> 0xF0 word": m2c's `sp48` IS that home; a target store + reload of a local = a volatile local, kit

**6. Rules.**
- Before hand-grinding an NM body, run the three sweeps over it; they cost minutes and find the cheap points.
- A target that stores a local to the frame and reloads it is a `volatile` local (now confirmed on cfe bodies too:
  469A8, 54E78); m2c's `spXX` name tells you which local.
- Independent statements are not free to reorder: IDO keeps source order for stores, and a store placed after a
  following load moves the load up. Sweep adjacent swaps, keep only swaps of independent statements.
- Check every de-naming hit for side effects before keeping it.

## kit CXXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 180): two cfe "colour caps" were C++ -- 525F0 (cfront `new` through an out-of-line ctor) and 39E24 (an inline member on a member of the same global block, through a local reference) land EXACT as NCC donors; spelling-grid.py / lever-sweep.py field report <a name="kit-cxxviii-agent-c-run-180"></a>

**Exacts (report.json 100, ROM byte-identical, 81.35 -> 81.39 % code).**

- **gl_func_000525F0 (132 B, cfe 99.55).** The cfe decode had `obj = gl_func(0, &D + 0x20FC0, self)`, i.e. a call whose
  first argument is a literal 0. That is cfront's `new Foo(cfg, this)` with an out-of-line constructor: the caller passes
  `this = 0` and the ctor allocates. Written as a member function `void Self::reg(Tgt *t) { if (obj == 0) obj = new
  Foo(cfg, this); Foo *f = obj; f->s.add(t); if (t->x14) t->x4 = 1; t->x14 = f; }` (the second call is a member call on
  the Foo's +0x10 subobject), NCC emits the target's fresh `lw v0, 0x1c(sp)` reload of f. That reload was the documented
  "ugen temploc" cap (12+ C spellings neutral). Donor: `src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_525F0.cpp`, with the Makefile
  renaming `reg__4SelfFP3Tgt` / `__ct__3FooFPcP4Self` / `add__3SubFP3Tgt` (names only). **Rule: a cfe NM with a
  `(0, ...)` call or a `this == 0 -> alloc` head is C++. Try NCC before treating the residual as a colour cap.**
- **gl_func_00039E24 (192 B, cfe 99.79).** The camera vector (D+0xA0, Vec3 at +0x30) is a MEMBER of the same global
  block as the scale triple (+0x128) and the root word (+0x254). It is scaled through an inline `Cam::mul(G &g)` called on a
  block-scope reference: `{ Cam &c = D.cam; c.mul(D); c.v.y += a0->x6C; }`. This gives:
  (a) `this` (D+0xA0, `lui v0`) is materialised BEFORE the re-materialised block base (`lui a2`), the target's order;
  the C version (and plain NCC) always emitted the block base first;
  (b) the reference parameter keeps every scale load after the previous vector store (may-alias). Two distinct globals
  or a by-value / pointer-to-V3 parameter hoist the loads;
  (c) `c.v.y +=` through the same reference keeps the `0x34(v0)` form. Without the reference, `D.cam.v.y` folds to an
  absolute `%lo(D+0xd4)`.
  Calling `D.cam.mul(D)` directly (no reference) holds the block base in s1 across the call (184 B). The bootup twin
  **func_000076F4** (99.82, "same residual" per its note) should take the same donor shape (agent-g's unit).
- Pins: gl_func_00000000_525f0_ct, gl_func_00000000_525f0_add, D_39E24_g, gl_proto_39E24, gl_func_00000000_39E24v.
  Neither NM length changed (post0b clip unchanged).

**NM.** game_libs_func_0002D374 99.59 -> 99.64: `raw` de-named to `#define raw (D_2D37C_raw[0x2E68 / 2])`, a
lever-sweep `denaming` hit. The c-1 / half t-registers now match. What is left: z/fr colour f12/f0 (target f0/f2), the
post-call i reload a3 (t2) and rec[2] t2 (t3). The target stores z to 35C BEFORE fr to 358. Swapping the two stores
scores 0.03 lower, but only because f0 then stops lining up by chance. Keep that in mind before rejecting a correct
reorder on score alone.

minute. Hits: the 39E24 C++ grid (18 probes) found the exact combination. Everything else was flat, and in the
99.x band those grids showed the residual was not a spelling.
- Biggest friction: **no nesting**. `@[ a @; b ]@` items cannot contain `@{..}@`, and a choose-one inside a perm makes
  the whole run fail with an unhelpful "baseline failed" plus one caret line from the compiler. Two asks: say so
  explicitly ("nested marker at line N"), and print the real compiler error with file:line for the rendered baseline.
- **Score ties hide register swaps.** On 2D374 the true store order scored 0.03 below the wrong order because one f0
  happened to line up. A "real rows" count (non-reloc diff rows) next to the percentage, as od.py-style output, would
  have shown the tie.

  perm3=2"` option to write any listed combination would save hand edits.

## kit CXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-27, run 180): NCC frame-layout model for the 1DDC residue (one top-down allocation sequence, pooled V3 return slot = named-area bottom - 12); 3558 node pointer through the Ctx accessor (75.62 -> 76.41); negatives <a name="kit-cxxix-agent-g-run-180"></a>

**Result.** NM game_uso_func_00003558 75.62 -> 76.41 (one commit). No exact. game_uso_func_00001DDC stays 99.97
(the committed donor with the `int e = 0;` filler is still the best report.json score); the run mapped WHY.

**1. 3558 = Ctx accessor, not a register local.** The target stores `s0->node` to sp+252 in the prologue and reloads
it (`lw v1,252(sp); addiu a0,v1,48`) before both 072EE8 calls. That is the 1DDC / 24BC / 28C0 `struct Ctx { Node *out;
Ctx(S *s) { out = s->node; } Node *getOut() const { return out; } }` stack object, read through `c.getOut()->...` at
every use. Replacing `Node *p = s0->node; p->...` with it is worth +0.8. Still open: frame 216 vs 256, and the zero in
callee-saved $f20 (NCC keeps const-propagating it; the cfe body gets the cross-call 0.0 web). The 28C0 sibling's inline
`M4::rotate(V3 &)` for the matrix block is a large NEGATIVE here (76.4 -> 60.8).

**2. NCC stack layout, measured on 1DDC (two-arm `if (key == 3) {...} else {...}`, ~60 probes).** One top-down
sequence from the frame top, in creation order:
- the arm-scope named locals (key-3 arm first, then the else arm), each arm's inline-call reference/`this` temporaries
  right after its locals (1DDC: the key-3 arm's `getPos(m)` + two `set(m)` calls = the 16-byte gap between the key-3
  locals and the else locals; dropping both `set(m)` calls moves every else local up 8);
- then, in source order across BOTH arms, nested-block named locals (`{ const M4 &mm = ...; }`, `{ Out *o = ...; }`,
  even dead `{ int zz; zz = 0; }`) and expression temporaries. A nested block in the key-3 arm is therefore allocated
  BELOW the else arm's named locals, not with its own arm;
- the pooled by-value return slot (shared by `r = f23D4(a0)` and every `V3 operator*` result) is created at the first
  V3-returning call, so it sits right below whatever nested locals precede that call: slot = (lowest earlier local) - 12;
- every named local gets a home even when uopt keeps it in a register (references, pointers, `register` too); only
  expression temporaries without names can be folded away, and even they leave their bytes in the frame (the target's
  20-byte hole at sp+232..251).
So "retslot 8 low + frame 8 high" means one 8-byte nested local sits ABOVE the slot that the target creates BELOW it.
1DDC target = no nested locals anywhere before the call, the slot at named-bottom - 12 (sp+252), then 8 more bytes of
temporaries after the call. Two reproductions: (a) direct `a0->src->mtx.getPos(m)` / `a0->obj->mtx.getPos(self)`, set(m)
for goal/pos, and 8 bytes after the call (two dead block ints) = every stack offset and the frame exact, 10 words left
(both matrix-base loads take v0 where the target has v1); (b) `{ const M4 &mm = a0->obj->mtx; ... }` in the else arm
only = every register in the else arm plus the frame, 9 words left (key-3 v0 + the slot at 244). The v1 appears only
with a NAMED pointer/reference to the matrix (block or arm scope), which always costs a home in the wrong place;
inline accessors (`Body::mr()`, `getPosF(const M4 &, V3 &)`, `getPosB(const Body *, V3 &)`, `(*a0->src).mtx`, an
inline `pos()` returning V3, `switch (a0->key)`) all give v0. `self += f23D4(a0)` with no named `r` reproduces the
target copy chain exactly (r's role becomes a materialised temporary at r's home) and adds a 4-byte temporary after
the slot -- half of what the target has there. Reading: the base register is v1 because the target's pointer is a
uopt-coloured VARIABLE (global colouring prefers v1, ugen expression temps take v0), yet it has no home before the
call. Next idea for whoever picks this up: a construct whose pointer temp edg creates AFTER the return slot, or a
variable that is never homed.

**Tool note.** objdiff fuzzy and rdiff `diffwords` disagree for layout work: the layout-exact 10-word variant scores
99.84 in objdiff, below the committed 12-word donor (99.97), because objdiff weights a frame shift lightly and a
register swap heavily. Rank layout probes by diffwords and the `addiu sp/offset(sp)` set
(`objdump ... | grep -oE "[-0-9]+\(sp\)" | sort -u`); confirm in report.json.

## kit CXXX (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 181): gl_func_000201B8 is OoT AudioHeap_AllocCached -- transcribe the reference source with its own types and control flow, then a hoisted constant with a kept EMPTY then-arm (`x = 0; if (c) {} else { x = v; }`) fixes the last delay-slot swap <a name="kit-cxxx-agent-c-run-181"></a>

**Exact (report.json 100, ROM byte-identical, 81.57 -> 81.81 % code).** gl_func_000201B8 (1796 B, 449 words, game_libs_post.c,
C body on the build path, no donor).

**1. Look for the reference source before grinding colours.** 201B8 sat at 97.94 as a "typed view" rewrite (decl-order
homes, goto ladder, six documented residuals). It is OoT `AudioHeap_AllocCached` (`references/oot/src/audio/internal/heap.c`),
an OLDER revision: no `if (temporaryPool->size < size) return NULL;` and no `AudioHeap_DiscardSampleBank` calls (the
discard after `loadStatus[id] = 0` is font-only). Mapping: tableType 0/1/2 = seq/font/sample caches at D+0x21F8 + 0x110 * k
with load-status tables at +0x2C70 / +0x2C40 / +0x2C10 (seq / font / sample); AudioCache = {persistent {numEntries, pool
(start, cur, size, numEntries), entries[16] {ramAddr, size, s16 tableType, s16 id}}, temporary {nextSide, pool, entries[2]},
16 pad bytes}; notes = recs (stride 0xD0, fontId +0x33, enabled = top bit of +0xB0), numNotes = +0x2070; seqPlayers = objs
(stride 0x160, enabled = top bit of +0, seqId +4), count = s16 +0x2048; DiscardSequence = the baked `jal 0x34238`.
Transcribing OoT's body as-is (else-if side chain, `goto done`, `if (0) { fail: return NULL; }`, `switch (nextSide)` read
through the cache with no `side` local, the persistent tail with `switch (cache) { case 2: return AllocCached(tableType, size,
0, id); case 0: case 1: return NULL; }`) gave 99.11 in one step: every old residual (multu by the held 12, the `v = 1`
webs, the r colour, constant-first compares, hA-before-w4) disappeared. **IDO -O2 turns the self tail call into the
branch back to the top** (uopt tail-recursion elimination), which is why the old decode had `op = 0; goto top;`. Adding
a `side` local (OoT's later revision) is -20 B.

**2. The last two rows: hoisted constant with a kept empty then-arm.** Target:
`lh t6,242(a3); li at,-1; or t3,zero,zero; bne t6,at,L+4; addiu a2,a3,212; b J; addiu a2,a3,212; L+4: lh t7,30(a2)` --
the 0 is materialised BEFORE the branch, and as1 then fills the bne slot with a copy of the else arm's first instruction.
The ternary `e0 = (tc->e[0].id == -1) ? 0 : ls[tc->e[0].id];` puts the 0 in the then block (as1 moves it into the delay
slot instead: `addiu a2; bne; or t3`). `e0 = 0; if (id != -1) e0 = ls[..];` hoists the 0 but drops the then block (-8 B,
the branch flips). **`e0 = 0; if (tc->e[0].id == -1) {} else { e0 = ls[tc->e[0].id]; }` = both: the 0 hoisted and the empty
then block kept (it still carries the `addiu a2` join copy)** -> 100. Only entry0 needs it; entry1 stays a ternary. Not an
uninitialised-local test: the tested value is a loaded field. Candidate shape elsewhere: a ternary / if-else whose
constant arm's `li`/`or rd,zero` sits in the delay slot where the target has it before the branch.

**3. Negatives / notes.**
- -O3 (umerge inlining) is not the audio file's flag: 201B8 at -O3 is 78 % (+84 B). 250C8 (ProcessAsyncLoad with
  FinishAsyncLoad inline) as OoT's two functions at -O3 inlines to 596 B / 93.6, below the in-tree 99.85.
- 250C8 retMsg-local vs re-read x fontId named / macro (8 probes): the committed body stays best.
- 2D374: z and the post-call 358 read through the same locals as d / fr (IDO colours per variable, so this was the
  "same register" hypothesis), 35C-before-358 store order: flat.
- 578B4 (7 words): `temp_ra_8` placement x the DL pointer in a block-scope local x the call result through a named temp: flat.
- 4B0A8 / 4B620: their literal-0 calls written as `new DL(name, ...)` through an out-of-line ctor are byte-identical to
  the `(0, ...)` calls (the 525F0 gain came from the result reload, which these members do not have).
- 40070 element store: `volatile float`, init-list, `*(volatile float *)&a = 0.0f`, double: all still `swc1` (flat).
- 35B1C vptr store: `if (1) { store; }`, store after `q = p`, four spellings of the q alloc test incl. empty arms: flat.
- 41D40 next() with a hoisted `r = 0` and an empty arm: -6 (the iterator returns must stay returns).

**Tool feedback.** lever-sweep.py standalone `.c` mode does not pass `-I include` (every probe of a donor that includes
common.h fails with "base does not compile/score"); workaround `--flags "... -I<wt>/include"`. spelling-grid.py: the
real-rows column made the 201B8 win obvious (48 -> 44 rows = the 2 real rows plus their 2 relocs); the "nested marker"
error now fires on named groups inside a named group's alternative too, so do placeholder substitutions before inserting
the outer group. `cc -S` writes `<name>.s` into the current directory regardless of `-o`.
3558 lead: writing the tail as `e.x = e.x * k + w.x; ...` (no operator*= / operator+=) gives the exact target length
(1008 B, 240 rows vs 241) but objdiff 74.68 vs 76.73 -- not taken; probably the right shape once the frame and the
$f20 zero are solved.

**kit CXXX addendum (same run): second exact, gl_func_0004E00C (300 B, NCC donor, 96.33 -> 100).** The residual was
"the target keeps the unrolled 4-trip loop's IV (`li v1,1; sll t6,v1,2; addu v0,a0,t6`) with ascending stores where ours
folds it". That shape is **uopt's unroll of a loop whose trip count is not a multiple of 4: (n mod 4) iterations are
peeled AHEAD of the unrolled body and the IV value after the peel survives as a register** (`li v1,K`). Target:
`sw zero,0(a0)` (peeled w[0]), then `li v1,1` + four ascending stores (k = 1..4), then `sw zero,20(a0)` (w[5]) = a FIVE-trip
loop followed by the last element: `zero(0); w[5] = 0;` with `void zero(int k) { for (; k < 5; k++) w[k] = 0; }`.
A 6-trip loop peels two (`li a0,2`), a 4-trip loop from 1 folds the IV to `addiu v0,a0,4`. The inline parameter `k`
(not a for-scope `int k`) keeps the 0xE8 spill temp at the target's sp+32 (the for-scope variant is 1 slot off).
**Rule: `li rX,K; sll; addu` before an unrolled run means K = trips mod 4 were peeled; set the trip count so the peel
matches.** The donor was renamed from `_nm`, the cfe body replaced by an empty placeholder, both trees splice it; post0b
NM clip 0x2ea94 -> 0x2ea9c (the NM donor was 0x124 bytes).

range when the region has no use of it). **Fix: give the region a use of 0.0f that emits nothing -- the wrapper ctor

uopt sees a 0.0f occurrence inside the protocol, keeps the constant's LR across it and rematerialises after each call.
(Not an uninitialised-local test: z is initialised.) A union element written through `.i = 0` works the same. Rule: a
constant that the target re-materialises after every call through a region with no visible use was live there in the
original -- add a folded use of that constant (an empty test of an initialised local) inside the region. The donor's
`gl_func_00034458` callee must be renamed to the 0-pinned `gl_func_00000000` (the target has `jal 0`); new pins
D_40070_vta / D_40070_vtb (the renamed vtables, both 0).

## kit CXXXII (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 183): no exact this run -- the jumptable bound-check delay census (82 target tables, 0 default steals), the 51AD8 / 396FC shared-default reproducer, 35B1C as an NCC ctor (structure word-exact, frame via one extra vreg local, vptr-store order still open), 37938's symbol ends one word early <a name="kit-cxxxii-agent-c-run-183"></a>

**1. Bound-check delay census (51AD8 / 396FC, read before probing these again).** A scan of every target object
(`build/src/*/*.o`, 82 IDO jumptables `sltiu at; beqz at,DEFAULT; <delay>; lui at; addu; lw; jr`) found **0 defaults
whose first instruction was stolen into the bound-check delay** -- every one keeps `sll tN,tN,2` (or an independent
pre-branch instruction). Of those defaults, 14 start with `jal` and 32 with `lw ra` (unstealable), and every other
stealable-looking head (`lw tN,k(sp)`, `lbu`, `or v0,zero`, `lui v0`) is in a matched function our as1 also leaves
alone (as1 does not steal loads into a non-likely slot, and v0 is live at the return of int functions). The only
non-matching cases are exactly 51AD8 (`lui a0,2`) and 396FC (`or a0,a3`), both `handler(this, msg)` message
dispatchers whose default is the base-handler / error call with an ALU head that writes a0. A third twin, 38A28
(default `lui a0,2`), keeps `sll` because its table has five holes that point at the default
(`extract-uso-jumptable.py gl_func_00038A28 --module 0xD9FE28 --vaddr 0x38A28 --size 0x144 --shim 0x1466C`; note
the `--size` must cover the default block, the bundle note's 0xEC hides those entries). 51AD8 (12 entries) and 396FC
(6) have no holes (same tool).
- **Reproducer for the mechanism (not a fix):** in 396FC, cases ending in `return`, `default: break;` and the base
  call after the switch steal as usual; making ONE arm (114) end in `break` (a real branch to the post-switch call)
  keeps `sll` in the slot. So the default needs a second predecessor, and in both targets no second branch exists.
- Negatives this run (396FC standalone, slot word checked): `default: if (1) {} f();`, a label plus `if (0) goto`,

  head, `while (1) { f(); return; }`, `if (a1[0] == a1[0])`, `default: f(); return;`, all-return arms with
  `default: break;` / `goto d` + call after the switch, `this` / `msg` through local copies in arms or default.

```cpp
struct W { int v; W() { v = 0; } };
struct Node { Node *next; W key; };  struct List { int pad; Node *head; };
struct X { X *next; W key; int c; virtual void f(); X(List *l, W a2, int a3); };
X::X(List *l, W a2, int a3) {
    int *a3p = &a3; W *p = &key; Node *n; Node *last;   /* p + a3p = the target frame 80 */
    c = *a3p;

    last = 0;
    for (n = l->head; n != 0; n = n->next) last = n;
    if (last != 0) last->next = (Node *)this; else l->head = (Node *)this;
    next = 0;
    *p = a2;
}
```

## kit CXXXIV (agent-c 2026-10-27, run 174 in commit numbering): EDG for-init iterator lever (41D40 / 49B3C / 34890 NM gains); no exact <a name="kit-cxxxiv-agent-c-run-174"></a>

**Summary.** No exact this run. Three NM donor gains from one lever: write an iterator walk as
`for (Iter it(...); it.next(); )` instead of `Iter it(...); while (it.next())`. 41D40 99.17 -> 99.26,
49B3C 99.01 -> 99.33 (also switched from the run 162 donor to the run 173 draft), 34890 98.10 -> 98.27
(objdiff diff scores, expected/ vs NM object). No NM length change, so the post0b clip did not move.

**1. EDG pooled temps, read from the itab dump.** `-Wo,-zdbug:1` on an NCC donor lists the inline-expansion temps
as `isvar M 4 -N vreg` entries. Every inlined call's `this`, each argument and each returned value gets a temp
from a pool, and the pool reuses temps across calls and across roles. In 41D40 one temp held the
`iter(*(Arr **)D)` argument, the array pointer inside next() and the one inside cur(). Because those are a
single variable, its live range crosses the body's calls and gets s1, and the condition's array load is
s1 as well. In the target that load is v0 (entry copy) / v1 (bottom copy). You can see the two copies of
the loop condition in the itab: they use different temps (entry copy: fresh temps; bottom copy: the
reused pool), so EDG emits the condition twice and uopt does not just duplicate one copy. `if (0) { ... }`
blocks and dead statements (`(void)it.cur();`) anywhere in the loop do not change which temps the pool
hands out (all 9-diff in 41D40).

**2. The lever: declare the iterator in the for-init.** EDG keeps the for-init statement's temps alive for
the whole `for` statement, so the entry copy of the condition gets fresh temps that do not cross a call.
- 41D40: entry next() array load s1 -> v0 (= target), result v1 (= target). The two extra temps add 8 to the
  frame. Take those 8 bytes out of the dead `volatile` pad block (6 -> 4 words) and go back to `return &(*a)[++idx]`
  (the run 173 `int n` spelling scores worse in this form). Left (8 words): the entry copy's index temp is a0
  (target a1) because that temp is also the bottom copy's result temp (a0 = target). In the target they must be
  two different temps. The bottom copy's array and index temps swap v0 / v1.
- 49B3C: the list walk `for (LI li(g->head); li.next(); )` fixes the entry copy's result (a1 = target). The same
  form on the ARRAY loop costs 16 words there, because its next() copies were already off s1. Use the lever only
  where the dump shows the condition's temp sharing a call-crossing register.
- 34890: `for (LIter it(o->list); it.next(); )`, 31 -> 28 words. What is left is the alloc cascade.
- Negative (scored with a scratch script that converts each adjacent decl + `while (x.next())` pair, alone and in
  every combination): 493AC (184 -> 191..204), 48AEC (258 -> 258..264), 4B0A8 (21 -> 24), 4B620 (49 -> 78),
  454C4 (the `while ((e = it.next()) != 0)` form, 261 -> 281 difflib rows), 3DF58 (for-init `Node *n`, a
  per-branch second iterator, `while` / `for (;;)` shapes: all 16 or worse).

**3. 37938 boundary (queue item 1) not done, on purpose.** The symbol does end at the bare `jr ra` (0x154; the delay
nop is asm-processor block padding at 0x3634, and the `_pad.s` word is at 0x3638). The recipe from MATCHING_WORKFLOW
(`#splat-symbol-boundary-trailing-delay-nop-2026-06-22`) would make it 0x158. But the body is not one word from
exact: the NM object has 11 more rows wrong, all stack offsets plus the final `s` reload. Those are the inline
temp homes in the wrong order: target holes between the named V3s are 5 / 6 / 1 / 5 / 3 words, the port's are
3 / 8 / 2 / 6 / 1, and the frame is the same size. A 4096-combination toggle search (kept `if (0)` parameters
on gp / operator* / ctor / operator=, named return locals, getPos vs getPos0, `V3 d = b - a;`, s escape
position, a/b declaration order) gave no improvement over the current donor (16 difflib rows each). Since the
fix moves the score less than 1% and needs a full `refresh-expected-baseline.py` run, it is left for a run that
also fixes the body.

**4. Other negatives (diagnosis only).**
- 578B4 s2_508 ra/t0 (7 words): kit XCIX's analysis still holds. Moving the `arg2 & 0x1FF` statement, splitting it
  or folding it into the packet store, and binding the FD50 pointer to temp_t0_25: all 8 rows.

## kit CXXXV (agent-g 2026-10-27, run 185): NCC block-entry allocation -- a block's named locals are placed at block ENTRY, below the enclosing blocks' temporaries; a nested block opened at the right statement moves homes the 5040-order declaration grids could not (timer-HUD 13B8 / 16F4 99.39 -> 99.43); spill-area rule; negatives <a name="kit-cxxxv-agent-g-run-185"></a>

**Result.** No exact (82.25 % code unchanged). NM (report.json): timproc_uso_b3_func_000013B8 and arcproc_uso_func_000016F4
99.39412 -> 99.42941 (680 B each, length = target). Commit `a5d7aff61` on agent-g.

**1. The allocation model, read off `-Wo,-zdbug:6` (`isvar M 4 -N vreg` lines = edg frame slots, offset from the frame top).**
- Function-block named locals come first (declaration order, top-down), then the function block's own inline temps.
- Each nested block (`if` body, plain `{ }`, loop body) allocates ITS named locals at block entry, then the temporaries
  of its statements as they are met, then its own nested blocks. A C++ declaration in the middle of a block is still
  allocated at that block's entry: moving `s32 xoff = ...` down to its first use changes nothing on its own (this is
  why kit CXXXIII's 5040-order grid and "function / block / nested-block" placement were inert -- they never put a
  block boundary AFTER the temporaries of earlier statements).
- So: when the target homes a group of locals BELOW slots that only inline temporaries can explain (the target has
  N vreg slots between the last function-scope local and the group, yours has the group right under the scalars),
  open a nested block `{` at the statement where the group starts and close it at the end of the region that uses it.
  13B8: `{` after `n = count(buf);`, `s32 xoff = ...; s32 xb = ...; s32 xa = ...; s32 x = ...;` inside, `}` after the
  last draw call: xoff / xb / x homes 164 / 160 / 180 -> 160 / 156 / 148 (target 148 / 144 / 136).
- The last three words came from three named panel pointers declared at the top of that block
  (`Spr *pC = &arg0->sC, *pA = &arg0->sA, *pB = &arg0->sB;`, used for the width() calls of xoff and xb -- the
  objdiff score is flat over which width sites use them, but dropping pB from xoff / xb puts the frame back up).
  1340 shows the same "three extra words above the block" (count is the first local of ITS nested block: target
  count / x / pos4 at 0x98 / 0x94 / 0x90); there the same pointers unused give the right relative layout but the
  frame stays +16 (the nested block keeps one more temp than the target), so 1340 is not landed.
- Inline-temp pooling (kit CXXXIV) is visible in the same dump: a `this` temp of an inline call in the enclosing block
  is re-used by the nested block (`ustr` into the same `-N` slot), named inline locals (`Img *i`) are not.

**2. Spill-area rule (ugen).** The spill slots sit directly under the lowest edg slot with ONE hidden word on top: lowest
local at L -> spills at L-8, L-12, (hidden L-16), L-20 in 13B8 (s1 / s2 / - / a2). If your spills are exactly 4 low
with the frame equal, you have ONE edg slot too many below your lowest named home -- count the nested block's vreg
slots in the dump (13B8: 7 `Img *i` + one fresh `this` temp = 8; the target needs 7). Dropping the loop's
`height()` named pointer (`return img->h;`) fixes the spill words but costs the loop's t0 image-pointer colour
(98.94 < 99.04), so the extra slot is a fresh `this` temp the target took from the pool.

**3. Left on 13B8 / 16F4 (22 rows):** spill words 4 low (above), the xoff-region int ring one register behind (sC / sA /
sB image pointers t2 / t0 / t1 vs t3 / t1 / t2: in the coloring order the copy LR of xa's `i` must win t0 first), the
loop's tim image load v0 vs t0. lever-sweep `all` after the restructure: no hits on either twin.

**4. Negatives (this run).**
- 63964: operator+ / operator* / operator= spelling grid (free vs member, named result, by-value parameters,
  `V3 r = a; r += b;`): 36 combinations flat at 99.8929; the arm-1 slot map is the vreg-before-T2 problem of kit
  CXXXIII and needs the block model above, not operator spellings.
- 97EC: e / f bound temporaries -- nested block for f (99.75), `XZ e = ...` copy-init (same bytes), named `Vec3 d`
  for either initializer (92.5 / 99.68), by-value operator* / XZ(Vec3) / operator-(Vec3) (90.9 / 83.0 / 95.2),
  declaring e and f in one declaration (same bytes). The dump shows the three temps (f-bound, T1, e-bound) in the
  ENCLOSING if-block's list, above e / f; the target has them in creation order.
- 32C8 (cfe): moving the v104 zero stores before vF8 / uE8, `0.0f` literals, `if (1) {}` moves: 96.5-96.6 (< 99.52).
- 1340 / 23FC with the nested-block lever: 1340 flat (98.18, frame +16 or +8), 23FC flat or 2 rows worse at every
  block start between `t = ...` and the digit loop (its homes are already the 5040-grid optimum).
- gui 2DE0: `{ Spr *spr = ...; s32 w = ...` after the gSPTexture statement puts w under the first statement's 5 temps
  (frame 64 -> 80; target 104 needs 10 words above w) -- the remaining 4 words are not the first statement's.
- Timer-HUD "begin" inlines with a named local (`void bs() { Spr *s = this; f(s); }`) or a dead `Img *i = img;` move
  the spill words / ring toward the target (13B8 sC 99.23 standalone, 1340 98.28) but are dead code -- not landed.

**kit CXXXV addendum (same run): deferred vs immediate temporaries, more negatives.**

- (same run, late) Slot-reservation corollary: a function-scope local that is only ever register-coloured does NOT

  Late in the run: gl 65494 (cfe) 79.53 -> 80.62 by loading the next node before the `it[1]` store (`it` is a
