## kit CXXXVII (agent-g 2026-10-27, run 186): lever-sweep de-naming cracks the kernel relocation applier (80001ADC 52.46 -> 93.32), gl 65494 as C++ (80.62 -> 89.98) -- int-typed float-bit call arguments, `(float)iz()` as a distinct zero, and an inline `set()` whose parameters are evaluated before the named result's stores <a name="kit-cxxxvii-agent-g-run-186"></a>

**Result.** No exact (82.25 % code unchanged). NM (report.json): kernel func_80001ADC 52.45522 -> 93.32089 (536 B,
length = target), gl_func_00065494 80.61976 -> 89.97904 (1336 B, length = target; new NM-only NCC donor
`src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_65494_nm.cpp`).

**1. kernel 80001ADC (USO relocation applier, cfe -O2).** Three steps, each found by a tool:
- The 4-entry jump-table cap (kit LXXVI) stays, but the best shape is not the phantom `case 4/5: break;` arm: put the
  phantom label ON the default arm (`case 5: default: printf(...); return -2;`). Same behaviour (type 5 already went to
  the default), the cluster is 5 labels long so cfe emits the 1..5 table, and no extra arm block is laid out (the
  `case 5: break;` arm costs its own loop-end recompute block: 74.0 vs 81.8 at the same point).
- Indexed `rel[i]` with every `info` read written through memory (no `info` local): the target re-reads `r->info`
  after the arms (the `lw a0,0(a1)` join copy in every arm's `b` delay slot) -- 76.35 -> 76.43 on its own.
- `scripts/lever-sweep.py all` on the in-tree body: de-naming the symbol pointer `sym = &symtab[info >> 4]` (both
  reads index the table afresh) gave 81.81 -> 93.13 in one probe -- the named pointer was the extra live range that
  pushed base / symtab from s3 / s2 into s2 / ra and the arm delay slots from the join copy to the end recompute.
  Then a bbsplit after the HI16 read (+0.11). Lesson: on a cfe body run the sweep BEFORE theorising about colours.
- Left: frame 0x48 vs 0x50 (the dropped `sym` local had the slot that put hiptr at 0x34; unused / volatile / other
  named temps do not restore it without code changes), sltiu 5 vs 4, val / p loads after the bound test.
- 800018F0 (same file, 89.19): target materialises the `& ~8` mask as a uopt constant register (t5, hoisted in the
  unrolled loop) where ours gets the as1 `at` expansion; `~8U`, `0xFFFFFFF7`, `(u32)` casts, a mask variable and
  if/continue polarity grids are all flat.

**2. gl 65494 as C++ (cfe NM 80.62 -> NCC donor 89.98).** The function walks the self->0x39C child list with the
{cur, nxt} iterator (if/return `next()`, kit XIX) and does Vec3 arithmetic through value-class temporaries. Port order
and what each step bought (standalone objdiff, then report):
- Straight port (by-value `operator=(Vec3 v)`, named-result operator- / operator* / dot, impulse as
  `const Vec3 &` parameter -> bound temp sp+0x9C): 78.9. NOTE: a `Hit` struct whose member Vec3 has a user ctor gets an
  implicit ctor with the cfront `this == 0` protocol (`bnezl s5; jal __nw__FUi`) -- give the hit record a POD member.
- **Float-bit call arguments as int.** The target passes 400.0 / 1.0 as `lui a2,0x43C8` / `lui a3,0x3F80`; with a
  `float` parameter uopt reuses the hoisted FP constant register (`mfc1 a3,fs2`) or hoists 400.0 into fs5. Declare
  those parameters `int` and pass `0x43C80000` / `0x3F800000` (79.9; same thing the cfe body did).
- **A second, uncombined zero: `(float)iz()` with `inline int iz() { return 0; }`.** The target keeps the normal's
  (0, 1, 0) zeros in fs1 apart from the accumulator zero in fs2. Every literal spelling (0.0f, 0.0, (float)0, a named
  zero) is CSE'd into one register; the inline-call cast is folded only after CSE (kit CIX's `(f32)full()`), so it
  becomes its own hoisted constant (80.48). Use it only on the sites the target keeps apart.
- Named-result dot (`float r = ...; return r;`, 80.73); h / w / dt / f as function-scope named locals (target homes
  n 0x134 / d 0x128 / hit 0xF8 -- the nested-block rule of kit CXXXV, 80.88).
- lever-sweep order: `psum += v * w;` before `wsum += w;` -> 86.37 (the FP accumulator colouring follows).
- **Inline `set()` for a named result whose loads must precede its stores.** `Vec3 r; r.x = x - v.x; ...` stores
  r.x before loading y (r's address escapes into the return copy, so uopt keeps the order); the target loads all six
  fields first. `Vec3 r; r.set(x - v.x, y - v.y, z - v.z); return r;` evaluates the inline's parameters before any
  store and keeps the return-temp copies (86.37 -> 89.46 standalone, length unchanged); a float-temp spelling
  (`float a = x - v.x, ...; r.x = a; ...`) reorders too but drops the return copies (-8 bytes, rejected). The same
  set() form on the impulse scale (`n.sc(k)`) gave 89.91; on psum's product it costs w a callee-saved register.
- Left: the target leaves self + 0x2FC uncoloured (reloaded from its spill home 0x6C before the 62F64 call, no s8);
  ours colours it s8 (+1 save word, the whole save area shifts); psum's product loads interleave with its stores.

**3. Negatives / sweeps with no hits (this run).** lever-sweep `all`: C234, b5 8FC8, 55A0, gui 2DE0 / 3714 / 0F04 /
329C, b5 C310 / D884 / CEB4, gl 3430 / 2840, 8BD4, mgrproc 2B7C / 1824, BB8C, kernel 1594, 24B8 (B75C / 591C / 76F0
hits rejected: length away from target, or a store moved across a call). 3558: `(float)iz()` zero and set()-form

## kit CXXXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 175): per-site "base-0 alias" globals were ONE struct read through a local base pointer -- same-base accesses keep the source store / load order and a g-relative read is not loop-hoisted; a parameter or a single pointer variable reused for the ring-register reads is the target's s0 web; 4FD00 / 54E78 as real C++ with by-value `V3::set(V3)` <a name="kit-cxxxviii-agent-c-run-175"></a>

No exact. Five NM gains in game_libs_post / post0b (report.json, objdiff): 4FD00 80.29 -> 95.51 (1004 B), 334E8
74.48 -> 96.20 (708 B), 33BE4 80.70 -> 96.66 (724 B), 33EB8 90.83 -> 98.70 (712 B), 54E78 86.62 -> 91.07 (552 B);
every length now = target. Fuzzy 98.953 -> 99.019 %.

**1. The 334E8 / 33BE4 / 33EB8 allocator family: the "per-site base-0 alias" convention was the residual.** These
functions had one extern per access site (`gl_d_33eb8_8a .. 8d`, all pinned to 8, ...) so IDO would rematerialize
`lui rX,0; lw off(rX)` at every site. That reproduced the loads but left two "caps" documented as unreachable:
(a) the flush-loop's 0x28 read hoisted to `lui s3; addiu s3,40` + `lw 0(s3)`, and (b) a call result stored AFTER the
following compare loads (target: store first, then the loads, with a delay nop). Both are one cause: the heap words
are fields of ONE struct reached through a local pointer, `u8 *g = &<base-0 sym>; ... *(s32 *)(g + 0x2C)`.
- g + constant offsets still fold to `lui rX,0; lw off(rX)` per site (g is a constant, IDO splits hi / lo and
  rematerializes, it does not hold the address in an s-register);
- accesses through the same base may alias, so uopt keeps the source order of a store and later loads (cap b; in
  33EB8 this also restored the `sll zero` delay slot = target length);
- a g-relative read inside an innermost loop is not invariant-hoisted (cap a), where a single-use global symbol is.
Moving every field of the family through g: 33EB8 93.63 -> 97.91, 334E8 92.21 -> 94.60, 33BE4 93.54 -> 95.83.
Rule: when a function reads several fields at the same small absolute offsets (lui 0 + field offset, baked USO
relocs) and the per-site alias trick leaves store/load-order or loop-hoist residuals, try one base pointer local.

**2. One variable for several roles = the target's mystery s0.** The target colours `lui s0,0; lw s0,40(s0);
jal; addiu a1,s0,8` (the ring-register pointer in a callee-saved register though it never crosses a call) and, at
other sites, `lui s0,0; lw a1,40(s0)`. That is one named variable whose web also covers a value that DOES cross
calls: in 334E8 the pointer that first carries the stack buffer (`p = buf; f(p, fmt); src = (s32)p;`), in 33BE4 /
33EB8 the `flags` PARAMETER (gate copy in s0, then `flags = G->p28` at every poll site; in 33EB8 `flags` is also the
chunk length). Writing `p = *(u8 **)(g + 0x28), f(base, p + 8)` at each 0x28 site: 334E8 88.42 -> 91.31 and freed
s1 for base (the extra saved register the target has).

**3. Decode fixes in the same family.** (i) The outer loop is a do-while (target back edge `bnez s4,top`, no rotated
head); the old `top: ... if (rem) goto top;` gave a rotated loop. (ii) The window min `if (avail < rem) chunk = avail;
else chunk = rem;` with `chunk = rem` also assigned earlier: the else copy coalesces into the earlier move and leaves
the target's `beqz at,L; nop; b L; move s2,v0` (a branch-always to its own fall-through label). A ternary or a plain
if gives `beqz; move` without the `b`. (iii) lever-sweep then found `rem = 8` after the second call (334E8 +0.79).

**4. 4FD00 = `int Col::side(int f1, int f2)` (C++, the 3B6A0 collision record).** Tells: Vec3 temps copied
with lw/sw into one low temp and then member-stored (`set(V3 p)` by value), and a double `move t6,t8; move t8,t6`

**kit CXXXVIII addendum (same run).** (i) 33EB8's frame 64 vs 80: an unused `s32 pad[4];` declared FIRST gives the

## kit CXL (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 188): the 4-entry jump table is not reachable from ANY front end we have -- cfe 5.3/7.1 (cluster rule), edgcpfe 5.3/7.1 (never tables), uopt/ugen (never shrink a table); a same-segment 4-label compare chain proves the 4-table units used a different compiler; side finding: `switch (x & M)` drops the bound check <a name="kit-cxl-agent-g-run-188"></a>

**Question.** gl_func_000076F0 (two tables), game_uso 0B3C / 8CD8, titproc 116C and kernel func_80001ADC (about 9.6 KB)
each dispatch through a table guarded by `sltiu at,x,4`. Our cfe emits a compare chain for every 4-label switch.
Is there a source spelling, flag, compiler version or front end that gives a 4-entry table? **Answer: no, with every
compiler in tools/. The units came from a compiler we do not have. Keep the phantom-5th-label shape.** Kit LXXVI
found the cfe rule; this run re-checked it and closed the other routes.

1. **cfe 7.1 (rule re-read, `tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/cfe.c` func_465d90, lines ~162100-162420).**
   It sorts the labels and walks them into clusters. A label joins the cluster while `value <= prev + 25`. A
   cluster with `count < 5` (`at = a1 < 0x5`, used both inside the loop and for the last cluster) is broken up
   into single-label entries, and those become a binary search of `equ` tests (func_465654). The direct
   `func_46508c` (the only `xjp` writer, opcode 0x8c) call at L4666b4 runs only when exactly ONE cluster is
   left and its count is not 1, i.e. after a 5+ cluster survives. A table's range is first..last label, so it always
   has at least 5 entries. No flag, pragma or selector type touches either constant.
   `default:` is not in the list.
2. **cfe 5.3**: the same code (`objdump -d ido/5.3/usr/lib/cfe`: `addiu t5,t9,25` at 0x470824/0x470868 next to
   `sltiu at,a1,5` at 0x4708f8/0x470b48).
3. **edgcpfe 7.1 AND 5.3 (NCC; IDO 5.3 ships `usr/lib/DCC/edgcpfe` too).** The switch lowering
   (7.1 `func_51d740`, called for statement kind 9 from `mbe_statement`; 5.3 the same code inside `mbe_block`
   around 0x51bac4) loops over every clause and every case value: `lod` (0x52) temp, `mbe_load_constant`,
   `equ` (0x23), `tjp` (0x7f) to the clause label, then `ujp` (0x88) to the default. No code path writes `xjp`.
   The only `li aN,0x8c` writers in either binary are initializer code (`scan_*initializer*`, func_43a878 / func_459f38).
   cfront `c++` (5.3) emits C for cfe and so follows rule 1.
4. **uopt / ugen never make a table smaller.** uopt re-emits `xjp` from the graph node's stored bounds (`f_reemit`,
   uopt.c ~55290). It does not turn `tjp` chains into tables: NCC's 16- and 40-case dense switches come out as chains.
   Dead and default-equal trailing entries stay in the table: `switch (x & 3)` with labels 0..4 deletes the
   case-4 arm but keeps 5 rodata words, the 5th pointing at the join. `case 5: default:` (kit CXXXVII) also stays
   `sltiu 5`.
5. **The ROM shows two compilers in game_libs.** The visible (uncompressed) dispatches scan as sltiu 4 x4,
   5 x7, 6 x5, 7 x5, ... and never 2 or 3, so 4 is the smallest table anyone built. The table contents
   (`scripts/extract-uso-jumptable.py gl_func_000076F0 --module 0xD9FE28 --vaddr 0x76F0 --size 0x904
   --shim 0x1466C`) are: 76F0 switch 1 = 6 entries (labels 0..5, 4 and 5 share an arm), **switch 2 = 4 entries
   for labels 0, 1, 2, 3 with 1 and 2 sharing an arm**, switch 4 = 4 distinct arms. The EXACT
   gl_func_0002FB74 (game code in the same segment, `game_libs_o2_2FB74.c`) has
   `switch (sel) { case 0: case 1: ...; case 2: ...; case 3: ...; }`. That is the same shape (4 labels, one shared
   pair, 3 arms + default), and the target has the cfe compare chain (`beqz; beq 1; beq 2; beq 3`). The OoT audio
   code (253C4, 28B0C, 28C6C) has more exact 4-label chains. One deterministic per-switch rule cannot give both, so
   76F0 / 0B3C / 8CD8 / 116C / 80001ADC were built by another front end, one with a 4-label threshold (the old
   pcc `n >= 4` rule) that we do not have. A donor splice therefore has no compiler to come from.
6. **What to do with these functions.** Keep a phantom 5th label, and attach it to an arm that already exists so
   that no extra block is laid out: on the default arm (80001ADC `case 5: default:`), on a shared arm (76F0
   switch 2 `case 1: case 2: case 4:`), or on an empty arm (8CD8 below). Then the residual is the `sltiu` word
   plus the table-base words. Do not spend more time on the table itself.

**Applied (NM).** game_uso 8CD8 83.97 -> 84.24 (report, length = target 745): the source had an explicit
`if ((u32)idxm < 4U)` guard around a 2-case chain. It is now a switch that puts `case 2: case 3: case 4: break;` on
one empty arm (table dispatch like the target, `sltiu 5` vs 4). Storing the increment and the mask straight through
`*(s32 *)(arg1 + 0x9C)` (no `idx` / `idxm` locals) keeps both in ugen t-temps, as in the target (`lw t5; addiu t6;
andi t8; sw t6; sltiu; sw t8`); `= (*p += 1) & 3` loses the first store (83.96). The other four already use the best
phantom shape: 0B3C 99.59, 116C 99.12, 76F0 95.00, 80001ADC 93.39.

**Side finding: `switch (x & M)` drops the bound check.** When the switch operand is literally `expr & M`,
lbound is 0 and hbound >= M, cfe/IDO emits `andi; sll; lui; addu; lw; jr` with no `sltiu/beqz`, and it deletes the
arms for labels above M (the table keeps its full length in rodata). Measured at -O2: `switch (x & 3)` with labels
0..4 or 0..7 has no check. These keep it: `(x & 3) + 1`, `x & 7` with labels 1..5 (lbound 1), `x & 7` with
labels 0..4 (hbound < M), unsigned `x % 4`, a named `y = x & 3` (also stored), and at -O2 `switch (g = x & 3)` (no
check at -O1). So a target table WITHOUT a bound check after an `andi` is `switch (x & M)` over 0..M plus enough
phantom labels to reach 5. A table of 4 or 5 entries cannot be told apart in .text. 8CD8's target keeps the check
after `andi 3`, which matches the assignment-operand form.

`lui s1; lui a1; addiu a1,a1,lo; jal; addiu a0,s1,0` in the target. The ugen trace (`-Wc,-d` on the dump compiler)
is the same for both orders (`la s1; move a0,s1; la a1; jal`); as1 merges the dead `la s1` + `move` into
`addiu a0,s1,lo` and then picks the delay-slot instruction -- and that pick follows the SOURCE LINE numbers.
Writing `if (flags & 1) { base = (u8 *)&D_00000000; call(base, &fmt);` on ONE line (the `}` may stay on the next)
gives the target; any single other join does not (an exhaustive 512-way line-join search on a 10-line reduction:
exactly the masks joining `{`, `base =` and the call match). Types, prototypes, `base =` placement, a macro base,
string literals and casts were all inert (uopt canonicalises them). Rule: when a jal delay slot holds the "wrong"
one of two independent argument setups and every expression spelling is inert, search line joins of the statements
feeding that call. spelling-grid marker for a join: append `@{\n@| }@` to a line (newline vs space).
- The same lever fixed 33BE4's copy-loop preheader (`lui a0; addiu a0; or v1,s5` vs ours `lui a0; or v1,s5; addiu
  a0`): `cpsrc = src; cpdst = &dst;` on one line.

**2. A parameter copied into a local after another statement = the target's entry move order.** Target entry
`or s0,a1` ... `or s4,a1` (rem) before the `beqz`, `or s5,a0` (src) in its delay slot; ours copied the a0 parameter
first. Params coloured into s-registers get their moves at the entry in our order; a LOCAL `s32 src;` with
`rem = flags; src = src0;` (parameter renamed `src0`) makes the move a body statement, emitted after `rem`. 33EB8
took the same fix (`dst = dst0`); the extra local costs one frame word there, so its unused `pad[4]` became `pad[3]`
(frame 80 = target).

**3. Decode fixes that moved colours (33BE4 96.66 -> 99.89; 334E8 the same set).**
- `mis` is REUSED for `8 - mis` (`mis = 8 - mis; if ((u32)mis < chunk) chunk = mis;`): the target keeps mis / 8-mis
  in a0 / v1, which is only reachable when the second value is in mis's web (a separate temp coloured v1 first).
- `mis = src & 7;` belongs INSIDE `if (chunk != 0)` (the target's `or s2,s4` precedes the `andi`).
- copy loop: init `cpsrc` first and bump `cpsrc` before `cpdst` -- uopt colours equal-priority loop variables in
  first-appearance order (dump `-Wo,-zdbug:6`: cnt v0, then the first-seen cursor v1, the next a0).
- the ring bump is `*(s32 *)(g + 8) += chunk;` with the call re-reading `*(g + 8)`; and the segment-end test compares
  two fresh reads, naming `cur` only inside the arm -- the old `cur = G->8; if (G->2C == cur)` joined cur's web with
  the earlier a2 argument and coloured it a2 (target: ring temp t4, `or a2,t4` in the bne delay slot).

**4. 334E8 frame 112 -> 104 = two fewer named locals; under cfe every named scalar local gets a vreg home that
counts toward the frame.** The `-Wo,-zdbug:5` itab shows `M 3 -N vreg` homes for every declared scalar (buf -8, then
one word per scalar in declaration order); the frame's local area spans down to the lowest home, rounded to 8.
334E8 had 15 words (buf + 13 scalars) -> 112; the target 104 allows 13. The two that go: `base` (a `#define base
((u8 *)&D_00000000)` -- uopt hoists the one address constant into s1 exactly as the named variable was) and the
block magic `sent` (a literal; uopt still hoists 0x12340002 into s3). Removing `cur` instead re-joins its web with
avail (avail coloured a2, wrong). Then `src = (s32)p; rem = 8; call(base);` on one line is the entry order (lever 1).
Note `#undef base` after the function.

**Negatives (same run).** 6126C: the char copy `or a0,v1` at the dispatch head is not a separate dispatch variable
(copy-propagated), not a type conversion (u8/char/u16/u32), not a switch (69-76, worse); all four reads through the
old-pointer copy without `if (arg3) {}` stay 496. 4F2DC: kit CXXXIX's advanced-pointer form (`cam += 0x70;` then
`+0x30` fields) reproduces the target's dead `addiu v1,v1,112` and replaces the `if (1) {}` length fix, but loses
6 points of schedule (store/mul interleave not found in a 730-probe perm search); line joins +0.08 only. 4FD00 NCC:
block scopes / one SV local / sum2 helper / line joins all inert or worse for the shared SV home. 469A8: advanced
pointers for p100 / p78 / pDC inert, the 0x158 / &D+0x254 store swap worse (needs a C++ port).
- (end) 31A74 frame lead (not landed): under the vreg-home rule (section 4) the target frame 24 (ra at 20) leaves NO
  room for a named local, yet the target keeps acc / ratio in f0 apart from v (f12). Dropping lp / lim and folding
  acc into r: 1 local, frame still 32; folding r into the parameter v: frame 24 = target but everything coalesces into
  f12 (89.14 < 90.38); a fourth float parameter or `register f32 r` do not help. The f0 ratio without a home is the
  open question (expression-only form? a by-value helper?).
- (end) 2D374: swapping the 0x35C / 0x358 stores gives the target store order but z stays f12 (target f0, fr f2);
  99.645 -> 99.615, reverted; `if (z) {}` / `if (fr) {}` and the z / fr / half statement order are inert.
- (end) 36694 C++ lead (not landed, 82.15 standalone vs cfe-lift NM 84.03, length 712 = target): `V3 Obj::proj(V3 p,
  V3 n)` (a1 = unused this, hidden return in a0) with inline by-value-returning `operator*(f32)` / `operator/(f32)`
  (local `V3 r; ... return r;` = the target's local + return-copy pairs), `operator-(V3 o)` BY VALUE (the third

## kit CXLII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 189): a multi-role variable is coloured into a callee-saved register only when its FIRST role is in the web -- route the first call's argument intermediate through it (bootup 24B8: arg0 -> s1, var -> s0 as the target); the four 0.1f "step" words in gl 3430 are one literal kept in caller-saved f2 by a live-range split; volatile never reproduces per-site `lui; lw lo(rX)` <a name="kit-cxlii-agent-g-run-189"></a>

No exact. One NM gain: bootup_uso func_000024B8 95.21 -> 97.05 (report.json, 700 B, length = target 175 words).
Fuzzy 99.0399 -> 99.0415 %.

**1. 24B8: the target's extra saved register is the reused pointer variable, and its first role is a call
argument.** The NM body already reused ONE `char *s0` for cfg / vtable descriptor / FP field pointers (agent-c),
but our build kept arg0 in s0 and the variable in v1 / a3 / a1 (frame and every later s-register off). The target's
first s0 write is in the gate block before the first call: `lw s0,16(v0); andi s0,s0,0x400; ... sltu a0,zero,s0`
-- the `(cfg->0x10 & 0x400) != 0` argument is computed IN the variable. Writing
`s0 = (char *)((FW(v0, 0x10) & 0x400) != 0); f((int)s0, (*(u32 *)(v0 + 0x10) & 0x1000) != 0, ...)` makes uopt
colour the whole web s0 and arg0 s1 (95.03 -> 96.58 objdiff, 173 -> 175 words, same as the target). Spellings
that lose: `s0 = (char *)FW(v0, 0x10)` + `((int)s0 & 0x400) != 0` (the raw field load is CSE'd with the second,
u32-typed read of the same word -> one load, 94.37); `s0 = (char *)(FW & 0x400)` + `s0 != 0` (95.03). Then the
`t0` latch and `k` as ONE int variable: 96.87 (objdiff), 97.05 in report.json.
Rule: when the target holds a value in an s-register that is dead before every call (no crossing) and our build
has that value in a temp, look for the earliest instruction writing that s-register: that expression belongs to the
same source variable as the later roles.
Negatives (24B8): restoring `s0 = cfg` inside the ramp block (95.07), dropping the `if (1) {}` after
`s0 = v1 + 0x14C` (one 95.74, both 94.50), `t0 = 0` in an else of the gate (93.33), the second argument through
the v1 variable (96.67), `r = 0` after the s0 statement (inert). Left: the latch var colours v1 (target t0, which
shifts the whole t-ring by one: t2 vs t3 ...), the first ramp pointer is a v0 temp (target s0), the cfg temp a0 (target v0).
Scan used to find it (cheap, all units): compare the prologue's saved-register set (`sw sN` / `sdc1 fN` in the first
40 words) of expected vs build/non_matching for every NM function. Only three differ in agent-g's units: 24B8 (target
+s0, fixed), gui 2DE0 (target +s0: ctx, switch value and the first MAX temp in one register; an NCC `s32 v` / `Ctx *v`
carrying CTX and the switch value scores 91.5-92.7 vs 94.50, not landed) and game_uso 3558 (target +f20 zero).

**2. gl_func_00003430: the "step" words are one 0.1f literal.** The target loads `lwc1 $f2,0xCC8` before the loop
(after the 0xEC store, after the 1.0f / 10.625f mtc1s) and reloads f2 from 0xCEC / 0xCF0 / 0xCF4 at the end of
cases 6 / 7 / 8, each right after that case's last call, with no f2 use in those cases: that is uopt's live-range
split of a constant in a caller-saved register (reload = rematerialisation; as1 emits a fresh literal per load, in
code order, which is why the pool has 0xCC8, the jump table at 0xCCC, then 0xCEC..0xCF4). The NM body models it with
a `step` variable re-assigned from four externs. With the plain literal (no step variable, `0.1f + FF(s0,0x88)` in
case 3; 7 spellings incl. `(f32)0.1`, `+=`) cfe colours the constant into a new callee-saved f24 (zdbug:5: LR const
0.1 adjsave 1.33, forbidden v-regs, assigned 32 = f24; 1.0 -> f22, 10.625 -> f20) -- the target split it instead,
so the target LR's adjsave x span was below f24's first-use cost (or its cost higher). Not landed; the lead is the
allocator inputs for that LR (BB count / span), not the spelling. Also: `FW(arg0,0xEC) = 1;` before the step load
puts the load after the store as the target but the constants follow it (at-chain order), 97.41 -> lower.

**3. timproc_b5 D884 / DF14 flag word (`G.f4 &= ~0x80000; &= ~1; |= 2; &= ~0x20000; |= 0x2000`).** The target has
per-site `lui tN,0; lw tN,4(tN)` loads, `lui at,0; sw 4(at)` stores sharing one `at` between some pairs, and every
load after the preceding store (= same symbol for as1). Probed under cfe 7.1, cfe 5.3 and NCC, standalone: volatile
array element, volatile struct member, volatile member of a plain struct, volatile cast of an element, a volatile
SCALAR extern -- all hoist the address into one register (`lui v0; addiu v0; lw 4(v0)` / `sw 4(v0)`); per-site
DISTINCT volatile scalars emit `lui; addiu; lw 0(rX)` (no lo fold). Non-volatile: mixing direct-member and cast
accesses, or s32 / u32 types, keeps every store (no DSE) but forwards the stored value into the next load (one load
total). No spelling in our compilers gives store-then-reload with folded lo16s -- with kit CXL's table result, a
second sign that these timproc units came from another compiler build.

**4. Negatives / no-hit sweeps.** lever-sweep `all` (no landable hits): game_uso 0B3C, 591C (one hit moves a load
across a call, +4 bytes: rejected), 8CD8, the 7C1C / BB8C NCC donors, gl 65494 donor. gl 65EE4 (-O2 -Olimit 1
donor): the whole three-block body on one source line per block is already the best layout (512-mask line-join
search; one statement per line scores 78.2 vs 88.7 standalone); argument spellings (`&G` casts, `G.base` vs
`*(int *)((char *)&G + 0x28)` / `((int *)&G)[10]` / `(B)`, data / base field types, data constant forms) are inert
at length (the offset spellings drop 24 bytes); cfe 5.3 = 7.1, NCC = cfe, -O1 adds three moves. kernel 18F0: store
block as `continue` / `if (found)` / `found != 0` / `found == 1`, the ~8 mask as `0xFFFFFFF7` / `-9` / hoisted
local, `&syms[i]` / char-offset / `syms +` addressing -- all byte-identical output; bitfield structs 47-72 (worse);
5.3 = 7.1. game_uso 97EC: a nested block for f (or for the tail) swaps the two bound temporaries but drops f and its
temp below every other slot (frame +8, 99.75); copy-init `XZ e = XZ(..)` / `= ..` inert; a by-value `XZv(Vec3)`
ctor for e changes FP colours (98.56). game_uso 3558 NCC donor: 288-way grid over the zero spellings (variable,
`0.0`, `(float)0.0`, `0.0f` for side / w.y / else factor / the zero init) all identical (NCC const-propagates every
one); note the donor is 1024 bytes (+16), not "251 of 252 words" as its header says. game_uso 8CD8 as real C++
(Vec3 with class-scope operator new, derived XZ / XZD / Perp ctors for every alloc guard, sub2 / sub3 by-value
return chains for the word-copy stages, `switch (s->phase = s->phase & 3)` with two arms): 76.90 standalone at +72
bytes after a 293-probe grid over the copy-chain depth per site, vs the cfe body's 84.23; the first guard's
`addiu a0,sp,504; bnezl a0` (this in a0, o3 reload in the delay slot) is not reproduced (ours this in v1, bnez).
Not landed.
- (end) 37540 NM 79.80 -> 81.17, length 760 -> 764 = target: the target re-reads `o->2C->0x10` on BOTH paths of
  the first flag test (`beqzl t9,L; lw t0,16(v0)` -- the reload in the likely-delay slot on the not-taken path, while
  `o->2C` itself is reused there). Ours CSE'd the flags word across the test (`beqzl; andi t6,v0,8`). Reading it as
  `((volatile s32 *)FW(o, 0x2C))[4]` gives the reload with the offset folded; `*(volatile s32 *)(FW(o, 0x2C) + 0x10)`
  computes the address separately (`addiu v0,v0,16; lw 0(v0)`) and overshoots the length by 8. Tell: a field load in a
  branch-likely delay slot that repeats a load the fall-through already did = a volatile (hardware-style) word.
  post0b NM clip 0x2eabc -> 0x2eac0.

**kit CXLII addendum (same run): where the other s-register mismatches point.** A second scan (count of
instructions WRITING each s-register, expected vs NM build) flags timproc_b5 8FC8 (target s1 48 / s0 29 writes, ours

**kit CXLII addendum 2 (agent-g run 189, kit CXLI line-layout lever tried on agent-g units, all inert):** bootup 6204

## kit CXLIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 177): the 308AC file-local static block also carries its sibling 307A8 -- NCC donor with two references per block for the shared-`lui at` pairs (96.38 -> 99.46, length = target); 38A28's 9-entry table is cfe-only while its colouring is edg-only; per-site alias pins retired <a name="kit-cxliii-agent-c-run-177"></a>

No exact. report.json: game_libs_func_000307A8 "96.38" -> "99.46" (260 B, NM-only NCC donor, 268 -> 260 bytes =
target); matched code unchanged at "82.53" %. Clean-up commit: the 66 unused per-site alias pins of the allocator
family (gl_d_334e8_8a.., gl_d_33be4_8a.., gl_d_33eb8_8a..) and their externs removed (the copy-loop bases
gl_d_334e8_dst / gl_d_33be4_dst / gl_d_33eb8_src stay); ROM byte-identical.

**1. One module-local data block = one family of lui-at shapes; port the siblings together.** 307A8 (fade tick)
reads the same 8-word block at Data sym1448 @0x338 that the exact 308AC (mode setter) reads as `static St308 A308`.
Its cfe body sat at 68 vs 65 words for exactly the cap documented in #shared-at-absolute-store-cap-66a50: the
zeroing pair `lui at; sw zero,12(at); sw zero,8(at)` and the down-arm pair `lui at; lwc1 $f0,16(at); lwc1 $f2,20(at)`.
Under NCC with the 308AC rule (as1 merges the `%hi` of two accesses only for the SAME LOCAL symbol whose address uopt
did not CSE) both pairs come out right when each pair is two references to fields of the static in ONE block:
`{ int &r = A308.fC; int &q = A308.f8; r = 0; q = 0; }` and `{ f32 &r = A308.f10; f32 &q = A308.f14; f = r; fl = q; }`.
Every other access stays a per-site extern alias (D_307A8_x): a second reference to the SAME field of the static in
another block is CSE'd into a base register (`lui a0; addiu a0,8` / `0(a0)`), which is wrong everywhere else in the
function. The cfe keep-alives carry over unchanged (`while (0) { f = c + c; }` for the up-arm load order, `if (c) {}`
in the down arm). Donor: src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_307A8_nm.cpp (NM only; the static's reloc is renamed by the splice
like 308AC's, and the D_307A8_x aliases would need pins before a build-path promotion). Search rule: when a residual is
a shared `lui at` pair, grep for an exact sibling that touches the same Data symbol -- if that one is a static-block
donor, the pair is reachable.
- Residual (5 words): the hold count. Target: `lui t8` hoisted above `beqz v0`, `lw t8,12(t8)`, `beqz t8`,
  `addiu t9,t8,-1` in the delay slot (t8 / t9 = the next two ugen ring slots after t6 / t7). Ours: the test + decrement
  of one alias are one uopt candidate (dump `-Wo,-zdbug:6`: candidate 35 = `uilod`, assigned v1), so the decrement
  lands in t8. Probed, none gives one load in the ring: `-= 1`, `--`, same-symbol `i = i - 1`, `+ -1`, a named int,
  `c = hold, c != 0` (comma), the access through a reference / pointer / `(*(int *)((char *)&D + 12))` / `((int
  *)&D)[3]` (all canonicalised to the same candidate), the static block with `A308.fC -= 1` (base CSE'd into a0),
  and typed loads (`*(unsigned *)` / `*(char **)` on the test or the decrement only): the test is then a ring temp in
  t8 exactly like the target, but the decrement reloads (+3 words). `if (int h = ...)` condition declarations are not
  supported by this edgcpfe (error 3112). The single target load that feeds both blocks is either a candidate coloured
  t8 or something our compilers do not do.

**2. 38A28's 9-entry jump table (`sltiu at,t6,9`, cases 0x64..0x6C) is cfe; its colouring is edg.** A cfe C body
with `case 0x68: case 0x69: case 0x6A: case 0x6B: case 0x6C:` on the default arm emits the target's table head, and
the decode fixes from the NCC donor port back (default call `(msg, code, o->0xC)`, unsigned key, `if (key >= 40)`;
new: arm 0x66 stores the TABLE ENTRY pointer to o->0x14, not the call result -- target `sw v0,36(sp)` in the jal
delay, `lw v0,36(sp)`, `sw v0,20(s0)`). Standalone 84.20 vs the NCC donor's 77.17, but 344 vs 324 bytes (the NCC body
is 316): cfe colours o into a3 with a save / reload around every call (dump: o = `P 0` candidate -> a3) and homes the
selector (`not colored, not splittable` across the `jr`), where the target keeps o in s0 and the selector in v0 exactly
as the NCC (compare-chain) build does. Neither a local copy of o, a named / unnamed selector, extra pad words nor IDO
5.3 cfe changes that. Not landed (length moves away). This is kit CXL's finding again from the other side: the
table units were compiled by a front end that has edg's allocation and cfe's switch lowering.

**3. Leads and negatives (same run).**
- 415A4 lead: the +0x28 pair (`addiu v0,zero,1030` early; `lui at; addiu t1,zero,1030; ori v0,v0,6; sw t1,40(at);
  ori v0,v0,0x400; sw v0,40(at)`) is again one `lui at` over two stores of one local symbol. NCC with `static T415A4
  T;` and `{ float *v = T.v30; v[3] = v[2] = v[1] = v[0] = 0.0f; }` reproduces the separate `lui v0; addiu v0,48`
  Vec4 base, the 12/8/4/0 store order and a2C through the t base -- all open in the cfe body. The OR chain is not
  found yet: `r |= 6; r |= 0x400` through a reference keeps three stores; `r = r | 6 | 0x400` folds to `ori 0x406`.
  The rest of the NCC port moves the frame (64 vs 56), so this needs the whole function under NCC.
- 35B1C as a real C++ constructor (`Obj { Obj *next; W key; int val; virtual f(); }`, vptr at +0xC, `W() { v = 0; }`
  member) reproduces the 77-word body including the target's `bne s4,-4` (the member ctor's null test folded to
  `this != -4`), but the vtable store still comes right after `addiu t6` (target: after `addiu v1; li at`) and the frame
  is 72 vs 80; ctor header / mem-init / brace line layouts (6 variants) inert.
- Flat grids: 41D40 next() / operator[] spellings (30), 3E5E0 K / CB ctor forms (24), 3AE58 pick / vtx / ent inline
  forms (60), 37938 operator- / operator* return forms x parameter types (36), 250C8 selector / arm spellings (64),
  33094 block-local / advanced-pointer forms for a / k (15: block locals shrink the frame 24 bytes).
- 250C8: fontId declared in the `case 1: { }` block gets its home between the compiler temps and the outer locals
  (sp+44, the reloc struct moves down 4), not the target's shared temp slot sp+36; removing the outer pad words moves the
  whole layout up instead. 2D374: d replaced by z and fr reused for the 358 reload, and the decl order z / fr: inert
  (FP z / fr are ugen temps, not candidates -- the dump has no FP candidate for them).

## kit CXLIV (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 190): gl 49B3C EXACT -- an array iterator's `cur()` that reads the array through a local reference (`Arr &r = *a; return r[idx];`) swaps the body's base-reload / vtable registers to the target's v1 / a1; a list iterator's `next()` written as an if-statement gives the bottom loop-copy's result v0; an inline `DLHead::inc() { return count++; }` makes edg's `this` temp the target's head-in-s-register for display-list appends (4B620) <a name="kit-cxliv-agent-g-run-190"></a>

Context: game_libs_post0b >= 0x48000 (new assignment), the NCC donor family of 49B3C / 4B620 / 4B0A8 / 48AEC / 493AC
(by-value AIter over the element array at +0x84, cfront ctor protocol, DL appends).

1. **49B3C (640 B) EXACT, three levers on agent-c's run-174 donor** (src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_49B3C.cpp, now
   spliced in both trees over a `void f(void) {}` placeholder; new pins D_49B3C_s1..s6, gl_49B3C_regf = 0).
   - `E1 *cur() { Arr &r = *a; return r[idx]; }` (was `return (*a)[idx];`): the body `it.cur()->tick()` re-reads
     it.a into v1 and the element's vtable into a1, as the target. The named reference costs edg one more pooled
     temp, and that shifts which candidate gets v1. The same edit on `ref()` or on next() does nothing or makes it
     worse; on 4B0A8 / 4B620 / 48AEC / 493AC it makes things worse (frame or length moves). So it is a per-function
     lever: try it when the target's in-loop element read colours base/vtable the other way round.
   - List iterator `E2 *next() { if ((cur = nxt) != 0) { nxt = nxt->next; return cur->data; } return 0; }` instead
     of the `?:` comma form: the bottom copy of the loop test (uopt duplicates the while condition) keeps its result

## kit CXLVI (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 191): a cfe NM body that is really C++ gains most by a plain NCC port plus three shape levers -- distinct base-0 alias symbols per global access (no &D CSE across a call), ONE multi-role pointer for every value the target keeps in the same callee-saved register, and the five stack args of a 12-arg call as named block locals (4C5E4 79.69 -> 87.06); `cell = &cells[base]; cell += i;` keeps uopt from reassociating a 2-D index (4A9F0 89.63 -> 98.0); a de-named once-used pointer frees a home word (4A308) <a name="kit-cxlvi-agent-g-run-191"></a>

Context: game_libs_post0b >= 0x48000. Every value below is report.json after `make non_matching_objects`. Probing was done
with a standalone NCC / cfe compile and a reloc-masked word compare against the INCLUDE_ASM object (~0.3 s per variant).
A difflib opcode-aligned score (full word = 1, same opcode = 0.5) followed objdiff's ranking well enough to grid with;
plain mismatch counts did not (one early ring shift makes every later word "wrong").

1. **gl 4C5E4 (836 B): the cfe NM body ported to NCC as `void Obj::run()`, 79.69 -> 87.06, 848 -> 832 bytes (target 836).**
   Donor src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_4C5E4_nm.cpp (NM only, symbol renamed). What moved it, in order:
   - Accesses to the module global after the first call go through the existing base-0 aliases (gl_d_4c5e4_sh / _flag /
     _word / _reg / _arg / _clr). With one `&D` symbol, uopt keeps &D in s1 across the first call. The target re-`lui`s
     every one of them, and its a0 = &D only lives up to that call.
   - ONE `char *s1` for the if-arm draw argument (sub->F0), the else-arm virtual result, and later for `dl` (re-read
     before the viewport). The target keeps all three roles in callee-saved s1 (kit CXLII multi-role).
   - The else arm's 12-argument call: `int c0 = mC0, c4 = mC4, b8 = mB8, bc = mBC, sb8 = sb->mB8;` named before the
     call (uopt t0..t4 + v0, as in the target). That also gives ugen back its t6..t9-only ring everywhere else: the first
     40 words went from a t2/t3 ring to the target's t6/t8/t9. This single step was the biggest one (F 63 -> 72).
   - `void *pf = sb->mF0; int m4 = m & 4;` named before `if (f) f = ...` (the target loads F0 and masks m78 ahead of
     the branch), and `Sub2 *e = s14c[idx];` (the target keeps the entry in v0, not a ring temp).
   - The four viewport floats named before the Vp append (`fw = x*2, fx = w, fh = y*2, fy = h`). The tail is in its own
     `{ }` block, which puts the zero-colour `float buf[4]` 3 words under the frame top, as in the target.
   - lever-sweep `order` hit: `vtrans[0]` stored first (86.23 -> 87.06; independent field stores, no loads moved).
   Left: frame 184 vs 208 (spill slots 68 / 72 vs 72 / 80). NCC drops never-read locals even when volatile, so the
   missing homes can only come from real named values. The target also materialises 2.0f TWICE (x*2 and y*2) and 4.0f
   once; every spelling we tried (2 / 2.0f / (float)2 / 2.0, named or unnamed products, `if (0/1) {}` splits) CSEs it.
   That is the 4-byte length gap. Packet registers: the target uses a2 / a3 for head / pkt and v1 for the second packet
   (home 80); we get v1 / a2. inc() / next() / named-count forms are flat.
2. **gl 4A9F0 (160 B) 89.63 -> 98.0: `Cell *cell = &g->grid->cells[base]; cell += i;`** instead of `&cells[i + base]`.
   Any single expression (`[base + i]`, `(cells + base) + i`, `cells + base + i`, byte-pointer arithmetic) is
   reassociated by uopt into cells + i*16 + base*16, or i*16 is evaluated first. The split statement keeps the target's
   `(cells + base*16) + i*16`, but the cell variable takes both sums (v1, v1) where the target has a ring t4 for the first.

4. Negatives (standalone grids):

**1. The scanner (`python3 ../../scripts/decode-scan.py [--unit S] [--min-fuzzy N] [--unpinned]`, run in a project dir,
read-only, needs fresh `make non_matching_objects`).** For every function < 100 in report.json:
- A1: each lui-based site's effective %lo -- NM side = pin + (hi<<16 + sext lo) of the reloc, target side = the raw word
  (USO expected objects have NO relocs: `lui r,0` + the real %lo; game_libs >= 0x8000 targets also bake `lui 2`). Found
  by a linear register dataflow from each `lui`, carried through `addiu` so `addiu v0,%lo; lw 8(v0)` counts as lo+8
  ("via"). An NM address the target never forms, built from a non-zero pin + non-zero addend, prints `A1-DOUBLE` (the
  33094 class); `A1-MISSING` lists target addresses the NM never forms. Own .rodata/.bss/.data section sites (unpinned
  `*_rodata` / `.rodata+K`) are placement and skipped; a PINNED `*_data` name is a real symbol and kept.
- A2-SPLIT: same address, different form (NM folds into the load/store, target holds it with addiu and goes "via", or
  the reverse) -- the 31A74 class, the only address class that changes instruction shape.
- A3-PIN: unpinned NM symbol at a site whose positionally paired target site forms another address; prints a pin hint.

  every hint with `rdiff --raw --pins`. `--unpinned` lists all 300+ unpinned symbols (the normal NM state; noise).

## kit CL (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 185): cfe gives EVERY declared local a frame home in declaration order, unused ones too, so a frame / stack-slot residual is solved by putting scalar declarations in the target frame's one-word gaps; split shifts re-phase the ugen ring in NCC gbi macros; NCC named-pointer homes do not follow declaration order <a name="kit-cl-agent-c-run-185"></a>

**game_uso 0B3C (cfe NM body, 99.59 -> 99.83; raw diff 172 -> 3 words, length = target).** Every stack offset was
off (frame 360 vs 336) while objdiff still said 99.59: objdiff's fuzzy barely weighs sp displacements, so read
`rdiff --raw -q` (diffwords) next to `--nosp` before calling a function "register only". In cfe (IDO 7.1 C front
end) each declared local gets a home in declaration order, register-allocated or not and even when never used
(two unused `f32 *q; s32 msk;` cost 8 bytes). Recipe:
1. List the target's aggregate offsets (the NM decl comments usually already carry them) and find the gaps between
   consecutive aggregates: here 1 / 6 / 3 / 1 words after nseg / zv / stage / fresh, and none below v30.
2. Count the NM scalars (including block-scope floats, which land at the bottom). 0B3C had 15 for 11 gaps.
3. Drop the extras without losing registers: unused locals; a call-result pointer used once (inline the call);
   `adv` folded into `tmp` (one variable, two roles); the block floats hoisted and one of them merged into the
   already-declared `f1`; the `one = 1` constant variable dropped. Each step is checked against `--nosp` (merging
   `bv` into `tv`, `selv` into `st` or inlining `cur` / `node` broke colours and were rejected).
4. Declare the remaining scalars in the gaps. That gave frame 336 and every offset at once.
5. The new layout changed the schedule of the Tri3i stage -> pos copies: natural x/y/z order was now right (the old
   z/y/x one-line copies had been tuned against the wrong layout), and the up-vector sums want x/y/z in source
   order through f1 / fy / fz, with f1's home highest. Re-run the old ordering grids after any layout fix.
6. `tmp = 1` as the constant holder for the head compares (`if (tmp == cur)`, `= tmp`, `tmp == seg->0x10`) gives the
   target's `bne t0,v0` operand order (`1 == cur` gives `bne v0,t0`). Any of tmp / st / selv works; tmp already
   has two roles.
LEFT (3 words): the capped 4-entry table (kit CXL) and two call arguments `1` that the target materialises with
`addiu a1,zero,1` while ours reuse the live t0 = 1 (`1U`, `(s16)1`, `(u8)1`, `!0`, `(s32)1.0f`, unsigned or s16 tmp:
no change, or worse).

**gui 4568 (NCC NM donor, 91.79 -> 96.01).** Same gbi macro family as 329C / 2DE0 / F04 / 3714. Split shifts on the
gSPTextureRectangle arguments (`y << 1 << 1`, `(x + w) << 1 << 1`, `(y + h) << 1 << 1`; x stays `<< 2`) add the
phantom ugen ring slot(s) the target has and make the first packet word-exact (95.68). In the Scis arm,
`int xl = x << 2;` passed as xl gives the target's `or t2,a1` copy and a3 for yl (96.01). `rdiff --noreg` is now one
word plus the delay slot. LEFT: MAX pool temps (target t0 for the pooled MAX, pkt in t1; ours v1 / t0) and the first
MAX arm's delay slot (target nop). The target object is 198 words because the `addiu sp,sp,8` delay slot sits past
the unit's TRUNCATE_TEXT 0x4738, so this function can't score 100 in report.json even when it matches.
Negatives: the same split-shift and `xl` levers do nothing on 329C, F04 and 3714 (flat or worse); on 2DE0 the
329C-style `Ctx::load()` (pool variable into s0) gives the s0 prologue but costs +4 words and lowers the score.

**game_uso 1DDC (NCC, 99.97, negative but narrowed).** `c.getOut()->goal.set(m)` in place of the `Out *o` block
gets rid of o's home and makes the key-3 arm exact. With `V3 e` back (in place of `int e`) and `M4 *mm = &X; mm->getPos(v)`
named pointers, `--nosp` is 0 words: every register matches. What's left is homes only. The key-3 arm's mm sits in the
top gap and the 23D4 return / operator* temp is 8 bytes low (target sp+252, ours 244). In NCC, the home position
of a named pointer does NOT depend on where it is declared: mm at arm scope, at function scope or in a block, in
any declaration position, gives identical layouts (unlike cfe above). Without the named pointers the pointers
colour v0, not the target's v1, and every non-named spelling tried also gives v0 (`getPosF/getPosP` free inlines,
member getters, `Body::getPos`, `const float *p = m[3]`). Not committed (99.79 < 99.97).
**game_uso 97EC (NCC, negative):** swapping the e / f ctor-bound temporary homes isn't reachable via copy-init,
`XZ(...)` spellings, by-value ctor parameters, friend / reversed `operator*` / `operator-`, named returns, nested
blocks or early returns (flat, or a +8 frame).
**game_uso 591C:** the scanner's five `!(a <= b)` compares match the target's `c.le.s` + bc1f forms (decode-correct,
leave them). The bc1t / bc1tl swap belongs to the first switch's per-case `or v0,v1` join copy; `v0 = vsel;
switch (v0)` and `*(self+0x74) = vsel = 1` spellings are flat or worse.
**game_uso 3558:** interleaving `vb.c += r` into the matrix rows (24 orders x store orders) is flat; the z-first order
stays best.
**Lead, game_uso 7C1C (NCC NM donor, 92.59; target frame 944, ours 864).** The donor is still the cfe emulation
(`p = 0; if (1) { p = &nA; } if (p != NULL || (p = alloc(12)) != NULL) {...}`). A real derived-class constructor

VN(a, 0.0f, c) {} };` with `XZ nA(q[0], q[2]); XZ nB(nA.x - a4.x, nA.z - a4.z);` declared in the arg3 == NULL block,

jal 055750; addiu a0,zero,12; beqz v0; or v1,v0`, then y / x / z stores). The score drops slightly (92.59 -> 92.30)
only because the block objects take low homes (136 / 124), where the target has nA / nB at 908 / 840, just under

if (p || (p = alloc(12))) {...}` + Tri3i word copies, all 60 Vec3s at function scope in target order) had every home right

refs, `operator*` returning `Vec3(...)`; `XZ : Vec3` with `XZ(const Vec3 &)` and `XZ(float, float)` base-initialiser
ctors; free `XZ operator-(const XZ &, const Vec3 &)` and `XZ perp(const Vec3 &)` returning `XZ(...)`) reproduces every guard,
every copy chain and the pooled slots 852 / 540 / 508 without any emulation. Spelling rules found on the way:
- Copy count tells the declared type: `XZ d = XZ(p) - q;` = inner XZ -> return slot -> d (two word copies, then-arm d /
  else-arm rd / e / dir); `Vec3 seg = XZ(p) - q;` adds the slicing temporary (three copies: mB -> 852 -> 820 -> 780).
- `result = rd` with an XZ `rd` and a by-value `operator=(Vec3)` costs a derived-to-base temporary first (+9 words over the
  function); `result = (const Vec3 &)rd;` copies straight into the parameter (the pooled slot) as the target does.
- **Pooled return slots are released at the end of the full-expression, not when the copy is done.** The loop's
  `lP -> s2 (sp+540) -> lDir` chain (the target's only use of s2 for a slot address) comes from ONE statement,
  `XZ ldir = perp(XZ(n->pos) - b->pos);`: operator-'s result sits in 852 and is copied into a binding temporary (380) for
  perp's `const Vec3 &`, but 852 stays allocated, so perp returns through the next slot (540). Written as
  `XZ lseg = ...; XZ ldir = perp(lseg);` perp reused 852 and the whole loop was off (89.37 -> 94.48 for this one change,
  length 1068 -> 1071). The mode chains (`result += dir * 250.0f * b->width * 0.5f;` -> slots 852 / 540 / 508) are the
  same rule. Tell: a target word-copy chain that goes through a SECOND pooled slot (a different address register / s-reg
  than the usual stage) = the call is nested inside a larger expression that still holds the first slot.
- Then-arm `const Vec3 &d = XZ(a->pos) - *pos;` (reference binding) +0.03 over `XZ d = ...`.
- **Unnamed booleans go to the spill area.** The target computes `hit != 0` and its negation at the loop top and spills them
  to sp+84 / sp+80, the two words under the lowest edg home (kit CXXXV spill area). Named `int notFirst = hit != 0; int
  firstFlag = !notFirst;` get edg homes instead. `if (!hit || (...))` at the top and `if (hit) {...} else {...}` BEFORE
  the `hit = 1;` (moved after the inner if/else; 3FAC cannot touch the local) give uopt's CSE temps and the target spills

## kit CLIV (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 187): NCC never emits a 4-entry jump table (the run-186 8CD8 claim was wrong; kit CXL stands); gui 329C's second MAX pool temp is coloured early by PRIORITY, not by ucode order; block-scope cfe locals home BELOW the function-scope ones; negatives (250C8 fontId, 37938, 396FC) <a name="kit-cliv-agent-c-run-187"></a>

No exact, no source change. Docs only.

**1. Jump-table verdict: negative. NCC (edgcpfe 7.1) lowers every `switch` to a compare chain.** Kit CLII (run 186)
said the 8CD8 C++ port "does emit its 4-entry jumptable". It does not. The 2772-byte draft that kit described
(`/tmp/claude-1000/r186/F2.cpp`, `switch (s->i9C = (s->i9C + 1) & 3) { case 0: ... case 1: ... case 2: case 3: break; }`,
built with the project's NCC flags `-G 0 -non_shared -Wab,-r4300_mul -O2 -mips2 -32`) disassembles to:

    93c:  30420003  andi  v0,v0,0x3
    940:  1040000a  beqz  v0,96c
    944:  ae02009c  sw    v0,156(s0)
    948:  10410016  beq   v0,at,9a4      (at = 1)
    950:  24010002  li    at,2
    954:  1041001d  beq   v0,at,9cc
    958:  24010003  li    at,3
    95c:  5041001c  beql  v0,at,9d0

No `sltiu`, no `jr` through a register, no `.rodata` section in the object. None of the run-186 8CD8 drafts (X1, Y1-Y3,
E1, F1, F2, agg/p8 c_best) has a table. The target has `sltiu at,t8,4; beqz; sll; lui; addu; lw t9,256(at); jr t9`.
Minimal test (`/tmp/claude-1000/r187/sw.cpp` and the same body as C):

    struct S { char pad[0x9C]; int i; };
    void sw4(S *s) { switch (s->i = (s->i + 1) & 3) { case 0: f0(); break; case 1: f1(); break;
                                                      case 2: f2(); break; case 3: f3(); break; } }
    void sw8(int x) { switch (x) { case 0: ... case 7: ... } }   /* 8 dense labels */

NCC: sw4 = `beqz; beq 1; beq 2; beq 3`, sw8 = an 8-step `beq` chain (no table even for 8 dense labels). cfe: sw4 = the
same chain, sw8 = `sltiu at,a0,8; beqz; ...; jr t6` with a 32-byte .rodata table. So the run-186 sentence was a
misreading (most likely the TARGET's table was taken for ours in a side-by-side), and kit CXL's conclusion holds:
4-entry tables (gl 76F0, game_uso 0B3C / 8CD8, titproc 116C, kernel 1ADC) cannot be produced by any compiler in tools/.
Keep the phantom-5th-label shape. The kit CLII text is corrected in place.

**2. gui 329C: why the second MAX temp is v1 (target t2) -- zdbug evidence.** `-Wo,-zdbug:5` on the NM donor (parse the
`>>>active<<<{var|n} LR colour` / `forbidden:` / `- live bb -` blocks):
- The second pool variable is edg temp M-48 (var 320), which is ALSO the gSPTexture `dl->n++` postfix temp: one LR over
  BB0 and the rectangle BBs (14..32), colour 2 (v1), forbidden only [v0, s0]. With `next()` for the texture packet the
  MAX temp becomes a FRESH temp (M-56, first ucode appearance at the yh MAX), still v1, still forbidden [v0, s0].
- Its neighbours with LOWER ucode bit numbers (the t0 / a0 / a2 LRs of the rectangle's first block) are NOT in its
  forbidden set, so they were coloured after it: uopt colours this function in PRIORITY order (the dump just lists LRs by
  bit number). The pool temp carries the refs of four MAX/MIN results, so it ranks just after s0 / v0. The target's
  t2 means it was coloured after the v1, a0-a3, t0 and t1 neighbours, i.e. it has a lower priority there (more BBs
  or fewer refs per BB).
- Lead (not landed): turning `spr` into an edg temp, as the `this` of an inline `Spr::prep(s32 &w_, s32 &h_)` holding
  `w_ = w; h_ = h; switch (fmt) { case ...: CTX->load(tex, w_, h_); }`, does put the MAX temps in t2 (`move t2,zero`
  x3) and gives BB0 the target's shape (spr t2, switch value s0, w / h through their homes). But the gSPTexture
  `this` and the rectangle's CTX then share spr's variable (t2, target s0), and the frame loses a home: 78.78. Attempts
  to give spr the SECOND temp of its statement (`CTX->prep2(arg0->spr, ...)` with the switch inside a Ctx member,
  `arg0->getSpr()->prep()`, `CTX->dlp()->nextp()` for the texture packet) fail (67-78).
- Negatives (all flat 98.76 or worse): x / y / fw / fh declaration orders, `t` removed (98.72), inline `MAXf()`
  (+4 bytes), `MAX(yl, (s16)0)` (+4), MAX spelled `<` / `!` (95.61, -8 bytes) or with casts (flat), nextp() with a
  `long` / `unsigned` index, `DL::n` as `long` / `unsigned`, every nextp spelling (flat), pre-increment / re-read
  next() forms (87-92, +12..+48 bytes), `if (1) {}` at each of the nine statement points of the expanded rectangle
  macro (flat or worse; note: expanding the macro over several LINES changes as1 scheduling by two words -- keep it on

**3. cfe frame homes of block-scope locals.** In gl 250C8 (cfe) moving `u32 fontId` into a `case 1: { ... }` block

**4. Smaller negatives.**

## kit CLIII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 194): literal / `mtc1 zero` count scan over the whole range (what it does and does not find); 4F2DC cfe -> NCC V3 port (90.45 -> 94.87, length = target); stale `if (1) {}` in a re-shaped donor (23FC 99.62 -> 99.94); NCC home-placement probes (block-scope locals, inline temps, volatile / dead locals); negatives <a name="kit-cliii-agent-g-run-194"></a>

No exact. report.json: game_libs_func_0004F2DC 90.45 -> 94.87 (1064 B, length = target), mgrproc_uso_func_000023FC
99.62 -> 99.94 (1108 B), gl_func_0004C5E4 87.16 -> 87.22, gl_func_00054E78 91.28 -> 91.33, gl_func_0004D688 96.59 -> 96.65.
post0b NM .text unchanged (0x2eadc).

**1. The literal / `mtc1 zero` count scan (kit CLI), run over every function < 98 % in the agent-g range.**
Script (scratch): per function, `objdump -dr -M no-aliases --disassemble=FN` on expected/ and build/non_matching/,
drop every instruction followed by an R_MIPS line, then count `mtc1 zero`, `lui K`, `li K` (addiu/ori from zero),
`andi/slti/sltiu/xori K`. Read the result with these filters:
- `lui 0x0` / `lui 0x2` / `lui 0x4` surpluses on the TARGET side are baked USO address halves (the target has no
  relocs), not literals. Ignore them.
- A surplus `li K` on one side is often the compare constant duplicated into a branch-likely delay slot
  (76F0 `li 2` x10 vs x5 = the switch-3 v1 web: the target's false exits jump straight to the `!= 2` compare
  with `beqzl ..; li at,2`; 6126C `li 102` = the known `bnel` dispatch copy; 8FC8 `li 1..5` = loop shape).
  Check where the extra copies are before reading them as spellings.
- `sltiu 4` (target) vs `sltiu 5` (NM) = the open 4-entry-jumptable cap (76F0 x2, kernel 1ADC, titproc 116C).
- Real decode signals this run: timproc_b5 C310 (`li 1` x2 in the target: `if (x->0x3BC == 1)`, i.e.
  `li t0,1; bnel t0,t4` -- the NM's `x - 1 == 0` gives `addiu -1; bnezl`). The decode-correct `== 1` scores
  LOWER (95.83 -> 93.09; the mv / mv2 copy and the t-ring shift); lever-sweep and a 60-cell mv / ternary / copy
  grid found nothing better, so the NM keeps the wrong spelling. **Flag: C310's `- 1 == 0` is a known wrong
  decode kept for score.** C234 (target 0x93C..0x944 stored from a second zero `$f0`, 0x968 from the `$f16`
  zero): NCC ignores 0.0 / (f32)0 / chained / local-zero / pointer spellings (8 variants flat). 1594's
  `lui 0x8000` is the known no-reloc word. B75C's remaining `mtc1 zero` surplus is the A74 / A70 stores
  (0.0f there loses: 92.6 / 91.3 vs 93.3, as the kit CLI grid said).
- decode-scan.py on the same range: only A2-SPLIT rows can score; E68's (the target holds `&dims + 4` in s8 for
  the last loop's `h` re-read) is not reached by a `s32 *hp = &import_8001FFA0_h[1]` block pointer (90.81 vs
  93.35, +16 bytes toward the target but the coloring shifts).

**2. 4F2DC was C++ (kit CXLVI lead confirmed).** The target's copy chains are the edg by-value temporaries of
a plain V3 class: `d = dir` through `void operator=(V3 v)` (word copy 200 -> 180, then float stores 212..220),
`V3 end = start + d * far;` through by-value `operator*` / `operator+` (products -> 160, copies 180 -> 412, sum
-> 112 -> 132 -> 84), `start *= kvec` in place, and the scaled end point through the 3-float ctor (no temporary).
Two details mattered: the ray direction built member by member (`dir.x = ...; dir.y = ...; dir.z = 8.0f / K;`,
the ctor form computes z first), `start` member-copied (not ctor), and `if (1) {}` after `start *= kvec`
(lever-sweep bbsplit, 91.11 -> 94.78). `f32 hits[8][3]` (a `V3 hits[8]` with a user ctor emits `__vec_new`).
Rule of thumb: when a cfe body needs volatile pads and Tri3i copies to imitate copy chains through stack slots
the code never reads back, port it to NCC with by-value operators before grinding the frame.

**3. 23FC: a re-shaping can make an older `if (1) {}` harmful.** The run-184 `if (1) {}` after `flag = 0`
turned the next test's `FW(..0x14) & 1` into a v0 candidate (`lw v0; andi v0,v0,1`) after later member rewrites;
dropping it gives the target's t9 / t3 and the rest of that block's ring (99.62 -> 99.94). Re-test every
bbsplit / barrier when a donor changes shape. Left on 23FC (all other words match): the 0x798 image load in
v0 (target t0; uoptlist: inline `i` web assigned reg 1 = v0, target 7 = t0) and the n / x homes (target 84 / 76,
ours 104 / 100).

**4. NCC home placement (23FC probes, frame 288).** Measured with a `volatile`-one-variable-at-a-time map and
an exhaustive placement enumerator (compile every combination, read the `sw` offsets and the frame):
- function-scope named locals take homes top-down in declaration order (p770 140 ... sec 92);
- block-scope locals come after ALL function-scope homes, depth-first: a block's own locals, then its nested
  blocks in order; declaring at the assignment point without a new block puts the local with the enclosing
  block's own locals (n / x right after sec);
- an inline member's named local (`Img *i = img;`) takes a home in the nested-block sequence; the FIRST inline
  call on an object expression like `(Spr *)(arg0 + K)` takes two homes (object temporary + local), later calls
  in the same function one (the object temporary is pooled);
- dead locals (`d = 0;` never read), non-volatile live temporaries split out of an expression, and volatile pads
  all land at the BOTTOM (frame +8 / +16), not above the function-scope homes -- they cannot push the top layout
  down. Nested blocks for n / x + function-scope `Spr *` objects reproduce the target's relative layout
  (min -192, sec -196, n -204, x -212 from the frame top) but at frame 296 and 99.70; not kept.

**5. Lever-sweep pass (all levers) this run.** Hits kept: 4C5E4 (bbsplit after the 0x294 call, vscale[1] before
vscale[0]), 54E78 (m[3][1] before m[3][0], local matrix rows, length = target), 4D688 (`m24++` before the m3C
store, no call between), 4F2DC (see 2). No hits: 4A890, 50444, 63964, 65494, 4E424, 5A2C4, 1824, 2B7C, CEB4,
23FC (after the fix). Rejected: 6126C `D_00000000 = 1` moved past a call (+0.65), 54E78 m[3][2] moved up (+0.15
but 548 vs 552 = away from the target). titproc 116C: lever-sweep's in-tree probe fails to score (the unit
compiles by hand; not chased).

**6. Negatives (do not repeat).**
- 8FC8 NCC donor: `w->pos` zero triple as `x = y = z = 0.0`, field stores (0.0 / 0.0f), `= V3(0.0, ..)`,
  `set(0, 0, 0)`, pointer form, FF() stores: none gives the target's three fresh `mtc1 zero` (NCC folds them
  into the f20 zero; best 90.41 = base).
- mgrproc 1824 outer two-case switch: case order, `default: break;` (both places), unsigned selector, goto

## kit CLV (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 188): a jump-table target is cfe -- retire an NCC NM donor for it (38A28 77.17 -> 84.59); cfe never gives a register to a value that stays live across a jump-table switch; distinct format-string symbols keep each arm's `lui a0`; frame homes for 33094; negatives <a name="kit-clv-agent-c-run-188"></a>

build/src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_38A28_nm.cpp.o.

**1. A target with a jump table (`sltiu at,tN,K; ... lw tN,%lo(jtbl)(at); jr tN`) was compiled by cfe.**
NCC never emits one (kit CLIV; checked again here with 9 and 11 dense labels, with and without
`default:`). So an NCC NM donor for such a function cannot reach the target's dispatch shape. 38A28 had
one. Putting the cfe body back gave the 9-entry table and the target's arm layout at once.
To find these: `objdump -d expected/<unit>.o`, list every function that has a `jr` on a register other
than ra, and check that list against the NCC donors in the Makefile. In game_uso / gui / post / post0b
38A28 was the only donor on that list.
Decode fixes read from the target in the same pass: the 0x66 arm stores the looked-up RECORD pointer to
o->0x14 (`sw v0,36(sp)` in the call's delay slot, `lw v0,36(sp)`, `sw v0,20(s0)`), not the call's
return value; the arms `return`, and the report call after the switch takes (code, o->0xC);
`case 0x6C: return;` gives the table its 9th entry. A cfe `case X: break;` that shares the exit gets no
compare of its own, so you can't see the table's padding labels in the text. Only the table length
(`sltiu 9`) shows them.

**2. Distinct format strings are distinct symbols.** Each target arm has its own `lui a0,0x2; addiu a0,..`
(baked 0x1EC6C / 0x1EC84 / 0x1EC9C, no shared hi). Written as `&D_00000000 + 0x1EC6C`, cfe CSEs the
common %hi, and uopt hoists the default arm's `lui a0` into the switch head. One pinned symbol per string
keeps each lui in its own arm.

**3. cfe never colours a value that stays live across a jump-table switch** (uoptlist: `0: not colored,
not splittable`). A 6-line test shows it: `int code = *c; switch (code) {...} f(code);` homes `code` in
memory even when no arm makes a call. The target keeps it in v0 (and o in s0, NCC-style), so 38A28 keeps
an allocation residual: `code` gets a memory home, and o sits in a3 with spills around the calls. Neutral: `register`,
copy-local, IDO 5.3 cc, -O2 -g3, default inside vs after the switch, return vs break arms, unsigned key.

**4. 33094 frame homes.** The target frame is 144: b at sp+132, a at sp+120, and the copy temp t at
sp+84. Declaring `Vec3 b; Vec3 a;`, then six frame words, then `Vec3 t;` puts every home at the target's
offset. The entry copy runs z, y, x like the target's loads. Still open there: the target keeps a.y / a.z
in their entry registers (f0 / f2) through the else arm and reloads only a.x (f12 is taken by 10.0f). Our
a members are not coloured. Held block locals (`f32 ax = ...`) colour them for the WHOLE function instead
(380 bytes, 78.1). Inline reference-taking emit wrappers are neutral.

  inline `has()`, and an inline `both(F100 *, Flags *)` helper all fold the offsets and evaluate the `&&`

  matrix block are <= 79.22. Lever-sweep hits (`volatile float zero` 80.99, a bbsplit 80.03) both move the
  length AWAY (1024 -> 1036, target 1008).
- 2DE0 / 3714 / 329C / F04: lever-sweep all, no hit. 2DE0's switch-temp spellings (`arg0->spr->fmt`,
  named t, block-scoped `Ctx *c`) cost about 3 points. F04's `(s16)(x << 2)` as a named s32 / s16 block local

## kit CLVII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 189): gui sprite-rect family -- when the edg CTX pool temp gets s0 (it must be ASSIGNED in the loader-call blocks, i.e. be the `this` of an inline member that makes the call), why 3714's a1 is not that case, and per-packet append spellings in the rectangle macro (329C 98.85 -> 99.06, 3714 96.10 -> 96.43) <a name="kit-clvii-agent-c-run-189"></a>

No exact. Two NM gains (report.json, length = target): gui 329C 98.84615 -> 99.05595, gui 3714 96.10156 -> 96.43359.

**1. The s0 condition (minimal form, standalone NCC, verified on 2DE0 / 3714).** In all four gui sprite-rect bodies the
gfx context is read through `CTX` (`*(Ctx **)&D_00000000`) and edg pools every 4-byte `this` / MAX temporary into
one function-scope variable A (uopt var 0, an `M -68 vreg` home in the zdbug:5 dump). uopt gives A a callee-saved
register only when one live range of A spans the loader-call blocks, and that only happens when A is assigned INSIDE
those blocks:
- `gui_func_00000000(CTX, spr->tex, w, h, 0, 0, w, h, 0);` -- the argument reads the global straight into a0, A is
  not referenced in the case blocks, its live ranges stop before the switch: A = t0 / t2 (2DE0 / 3714 bodies).
- `struct Ctx { ... void load(int t, s32 w, s32 h) { gui_func_00000000(this, t, w, h, 0, 0, w, h, 0); } };` +
  `CTX->load(spr->tex, w, h);` -- the inline's `this` is A, assigned in each case block (the target's
  `b join; lw s0, 0(t3)` default-arm delay slot), one live range over the switch: A = s0 and the switch value
  shares it. Applied to 2DE0 this reproduces the target's s0 everywhere (head, switch, rect, first MAX temp) and,
  with the texture append spelled `n + 1` and the rectangle's `n = dl->n; dl->n++`, the whole head and switch
  match (96.42 standalone) -- but the body is 1196 bytes (base 1208, target 1212): the rectangle's RDPHALF_2 append
  re-reads `&D_00000000` as `lui s0; lw s0, %lo(s0)` instead of keeping the target's t3 (the target re-materialises
  `lui t3 / addiu t3` in four branch arms of the RDPHALF_1 MIN/MAX tree). Every append-spelling combination with
  load() inline stays at 1196-1204 (`n++` everywhere: 1216, 92.23), so it is NOT landed (length away).
- 3714's target A is **a1, not s0**: A is reloaded after the call (`lw a1, 0(t4)`), so it never spans the call
  and `CTX->load()` is wrong there (gives s0, frame +8, length 1032). In the dump A (var 0, priority 2.625, 11 BBs)
  is coloured t2 with forbidden [v0 .. t1]: a1 is taken by the MAX expression value it is copied from (var 1277,
  `ugeq {1277} 0` -> `ustr {0} {1277}`), which the target puts in a0. So 3714 is a colour-order cap between A and
  the MAX value, not a call-crossing one. Neither a struct-by-value (x, y) parameter, a `volatile` param, `fl(const
  s32 &)` nor an `if (1) {}` after gSPTexture moves A off t2 (params are homed at entry either way; a1-a3 forbidden).

**2. Per-packet append spellings (the landed gain).** The stock gbi.h gSPScisTextureRectangle evaluates `pkt` three
times (rect, RDPHALF_1, RDPHALF_2). Giving the macro three packet arguments (`pkt, pkt2, pkt3`) and gridding the
three Ctx append spellings independently (`n = dl->n++` / `n = dl->n; dl->n = n + 1` / `n = dl->n; dl->n++`, 81
combinations with the texture append) picks the same pattern in both functions: RDPHALF_1 as `n = dl->n; dl->n++`,
RDPHALF_2 as `n = dl->n++`. In 329C the second MAX temp's zero then schedules at the join exactly where the target

one step. 2DE0 (no load inline): best 96.94 but 1204 bytes (base 1208): away, not landed.

Negatives: 2DE0 declaration-order x pad-count grid with load() inline (5! x 3, flat 96.42, length 1196); 2DE0 `t =
spr->fmt` / `arg0->spr->fmt` (329C recipe) 88.9-89.0 (1200); 329C Spr::prep / Obj::prep / free prep(Spr *) /
`prep(int f, ...)` (72-79); 3714 bbsplit sweep (no hit).

scratch lever-sweep subcommands: `declmove` (move one declaration of the first declaration block to every
other slot) and `hoist` (move a mid-body C++ declaration to the top / bottom of the function's declaration
block; an initialiser becomes an assignment at the old spot). The big one was by hand first:

## kit CLVIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 190): gui sprite-rect family -- the per-packet append grid (kit CLVII section 2) generalises: F04 97.44 -> 98.59 and 2DE0 94.59 -> 95.53 with the length reaching the target; why the 2DE0 load() variant loses the target's four-arm `lui/addiu t3` &D rebuilds; 7C1C / 3558 / BB8C negatives <a name="kit-clviii-agent-c-run-190"></a>

No exact. Two NM gains (report.json): gui F04 97.44409 -> 98.58786 (length 1252 = target), gui 2DE0 94.59076 ->
95.52805 (length 1208 -> 1212 = target).

**1. Per-packet append spellings, applied to F04 and 2DE0.** Give gSPScisTextureRectangle three packet arguments
(`pkt` for the rect words, `pkt2` for RDPHALF_1, `pkt3` for RDPHALF_2), write each append as a separate inline Ctx
member, and grid the texture append plus the three rectangle appends independently. Nine spellings are worth
including (all return `&buf[old n]` and store `old n + 1`): `n = dl->n++`; `n = dl->n; dl->n++`;
`n = dl->n; dl->n = n + 1`; `n = dl->n; dl->n += 1`; `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`; and the same through a local
`DL *d = dl` (`d->n = n + 1` / `n = d->n++` / `&d->buf[d->n++]`). Each one changes the ugen temp order of that
append, and the effect reaches the MAX / MIN tree after it.
- F04 (4^4 grid): texture `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`, rect `n = dl->n; dl->n++`, RDPHALF_1 `n = dl->n; dl->n = n + 1`,
  RDPHALF_2 `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`: 97.25 -> 98.51 standalone. The run-173 one-packet donor had the rectangle's
  slot as `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`. Left: the rect append's dl in a0 (target v0), the second MAX temp in v1 (target
  a0), and one spill slot 4 bytes low (120 vs 124: the `y & 0xffff` CSE held across the glyph-index call). A
  7! declaration-order grid and the 9-spelling 9^4 grid are both flat.
- 2DE0 (exhaustive 9^4 grid, direct loader calls, 10 pads): texture / rect / RDPHALF_2 `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`,
  RDPHALF_1 `n = dl->n; dl->n += 1` (the `+=` spelling: `n + 1` gives a different length) is the only
  spelling family at length 1212 above 95: 95.43 standalone. Only 30 of 6561 combinations reach 1212, and most
  of the grid sits at 1180-1192. Higher scores are all shorter (96.94 at 1204), so they are not landed.
- The same grid with `CTX->load()` inline in the three arms (kit CLVII, s0 as in the target) gives 251
  combinations at 1212, best 95.05 (texture / rect / RDPHALF_2 `&dl->buf[dl->n++]`, RDPHALF_1 `n + 1`): s0, the
  switch and the arm loads all match, but &D is in t2 (target t3) and the w / h homes are swapped (56 / 60). A
  7! x 2 declaration-order x pad grid peaks at 95.10. So the load() form gets the target's registers but loses
  on everything else. The direct-call form is landed.
- No gain from the 9-spelling grid on 329C (99.06, 4096 combinations), 3714 (96.43, 4096) or 4568 (96.01, five
  spellings over its six packets).

**2. Why 2DE0 + load() loses the four-arm `lui/addiu t3` rebuild (zdbug:5).** &D (`&D_00000000`) is a `const`
live range coloured t3 in both forms, and uopt splits it. Without load() (base donor) the coloured piece covers
the head, the switch and the whole RDPHALF_1 tree up to the RDPHALF_2 append (blocks 29-38, 40-42, 45, 46). Only
the case arms after each call (blocks 5 / 7 / 9) and the two yl < 0 MAX arms (39 / 43) split off, uncoloured,
`needreglod`. That is exactly the target's `lui t3; addiu t3` after each loader jal and in the y arms. With
load(), `this` is the pool variable A (s0, forbidden for &D) and the coloured piece stops at block 28. Everything
from the y tree to the end (blocks 29-46) becomes ONE uncoloured split piece, so the final RDPHALF_2 append
folds to `lui s0; lw s0, %lo(D)(s0)` and the y-arm rebuilds disappear (-16 bytes). Reaching the target needs A
in s0 and the &D piece still running to block 46, and no append-spelling combination gives both (part 1).

**3. Negatives.**
- 7C1C: the target loads the stack argument `out` straight into s0 (`lw s0, 964(sp)`, used only for the
  `*out = 0` store), then reuses s0 for the ctor-protocol pool `this`. That suggests `out` was copied into the
  pooled edg temporary (one uopt variable over both uses). None of these spellings does it: `clr(out)` /
  `clr(float *&)` inlines, placement `new (out) float(0.0f)` (null-checked: +4 bytes), `((Flt *)out)->clear()`,
  `(*(Flt **)&out)->clear()`, `((Flt *)(out + 0))->clear()`. edg passes `out` directly in each case, so `out`
  stays in v0 / t6 (95.12 flat or lower). lever-sweep all: no hit.
- 3558 (target holds 0.0f in f20 across four calls: side.x / side.z / w.y and the else-arm `w *= 0` muls): a
  reused variable (`zero` reassigned as the final k), `zero = 0.0f` after the first call, `const float &`
  Vec3 ctor / operator*= params with `Vec3 side(0.0f, k, 0.0f)` / `side(zero, k, zero)`, and `w *= zero` /
  `0.0f` / `0.0`: still one mtc1 per site (the 0.0 constant becomes 4 block-local const LRs, never one
  call-spanning LR). Spellings that score higher are 1036 bytes (away). lever-sweep: the hits (volatile zero

- Tooling note: spelling-grid probe directories are named by the source hash, so duplicate alternatives (the
  same text twice in one marker) race on makedirs / rmtree under parallel jobs (FileExistsError /
  "could not open source file"). Keep the alternatives in each marker distinct. A literal `}` right before
  `@|` or `}@` closes the marker early (write `} @|`).

only after uopt has chosen its candidates. So that store materialises its own zero instead of joining the
function's shared 0.0 constant candidate, which shortens or splits that candidate's live range. A quick sweep
is cheap: wrap every `X = 0.0f;` statement in a donor as `@{X = 0.0f; @|zf(X, 0);}@` and run spelling-grid.
- game_uso BB8C (NCC): the probe direction's `q.dir.x / q.dir.y` zeros through zf. In the target they use their

  (length 1116 = target).
- Flat or away: 7C1C (`*out`, `result.y`), 36694, 36F0C (+0.9 but 976 vs 968, away), 3B2EC, 3C43C, 27804.

## kit CLX (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 191): cfe stack arguments evaluated into locals before a many-argument call (post0b 469A8 74.77 -> 90.45); zf / declmove / hoist sweep over agent-c's range (small hits only); 1DDC / 97EC / 40304 / 2D374 / 307A8 / 250C8 / 38A28 negatives <a name="kit-clx-agent-c-run-191"></a>

78.61649 -> 78.71684, post0b 36F0C 93.28513 -> 93.30991, game_uso 3558 79.21825 -> 79.23016, post0b 38A28 84.59259 ->
84.61729.

**1. Stack arguments read into locals first (469A8).** The target's 12-argument call loads the five memory stack
arguments into t1-t4 and `ra` (`lw t5,0x148(v1); lw t1,0xc0(v1); lw t2,0xc4(v1); lw t3,0xb8(v1); lw t4,0xbc(v1);
lw ra,0xb8(t5)`) and only then stores them (`sw t1,0x18(sp)` .. `sw ra,0x28(sp)`). cfe evaluates and stores
each argument in turn when the argument is written in the call, so the loads and stores alternate. Reading the
arguments into block locals first, then passing the locals, gives the target's load-then-store shape:

    { s32 a6 = FW(o, 0xC0), a7 = FW(o, 0xC4), a8 = FW(o, 0xB8), a9 = FW(o, 0xBC), a10 = FW(FW(o, 0x148), 0xB8);
      f(s1, s0, st, m4, t0, pDC, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10, FW(o, 0x1B0)); }

This is what cfront's inline-argument temporaries produce. The last argument (0x1B0) stays in the call: the target
loads it just before the jal (in the delay slot). Writing it as a local too scores lower (88.28 vs 90.05).
The same commit puts the `&D + 0x254` store before the object's 0x158 field store (the target's order). 74.46 -> 90.06
standalone. Frame: the target is 0x58 vs our 0x50, with three homes at 0x4c..0x57. Two unused `volatile s32` pads
declared before the volatile sp48 home give 0x58 and sp48 at 72 (90.39 -> 90.45). The target keeps `v1 + 0x100` / `v1 + 0x78`
in registers (a2 / t1, which suggests real pointer variables with homes). cfe folds them into 0x104(v1) / 0x78(v1)
in every spelling tried (`int *` / `&FW()` / casts, function or block scope). Other leftovers: the early
`or a1,s0,zero` and the held `lui v1; addiu v1` &D base.
Scan for more cases: compare the longest run of consecutive outgoing-argument stores (`sw rX,16..60(sp)`) in the
target against the NM build. In agent-c's range only 469A8 had a longer run in the target (38A28's run is a spill,
a false positive).

**2. Sweeps (zf, declmove, hoist) over every NM body / donor in agent-c's range.**
- zf (`X = 0.0f;` -> `zf(X, 0)`, and each `0.0f` literal -> `0`, one site at a time; scratch script over
