## kit CLXII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 192): deep session on gl_func_0002E354 (91.55 -> 93.29) and gl_func_00030AF4 (92.52, no gain) -- full region maps; UNNAMED FIELD EXPRESSIONS beat m2c's named copies (uopt keeps a plain `o->f` load in one register across a region and re-loads it only where a store kills it); selector-and-result in ONE variable; u32 selector holds a shared compare constant; 30AF4 negatives <a name="kit-clxii-agent-c-run-192"></a>

Both functions are cfe NM bodies in `game_libs_post.c` (jump tables). Region maps were made with a small
basic-block classifier over `scripts/rdiff.py`'s disassembly (raw branch offsets + pins): the TARGET is split
at every branch / branch target, each block is aligned to ours on the register- and sp-normalised stream, and
classed **M** (raw-identical), **S** (only sp offsets differ: frame 0xA0 vs 0x80 in 2E354), **R**
(register names only), **X** (shape: unaligned / missing / extra words).

### 1. The lever: un-name single field reads (2E354, five hits)

m2c gives every field read a temp (`temp_v1_2 = o->0x1D; if (o->0x34 != temp_v1_2) ... if (temp_v1_2 == 1)`).
When the target re-uses one register for the read across several statements and *reloads it only after a
store or call that kills it*, the original source simply repeated the expression `o->0x1D`: uopt's
redundancy elimination keeps the load in a register on the store-free path and re-materialises it (fresh
`lbu`) in the arms that stored. A named copy instead becomes a candidate of its own: an extra `or aX,aY,zero`,
a different colour, and sometimes a lost delay-slot fill.

| site in 2E354 | change | fuzzy | length (target 921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| o->0x0 / o->0x4 product + 0x32 block | product of plain reads, spelled `o4 * o0` (cfe swaps it to the target's `lwc1 f2,0; lwc1 f14,4`); in-block `o->4 = o->4 * f` | 91.99 -> 92.11 -> 92.15 | 923 -> 922 |
| o->0x50 average | plain reads, `(o0 + o50) * 0.5` (target `add.s f10,f16,f2`) | -> 92.16 | 922 |
| o->0x1D compare / == 1 / default-arm store | plain reads | -> 92.99 | 922 -> **921** |
| o->0x26 (u8 -> float) + switch-2 selector o->0x21 | plain reads | -> 92.996 (rdiff rows 500 -> 377) | 921 |
| odd-case selector o->0x29 | plain read | -> 93.007 | 921 |

Not every named read is a copy: un-naming o->0x15, o->0x22, o->0x2E, the switch-1 selector o->0x21 and the
race-block `temp_f16 = o->0` all LOWERED fuzzy (those reads really are single register values the target
keeps). Test each site; keep only the risers.

### 2. Selector and result in one variable (2E354 pan pick, 93.007 -> 93.289)

Target: `lbu v0,46(s0); li at,1; bne v0,at,A; ...; b J; li v0,127 / A: li at,3; bnel v0,at,J; li v0,64;
b J; move v0,zero; li v0,64(dead) / J:`. The selector is loaded straight into the RESULT register. Source:
`v = o->0x2E; if (v == 1) v = 0x7F; else if (v == 3) v = 0; else v = 0x40;` -- word-for-word. (The previous
`t = o->0x2E; if (t == 1) v = 0x7F; else { v = 0x40; if (t == 3) v = 0; }` was two words short here.)
FLAG: function length 921 -> 923 (the short spelling had been hiding surplus words elsewhere).

### 3. u32 selector holds a shared compare constant (2E354 raceB, +0.24)

`(v == 4 || v == 10) && (v != 4 || o->0x21 != 2)`: the target materialises 4 once (`li v1,4; beq v1,v0 /
bne v1,v0`). With `s32 v` the 4 joins the function-wide signed-4 constant web and is rematerialised into `at`
at each test; `u32 v` gives it its own web -> held register. (Operand spelling `4 == v` changes nothing.)
FLAG: 922 -> 923 words at the time. The same trick on 30AF4's case-5 `c14` (u32) holds 14 in a0 as in the
target but not 13, and costs -0.18 -- not kept.

### 4. Smaller 2E354 items

- the 1C73C easing result reuses `temp_f0` (target `add.s f0,f6,f0`): +0.03.
- `if (1) {}` after the 1C738 ratio division (lever-sweep bbsplit hit): +0.16.
- negatives: one `D_E354_1C738` / `1C73C` symbol instead of six per-site externs (-1.15, the per-site
  `lui at,2` lever of run 109 still stands); `static` instead of extern for them (no change at all);
  split base symbol for the G+0x14 countdown (-0.6: holds the wrong one of the two bases); a
  multi-role `temp_f16 = 0.5f` clamp variable (identical code); o->0x15 chain as a switch / else-if chain
  (closer shape, -0.9 / -0.3); `(unsigned)o->0x14 + 2` in the switch-6 default arm (that block becomes
  word-exact and length 923 -> 922, but -0.16); `sp78 = sum; sp78 = sp78 * sp64` (reproduces the target's
  two `swc1 ...,120(sp)` but reorders the u32 conversion, 87.4); `volatile f32 sp78` (+0.05 but 921 -> 922,
  not kept).

### 5. Region maps after this run

**gl_func_00030AF4** (533 vs 528 words; M 215 / R 182 / X 131; unchanged this run):

              target once; target hoists &gl_state (lui/addiu v0) above the switch, ours sinks it into case 6

30AF4 diagnosis: the target uses ZERO s-registers, homes a0/a1/a2, keeps flag / prev / w in stack slots and
re-loads params once per region (CSE inside a block). Ours gets the zero-s-reg shape only through the
`volatile modeSel`, which also makes every param-home read uncacheable (the double `lw 60(sp)` in case 4,
the double `lw 56(sp)` at 0xb0). Negatives: kit 63964 K&R-int reinterpret-cast params (`#define mode
(*(u32 *)&mode_)`) for mode+sub 90.48 / mode only 91.79 (a2 still unhomed); IDO 7.1 -O1 standalone 61.0
(not -O1); dropping the `if (1) {}` after `modeSel = mode` 91.87; `(void)&param` statements fold away;
u32 c / c13 / c14 (see 3); `D_h = sv = sub`; un-named `*cp` reads (identical); lever-sweep all + declmove:
0 hits. `gb = ...; modeSel = mode;` without the `if (1) {}` gives the target's single `lw 56(sp)` with the
modeSel store in the beqz delay slot, but the jump-table index lands in t9 where the target uses a FRESH t0
(and every later t-reg is one behind the target's rotation, 91.87); `switch (modeSel)` on the volatile copy
92.42. The same one-ahead t-reg rotation is the 2E354 0x3e8 residual: find the extra integer temp the
target spends before the region and the whole tail re-colours.

## kit CLXIV (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 193): COMPUTE-ORDER DECODE in NCC donors -- the target reads every operand of a group of independent computations before the first store / before the second group (454C4 colour products before the Light byte stores 91.71 -> 95.72; collision-edge loop dx / dy before ex / ey in the 3BE1C / 3B9C0 / 3B2EC triangle-test family 88.64 -> 94.98, 78.72 -> 86.91, 95.62 -> 96.05); region maps of 591C / 7C1C / post0b donors; 591C tail / switch negatives <a name="kit-clxiv-agent-c-run-193"></a>

Region maps were made with a small basic-block classifier over `scripts/rdiff.py --raw --pins` (target split at
every branch and branch target, each block aligned to ours on the register- and sp-normalised stream, classed
**M** raw-identical, **S** sp offsets only, **R** register names only, **X** shape: unaligned / missing / extra).

### 1. The lever: statement order of independent computations = load order

IDO keeps the source order of independent loads unless a store in between could alias them. Two cases in
agent-c's range where the m2c / earlier body wrote the groups in the wrong order:

- **Loads before stores (454C4 light loop).** Target: all six colour operands (`s[0..2]`, `e->col[0..2]`) are
  loaded before the first `sb` into the Light record. The body wrote
  `cv = (s32)(s[i] * e->col[i] * 255.0f); l->col[i] = cv; l->colc[i] = cv;` per component, and the byte stores
  (which may alias the float loads) pinned each next component's loads behind them. Fix: three products
  first (`s32 c0 = ..; c1 = ..; c2 = ..;`), then the six stores (`colc[0]` first, as the target's schedule),
  plus the bb split after `dir[0]`. 91.71 -> 95.72; 2032 -> 2020 bytes (target 2028): the old order had been
  hiding three surplus words; what is left is the hoisted 0x03000000 gSPLight constant (s5, target `lui at`
  per site), 255.0f in fs1 (target f0, rematerialised after the loop's call) and its sdc1 / ldc1. FLAGGED:
  length moved past the target.
- **Operand group order (triangle edge test).** Target edge loop: `lh v0[a]; lh v0[b]; cvt; cvt;` then the v1
  reads -- i.e. `dx = (int)(qa - v0[a]); dy = (int)(qb - v0[b]);` are evaluated BEFORE
  `ex = v1[a] - v0[a]; ey = v1[b] - v0[b];` (no stores in the loop, so this is pure source order). With dx / dy
  first the whole 3BE1C loop block aligns word-for-word (X 30 -> 13 words): 88.64 -> 94.98, 1560 -> 1552 bytes
  (target 1568; FLAGGED: the remaining deficit is the face-pointer / r copies and the two-arm inner MAX). The
  same order in the twins: 3B9C0 78.72 -> 86.91 (1116 -> 1104, FLAGGED; the rest is the f24 save and the
  spilled loop offset), 3B2EC 95.62 -> 96.05 (length unchanged). Found by a permutation marker
  (`@[ex = ..@;ey = ..@;dx = ..@;dz = ..]@` with split declarations) in `scripts/spelling-grid.py`;
  `lever-sweep.py order` did not propose it (it skips initialised declarations).

Smaller order fixes, same idea: 42938 `G.m228 = G.m224 = 8` (target stores 0x228 first) and the rectangle read
`x, w, h, y` (97.39 -> 97.43), setvp constant stores `vtrans[3], vscale[2], vscale[3], vtrans[2]` (-> 97.44);
3B9C0 zero vector `zf(d.x, 0); zf(d.z, 0);` (target stores x then z; the run-190 z-first spelling scored but
was the wrong order) 78.72; 46050 texrect w1 `((0x220 * 4) & 0xFFF) | (((0x21C * 4) & 0xFFF) << 12)` (target
loads 0x220 first) 89.68 -> 89.71.

How to find more: count insert/delete rows that are loads in the noreg/nosp diff
(`rdiff.py --raw --pins --noreg --nosp | grep -A20 '^--- \(insert\|delete\)' | grep -cE '^  [<>] (lwc1|lw|lh|lhu|lb|lbu) '`).
Agent-c's range after this run: 8CD8 41, 3558 22, 37540 20, 46050 15, 3B9C0 15, 7C1C 15, 591C 12, 3B6A0 11,
38A28 11, 36694 11, 469A8 10. A generic permutation sweep over every block of 2-5 independent assignments
in all 31 NCC donors of the range found nothing beyond the fixes above (each needs splitting a compute
from its store, or a declaration from its initialiser, first).

### 2. Region maps (start of run)

- **game_uso_func_0000591C** (cfe NM, 1095 vs 1093 words; M 711 / S 7 / R 195 / X 180): head 0x0-0x80 M;
  0x80-0x158 X = the scaled-axis products (target f14 / f2 / f0 for x / y / z, ours f14 / f0 / f2; no statement
  order or temp-name choice of x / y / z or the pool floats reproduces it: register-only); 0x178-0x2b4 R / X =
  first switch (target keeps the selector COPY `or v0,v1` in both dispatches and a `b J; or v0,v1` join block
  on every case-0 exit, ours coalesces the copy -- `v0 = vsel; switch (v0)`, `switch (v0 = vsel)`, a
  `= vsel` 0x74 store are all identical code); 0x2b4-0x404 transform dispatch / dead-sentinel alloc
  (R + delay-slot shape); 0x418-0x470 accel block (target `addiu v0,a0,1784` + `lwc1 16(v0)`, ours folds
  1800(a0); `p = sub; p += 1784/4` changes nothing); 0x4a0-0xcdc case-0 body: 13 `goto tail_common` /
  if-exit branches -- target branches to the case-0 `b J` block (`b Lce8; lw v0,44(s0)`), ours threads them
  to the join and fills each delay with the join's `lw v0,44(s0)` (one extra word per site, every later

- **game_uso_func_00007C1C** (NCC donor, 1071 = 1071; M 438 / S 238 / R 311 / X 84): S = edg temporary homes
  (deferred temporaries listed in reverse creation order); the X islands are XZ(const Vec3 &) ctor operand
  folding (target `lwc1 56(v0); lwc1 48(v0); ... addiu v0,v0,48` after the loads, ours advances the pointer
  first) and by-value copy pairs `lw/sw` interleave vs `lw lw sw sw`; the rest is the t-register ring.
- **gl_func_000454C4** (NCC, 508 vs 507): prologue X (extra fs1 save), loop X (fixed above), constant hoists.
- **gl_func_00046050** (NCC, 460 vs 462; M 311 / R 121 / X 30): the margin pointer: target holds `&D` in s8
  (lui / addiu before the loop, `lw t6,0(s8)` at both uses), ours holds 0xE4000000 in s8 and folds the margin
  load to `lui; lw 0(t6)` -- `register`, `const`, reference, assignment after the header, all 0xE4000000
  spellings: no change (uopt constant-candidate priority).
- **gl_func_0003BE1C** (NCC, 390 vs 392; X 0x21c-0x350, 0x43c-0x568): MAX block shape + edge loop (fixed).
- **game_libs_func_00042938** (NCC, 389 = 389; M 286 / R 96 / X 5): 5 schedule pairs (3 fixed), rest colours.
- **gl_func_0003B9C0** (NCC, 279 = 279; M 86 / S 23 / R 83 / X 87): target saves f20 / f22 / f24 (n->z held
  in f20 across the dn test and the t computation), loop offset spilled at sp+128 while its register is reused
  for the recomputed i*12; edge loop fixed above.

### 3. Negatives

- 591C: `0.0f` instead of `(f32)0.0` in the yaw absolute value gives the target's single `mtc1 zero,f16`
  (function-wide mtc1-zero count 19 -> 18 = target) but re-colours the FP web (M 711 -> 613), 94.78 -> 94.70:
  not kept. Tail selector read through `unsigned` / `short` / `volatile` / `void *` at the tail breaks the
  join's load reuse but deletes the case-0 `b J` block (1087 words, 86.6); the same type change on the
  0x10000 arm's selector read scores 95.31 but at 1096 words (away from 1093): not kept. `tail_common: break`
  -> fallthrough into `case 1` (86.9), `if (1) {}` before the break (90.2), `break` instead of the gotos, a
  `do { } while (0)` wrapper, `case 1: default:` with the selector load in each arm: identical or worse.
  Volatile `out_flags` 81.1.
- 3B9C0 rewritten in the 3BE1C member-function style (Obj::cast, Col::face, p as f32[3]): 70.7 at +24 bytes.
- 3B9C0 order sweep of the zero stores: only x-then-z both matches the target and scores.

Addendum (same run): **3B6A0** (`Obj::below`, the fourth member of the triangle-test family) takes the same
order: `px = (int)(qa - v[a]); py = (int)(qb - v[b]); ex = w[a] - v[a]; ey = w[b] - v[b];` read straight
from v[] (the named `int ax = v[a], ay = v[b]` copies of runs 160 / 179 hide the order: every permutation of
the four statements scores the same while they exist), `a` named again for `qa = pt[a]`: edge loop

## kit CLXVI (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 194): POST-INCREMENT POINTER COPY -- `v = tbl[*tp++]` copies tp into a second register (`or a3,a2,zero`) where the target loads through tp and steps it in place (3B6A0 87.65 -> 90.12, 820 -> 800 bytes = target; 3B9C0 edge loop word-for-word); pointer arithmetic HOISTED ABOVE AN EARLY `continue` (3B9C0 88.42 -> 91.18); face() on the member pointer (3BE1C 94.98 -> 95.45); lever-sweep re-runs (3B6A0 -> 93.65, 454C4 -> 95.94, BB8C -> 98.50); 591C tail-reload diagnosis; negatives <a name="kit-clxvi-agent-c-run-194"></a>

### 1. Post-increment in an index expression = an extra register copy

`s16 *w = verts[f->vi[*tp++]];` (3B6A0) / `v1 = vt[f->vi[*nx++]];` (3B9C0): edg evaluates the post-increment as
`tmp = tp; tp = tmp + 1; ... *tmp`, and uopt keeps both values live, so ours has `or a3,a2,zero; lh t7,0(a3);
addiu a2,a2,2` where the target has `lh t7,0(a2); addiu a2,a2,2`. Fix: read `*tp` and step the pointer as its own
operation -- `++tp` in the loop test (`while (inside && (fp++, ++tp != tbl + 3))`, 3B6A0) or a separate `nx++;`
right after the read (3B9C0; the test-side `++nx` scored lower there). Same semantics: the old step only differed
on the exit path, where tp is dead. 3B6A0 87.65 -> 90.12 and 820 -> 800 bytes (= target, the run-193 overshoot was
this copy); 3B9C0 86.91 -> 88.42 with the edge-loop block now word-for-word up to register names
(ours[158:214] = target[161:217] under `rdiff --noreg --nosp`), length 1104 -> 1100 (target 1116; FLAGGED, the
copy word was one of ours). How to spot: an `or rX,rY,zero` in ours right before a load through rX, with an
`addiu rY,rY,k` next to it. 3BE1C already had the split form (run 178); 3B2EC / 3BE1C `*list++` in the outer
`while ((i = *list++) != -1)` must stay (splitting it: 93.0 / 93.3).

### 2. Re-sweep after a decode fix, and NCC line layout

After the ++tp fix `lever-sweep.py all` on 3B6A0 found a bb split after `verts = c->verts` and de-naming qa / qb
(read `pt[a]` / `pt[b]` in the loop): 90.12 -> 93.65. The `if (1) {}` had to stay ON THE SAME SOURCE LINE as the
statement: on its own line the same code scored 92.77 (NCC donors are line-layout sensitive; keep sweep hits
exactly as the tool rendered them). 454C4: bb split after `n++` in the light loop 95.72 -> 95.94 (any split in that
loop gave the same 95.903 standalone). A sweep of all 22 other NCC donors in agent-c's range found only BB8C
(`if (1) {}` after `f24 *= obj->sub->k`, 98.33 -> 98.50); volatile hits on 36694 / 3558 move length away.

### 3. Pointer arithmetic above an early `continue`

3B9C0's loop: target `lw t7,84(s5)` (col->nrm) and `addu v0,t7,a1` BEFORE `bltzl t9` (the `grp < 0` continue),
with `addiu s3,s3,1` (i++) in the bltzl delay slot. Moving `n = (V3 *)((char *)self->col->nrm + off);` above the
`if (grp < 0) continue;` (a pure load + add, no store or call in between): 88.42 -> 91.18. The 3B2EC / 3BE1C
analogues (verts / face before the test) are worse (94.4 / -).

### 4. Member pointer vs cached copy (3BE1C)

`Face *f = col->face(i); cc = col;` (face on the member, the cached cc assigned after) instead of
`cc = col; Face *f = cc->face(i + 0);`: 94.98 -> 95.45, 1552 -> 1556 (toward 1568). The `this` copy (`or v0,v1`)
now appears, but in v1 where the target uses s1 (cc); `(cc = col)->face(i)` loses the copy again.

### 5. 591C tail reload (diagnosis)

Target: all 13 case-0 exits of the second switch (gotos + if-exits) branch to `b J; lw v0,44(s0)` and the case-1 /
default dispatch to J with the load in the delay slot, i.e. EVERY path reloads `self->0x2C` before the common
tail. Ours CSEs the proximity block's `v0 = self->0x2C` into the tail on the fall-through path (`bc1f J+4`, the
`out_flags |= 0x80` arm ends `b J+4; sw t5,436(sp)` without a reload), which is why the case-0 jump block
disappears and the gotos are threaded. Something in the original kills that availability on the last path only.
Tried: `out_flags` address-taken (`int out_flags[1]` or `{ int *ofp = &out_flags; }`) reloads it but kills five
other CSEs (94.79 -> 83.02); `(void)&out_flags`, a `v0 = self->0x2C` at tail_common, `tail_common:` moved out of
the switch: identical code.

### 6. Negatives

- 3B2EC: the 3B6A0-style table / face-word pointer walk instead of the `k` loop: 96.05 -> 94.57 in tree and
  948 -> 940 bytes (the k loop is already 0.92 shape-aligned).
- 3B9C0: loop count cached in a local `ntri` 83.67 (the target keeps it in a0 and reloads only after the stores).
- 3B6A0: `Col::face()` member spellings, volatile pads for the 128-byte frame: flat.
- 3BE1C: face() spellings (6), r type (int / u32 / u16 / const / volatile), ok declaration position: flat.
- 3558: the three matrix-row statements in all 6 orders x 6 store orders: flat; `Vec3 r(...)` / `stage = Vec3(...)`
  / per-component `vb.x += ..`: 55.9 - 59.4.
- 33094: `a` loaded into block locals before the stores (the CLXIV lever): 78.1 (-24 bytes).
- 36694: product operand order (`p.x * n.x`): +0.1 only; 36F0C declaration permutations (120): flat;
  46790 `put()` increment spellings: 75.3.
- 8CD8 as an NCC donor with the 7C1C classes (XZ temporaries, by-value operator=, `XZ - Vec3` through the return
  slot; first draft): 77.26 standalone vs the cfe body's 84.24, 2876 bytes (target 2836) -- the shape is right
  (guards, copy chains) but the first copy chain has one extra binding copy and the guard calls spill differently;
  a multi-run project, not kept.

Load-order rows (`rdiff --raw --pins --noreg --nosp`, insert / delete blocks only) at the end of the run: 8CD8 23,
37540 14, 7C1C 13, 46050 12, 3B9C0 11, 38A28 6, 591C 6, 36694 4, 3558 4.

## kit CLXI (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 197): timer-HUD 13B8 / 16F4 EXACT -- edg pool-temp order set by a folded `0 * inline()` term; zdbug reading of pooled temporaries <a name="kit-clxi-agent-g-run-197"></a>

EXACT: timproc_uso_b3_func_000013B8 (680 B) and arcproc_uso_func_000016F4 (680 B), 99.91 -> 100. Code 82.62 -> 82.79 %.
No pins. Donors renamed `_nm.cpp` -> `.cpp` and spliced into both trees (16F4's calls rebound to `gl_func_00000000`:
the arcproc ROM holds `jal 0`; the NM-only `arcproc_uso_func_00001B88` binding gave 12 wrong jal words).

**1. Reading pooled temporaries in zdbug:5.** edg turns every inline `this` copy and every inline result that is an
operand of a later inline call into a function-scope pool variable. Homes are top-down in edg CREATION order
(`isvar M 4 -N`), but the itab bit (= the colouring tie-break) is the order of FIRST REFERENCE in the ucode. Within one
inline expansion the result variable is created before the `this` copy, yet the copy is stored first, so a fresh result
variable always gets a higher bit than its own copy. A pool variable freed at the end of a full expression is reused by
the next expression's temporaries (first free first), and its whole LR (all reuses) is one uopt candidate: that is how
the loop's `tim.img->gh()` temp shares the pA copy's variable (adjsave 11, t0).
- 13B8's last pair: pB width (fresh, bit 64) vs pB copy (fresh, bit 60), both adjsave 2.0 -> copy t4, width t5.

**2. The fix: create extra pool temporaries in an EARLIER statement.** `s32 w = arg0->tim.width() / 12 + 0 *
arg0->tim.pw();` -- uopt folds the zero term away (no code), but edg has already created the pw() temps (and a result
temp for width()). They are free at the sum, so pA result / pA copy / pB result reuse them; pB's width now has a lower
bit than its fresh copy: width t4, copy t5, as in the target. The three extra enclosing-scope homes push the nested
block's named locals 12 bytes low; declaring `s32 xoff, xb, xa, x;` BEFORE `Spr *pC.., *pA.., *pB..` (assignments
after) puts them back on 148 / 144 / 136. Flat / worse: `if (0)` / `while (0)` blocks with inline calls before the sum
(92.9: they split the BB), operand order / parenthesisation of the sum (edg expands pA, pB, then pC regardless), panel
pointer declaration order, 4^6 per-site pw / gw / width / direct spellings, `Spr::dr()` draw members.
- Check for any pooled-temp tie: if the wanted winner is a fresh variable created after its rival in the same
  expansion, give it an earlier free pool variable by adding a folded `0 * member()` term to a preceding statement.

**3. Not done (time).** timproc_b1 1340 (same pair + count spill 172 vs 152): apply section 2 first. 578B4 declmove
sweep: variants 1000-2500 scored (base 99.9508, best 99.9409, no hit); 2500-13340 not run.

## kit CLXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 195): GUARDED DO-WHILE for a counted loop inside `if (count != 0)` removes the duplicated count test (3B6A0 93.65 -> 95.47); a local ALIAS COPY of a pointer re-ranks an s-reg tie (3B6A0 -> 95.595); post-increment and same-line `if (1) {}` sweeps (negative); NCC temp-slot reuse in 97EC / 1DDC; 454C4 FP fix vs s-reg set; negatives <a name="kit-clxviii-agent-c-run-195"></a>

**1. Guarded do-while (3B6A0, NCC).** `if (count != 0) { int off = 0; for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++, off += 12) {...} }`
emits the count test TWICE (`beqz t7; sw t7,52(sp); beqz t7; sw zero,48(sp)`): the outer if, then the for-loop entry test.
The target has one `beqz t7 / sw t7,56(sp)` with `sw zero,48(sp)` after it. Spelling that gives the target head:
```
if (count != 0) {
    int off = 0;
    unsigned int i = 0;
    do { ... } while (++i, off += 12, i < count);
}
```
(`continue`-free body; the guard keeps the semantics of the for loop, `count` is still re-read after a hit.) The prologue
through the count home now lines up word-for-word up to registers: 93.65 -> 95.47, 800 -> 796 bytes (target 800, AWAY,
flagged as a verified decode fix; the 4 bytes are the target's `or v0,s8,zero` copy of col for the faces load, not
reproduced by face() inlines, ternaries, `c->faces + i` or a pre-loaded faces base). Dropping the if and keeping the for
gives the same head but scores lower (94.65). The same rewrite is neutral on 3AE58 (98.905 both) and lowers 3B9C0.

**2. Alias copy re-ranks an s-reg tie (3B6A0).** `Col *cc = c;` declared right before the face pick and used for the
remap / faces reads (`cc->remap`, `cc->faces[...]`) emits nothing (uopt propagates the copy) but swaps the s5 / s6
colours: the triangle record pointer t takes s6 as in the target. 95.47 -> 95.595, length unchanged.
Mechanised as an ALIAS SWEEP (scratch script: for every statement / `if (` line that dereferences a typed pointer local or
parameter P, insert `T *P_al = P;` before it and use P_al on that line and the next 0-8 lines at the same or deeper
indent, skipping ranges that assign P; score each variant standalone). Hits kept (report.json):
- 3B9C0 `ObjB9 *self_al = self;` for the per-triangle group test: **the triangle count stays in a0 across the loop like
  the target** (single `lw a0,68(s5) / beqz a0` head; the continue paths step i in the `bltzl` delay slot instead of
  reloading self->col->ntri), that block word-for-word up to registers: 91.18 -> 92.55, 1100 -> 1096 (target 1116, AWAY,
  flagged by the alignment). Residual: the target spills off (`sw a1,128(sp)`) where ours keeps it in s6, and holds
  &p in t9 for the pp[ia] / pp[ib] reads (`addiu t9,sp,184`; inline at() / get() accessors and `(&p.x)[ia]` still fold).
- 7C1C `Node *a_al = a;` for `XZ(b->pos) - a->pos`: 95.12 -> 95.20. 3BE1C `V3 *n_al = n;` for the d / q[0] / q[1]
  reads: 95.45 -> 95.48.
No hit on 3B2EC, 36F0C, 3C43C, 42938, 454C4, BB8C, 329C, F04, 1DDC, 97EC, 3714, 2DE0, 4568, 3558, 41D40, 3AE58, 34890,
37938, 3DF58, 33094. A scalar version (`int X_al = X;`) and `Obj *me = this;` aliases of implicit member reads: no hit
anywhere tried. cfe NM bodies mostly use `*(T *)((char *)p + off)` casts, so the pointer sweep finds few sites there.

**3. Sweeps (queue items 1-2).**
- Post-increment split across every NM body / donor in range: only four in-expression sites exist. `while ((i = *list++)
  != -1)` (3BE1C, 3B2EC; loops with an early `continue`) split to `*list` + `list++` at the body top or a `for (; ...;
  list++)`: both shrink AWAY from target (3BE1C 1556 -> 1544, 3B2EC 952 -> 940). 3B2EC `out[cnt++] = ...` split reaches the
  target length (948) but 95.99 -> 95.55 (no lever-sweep hit on it). 3B6A0 `outp[nfound++]` split: 93.64 -> 90.64 (792 B).
  454C4 DL counters (`&dl->buf[dl->count++]` as `n = count; count = n + 1` or `int n = count++`): all lower.
- Same-line `if (1) {}`: no own-line `if (1) {}` exists in the in-range NCC donors. The own-line ones in cfe NM bodies
  (250C8 x2, 396FC x3, 40304 x2, 415A4 x2) score identically when moved onto the preceding statement's line: **cfe is
  line-insensitive here; NCC is line-sensitive** (3B6A0's `verts ...; if (1) {}` moved to its own line: 93.64 -> 92.77;
  3B9C0's `qa = pp[ia]; if (1) {}` is insensitive).

**4. NCC temporary slots: target fresh, ours reused (97EC, 1DDC).** Both near-exact donors differ only in stack offsets
of C++ temporaries: the target gives the late temporary its own slot where our edg reuses an earlier temp's slot.
- 97EC (99.97): the `(a - b) * s->k` result temp is at 204 in the target and at 180 in ours (180 is the target's slot
  for `other->pos - pos`). Copy-init spellings (`XZ e = ...`, `XZ f = ...`) change nothing; explicit `XZ(...)` / `Vec3(...)`
  casts add code (944 B).
- 1DDC (99.97): `V3 e;` declared right after `V3 r;` (instead of the `int e = 0;` placeholder) with `e = diff * sel;
  a0->vel -= e;` puts r at 340 and e at 328 = the target, but the frame grows 384 -> 392 (every top-region offset +8).
  `c.getOut()->goal.set(m);` in place of the `{ Out *o = c.getOut(); ... }` block brings the frame back to 384 with every
  REGISTER identical to the target but all homes below the key==3 block 4 low; adding any one scalar (int / short / char,
  anywhere) re-rounds the frame to 392. Frame-word census for NCC: each `{ named local; inline call }` block costs two
  words (the named local + the inline's this temp), an unused scalar or unused (even volatile) array costs nothing, an
  inline-call statement without a named local costs nothing. Open: a 1DDC spelling with exactly one word less between
  the key==3 block and r.

**5. 454C4: FP fixed, s-reg set not.** One `if (1) {}` after the final `gSPNumLights(c->next(), 1);` (or before the
`return` / `LIter`) moves 255.0f from f22 to f0 with the post-call remat and drops the f22 save (FP allocation = target,

## kit CLXIII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 198): timer-HUD 1340 + results panel 23FC EXACT -- edg homes: a scope's NAMED locals at scope entry, POOLED inline temps at first use; a named inline local is a FRESH variable per expansion, a pooled temp is reused; 4A308 v0/v1 via a folded term <a name="kit-clxiii-agent-g-run-198"></a>

**1. Where edg puts a home (zdbug:6 `isvar M 4 -N`).** All named locals of a scope get their frontend address when the
scope is ENTERED, in declaration order; a declaration later in the same scope (`s32 count = f(buf);` mid-block) is
still allocated at scope entry. Pooled inline temporaries are function-scope variables allocated at FIRST USE, after
every named local of the scopes entered so far. So a named local can be placed BELOW (after) a set of pool temps only
by declaring it in a nested block opened after the statements that create them. Spill words of a named local are its
own home (the "count spill" of 1340 = count's home).
- 1340: count declared at the top sat above the five pool temps (sp+172); declared as the first local of the nested
  block (`{ s32 count = f(buf); s32 x, pos4, posA1, pos6; ...`) it lands right above x (sp+152) = target. Together with
  13B8's kit-CLXI fix (`+ 0 * arg0->tim.pw()` on the glyph statement, `tim.img->gh()` in the loop, x / pos4 / posA1 /
  pos6 declared before the panel pointers) and one[] stored in index order: EXACT.
- 23FC: n / x in nested blocks opened after the glyph-width / vt statements, min / sec in the timer block, and a folded
  `+ 0 * SPR(0x788)->width()` in the first panel test (two function-scope pool temps above min / sec, no code) put
  min / sec / n / x on 96 / 92 / 84 / 76. Bracing case bodies or other statements does NOT move pool temps (they are
  function scope); only named locals follow scopes.

**2. Named inline local vs pooled temp.** `s32 width() { Img *i = img; return i->w; }` gives every expansion a FRESH
function-scope variable for `i` (never reused, one short live range). `s32 pw() { return img->gw(); }` (img as the
`this` of a tiny Img member) uses a POOLED temp, which later expressions reuse, so its uopt live range is the union of
all reuses. In 23FC the glyph-width image load was v0 (zdbug:5: forbidden only a0, interferes with 10 ranges) where
the target has t0; reading the width and vt through `pw()` made the variable shared and long: t0. With that change the
loop height had to go back through `height()` (named local, two fresh homes) and one unreferenced `volatile s32` in
the n block restored the x home and the spill words: EXACT. Rule: a value whose register is too LOW (v0 where the
target has t0) wants a pooled spelling; one that is too HIGH wants a named inline local.

**3. 4A308 (NM 99.85 -> 99.99).** `entry = ... + arg3 * 8 + 0 * (int)(*(char **)(arg0 + 0x60));` (folded, no code)
references the 0x60 load before entry: v60 v0 / entry v1 as in the target. Left: the arg3*8 spill word 56 vs 60.

**1. Parameter read vs local-copy read (the gain).** 591C copies its parameter once (`self = a0;`, self homed and
held in s0). Spelling ONE read as `*(char**)((char*)a0 + 0x30)` (the chain-1 `sub = ...` before the speed product)
instead of `self + 0x30` fixed the 0xba8 / 0xc14 rows: the target loads self->0x30 in the predecessor and self->0x2C as
the join's first instruction (stolen into the branch delay slot), ours had them the other way round. The a0 read emits
the same `lw rX,48(s0)` (copy propagation), but it is a different expression for CSE / PRE, so that site no longer
belongs to the self->0x30 code-motion web and PRE places the later loads differently. Sweep it: every `self` read one
at a time (80 variants), then pairs of the self->0x30 / self->0x2C reads (325 variants): only that one site moved
anything, but it is cheap and works only in functions that copy a parameter into a local. Some a0 reads add a home
reload and change the length (the 0x318 head / 1784 reads), so check the length.

**2. zdbug:6 colour order for the 591C pointer rows.** Every LR involved is `assigned (constrained)`, so the order is
plain adjsave priority. Ours: self->0x30 code-motion temp (bit 1400, adjsave 2.67, spans the three dispatch arms AND the
post-3ED4 `sub` block) -> v1; scratch / chain destination copies (2.5) -> v1 or a0; source pointers (1.5) -> a1;
`&res_a` / `&res_b` address constants (1.0) -> a0. The target's registers need `&res_a`/`&res_b` (v1) coloured BEFORE
the prefetch (a0), and the source pointer coloured before the destination at the scratch block and chain sites 2 / 4
but AFTER it at sites 1 / 3 (whose code is word-for-word the same shape). Levers that did not change the order:
dead `if (0)` / `while (0)` defs (deleted by cfe), moving the source def before / after the `p = 0; if (1)` split,
index / char* spellings, sharing destination variables across sites (a merged LR only gets denser), adding webs
(1784 base, head 0x318 base, scratch source, site-3 source) to accel_params (densities stay below 2.5), int /
unsigned / a0 spellings of the arm load (length changes: PRE no longer puts it in the arms).

**3. Negatives.** Axis region: x / y / z products into any of 9 float variables x the 0xA8 factor in any of 10
variables (1022 variants): x-first loads are reachable (`x = ax[0] * f; z = ax[1] * f; scale = ax[2] * f`, loads now
x, y, z) but the x / z products then colour f0 / f14 (target f14 / f0), and putting the x product into the f14
variable recolours fsel (f12 -> f2) -- 62 rows but lower fuzzy, not kept. Counter at 0xd84: fresh int variables
(vsel, t0, bits) still colour v0; field `+=` forms change code. `bne v1,v0` operand order: assign-in-condition,
swapped, `!(!=)`, `^`, field re-read, unsigned forms all canonicalise or change code. lever-sweep bbsplit / order /
hoist on the current body: no hit. 0xc88 mul order: the inline ternary `K * (c ? a : 1.0f)` puts the join temp
first like the target (mul.s f4,fJ,f8) but the shared cfe join temp colours f14 (target f2): 66 rows, not kept.
Chain sites: renaming the destination / holder / source variables (all five Vec3* and four float* locals, per site
and across sites, holder / copy role swap) never changes a single word -- copy propagation erases the variable
identity of these pointer webs, only their structure counts. cfe folds `+ (FW(p,K) & 0)` before uopt (no unit
shift, unlike NCC in kit XCIX).
game_uso 0B3C (99.83, 3 rows): the two `or a1,t0` literal-1 call arguments (target fresh `addiu a1,zero,1`) are
immune to literal spellings (`1u`, `(char)1`, `(short)1`, `!0`, `1L`, `(int)1.0f`) and to moving the head
constant into any other int local (constant propagation); `sltiu 4` stays the proven 4-label jumptable cap
(default / case 4 / case -1 / unsigned selector placements re-probed).

**Region map (end of run, 64 rows):** 0xb8-0xe4 axis loads y/z/x (6); 0x2b0-0x3d8 prefetch v1 / &res a0 / scratch
src a1 / dst a0 (27); 0x630-0x684 and 0x8bc-0x910 chain sites 2 / 4 src / dst v1 / a1 swap (22); 0xae4 bne operand
order (1); 0xc88 mul.s operand order (1); 0xd84 counter v0 vs v1 (4); 0xfe4-0x1004 sacrificed z selector (3).

## kit CLXVII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 200): m2c-ORDER STATEMENT GRIDS -- bootup C234 91.66 -> 95.05 from statement / operand order alone; lever-sweep's 2-4 line moves skip every statement containing `(` (all cast-style field stores); operand-order and store-order sweeps over 20 NCC / cfe bodies (mostly flat) <a name="kit-clxvii-agent-g-run-200"></a>

No exact. report.json gains: bootup func_0000C234 91.65818 -> 95.04727 (2200; 550 -> 549 words, target 550, FLAGGED),
post0b gl_func_00054E78 93.78986 -> 94.03623 (552, length = target), bootup func_0000B75C 93.58206 -> 93.60878
(2096, length = target).

**1. The blind spot.** `lever-sweep.py order` tries adjacent swaps and 2-4 line moves, but the move pass skips any
statement with `(` in it (`if not la or '(' in a ...`). In an m2c-literal body every field store is
`*(f32 *)((char *)(arg0) + K) = ...`, so only adjacent swaps were ever tried there. C234's NCC donor is such a body (it
was lifted from the cfe NM body), and its biggest miss was a five-line move.

**2. C234 fixes (all confirmed in-tree):**
- `0x290 = D_940` moved up next to the 0x288 / 0x28C stores in both the default and the 0x62 arm (5! x 4! permutation
  grid): the target loads the pool constant before the four `sb zero,0xA30..0xA33` stores and puts its `swc1` in the
  branch delay slot. With the m2c order (0x910 store first, 0x290 last) the byte stores could alias the global and
  pinned the load behind them. 92.79 -> 94.70.
- The 0x93C / 0x940 / 0x968 / 0x944 divide group: the target LOADS 93C, 940, 944, 968 and stores 93C, 940, 968, 944
  (div latency puts the 944 store last). With 0x944's statement written before 0x968's, the block lines up word-for-word
  up to registers, including the target's `nop` before `bc1f`. Alone that made the body 551 words. After it, run 182's
  `volatile f32 hz` (+2 words then) was surplus; dropping it gives 549 (target 550). 91.85 -> 92.79.
- Operand order from the target's `mul.s` operands: the A20 / A24 dot products read 0x3B0 / 0x3C8 first, the impulse dot
  product is `0x33C*0x93C + 0x340*0x940 + 0x344*0x944`, and `0x9D4 = 0` goes after the 0x934 store.
- Negative: the floor test spelled exactly as the target's operand order (`D128 * (0xDC*e4 + (0xE0+K)*e8 + 0xE4*ec)`)
  scores 94.62 vs 95.05 for the grid's best (`e4*0xDC + e8*(0xE0+K) + ec*0xE4`, `* D128` last). Writing A1C / A20 as
  `(sum) * temp_f16` (the target's operand order) also scores lower (95.03): the operand order changes the FP colouring.
  The residual word is the target's `mov.s f0,f12` copy of the 0x968 quotient before the held products.

**3. 54E78 (NCC).** An operand-order grid over the nine `p.n.a * p.n.b` products, the dot, and the translation-row
order: m[0][1] = `y*x`, m[2][0] / m[2][1] = `x*z` / `y*z`, dot = `y*o.y + x*o.x + z*o.z` (the first two terms commute
exactly), and the translation row back in x, y, z order (run 194's y-first order had been compensating for the old dot).
93.79 -> 94.04.

**4. Mechanised sweeps (scratch scripts, not committed).** (a) Operand swap: every binary `*` whose operands are
whole terms (not part of a `*` / `/` chain, not after a cast) gets an `@{ A * B @| B * A }@` marker. (b) Statement
permutation: every run of 2-6 simple assignments with no calls, no `++` / `--` and no textual write/read overlap becomes
a `@[..]@` marker. Then greedy spelling-grid. Results (standalone): C234 +0.34 (the 0x9D4 move), 2840 / 4BAF4 / 493AC /
4F2DC / 50444 / 4D688 / 8BD4 / 48AEC flat, 65494 +0.03, 4C5E4 +0.02, 55A0 +0.06 at +8 bytes (away), B75C / 6808 / 76F0
/ E68 (cfe, extracted standalone) flat. Bodies that were already hand-ordered have nothing left at this level; the win is
in bodies that still carry m2c's statement order. Extraction gotcha: an extern declared with the wrong type (B75C's
D_000008E0 is `f32` in bootup_uso.c, not `f64`) gave a false +1.0 in the standalone grid.

**5. Negatives.** 76F0 switch 3 `switch (var_v0 = self->unk4DC)`: identical code (the dead copy is propagated);
`switch (temp = ...)` with a live `temp` gets the copy but colours it a1 (93.39, worse). 18F0 (kernel): the peel's
`bnezl found` layout and the hoisted `-9` mask are unchanged by `if (found)` vs `continue`, a named mask local or
nested ifs (all 89.19). 65EE4 (-Olimit 1 donor): call-argument spellings (`&g` vs `g.base` order, prototypes, local
copies) all identical. 8FC8 S70 rows: `o = m38` as a block local or inline: flat. 50444: a `volatile` pos parameter is
ignored by edg (identical code).

## kit CLXIX (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 201): re-sweep with the fixed lever-sweep `order` (deref field stores now count as statements) over agent-g's range -- small order / bbsplit / declaration hits only (B75C 93.61 -> 93.93, DF14 96.27 -> 96.31, D884 96.63 -> 96.65, C234 95.05 -> 95.07, kernel 1ADC 93.39 -> 93.54, 6808 94.864 -> 94.875); four lever-sweep false positives; 32C8 / 578B4 / E2D0 / 1ADC / 4C5E4 grid negatives <a name="kit-clxix-agent-g-run-201"></a>

**Sweep counts (fixed `order`, then `all`, `hoist`, `declmove`).** 50 bodies (36 from the run-201 list + 14 further
in-range NM bodies / donors at 85-99.99: post0b 48510 / 48AEC / 493AC / 4A9F0 / 4B2F4 / 4BAF4 / 4FD00 / 51AD8 / 578B4 /
59E80 / 5F5F0, kernel 1ADC, timproc_b5 32C8, bootup E2D0). `order`: 4 bodies with hits (8FC8 1, 6808 10, 55A0 1,
D884 2) -- 2 kept (6808 `c8 = 0.0f` moved up past the 0x8005EE6C store, D884 `p->0xB4 = 0` moved down past the first
0x8005EE6C read-modify-write; p is the child's 0x108 sub-object, so no alias with the global), 2 false positives (below).
`all`: bbsplit hits kept in B75C (`if (1) {}` after the 0xA6C counter store, 93.61 -> 93.89 in report.json), C234
(after the 0x968 divide store), DF14 (after the rr->0x134 store), kernel 1ADC (after the case-2 HI16 store, 93.39 ->
93.54); 54E78 bbsplit x5 (+1.8 standalone) and 65494 `hoist` x4 (+0.5) REJECTED (length 552 -> 560 / 1336 -> 1340,
away from the target); 6808 de-naming of gD (94.25 -> 95.38 standalone) REJECTED: length 2380 -> 2372 crosses the
target 2376 to the same distance (structural rows 25 -> 18, but the arg rows grow 194 -> 230). `declmove`: only B75C
(5 hits). Re-sweeps after every kept change: no further hits.

**Declaration grid beats single declmove.** B75C declmove's best single move (sp60 after sp1C) gave 93.645 standalone;
a 56-way grid moving sp60 AND sp6C together found sp6C between sp28 and sp24 + sp60 after sp1C (93.662 standalone,
93.89 -> 93.93 in report.json). cfe homes every named local by declaration position, so two moves interact; a pair grid
is cheap once a single move has paid. A 720-way grid over 6808's first six declarations: flat (the g0/g00-before-e4/e0
swap from the order sweep, +0.003, is the only gain).

**lever-sweep `order` false positives (fixed version, 6187dc5).** All four reorder a memory access the tool took for a
local:
1. C++ member store written unqualified (`f124 = 1.0f;` inside a ctor = `this->f124`) swapped with a call
   (`w->pos.set(...)`, 8FC8).
2. Plain global assignment (`D_00000000 = 1;`) swapped with a call (6126C, in-tree post0b).
3. Write through a cast deref (`*(SC4_ *)&(t4.w) = ...;`) is not seen as a write of t4, so it was swapped with its own
   reader `p1.w = t4.w;` (55A0) -- semantics-changing, and the length also moved away.
4. ALL-CAPS macros that expand to a call plus stores (`PKT(c, a, b)` = `c->next()` + two stores) are treated as access
   macros, so two display-list packets were swapped (59E80) -- changes the emitted DL.
Suggested fixes: treat any identifier not declared as a local in the function as memory; treat `*(...)&(x...)` as a
write of x; treat ALL-CAPS macros whose expansion contains `(` after `->`/`.` (a call) as calls.

**In-tree statement-order grids (whole-file template, asm-processor + cfe per probe).** A small harness that renders
`@[a @; b]@` / `@{a @| b}@` markers in a copy of the whole src file and scores with lever-sweep's probe gave: D884
store block (162 interleavings of p->0xBC/0xB8/0xB4 and child->0x124 into the 0x8005EE6C sequence): the order-sweep
result is the optimum. B75C seven store groups (sp6C init, the 0x978 / 0x30C / 0x310 loads, both A04/A08/A0C triples,
the 0x938 five-store block, the A6C/A74/A70 block, the final scale block), greedy: flat. DF14 12-store child block
(3 groups, 25920 combos, greedy): flat. 6808 init block (d4/dc/p, bC..b0, c8/import/c4/c0): dc before d4 only (+0.003).
Keep `@{..}@` alternatives ending in a newline: an alternative ending in `{}` closes the marker early (`{}@|` contains
`}@`).

**timproc_b5 32C8 (99.96, 1480 B; one register row).** All other rows are reloc-symbol names. Target: l134 in $f2,
zero in $f0 (the zero is colored first and interferes); ours l134 $f0. 145 orders of {vF8 line, uE8 load, vEC line,
v104 zero line} x `if (1) {}` position, and 61 zero spellings (0 / 0.0f / chained / via `fa`) x 10 layouts: nothing
beats the current layout. Without the `if (1) {}` the zero and l134 share a block but the zero then takes $f12 (both
v104 and vDC zeros), l134 still $f0 -- the zero is not a local first-free pick. Negative.

**post0b 578B4 (99.95, 9676 B; s2_508 FD packet).** Target holds the sp50 packet pointer in ra and reloads arg2 into
t0; ours t0 / ra. Spelling grid (sp50 char* / int*, the FD packet on one / two lines / with blank, `arg2 & 0x1FF`
in four positions around the next DL-index increment): 24 combos all identical (99.9508). bootup E2D0 (99.54): the
`dot *= 1.0f + arg4` spelling (6) x scale-statement order and form (18): flat. kernel 1ADC: val / p / orig statement

## kit CLXXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 200): 37540 ported to C++ from its exact sibling 37348 (cfe 81.17 -> NCC 93.58, length = target); 8CD8 frame question answered (no natural aggregate; the pads are worth +0.07) <a name="kit-clxxviii-agent-c-run-200"></a>

**1. Sibling-template port (37540, post0b).** The cfe body (81.17, every frame offset already exact) was the "C++
decoded as C" pattern: its header named 37348 as the sibling (same homed-r reload idiom, same callback triple), and
37348 has an EXACT NCC donor. Copying that donor's kit -- `Node *s = o->s; if (0) gl(&s);`, every access to s through
a kept `Node *` inline parameter (`if (0) { n = 0; }`), the block-scoped `{ V3 v1(0.0f, -b, 0.0f); call(s, &v1, o); }`
push vector, the volatile flag word read through `Inp::fl()` -- gave 84.28 on the first build (756 bytes, target 764).
Then three spelling grids, each found by reading one region of the target:
- **Saved vector = one inline that reads all three and clears x.** Target: ONE `lw v0,96(sp)` serves the y / x / z
  loads AND the x zero store, y and z are stored to their slots at once (sp+172 / 176), x stays in a register until
  the call (spilled to sp+168 in the jal shadow). Spelling: `f32 gr(Node *n, f32 &y, f32 &z) { if (0) { n = 0; }
  f32 x = n->v60.x; y = n->v60.y; z = n->v60.z; n->v60.x = 0.0f; return x; }` -- y / z through references are
  memory (early stores), x as the return value is a register. A V3 out-parameter (all three early) or three
  separate getters (one s reload per getter) both lose. 87.17 -> 93.47 together with:
- **Store / re-read of a built vector.** Target builds vB4 from s->v50 with x / y stored and re-read but z kept in
  f12, then multiplies. `V3 vB4; vB4.set(s->v50.x, s->v50.y, s->v50.z); vB4 *= a;` with the COMPOUND
  `void operator*=(f32 k) { x *= k; y *= k; z *= k; }` reproduces it word-for-word (`x = x * k` re-reads all
  three or none, depending on the build-up). Length 756 -> 764 = target, so the post0b NM clip is unchanged.
- **v6C / v90 copies** are a BY-VALUE `void operator=(V3 v) { z = v.z; y = v.y; x = v.x; }` (word copy into the
  sp+28 parameter temp, then the z, y, x float stores the target has).
Report: 81.17 -> 93.58. Left: zero / a colouring (target zero f14, a f16; ours swapped -- int zeros, decl order,
abs spellings, split ab: all flat), the v9C serial `lwc1 f4 / swc1 f4` copy + re-read before `+=` (set(), ref
inline, `V3 &r` alias: all flat or +12), the target frame being 24 bytes bigger (two unused V3 between v6C and v90:
+0.03 only, not kept). **Lesson:** when a near-miss header names an exact sibling, port the sibling's donor kit
before any lever work -- the 37348 kit was worth +3 on the first compile and the region grids another +9.

**2. 8CD8 frame (queue question).** Are the six unused Vec3 locals the natural source of the 528-byte frame? Tested:
(a) a 2401-probe grid over pad placement (function top / then-arm / else-arm / inner if, 0-6 each): the current
else-arm six is the best row, and NO pads scores 87.12 vs 87.19 -- the pads are worth +0.07 only; (b) by-value
parameters on `XZ(Vec3)`, `perp(Vec3)`, `operator-(Vec3, Vec3)` (six XZ(v) sites = exactly six Vec3 temps) add
copy code (+60 .. +432 bytes, 70-85); (c) body-assigned XZ ctors (`{ y = 0; z = v.z; x = v.x; }`, the target's
y, z, x store order) drop the edg `this == 0 -> new` guards (-96 .. -124 bytes). No natural aggregate found; kept
the pads. lever-sweep `all` on 8CD8 and on the 3BE1C / 46050 / 3B9C0 / gui 2DE0 / 3714 donors after the order fix:
no same-length hit.

**3. 36694 diagnosis (no gain kept).** The target RE-LOADS n.x / n.y / n.z for `n * dot` after the dot product;
ours CSEs them (n.x even spilled to sp+24, the target's px slot). Computing l from t's members inside t's block
(`l = t.x * t.x + ...; px = t.x; ...`) reproduces the target's `mov.s f18,f8 / mov.s f2,f4` px/py/pz copies and

**1. The sibling port.** `scripts/sibling-scan.py --exact-only` pairs 32C8 (cfe NM, 99.96, 3 words: l134 $f0 vs
$f2, kit CLXIII section 3) with timproc_uso_b5_func_00002B74 (EXACT NCC donor, similarity 0.75). Compiling the cfe
body unchanged under NCC drops to 96.49; rewriting it on the 2B74 donor's shape gets every word before the vec3
children right at once: the braced child blocks, the TimB5Nm name copies (`uK.v = B5_NAME(..); nm = uK;` for the
rows, `uK = *(TimB5Nm *)(&sym + lo); nm.v = uK.v;` for the vec children), the vec3 constants as SOURCE LITERALS
(donor .rodata = -2500, -1500, 2500, 1500, -pi, pi in first-use order = the ROM words at RoData +0x134; renamed
timproc_uso_b5_func_000032C8_rodata by the splice and pinned), and the alloc-fallback comma
`(cA = alloc(0x20)), (h = ...), (cA != 0)` plus `h = ...;` after the ctor call: the target's two `mtc1 zero,$f0`
after the calls are the zero vector value h re-assigned on both paths.

(length 1476, no path mtc1s). `h = (f32)iz()` (inline int returning 0, kit CXIX / CLXIII) keeps h a variable:
length 1480 = target, path mtc1s present, but h first coloured $f12.

80 / 60); the cfe body's own list (cB right after cp2, then only padF0 / padF1, no padF2) gives the target homes.
**4. The colour residual was statement / BB order.** Normalising the pool offsets (`lwc1 $fN,K(at)`), a 768-variant
grid of `if (1) {}` after each of the seven vec statements x h-site spellings found 9 -> 7 words (`if (1) {}` after
vA, after vC2 and after vD: the -pi / pi loads then reuse $f0 one at a time, as in the target); a 1152-variant
permutation x same-line grid over {h + vC, name load, vA, split, vB} got 2 words (mtc1 / lwc1 adjacent swap); adding
a SECOND `if (1) {}` token to the permutation (1200 variants, all-one-line or all-separate) found 17 exact orders,
e.g. one line: `h = (f32)iz(); u12 = ..; if (1) {} vC = {h,h,h}; vA = ..; if (1) {} vB = ..;`. Single-split and
single-token grids never reach it: the target needs the zero's BB boundary on BOTH sides of the name load.
Takeaway: when an NCC port sits a few colour words off, grid BB splits in PAIRS together with statement order
and line layout before declaring a coloring cap (NCC compiles take ~5 ms, so thousands of variants are cheap).

= 0x134. ROM byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6.

## kit CLXXXII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 202): 33094 rewritten as real C++ on the 432BC V3 kit (87.65 -> 93.62, length = target); 35B1C is a C++ ctor (member Key ctor = cfront `new(4)` protocol) that reproduces every word but the vtable-store slot; near-exact sibling ports flat <a name="kit-clxxxii-agent-c-run-202"></a>

**1. 33094 (game_libs_post, NM donor) -- "C decoded as C" on a V3 function.** The C lift under NCC (volatile
pads, block locals) was 87.65. Read against the exact 432BC donor's V3 class (`set(const V3 &)`, by-value
`operator=(V3 v) { set(v); }`), the target words are:
- `a = o->pos` and `b = p->pos`: three float LOADS into registers, then the three stores. That is
  `set(f32 a, f32 b, f32 c)` called with `(o->pos.x, o->pos.y, o->pos.z)`: edg evaluates the call arguments RIGHT
  TO LEFT, so the target's z, y, x load order at the top falls out (no z, y, x spelling needed).
- the else arm `b = o->v104; b *= 10; b += a;`: the by-value operator= is the word copy into the sp+0x54
  parameter temp, then set(v); uopt forwards b.z and keeps the b.x / b.y stores the target has.
- then `a.mul(k); b.mul(k)` (component products with `const V3 &k`), the emit call, the two flag calls.
First compile 78.69 at 412 bytes; the set(f32 x3) form for the p arm 84.70; for a as well 89.71 (400); then the
kit-CLXXX OPERATOR-BODY ORDER grid (set / *= / += bodies, 1296 probes): set y, x, z; *= x, z, y; += y, z, x ->
93.44 at 404 = target; the two unused volatiles in a block at the end +0.02. Report 87.65 -> **93.62**. Left: the
FP colours of a (target x f12 / y f0 / z f2 with x split and reloaded in the else arm; ours f0 / f2 / f12 = the
set() inline parameters a, b, c coloured in bit order at equal priority) and the parameter temp 8 below the
target's. Not moved by: V3 ctor instead of set, set(const V3 &) for p, an explicit `Obj *p`, k as a reference,
k folded, an explicit `b.x = b.x + a.x ...` for += (+4 bytes), lever-sweep `all` (no hit).
**Lesson:** when a function loads all three components before storing any, try a three-float setter called
with the member expressions -- edg's right-to-left argument evaluation gives the load order for free.

**2. 35B1C (post0b, 97.40) is a C++ constructor -- one scheduling slot short of exact (not landed).** The cfe body's
"list-append constructor" (vtable at +0xC, placement-construct a 4-byte member at o+4 with `alloc(4)` if null,
o->8 = a3, duplicate scan, tail append, `next = 0`, key copy) is:

    struct Key { int v; Key() { v = 0; } int operator==(Key o) { return v == o.v; } };
    struct Rec { Rec *next; Key key; int val; virtual void f(); Rec(List *l, Key k, int v); };
    Rec::Rec(List *l, Key k, int v) : val(v) {
        Rec *n;
        for (n = l->head; n; n = n->next) if (k == n->key) gl(&gl_ref_0001E6B0, &k);
        Rec *last = 0;
        for (n = l->head; n; n = n->next) last = n;
        if (last) last->next = this; else l->head = this;
        next = 0; key = k;
        { volatile int z0; }
    }

(renamed `__ct__3RecFP4List3Keyi` -> gl_func_00035B1C, `__vtbl__3Rec` -> D_00000000). A data member with a ctor
gets edg's cfront `this == 0 -> new(4)` protocol (`addiu v1,s4,4; addiu at,zero,-4; bne`), the by-value
`operator==` makes the n->key copy temp at sp+0x3C, `k == n->key` (not `n->key == k`) gives the target's operand
roles, and the end-block volatile gives frame 0x50 with the &key temp at sp+0x34. Every word matches up to
relocations EXCEPT the vtable store: target `addiu v1,s4,4; addiu at,zero,-4; sw t6,12(s4); bne`, ours
`sw t6,12(s4); addiu v1,s4,4; addiu at,zero,-4; bne` -- the same residual the cfe body has, so the report does not
move (97.40 both ways) and the donor was not wired (source kept in the run-202 scratch). `NCC -S` shows our
pre-scheduling order is vptr store, then `this + 4`; the target needs `this + 4` first. Not moved by: Key as a
base (`Rec : Link, Key`: protocol before the vptr store, worse), a non-polymorphic base holding the data (+16
bytes), `Key() : v(0)`, `Key(int)` with `key(0)`, an explicit `key()` mem-initializer, `val = v` in the body,
`virtual ~Rec()`, volatile pads at 4 positions. Open: whatever makes edg / uopt compute the member address before
the vptr store.

## kit CLXXXIV (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 203): a FAITHFUL as1 lab (as0 + as1 by hand, without the driver's `-noglobal`) shows that 35B1C's vtable-store slot cannot be reached by any order of the ugen output; 33094's FP colours follow the parameter declaration order <a name="kit-clxxxiv-agent-c-run-203"></a>

No exacts this run; no source changes (gate re-run on the unchanged branch: ROM byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6,
non_matching_objects 0 errors).

**1. The as1 lab that matches the real build.** `cc -c x.s` is NOT the as1 of a C/C++ compile: the driver runs
`as1 ... -noglobal` for `.s` input, which switches off as1's global pass (the store-then-reload elimination that turns
ugen's `addu $15,$20,4; sw $15,52($sp); lw $3,52($sp)` into `addiu v1,s4,4; sw v1,52(sp)`), so `.s` experiments
schedule differently from the real object. Run the two stages yourself instead (paths in the worktree's
`tools/ido-static-recomp/build/7.1/out/`):

    NCC -S -G 0 -non_shared -Wab,-r4300_mul -O2 -mips2 -32 x.cpp        # ugen listing = the as1 input text
    as0 -G 0 -r4300_mul -mips2 -EB -g0 -O2 x.s -o x.B -t x.T
    as1 -t5_ll_sc_bug -elf -G 0 -p0 -r4300_mul -mips2 -EB -g0 -O2 x.B -o x.o -t x.T

The unedited `-S` listing of the 35B1C donor assembled this way gives a `.text` byte-identical to the NCC object, so
hand-edited orders of the listing are a trustworthy model of what as1 does with a given ugen order. (`-O3`, `-mips1`
and the IDO 5.3 as1 schedule this block the same way as 7.1 `-O2`.)

**2. 35B1C: the target's block is not an as1 schedule of any order of the ugen instructions.** The block is
`la t6, vtbl / sw t6,12(s4) / addu v1,s4,4 / sw v1,52(sp) / bne s4,-4` (vptr store, the member-ctor `&key` temp and
its home store, the `&key == 0` test folded to `this == -4`). Target: `lui t6; addiu t6; addiu v1,s4,4; addiu
at,-4; sw t6,12(s4); bne; sw v1,52(sp)`. Probed with the faithful lab: every dependency-legal order of those
instructions (with the home store / reload / move forms of the temp: 6 + 10 + 20 orders), every placement of one or
two labels or `.loc` group boundaries in them (120 + 420 + 630 probes, also with `la` split into `lui` / `addiu`),
an explicit `li $1,-4`, the vptr store through `8($3)`, and an exhaustive enumeration of all 9639 dependency-legal
sequences of 3-6 items drawn from {la, vptr sw, `addu` into $3 / $15 / $2, the three home stores, the reload, two
moves, a label, a `.loc`} (as1 does delete a duplicate `addu` and a store-reload pair, so extra ugen instructions were
in scope): NOT ONE gives the target. The only input that does is
`la t6; addu v1; li $1,-4` + label + `sw t6; sw v1; bne s4,$1` (the -4 constant materialised in an EARLIER basic
block than the vptr store), which ugen never emits (it emits `bne $20,-4` and as1 expands the `li at` next to the
branch). as1's rule seen in the lab: the bne delay takes the last movable instruction, and the macro's `li at` lands
just before the last remaining instruction only when that one is the vptr STORE (the exact sibling 37AF0 / 3E0F0
block `la; sw vptr; addu v1; bne` gives `lui; addiu; li at; sw vptr; bne; addiu v1` -- matches its target); with
the `&key` home store present, as1 always issues the vptr store right after `addiu t6`. The 5-word window

is no exact reference. This also corrects kit CXXXII's addendum (its "as1 input `la; addu; sw t6; sw v1; bne` gives
the target" was read off delay slots; in the lab that order gives our build). Treat 35B1C as capped unless a
different construct (not this instruction set) is found. The run-202 C++ donor (every other word exact) stays in
the run-202 scratch.

## kit CLXXV (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 204): a target stack slot BELOW the uopt spill area that is re-loaded into the LR's own register is a register LR spilled to its NAMED home, not an address-taken local -- 4D688 96.65 -> 97.84 (53 -> 2 words off standalone); 54E78 colour-order diagnosis (zdbug:5 + :6 per-LR table); 4A308 / 63964 / 31C0 / 4B0A8 / 4B620 / 4C5E4 / 50444 / 48510 / 4A890 / 493AC negatives <a name="kit-clxxv-agent-g-run-204"></a>

**1. 4D688 (post0b NM donor, debug-console loop).** The donor kept the polled event pointer `e` in memory with
`if (0) gl(&e);` (homed sp+60, every reload into a fresh ring temp t7). The target's word is at sp+56 and the
reload goes back into a0 -- the register the LR was coloured -- and the ring after it is one register lower. That
is the "named local saves at its decl-order home" signature (kit CI): `e` is a REGISTER live range that uopt splits
around the poll call and spills to its own named home, so (a) declare `int k;` (the switch selector) before `e`,
which moves e's home from 60 to 56, and (b) replace the `&e` keep with a dead multi-def `if (0) { e = 0; }` (the
LR keeps a spill home but stays a register candidate). The t-ring then lines up through the 'e' case. A statement
grid on top: `m3C = DSTR(..)` back before the volatile `m24++`, and the 'g'/'h' handover as
`m4 = m8; m8 = 0; m28 = 0;` (the named `int t` made a v0 LR; the target reads m8 into a ring temp). Report
96.64706 -> 97.84034, length unchanged. Left: the old-n copy of `if (n++ & 1)` (edg's pooled post-increment
temp, hoisted into the switch-compare delay slot) colours v0, target a0; `n++ % 2`, `(n++ & 1) != 0`, a named
`int o = n++`, `n++; if (!(n & 1))`, dead multi-def on n and the dispatch-statement permutations are all flat.
**Rule:** when a target slot at the spill end of the frame reloads into the SAME register as the def, try
"register LR + named home" (decl order + dead multi-def) before any `&x` keep; `&x` gives the home but reloads
into ring temps.

## kit CLXXVII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 202): **NCC `(&x)[0]` re-read = a load uopt will not CSE but ugen still reuses: turns a candidate (v1) into the target's ugen-ring temp (t8 / t9) -- game_libs_func_000307A8 EXACT** <a name="kit-clxxvii-agent-g-run-202"></a>

Fresh-eyes run over agent-c's range (game_uso, gui_uso, game_libs_post.c, post0b < 0x48000).

**The lever.** Shape: the target loads a value once, tests it (`beqz t8`), and the fall-through block uses the
SAME register for a derived value (`addiu t9,t8,-1` in the delay slot); the build has the value in a coloured
candidate (`lw v1` / `addiu t8,v1,-1`). That target register is a *ugen* temp, not an LR: uopt did NOT CSE the two
reads (no live range), and ugen's own register-content tracking across the fall-through edge recognised the second
`lw 12(sym)` as already sitting in t8 and reused it. Reproduce by spelling the second read so uopt's expression
hashing sees a different tree while the emitted load is identical:

```
} else if (D_307A8_i.fC != 0) {
    D_307A8_j.fC = (&D_307A8_i.fC)[0] - 1;   /* plain D_307A8_i.fC: CSE'd candidate v1 */
```

Under NCC (edg) the `(&x)[0]` survives into ucode as an address-of + index (ilod through the address) and is
hashed apart from the plain member load; the zdbug:6 dump confirms the candidate disappears (307A8: LR 35 `assigned
(constrained) 2` gone). 98.89 -> 100 standalone, 99.46 -> 100 in-tree; donor promoted to game_libs_ncc_307A8.cpp
(.bss reloc renamed `game_libs_func_000307A8_bss`, per-site aliases + `D_00000000_1c0a8` pinned to 0).

Things that do NOT work for this shape: `*(volatile int *)&x` / `*(unsigned *)&x` re-reads (ugen reloads, +3 words),
`((int *)&D)[3]` (still CSE'd), the static block alias, `--x`, `x + -1`, `0 * c` terms, `if (1) {}` after the
store, comparing against the known-zero local (`!= c`: candidate stays v1).

## kit CLXXXVIII (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 205): a register copy in the FIRST compare's delay slot is the else block's first insn -- block-local `u8 d = c` dispatch copy (6126C 93.81 -> 99.35, 484 -> 492 bytes = target); negatives on 4E424 / 18F0 / CEB4 / 4A890 / 578B4 / 63964 / 50444 / 4C5E4 <a name="kit-clxxxviii-agent-c-run-205"></a>

**The tell.** In an if / else-if dispatch chain, the target's first `bne vN,at,ELSE` carries `or aK,vN,zero` in its
delay slot, and every later test of the chain reads aK (`bnel aK,at` for the second one). as1 fills a plain
branch's delay slot with the first instruction of the branch TARGET when that instruction is harmless on the
fall-through path (the then-arm overwrites aK right away), and retargets the branch past it (the ELSE label
then sits on the `addiu at,zero,K2`). So the copy is the first statement of the else block, not a copy at the
loop head.

**Spelling (gl_func_0006126C, printf-style formatter).** `if (c == 'd') {...} else { d = c; if (d == 'x') ... else
if (d == 'f') ... else if ((c >= '0') && (c < ':')) { A = (u8)(d - '0'); ... } else ... }`:
- `int d = c` (or a reused int / char * parameter, or `if (1)` around the copy, or `(d = c) == 'x'` in the condition) is
  copy-propagated away: same 484-byte code as with no copy.
- `u8 d` keeps it (the int -> u8 conversion is not a plain copy): d colours a0, the 'x' test turns into the
  target's `bnel a0` with the 102 constant duplicated in its delay slot (+4 bytes), and the target length is reached.
- The range test must read `c`, not d: that keeps c live past the copy, so c (v1) and d (a0) do not coalesce.
  With all tests on d, d and c share one register (`andi v1,a1,0xff`, 488 bytes).
- `s16 d` also reaches 492 bytes, but by coincidence (sll in the delay slot + a later sra), 95.10.
- Left: the copy is `andi a0,v1,0xff` where the target has `or a0,v1,zero` (every no-op conversion I tried propagates;
  every conversion that survives emits an extension), the range test on v1 (target a0), and the digit value goes
  straight into s8 (target via v1).

**Negatives this run (all spelling-grid, standalone, calibrated against the in-tree NM):**
- 4E424 (95.37): all three subtractions written back into their parameters (x1 -= x0, y1 -= y0, z1 -= z0, then min /
  mid in x0 / y0, max in zero) is 79 at 212 bytes; the current named-`b` shape stays the best.
- kernel 18F0 (89.19): the peel's `bnezl found` + `b next` layout does not respond to nested vs continue skips,
  `goto` to the store, `switch (found)`, `found != 1`, the `found` assignment as an expression or nested ifs,
  `&= ~8` / `0xFFFFFFF7U` / `-9` mask spellings, or `&syms[i]` vs `syms + i` vs byte arithmetic. Every variant gives
  identical code (89.19), so cfe / uopt normalise all of them.
- timproc_b5 CEB4 (97.13): the empty then-arm that keeps `bc1f else; b join` -- negated conditions, `{}` else, goto
  forms, and `f = 1.0f` / `a1 = a1` / `pad[0] = pad[0]` / `v[3] = v[3]` / all-four `v[i] = 1.0f` then-arms all fold to
  `bc1t` or keep a store; only `v[0] = v[0]` / `v[1] = v[1]` / `v[3] = v[0]` / `pad[0] = 0` hold the shape (with a store).
- 4A890 NCC donor (93.47): an id-cursor copy `s = ids` reused as the list pointer (`s = list` inside the if and after
  it), and a non-volatile size: inert or worse (the target's s0 / s1 split does not appear).
- 578B4 NCC donor (99.95): `(&arg2)[0] & 0x1FF`, `FW((&sp50)[0], 4)`, `(&FW(sp50, 4))[0]` and a 4-statement permutation
  of the post-call DL-append lines do not swap the t0 / ra pair (kit CLXXVII's `(&x.f)[0]` does not reach a spill
  reload's colour).
- 63964 NCC donor (99.96): member vs free operator* / operator+, `V3 r; r.x = ...; return r;` bodies, a direct ctor
  (no set()), and `n * va.y + va` / `va + va.y * n` / an explicit `V3 t = n * va.y` temp do not move X / T1 / T2 (8 / 12
  bytes high).
- 50444 NCC donor (91.83): NCC ignores `volatile` on a parameter (`float *volatile pos` gives the same code); an
  `if (0) f(&pos)` escape homes EVERY parameter and drops s0 (+12 bytes).
- 4C5E4 NCC donor (86.87): reading `m78` at both uses (no named `m`) makes the else arm word-for-word the target up to
  registers (`lw a0,120(s0)`, `andi a3,a0,4` in the beqz delay, 836 bytes = target) but shifts the ugen ring by 3
  from the first flag test on, so it scores 78.1. A folded `(m78 + 0 * mC0) & 4` re-phases the ring (KEPT: report 87.22 ->
  88.48, objdiff diff 86.87 -> 88.12, length unchanged). The phantom's member load is CSE'd with the later mC0 stack-arg load and
  hoisted into t5, so the sub load takes t4 (target t5). Phantoms on m104 / mB8 / m78 / mBC score 87.95 - 88.07, and

## kit CLXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 203): **NCC folded `+ 0` on a POINTER-valued inline-call result (or its return expression) re-pools EDG's temporaries: same ucode shape, different vreg sharing between the two rotated copies of a loop condition -> different uopt colours, zero emitted code** <a name="kit-clxxix-agent-g-run-203"></a>

Fresh-eyes run on agent-c's usual range (game_uso / gui_uso / game_libs_post.c / post0b < 0x48000). No exact.

**The lever.** Under NCC (EDG front end), `p + 0` on a pointer is folded to no code, but EDG still routes the value
through a fresh pooled temporary when the `+ 0` sits on the result of an inline member call or on that inline's
`return` expression. The pooled temps become `vreg` homes in the ucode (`isvar M ... vreg` in the `-zdbug:6` itab);
two inlined copies of the same call that share a pooled vreg get the same colour. Changing which pool slot a copy's
temporary lands in moves its colour without changing a single instruction. cfe folds `+ 0` away before uopt (no effect
on in-tree C bodies, 250C8 / 2D374 / 591C checked).

- gl_func_00041D40 (99.61 -> 99.90, report): `return &(*a)[++idx] + 0;` in `next()` moves the ENTRY copy of the for
  condition's index temp a0 -> a1 (target); `for (AIter it = iter(..); it.next() + 0; )` then moves the BOTTOM copy's
  index temp v1 -> v0. Left: the bottom copy's array pointer in a1 (target v1). The dump shows why: EDG pools the bottom
  copy's array load into the same vreg (-64) as the entry copy's index temp, which the first lever coloured a1. 1300+
  further spellings (cast routing, `(&it)[0]`, named `r` returns, `Arr *b = a`, cur() / body / if(1) grids, a
  do-while with a second inline `next2()` for the bottom copy -- 8 bytes of frame lost, worse) leave it there.
- game_libs_func_00042938 (97.44 -> 97.60): `+ 0` on three DL packet pointer arguments (`ctx->next() + 0` /
  `ctx->nD() + 0`) found by a site sweep.
- gui_func_00003714 (96.43 -> 96.51): `gImmp1(pkt3 + 0, G_RDPHALF_2, ...)` in the texrect macro.

**Site sweep (reusable recipe).** A throwaway generator inserted an `@{ @| + 0 }@` marker at the end of every `return E`,
`if (E)` / `while (E)` / for-condition, assignment right-hand side and call argument of each NCC NM donor, and
spelling-grid ran greedy coordinate descent (`--rounds 3`). 30 donors: gains only in 42938 and 3714 (above); flat
(every site folds to identical code) in 3DF58, 46790, 3B6A0, 36F0C, 3B2EC, 3BE1C, 3E5E0, 3C43C, 3AE58, 37938, 34890,
3B9C0, 46050, 454C4, 36694, 37540, 33094, gui 329C / 2DE0 / 0F04 / 4568, game_uso 97EC / 1DDC / BB8C / 3558 / 7C1C /
8CD8. The lever is specific to inline calls returning pointers whose temporaries EDG pools; scalar `+ 0` and `+ 0` on
plain variables never move anything.

**Negatives.**
- 3DF58 (99.06): the whole-function v0 / a1 swap (iterator result vs the loop's `n`) does not respond to next() /
  first() spellings (ternary vs if, `(&cur)[0]`, `+ 0`, named `r`), shared vs per-loop `n`, `return best + 0`, or
  decl / store order.
- 46790 (99.25): the t8 / t9 ring parity from `sll ...,0xa` on is unmoved by `0 * c` phantoms (EDG folds them before
  ugen, unlike cfe's ring phantoms), shift vs multiply, cast spellings of `c & 15`, operand order, or named hi / lo
  temps.
- 3AE58 (99.26): `pick()` routing (direct `->vi`, `+ 0`, named `vi` u16 / int, `!a1->tbl` arm order, `(&e)[0]`) and the
  three `fv[]` store orders are flat.
- 250C8 (99.85, cfe): the OoT-faithful FinishAsyncLoad shape (cases read the `retMsg` local, separate `doneMsg`) DOES
  put fontId in the shared temp slot sp+36 like the target, but costs 4-8 bytes in the switch arms (95.37);
  block-scoped `u32 fontId` lands below the reloc struct (sp+44, struct pushed to +48). Mixed local / memory reads per
  arm: nothing beats the current body.
- 2D374 (99.67, cfe): z / fr FP colours: assignment perms x keep-alive sets x store order x decl perms and dead
  `while (0)` ref boosts are all flat -- z is the propagated 0.0 constant, not a candidate, so ref boosts on it vanish.
- 591C (99.72, cfe): writing the scaled-axis products in X / Y / Z order makes the three loads match the target
  (792 / 796 / 800) but rotates the f14 / f2 / f0 colours; all 6 x 24 assignment / store / `if (1)` orders score at or
  below the current body.
- 97EC (99.97) / 1DDC (99.97): pure frame-slot swaps of two by-value Vec3 temporaries (kit CLII's deferred-temp order);
  copy-init vs direct-init, explicit `Vec3(...)` / `operator*` calls and a / b order do not swap them.
- game_uso 0B3C (99.83, cfe): the mode switch's empty `case 4: break;` gives `sltiu 5` (target `sltiu 4`), but dropping it

  test's delay slot; every later test and the digit arm read a0, and v1 is reused as a scratch value in the digit
  arm. Kit CLXXXVIII read this as a block copy `u8 d = c` in the else block (andi, not or) and run 206 as a uopt
  live-range split. Neither: the zdbug:6 dump shows the plain body never splits c. The two registers are two
  different candidates:
  - v1 = the CSE expression `*q` from the loop test, and
  - a0 = the VARIABLE c assigned from it at the top of the body.
  Spelling: top-tested `while ((q = fmt, fmt = q + 1, *q) != 0) { c = *q; if (*q == 'd') ... else if (c == 'x')
  ... }`. IDO rotates the loop (the bottom keeps the load + test, the head the first compare), the first test
  reads the expression (so it stays on v1), and `c = *q` is the `or`. Every same-width source copy
  (`d = c`, `int d`, `(&c)[0]`, ...) is copy-propagated away, which is why the old grids never found an `or`.
- **Colouring order matters.** With all four tests on c, c (more refs) colours first and takes v1, pushing the
  expression to a1 (95.30). Reading `*q` in the FIRST test raises the expression's priority so it takes v1 and c
  falls to a0 (v0 is q's register, live across). The other tests reading c or `*q` makes no difference.
- **Left on 6126C (2 words): the digit arm.** Target `addiu v1,a0,-0x30; andi s8,v1,0xff` (c - '0' in its own
  candidate, then truncated into A); every spelling gives `addiu s8,a0,-0x30; andi s8,s8,0xff`. Negative grid
  (standalone, 99.56 plateau): `A = (u8)(c - '0')`, `(c - '0') & 0xFF`, `0xFF & (c - '0')`, `(int)(u8)`,
  `(u8)(u32)`, `(u8)(c + -'0')`, named int / u8 / u16 / s16 / u32 block temps (`d = c - '0'; A = (u8)d`, `A = d = ...`),
  `d = c; d -= '0'`, A typed int / u32 / s16 (u8 / char A goes to memory, 89.6), A assigned after or inside both
  arms of the next-char `if` (87.9 / 89.5), and `c -= '0'` (c's new value stays in a0, and with the 'x' test on c
  it costs 99.52). Any no-op temp is copy-propagated. The target needs a candidate for `c - '0'` that is
  not merged into A; I could not find the source shape that creates it.
- **4D688 (NCC donor, 96.95): the old-n copy of `n++ & 1`** goes to v0 (target a0; the target uses neither v0 nor v1
  anywhere in the function). zdbug:6 shows the LR coloured `1` (lowest free). Inert: `int o = n++; if (o & 1)`,
  `o = n; n = o + 1`, `(n++ + 0) & 1`, `1 & n++`, `(unsigned)n++`, `!= 0`, `& 1U`, `(&n)[0]++`; `n++ % 2` and
  `(n += 1, n - 1)` are worse.

  candidate) where the target uses ring temps t7/t8, which shifts the temp ring for the next 40 words. `-= 1`,
  `= x - 1`, a named pointer, `+ 0`, array indexing, `(&*p)[0]`, the 0x2BC update spelling and an `if (1) {}` split

## kit CLXXXIII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 205): **count the by-value copy hops per expression (8CD8 87.19 -> 89.48), score with the report's `functionRelocDiffs=none` (30AF4 92.52 -> 93.20), 3558 operator= order, constant-hoist pattern in 46050 / 454C4** <a name="kit-clxxxiii-agent-g-run-205"></a>

## kit CXCIV (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 208): 6126C EXACT -- a "subtract into a temp, truncate into the variable" pair is a self-referencing update of a copy (`ch = c` earlier, `ch -= '0'; A = (u8)ch`), and a folded `+ 0 * x` in cfe still counts as a use of x for uopt's colouring priority <a name="kit-cxciv-agent-c-run-208"></a>

_Exact: gl_func_0006126C (492 B, 99.92 -> 100). cfe C body on the build path, no donor._

- **The tell.** Target digit arm `addiu v1,a0,-48; andi s8,v1,0xff` (c - '0' into a free caller-saved
  register, then truncated into A in s8). Every direct spelling (`A = (u8)(c - '0')`, named block temps
  `d = c - '0'; A = (u8)d`, `d = c; d -= '0'` in the same block, ...) is forwarded by uopt copy propagation
  into A's register (`addiu s8,a0,-48; andi s8,s8,0xff`): a single-use temp whose operands are still valid at
  the use is always substituted.
- **What is not forwarded:** an update whose expression reads the variable it writes (`x = x - 48`): after the
  store the expression `x - 48` means something else, so the def keeps its own register. If x's OLD value is a
  copy of c made in an EARLIER block (`(ch = c, c >= '0') && (c < ':')` in the range test), copy propagation
  rewrites the read to c (a0) while the def stays ch: `ch -= '0'` emits `addiu ch_reg, a0, -48`, and
  `A = (u8)ch` is the andi. ch's live range is only the digit arm, so it takes v1 (free there). A copy in the
  SAME block as the update is folded with it (`ch = c - '0'`, forwarded again).
- **Colouring priority side effect, and the zero-code fix.** The copy `ch = c` is one more counted use of c
  (the zdbug:5 dump shows the copy's block with 2 refs even though the copy itself is dead after
  propagation), which lifts c's `adjsave` from 20 to 23.33 above the `*q` CSE expression's 21: c takes v1,
  the expression a1, ch a0 (31 diff rows). Reading `*q` in the 'x' test raises the expression to 26 (ch
  then lands on v1, but that compare reads v1, target a0). The match: a folded `+ 0 * *q` on c's assignment
  (`c = *q + 0 * *q;`) -- zero code, but uopt counts it as a use of the expression, restoring expr > c with
  every compare on c. Kit CLXXIX's note that cfe folds `+ 0 * Z` away before uopt is true for its `(int)(Z)`
  inline-call forms; `0 * VAR` / `0 * *p` still adds a counted reference (also seen with `+ 0 * (c - '0')`,
  which flipped c above the expression). Use it as a priority lever for two-candidate colour swaps in cfe.
- **Reading the priorities:** `-Wo,-zdbug:5` with the dump cc prints, per live range, `>>>active<<<{expr|0} LR reg`
  followed by `adjsave, hasstore: <priority>`, `forbidden: [...]`, the interference list and the per-block ref
  counts (`- live bb - <bb> <refs> ...`). Comparing two variants' adjsave for the two swapped candidates
  told directly which reference was flipping the order.
- **USO jal binding:** the in-unit callee gl_func_00034458 resolved to its real address on the build path
  (ROM words are `jal 0`); called through a blank alias `gl_func_00034458_6126C = 0x00000000` (pinned).
- **Negatives this run:** 4A890 NCC donor -- holding the id cursor copy as a pointer later reassigned to the
  list (`s = ids; end = s + n; ...; s = list`) is copy-propagated away (93.48 flat; the target keeps ids in s0
  then reuses s0 for &list, and the byte size in s1). timproc_b5 CEB4 -- the D-grey load before the 1.0
  materialisation in blocks 2/3: negated condition (95.07), a named `one` (flat), else-arm D reads without f
  (78.95), chained stores (78.08).
- **Re-scored with `functionRelocDiffs=none` (kit CLXXXIII):** 59E80 NCC donor -- a 4^5 grid over the BA
  packets' `next()` spellings now prefers plain `next()` everywhere; the run-164 `nextD()` on 0xBA000602 was a
  CLI-scoring pick (97.86 -> 98.48, length = target). Re-run any `next()`/inline-routing pick made before the fix.
- **bootup 6808 (cfe, 94.88 -> 95.62):** the last two case-0 attach calls load a1 (obj+0x90 / +0x94) BEFORE a0
  (the root import): read the field into the existing va / vb locals first. Left there: the target stores the
  outgoing by-value word (8(sp)) before its home temp (store in the jal delay), ours the other way round; the
  comma form `f(root, va, (t70.w = D, t70))` is only +0.01.
- **Negatives (corrected scorer):** zero-lever-grid.py one round over the NCC donors 4F2DC, 50444, 4A890, 4BAF4,
  48AEC: all flat. Kernel 18F0 (cfe, 89.19): `+ 0 * i` / `+ 0 * found` / `+ 0 * arg3` on the loop bound,
  the found stores/test and the symbol index: flat (the i / remainder-temp register swap there is not this
  priority pair). post1b 65EE4 (-Olimit 1 donor): data as `(B) + 0x10` vs `g.data` vs `g.base + 0x10` in the
  first call: flat (the `lui t; ori a2,t` split is not source-steerable that way).
