## kit CXCVI (agent-c 2026-10-28, run 209): 50444 EXACT -- the kit CXCIV `+ 0 * x` counted use swept over cfe bodies and NCC donors (a brute site x identifier grid); in NCC it can decide whether a parameter keeps its memory home; `(m->n += 1) >= max` vs `++m->n >= max` swaps the v0 / v1 pair <a name="kit-cxcvi-agent-c-run-209"></a>

_Exact: gl_func_00050444 (488 B, 91.94 -> 100), NCC donor `game_libs_ncc_50444.cpp` over an empty placeholder in both trees._

- **The sweep.** One variant per (site, identifier): append ` + 0 * (int)(X)` before the `;` of every `= E;` /
  `return E;` and wrap every `if (E)` / `while (E)` as `((E) + 0 * (int)(X))`, X over every identifier in the
  body (out-of-scope ones just fail to compile). Score with objdiff `-c functionRelocDiffs=none`, keep only
  same-length (or toward-target) gains, then REJECT every hit whose X is not yet assigned on all paths to the
  site (an uninitialised read, same class as an empty test on an uninitialised local) -- a lot of the biggest
  hits are exactly that (kernel 1594 `0 * i` before the loop, 76F0 `0 * var_v0` / `0 * temp` on a path where
  temp is conditionally set, 24B8 `0 * pad` on the volatile pad, 4BAF4 `0 * iz` before iz). In float context
  the term is not folded (code emitted: CEB4 / E2D0 only lose).
- **50444 (NCC).** `return m->n - 1 + 0 * (int)(pos);` -- pos was a register candidate in ours; the extra
  counted use makes uopt keep it in its memory home (`sw a2,0x38(sp)`, base reloaded into t7 per use) as in
  the target: 91.94 -> 98.30, every t-register then in phase. Then a spelling grid: operator== written
  argument-member first (`o.x == x && o.y == y && ...`, the key from its home loaded first, 98.73) and the
  count bump `if ((m->n += 1) >= max)` instead of `if (++m->n >= max)`: the element pointer and the count take
  v0 and the == results v1 (was swapped) -- 100. (`m->n++; if (m->n >= max)` and `m->n = m->n + 1;` are 99.10.)
- **Gains (report.json):** bootup 6808 95.62 -> 95.65 (`gD = D_bu_776C + 0 * *arg1`), E68 93.44 -> 93.97
  (`m = E68_MGR + 0 * *cfg`, 3008 -> 3016 B toward 3036), B75C 93.929 -> 93.933, game_libs.c 76F0 94.998 ->
  95.023 (`vt = self->vt + 0 * temp` inside the arm where temp is set); NCC 48AEC 96.88 -> 97.24
  (`Flags::test` returns `(v & m) + 0 * (int)(v)`, `dlcall`'s t `+ 0 * (int)(dl)`), 4BAF4 95.70 -> 96.33
  (`ctx = ... + 0 * w`, `w = spr->w + 0 * y`), 4F2DC 94.89 -> 95.26 (`p = ... + 0 * (int)(cam)`), timproc_b5 C310
  96.02 -> 96.25 (`return i->w + 0 * (int)(i)` in an inline accessor).

## kit CLXXXVII (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 207): **cfe `+ 0 * VAR` as a uopt PRIORITY lever, read in the zdbug:5 list -- 591C 99.73 -> 99.85 (57 -> 34 rows), post0b 38A28 84.62 -> 92.49 at target length (a counted use keeps a switch selector coloured), post 30AF4 93.20 -> 93.55; the one-zero-use-per-dominance-path rule** <a name="kit-clxxxvii-agent-g-run-207"></a>

_No exact. report.json: game_uso_func_0000591C 99.73376 -> 99.85270 (4372, length = target), gl_func_00038A28
84.61729 -> 92.49383 (344 -> 324 bytes = target), gl_func_00030AF4 93.19697 -> 93.54735 (2132, target 2112, length
unchanged)._

**1. Reading priorities.** Compile the asm-processor output of the whole unit with the dump cc
(`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/.../cc ... -Wo,-zdbug:5`, diagnosis only) and summarise `uoptlist` between
`global coloring of FN` and `REEMISSION OF FN`: each `>>>active<<<{expr|n} LR reg` block, its `adjsave` and the
`- live bb - <bb> <refs>` lines. The reg column is machine number - 1 (1 = v0, 2 = v1, 3 = a0, 4 = a1, 5 = a2).
`forbidden:` is the set at colouring time (already-coloured neighbours + precoloured argument registers in the
LR's blocks, e.g. a0 when the LR spans an alloc call block that loads `a0 = 12`). Ties in adjsave go to the lower
LR number. Empirically adjsave = (refs + const) / spanfactor, so each counted use in an LR of n blocks adds
1 / spanfactor (0.25 for a 4-block LR, 0.5 for 2 blocks).

**2. Counting rules for the folded use (cfe).**
- Pointer variables need an int cast: `+ 0 * (int)p`. Put it in an INT context (an address offset
  `*(float *)((int)p + 8 + 0 * (int)p)`, an index `p[0 * ((int)p | 1)]`, an int call argument
  `alloc(0xC + 0 * (int)src)`, a pointer built through `(T *)((int)q + 0 * (int)p)`). In a float expression it
  adds an int->float conversion (code); pointer arithmetic `ptr + 0 * x` is folded before uopt and counts nothing.
- At most ONE counted use per block, and never two uses of the same variable where one block dominates the other
  (57 dominating 61): uopt then CSEs `0 * x` into a live zero (`or a2,zero,zero` + spill, +16 bytes). Different
  spellings (`(int)p * 0`, `0u * (unsigned)p`, `0 * ((int)p + 1)`) are the same expression for this. A second use
  in the same block needs a different sub-expression of the variable (`0 * ((int)src | 1)`, `0 * (int)src[0]`).
- A use in a block where the variable was not live EXTENDS its live range there: the rank changes, and the
  extended LR now blocks its register for every LR in that block (that is how the 591C site-4 address constant
  moved a1 -> a2: `accel_params = (float *)((int)hit_parent + 48 + 0 * (int)child_flags)`).
- Only use variables that are definitely set on every path to the use (coordinator rule after agent-c's run):
  the grid's biggest 591C hits were `+ 0 * (int)delta_g_dst` reads before the variable's first assignment --
  rejected. A use of the variable inside its own initialiser (`int code = *(int *)c + 0 * code;`, 38A28 grid top
  hit) is an uninitialised read -- rejected; the same use one statement later is fine.
- A use of a LOAD expression (`0 * *(int *)((char *)self + 0x30)`) is folded together with the load and does NOT
  count for that expression's code-motion candidate.

**3. 591C (cfe, 4372 B).** Order before: self->0x30 prefetch (2.67, spans the dispatch arms, the scratch block AND
the post-3ED4 block 66) -> v1; scratch dst copy (2.5) -> a0; scratch src (1.5) -> a1; &res_a (1.0) -> a0; sub
(0.63) -> a0. Kept (all zero-code, length = target):
- scratch src raised to 3.0 (`alloc(0xC + 0 * (int)src)` in the call block, `src[0 * ((int)src | 1)]` and the z
  offset in the body): src now outranks its copy destination and colours v1 as the target;
- chain site-4 source (`accel_params`, one LR across both chains) raised 1.5 -> 2.5 with the z offset in both
  chains and `stage = *(Vec3 *)((int)p + 0 * (int)accel_params)` after each block: it ties the 2.5 destination
  and wins on LR number -> v1 as the target;
- `axis_src` (the 1784 base) read through the PARAMETER (`a0->0x30`, kit CLXXIV): block 66 leaves the prefetch
  web, so sub stops interfering with the prefetch and colours a0 again (99.79);
- `+ 0 * (int)child_flags` on both site-4 source definitions (child_flags is set by site 3 just before): the
  address constant colours a2 (99.85).
Left (34 rows): the three copy destinations colour a0 (target a1) and the prefetch then a1 (target a0). The target
needs a0 blocked for the destinations; only the prefetch can do that at the scratch block, and it ranks 1.33 once
block 66 is out of its web (2.67 with 66 in, but then it interferes with sub and sub loses a0). Merging the three
destination variables into one gives the merged LR 3.75 (span compression), above every source. Fresh counter
variable + `0 * v0` around the 0xd84 counter: flat or longer. Region-wide grid (3872 single insertions, 22
variables; then 1111 on the scratch / chain region and 564 on the tail after each kept step): no other hit with a
defined variable.

**4. 38A28 (cfe jump-table interpreter).** `if (key >= 40 + 0 * code)` in the 0x66 arm keeps `code` live and
coloured across the jump-table switch (it had a memory home + reload): 344 -> 324 bytes = target, 84.62 -> 92.49.
The remaining rows are the target's 64-byte frame (key spilled at 60) and p/key in a2/a3 (ours v0/a2). Second
grid round on top: flat.

**5. 30AF4.** `gl_cmd_30AF4 = 16 + 0 * prev;` in case 2 (any defined variable gives the same +0.35; the same
store in the later case is +4 bytes and lower).

**6. Grid results on the other cfe bodies (one insertion per statement x every local / parameter).** 396FC
(98.66, 264 variants), 35B1C (97.40), 415A4 (93.38; the only hit shortens 452 -> 444, away from the 452 target,
rejected): flat.
31A74 (90.73), 250C8 (99.85), 30AF4 second round on the kept body: flat. 2E354 (m2c body, 8792 variants, 4907
probed in the time box): the only length-toward-target hit (`+ 0 * var_v0`, 3692 -> 3688) reads a variable that is
only assigned inside earlier `if` arms -- rejected under the defined-variable rule.

**7. 38A28 frame.** After the counted use the target length was reached but the frame was 48 bytes (target 64, key
spilled at sp+60). A 120-way declaration grid over {r, p, key, `volatile int pad[4]`} x the position of `code` gave
`key; code; volatile int pad[4]; r; p` -- frame 64 and every home as the target (92.49 -> 92.59).

**Tools (scratch, /tmp/claude-1000/g207):** `zsum.py` (colour-order summary of a uoptlist), `lr.py` (forbidden /
interference for chosen LRs), `grid.py` + `batch.py` (line-anchored counted-use grid scored in-tree; 0.7 s a probe,
which makes a 4000-variant grid on a 4 KB cfe body a few minutes -- lever-sweep's in-tree probe path was ~20x
slower here).

## kit CLXXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 208): **uopt priority TIES break toward the lower LR number -- 591C scratch site fixed by bringing the prefetch (2.0) and the copy destination (2.0) to a tie: the guard-pointer setup moved above the transform dispatch drops two "default" (live-through) blocks from the prefetch's span, and an empty `do { } while (0);` between the copy's loads and stores adds one block to the destination's span; 38A28 case-0x65 value through `key`** <a name="kit-clxxxix-agent-g-run-208"></a>

_No exact. report.json: game_uso_func_0000591C 99.85270 -> 99.89387 (4372, length = target), gl_func_00038A28 92.59259 ->
93.33334 (324 = target). post0b NM clip unchanged 0x2eacc._

**1. What the span is.** In the zdbug:5 colouring dump, an LR's adjsave is divided by the blocks in its `- live bb -` rows PLUS
the `- live bb (default) [...]` list (blocks it is merely live through). 591C's self->0x30 prefetch (defs in the three
transform-dispatch arm exits, one use in the scratch block) had span 6 (48, 50, 54, 57 + default 55..56) = 8 / 6 = 1.33; the
default blocks 55..56 were the `p = 0; if (1) { p = &scratch_xz; }` anti-fold blocks sitting between the switch and the
scratch block. Moving those two lines ABOVE the transform switch (same code: p is an address constant, rematerialised) gives
span 4 = 2.0. The copy destination (defs at the copy from p and the alloc result, three store uses) was 10 / 4 = 2.5; one
`do { } while (0);` AFTER the second source load (before the first store; also works between stores, not before the
loads -- that splits the src LR instead, 98.5) makes it 10 / 5 = 2.0.

**2. Tie order.** At equal adjsave the LR with the lower number is coloured first. The prefetch's LR number is set by the
first occurrence of ITS expression in the candidate table (here 195 vs the destination's 190 before the move; reading the
first-region `sub->0x348` compares through the parameter (`(char*)a0 + 0x30`) drops it to 127). In this case the move
alone already ordered them correctly; check `>>>active<<<{expr|n} LR reg` in the dump. Result: prefetch a0, destination
a1, src v1 -- the target's three registers at the scratch site (11 rows gone).

**3. Same idea, chain site 4 (still open).** The two chain site-4 destinations (delta_b_dst / delta_g_dst) colour a0
(target a1) with forbidden [v0 v1]; nothing visible holds a0 there in the target. Tried: do-while splits at every
statement of both chains (94 singles, flat); merging the site-4 destinations with scratch_dst (merged LR 2.5 = 45 / 18 --
the per-ref weight is NOT constant, so don't extrapolate), with / without do-while at site 4 (that also splits the
accel_params LR: 2.5 -> 2.0), with / without the `+ 0 * child_flags` lever: all lower. A destination use in the alloc call
block (to make a0 = 12 forbidden) is copy-propagated to p (or constant-propagated to &scratch_xz) and never extends it.

**4. Negatives on 591C (all at target length).** Axis-load order (x first) with every permutation of 6 float variables x
`if (1) {}` position (720 variants) / 9 variables (1008): order fixes but colours move, best 99.84. Prefetch as a named
variable assigned in each arm (+ default): the src addition sinks below the alloc and the variable spills (99.47). Dropping
the `sub` variable for direct `self->0x30` expressions (per region / all): one long expression LR coloured a2 with a0
copies, 95.9-99.6. Self/a0 spelling flips of the 17 self->0x30 reads (singles + pairs, 153): flat except the known axis_src
one. Alternative null-guard shapes (`if (dst == 0) dst = alloc(); if (dst)`: prefetch a0 but src / dst swap; ternary,
comma forms): lower. Small rows: `0x10000 == v0`, mul operand swap, other counter / selector variables: flat.

**5. 38A28.** Case 0x65 stores `*p` through `key` (`key = *p; o->0xC = key;`): the target's a3 value register and the
shifted t-ring line up (92.59 -> 93.33). Left: `code` colours a3 (target v0) because the cursor web (6.0) takes v0 first;
counted uses of `code` in any case / the default call: flat.

**6. Checked, nothing found:** 41D40 (NCC, 99.90): 62 next()/condition spellings, the bottom copy's array temp stays a1
(target v1). 97EC (NCC): declarator / copy-init forms of e / f don't reorder the two edg temp homes. 0B3C: the 4-entry
table is the known cfe cap (kit CXL); `default:` instead of the phantom `case 4:` drops the table.

## kit CXCI (agent-g 2026-10-28, run 209): **the `- live bb -` 4th column is a CALL-ARGUMENT register preference: an LR that is moved into an argument register colours that register, else the next free argument register above it, and is left UNCOLOURED (never v0 / v1) when a0..a3 are all forbidden -- post0b 38A28 EXACT by steering two preferences (default's third argument through the case cursor `p` -> a2; selector copied and killed before the call -> no preference -> v0); zero-use-sweep fixes (goto-aware def check, member names / labels / aggregates, multi-line macros) give 591C +0.01 and post 2E354 93.29 -> 93.79** <a name="kit-cxci-agent-g-run-209"></a>

_One exact: gl_func_00038A28 (post0b, 324 B) 93.33334 -> 100.0 (donor splice, jumptable pinned at RoData +0x1A1C).
report.json: game_uso_func_0000591C 99.89387 -> 99.90302 (4372 = target), gl_func_0002E354 93.28882 -> 93.7937
(NM 3692 -> 3688 bytes, target 3684); 83.42 -> 83.46 % code, 3195 -> 3196 exact. post0b NM clip unchanged 0x2eacc. (CXC was already taken by agent-c run 206.)_

**1. Reading the column.** In the zdbug:5 dump each `- live bb - <bb> <refs> <x> <reg>` row's last number is the
register the LR's value is passed in at a call in that block (same numbering as the colour column: 3 = a0, 4 = a1,
5 = a2, 6 = a3), 0 = none. An LR with such a preference does not take the lowest free register: it takes the preferred
one, or the next free ARGUMENT register above it (38A28: `code`, preference a1, forbidden [a0 a1 a2] -> a3; key,
preference a1, forbidden [v0 a0 a1] -> a2). With a0..a3 all forbidden it is NOT given v0 / v1 / a t-register: it stays
uncoloured (`>>>active<<<{1015|0} 0 -1`, a stack home + reloads, +4..+20 bytes) even though the forbidden set printed
only a-registers. So a target that holds a call argument's source value in v0 had no preference on that LR.

**2. Steering it.**
- To put an LR in aN, give it a use as the N-th argument of a call inside its live range. 38A28's default called
  `report(fmt, code, o->0xC)`; writing `p = *(int **)(o + 0xC); report(fmt, x, p);` gave the case cursor variable `p`
  (one LR over every case arm) preference a2, so all case cursors coloured a2 and the key value (preference a1, a1
  forbidden by the param) moved up to a3 -- the target's pair. The case-0x64 cursor was a different register in the
  target (a3), i.e. a different variable: that arm reads its cursor through `key` (`key = c->4; c->4 = key + 4;
  o->0x20 = *(int *)key;`).
- To REMOVE a preference, end the web at a plain copy before the call and kill the original:
  `key = code; code = 0; report(fmt, key, p);`. The dead `code = 0` keeps uopt from propagating the copy, so the selector
  web stops at the copy (no argument use, colours v0 = lowest free) and the copy's web (`key`, already a3 elsewhere)
  supplies a1 via `or a1,v0,zero` in the delay slot -- the target's exact shape. `x | 0` and `+ 0` are folded and do
  not do this; a second named variable for the copy (`k = code; code = 0;`) also works but needs its own frame slot.
- Side facts from the same function: the selector as a plain `switch (*(int *)c)` expression (no named variable) gave
  97.2 on its own but still got the a1 preference through the default's `*(int *)c`; the p assignment and the call
  had to share ONE source line for as1 to order `lui a0; addiu a0; lw a2,12(s0)` (separate lines: `lw a2` between the
  lui / addiu, 94.9 -> 99.8 on one line); `int code = 0;` or `pad[5]` restored the 64-byte frame when the variable
  was dropped.

**3. Landing.** cfe jumptable in post0b = the 52CD4 / 3AC5C donor recipe (docs/MATCHING_WORKFLOW.md#post0b-jumptable-
donor-52cd4): donor `game_libs_o2_38A28.c` (in the C_FILES filter-out), `GAMELIBS_38A28_DONOR` + `private
REPLACE_FUNC_BODY +=` after the post0b `:=` line, placeholder body in post0b.c, pin `gl_func_00038A28_rodata =
0x00001A1C;` (the target's `lw t6,0x1A1C(at)`). The three message addresses were already pinned (D_0001EC6C ...); the
callbacks are `jal 0` in the ROM (0-pinned gl_func_00000000). ROM byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6.

**4. scripts/zero-use-sweep.py fixes (monorepo, uncommitted).** Run 208's "284 / 461 --exprs variants failed" were
script bugs, not compiler limits: (a) member names (`.y`, `->x`) and goto labels were taken as variables (`+ 0 *
(int)(y)`: 604 of 638 failures on 591C); (b) aggregate copies (`*(Tri3i *)&a = ...`, `stage = *p` with Vec3) got a
`+ 0 * x` appended; (c) an `=` inside a condition (`if (!((v0 = x) & 1)) goto L;`) was taken as a statement; (d) Vec3
locals were in the vocabulary; (e) `--exprs` read `a * x` as a dereference `*x`; (f) multi-line `#define`s with braces
broke the other-function reduction (fell back to whole-file compiles: post 2E354). Also: (g) the def check rejected
EVERY local of a function containing `goto` -- it now rejects only when a label sits between the assignment and the
site (591C, 0B3C and 2E354 were effectively unswept for locals); (h) variants are built in the workers from a
(kind, pos, text) edit instead of holding every 800 KB file text in the parent (the 3500-variant 591C run sat at 6 GB).
591C after the fixes: 3363 local variants, none above base; `*a0` on the proximity accel gate condition flips one
mul.s operand order (99.894 -> 99.903, kept). 0B3C: 2618 variants, flat. 2E354: three greedy rounds (arg0 on the 0x32
countdown store 93.63, `*arg0` on the recomposed (u32) conversion 93.79 at 3688 toward 3684). The third round's only
hits (94.01) were `+ 0 * (int)(D_E354_1C330[temp_v1_2])`, a float-table read at an index the table may not cover --
not kept. Variants that moved AWAY from the target length (3704) were skipped as the policy says.

**5. Negatives.** 591C chain site-4 destinations (still a0, target a1): the destination LR has no argument preference
and is coloured early (2.5) with only [v0 v1] forbidden, so a0 is lowest free; nothing in the target holds a0 there.
A destination use in the alloc call (`alloc(0xC + 0 * (int)dst)`) is copy-propagated (flat); making the copy
`(Vec3 *)((int)p | 0)` drops 8 bytes (97.2). 250C8: moving the FinishAsyncLoad locals into the `bytesRemaining == 0`
block: flat. 41D40 / 3DF58 / BB8C: the remaining register swaps are not argument-preference cases (no call in the LR).

Most a-register rows sit in functions that also have insert/delete rows (2E354, 30AF4, 7C1C); the pure-register ones (41D40, 250C8, 3DF58, 3E5E0, 34890, 3AE58, gui 329C) did not move under hand-made hint variants (copy-then-zero, `+ 0`, block-scoped copies, member / free inline spellings).

**What paid: `scripts/zero-use-sweep.py --exprs` on the NCC donors, stacked.** Each pass applies the best SAME-LENGTH (or toward-target length) hit, then re-sweeps; a second or third pass often finds a bigger hit than the first (3BE1C +0.9, +0.7, +0.2, +0.08; 3B9C0 +0.15, then +1.2 on the next line). report.json before -> after:

| function | bytes | before | after | terms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| game_uso 7C1C | 4284 | 95.26 | 96.31 | `n = n->next + 0 * (int)(n->next)`; alias copy `a + 0 * (int)(out)`; compare `+ 0 * (int)(n2.z)` |
| post0b 3BE1C | 1568 | 95.48 | 97.33 | cc / va / vb / `*list` (length 1556 -> 1568 = target) |
| post0b 3B9C0 | 1116 | 92.55 | 93.96 | self->tris, self_al->tris, i |
| gui 3714 | 1024 | 96.51 | 97.41 | `h = spr->h + 0 * (int)(spr->w)`, `w = arg4 + 0 * (int)(arg4)` |
| post0b 3C43C | 872 | 96.08 | 96.78 | `best = i + 0 * (int)(r)` (868 -> 872 = target) |
| post0b 3B6A0 | 800 | 95.80 | 96.25 | inside, off (796 -> 800 = target), cc->remap, c |
| post0b 3B2EC | 948 | 96.05 | 96.36 | col->nrm, col->grid->cells (list() already reads it) |
| post 415A4 (cfe) | 452 | 93.38 | 94.44 | `t->a4 = 2 + 0 * (int)(t->v30)` (array ADDRESS, no read) |
| game_uso BB8C | 1008 | 98.50 | 98.52 | obj->sub on the early-return test |

Notes: (1) a parameter folded into its OWN copy (`w = arg4 + 0 * (int)(arg4)`) is a valid counted use and moved 3714. (2) `0 * (int)(float)` is zero code when the float is already in a register for the same statement (7C1C: no cvt emitted, FP colouring only) but not in general (kit CC: +4 bytes); check the disassembly, and only use it on bounded values. Prefer adding the term to an INT expression before an int -> float conversion (3B9C0 `sg = s8 + 0 * ...`), never `f + 0 * ...` on a float (IDO keeps `x + 0.0f`). (3) Read the sweep's `L<n>` as the source line of the statement it edits, not of a neighbour -- one misplacement here (`lo` instead of `ok = 0`) gave 96.45 / 1572 instead of 97.05 / 1564; always re-sweep after an edit, the new base exposes it. (4) The in-tree cfe sweeps (2D374, 40304, B3C, 30AF4, 31A74, 469A8, 396FC, 35B1C, 250C8) were flat; the donor sweeps of 2DE0, 329C, 0F04, 4568 (needs `--flags ... -I src/gui_uso` for its quoted gbi header), 46790, 37540, 42938, 36694, 33094, 37938, 1DDC, 97EC, 3AE58, 3E5E0 were flat; 34890 has no non-inline sites.

Not moved by: first() / next() exchange, single function-scope `n`, for-init declarations, copy-then-zero of the a1 parameter, folded terms on best / return / loop heads.
- 97EC / 1DDC (99.97, NCC): two EDG temporaries' frame homes are exchanged (97EC: the `(a - b) * k` product temp and the `pos - pos` difference temp). Block nesting, reference-bound or named Vec3 temporaries, NRV operators, free operators and by-value XZ constructors all reorder other homes or grow the frame.

## kit CCIII (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 213): structural pass -- trailing empty blocks un-colour a loop-invariant address (65494), a by-value operator returning `T(a, b, c)` evaluates every component before the temp stores; negatives on 8FC8 / 4C5E4 / 65EE4 / 18F0 / 5A2C4 / 4A890 <a name="kit-cciii-agent-c-run-213"></a>

**65494 (post1b, NCC donor) 91.75 -> 98.64, 1336 = target length, mnemonic sequence now identical.**
Two independent fixes:

1. *Trailing `if (1) {}` blocks flip a held address to a spill home.* The target computes
   `self + 0x2FC` once before the loop, stores it to a frame home (`addiu t0,s3,764; sw t0,108(sp)`)
   and reloads it before the one call per iteration; our build gave it `s8` (+1 save word, every
   later s-register and FP temp shifted). Three or more `if (1) {}` at the very end of the
   function (after the last call, nothing for as1 to schedule across) raise uopt's basic-block
   count, which raises the callee-saved cost (kit run 111: firstUseCost = 0.25 x BBs, clamped
   4..60) above the cost of a home + reload, so the address drops out of colouring -- exactly
   the target's shape. 1-2 blocks do nothing, 3-32 all give the same result. The same sweep
   (1/2/4/8/16 trailing blocks) over 26 other NCC donors and 19 cfe NM bodies in agent-c's
   range found nothing else: the lever only applies where a value is coloured callee-saved in
   the build but home-spilled in the target.
2. *By-value operator* evaluation order.* `Vec3 operator*(float s) const { Vec3 r; r.x = x * s;
   r.y = y * s; r.z = z * s; return r; }` interleaves load / mul / store; the target loads all
   three components, issues the three `mul.s`, then the three `swc1` into the return temp.
   `return Vec3(x * s, y * s, z * s);` (constructor parameters are evaluated before any member
   store, same rule as the inline-set() form of kit CXXXI) reproduces it and restores the
   target's load-delay nop (1332 -> 1336 bytes). The `r.set(...)` member form adds three words
   here; the named-ctor form `Vec3 r(x * s, ...)` is identical to the return-ctor form.
   Left: frame 384 vs 392 (block-temp homes shifted by 4-8 bytes; unused class objects and
   arrays are dropped by NCC, so pads do not move them), the operator- sub / store interleave,
   and an s1/s2/s3 permutation of self / &d / &node->v120.

**Negatives / diagnoses (no source change kept):**

- *8FC8 (timproc_b5, NCC donor 91.51).* The four S70 row blocks: the target holds `o = m38` in a
  caller-saved `v1` saved / restored around EVERY call (`sw v1,224(sp)` in each jal delay, `lw`
  after), the new-expression result in `s0` and the base-ctor `this` in `s1`, and rematerialises
  `&import_80020098` per block. The NCC body gives `o` one home (284), np `s1`, bp `a2`
  (spilled), and holds `&import_80020098` in `s0` across all four blocks. Writing the blocks as
  the explicit `NEWS70` alloc / test / init macro DOES reproduce the per-block `lui v0` remat and
  the target's `lui; lui; addiu; addiu` vtable/name pair, but np coalesces with the long-lived
  row variable (homed) and the score drops to 88.3; a function-scope np takes a fourth s-reg
  (87.5). The cfe C body (in-tree, 86.64, 1603 words) already has the `v1` spill-around-call
  shape for `o` and the jumptable -- the target is cfront output compiled by cfe -- but differs in
  many small places. Trailing-BB counts 1..64 inert on this function. WB / WC's kid loop: the
  target keeps a `blez` guard on the stored count (`n = 1`), `n = 1; if (1) {}` reproduces it
  (+2 words toward the target, 6468 -> 6476 of 6496) but the counter then spills (a2 at 116)
  where the target colours it s0: fuzzy 91.030 -> 91.024, not kept.
  The three W16C `pos` zeros: the target materialises three separate `mtc1 zero` and stores x,
  y, z in order; every spelling tried (int / unsigned / short / char seti params, float locals,
  `if (1) {}` between stores, direct int-literal stores, a `V3 *p` walk, V3 temporaries) gives
  one shared zero (or `$f20`) with stores in z, y, x order.
- *4C5E4 (post0b, NCC donor 88.29 standalone).* The viewport block materialises 2.0f twice
  (`lui at,0x4000` at 0x1E4 and 0x24C, two `mtc1`) while 4.0f is held in f18; NCC CSEs both
  2.0f uses. `int two = 2` turns `y * 2` into `add.s y, y` (worse).
- *65EE4 (post1b, -O2 -Olimit 1 donor 89.73).* IDO 5.3 at -O1 / -O2 / -O2 -Olimit 1 gives the
  same bytes as 7.1; a `Save65EE4 *g` local or a named `int b` both lose. The residual call-2/3
  argument order (target `lui a1` before `lui a0`) is the a1-load-first emission of a memory
  argument.
- *18F0 (kernel, cfe 89.19).* The peel copy's `bnezl found, store+4; b next` (store block after
  an unconditional jump) and the hoisted `-9` mask register are not reproduced by any of:
  `if (found) {...}`, if/else, goto, `while (found) {...; break;}`, `found == 1`, a mask local,
  IDO 5.3 -O1/-O2/-O3/-g3; lever-sweep all: nothing.
- *5A2C4 (post0b, cfe 90.47).* The colour block is word-identical to the target in mnemonics;
  the residual is the target's live-range split of the three surviving `(u32)(c * 255.0f)` temps
  (spill 0x20 / `or t1,t6` / `or a1,t7` at the merge), which in turn moves sp2C / sp30 from
  0x24 / 0x20 to 0x2C / 0x30 and the call's outgoing-arg stores. Named u32 r/g/b/a locals: no
  change; s32: much worse.
- *4A890 (post0b, NCC 93.28).* The target copies `ids` into `s0` at entry (`or s0,a2,zero`,
  then `end = s0 + 2n`, then `s0 = &list`), i.e. one variable that is the id copy and later the
  list base; every spelling (copy before the `n > 0` test, explicit `s = list` reuse, non-
  volatile byte size) compiles to the same bytes -- edg / uopt copy-propagate the copy away.

## kit CCIV (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 211): structural pass -- kit CCIII trailing blocks crack a copied loop-end constant (3B2EC 96.36 -> 99.92, length = target), edg temp-slot layout steered by named expression temps and reference-parameter helpers (37938 every slot = target), a char-prototyped callee alias for a re-extended char argument (31A74 length + frame = target) <a name="kit-cciv-agent-g-run-211"></a>

**3B2EC (NCC donor, `int Obj::height`).** Ours saved s8 and kept the post-loop `k != 3` end constant as a register copy of the inner loop end (`or s6, s0, zero`); the target rematerialises it (`lui t7; addiu t7, 6` before the `bnel`) and saves s0-s7 only. Two `if (1) {}` after the outer `while` (before `return cnt;`) flip it: 952 -> 948 bytes = target. One block does nothing, two to four give the same code, six or more break it. The donor then needed 13 unused volatiles (not 10) to keep the 0x98 frame, because the s8 save area was gone. After the structural fix, re-check every earlier counted-use lever: the run-210 `(list == 0) + 0 * (int)(cells)` and `+ 0 * (int)(col->nrm)` terms each became a loss (dropping them gave +0.5 and +0.1). Two more pure-spelling fixes: `return cx + cz * w;` (target `addu a0, cx, prod`; the IDO addu operand order follows the source here) and `int off = i * 12;` instead of `((i << 2) - i) << 2`. The multiply's shift expansion builds the value in the destination s-register (`sll s2; subu s2, s2, a0; sll s2`), where the hand-written shifts go through a t temp. 99.92 standalone. Residual (3 words): the loop-bottom `*list++` cursor copy is in v0 (target t4, the register f also uses). Neutral: do-while / goto / for(;;) rewrites, s16 / u32 `i`, counted uses on the condition, f at function scope, decl orders.
Trailing blocks did nothing on 3B9C0, 3BE1C, 3B6A0, 3C43C, 36694, 36F0C, 7C1C, 8CD8, 2DE0, 3714, 42938 or 33094, and they hurt 46050, 454C4 and 3558. cfe (in-tree 2E354, 30AF4) ignores them. The lever applies when OUR build has an extra callee-saved register the target lacks.

**37938 (NCC donor, push-apart).** Frame slots are allocated in edg temp creation order, so they can be moved with temps that emit no code. (1) Naming the scalar inside the expression, `arg = (b - a) * (kk = o->k);`, inserts its slot between `arg` and operator-'s ctor and return temps and moves them 8 down to the target's sp+0x78 / 0x84. A separate `kk = o->k;` statement moves the load and is worse. A `volatile int pad;` in the same place gives the same slots. (2) A by-value `operator=(V3 v) { set(v); }` with `set(const V3 &)` adds the reference temp below the by-value parameter, which moves the parameter up to the target's sp+0x24. (3) Dropping the named `f32 k = s` in operator* restores the 0xD8 frame. The s reload through an inline `Ctx::getOut()` (the 3558 kit) gives the target's `lw vN, 200(sp); addiu a0, vN, 48` form instead of `lw a0; addiu a0, a0`, but only with an `if (1) {}` after the arg statement. Without it, sp+0x54 is hoisted into v1. Residual: the reload lands in v0 (target v1). A 256-variant grid of gp / getPos / if (0) / Ctx const / named n / statement order / pad, ring-burn counted uses, member-call `this` forms, trailing blocks and in-arm BB splits never reached v1. The coloring dump shows the copy-chain address webs (sp+0x84, sp+0x54) colored v0 as uopt candidates. The getOut temp must lose priority to sp+0x54 in the same block, and no spelling here does that.

**31A74 (in-tree cfe).** The target's `lb a2, 35(sp)` followed by a `sll / sra 24` re-extension of the char argument at the call means the callee is ANSI-prototyped with a `signed char` parameter. A per-site alias `extern int gl_func_00000000_c(int, s8);` (pinned to 0) reproduces it. A trailing `if (r) {}` had kept r live across the call (frame 0x20, target 0x18). Moving `sel += 63` above the `mode == 255` test puts the addiu in the bne delay slot, as in the target. 560 -> 564 bytes = target; 90.73 -> 91.55. Residual: the `ACC = r` store is scheduled before the arg `mfc1` (the target stores after it), and the late `sll / sra` of sel.

**Negatives / diagnoses.** 3B9C0 (-20 bytes): all blocks line up; the gap is the target's `off` spill (sw / lw a1, 0x80(sp)), its f24 save, and a materialised `&D` (lui / addiu a2). All are register-pressure effects, not structure. 46050 (-8): the target keeps `&D` (margin) in s8 and rematerialises `lui at, 0xE400`; ours holds the 0xE4000000 constant in s8. Insensitive to the margin spelling, the E4 operand order, a named e4, or the position of the B3-word local. 3558: target matrix rows run x, y, z, with vb kept in registers through `+=` and `-`. The x, y, z row order lines up the block, but every vb rewrite loses the r temp chain (-20pp). 30AF4: the case-5 constants 13 / 14 / 16 live in a0 / v1 webs in the target; u32-typed c13 / c14 gets 14 into a register (2132 -> 2128 bytes) but scores lower. gui 4568 (+4): the target symbol ends at `jr ra` because the delay slot `addiu sp, sp, 8` (0x27BD0008 at ROM 0x591DB0) sits in the gui_uso_post bin. That is a splat boundary to fix (c segment end 0x591DB0 -> 0x591DB4), not a code difference.

## kit CCV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 214): NCC frame-home fitting on post1b 65494 -- every stack home and the s-register permutation exact, 98.64 -> 99.91 <a name="kit-ccv-agent-c-run-214"></a>

**Method (fast loop).** Compile the donor standalone with the matching NCC line, objdump the function, and
compare against the expected object with three scores: exact line LCS, LCS with sp offsets masked (= register
diffs only), and LCS with registers masked (= structure). Then list the homes: `-Wo,-zdbug:6` with the dump NCC
and grep `isvar M <size> <off>` (off is from the frame top, `vreg` = register candidate), plus a positional
map target-offset -> our-offset over the aligned listing. Fix the frame from the top down: named block homes
first, then the edg temp area.

**Rules confirmed on 65494** (each step kept only when the scores rose; objdiff in-tree in brackets):
1. Named locals home top-down in declaration order, function scope first, then the loop block. Register-only
   scalars still take a home, so a home can be moved by moving a scalar's DECLARATION: `float f` hoisted from
   the `if (count)` block to function scope, and `float h, w, dt` declared before `Vec3 n, d, hit` in the loop
   block, put n / d / hit on the target's 0x134 / 0x128 / 0xF8 (frame 384 -> 392 with `Vec3 &operator=`).
2. A 3-float ctor forwarding to `set(a, b, c)` instead of member stores fixed the s1 / s2 / s3 permutation
   (self / return slot / &node->v120) [99.41].
3. `operator-` as `return Vec3(...)` (ctor -> set) plus the loop-head normal as field stores (no set()
   parameter temps above the return slot) put R / op- result on the target [99.44].
4. A real C++ virtual call (`struct NB { char pad[0x28]; 11 dummy virtuals; virtual void contact(...); }`)
   gives `addu a0,t2,s0` where the hand-written `vt[12].fn(vt[12].off + (char *)node, ...)` gave `s0,t2`;
   `nsum /= f` (operator/=) gives the target's y / x / z division schedule where the element-wise spelling
   in any order did not [99.56].
5. A call statement in its own `{ }` homes its reference-bound temp BELOW the earlier statements' bound temps
   (block-level binding temps are otherwise newest-on-top); a NAMED `Vec3 imp = n.sc(...)` in the block took
   the target's bound-temp home directly [99.57].
6. By-value `operator=(Vec3 v) { cp(v); }` with an inline `cp(const Vec3 &)`: cp's this / reference temps are
   homed BELOW the by-value parameter (the target's two unreferenced words under the parameter), as in 63964
   (kit CXV/CXXXI line) [99.59].
7. The temp below an inline's named result (sc's `s` parameter temp) disappears when the argument is an
   assignment to a named scalar `n.sc(k = ...)` with k declared in the loop block; `nsum /= (float)count`
   (no named f) removes another; a `const Vec3 &ri = imp;` passed to the call adds one pointer home right
   below imp: with these every sp offset and the frame match [99.70].
8. `float dot() { float r = ...; return r; }` leaves r as a PHANTOM FP LR coloured f0 (dt then f2);
   `const Vec3 &u = *this; return u.x * v.x + ...` keeps the home without the phantom (dt f0 as target) [99.76].
9. One `if (1) {}` after the dt clamp (BB split before the impulse) swaps the k / w colour order: k f14,
   w f16 as in the target [99.91].

**Left (6 words):** the three operator* products colour f0 / f2 / f12 vs the target's f2 / f12 / f14 -- the
target has an f0 holder live across the products. Making operator*'s `s` a parameter temp (`* (0, w)`,
`* -h`, `float t = s`, `if (0) { s = 0; }`) does produce exactly that phantom (products f2 / f12 / f16) but
adds a float home and reschedules the whole function (length 333, frame 400): not the target's spelling.
Negatives: statement order of nsum / count / w / psum / wsum, element-wise nsum +=, minv forms, op* spellings
(named r, set(), field stores, s * x), plain ctor for op* only (products become ugen temps, still f0..),
`if (1) {}` at every loop-body position. 63964 (99.96): free vs member operator+, by-value / named-result /
reference-local forms of operator+ do not move the op+ reference temps from below X to above T2.

## kit CCVI (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 212): two jr-ra delay-slot boundary fixes (gui 4568 delay word in the tail bin, post0b 37938 delay nop emitted by an 8-byte `_pad.s` block); the NCC reused edg temp is ONE uopt LR (3B2EC cursor copy, 37938 final reload diagnosed); 97EC temp-order negatives <a name="kit-ccvi-agent-g-run-212"></a>

**Boundary class: a NM donor's last word scored as an INSERT = the function `.s` stops at `jr ra`.**
Two instances this run, both legal boundary fixes with ROM byte-identical:

- *gui_func_00004568* (96.01 -> 96.53, 792 -> 796 B): the delay slot `addiu sp,sp,8` at ROM 0x591DB0
  sat at the start of the `gui_uso_post` bin (the USO's own section header says text size 0x4880, i.e.
  the original tool counted the delay word outside .text, which is why splat ended the c segment there).
  Fix: yaml tail bin -> 0x591DB4 under a NEW name (`gui_uso_tail`, bin force-added) so other checkouts
  don't link their stale untracked `gui_uso_post.bin`; `.s` + the word; TRUNCATE_TEXT +4; expected/
  .text grown by 4 bytes. Growing an expected `.o`'s .text: `objcopy --update-section` DROPS the
  relocations -- instead append the new .text bytes at EOF and repoint the section header (sh_offset /
  sh_size), leaving .mdebug's internal file offsets untouched, then patch the symbol sizes; build it in
  /tmp and `cp` it over.
- *gl_func_00037938* (98.71 -> 99.88, 340 -> 344 B): the `.s` ended at `jr ra` (0x154) and the
  one-word `gl_func_00037938_pad.s` GLOBAL_ASM block emitted EIGHT bytes (asm-processor pads a 1-word
  block), silently covering both the delay nop and the real alignment word. Fix: delay nop into the
  `.s` (0x158), pad pragma + `_pad.s` removed, `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE += gl_func_00037938=0x00000000`
  (+ NM mirror), expected symbols resized in place; the NM object shrinks 4 (old 2-word block vs the
  1-word suffix) so the post0b NM clip moves -4 and gains a `gl_func_00037938=0x158` symbol trim (the
  NM suffix otherwise lands inside the symbol). Scan: `tailscan.py`-style check of every 80-99.99
  function's last three objdiff rows for an INSERT/DELETE found no other case in game_uso / gui /
  post / post0b<0x48000.

**NCC reused edg temp = one LR, so its colour is set by its WHOLE union of pieces.** zdbug:1 shows edg
reusing one `M` temp (3B2EC: M -84, 13 versions -- inline `this` copies, the `list()` result, the
`*list++` old-value copy, the `cnt++` old-value copy; 37938: M -60, `&c`, `o->s`, the `getOut()`
result) and coloring-solve shows a single LR for it. Consequences found:
- 3B2EC (still 99.92): the loop-bottom cursor copy is that temp (ours v0 = first free at ord 13). For the
  target's t4 the copy must interfere with every v0..t3 owner, and those are exactly the inner edge-loop
  LRs (v0 / v1 vertex pointers, a0 / a1 halfword loads, a2 / a3 dx / dz, t0 / t1 ex / ez, t2 the vi
  walk, t3 the next-index table) -- while the entry copy stays v0. So in the original the copy shares
  a variable with something live across the edge loop but not past it (the face pointer f is the only
  such value and is t4 in both). Not reproduced. Negatives (all 4 words or worse): for-loop init/incr
  (identical: edg reuses the same temp), explicit pre-test + bottom statement (entry schedule moves),
  named cursor q (copy coalesces at entry, 236 words; bottom q goes v1), q shared with the face pointer
  (still v0), `Face &` / `const Face *` / `Face *const` f, unnamed remap in face(), s16 i, const list,
  `cnt++` split (moves the cnt copy, cursor copy still v0), an inline `Face::edges()` holding the edge
  loop (edg does not inline a function with a loop: emits a call), single `if (1) {}` at every body line,
  face() moved into the edge loop's for-init (`for (f = col->face(i), k = 0; ...)`: the whole temp
  web swaps v0 / v1, copy v1, 37 words; `vt` in the same init too: unchanged 4 words; `Face *f` declared
  in the for-init: 240 words).
- 37938 (99.88): the final `c.getOut()->m30` reload is in the M -60 temp LR (v0); target v1. A member
  returning `char *` (`c.m30()`) makes a separate return temp but it takes a0 (argument preference) and
  evicts o to a1 (30 words). Evaluating the reload before `o->k` via a named `Node *n` copy-propagates
  from the entry `o->s` load (no reload, n in v1 -- the colour the target wants, but not its reload);
  `if (0) { gl(&a, &b, &c); }`, `Node * volatile out`, call-argument comma forms (frame +24) all worse.
- game_uso 97EC (6 words, e-bound / f-bound temp homes swapped): f in a nested block (frame +8),
  reference casts on either ctor argument, copy-init `XZ e = ...` (identical), `XZ f = XZ(...)` (+8
  words), a named `Vec3 te` for e all negative.
- post0b 41D40 (99.90, bottom next()'s array load a1, target v1 = the entry next()'s result register, so
  in the original the two share a pooled edg temp): extra folded `+ 0` on the result / index / array /
  condition, `a[0][..]`, `a->data[..]`, a named `r`, `idx += 1` / `idx = idx + 1`, and an `if (1) {}` /
  `if (0) {}` / `{}` at every body line all negative.

## kit CCVII (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 215): an inline operator's PARAMETER TEMP is a zero-code f0 phantom -- post1b 65494 EXACT (99.91 -> 100); 63964 / 65EE4 negatives <a name="kit-ccvii-agent-c-run-215"></a>

**1. 65494 closed.** Kit CCV left the first `operator*` products in f0 / f2 / f12 where the target has
f2 / f12 / f14: some floating LR holds f0 across the three `mul.s` with no instruction of its own. That LR is
operator*'s float parameter when the argument is a non-trivial expression: `psum += node->v120 * -h` (with
`w = -h` still named for `wsum += w`, and the impulse spelled `k = -h * self->f290 + ...`). edg makes a
parameter temp `s = -h`, uopt CSEs `-h` with w (neg.s f16 once), and the temp's live range survives as the f0
holder: every register then matches (standalone "reg-only" LCS 335 / 335). It costs one 4-byte home in the edg
temp area (frame 392 -> 400); dropping the run 214 `const Vec3 &u = *this` pointer home from `dot()` (plain
`return x * v.x + y * v.y + z * v.z;`) gives that word back and every sp offset is the target's: 334 / 334
words, ROM byte-identical. Same phantom from `* (w + 0.0f)` and `* -(h)`; NOT from `* +w`, `* (float)w`,
`* *&w`, `* (1 ? w : h)`, `* (w = -h)` (edg passes those as plain operands, no temp).
Method note: the fast standalone loop of kit CCV plus a positional sp-offset map (target offset -> ours over
the aligned listing, grouped by delta) shows where the extra / missing home sits (here: one word right above
the lowest temp, one in the loop block); then look for an existing home whose removal is register-neutral.

**2. 63964 (99.96) negatives, arm 1 only (arms 2 / 3 already match).** uopt expression dump: the op* ctor
products go to pooled float temps (-88 / -92 reused from op-, the third one fresh at -148), and op+'s two
reference-parameter pointer temps are fresh at -168 / -172 below the by-value operator= parameter; the target
has those three fresh words ABOVE the bound copy C. Flat or worse: named `const V3 &` locals for va / n / the
product (frame +8, ptr temps vanish but two words land between R and C), pointer locals, `if (0) { ... }`
pre-statements (edg keeps a branch: +1 word), `(void)(va.y + va.y)`, operator= as field stores / set() /
`V3 &` return / const-ref, operator- as field stores / named r / set(), `V3 n(...)` direct init, `V3 n; n = ...`,
out ctor `(0.0f, ...)`, `va.y + 0.0f` / `(0, va.y)` / `+va.y` / ternary arguments, a block-scope `f32 d = va.y`,
statement order of `count = 1`, removing the `if (1) {}` blocks.

**3. 65EE4 (-Olimit 1, 89.73) is not C++:** an NCC `Save::blk(int, int)` member version holds `&g` in s0 and
stores through it (106 / 123 words at -Olimit 1 / plain -O2 vs 146); the target's `lui at` per store is the cfe
-O1-style fallback. Literal `G.data = 0xB1FF0010` (macro third parameter) still gives `lui t7; ori a2,t7,0x10`.

## kit CCVIII (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 213): whole-project boundary scan finds nothing new; 3B2EC's cursor copy has to share the face-result temp's live range, and edg's temp pool can't be made to give it that slot; 37938's final reload stays in v0 <a name="kit-ccviii-agent-g-run-213"></a>

**Boundary scan (read-only, every non-exact report.json function, 92 of them).** The scan checks four things:
(a) a `.s` whose last text word is `jr ra`; (b) objdiff target vs base size differing by one word; (c) a single
INSERT/DELETE among the first or last three objdiff rows, or exactly one gap row in the whole function; (d) a
`_pad.s` next to the function (odd word count). Results: (a) none among the non-exact functions. Across ALL `.s`
files only seven end at `jr ra`: the sentinels C5B0 / EBC8 / 551E0 / 55B10 (delay words in their pads, on purpose)
and game_libs tail 6C9E4 / 6D94C / 70AE4 (exact). (b)/(c) gave hits only where the code itself differs, not the
boundary: 2E354 (+1 word in our build, register diffs at the tail), game_uso 3558 (an `ldc1 fs0` restore missing,
frame 0x100 vs 0xF0), 36F0C (frame 0x88 vs 0x80), 3430 / 4A890 (prologue order), bootup 6204 / E9FC (an extra
`sw ra`), bootup 6808 (an extra trailing store), C234 / 55A0 / 18F0 / b5 D884 / 4C5E4 (size off by one word, the
diffs spread through the body). (d) found no odd pad next to a non-exact function. Every non-exact function's
expected symbol size matches its `.s` word count (count the `jal` lines that have no `/* addr word */` prefix as
well, or USO functions look short). Run 212's two fixes (gui 4568, post0b 37938) were the only ones in the project.

**3B2EC (99.92): the coloring dump narrows down where the cursor copy has to live.** `-Wo,-zdbug:5` prints the
itab plus each LR's live BBs, forbidden set and register (1 = v0 .. 10 = t3, 11 = t4, 14..21 = s0..s7). The face
result temp (M -88) is t4 in BBs 22-25. BB 25 is the edge loop, and v0..t3 are all live there. The target puts
the loop-bottom `*list++` copy in t4, so that copy has to be in a live range that crosses BB 25 without t4 being
forbidden. Only M -88 itself fits, so in the original the post-increment temp IS the face-result temp (edg pool
slot B). Ours puts it in slot A (M -84, with the `list()` result and face()'s `this` copy, v0). For the copy to land
in slot B, slot A must already be taken when edg allocates it, and none of the ways tried get that:
- argument temps are allocated BEFORE the callee's parameter / `this` temps (`rd(this, list++)` with
  `if (0) { o = 0; }`, `col->rd(list++)`, `Col::rd(col, list++)`: the copy only moves to v1, 37 words);
- a reference or pointer-to-pointer helper (`nextIdx(list)`, `it.next()`) takes list's address, so list gets a
  stack home (238 words);
- edg will not inline a function that contains a loop (kit CCVI), so the loop can't be put inside an inline
  body that holds a `this` temp;
- for-init / for-step, `for (int i = ...)`, do-while with its own pre-test, the step written inside the body's
  scope with gotos, declaration-initialized `list` / `cell`, `?:` around the post-increment (non-constant
  conditions add code, constant ones fold), `*&*list++`, a cursor q or the face pointer f shared with the
  cursor (copy-propagated back to the temp, or a separate web in v1), and five face() spellings (named `Col *c`,
  if/else into a named f, no named r) all stay at the same 4 words or get worse. A named pointer local adds one
  frame word (drop one of the 13 volatiles to compensate when testing).
- `col->face(i + 0)` (by-value parameter temp, the kit CCVII lever) shifts the pool and costs 18 words.

**37938 (99.88): the final reload.** The coloring dump: the getOut() result (M -60, or M -68 when it goes through
a wrapper) is v0 because no v0 live range shares its BB (12). The sp+0x54 address (595) is the v0 range in BB 11.
Reloading into a named `Node *n` / `char *m` before the `if (1) {}` puts it in BB 11. But `m` takes a0
(argument preference, 8 words). A named `n` lets code motion hoist the sp+0x54 address into v1 at entry (52 words),
the same as dropping the `if (1) {}` (46 words). Inline wrappers that pass the reload as a parameter temp
(`fin(c.getOut(), &arg)` with or without `if (0) { n = 0; }` / an inner `if (1) {}`), Ctx::fire(&arg), returning the
callee's value, `+ 0` on either argument, and operator= / set() spellings are all inert (2 words) or worse.

## kit CCIX (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 216): post0b 4A890 parameter-in-s0 from entry (93.48 -> 94.73); timproc_b5 D884 / DF14 EE6C flag chain is NOT volatile (IDO volatile never emits the direct `lui rd; lw rd,%lo(rd)` form) and no cfe/NCC spelling found; bootup C234 C++ port gets frame / top homes exact but scores below the C body <a name="kit-ccix-agent-c-run-216"></a>

**1. 4A890 (NCC NM donor, 93.48 -> 94.73, 344 -> 348 bytes, target 352).** The target's leading
`or s0,a2,zero` (s0 then reused for the list base after the loop) is the PARAMETER's live range in a callee-
saved register: the loop walks a COPY (`s = ids; ... *s ... s++ ... while (s != end)`) and the end pointer is
computed from the parameter (`end = ids + n`; `n + ids` gives the same bytes). Walking `ids` itself and
taking `end` from the copy (the old body) leaves the copy in a t-register and no early s0. Still left: the
byte size `t0 * 2` that the target holds in s1 across alloc + copy (ours: volatile home reload, or with a plain
`s32 sz` the value colours a2 and is spilled around the call / re-derived from t0's home); flat:
`t0 + t0`, `t0 << 1`, `sizeof(s16) * t0`, unsigned, function-scope / register sz, typed alloc / copy
prototypes, `new s16[t0]` through an inline operator new (94.11 at best).

**2. D884 / DF14 flag chain (96.65 / 96.31): what the target is NOT.** The residual is one block: six
read-modify-writes of `import_8005EE6C + 4` where every load is a fresh direct access (`lui tN; lw tN,4(tN)`),
every store keeps its own `lui at` (shared only between adjacent stores with no `$at` clobber -- as1 tracks
`$at` per symbol inside a block), and each load follows the previous store. Probed (standalone file with the
D884 body, `-S` and objdump):
- `volatile` in every form (scalar at offset 0, struct member, `*(volatile s32 *)`, array, per-site distinct
  volatile scalars): IDO 7.1 and 5.3 ALWAYS materialise `la reg; lw 0(reg)` for a volatile access (`.set
  volatile` around the access in `-S`), even for a single-use symbol: +1 word per access. So the target is
  non-volatile.
- non-volatile, one symbol: uopt forwards every stored value (only the reload after an aliasing pointer
  store survives) and CSEs the address into a register; mixing access forms on the same symbol (struct
  member vs cast arithmetic vs scalar vs array) is canonicalised by cfe -- still forwarded.
- per-site distinct symbols (the current body): direct form, but as1 hoists each load above the previous
  store (different symbols = independent; `-S` shows source order, the hoist is as1's) and adjacent stores
  can't share `lui at`.
- NCC bitfields: word RMWs (not cfe's byte RMWs) but forwarded, and a 1-bit set is `and ~m; or m`.
- C++ inline `clr()/set()` members on a global object: the first two loads stay separate (like the target's
  L1/L2), the rest forwarded.
- the whole C body under NCC: 76.6 (the cfe-tuned volatile/pad homes don't transfer); with one volatile
  symbol the LDA live range spans the switch and is rematerialised after every case's calls (`lui/addiu t0`).
So the target needs an address that is non-volatile, never forwarded and never CSE'd -- no source form found.
`if (1) {}` between the statements is inert here.

**3. bootup C234 (95.07) as real C++: frame and top homes exact, score lower (94.69).** The m2c names map
onto target homes exactly (spCC 204, spB4 180 = the shared copy temp, sp8C 140, sp7C 124, sp68 / sp40 = the
two `operator*` results 104 / 64, sp54 84 = the by-value `operator=` parameter shared by both arms, sp3C 60).
NCC home order observed with `-Wo,-zdbug:6` (`isvar M` offsets): function-scope declarations first (in
declaration order, wherever they appear in the body), then everything else in SOURCE order (block locals,
edg temps, inline locals), so moving a scalar into a `{ }` moves its home to that point in the source. With a
by-value `operator=(V3 o)` (element-wise, no `cp()`), `operator*` as `return V3(a.x * s, ...)` (field-store
forms: 88.6), `V3 p = *(V3 *)(q + 0x30)` copy-constructed in its block, `S4 sp8C` in its block and `var_f2`
wrapped in a block, the frame (248), spCC and spB4 land on the target. Left: the then-branch needs 3 more homes
(target 9 words between spB4 and sp8C, ours 6), the `if (count)` block 4 fewer before the first `operator*`
result and the arms' temp pairs differ (target 2 / 2 / 2 words around X1 / param / X2). Also: the plane test
in the target is `K * (p.x * n.x + (p.y + c) * n.y + p.z * n.z) + 4 > d` with the product in f0 and `d` loaded
last (point-first operands); the C body has normal-first operands and scores higher as it stands.

## kit CCX (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 214): every object of a class with an inline default constructor is an edg basic block, and uopt's callee-saved cost grows with the BB count -- a constructor-less Vec3 brings back game_uso 3558's held $f20 zero; vreg Vec3 locals need no member call on them <a name="kit-ccx-agent-g-run-214"></a>

**game_uso 3558 (NCC donor) 85.86 -> 89.21, two commits.** The target keeps one FP zero in callee-saved
$f20 (`sdc1 $f20` save, `mtc1 zero,$f20` once after the first 070238 call) for the side x / z stores, the w.y
store AND the three live else-branch `mul.s` by zero, and reloads w.y from its home in |w|^2 (x / z come from
registers). Every earlier donor const-propagated the zero per site; the cfe body did hold it, so the spelling
was never the issue.

1. *The BB count decides it.* `-Wo,-zdbug:5` coloring dump: the zero is a constant LR (`{0|n}` in the active
   list). With few BBs it is coloured whole into reg 30 ($f20); with more BBs it is split into per-BB pieces
   and rematerialised. Kit run 111's firstUseCost (0.25 x BBs, clamped 4..60) is the threshold: on one
   reduced body 19 BBs held it and 20 did not (one trailing `if (1) {}` flipped it); on the donor 15-19 hold,
   20 does not. Count BBs from the dump's flow graph (unique node numbers between `flow graph` and the next
   `SECONDS` line; nodes with a non-zero second number are label targets).
2. *Where edg's BBs come from.* Measured on one-statement probes: each OBJECT of a class with a
   user-written inline constructor (`Vec3() {}`, `Ctx(S *s) { ... }`) adds a labelled BB at its declaration
   (moving all declarations to the top does not help -- consecutive empty labelled BBs still count); an
   inline member with a named return object (op- `Vec3 r; ...; return r;`) adds ~2; a by-value copy of a
   local adds 1; `if (1) {}` adds 1 (inside an inline: once per expansion). Plain member functions without
   a return object, member access, `{ }` blocks with declarations, aggregate init (`Ctx c = { s0->node };`)
   add none. The old 3558 donor had 25 BBs; removing both Vec3 constructors and the Ctx constructor gave 15
   and the whole f20 web (zero hold, live muls, w.y reload) came out as in the target.
   Tell: target has an `sdc1 $f20` save and a single `mtc1 zero,$f20` used across calls, ours materialises
   the zero per site -> count the donor's BBs; a class used for many locals must not have a constructor.
3. *Homes, then vreg.* With the BB fix the frame homes were refitted top-down (kit CCV method; `-zdbug:6`
   `isvar M 4 <off>[vreg]` list vs the target's map): three function-scope scalars between e and stage, a
   named matrix block (`M4 *m`, `const Vec3 &v = stage`, named x / y / z) for the 6 temp words between the
   by-value temp and op-'s r, op- computing into named a / b / c after `Vec3 r` for the 4 words between r
   and the binding temp. That reproduced the sp+40/44 spill juggle and mixed `b0+112 / b0+128` then
   `addiu v0,v0,112` addressing (88.56). The target then reloads vb into f14 / f16 / f18 at the top of the
   matrix block and adds each row as it completes: vb (and va) are uopt REGISTER candidates (`vreg` in the
   isvar list). Any member call ON the object or reference parameter bound to it (`vb - va`, `getPos(vb)`)
   goes through an edg this / reference temp and drops the vreg flag; direct field stores plus a free
   by-value `inline Vec3 mk(float, float, float)` (named return -> return temp -> by-value op= binding temp
   -> e: the same r / tmp / bt copy chain as the member op-) made both vreg, frame 256 = target (89.21 with
   one `if (1) {}` after the stage copy).
   Residual (13 words short): the target stores vb after its init and reloads it in the block (split LR;
   ours stays in f14..f18 -- 1..4 `if (1) {}` between init and block do not split it), va.y is coloured f20

## kit CCXII (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 217): a repeated `lui rd; lw rd,%lo(sym)(rd)` / `lui at; sw` chain on ONE symbol = an UNCOLOURED address web: per-pair aliases reused after a call reproduce it -- timproc_b5 D884 (96.98 -> 100) and DF14 (96.44 -> 100) EXACT <a name="kit-ccxii-agent-c-run-217"></a>

Target shape (D884 / DF14 EE6C flag chain): six reads and five writes of `import_8005EE6C + 4` in one
basic block, every read the destructive macro form `lui tN,%hi; lw tN,4(tN)` issued AFTER the
previous store, and two store pairs sharing one `lui at`. What produces each part:

1. *as1 is the scheduler and its alias test is by symbol.* `cc -S` (ugen output, before as1) shows
   the source order; as1 then hoists a `lw sym_b+4` above a `sw sym_a+4` whenever the symbols differ
   (the `.extern` size does not matter, 0 or 1). It keeps a load behind a store only when both name
   the same symbol + addend. It reuses `$at` for a second store only when the symbol AND the addend
   are equal (`ee+0x414C0` / `ee+0x414C4` get two `lui at`: the post1b 66B64 / 66A50 shared-$at cell
   stays a cap). Assembling a hand-edited `-S` file with one symbol everywhere gave the target
   chain word for word, which is how the shape was identified.
2. *uopt holds a global's address in a register (`la` = lui + addiu, then `lw K(reg)`) whenever
   the address is used twice in a region -- even one `g = g & m` RMW --* for plain scalars, struct
   members, unions, arrays and every `(char *)&sym + K` spelling alike (all canonicalise to
   `LDA sym` + offset). IDO 5.3 does the same. It leaves the address UNCOLOURED (direct macro form
   at every access) when the web spans a call and has few uses: `x = g; foo(); g = x | 1;` compiles
   to `lw sym` / `sw sym` with no base. With a held base, as1 also forwards same-base reloads (`lw
   4(v0)` after `sw 4(v0)` disappears).
3. *uopt never forwards a store into a later load of the same global through `-S`,* but with the
   address uncoloured a reload of the same type as the preceding store was dropped; stores typed
   `u32` and loads typed `s32` keep every reload (two adjacent loads are CSE'd unless their types
   or symbols differ).
4. *Recipe.* Use per-PAIR aliases (all pinned 0, like the import): each store and the load that
   follows it name the same alias (as1 keeps the order, and reuses `$at` when the next store uses
   that alias too); the first two reads get their own single-use aliases; every pair alias is used
   again AFTER the switch's calls (the restore if/else: then-arm load s1 / store s2, else-arm load
   s4 / store s7), so its address web crosses calls and uopt leaves it uncoloured. D884:
   `l1, s1=l2.., s2=s1.., s2=s2.., s4=s2.., s4=s4..` (loads `s32`, stores `u32`). One alias per
   access (the old spelling) is right for single RMWs but loses the store/load order and the $at
   reuse in a chain.
5. *Smaller fixes that fell out.* Two adjacent constant stores (`0x140 = 1; 0x13C = 1;`) on one
   source line put the second constant in the preceding `lw` delay (as1 order). DF14 only: an
   `if (1) {}` right after `char *rr = r;` issues the r reload before the arg2 reload; a tail block
   writing through an existing local (`gsub = r;`) instead of a new block-local `rr` gives r v1 and
   the following `FW(arg0, 0x38)` v0 (the block-local took v0 first). Both functions are cfe donors
   (the 14-entry jumptables are read through `D_807FF3E0 + 0x3C0` / `D_807FF420 + 0x400`; donor
   `.rodata` pinned with `<func>_rodata = 0x3C0 / 0x400`).
6. *Negatives (do not retry):* volatile (scalar, array, struct member, per-site, cfe or NCC) always
   materialises `lui; addiu; lw 0(reg)`; bitfields compile to byte `lbu/sb` RMWs; `-Olimit` skip
   (unoptimised ucode) gives an -O0-like body, not this one; `-Wo,-zscm:0 / -zcomo:0 / -zcopy:0 /
   -zstor:0` do not remove the `la`; block-scope `extern` redeclarations are the same symbol, and a
   conflicting-type redeclaration is a cfe error.
7. *timproc_b5 CEB4 (97.13) negatives:* `(f32)1` / `1.0` / `(f64)1` for the blocks 2-3 then-arm
   constants (26-27 diffs vs 14), the D load in a comma expression in the condition (14, no change),
   then-arm `a1 = a1;`, `f = f;`, `if (1) {}`, `while (0) {}`, `a1 = 0;`, `goto join;` (all fold the
   arm, 23); `v[0] = v[0]; if (1) {}` (14).
8. *post0b 4A9F0 EXACT (98.00 -> 100, NCC donor over an empty placeholder).* The run-133 NCC NM
   donor had the inner cursor copy in t1 (target v0) and the cell sum in v1 twice. An `if (1) {}`
   right after the inner `self->put(...)` call ends that block before the `*cursor++` re-read:
   the copy then colours v0 (the dead grid-root register) and the -1 / &D registers drop back to
   t1 / t2. Writing the cell address as ONE expression (`&g->grid->cells[base] + i`, not
   `cell = &cells[base]; cell += i;`) sends the row sum to a ugen temp (t4) and the cell to v1,
   which also re-phases the byte loads onto t6 / t7 / t9. Same length as the NM donor: post0b
   clip unchanged.
9. *bootup 31C0 (99.86) notes:* the target reads obj from the copy home (0x78) in case 0 and from
   the new-temp home (0x74) in case 1; ours does the reverse (new-temp at 0x70) and puts the KB
   new-temp at 0x74 (target 0x68). `Obj *obj = new Obj2;`, `{ obj = new Obj2; }`, a block around
   `new KB`, a named KB pointer, an extra block volatile or moving obj's declaration did not move
   the homes (12 raw words, or much worse).

## kit CCXIV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 218): a RoData float read through `D + off` / an extern alias is often a compiler LITERAL -- check the ROM word and its neighbours; as a literal, uopt treats it as a constant (hoisted, register-allocated, rematerialised after calls, one fresh literal word per `l.s`): game_libs 3430 and timproc_b5 CEB4 EXACT; C310 96.45 -> 99.89 (`== 1` held constant); the CCXII address-form scan has no further hit <a name="kit-ccxiv-agent-c-run-218"></a>

**The literal tell.** USO code reads a pooled float as `lui at,0; lwc1 fN,OFF(at)` whether the source was a
literal or a RoData global, so NM bodies spell many of them `*(f32 *)((char *)&D_00000000 + OFF)` or a
pinned `extern f32 D_xxx`. Read the word at RoData+OFF in the ROM (bootup.uso RoData = ROM 0xD9FE44:
it holds 0.1f at 0xCC8 / 0xCEC / 0xCF0 / 0xCF4 / 0xCF8; timproc_b5's RoData is the expected object's
`.rodata`). A run of IDENTICAL values (four 0.1f around a jump table, four 0.3f at timproc 0x390..0x39C,
five 0.17f at bootup 0x59C..0x5AC, -1500.0f twice at 0x530 / 0x534) is a literal pool: as1 emits a new
literal word for every `l.s`, so each rematerialisation of one source constant gets its own address, in
emission order, and the function's switch tables sit between them (`.rodata` order = first use). The
spelling decides codegen: a memory read stays where the statement is; a literal is a constant uopt can
hoist into the test block, colour and order with the other constants, keep in a caller-saved register
and reload after calls, or hold in a callee-saved one. Landing a literal needs a donor (the in-unit
`.rodata` cannot be placed): REPLACE_FUNC_BODY renames the donor's `.rodata` reloc `<fn>_rodata`; pin it
to the ROM address of the donor's `.rodata` +0 (an unused leading literal included -- CEB4's pool starts
at 0x390 although the first read is 0x394, like the ROM).

1. *game_libs 3430 (97.52 -> 100, 1220 bytes, cfe donor `game_libs_o2_3430.c`).* The NM body had a
   variable `step` loaded from `D_..._cc8` and reassigned from CEC / CF0 / CF4 in cases 6-8. The real code
   has no variable: case 3 adds the literal 0.1f, which uopt keeps in caller-saved f2 and rematerialises
   after the calls of cases 6 / 7 / 8 (the three "reassignments" were those reloads), and since the first
   load is a hoisted constant it follows the f22 / f20 (1.0f / 10.625f) constants in the prologue -- the
   order no placement of a memory load could produce (store-first, `if (1) {}`, for-init: all tried).
   With 0-2 BBs the literal is held in callee-saved f24 instead; THREE trailing `if (1) {}` (kit run 111's
   firstUseCost lever) flip it to f2 + reloads: 100. Donor `.rodata` = literal +0, 8-entry table +4,
   literals +0x24..+0x2C, pinned `gl_func_00003430_rodata = 0xCC8`.
2. *timproc_b5 CEB4 (97.13 -> 100, 428 bytes, cfe donor `timproc_uso_b5_CEB4.c`).* The grey colour is the
   literal 0.3f (four 0x3E99999A words at 0x390). As a literal it is hoisted with 1.0f into each test
   block; an `if (1) {}` closing each white arm puts 0.3f ahead of 1.0f (target f0 / f2 and order), and in
   block 1 the same lever replaces the old `v[0] = v[0];` self-assignment that kept the `bc1f else; b join`
   shape (the white arm's stores are redundant with the init and vanish, the join's `lw a1` fills the
   delay slot). Pinned `timproc_uso_b5_func_0000CEB4_rodata = 0x390`.
3. *timproc_b5 C310 NM (96.45 -> 99.89).* The target's loop test is `bnel t0,t4` against a register-held 1
   (`li t0,1` rematerialised at the loop top) that is the same constant web as the ring reset's `= 1`: write
   `== 1` (the old `- 1 == 0` avoided an s8 hold that the current body no longer gets) and put the reset
   after the `+= 2`. Both ring counters field-form (`-= 1;` / `+= 1;` then the test) so load and adjust are
   ugen temps; `*(f32 *)(e + 0x10C) == 0.0f` (field first: `mtc1 zero` / `lwc1` order, no nop); the min
   selection in mv2 with a folded `mv = mv2 + 0 * (int)(*arg0)` copy (target `move v0,v1`) and an
   emission-free `if (m) {}` (m v0 / selection v1). Left: the `arg1 + 0x230` hoist one slot early and the
   shared colour-value spill at 80 (target 96: the target has 16 more bytes between the saves and the
   spill, like 4A308's 8 below its spill word -- unexplained).
4. *Literal swaps that are neutral or small:* post0b 4F2DC far / best = -1e5 / 1e5 literals (0x1BA8 /
   0x1BAC; 95.26 -> 95.45, committed); 5F5F0's 0x205C / 0x2060 are 10000.0f / 1e-7f literals (identical
   code); bootup C234's 0x920 / 0x924 / 0x928 / 0x94C are 1e5 / 335 / -335 / 0.4 (identical code); 55A0's
   0.2f / 0.17f pool (slightly worse in the current NM donor). An automated literal sweep needs the per-USO
   RoData base and the body's spelling; most NM bodies here read pools through other forms.

Scan (`/tmp/claude-1000/c218/hiscan.py`, throwaway): for every non-exact function in post0b >= 0x48000,
bootup_uso, timproc_b5, post1b, kernel, game_libs.c, titproc, mgrproc, arcproc, compare the count of `lui`

hit here. Equal counts do not prove equal placement, but every listed near-miss checked by hand (6204, E9FC,

## kit CCXVIII (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 219): post0b 36F0C EXACT -- an inline's BY-VALUE float parameter is a uopt variable (f0 first) while a CONST-REFERENCE parameter read is an ugen temp (the f4 / f6 / f10 / f8 ring); a kept-parameter accessor `Cam *n = gc0(c)` gives a pooled v0 web that no setter web interferes with; replace-function-body.py now names objcopy-renamed section symbols; 35B1C is a C++ constructor (same residual); 591C / 2E354 / 40304 / 37938 negatives <a name="kit-ccxviii-agent-g-run-219"></a>

**1. 36F0C closed (99.73 -> 100, 968 B, ROM byte-identical).** Run 218 left the six tail stores
(`c->pos = w`, `c->tgt->m.t = pos`) with every value in f0 where the target cycles f4 / f6 / f10 / f8. The setters
were `static inline void spy(Cam *n, f32 v) { if (0) { n = 0; } n->pos.y = v; }`. Once one parameter of an inline
is kept (the dead `n = 0`), edg makes a parameter temp for EVERY parameter, and the float one is a uopt variable:
f0 is its first colour, for every call. Written `const f32 &v` the value is read through the (constant-folded)
reference inside the inline: an ordinary load into the ugen temp ring, exactly the target's registers. The same
change on the x setter reloads w.x from the stack (an indirect load is never forwarded from the `w += pos` store),
where the target keeps the add result in f4. The target's x store is a DIRECT `n->pos.x = w.x` (forwarded), with n in
v0: `Cam *n = gc0(c);` (`static inline Cam *gc0(Cam *n) { if (0) { n = 0; } return n; }`) taken right after
`pos += v` and before `w += pos`. A plain `Cam *n = c; if (0) { n = 0; }` gets the same shape but colours a1: the
zdbug:5 dump shows its LR interfering with the pooled edg temp that carries tm()'s / the setters' kept parameter (LR
in v0 across the whole tail); the accessor's return value IS that pooled temp, so it lands in v0 with no
interference. The accessor's frame word also replaces run 218's named `f64 h = 100.0` step (frame 136 kept).
Rule: in an NCC donor where a value that the target keeps in the temp ring comes out in f0 (or f2 / f12 / f14) through
an inline, make that parameter a const reference; if the target also forwards the value from an earlier store, do
the store directly through a kept-parameter accessor result instead of an inline call.

**2. Infra: replace-function-body.py and objcopy-renamed C++ donors.** `objcopy --redefine-sym` (needed to rename a
mangled member such as `update__7FreeCamFv`) rewrites the donor's section symbols with st_name 0, so the splicer saw
an empty name and bound the donor's `.rodata` literal relocs to an anonymous symbol (`*ABS*`, %lo 0 in the ROM).
STT_SECTION symbols with no name now take the section header's name, so the reloc is renamed `<func>_rodata` as for
every other donor (36F0C: `gl_func_00036F0C_rodata = 0x19E8`). Side effect, NM-only: redefine-sym'd NM donors with
literals now score their literal loads properly (bootup 31C0 99.86 -> 99.96, post0b 4D688 97.84 -> 97.86, b5 8FC8
91.51 -> 91.56); no ROM byte changes.

**3. post0b 35B1C (97.40) is a C++ constructor.** `if (o != 0 || (o = alloc(0x10)) != 0) { o->vt = &D; placement
member at o+4 with an (o+4 != 0) test ... }` is the edg ctor protocol; `struct Node { Node *next; Key k; int x8;
Node(List *, Key, int); virtual void f(); }` (cfront layout puts the vptr after the members = 0xC) with
`struct Key { int v; Key() { v = 0; } }` reproduces the body word-for-word with frame 0x48; a dead

## kit CCXIX (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 220): a global read through `&D` / a held `int *` is a DIRECT variable access that uopt folds into `lui; lw %lo` and never hoists; the same word read as an ARRAY element (`extern int D_x[]; D_x[0]`) makes its address a loop-invariant web (hoisted into an s-register across calls) -- post0b 46050 89.71 -> 92.20 at target length with the real-C++ append kit; gui 2DE0 95.53 -> 96.65 (329C-shape port) <a name="kit-ccxix-agent-g-run-220"></a>

address in the loop preheader and reads it as `lw t6, 0(s8)` every iteration (s8 survives the else-arm call). Every
spelling of the read as `*(int *)&D_00000000` -- direct `D_00000000`, a held `int *margin = &D`, `int &`, `char` symbol
plus cast, a struct accessor inline, `register`, `const` pointer, late init, a free inline `scrw(int *)` -- gave
byte-identical code: `lui t6,%hi(D); lw t6,%lo(D)(t6)` inside the loop. uopt treats `*&D` as a direct memory
variable, so there is no address expression to hoist. Declaring the word as an array and indexing it
(`extern int D_46050_m[]; ... D_46050_m[0] - 0x14`) turns the read into an address computation plus an indexed load;
that address is a loop-invariant constant web and takes s8 exactly as in the target (and pushes the 0xE4000000

a global's address in an s-register across a loop / call but the build folds every access to `lui; lw %lo`.
