## kit CCXX (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 221): a target global read-modify-write whose value stays in ONE caller-saved register (`lui v0,0; lw v0,0(v0); and v0,v0,s6; ori v0,v0,0x100; sw v0,0(at)`) is a LOCAL's chain, not an expression -- `x = G; x &= m; x |= k; G2 = x;`; a target `addiu rX,base,K; lw/sw 0(rX)` field RMW is the documented if (1) pointer-mutation barrier; a folded counted use stretches its operand's live range, so pick the operand <a name="kit-ccxx-agent-g-run-221"></a>

Fresh-eyes swap run (agent-c's near-exact bootup / post0b / post1b / kernel list). Gains: bootup 6808 96.61 -> 98.34
(the last +0.02: `g0 = p->0x40; ... func(g0 * 4)` = the target's `lw v1,64(s1); sll a0,v1,2`),
post0b 493AC 97.18 -> 97.33, bootup E68 94.54 -> 94.57 (report-equivalent in-tree objdiff); no exact.

1. **Global RMW as a local's v0 chain (bootup 6808, 96.61 -> 97.92).** The target's four `import_8005EE64` flag
   updates keep load, and/or results and store value in a single register (`v0`) -- ugen temps would rotate
   (t6 -> t7 -> t8). Writing each as `g00 = G1; g00 &= ~8; g00 |= 0x100; G0 = g00;` (separate compound
   statements on a named int local; a single `x = (G & m) | k` still leaves the intermediate in a ugen temp)
   makes uopt carry one live range through the whole RMW. Use dead / dummy-home locals (here the unused `g0, g00`
   at the top of the declaration list) so no new home appears.
   - The register is v0 only where the RMW's basic block has nothing else claiming v0: the first site sits in the
     join block after an if / else and got v0 once the mode-word address (`import_8005EE6C`, stored twice right
     after) stopped being hoisted into v0 above the branch -- an `if (1) {}` between the RMW and the mode-word
     stores did that (97.14 -> 97.86), with the `D_bu_1EBDC[0] = 6` store written first as its own statement.
   - The other three sites (each after a call in the same block) stay v1: per-site distinct locals (op / dc / d0 /
     b0 / d4 grid, 120 variants), `if (1) {}` before / after / both, making the variable's first role a call result
     (`g0 = f(); ...`), block-scope / `register` / u32 locals: all flat or worse. Open.
2. **Field RMW through a materialised address (`addiu v1,v0,0x18; lw t1,0(v1); ...; sw t2,0(v1)`).** Plain
   `*(int *)(res + 0x18) &= ~0x40`, a named pointer, `volatile`, `(int)res + K`, `+ 0 * (int)res` index tricks and
   C++ reference / pointer inline helpers all fold to `lw 0x18(v0)`. The pointer-mutation barrier from the
   arcproc 1F54 / mgrproc C14 notes reproduces it word-for-word: `rec = (int *)res; if (1) { rec += 0x18 / 4; }
   *rec &= ~0x40;` (6808 97.92 -> 98.32; length 2376 -> 2380 = a verified decode fix: the old equal length came
   from an unrelated extra `or a3,v1` cancelling this missing addiu). Same lever in NCC on a member:
   `pad1 = (int)this; if (1) { pad1 += 0x30; } *(int *)pad1 |= 0x80;` (493AC 97.18 -> 97.33, reusing an
   unexplained pad home; a new `int *f` local costs a home and scores 97.19). In 6808 the second site (p+0x30)
   lines up up to registers only with the flag local itself as the pointer (`g0 = (int)p; if (1) { g0 += 0x30; }
   *(int *)g0 |= 0x40;` -- the target reuses v0 for flag and pointer), but stays v1 like item 1 and scores lower
   (+4 bytes): not kept.
3. **Folded counted use: the operand matters, not just the site (bootup E68).** Agent-c's run-209 `m = E68_MGR +
   0 * *cfg` raised E68 by keeping *some* use at that point, but it also kept `cfg` alive into the second loop nest,
   so `arg2` out-prioritised it for s0 (`or s0,a2 / or s1,a1` vs the target's `or s0,a1 / or s1,a2`). The same
   folded term on `arg3` (or `y`, `row`, `(int)self`, `arg2`, `(int)buf`, `(int)tlut`) keeps the gain and fixes the
   prologue (94.54 -> 94.57). Rule: when a counted-use hit lengthens a parameter's live range, re-sweep the
   operand at that site. The 6808 `*arg1` uses (which make the target-absent `sw a1,244(sp)` home store) and the
   B75C / 4C5E4 member uses: no better operand.
4. **Negatives.**
   - 18F0 (kernel): the `& ~8` mask as a bitfield clear (`unsigned done:1` -> lbu / sb byte access), mask / flag
     variables, `^= 8`, if / else polarity: flat or worse.
   - 4C5E4: an inline `setvp(Vp *, x, y, w, h)` DOES re-materialise 2.0f per use like the target (`lui at,0x4000`
     twice), but also 4.0f, and the Vp append moves ahead of the member loads (+4..16 bytes, 78-85).
   - 65EE4: all-distinct per-access aliases at -O2 with the first call's third argument as the constant itself
     (`f(&a6, B + 4, B + 0x10)`) reach the target length (584) but only 67.98 (agent-c's figure); prototypes
     (`(Save *, ...)`, `(void *, ...)`, 3-int with padding args) and pointer-typed fields under -Olimit 1: flat.
   - 5A2C4: consecutive `if (1) {}` blocks collapse (1 = 2 = 5 in score) -- no BB-count lever in cfe; named
     post-conversion r / g / b locals: 90.40 < 90.47. The target's uncoloured CSE temps stay open.
   - C234: the 0x920 / 0x924 / 0x928 / 0x94C pool reads as literals (100000.0f, 335.0f, -335.0f, 0.4f): identical
     code. 0x128 is an imported object (1.07e21), not a literal.
   - Declaration moves in 6808 (46 variants) and objdiff fuzzy: sp offsets do not count, so home-layout fixes
     only matter for an exact.

## kit CCXXI (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 222): uopt's v0 interference is BLOCK-granular -- a short local web never gets v0 in the block right after a call (dead int return OR a return consumed by a store in that block) or in the block that holds the final `return x` copy; wrapping the web in `do { ... } while (0)` (a macro body) gives it its own block and the v0 colour back; the target's flag-store-before-`or v0,s0` epilogue order is the same tell <a name="kit-ccxxi-agent-g-run-222"></a>

Found on bootup 6808 (98.34 -> 99.98 NM over the run) with the coloring dump (`-Wo,-zdbug:5`, zsum-style parse of the
`>>>active<<<` records: lr / reg / priority / live-bb list; reg 1 = v0, 2 = v1, ... 6 = a3, 7 = t0, 14.. = s0..).

- Four global flag RMWs (`x = G; x &= m; x |= k; G2 = x;`, kit CCXX) sit right after calls. Only the first one
  (after a branch join) coloured v0; the other three came out v1 even with FRESH per-site locals or block-scope
  locals. The dump shows the precoloured `isvar R 2vreg` record (the physical v0) live in the blocks where a call
  result is used (`*gD = f(...)` -> `sw v0,0(s4)`) and in the block with the final return copy; the flag web in
  the same block conflicts with it at block granularity, although the two never overlap in the instruction
  stream. A call whose int return is discarded blocks v0 the same way in the block that follows it (moving the
  first flag site behind a `func();` statement flipped it v0 -> v1; void-aliasing that call flipped it back).
- `do { x = G; x &= m; x |= k; G2 = x; } while (0);` puts the RMW in its own block (the loop labels survive;
  `if (1) {}`, `goto L; L:`, a bare label, `switch (0) { default: ; }` after the store do NOT split -- uopt
  merges them). With all four sites wrapped and on ONE dummy-home local (g00), all four colour v0 and no void
  alias is needed; at the end the flag store now precedes `or v0,s0,zero` like the target (the return copy is in
  a later block). `return` inside `do { return res; } while (0);` / `goto out; out: return res;` also split the
  return block (same effect on the last site).
- A variable is ONE live range across all its webs here (g0 = {x40 site, site 3, site 5, site 7} coloured as a
  unit): one site whose web touches a call argument (`f(g0 * 4)`, v0 blocked by that call's def) drags every
  other site of the same name to v1. Keep the v1-target web (x40) alone on its own name.
- Tell: target `lw v0; op v0; sw v0` RMW right after a `jal` / `sw v0,0(sN)` of the call result, or a flag store
  scheduled BEFORE the epilogue's `or v0,sN,zero`, while ours has v1 and the return move hoisted = the original
  had a block boundary there (macro `do { } while (0)` body).
- Also: the `addiu v0,s1,48; lw/sw 0(v0)` field RMW after the flag = `g00 = (int)p; if (1) { g00 += 0x30; }
  *(int *)g00 |= 0x40;` on the same dummy-home local (the block lines up word for word; +1 word, a verified
  decode fix).
- DECODE FIX via colouring: target `addiu a3,zero,6; beq a3,v1` + `sw a3,0(s5)` + a jal with NO `or a3` copy, ours
  v1 + `or a3,v1` = the call takes THREE args, not four: a3 is just the lowest free register for the compare
  constant (v0 blocked by the preceding call's dead return, v1 = the compared word, a0..a2 = the call's args); a 4th
  argument makes a3 refuse the constant (t0 / v1 + move). Also drop a bbsplit `if (1) {}` right after that call: it
  hid the dead-return v0 block, so the compared word took v0 instead of the target's v1. 99.74 -> 99.98.
- A target with NO `sw a1,K(sp)` arg home where ours has one: a folded counted use `0 * *arg1` keeps arg1 live
  across calls. The int-cast held base `gD = (char **)(int)D_bu_776C;` (kit-documented unfold) keeps &sym in s4
  without it; also a folded use on a global read (`G | K + 0 * G`) turns the read into a v0 candidate where the

- A by-value 4-byte struct arg whose target order is `sw a2,8(sp)` (arg slot) BEFORE the jal and the local home

- Frame residual (6808 now 12 words = t78..t6C and v4C homes +4): target = op's spill word at 72 directly under a

   `{t6C}`) identify it: cfe saved the call result of `t = (char *)func_00000000(0) + 0 * (int)(*arg1)` (the other
   operand must be evaluated after the call) and reused the same temp as the value of the comma arguments
   `(t70.w = X, t70)`. Temps are allocated after ALL homes, block-scope ones included (a block-scope v4C still went
   above it), and are shared across sites of the same size.

## kit CCXXIV (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 224): count the target frame word by word and re-declare the cfe locals to fit -- m2c `spNN` names that are dead copies of another variable's home or of a spill slot go, unused m2c temps go, disjoint same-type temps merge, char locals pack into one word; a frame pad declared LAST sits under the homes; 2E354 frame 0xA0 -> 0x80 with every home on target, then a 1 / 2 / default pick as a switch <a name="kit-ccxxiv-agent-g-run-224"></a>

1. *Reading the target frame* (cfe, game_libs 2E354). Target `addiu sp,-0x80`, saves s0/ra at 0x20/0x24 (end

   the target's sp accesses: sp7D at frame-3 (byte), sp78 -8, sp6B -21 (byte), sp64 -28, sp60 -32, a `sw v0` home
   at -40, sp50 -48. cfe allocates chars at BYTE granularity downward (two u8s before sp7D put it at -3; the three
   bytes under sp6B take three more u8s), then the next word-aligned slot. Fill the gaps (three words between sp78
   and sp6B, one each around the -40 home) with other locals and leave exactly the remaining count below sp50.
2. *Which m2c names to drop.* `sp58 = var_v0;` before a call was the target's `sw v0,0x58(sp)` = var_v0 spilled to

   into var_t9 scored best of 11 pairs; temp_v0_7 into anything scored lower). Result: frame and all seven homes on
   target (fuzzy +0.04 only: objdiff scores sp offsets loosely, but the frame must be right for an exact).

   declared after the last local it lands below the named homes. E68: target ult at frame-40 and i/head at -184
   (ours -56 / -200 with the pad in the middle); moved last -> every frame-relative home matches, frame unchanged.
4. *Small levers that stuck in 2E354:* a `v == 1 -> 0, v == 2 -> 1, else 2` pick written as a `switch` (target:
   `beq v1,at(1); beq v1,at(2); b; li 2` with one `b` block per case -- an if/else chain emits a bne tree);
   `o->0x1C == 1U` gets the target's fresh `li at,1` instead of sharing the stateB / stateD constant register

   0x3C4 load like the target but the spill slots come out in a different order (92.47). 5A2C4: the four
   0x2C..0x38 words are spill slots in both builds (pad sizes change nothing); 591C: renaming the three scaled-axis
   temps to the target's colours costs 0.7 (their other uses decide); B3C: the jump table's 5th entry (`case 4`)
   cannot go (4 cases -> compare chain); 30AF4 sv copy forms flat.
6. *Adjacent-statement / declaration swap + `if (1) {}` sweeps over the NCC NM donors* (independent statements
   only; reject any swap that moves a read above the write it depends on -- 55A0's best hit did and was dropped):
   post0b 3BE1C 97.33 -> 97.60 (`Tri *t` initialiser before `V3 *n`), 3C43C 98.24 -> 98.26 (hitbuf before dist),
   4F2DC 95.45 -> 95.67 (count after hits, then a declaration-MOVE sweep: `V3 d;` declared before `V3 dir;` --
   in C++ donors moving a mid-body declaration up re-orders the stack objects without touching code), 4C5E4 88.65 -> 88.67 (vscale[0] before [1]), game_uso 7C1C
   96.31 -> 96.33, 8CD8 89.499 -> 89.506 (BB split); B75C (cfe) 94.00 -> 94.01 with the f64 declared before
   var_f2 (moves the a0 spill slot to the target's 0x24). Flat: 3B6A0, 3B9C0, 37540, 46050, 46790, 41D40, 3AE58,

## kit CCXXV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 222): a C++ ctor that only matches through cfe (its switch is a jumptable) can be written as cfront-style C -- `this` IS the parameter, inline members are statement macros, and the inline temporaries are a FEW reused function-scope pointers; then frame-order locals, one-line comma runs and held vtable locals; timproc_uso_b5 8FC8 NM 93.39 (NCC) -> 96.01 (cfe, jumptable included) <a name="kit-ccxxv-agent-c-run-222"></a>

Target: timproc_uso_b5_func_00008FC8 (6496 B), the timing-screen master constructor. The NCC donor
(timproc_uso_b5_ncc_8FC8_nm.cpp) reached 93.39 but NCC lowers the 5-case tail switch to compares, so
only cfe can ever be exact. The m2c C body was 86.64. New donor: src/timproc_uso_b5/timproc_uso_b5_8FC8_nm.c
(IDO 7.1 cfe -O2), spliced over the NM object (Makefile TIMB5_8FC8_NM_DONOR, filtered out of C_FILES);
its jumptable reloc is renamed timproc_uso_b5_func_00008FC8_rodata (pinned to RoData +0x324).

Steps, standalone objdiff (each kept only when length did not move away from 6496):
1. **Transcribe the NCC donor as cfront would emit it.** `void **f(void **arg0, ...)` with
   `if (arg0 || (arg0 = (void **)alloc(0x60)))` testing the PARAMETER (gives the target's early
   `move s2,a0` in the prologue; a `char *self = arg0` copy moves it into the bnez delay slot: +0.15).
   Inline members (B::add, the S70 / Panel / W16C ctors with the nested `if (bp || (bp = alloc()))`
   base check, V3::seti, attachKids, the 0x80000 restore) as one-line statement macros.
2. **Inline temporaries must be a few REUSED function-scope pointers.** One block-scope variable per
   expansion site (the literal cfront shape) gave frame 0x280 with everything spilled (77.6): uopt
   gives up colouring that many candidates. Five shared pointers (w / _wp / n / t / _at) -> 85.8 -> 90.7
   once the macros were mapped onto them (`#define _np w`-style aliases swept with spelling-grid).
3. **Which shared pointer each expansion uses picks s0 / s1.** The panel-tail `add()` through `t`
   (+0.3), the first S70 row's `add()` with `_at` / `w` (+0.2): sweep the variable per expansion.
4. **Switch arm with fallthrough written as duplicated stores + break** (`case 1: e2 = 0; e3 = 0;
   break;`, all `0.0f` so they use the held f20 zero) and the third tail-call zero argument `0.0f`
   (not `(f32)0.0`): 93.36 -> 94.31.
5. **Declare the locals in the target's frame order** (read homes from the target's sp offsets):
   per-site V3 temporaries v2a..v3b at the top (0x154..0x130), the row pointers, items, the tail
   block's locals hoisted to function scope (e2 home 0xF0), the spilled n pointer's home (0xE0),
   v1a / v1b, sb1 0xC0, a NAMED site-1 loop counter (its spill home 0xBC), the two by-value V3 copy
   buffers as `s32 t1[10]; s32 t2[4];` (0x94 / 0x84), sb2 0x80, sb3 0x68: frame 0x150 -> 0x160 and
   all homes on target (+0.07). Block-scope `int x` / `int fl` chain temps -> the shared `_x`.
6. **A run of ctor calls whose results are stored (`kid[i] = new Kid(...)`) on ONE source line as a
   comma expression** moves each result store behind the next call's argument setup (`lui; lui;
   addiu; addiu; sw v0; or a0; jal`), as in the target: 94.49 -> 95.35; the saved-bit load and the
   flag chain joined onto the same line: 95.60. Line layout alone does it (statements on one line
   score the same as the comma form for the flag part); a coordinate sweep over every line break in
   the body found two more joins (+0.17) and then converged.
7. **Virtual calls through a held vtable local** (`w = FP(obj, 0x28); (*(fn *)(w + 0x5C))(*(s16 *)(w +
   0x58) + obj, ...)`): the target keeps the vtable pointer in s1; +0.19. Writing it as a comma
   expression `(w = ..., fn)(...)` instead is -9 (evaluation order changes).

Negatives / open: the per-site three `mtc1 zero` (target ft1..ft3 then three swc1) stay one shared
mtc1 under every spelling (int 0, 0.0, (float)0, (f32)0.0, per-store `if (1) {}`, int / float locals);
the item loop's vtable through `t` removes the DF_320 hoist and lines the loop up word-for-word but
the function then ends 8 bytes short (6488) because the missing mtc1s are no longer offset, so it
was NOT kept (u: 6492); sites 2 / 3 want the loop counter in s0 and the seti / element pointer in a
caller-saved temp (dead `addiu a1,a1,0xb4` survives in the target) -- block-scope pointers, an outer
counter and a fresh pointer for the element all lose; the site-3 0x80000 restore CSEs the EE6C address
into v1 (target re-forms `lui at` per store).

## kit CCXXVI (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 223): a t-register that NEVER appears as a temp in the build is held by a uopt-allocated VARIABLE -- find the local whose web landed in that caller-saved register and move its role; then sweep which reused cfront temporary each inline expansion uses (per-line var swaps), one-line store pairs, and an extern alias per un-CSE'd store; timproc_uso_b5 8FC8 NM 96.01 -> 98.81, length = target <a name="kit-ccxxvi-agent-c-run-223"></a>

1. **Off-by-one t-register cascade = a variable parked in a temp register (96.20 -> 97.08).** Every ugen
   temp after the head was one later than the target (`lw t1` vs target `lw t0`), but deleting / joining
   statements around the first diff never removed the skip. Grepping the build's column for the
   skipped register showed `t0` used ONLY by two `lw t0, ...` that hold a named local (the shared `u`
   pointer: a zero-fill base and the item-loop vtable). uopt colours that web to t0 and ugen then
   excludes t0 from its temp ring for the whole function. Fix by moving the role, not the code: the
   item loop held its vtable in `w` (s1 like the target), and the loop's RoData float argument read as
   `FF(import_808000CC, 0x320)` instead of a named `DF_320` extern (uopt hoisted the named symbol's
   address into s0 out of the loop -- `lui s0; addiu s0` -- which pushed the mask local `tu` out of s0
   and spilled it; the target reloads `lui at; lwc1 0x320(at)` per iteration). **Check: if a temp
   register is missing from the build's whole function, look for a variable in it before touching
   statement order.**
2. **Per-expansion temp-role sweep (97.08 -> 98.67).** With the inline temporaries reused function-scope
   pointers (kit CCXXV), which one an expansion uses decides s0 / s1 and whether a row pointer is
   spilled-and-reloaded: S70 row ctor outer allocation in `t`, nested base-ctor `this` in `w`, and each
   row's `B::add` binding through `t` (ADDW) gave the target's `sw s0, 0x12c(sp)` / reload; the panel's
   +0x284 float store and the 0x2B8 -> 0x29C copy go through `w` (target holds the copied pointer in
   s1, the plain field-to-field copy used a temp) -- 97.27 -> 98.41 in one step. A scripted per-line
   swap of one temp name for another (`re.sub` on a single body line, ~100 variants a pass, 6
   parallel compiles ~12 s) finds the rest, BUT it also proposes semantics-changing swaps (passing
   the stale `t` instead of the fresh `w` to a call scored +0.04) -- only keep swaps where the line
   assigns the variable before using it.
3. **A target's dead `addiu aN, aN, 0xb4` after a zero fill** is the inline `V3::seti` pointer
   (P = V + 0xB4) kept because the SAME variable is read again later: SETI(u, ..) at sites 2 / 3 plus
   `u` reused by site 3's +0x284 store brings both dead adds back (length 6492 -> 6496 = target).
4. **Small levers:** two vtable / name stores written on one source line give the target's addiu
   order (as the 0x2C block already showed); the "hidden item" store through `items[i]` rather than the
   call-result local (+0.10); a store-only extern alias (`f8fc8_ee6c_r3`, pinned 0) on the site-3
   flag-restore store stops the EE6C address CSE (+0.19 and +1 word to the target length).
5. **Negatives (do not repeat):** the per-site triple `mtc1 zero` at sites 1 / 2 (site 3 already has
   it): per-site spellings 0 / 0.0 / (float)0 / (f32)0.0 / 0.0f / 0L / 0U / '\0' / casts, f32 or int
   locals per component (int locals keep a live cvt.s.w; f32 locals propagate to the fs0 zero),
   volatile pad, do-while / if (1) {} / if (P) {} between the stores, comma-with-`*P` value, stores
   through V with a late `P += 0xB4`; site 2 / 3 loop counter in s0 (target) vs a spilled caller-saved
   register: while / reversed compare / guarded do-while / array index / RMW spellings, `register`,
   unsigned / short counters, a fresh function-scope counter at every declaration position, a fresh
   element pointer (moves P to v1 but the counter stays spilled); decl-position sweeps of i1 / u / _x /
   fv / t / n / w / i / tu / e3 / the row pointers (all <= base); `if (1) {}` after every body line and
   every line join (none raise it). game_uso 8CD8 is the only other NCC NM donor in range whose target
   has a jumptable, but it is the 4-entry table kit LXV found below cfe's threshold -- not ported.
6. **Addendum -- an unused int-returning prototype steals v0 from a loop (98.81 -> 98.88).** The coloring
   trace (`-Wo,-zdbug:6` with tools/ido-static-recomp-dump + scripts/coloring-solve.py; candidate
   colours 1 = v0, 2 = v1, 5 = a2; frame `off=-N` = sp + frame - N) showed each attach loop's
   strength-reduced kid pointer colouring v1 and the counter a2 (target v0 / v1) although nothing held
   v0: the K&R `extern int f();` callee called in the loop defines v0 inside the live range. Declaring
   the never-read callee `void` frees v0 (site-1 loop word-for-word). Same idea as kit IX's dead-v0
   void alias, but here it re-colours a loop induction variable, not the call site. Sites 2 / 3 still
   want the counter in s0 (the build keeps it caller-saved and spilled).

## kit CCXXVII (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 225): a target delay-slot instruction that belongs to the TAKEN block (the branch falls through to a return path) means its statement starts the next block -- move the statement down to just before its first use, not merely below the branch; and a dead-looking first store to a homed float (`swc1 sum,0x78` then `swc1 sum*k,0x78`) is a store cfe keeps only for a volatile; a volatile copy on a target stack word can be uopt's spill slot (drop it and the scratch locals); game_libs 30AF4 NM 93.55 -> 96.98, 31A74 91.55 -> 95.28 <a name="kit-ccxxvii-agent-g-run-225"></a>

1. **Taken-block delay fill.** 31A74's `if (mode == 255) { call; return; }` is a `bne a3,at,Lv` whose
   delay slot holds `addiu a2,a2,0x3f` (`sel += 63`) while the char re-extension `sll a2,24 / sra a2,24`
   sits in the Lv block. as1 fills a conditional branch's slot with the first instruction of the TAKEN
   block when it is harmless on the fall-through path (a2 is dead on the 255 return path). So `sel += 63`
   is not "above the test" (that puts addiu+sll+sra all before the branch). Moving it to the top of the
   Lv block still lost the slot to `lui a0,0x100` (the hoisted call constant) -- 90.56; moving it to
   just before its first use (`if (sel >= 127)`) gave the target's block schedule: 91.55 -> 95.28 at the
   same 564 bytes. The same shape appears in 2E354 (`lui v1,%hi(G)` in a `bnez` slot whose taken block
   is the else arm that reads `G+0x14` through the held address).
2. **Split a sum to order its loads.** 2E354's `t = o0 / 200.0f + K` loaded K before 200.0f / o->0;
   `t = o0 / 200.0f; t += K;` loads o->0 first (target), and `sp78 = t * sp64` (sum first) gives the
   target's `mul.s ft2, ft0(sum), ft1(sp64)`: 93.90 -> 93.94 at 3684 bytes.
3. **Negatives / leads.** The target also keeps `swc1 sum,0x78(sp)` before the product store to the same
   home; `volatile f32 sp78` reproduces exactly that word (block then lines up up to registers) but the
   function becomes 3688 (target 3684) until another word comes off, so it was not kept. A
   separately-named char-array alias for the else arm's `G+0x14` read/write (`D_E354_Gc`) gives the
   target's `addiu v1,%lo; lw 0x14(v1); ... sw 0x14(v1)` held-address web, but the `lui v1` cannot go into
   the `bnez` slot while the o->0x14 value sits in v1 (target: t0), so 3688 and 93.48.
   NCC 41D40 / 454C4: next() / condition fold-and-split variants all <= base.
4. **A volatile "copy" sitting on a target stack word may be a SPILL slot -- delete the scratch locals
   and let uopt spill.** 30AF4 had `volatile u32 modeSel` at sp+28 plus volatile pad words and seven
   scratch locals (g / m / c / sv / c13 / c14 / cp). The target loads `mode` once into t9 and
   `sw t9,28(sp)` is uopt's spill (three reloads for the second switch). Dropping the volatile alone
   reproduced the load + spill but moved the homes up 0x20 (frame 0x58): the named register locals
   took frame words once the function spilled. Removing them (direct global reads; `sub` forwarded
   through the `D_30AF4_h = sub` store; one named local reused for the case-9 `&gl_state` base and the
   case-10 sub copy) gave frame 0x38 with the spill and all four homes on target: 93.55 -> 96.98,
   2132 -> 2116 bytes (target 2112). Then a store-order swap and a BB split (normal sweeps).
   Counting rule seen here and in 2D374: frame = 0x18 + named-local words + spill words, rounded to 8 --
   an extra unused or scratch local shifts every home and the spill slot by a word.
   Open on 2D374: {fr, z, i} with `&i` kept gives the target code word for word up to registers but

    ...
    fr = D_358;                        /* post-call reload into the SAME variable (separate web) */
    cb(0x4D010000, ((f32)i + fr) / fr);

The two fr webs are separate live ranges (they are not connected), but once the 256-block web holds f2, the
reload web picks the same register. With the reload in fr alone the reload web still coloured first and took
f0 (99.73). With the `if (fr) {}` after the store, or two of them, the order moved the wrong way (99.73 /
98.61). The same with `(fr = D_358)` inline in the argument: 99.94.

**1. Check the dump before assuming a block runs across a call.** `-Wo,-zdbug:5` (diagnosis-only dump build,
`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/out/cc`, section between `global coloring of <fn>` and `REEMISSION OF <fn>`)
prints every live range with its `live bb` list, `forbidden` colours (= colours already given to coloured
neighbours, not a fixed constraint) and `interfere with` list. In game_libs_func_0002D374:
- d (`{1224|1}`, LR 96 -> 24 = f0) is in bb36 only; i (`{1544|1}`, LR 106) is in bb36 + bb37, and bb37 has
  needregsave (the call); the 0x358 reload CSE (`{1102|0}`, LR 111 -> 24) is in bb38 alone with nothing in its
  interference list. Without the `if (0) { f(&i); }` home the reload is in bb37 alone, also with nothing to
  interfere with. So the call ends the block here, and `if (1) {}` before / after either call is inert.
- The coloring order is d, reload, constant 0 (`{1550|0}`, bb32-34), fr. For the target's reload = f2 some f0
  range would have to share the reload's block. A range that crosses the call needs a save (an `if (d) {}`
  after the call spills d: frame 0x38, 99.12), and the constant-0 range stays in bb32-34.
- Inert (all 99.91, or lower): dead float defs / self-copies of d / z / fr after either call; `if (D358 == 0) {}`
  / `if ((f32)i == 0) {}` keep-alives; void / float / double / short prototypes for both calls; the reload in a
  named block-scope float, in fr / d / z, operand swaps, a separate alias for the divisor (+2 words);
  zero-literal spellings of z and of the 0x1010300 argument (`0.0` / `0` there cost +3 words); the i home
  moved to the function top, the c block top, or after either call.

**2. CCXXVIII literal identity applies only to cfe (C) bodies.** An automatic sweep (one `if (1) {}` after
each call statement, plus every float literal respelled `N.f` / `N.0` / `N.0f` / `N.00f` / `.0f` / `0`) over
17 non-exact functions: game_libs 30AF4 / 31A74 / 5A2C4 (C), bootup E68 / B75C (C), and the NCC donors 36694,
4C5E4, 3B9C0, 46050, 4BAF4, 48AEC, 4F2DC. Nothing scored above base. In the NCC donors every float respelling
(`N.f` / `N.0f` / `N.00f` / `.0f`) scored exactly base. Only the `N.0` spellings moved, and they lose because
they turn the literal into a double. So edg normalises literal text before uopt sees it.

**3. game_uso 7C1C (NCC 96.33, 1071 words = target): cfront shape tells, but no cheap lever.** In the target,
every alloc-guard ctor site loads x into f12 and z into f0 (`lwc1 fa0, 0(p); lwc1 fv0, 8(p); swc1 fs2, 4(v1)`),
and the 0.0f constant sits in f24 for the whole function. Coloured registers that repeat the same way at
every expansion fit cfront's shared per-inline-function parameter temporaries (the kit CCXXV/CCXXVI recipe),
not edg's per-expansion temporaries (ours: x f2 / z f12). The NCC body is at a local optimum: 12 XZ / Vec3
ctor and literal spellings scored base or much lower (member-init lists +1..+82 words). A cfront-style port
(explicit ctor macros with function-scope `a` / `c` param temporaries, locals in target frame order) is the
open lead, but it is a multi-run job. The old in-tree cfe emulation (game_uso.c, 88.20, 1058 words) is not a
usable base.

**4. The 4-entry jumptable riddle (game_uso B3C 99.83 / 3 rows, kernel 1ADC).** Both targets dispatch a
4-label switch through a 4-word table (`sltiu at, t, 4`). Standalone probes, IDO 7.1 cfe -O2 and -O1:
- Every 4-label form compiles to a compare chain: plain, `default` in each of the five positions (empty or
  with a call), fall-through, `return` arms, a shared `case 0: case 1:` arm, `case 3: default:`, big arms, enum
  labels, and selectors typed `(unsigned)`, `(char)`, `s16`, `u8`, `long long` or `& 3`. Labels 1..4 also
  chain.
- Five labels in one dense run (0..4) give a table with `sltiu 5`. 0..3 plus a far label (100 or 0x7FFFFFFF)
  still chain: the 0..3 cluster gets no table of its own.
- NCC (edg) gives no table even for 0..4.

So no cfe spelling tried gives a 4-word table. B3C keeps its harmless `case 4: break;` (table + sltiu 5), 3
rows short. The other two B3C rows are a constant 1 call argument that the target materialises (`addiu a1,
zero, 1`) and ours takes from the t0 web of the `1 == x` compares.

**5. The preference lever, applied again: game_uso 591C NM 99.903 -> 99.973.**
- Alloc-guard destination pointers: target `or a1, a2` / `or a1, v0`, ours a0. Fix: route the destination
  through `child_flags`, the variable whose web at the previous site (`child_flags = sub + 180` source
  pointer) is already a1: `child_flags = (int *)p; if (child_flags != 0 || (child_flags = (int *)alloc(12))
  != 0) { ((Vec3 *)child_flags)->y = 0.0f; ... }`. Two sites, +0.046.
- The 0x54 counter: target v1, ours v0. A fresh block-scope `cnt` with no other change still took v0. With
  `if (child_flags) {}` after the counter store, child_flags' v0 range reaches the counter's block and the
  counter colours v1 (+0.023). Placed before the load, the keep-alive is inert. An `if (v0) {}` keep-alive
  also fixes the counter, but it moves child_flags off v0 (net loss).
- The general recipe: when a value takes the wrong register, find the variable that holds the target
  register just before or after, and either reuse that variable (same register) or extend its range into
  the value's block with a zero-code read (forbids that register).

**6. Kit CCXXXIV goto block on gl_func_00031A74 (95.28 -> 97.16).** The mode==1 `cb(0x1000A00, ACC = acc)`
became `goto Z; C: cb(0x1000A00, acc); return; Z: if (1) {} ACC = acc; goto C;`. The argument `mfc1` is now
issued before the store's `lui at`, and as1 copies it into the join branch's delay slot as in the target.
Without the `if (1) {}` it is inert. The same form on the tail store (`goto ... return;`) adds 4 words of
branches with the `if (1) {}` and is inert without it. The tail's sel-spill `sb` / store order is still open
(line splits and statement moves are inert). Also inert: post0b 35B1C's `&D` store (statement order, line
joins, goto block).

**7. Automatic CCXXXIV join sweep (adjacent `;` statements joined one pair at a time, NCC donors included:
the issue order is as1's, so edg bodies respond too).** Run over 30 non-exact functions; gains:
- game_uso 3558 (NCC): 89.21 -> 89.98, from the `side` stores joined with the 072EE8 call line.
- post0b 46050 (NCC): 92.20 -> 92.23, from `charw = ...; lineh = ...;`.
- game_uso 7C1C (NCC): 96.331 -> 96.347, from `result.z = d.z; result.x = d.x;`.
- post0b 415A4 (C): 94.49 -> 94.59, from `t->a8 = 320; t->aC = 240;` (the order swapped as well as joined).

Flat (no join scored above base): 31A74, 250C8, 30AF4, 2E354, 40304, 35B1C, 5A2C4, 591C, B3C,
bootup E68 / B75C, and the NCC donors 41D40, 37938, 3B9C0, 4BAF4, 36694, 4C5E4, 97EC, 1DDC, 48AEC, 4F2DC, 493AC,
3E5E0, 3AE58, 46790, 3DF58, 34890, 3B2EC, 454C4, BB8C, gui 329C / F04, bootup C234 / 55A0.

## kit CCXXXIV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 227): bootup 90CC EXACT (8424 bytes) -- as1 issues equal-ready instructions in SOURCE-LINE order; a store that must precede a call can be given a line AFTER the call's line with a goto block <a name="kit-ccxxxiv-agent-c-run227"></a>

The last two 90CC rows (cfe donor 99.904) were as1 reorders. Both closed by source layout alone.

- **Rule (measured on a 15-line repro, `t1.c` shape below).** Inside one as1 block (call to call), as1
  issues instructions by readiness first (an operand loaded earlier wins: `v.x = a5` stores before `v.z = a6`
  even when `v.z` is written first in the source, because the a5 stack load comes first). Between two
  instructions that are ready at the same time, the one whose `.loc` line is LOWER goes first; on the same
  line it is not simply input order (the 90CC id load went behind the address it preceded in the input,
  see the loop item). Source order of independent statements, `if (1) {}` after them, comma
  expressions inside the call and one-line layouts did not change the order of `v.z = a6` vs the call's
  stack-argument `swc1 a6, 0x10(sp)` (both ready on the same f2): ugen always emits the side effect before
  the call's argument stores, and both carry the call statement's line or an earlier one.
- **The goto block.** A statement written textually AFTER the call but executed before it gets a later line:
  ```c
  vpos.x = arg5;
  vpos.y = 0.0f;
  goto bu_90cc_lz;
  bu_90cc_lc: call(D, 1, &vpos.y, arg5, arg6); goto bu_90cc_le;
  bu_90cc_lz: if (1) {} vpos.z = arg6; goto bu_90cc_lc;
  bu_90cc_le: ;
  ```
  uopt straightens the jumps (no branch code), and the `if (1) {}` keeps the moved block's own line (without it
  the store is relabelled with the `goto` line, which is before the call: no change). The stack-argument store
  then precedes the `vpos.z` store, as in the target. Same words, same frame.
- **Loop preheader version.** The d148 walk loaded its first id (`lw v1, 0(t6)`) one slot before the d148
  address `addiu`. The preheader code (arg reload, address) carries the `do {` line; `cg = *d00_b;` on its own
  line before it is lower and is issued first. Writing `cg = ...; do {` on ONE line ties the lines, and the
  load drops behind the address as in the target. Moving the statement above or below the address
  assignment, or joining it with other lines, did nothing.
- **Same rule, other direction (bootup 24B8 NM 98.91 -> 99.02).** `s0 = (char *)((cfg & 0x400) != 0);` then
  `f((int)s0, (cfg2 & 0x1000) != 0, ...)`: the a0 compare carries the earlier line and went first; the target
  issues the a1 compare first. Both statements on ONE line tie the lines and as1 then emits a1 first. A
  join sweep (every adjacent pair of lines, 61 variants) over the rest of 24B8 and over E2D0 / 31C0 / 63964 /
  C310 found nothing else: their rows are colouring / frame homes.
- **Negative (timproc_b5 C310):** the `addiu s6, s2, 0x230` / `addiu s4, sp, 0x9c` preheader swap is not this
  class: a named local for `arg1 + 0x230` at 16 positions and 41 join / move layouts of the preheader all
  scored base. The hoisted invariant's order there comes from uopt, not from as1 lines.
- **Landing notes.** A `.c` donor that becomes a prerequisite of the MATCHING object inherits that object's
  target-specific variables: `TRUNCATE_TEXT` and `SUFFIX_BYTES_FORCE` on bootup_uso.c.o had to become
  `private` (else the donor build runs inject-suffix for functions it does not have). Pin values come from the
  target relocs, not the old NM pins: `bu_90cc_d148_18` was 0 (fine for the reloc-blind NM score) and must be
  0x160 (`func_00000148 + 0x18`) for ROM bytes. Compute each pin as target symbol + target addend - donor
  addend from the HI16/LO16 immediates of both objects (a per-function script, /tmp/claude-1000/c227/pins.py).

## kit CCXXXV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 228): as1-order scan over the 81 non-exact functions; the line tie works on a hoisted loop-entry load (4B2F4 98.37 -> 99.36), not on prologue / priority / spill / delay-slot reorders <a name="kit-ccxxxv-agent-c-run228"></a>

- **Scan.** objdump both objects (target `expected/`, base `build/non_matching/`), cut blocks after each
  branch delay slot, key each instruction by mnemonic + non-register operands (lui/addiu/ori immediates and
  non-sp load/store offsets wildcarded), and flag blocks whose key multiset is equal but whose order differs.
  Equal-length functions only. 13 functions have such a block; most are not as1 line ties.
- **Hit (NCC donor game_libs_func_0004B2F4).** The matrix loop's preheader: target `addiu t2` (row bound) /
  `addiu a0` (a) before `lw t1, 0xE4(t3)` (b); ours loaded b first. `b = ...;` then `a = ...;` each on its
  own line: b's line is lower, so it goes first. Swapping the two lines or joining only the two did nothing;
  joining b, a AND the `for (i = 0; ...) {` line onto one line (the bound / a addresses carry the `for` line)
  ties them and as1 then issues b last: 98.37 -> 99.36, registers only left. Same as the CCXXXIV `do {` case:
  when a load must issue after loop-setup addresses, put it on the loop header's line.
- **Hit (kernel func_80001594, cfe; 96.80 -> 99.82).** A 28-store callback-table fill (`*(s32 *)(cb + K) = addr;`).
  Three as1 reorders, all closed by layout:
  - A CSE'd address used by several stores (uopt keeps `14A8 + 0x24` in a0 for the 0x84 / 0x88 / 0x8C stores)
    issues at the line of its EARLIEST use. Moving one use line did nothing (the other early use still set
    the line); moving BOTH early uses (0x84 and 0x88) together to just after the 0x68 store put the `lui a0`
    after the 0x64 / 0x68 stores as in the target (pair sweep, 81 layouts: one position wins).
  - Loop-entry addresses: target `lui a0, %hi(bound)` before `lui v1, %hi(p)` / `lui v0, %hi(q)`: `p = ...; q = ...;
    do {` on ONE line (the bound carries the `while` line; the tie lets it lead). Two lines or q-first: no.
  - Loop body: target `sltu` (the while test) before `sw zero, 0(p)`: `*p = 0; q[-0x2A] = 0; p++;` on one line
    (48-variant join x order grid; every winner has the three statements on one line after `q += 0x9C;`).
  Left: the second CSE'd constant (`480 + 0x30`) colours a1, target a2 (single-line moves of both uses, a named
  local, `if (1) {}` after each store, `i = 0` hoists: base or worse).
- **Not line ties (each probed with joins / goto blocks, all at base or worse):**
  - bootup 6204 / E9FC `lui a0` before `sw ra`: one-line function, goto block with `if (1) {}`, return
    value, array extern, varargs prototype, local pointer, NCC (`extern "C"` and a member function) -- the
    prologue ra save always issues first. Not reachable through lines.
  - mgrproc 2B7C `lw a3, 0xD4(a0)` above the four volatile 1.0f stores: same-line, after-line and goto-block
    layouts change nothing (the load heads the switch's critical path: priority, not a tie); putting the
    load after the stores in source makes uopt read it from s4. A copy `self = arg0` coalesces.
  - post0b 5F5F0 `sw a1, 0xA0(sp)` (home store) after the v[] stores before the normalise call: NCC does not
    straighten a goto block that holds `if (1) {}` (real branches, 58.7); without it the home store moves
    further down (98.54). One-line `v[..]; call(v);` = base.
  - post0b 59E80 early `li 3` / `li 0xFFFD` (ClipRatio constants): a 28-variant NCC join sweep is all base.
  - post0b 4E424 FP load order y1 / z0 / z1: 8 layouts of the three subtractions all base (colouring).
  - post0b 51AD8 delay slot (default arm's `lui a0, 2` stolen into the bound-check `beqz`): not a reorder.
- **Shared open shape.** titproc 116C (`sltiu at, t6, 4` vs our 5) has the same 4-entry jump table as kernel
  1ADC and game_uso B3C: IDO 7.1 / 5.3 at -O1 / -O2 / -O3 and NCC all lower a 4-label switch (int / unsigned /
  short / char / long long selector, with and without default, break or return arms) to a compare chain.

## kit CCXXXVI (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 229): 591C head store order (99.973 -> 99.977), the last 591C row is a coloring-priority swap, and first cfront-style cfe ports of 97EC / 7C1C <a name="kit-ccxxxvi-agent-g-run229"></a>

- **591C head scaled axis (99.973 -> 99.977).** A 144-cell grid (which of `x / z / scale` holds each
  component x compute order x store order x where the `if (1) {}` goes): the x component goes in `scale` and is
  computed first, the stores run Z, Y, X, and the bbsplit sits after the first store. That fixes the head
  `lwc1 0x318 / 0x320` order and the `0x148 / 0x150` stores, and it also flips the `bne v1, v0` operand
  order at the `0x4c4` test far below (the head temps change the global colouring order).
- **The last 591C row (the 0x204 selector outer: target f12, ours f2) is a two-LR priority swap, not a
  spelling.** The `z` variable (one LR: head Y component, scratch / delta Z sites, the 0x204 selector)
  colours f2 just before `fsel` (f12) in the constrained order. Moving the 0x204 selector into `fsel` fixes
  that site but drops z's priority below fsel, so the two swap EVERYWHERE (99.39). Moving it into
  `f12v` / `x` / `scale` / a fresh local / a direct `if ((...) <= metric_a)` (the cfe temp gets a frame
  home, +8) does the same or worse. Compensating moves (each tail selector group moved from fsel to z, each
  f2v / yaw_raw group moved to z, pairwise combinations of the 14 tail groups, all 47 def-to-last-use
  groups of every float local, z's non-tail groups moved to f2v / dot / ...) either move the f2 error to
  the moved selector or let the shared selector join temp drop from f14 to f2: z's tail use is what makes
  the join temp interfere with f2. `if (1) {}` after any of 224 statements, 153 call / literal variants
  and 149 line joins on the fsel-site version all leave the swap. Still open.
- **cfe keeps a stack-temp ctor guard.** `p = &t; if (p || (p = new12(12))) { ... }` (statement or
  comma-expression form) keeps `bnez; jal new; beqz v0` in cfe -O2, as in the edg / cfront targets. The
  folded form is `q = &t; p = q; if (p != 0 || (p = new12(12)) != 0)`: there the guard and the call disappear.
  No `p = 0; if (1) { p = &X; }` hack is needed in a cfront-style port.
- **cfe gives every declared local a frame home, register-coloured or not.** So the target frame bounds the
  number of named locals. In the 7C1C port, eleven scalars dropped into the target's 44-byte gap above the
  pooled slot gave frame 0x3B0 exactly. Fill the remaining gaps with `int gN[k];` placeholders while porting,
  then swap real temporaries in.
- **97EC cfe port (95.16; the NCC donor is 99.974).** Every edg temporary home put at its target address by
  declaration order (the NCC donor's only residual is two swapped edg temp homes). `vp = &s->w->vel` is
  bound BEFORE the guard: it is the reference argument, spilled across the alloc call to its home 0xEC.
  `Self **ps = &s` keeps s in memory as in the target, 80 -> 90.9; with it in a register uopt colours it into
  a3 and splits it around every call. `kk = s->k` binds operator*'s float argument. The other's-position
  `this` goes through the shared ctor pointer `p` (target v1, `addiu v1, v1, 0xb4` after the folded loads).
  Left: the FP colours of the ctor-argument values differ at every site (target a/b x f12 z f0, e x f2
  z f14, f x f0 z f12, operator* f2 / f12 / f14), and one shared tx / tz or one pair per site cannot give
  that. Files: /tmp/claude-1000/g229/cf/c97g.c (best), c97k.c (one pair per site).
- **7C1C cfe port, first pass (24.9 vs the NCC donor's 96.35).** /tmp/claude-1000/g229/cf/c7c5.c is
  the NCC donor's semantics in cfront form: the pooled return slots are ONE function-scope `Vec3 R`
  (s1, 0x354) for first-level results, plus P2 (0x21C) / P3 (0x1FC) for nested operator* levels and
  the loop's perp. Each operator* expansion has its own r / V pair, every home is at its target address, and
  the frame is 0x3B0. The structure lines up block for block. The score is low because `b` colours s4 (the
  target keeps it in its home 0x3BC; the target's `lw t6, 0x3bc(sp)` is the first t-register use), so the
  ugen temp ring is one register short everywhere. Next step: get b out of registers (cf. the 97EC `&s`

## kit CCXXXVII (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 229): kernel func_80001594 EXACT -- a CSE'd address that takes a1 where the target has a2 gets a2 when a LOOP INDEX's web overlaps it: write the following pointer-walk clear loop as a one-line index loop; 65EE4's `lui a2; ori a2,a2` is ugen's register-variable path, which needs a function with one call <a name="kit-ccxxxvii-agent-c-run229"></a>

**1. func_80001594 (99.82 -> 100, 544 B).** The last row was the `func_80000480 + 0x30` address (stored to
cb+0x34 and cb+0x30): ours a1, target a2. The `-Wo,-zdbug:5` dump showed its LR (adjsave 3.0) forbidden
`[v0 v1 a0 a3]` only; the only a1-coloured LR was the loop-2 index `i`, which did not interfere. Nine
splitter / `i = 0` / copy-local / `if (arg1) {}` placements were flat, and an `i = 0` hoisted above the
stores lost the loop inversion (75 %). What worked: the following slot-clear loop rewritten from the p / q
pointer walk to an index loop on the same `i`, all on one line:
`for (i = 0; i < 135; i++) { D_80012D60[i] = 0; (&D_800130A0)[i * 0x9C + 0x72] = 0; }`.
uopt's IV elimination still emits the target's pointer loop (bound `D_800130A0 + 0x5244`), but i's web now
reaches into the store block, so the address CSE gets a2. The one-line form keeps the target's
`sltu / sw / sb / bnez / addiu` order (CCXXXIV line ties). Splitting the body over two lines puts the
`addiu v1,4` first (`sw zero,-4(v1)`, 97.05); the two stores in reverse order give 99.07. A `do { } while
(++i < 135)` and `p = D_80012D60; for (i...) { *p = 0; ...; p++; }` are also 100. Splice notes: the donor
(src/kernel/kernel_000_1594.c) goes over a C-stub placeholder, not INCLUDE_ASM. The asm body defines labels
inside the replaced range (D_800016BC), and replace-function-body refuses with "lies inside replaced body".
The target's `.text`-relative and `.L800007A8` references are pinned as `func_80001594_L80000C5C` /
`func_80001594_L800007A8`. The target's reloc-less `lui 0x8000; addiu 0x1994` comes out as a
func_80001994 reloc, which gives the same ROM bytes; objdiff report scores it 100.

**2. game_libs_func_00065EE4 (-Olimit 1, 89.73): what the fallback really is.** With `-Olimit 1`, uopt
does nothing at all: the dump shows 0 LRs and 0 colours. The body is pure ugen -O2 on unoptimised ucode.
Micro-tests at `-O2 -Olimit 1`:
- `G.data = C; f(&G, 1, G.data)`, `f(&G, 1, G.data = C)`, plain / `u32` / block-scope locals and `register`
  locals all give `lui tN; ori a2,tN,lo` (li into a temp, then as1 folds the `move a2,tN` into the ori).
- `f(&G, 1, C)` gives `lui a2; ori a2,a2` directly, and so does `f(&G, 1, d = C)` with the store after the call.
- `register int d = C; G.data = d; f(&G, 1, d);` gives the target's `lui a2; ori a2,a2; sw a2` ONLY in a
  function with a single call. With two or more calls, ugen puts the register variable in s0, whatever its
  scope or position (`lui s0; ori a2,s0`).
So the a2-born constant would need a ugen register variable that does not cross a call, which 65EE4's 15
calls rule out. Also flat: splitting the macro into statements, joining it per block, or splitting call
arguments across lines (ugen order is per statement, and the whole block is one macro line anyway). The same
goes for 15 data / base / end literal spellings, char * / unsigned fields, `G.data = G.base + 0x10` (ugen
forwards the stored base), IDO 5.3 `-Olimit 1`, `-mips1`, `-O3 -Olimit 1`, `-Wb,-O0/-O1`, and
per-field volatile casts (91.10 at 560 B, too short). `-g3` keeps the ugen order unscheduled and shows the
call-2 `lui a0; lui a1; lw a1; jal; addiu a0` is ugen's own argument order (load before address). The
target evaluates `&G` first. Arguments tried with no change: `&G.a`, `(char *)&G`, `extern S H[]`, `(&G)->base`,
casted-pointer chains, prototyped / varargs callees, an `S *p = &G` local.

**3. Negatives (no fuzzy gain).**
- bootup E2D0: arg4 colours fa1 because of the `if (arg4) {}` keep-live. Without it the arg4 load issues

## kit CCXXXIX (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 231): FLOAT OPERAND ORDER and TEST OPERANDS ON THEIR OWN LINE are the big unswept levers on FP-heavy near-misses (bootup C234 95.07 -> 98.17, game_uso 3558 89.98 -> 91.56, 2E354 93.94 -> 94.23, B75C 94.01 -> 94.37); stale folded uses are worth re-dropping (4BAF4 96.36 -> 96.82) <a name="kit-ccxxxix-agent-g-run231"></a>

_No exact. report.json (non_matching build): bootup C234 95.07 -> 98.17 (2200 B), game_uso 3558 89.98 -> 91.56 (1008 B),
post0b 4BAF4 96.36 -> 96.82 (1692 B), bootup B75C 94.01 -> 94.37 (2096 B), post 2E354 93.94 -> 94.23 (3684 B),
post0b 4C5E4 88.67 -> 88.69 (836 B); the same commute sweep over older agent-g donors: game_uso 8CD8 89.51 -> 90.41
(2836 B, `speed * kDC`), post0b 3BE1C 97.60 -> 98.16 (1568 B, `cx + cz * w`), post0b 54E78 98.22 -> 98.66 (552 B: run
200's y-first `dot()` is stale, x first again). Leads not taken (other owners / length): post0b 469A8 95.12 -> 95.36
(`FW(0x204) * 4 + FW(0x240)`), game_libs 76F0 95.02 -> 95.80 with a hoisted `D_76F0[0x34/4]` test operand but
2308 -> 2312 bytes (try an existing temp). A zero-use-sweep re-run after these changes found new folded uses:
post0b 3B9C0 93.96 -> 94.27 (`+ 0 * (int)(self)` on the ok clear), 3BE1C 98.16 -> 98.34 (v1, v0 on the ok clear, vc on
hi), 46050 92.23 -> 92.27 (arg2 / o on the two cursor reads): re-run zero-use-sweep after every operand-order
change (493AC's hit, `pad0`, is 1936 -> 1948 bytes: not taken)._

1. **A compare operand on its own line (as1 line order, kit CCXXXIV) on an NCC donor (bootup C234).** The target loads
   `spCC.f0` AFTER the whole plane-distance expression it is compared with (`lwc1 ft2, 0xf0(sp)` right before the
   `c.lt.s`); as one `if (spCC.f0 < (...)) ` line the load is ready first and issues first. Moving the right-hand side
   into a temp assigned on the line before the `if` (`t = 4.0f + K * (...); if ((spCC.f0 < t) || ...)`) gives the load
   a later line: 95.45 -> 96.59. An existing f32 local works (any of five scored the same); a NEW NCC local scored
   0.06 lower (it costs a frame slot). Same trick, in-tree cfe (post 2E354): `temp_v1 = o->m48; if (temp_v1 == 0)`
   at two sites and `temp_f0 = D[0x172C/4]; if (temp_f0 < o->mC)`, reusing temps that are assigned before every
   later read: 93.94 -> 94.23 with the 0x80 frame kept. A fresh cfe local scored similarly but grew the frame
   0x80 -> 0x88 (it took a home): reuse an existing dead temp instead.
2. **Operand order inside FP expressions is a separate lever from statement order (C234, 3558, B75C, 4C5E4).** ugen
   emits an operand's loads in tree order and as1 only breaks ties by line, so `a * b` vs `b * a` and the order of the
   terms of a sum change the load / multiply sequence and the colouring. C234 after item 1: each product written
   `member * spCC.field` (the target loads the member first) -> 96.75, the scale `K * (sum)` -> 97.49,
   `4.0f + K * (sum)` -> 98.17 (`(K * sum) + 4.0f` 97.49; the other sum-term orders 94.6 - 97.4). 3558 (three greedy
   rounds): `len2() = y*y + x*x + z*z`, the z row `m02*vx + m22*vz + m12*vy`, `k2 = f118 * (mag - fB8)`. B75C:
   `(f64)ptr * 0.015 + (f64)o->A70` product first, `temp_f14 * o->m3D0`. These change FP rounding order in principle,
   which is the point: the target's own order is the one that compiles to its bytes.
   Sweep: `/tmp/claude-1000/g231/commute.py --src <donor or src/*.c> --fn F --target expected/...o [--out best.cpp]`
   (adjacent swaps in every top-level `*` / `+` chain of a parenthesised group or assignment rhs, all permutations for
   3-4 term chains; skips address arithmetic and comma lists; `--out` writes the best variant for greedy rounds on a
   standalone donor). `/tmp/claude-1000/g231/hoist.py` (item 1 with a new local, discovery only: rediscovers the
   C234 hit on the old donor), `/tmp/claude-1000/g231/dropfold.py` (drop each `+ 0 * X` term / `if (x) {}`),
   `/tmp/claude-1000/g231/join.py` (k-line joins). All reuse lever-sweep.py's probe (standalone and in-tree).
3. **Re-drop stale folded uses (post0b 4BAF4).** Agent-c's run-209 `+ 0 * w` on the ctx load was a gain then; after
   run 211's `+ 0 * (int)(spr->w)` it is a loss: dropping it gives 96.36 -> 96.82. Run dropfold.py after every
   structural change to a donor that carries folded terms.
4. **C234 pool load above the 0x9A2 store (line order).** `o->m9D0 = D_bu_ro_pool[0x920/4];` written before
   `o->m9A2 = 0;` makes the pool `lwc1` issue before the four spCC stores as in the target (store order unchanged):
   95.07 -> 95.45. A temp for the pool value on an earlier line moved the load too but cost the `at` order / frame.
5. **NCC frame slots (C234 negative / mechanism).** NCC gives a frame slot to every USED local in declaration order
   (descending addresses); unused ones (never referenced) get none, and an unused struct gets none either. A uopt
   spill (the target's `sw a1, 0x3c(sp)`) goes to a temp area at the bottom, not to the variable's declared slot.
   Moving `sp40` last, block-scope `hx/hy/hz` to function scope and 5 / 2 / 2 scalars between the structs reproduces
   the target's struct offsets (sp40 0x40, sp54 0x54, sp68 0x68, sp7C 0x7c, sp8C 0x8c) with frame 0xf8, but spB4 /
   spCC stay 4 high and the spill lands at 0x34 (target 0x3c), and the score drops (98.17 -> 98.15): objdiff
   weighs sp-offset rows lightly, so frame fitting is not worth it until the colouring rows are gone.
   Negatives: line joins (k = 2 / 3) on C234 / B75C / 2E354 / 3558 / 46050, the hoist sweep on 3B9C0 / 36694 /
   48AEC / 4C5E4 / 46050 / 3558 / 2DE0 / 55A0 / E68 / 5A2C4, the commute sweep on E68 / 5A2C4 / 46050 / 48AEC /
   493AC / 4F2DC / 2DE0 / 55A0 / kernel 18F0, dropfold on all of them; 46050 dsdx / dtdy / s / t named before the
   texrect macro (91.4 - 92.2, base 92.23).

## kit CCXL (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 230): game_uso 7C1C cfront-style cfe port 27.7 -> 98.52 (NCC donor was 96.35) -- `hit != 0` / its negation as spilled CSE values, shared set() temporaries, firstUseCost empty blocks for an un-held &local, a do-while block that keeps a reference temp coloured (as1 then sinks the `addiu` past the loads), a flag re-read after its stores (forwarded value), as1 line ties <a name="kit-ccxl-agent-c-run230"></a>

(was the NCC donor). Started from agent-g's /tmp/claude-1000/g229/cf/c7c7.c (27.7, frame 0x3B0, 1055 words)._

objdiff's fuzzy is ALIGNMENT-bound on a port this size: c7c7 at 27.7 was structurally almost right, and one change
that fixed a 9-word gap in the loop head jumped it to 85.9. Get the length and block shape right before colours.
Scorer: compile standalone, `objdiff-cli diff -1 expected/... -2 x.o -c functionRelocDiffs=none` (0.2 s / variant,
so coordinate descent over per-site macro choices with 6 threads covers ~150 variants in ~10 s).

1. **`!hit` and `if (hit)` the target spills as two CSE values** (`sltu v0, zero, hit; sltiu t7, v0, 1; sw t7, 80(sp);
   sw v0, 84(sp)` at the loop top, `bnez t8` / `beqz t1` on them later). cfe folds `!(hit != 0)` to `hit == 0`
   (27.7, flat). `(hit != 0) == 0` in the loop test with `if (hit != 0)` in the body: hit != 0 becomes one CSE,
   the `== 0` folds into a branch (85.9). `(unsigned)((hit != 0) == 0) || ...` keeps the negation as a value:
   both CSEs materialise and spill exactly like the target. The second spill word grows the frame by 8: move
   unused-home locals (n, pb at the bottom) into a placeholder gap instead.
2. **cfront's inline parameter temporaries are FUNCTION-WIDE shared variables.** Vec3::set(a, b, c) behind every
   operator* as `tx = v.x * s; ty = v.y * s; tz = v.z * s; r.x = tx; ...` (one tx / ty / tz for all twelve sites)
   took the products from ugen temps to the target's coloured f12 / f2 / f0 (85.9 -> 89.0); the operator* `this`
   through a pointer (`vp = &(V); tx = vp->x * s`) is needed or uopt propagates the loads into the stores. Which
   colour each role gets is the priority order of the three variables (permuting the names changes nothing):
   roles are moved by reusing the variables elsewhere (the sqrt result in tx, the threshold in ty: METV / THRV
   macros swept). The operator- / perp temporaries are a second pair (sa / sc: the target's f0 / f2 at those
   sites, while XZ(const Vec3 &) sites keep tx / tz = f12 / f0). Three third-level sites want the rotated trio
   (x / y / z -> ty / tz / tx: 98.33 -> 98.42).
3. **A pooled &local that the target re-forms with `addiu tN, sp, K` at every use but ours holds in a fresh s3
   (P3 here) = firstUseCost** (0.25 x basic blocks, kit run 111). Sixteen `if (1) {}` before `return result;`
   (fifteen are not enough) push the s3 cost over P3's savings: s3 gone, prologue exact, 91.4 -> 93.0.
4. **Per-site ctor pointers assigned at the full-expression start.** In the loop the target sets the XZ / sub /
   perp temporaries' pointers (`addiu v1, sp, 0x170; addiu a2, sp, 0x134; addiu a1, sp, 0x140`) before the first
   guard and spills two of them around the first alloc call: `p = &t170; pC = &t134; pB = &t140;` then guards on
   pB / pC, and the copies out of each temp read the temp BY NAME (`R = t140;`), not through the guard pointer
   (the alloc result). Pointer homes (pB 0x2AC, pC 0x1DC) taken from placeholder arrays.
5. **Pattern `lw v0, b_home; lwc1 56(v0); lwc1 48(v0); ...; addiu v0, v0, 48` (b in memory) is a coloured
   reference temp that as1 rescheduled**: the source is `vp = &b->pos; tx = vp->x; tz = vp->z;` with vp colouring
   v0, and as1 sinks the `addiu` below the dependent loads by adjusting their offsets (load-delay fill), so it
   looks dead. In plain form uopt propagates vp into the loads (`lw t2; lwc1 56(t2)`, one word short and one
   ugen temp more, which shifts the t-ring). Putting the uses in their own block keeps vp a value:
   `vp = (V); do { tx = vp->x; tz = vp->z; } while (0);` -- 95.39 -> 96.64 for the two XZ(b->pos) sites, 96.92
   with the loop's operator-(..., b->pos), length = target. The same block trick on perp (`do { sa = v.z;
   sc = -v.x; } while (0)`) gives the target's coloured perp temps: 96.93 -> 98.24.
6. **A constant store whose register is the flag's register = the flag is RE-READ after the stores.** Target:
   `addiu v0, zero, 1; sw v0, 0xa4(a1)` and later `bne v0, at` -- with `active = 1; s->active = 1;` cfe/uopt
   materialise the store constant in a separate temp hoisted above the compare (one extra word, every later
   t-register one late). The arms only store (`s->active = 1;` / `s->active = 0;`) and `active = s->active;`
   follows them: uopt forwards the stored value into v0. `active = s->active` before the first test too (else v1).
7. **as1 line ties again (kit CCXXXIV):** `result.x = d.x; result.z = d.z;` on one line gives the target's z-first
   loads; `mode = c ? 2 : 1` as a four-line if / else materialises 2 before 1 (target `addiu t0, zero, 2;

   `+ 0 * (int)(n1.z + n2.z)` (unit normals) to colour like the target (94.78 -> 95.39).

Last step: a joint 2-D grid over the perp temporaries (single-coordinate descent was flat) -- main perp `sc = v.z;
sa = -v.x`, loop perp `ty = v.z; tz = -v.x`: z takes the target's f0 at both, 98.42 -> 98.46 (x still f2).
Then the final compare's folded use moved onto what the target colours (the first sum in f12, n0.z in f2):
`+ 0 * (int)(n0.x * n2.x + n0.z * n2.z + n0.z)` 98.46 -> 98.52 (sum and n0.x still swap f12 / f0).

Left (98.52): b->width loads into f14 at the four operator*(width) sites (target f0, so z goes to f14): MULW /
MULX named-width spellings, commuted products (`s * v.x`), sa / sc trios: flat. The main-path third-level

line, METV / THRV / M2V / DOTV roles, per-site XZ / SUB / perp / MULS macro variants incl. do-while forms,
agent-g's commute.py (23 variants outside macros). Files: /tmp/claude-1000/c230/ (cd.py coordinate descent over
`{{a||b}}` slots, sw.py join / split / bb sweeps, ringn.py ring-normalised diff, best_*.c snapshots).

## kit CCXLV (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 233): an unhoisted in-loop `sll n,2; sll 4; addu p` step is uopt STRENGTH REDUCTION of an indexed pointer (`&buf[i * (n * 4)]`), not a `p += n * 4` increment; `*(T *)(int)&g[1]` holds a global's field address (sym+4 folded) in a register; reading one global through `(int)&` adds a held address that raises loop pressure; loop-counter reuse <a name="kit-ccxlv-agent-c-run-233"></a>

_bootup func_00000E68 (3036 B, cfe NM body) 94.59 -> 96.72 (report.json), length 3020 -> 3032 of 3036. No exact._

1. **Strength reduction vs a hand increment.** E68 phase 3 (one `gSPVertex(&vtx row)` per outer iteration) had
   `vp += n * 4;` at the loop bottom: uopt PRE hoists `n << 6` out of the loop (and, under pressure, keeps it in a
   caller-saved register saved around the call / spills it). The target recomputes `sll t8,n,2; sll t7,t8,4;
   addu s5,s5,t7` inside the loop and never hoists it. The two shifts (not one `<< 6`) are the tell: the `* 16`
   is the element scaling uopt's strength reduction applies to an INDEX expression. `func(&vp[i * (n * 4)])`
   (vp = buf, no increment) reproduces it exactly; `&buf[i * n * 4]` / `buf + i * n * 4` (multiply order
   `(i*n)*4`) do not (92.2, multu kept), nor do `vp += n << 2`, `vp = &vp[n * 4]`, a named `nn = n * 4`,
   for-increment / while forms (all still hoisted). With it the whole phase-3 block lines up word-for-word up to
   registers. Rule: an in-loop pointer step built from a loop-invariant count, with an unfolded scale shift, is
   `&base[i * (count)]` with the counter i -- write the index, let uopt reduce it.
2. **Holding a global field's address.** The target keeps `&dims.h` (`lui/addiu sym+4`) in s8 for the phase-3
   loop test. `*(s32 *)((int)h + 4)` holds the base and adds a separate `addiu +4` (one extra word);
   `*(s32 *)(int)&import_8001FFA0_h[1]` (also `((int)&h[1] + 0)`, `(int)(h + 1)`) folds the +4 into the %lo
   and holds the field address like the target (95.17 -> 95.31). Plain `h[1]` / `*(h + 1)` fold into the lw
   and hold nothing.
3. **One `(int)&` read as a pressure lever.** E68 phase 2 spills the loop-invariant `((ult + 31) << 2) & 0xfff`
   to sp+0x54 in the target but keeps it in s8 here. Spelling the LoadTextureTile width read (only that one of
   12 global read sites) `*(s32 *)(int)&w` hoists its address into an s-register -- one more live value -- and
   uopt then spills the invariant exactly like the target (95.31 -> 96.42, +12 bytes toward the target). The
   target itself re-reads w with a folded lui/lw there, so this is a pressure proxy for a value we have not
   identified (see 5); keep it only because it raises the score.
4. **Loop-counter reuse.** The target's phase-1 column counter has phase 2's j colour (s3): writing the column
   loop with `n` (assigned again before phase 3) gives s3 (96.42 -> 96.54; reusing `j` gives 96.49). A pair
   sweep that renames one local into another (`e17.py`: every A->B over the body) also proposes merges whose
   lifetimes overlap (k2 -> tlut "gained") -- check every hit's lifetimes by hand.
5. **Residual (E68).** The target's manager pointer is one variable split by uopt into t0 (entry) / v0 (phase 2)
   / s1 (phase 3) because phase 2 holds the vidx*2+6 / +2 / +4 reduction temps in s0-s2; ours keeps m in s0
   whole and those temps in t4 / ra / s1. Any separate phase-2 manager variable (m2, mm copies, with the home
   count kept by shrinking padq) makes uopt hoist `m2->dl` into a register (85-86). The target's two dead
   copies `or a3,t5` / `or t0,s0` after the cull packet are copies of the cull's vs*2 / ve*2 reduction temps.
   Also after the structural fixes: lever-sweep found one more bbsplit (after the phase-3 gSPVertex, +0.07), a
   now-harmful run-182 `if (1) {}` at vertex 1 (unlever, +0.16) and vertex 2 s-before-t (+0.02).
6. *Negatives this run.* post0b 5A2C4: lever-sweep all, 720-way decl permutations of sp38 / sp34 / sp30 / sp2C /

   head append took the target's v0 / a0 and the spBC value the target's t0 at once. Side effect that confirms it:

## kit CCLI (agent-c 2026-10-29, run 236): post0b gl_func_000578B4 EXACT (9676 bytes, +1.27% code) -- a call-crossing pointer and a later value that BOTH take ra in the target are ONE variable kept non-propagated by a folded read; adjsave = refs / units-with-refs, so a zero-code `if (1) { stmt; }` that spreads the refs over one more unit drops a variable below a tie group; a `lw tN; andi ra,tN` scratch load is the source copied into its OWN non-propagated variable first <a name="kit-ccli-agent-c-run236"></a>

Exact. gl_func_000578B4 (NCC donor) 99.985535 -> 100 report.json in two commits (99bbe684 99.9959, 3c9763d3 exact);
code 87.55 -> 88.82 %, exact 3210 -> 3211. Donor renamed `game_libs_ncc_578B4.cpp`, spliced over an empty
placeholder on both paths; the 15 `gl_func_00034458` calls go through the new 0 pin `gl_578b4_c34458` (the target's
blank USO jal words). ROM byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6, post0b NM length unchanged (clip 0x2eb00 untouched).

**1. Diagnosis with the zdbug:5 dump (kit XCIX recipe).** The residual (kits XCIX ... CCXLVII) was the s2_508 FD50
packet pointer `sp50` (t0 ours, ra target) and the following `arg2 & 0x1FF` load. Facts read off the dump:
- colours go by `adjsave` descending; equal adjsave colours in itab-bit order (the four `temp_t2..t5` shift
  expressions, adjsave 1.5, low bits, colour t2..t5 BEFORE sp50, adjsave 1.5, high bit);
- **adjsave = (refs) / (number of live units that contain a ref)**; pass-through units do not count
  (sp50: def + FD50 store in one unit, result store in the next = 3/2 = 1.5; merged variable below = 7/4);
- ra (colour 13) is taken only when v0..t5 are all forbidden; the tmem expression `arg2 & 0x1FF` is ONE expression
  LR across all six arms (ra everywhere), so sp50 = ra needs (a) no shared unit with it and (b) t0 forbidden.
  The only t0 users near the call are after the tmem definition, so a separate short-lived pointer LR can never
  reach ra.

**2. The fix: one variable for both values, kept a variable by a folded read.**
```c
s32 sp50;                                   /* was char *; temp_ra_8 keeps its home via the `= 0` pad line */
sp50 = (s32)( FW(FW(arg0, 0xC), 0x0) + (temp_a1 * 8));
if (1) { FW(sp50, 0x0) = 0xFD500000; }      /* def and FD50 store in different units */
FW(sp50, 0x4) = gl_578b4_c34458(...);
...
temp_ra_8 = arg2 + 0 * FW(arg1, 0x0); sp50 = (temp_ra_8 & 0x1FF) + 0 * FW(arg1, 0x4);
```
- Without the folded read uopt copy-propagates `sp50 = arg2 & 0x1FF` and the variable's LR ends at the result
  store (flat). With it the variable lives to the last tmem use, so the later t0 / t1 users forbid t0 / t1.
- Merged alone it has adjsave 7/4 = 1.75 and colours BEFORE the t2..t5 group (takes t2, 563 rows). Wrapping the
  FD50 store in `if (1) { ... }` adds a unit with a ref: 7/5 = 1.4 < 1.5, so it colours after them and gets ra
  (99.9959). Every other single-statement `if (1) { stmt; }` wrap that leaves 5 ref units works the same; the
  plain trailing `stmt; if (1) {}` form did NOT split the unit here (all 88 positions flat).
- **Scratch load.** The target's `lw t0,504(sp); andi ra,t0,0x1ff` is not a ugen rule: arg2 goes into its own
  non-propagated variable first (temp_ra_8, coloured t0 in that unit), then is masked into sp50. A plain
  `t = arg2;` copy is propagated (flat); the folded read is needed on BOTH statements (`t = arg2 + 0*...;
  sp50 = t & 0x1FF;` without the second read is 505 rows).
- Folded reads use arg1 words 0x0 / 0x4 (inside the descriptor, never otherwise read, so no CSE temp).

**3. Negatives on the way (for similar call-crossing ra/t0 pairs).**
- goto-reordering the w1 store before the w0 store (to put the t2..t5 defs in the pointer's unit): as1 keeps the
  IR order (w1 first), 57 rows.
- folded uses of the propagated temp_t2..t5 (`+ (temp_t2 & 0)`) are removed before LR building (identical).
- phantom loads at the arm head (4+) make sp50 ra but recolour the tmem LR t0 in all arms and grow the frame by 32.
- post-call phantoms (11+) separate sp50 from the tmem LR but leave t0 free (sp50 = t0).
- tmem in a separate variable with or without folded reads, with `if (1) { }` around the call / tmem / FD50 store
  (16 combos): sp50 stays 1.5 / t0.

Reproduce: compile the donor with
`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/out/NCC -c -G 0 -non_shared -Wab,-r4300_mul -O2 -mips2 -32 -Wo,-zdbug:5`
in a scratch dir and grep `>>>active<<<` for the bit whose itab line is `isvar M 4 -416` (sp50's home).

   declaration the ctor-argument temporary (created first) is BELOW the operand temporary. So edg prepends each new
   temporary to the block list and the list is homed top-down; named locals (`e` 168, `f` 156) are homed below all of
   the block's temporaries in declaration order.

   and the rest in a nested block:

       Vec3 pe;
       {
       Vec3 pf;
       XZ e(pe = (a - b) * s->k);
       XZ f(pf = s->w->other->pos - s->w->pos);
       ...
       }

   above its named locals pf, e, f -- so the frame reads pe 204, `a - b` temp 192, pf 180, e 168, f 156 =
   target, frame 272 unchanged, same code (the implicit Vec3

   99.9697) pf matches but pe / the `a - b` temporary are swapped; `const Vec3 &re = ...` lifetime-extended

   in the source; move each one to a named local assigned in place (`T x(name = expr)` keeps the code: the name gets

   expression, so the argument reads the register. The target materialises a fresh `addiu a1,zero,1` at both
   sites while the compares keep t0. A function-pointer cast to `(void (*)(int *, unsigned, int))` proved the
   mechanism (the literal becomes `addiu`, but the call becomes `jalr`, +8 bytes): the converted constant has
   a different data type, so it is a separate uopt expression and never joins the int-1 LR.

   int works, narrower types fold back to int) and that is semantically neutral -- best by retyping the callee

## kit CCLIX (agent-g 2026-10-29, run 240): the jump-table BOUND CHECK is synthesised by ugen from the table length, and ugen can only DELETE it, never narrow it -- `ugen -d` tree dumps show the mechanism; game_uso 57D8 vs 8CD8 proves a second (table-emitting, EDG-family) C++ compiler inside one USO; no spelling reaches a 4-entry table <a name="kit-cclix-agent-g-run-240"></a>

Re-opened the 4-entry table cap (`sltiu at,x,4` + table: game_uso 0B3C 99.9986 / 8CD8 90.41, titproc 116C 99.44,
game_libs 76F0 95.02, kernel func_80001ADC 94.32, about 11 KB). Kits LXXVI and CXL already read the cfe rule; this run
re-verified it, found where the bound check itself comes from, tested every "guard + check-free table" route, and
added new cross-function evidence. **Answer: still negative. Keep the phantom 5th label.**

**Tool: the ugen tree dump.** `cc -K` keeps the intermediates (`t.B` = cfe ucode, `t.O` = uopt output); then
`tools/ido-static-recomp/build/7.1/out/ugen -G 0 -mips2 -EB -g0 -O2 t.O -o x.G -t t.T -d` prints "Tree dump after
Build / Translate / ..." with every ucode node, its opcode, operands and `prior=`/`next=` links (use `t.B` and `-O0`
for the raw cfe ucode). Opcode numbers (ugen's name table): and 0x04, equ 0x23, fjp 0x26, lab 0x42, ldc 0x49,
loc 0x51, lod 0x52, str 0x7b, tjp 0x7f, ujp 0x88, xjp 0x8c, clab 0x11.

1. **Who decides table vs chain:** only cfe (`func_465d90`, `sltiu at,a1,5` at 7.1 0x4660c4 / 0x4662dc and 5.3
   0x4708f8 / 0x470b48, `addiu t5,tN,25` for the 25-gap cluster join). Re-checked: case ranges (`case 0 ... 3:`) are
   a syntax error; trailing `case 4: ;`, `case 4: break;` first, `case -1: default:` all stay `sltiu 5` (7.1 and 5.3);
   no cfe option string mentions switches/tables. edgcpfe 7.1's switch generator (`func_51d740`, statement kind 9 of
   `f_mbe_statement`) loops `lod` 0x52 / `mbe_load_constant` / `equ` 0x23 / `tjp` 0x7f / `ujp` 0x88 per case -- it has no
   `xjp` path at all. A C if/else chain over 0..7 never becomes a table at -O2 or -O3 (uopt does not build `xjp`).
2. **The bound check is NOT in the ucode from cfe.** cfe writes `xjp lbound hbound`, `clab length=N` and N `ujp`
   entries (N = hbound - lbound + 1). ugen's `build_tree` (ugen.c ~12860, the code after it finds the `xjp` for the
   table it is reading) synthesises `fjp (les dtype=L (sel) (ldc N))` in front of the `xjp`, sharing the selector
   node (`ref_count=2` in the dump). So the `sltiu` immediate is the TABLE LENGTH, always >= 5 from cfe.
3. **ugen only ever deletes that check.** It skips the synthesised `fjp` when it can prove the selector is masked:
   (a) the `xjp` operand itself is `and(E, ldc K)`, K >= 0 (ugen.c L4105f4); or (b) the two statements before the
   `xjp` are `str X <- and(E, ldc K)` then an `fjp` whose condition's left operand is `lod X` (or a cvt of it), same
   memory type / offset / block (L4106bc..L4107f8). Then (CXL measurements) the check vanishes when K <= hbound with
   lbound 0. There is no path that emits a smaller N.
4. **Every "guard + check-free table" spelling costs at least one word**, so none can make 0B3C exact (0B3C's only
   residual is the `sltiu 5` vs `4` immediate; the donor's own table length does not matter because the table reloc
   is pinned to the USO RoData offset, so only .text counts):
   - `if ((unsigned)x < 4) switch (x & 3) {0..3, case 4}` = `sltiu 4; beqz; andi; sll; lui; addu; lw; jr` -- the
     target shape plus one `andi` (rule 3a).
   - a CSE'd mask (`m = x & 3; if ((unsigned)m < 4) switch (m)`, or the guard and selector both spelt `c & 3`) makes
     the selector a register `lod R`, so ugen keeps the check: `sltiu 4` AND `sltiu 5`.
   - rule 3b can never be met by a source guard: cfe emits a `loc` node for EVERY statement whose line is > 0
     (`func_466804` entry, cfe.c ~162880), even on the same source line, and that `loc` sits between the guard's
     `fjp` and the switch's `xjp` (dump: `str R8 <- and; fjp; loc; xjp`). 11 guard spellings x 5 statement forms
     (if / if-else / early return / goto / while; 55 functions) at -O0 and -O2: no check removed. cfe's own binary search over
     clusters uses `tjp` to the low cluster and falls into the high one, so 3b does not fire there either (24
     two-cluster probes on `x & 3` / `(x + 1) & 3` / `x & 4`, int and unsigned).
   For 8CD8 (target `andi t8; sw t6; sltiu at,t8,4; beqz; sw t8; sll t9,t8,2; ...`) the masked value is used three
   times, so it is a register and rule 3a/3b cannot apply.
5. **New evidence that a second C++ compiler built these units.** Inside game_uso, the EXACT NCC donor
   `game_uso_ncc_57D8.cpp` has a 7-label dense switch (1..7 + default) AND a 4-label `switch (a0->0x64) { case 0..3:
   call; }` (no default), both as edg case-order compare chains in the target. game_uso 8CD8 has the SAME shape
   (4 labels 0..3, memory selector) as a 4-entry TABLE, while the rest of 8CD8 follows edg's temp-pool / by-value-
   return codegen (NCC NM 90.41 vs the cfe NM 86.05). One front end cannot give both, and the table one is
   EDG-family (C++ temporaries), not a cfe variant: look for a later/other edgcpfe that writes `xjp` with a
   4-label threshold, not for a C spelling. (Same-segment C example from CXL: exact game_libs 2FB74 has a 4-label
   chain; its 5-label switch [19, 32, 34, 36, 39] is a 21-entry table, i.e. cfe's 25-gap rule, not pcc's
   range <= 3n.) ROM scan of `sltiu` + `jr tN` dispatches: smallest table size is 4 (six tables in the five
   functions above), never 2 or 3.

**Nothing applied.** 0B3C stays 99.9986 with `case 4:` on an existing arm; 116C / 76F0 / 1ADC (agent-c) and 8CD8
keep their phantom-label shapes. Do not reopen this cap without a new compiler binary.

**Addendum (same run): the bound check's DELAY SLOT across the ROM (396FC / 51AD8 diagnosis).** A scan of every
target `sltiu at,x,N; beqz at,L` table dispatch (raw words of all `asm/` .s files) finds NO target that steals the
default block's first instruction into the check's delay slot: every one keeps the fall-through `sll` (or an
earlier instruction) there. Our as1 steals the default head whenever the default block is exclusive to the check
(as1 rule 2) and the head's destination is dead on the table path; every EXACT table function whose default head
would be stealable (38A28, 68990, 343F4, 2E290, 52CD4, timproc_b5 8FC8, ...) has the default SHARED -- table holes,
a `case K: default:` label inside the range, or default = the switch's end label. The only exclusive-default
functions with a stealable head are the open near-misses gl 396FC (`or a0,a3`, 98.66) and post0b 51AD8
(`lui a0,2`, 99.15), whose six / twelve table entries are all distinct and in range. A far case label merged
into default (`case 500: default:`, `case -500: default:`) does add a predecessor but also emits a compare
block (+4..6 words). So the "default has a second predecessor" residual is consistent with the same second
toolchain (an as1 / ugen that never steals into the bound check), not with a missing C spelling; treat both as
the same cap family as the 4-entry tables unless a zero-code second reference to the default label turns up.
Dead references do not count (standalone 396FC, still `or a0,a3` in the slot): `goto dflt;` after an arm's
`break`, `if (0) goto dflt;` before the switch or at the head of an arm, an unreachable `goto dflt;` after a final
`return` -- cfe/uopt drop them before as1 sees the label.

250C8 / 31A74 / 4E424 / 35B1C all re-swept flat this run, see 6).

   `it` lived in memory. Without the `&it`, uopt gave it s1 (callee-saved, extra prologue save): six post-loop

   target's sp+0x24 temp slot but splits a second temp (frame +8, 612 B); 124-variant use grid flat. 40304: 120
   anchor permutations / named 1/32767 constant flat. 31A74: the ACCS2 store after both sel clamps gives the target
