## kit CCCXVI (agent-g 2026-11-03, run 269): a switch selector that the target keeps in ONE t-register across a call-bearing if-chain -- read it BEFORE the chain into a local and re-read it right after EACH call (not once at the switch); a store the target re-bases late is a DIFFERENT 0-placeholder base (decode, not a CSE lever); `(++*p & 0xFF) == K` for an ugen-temp increment test (post 2E354 98.15 -> 98.60) <a name="kit-cccxvi-agent-g-run269"></a>

_Commits fc9830c12, 705cb7929, 3b54b312b, 9ca35a961 (post 2E354, 3684 bytes = target throughout) and b733db137 (post0b 59E80 NM 98.48 -> 98.50) on agent-g._

1. **Selector read before the chain, re-read after each call (2E354 switch 6).** Target: `lbu t0,0x14(s0)` hoisted
   above the race test, the race arms test t0, and `lbu t0,0x14` appears ONLY after the three `gl_E354_setf` calls
   (in the `b` delay slots / at the fall-through), never on the call-free arms that store D_E354_1C738; the switch
   and its default arm (`addiu t2,t0,2`) use t0 with no copy. Ours re-read o->0x14 once at the switch (`temp_v1 =
   o->0x14; switch (temp_v1)`): the selector took a0 and the default arm needed an `or v0,a0` copy that stole the
   next lui's delay slot (one word long). Step 1: `sel = o->0x14;` before the `if (raceA ...)` (a u8 local) + the
   switch re-read into the SAME local -> t0, copy gone, 3688 -> 3684 (98.15 -> 98.24). Step 2: drop the switch re-read
   and put `sel = o->0x14;` after each call inside the chain instead (every read still sees a value written on all
   paths) -> the reload on the store-only arms disappears like the target. A global store (even to a `static`, or
   an absolute `*(f32 *)0x1C738`) KILLS the o->0x14 availability in uopt, so the target's missing reload there is
   not an alias effect: the source simply has no read on that path. Which local carries it matters (temp_v0_2 >
   temp_v1_2 > temp_v1 for the colours here); sweep the variable over every same-width local.
2. **Late base recompute = a second placeholder symbol (decode).** The target recomputes `lui v1,0; addiu v1,v1,0`
   right before `sw t8,0x14(v1)` although v1 already held the GA base used three blocks earlier. A distinct alias
   extern (GA2) is PRE-hoisted to the top of the arm (lui t7 at the block head) and a CSE'd GA reuses v1 -- neither
   is the target. The value semantics decide it: the 0x20 store is the fade COUNTER that the sibling arm counts down
   (`f = (1 - f) / n + f; n--` through `GB+0x14`), so it is `*(s32 *)(GB + 0x14) = 0x20`, GB's own LR (hoisted into
   the `bnez` delay slot before the arm split) re-materialised after GA takes v1. Byte-identical (both bases are
   0-placeholder lda's); the remaining open item is that ours still places the GB remat at the arm head (t7), the
   target at the join block (v1).
3. **Increment-and-test without a variable.** `t = o->x + 1; o->x = t; if ((t & 0xFF) == K)` colours t into v0;
   the target's lbu / addiu / andi / bne / sb run in ugen temps (t7 / t8 / t9): spell it `if ((++*(u8 *)(o + x) &
   0xFF) == K)` (`(o->x += 1) & 0xFF` is equivalent; `++o->x == K` / `(u8)++` / `(o->x = o->x + 1) & 0xFF` are not).
   Also moving an unrelated read (`raceD`) off the selector variable onto another local gave the target's v1.
   Together 98.45 -> 98.60.
4. **Switch-3 copy.** `temp_v1_5 (u8) = o->0x15; switch (temp_v1_5)` -> `lbu v0` + `or v1,v0` copy; an s32 local with
   a `(u8)` switch cast (`temp_v1 = o->0x15; switch ((u8)temp_v1)`) loads straight into v1 (98.24 -> 98.41).
5. **Negatives.** 2E354: GA2 / array / volatile / `if (1) {}` spellings of the 0x20 store at four positions (32),
   GB store at four positions (4), GA load / if-block reorders, `--` / `-=` spellings, index forms (16), selector x
   counter-variable grids (54 + 99 + 70), zero-use sweeps over 13115-13380 and 13425-13545 (all flat), the 128/130
   `lwc1 f2,0(s0)` schedule (7 spellings of the /200 + 0x16E0 sum), var_v0 (0x40 / 8) variable sweep (11). 30AF4:
   case-6 `gl_state.fC` through `sv` / casts / folded `0 * sv` in the switch / BB splits (26: the head lda appears
   only with `switch (mode + 0 * sv)`, 95.8), case-4 D_30AF4_h read forms (35): flat at 98.08. gui 0F04: kt() / kc()
   on each of the four appends (80), BB splits around the loader call (20): flat at 98.59. post0b 42938: next / nA-nD
   x `+ 0` x kt() per append site (115): flat at 97.60. post0b 493AC: kt() / kf() on each grid / ctx6C / tab68 site

## kit CCCXVIII (agent-c 2026-11-04, run 271): a DEAD conditional arm allocates edg pool temps WITHOUT live writes -- `(x * 0) ? (void)dummy(a) : (void)(live code)` holds the dummy's parameter temp through the full-expression (the live arm's temps land past it) while uopt folds `x * 0` and deletes the dead arm, so an entry like a new-temp's never sees a redefinition on the live path (bootup 31C0 99.995 -> EXACT); a compare spelled `max - 1 < n + 1` gives ugen's addiu-then-slt order and dropping a folded `& 0xFFFF` on a halfword store frees one ring slot (post0b 48510 98.73 -> EXACT) <a name="kit-cccxviii-agent-c-run271"></a>

1. **The problem kit CCCXV could not solve.** In 31C0 the target keeps edg's `obj = new Obj2` new-temp T live at
   sp+0x74 and puts case 1's `new KB(obj, a3v)` new-temp on a FRESH pool entry (sp+0x68), and the inline KB ctor's
   out-of-line base call `B2(o, ...)` reads T (`lw a1,0x74(sp)`), not obj's own home (0x78). edg hands out pool
   entries lowest-offset-first, and T's entry is free again after its statement, so a plain `new KB` takes T's entry
   (`sw v0,0x74`); every way of pushing the new-temp past it with a wrapper / comma dummy (kit CCCXV mk(o, a), a comma
   `(mk(obj, a3v), new KB(...))`, unused or kept dummy params, reference params) puts the dummy's first parameter on
   T's entry -- the store `T_entry := obj` (or `:= 0`) is a redefinition, so uopt's copy propagation of the B2
   argument stops at obj and reads 0x78. Dead blocks (`if (0) { mk(...); }`) and constant-folded `0 ? :` are removed by
   edg BEFORE temp allocation (no effect).
2. **The lever.** A conditional whose condition edg does NOT fold but uopt does: a folded zero on a well-defined value
   (`mode * 0`, `0 * (int)a3v`). Put the dummy in the TRUE arm (edg allocates the arms in tree order and frees the
   temps only at the end of the full-expression) and the real code in the FALSE arm:
   ```
   inline char *dm(char *a) { if (0) { a = 0; } return a; }   /* kept parameter -> one pool temp */
   ...
   case 1:
       (mode * 0) ? (void)dm(a3v) : (void)(h = (char *)new KB(obj, a3v), v = (char *)new WV(a3v, a3v, D_74B0));
       fn_link(obj, v);
   ```
   dm's temp (and its return temp) take the free entries first, the KB new-temp lands on the next fresh one (0x68), uopt
   deletes the dead arm and its stores, and on the live path T's entry still holds T: the B2 argument (KB's `o` :=
   obj := T, two copy levels are fine) reads 0x74. Zero code: same 808 bytes.
3. **Where the live code must sit.** The real code has to be INSIDE the false arm. `(mode * 0) ? (void)dm(a3v) :
   (void)0, h = new KB(...)` (dead conditional as a comma operand before the code) still allocates the entries, but the
   dead arm's store reaches the join, so the B2 argument reads obj again. Conversely the arm's BB shape changes
   colouring: with only `h = new KB` in the arm the KB new-temp variable was coloured a0 through the join (h stored
   from the register, 804 bytes vs 808); with the WV new in the same arm and the link / field store as plain
   statements after it, every word matched except the tail's v0 / v1 pair, fixed by swapping the old BB-split
   `if (1) {}` for a code-free `if (obj) {}` at the same spot. A link call inside the arm read T where the target reads
   obj (a `(Obj *)obj` conversion did NOT block that inside the arm), so keep obj-home uses outside it.
4. **Frame / pool accounting.** The dead-arm temps count toward the pool high-water mark: a conditional with a non-void
   result (`h = (mode * 0) ? dm(a3v) : (char *)new KB(...)`) adds a result temp (frame +8, `sw a0,0x74` result
   store); void arms add none. Re-check the frame and re-balance volatile pads (31C0 kept its three).
5. **48510 (Strip::add) EXACT from 98.73 with two spellings** (no pool lever): `if (max590 - 1 < nv + 1)` instead of
   `if (nv + 1 >= max590)` (ugen evaluates `max590 - 1` first, then `slt at, nv, t` -- the target's lw / addiu -1 / slt;
   `nv >= max590 - 1` and five other spellings do not), and `out[k] = idx[k];` instead of `idx[k] & 0xFFFF` on the s16
   store (the folded mask burned the ugen ring slot that was the one-register offset left in the copy loop). Found by
   the comparison-spelling grid after the fixed zero-use harness came up empty.
6. **Harness fix.** zero-use-sweep.py did not apply the donor's objcopy renames, so mangled C++ donors (48510
   `add__5Strip...`, 54E78 `reflect__3Obj...`, 36694, 4B620) failed to score. A copy at /tmp/claude-1000/c271/zs/ adds
   `--rename OLD=NEW` (repeatable) and by default reads the `--redefine-sym` pairs from the Makefile recipe that builds
   `--src`; lever-sweep.py's probe applies them before the auto-pick. For a member function also pass `--lines` covering
   the body (the def-check otherwise treats its parameters as maybe-unset). With it: 54E78 (+ / |, --exprs), 48510,
   36694, 4B620 zero-use sweeps all flat.
7. **Negatives this run.** 34890: the two ternary results are pool temps (zdbug:1: first M-16 := data / := 0 -> v0,
   bottom M-12 -> a1); the target's a2 / v1 = the colours of the `a` (M-24) and Base-this (M-36) entries. A kept
   dummy in the for-condition (`k1(o) ? 0 : (T)`) moves them to v1 / a2 (swapped) but recolours the alloc cascade
   (98.62); dead-arm dummies, `void *d` result variables, explicit `if (C1) do ... while (C2)` (frame +8): no gain.
   36694: dead-arm / comma dummies around the bound difference change the frame (232 / 716 B); unused V3 ctor parameters
   take no entry (set() body). E2D0 (cfe): empty FP tests emit code in cfe; `if (arg4) {}` moves and scale spellings

31A74 97.7305 (564)._

0. **Unfolded constant-OR chain = a store-forwarded read-back (415A4).** The target writes the +0x28 mode word as
   `addiu v0,1030` (hoisted with the record's other constants) ... `ori v0,v0,6` ... `ori v0,v0,0x400; sw v0,40(at)`,
   although 1030 | 6 | 0x400 == 1030. uopt folds `v = 1030; v |= 6; v |= 0x400` completely (no ori, even with BB
   splits or `v = 1030` moved into an earlier block: 128 placements). Reading the value back from the word just
   stored -- `t->a28 = 1030; if (1) {} v = (float *)(t->a28 | 6); if (1) {} D_415A4_tA.a28 = (int)v | 0x400;` --
   gives the load-forwarded register (redundant-load elimination runs after constant folding), so the ors survive
   (here merged into one `ori 0x406`; a separate `v |= 0x400` statement re-folds: 96 three-step forms <= 95.58):
   95.58 -> 95.92. Use it wherever a target keeps arithmetic on a known constant unfolded.

1. **250C8: -O3 is not the unit's level (decided).** Repro: extract the in-tree NM body plus its typedef block into a

   the project flags. `-O2` reproduces report.json exactly (99.846664, 600). The SAME file at `-O3` (no static, so
   nothing is inlined; only uopt's level changes) scores 96.73 at 596 bytes: `lw t0,16(s0); bnezl t0,..; lw a2,20(s0)`
   -- bytesRemaining's CSE temp is coloured t0. zdbug:6 (dump compiler, -Wo,-zdbug:6) on the -O2 build says
   `24: 24 not colored, not splittable` for that LR (adjsave 2.5, forbidden only a0-a3, no t-colour taken by anyone:
   no LR in the whole -O2 function gets a colour >= 7), while at -O3 the same LR is `assigned (constrained) 7` and the
   hoisted constant 1 gets colour 8. The target keeps the temp uncoloured (`sw t7,36(sp)` in the bnez delay slot,
   reloads at the sltu and the AsyncDma delay slot) and the constant 1 in a3 -- the -O2 behaviour. So the inlined
   static of kit CCCXXIV cannot be the explanation (umerge inlining only happens at -O3), and no per-file -O3 split
   was made. Side facts for anyone revisiting: single-file `cc -O3 -c` leaves an 8-byte `jr ra; nop` stub for the
   deleted static (harmless for a REPLACE_FUNC_BODY donor, but not in the target TU); variants of the inlined callee
   (fontId as variable / direct ASYNC_ID(retMsg or asyncLoad->retMsg), pad, doneMsg, retMsg init, 96 per-use
   retMsg / asyncLoad->retMsg grids) top out at 96.73. Still-open -O2 question: fontId (case 1) lives in the SPILL

2. **bootup 24B8: latch spilled to its home.** The target's `sw zero,76(sp)` (jal delay) / `lw t0,76(sp)` is the
   0/1 latch `t` (k = 0 at the top) being live across the first 4-argument call in caller-saved t0 -- uopt stores it
   to its HOME (0x4C, so it is the first-declared local) and reloads it; there is no `r` out-variable. That also
   explains why the latch is t0, not v1/a3: its LR covers the call block, where a0-a3 are precoloured. Rewrite:
   drop `r` and `k = r`, give the latch its own `int t` (k = 0 / k = 1 / both `if (k != 0)` tests) and keep `k` only
   for FW(p, 0x3C); decls `t; v0; s0; p; volatile pad0; tb; v1; volatile pad1; k` put t at 76, p 64, tb 56, the k
   spill 44 = target (all homes on target, store in the jal delay slot). Score 98.23 < 99.05 because t colours v1

   live into the ramp blocks (empty tests, `+ 0 * t` counted uses, `t != (int)v1`: 23 forms) gives t0 but adds 2-6

## kit CCCXXVIII (agent-g 2026-11-04, run 275): a ZERO-CODE CSE candidate is a real live range for globalcolor -- place one so it takes the register the target leaves "mysteriously" unused (latch v1 -> t0); read who holds a register with zdbug:5, split a shared int into its two homes, then re-phase the folded uses <a name="kit-cccxxviii-agent-g-run275"></a>

bootup func_000024B8 99.05 -> 99.91 (NM, same length 700, 5 commits; only the final p reload register is left).
Findings, in the order they paid:

1. **zdbug:5 is the tool for "why this register".** `cc ... -Wo,-zdbug:5` (dump compiler
   tools/ido-static-recomp-dump, writes ./uoptlist) prints one `>>>active<<<{ichain|n} LR colour` block per LR
   with `adjsave`, `forbidden: [...]` (colour codes 1 v0, 2 v1, 3..6 a0..a3, 7.. t0.., 14 s0, 15 s1),
   `:::interfere with:::` and the `live bb` list. The globalcolor rule is "lowest non-forbidden colour"; forbidden
   = colours of already-coloured interfering LRs plus a0..a3 in a call block. A value the target puts in t0 with
   nothing visible in v0..a3 around it therefore needs an INVISIBLE LR in v1 (here: the latch, LR 0, adjsave 1.33,
   coloured last; forbidden [1 3 4 5 6 14 15] -> it took v1).
2. **Folded counted uses create such invisible LRs.** `x + 0 * (int)(E)` / `if (E) {}` keep E (or the umpy of
   its cvt) as a CSE candidate when E appears at two or more sites; the candidate is coloured like any LR and
   then emits nothing. Map an LR back with `-Wo,-zdbug:1` (`{844|0} 70 isop umpy{733}{0}` = the `0*(int)(*arg0)`
   product). Two uses of `arg0[0x4C]` -- an empty test after `k = 0;` (entry block) and a folded use in the gate
   block's `v0 = FW(arg0, 0x38) + 0 * (int)(arg0[0x4C])` -- give one candidate over the latch's blocks that
   interferes with the gate v0 web, takes v1, and the latch falls to t0 (a0..a3 forbidden by the gate call): the
   head became instruction-exact. The same candidate in the toggle test / `k = 1` instead lands in v0 (no
   interference with the gate web) and does nothing for the latch.
3. **Each folded use also costs one ugen temp-ring slot** at its site: after the head candidate the then-branch
   temps were one late; dropping two of agent-c's `0 * (int)(*arg0)` uses and counting `*s0` in the 0x14C copy
   instead put the ring back (a 576-variant mask/expression grid over the five existing sites).
4. **A CSE'd copy target stays in the variable's web only with a counted use of the variable**: `s0 = v1 + 0x14C;`
   became a v0 CSE temp (target `addiu s0,v1,332`); `s0 = v1 + 0x14C + 0 * (int)(*s0);` (s0 = cfg, set just above)
   keeps it in s0. Same for the 0x134 copy.
5. **Shared int split by homes**: the latch and the later `p->0x3C` value shared one int (one home, 44); the target
   spills them to 76 and 44. Two variables + a decl-order sweep that tracks every `(sp)` offset in the output (not
   just the score) found the order with the target's exact home set (4 20 24 28 44 56 64 76); score fell first
   (98.2) and rose once the colouring caught up (99.26) -- keep structural home matches as a base even when the
   score dips.
6. Empty blocks after the three cam loads (1 / 2 / 1) dropped the cam web's adjsave under the cfg CSE once (cam v1
   like the target); later the same grid was inert.
7. **The same lever the other way round** (99.63 -> 99.91): the cam web coloured before the cfg CSE and took v0. A
   second zero-code candidate, `arg0[0x40]`, at three sites that live ONLY in the cam blocks (`if (arg0[0x40]) {}`
   at the top of both clamp ifs + a folded use in the 0x14C copy) takes v0 there; cam then gets v1 and the cfg CSE
   (which never overlaps that candidate) gets v0. Recipe: list the blocks of the two LRs that swap (zdbug:5 `live
   bb`), put the phantom only in the blocks of the one that must move UP. Watch the int-vs-cast trap: an empty test
   on the raw `FW(arg0, 0x38)` made a second LR (the raw load, separate from its `(char *)` cvt LR) that grabbed v0.

Negatives: an `int` / `long long` return alias on any of the four placeholder calls (no colour change for the
latch); volatile latch (`sw` hoisted out of the jal delay slot); coloring-search.py depth 1 (EXHAUSTED);
lever-sweep bbsplit / order / volatile / denaming on each intermediate. A test `if ((char *)FW(arg0, 0x38) != v1) {}`
inside the k-block gave 99.91 by extending the UNINITIALISED cam variable from entry -- banned, not kept; it says the
cfg / cam swap wanted the cam web pushed off v0 -- done legally by point 7. Left (99.91): the tail p reload is a
coloured split piece (v0, adjsave 0.5; target reloads into the ugen temp t6) -- empty blocks / tests / volatile p in
the poll tail are inert or worse.

Also run 275 (no gain): 35B1C vtable-store order -- 12 statement orders and comma / bb-split spellings of
`o->0xC = &D` vs `p = q = o + 4` (the store either leads the block or drops into the bne delay slot; never
between `addiu at,-4` and the spill); 415A4 116 compound / read-back spellings of the 1030 | 6 | 0x400 chain
(uopt always merges 6 | 0x400); 31A74 the swc1 / sb pair in the jal delay slot (24 clamp / store spellings; the
call-site spill is always last); 30AF4 `&gl_state` hoisted into v0 before switch 1 (sv / separate pointer forms
rematerialise); 2E354 c.eq.s / addu operand orders are not source-order (12 spellings inert); 415A4 the v30
pointer takes a2 (target v0; v0 forbidden by a split piece of self) -- 160 random code-free tests on self / t
fields, unlever / bbsplit sweeps, p or another symbol as the holder: inert.

## kit CCCXXIX (agent-c 2026-11-04, run 277): a permutation that maximises the objdiff score but puts loads / stores at the WRONG field offsets is a false optimum -- restore the target's own field order (score may dip a hair) and then RE-TEST every lever that was fitted on top of the wrong order: levers tuned to a mis-ordered body (ugen-parity casts, code-free tests) go stale and now cost score <a name="kit-cccxxix-agent-c-run277"></a>

Run 276's joint grid lifted post0b 5A2C4 98.47 -> 98.89 with a b / g / r read + convert order -- but the
immediate scan (kit CCCXXVII) still showed `lwc1 $f2,8(v0)` where the target has `lwc1 $f2,0(v0)` and
`sb t8,166(sp)` where the target has `sb t8,164(sp)`: the score optimum loaded / stored the colour fields in
the wrong order. The target order is the plain one (r, g, b, a reads, conversions and read-backs).

1. Restoring it alone: 98.8936 -> 98.8914 (a hair DOWN), but the raw mismatch count drops 88 -> 85 lines and
   no immediate differs any more. A random code-free test search on that base (`rnd.py`, 200 variants, one or
   two tests) then found `if (base) {}` on the F7 w1 line: 98.92.
2. The win was the next step: a singles + pairs TOGGLE grid over every earlier lever (remove each `(u16)`,
   `if (1) {}`, `if (X) {}`, `+ 0 * (int)(X)` one at a time and in pairs, 66 variants). Dropping BOTH the
   run-266 `(u16)` on the head `f & 0x100` test and the run-275 `(u16)` pair on the ED w1 fields (both
   ugen t-register parity levers fitted while the colour block was in the wrong order) put the whole head
   block (0x10..0x144) on the target registers: 98.92 -> 99.26, mismatch lines 83 -> 63. Either removal
   alone loses; only the pair wins (the two parity shifts cancel).
3. With the base fixed, re-running the full read x convert x read-back grid (200 random of 3456) confirms
   r / g / b / a is now also the score optimum.

Recipe: after any structural / order fix, (a) run the immediate scan to make sure every load / store offset
matches, (b) if a "better" permutation leaves offset mismatches, keep the target order, (c) run a toggle
grid (singles + pairs) that REMOVES earlier levers before adding new ones.

## kit CCCXXXII (agent-g 2026-11-04, run 277): a spill word that sits at the wrong offset with "unused words below it" is often an ADDRESS-TAKEN local's own home, not a uopt temp -- a scalar that is copy-propagated lives in a spill temp placed directly under the locals (its offset only follows the local count), while a code-free `if (&x == 0) {}` keeps x a memory variable stored to its declared home (call argument still forwarded in the register, reload after each call); then place the declaration for the home and re-grid the assignment's statement position <a name="kit-cccxxxii-agent-g-run277"></a>

_Commits 418b8ace1 (game_libs 2840 EXACT), 5726930e1 (post0b 3BE1C NM 99.11 -> 99.17)._

**The frame model (measured on 2840, NCC and cfe identical).** With p scalar, `p = arg0 + 0x2E4` is
copy-propagated: every use becomes the item arg0 + 0x2E4, which is live across three calls, uncoloured, and
gets a uopt spill temp. That temp is allocated DIRECTLY below the last declared local (M-vars, including
unreferenced volatile pads and edg pool entries), so its sp offset moves 1:1 with the number of declared
words: frame = 24 (args + ra) + locals + temps, rounded to 8; a local array passed by address adds one more
unused 4-byte word. Removing two pads moved the frame 0x70 -> 0x68 with p still at sp+0x20; adding pads moved p
down. "Four unused words below p" in the target was therefore NOT four extra temps (no code-free statement,
edg pool lever -- kits CCCXV / CCCXVIII dead-arm dummies, inline-param dummies, by-value struct temps -- adds
words BELOW the temp; pool entries are M-vars and land above it).

**The lever.** `if (&p == 0) {}` (anywhere in the function; folds to nothing) makes p address-taken: uopt keeps
it a memory variable, stores it once to its OWN home after the computation, forwards the register value to the
first call (`sw a0,0x28(sp)` + `jal` with a0) and reloads after each call -- the same instruction pattern as a
spill. Its home then follows declaration order: p declared after f18 (M-72 = sp+0x28), a pad where p used to be
(keeps every other home), one pad after it (frame 0x70). Second effect to fix: as a memory variable, the store's
expression is hoisted by uopt above the preceding `if (len != 0.0f)` branch when the assignment is the first
statement of the join block; placing `p = arg0 + 0x2E4;` after `vec[0] = 1.0f;` gives the target's join block
(arg0 reload copied into the bc1tl delay, the D + 0xCB4 lui above the branch). 99.97 -> 100. Diagnostic: if
the target's spill word is ABOVE some unused words and every other home already matches, try the address-taken
form before searching temp levers. `(void)&p;` and member / array forms (`char *pa[1]`, struct member, `*&p = `)
do NOT alias -- they are scalar-promoted like the plain local; a dead `if (0) { f(&p); }` does (same as the test).

**3BE1C (99.11 -> 99.17).** The target loads `this->col` straight into cc's colour s1 before the face()
expansion (`lw s1,132(s5)`, expansion `this` = `or v0,s1`, call argument `or a0,s1`); ours loaded it into t0
with `cc = col` after the expansion. `cc = col;` BEFORE the expansion and the expansion called on an rvalue of
cc (`(cc + i * 0)->face(i)`: a plain `cc->face(i)` uses cc itself as `this` and loses the v0 copy, 98.63) puts
the load in s1. The run-238 folded use in the grid test went inert and was pruned (kit CCCXXIX). Left: the off
spill temp at sp+0x50 (target 0x54; address-taken off with a declaration sweep is 95.2, so it is a real temp).
zdbug:1 shows the deepest M word at M-156 (= sp+0x54) and off's temp just below it at M-160: the target has one
M word fewer above its temp but the same 0xF0 frame (so 4..8 more bytes below). Dropping the run-195 `n_al` alias
copy puts off at M-156 but shrinks the frame to 0xE8 and loses that copy's colour tie (99.03); moving `r` / `d`
to function scope or inlining list() / cellOf() changes nothing or regresses. Also left: the ugen ring after the call (col / nrm / tris / t = t6 / t8 / t9 / t7 in the target; t as an expression
instead of the variable puts it in the ring but rotated, 97.98; statement-order permutations of ok / t / n /
n_al are flat).

**37540 lead (not landed, 96.43 kept).** Same family of slot diagnosis, other direction: the target spills hx
(the v60.x read) LATE (`swc1 f18,0xA8(sp)` just before the jal) to hx's OWN home M-24, while ours spills it to a
pool word at sp+0x48 -- in ours hx is the inline gr()'s local x (an edg pool M-var), not the declared hx. With
gr() expanded at the call site (`hx = s->v60.x; hy = ...; hz = ...; s->v60.x = 0.0f;` plus `if (&hy == 0) {}`
/ `if (&hz == 0) {}` so hy / hz stay stored-at-definition memory homes like the target's early `swc1 0xAC / 0xB0`)
and the declarations `vB4, hz, hy, hx, v6C, v90, p1 p2, b ab, pad, pad, a, s` every home lands on the target
(frame 0xC0, hx 0xA8, a 0x64, s 0x60) -- but the f14 / f16 colours of 0.0f / a swap, s is read once into t7
instead of per store, and the block V3 v1 sits one word low: 93.42 (r5 grid). Keeping the original gr() call on
that declaration order without the two pads (frame 0xC0) gives the target's instructions word for word except hx's
spill word (pool 0x48 vs home 0xA8) and the V3 v1 block (one word low): 96.42 (current body 96.43). So the open
problem is exactly "gr()'s x is a pool entry where the target's value lives in the declared hx": an inline that

**Negatives this run.** 250C8: OoT FinishAsyncLoad spellings (fontId variable vs `ASYNC_ID(retMsg)` with retMsg a

right after the second call (target: after the 0xBA000602 packet, whose pointer is t1), shifting every later

493AC (99.43) is a spread of v0 / v1 / a1 / a2 swaps (not attempted beyond the diff). 35B1C: written as a real
C++ ctor `O::O(char *a1, W a2, int a3)` (members next / M m / c, vptr at 0xC by cfront layout, inline `M() { v
= 0; }` giving the this==0 alloc(4) protocol) it compiles to the cfe body's code word for word (frame 8 bytes

after the sel clamp gives the target's `lui at` in the bgez delay but `swc1` before the sel home spill `sb`

## kit CCCXXXIV (agent-g 2026-11-04, run 278): a call argument whose C type differs from the parameter type (u32 message passed to a `void *` OSMesg parameter, u32 id to an `s32` parameter) is a CONVERSION node in uopt's IR: the argument becomes its own expression / web instead of the variable or load it converts, which moves colours and spill words around it; when a near-miss's residual sits on a value that is passed to a call, re-type the prototype to the argument's own type (the o32 calling convention is identical, so this is a semantics-preserving prototype fix) before searching statement levers <a name="kit-cccxxxiv-agent-g-run278"></a>

_Commit 06a137974 (game_libs 250C8 EXACT, 99.85 -> 100, 600 B, promoted out of NON_MATCHING)._

**The case (OoT AudioLoad_ProcessAsyncLoad with FinishAsyncLoad inline).** At 99.85 the last residual was
(1) case 1's fontId homed at sp+0x54 where the target keeps it in the uopt spill-temp word sp+0x24 that it
shares with the bytesRemaining temp, and (2) the retMsg web loaded into v0 with a copy to a1 where the target
loads a1 and copies to v0. The run-144 / 149 body read `asyncLoad->retMsg` in every case (CSE'd to the switch
load) and re-read retMsg into the same variable for `osSendMesg(q, (void *)retMsg, 0)`. Writing it the OoT way
(every case reads the retMsg local, `fontId = ASYNC_ID(retMsg)`, the done message sent straight from
`asyncLoad->retMsg`) was 95.66 with the original prototypes -- run 277 measured the same family at <= 98.65 and
called it a negative. Three prototype changes turn it into the target:
* `SetFontLoadStatus(u32, s32)` and `RelocateFontAndPreloadSamples(u32, ...)` (was s32): fontId stops needing a
  home -- it is copy-propagated into ONE temp shared by the status call, the index and the reloc call, and that
  temp lands in sp+0x24 (with the s32 parameters the u32 -> s32 conversions made two separate temps, frame +8);
* `osSendMesg(void *, u32, s32)` (was `void *` message, the C cast `(void *)` on the argument): with the
  pointer conversion the final reload is its own web (coloured a3, then `or a1,a3`), with u32 the reload goes
  straight into a1, retMsg's web splits a1 (load / selector) + v0 (case bodies) exactly like the target, and
  the constant-1 web gets a3 back. void * message 98.43, s32 below 99.3, u32 = 100.
The (s32) switch-selector cast had to stay (no cast 99.30), the unused `pad` / `doneMsg` words stay (frame), and
the old run-144 `if (asyncLoad) {}` / run-149 retMsg reload + `if (1) {}` levers are no longer needed.
Generator sketch (reproducible): start from the OoT body; grid {selector var, body var, final var (retMsg /
doneMsg / pad / inline `asyncLoad->retMsg`), fontId named or not} x {callee parameter types u32 / s32 / void *}
x {selector cast none / (s32)} -- the parameter-type axis is the one that moves.

**Where it did NOT move (negatives this run).** 31A74 `_f` / `_c` prototypes (int / u32 / void * first
parameter, s8 / int / s16 / u8 / char second, int / void return, 90 variants), sel clamp spellings x store
position x code-free def (36): flat at 97.73 -- the sel spill `sb` is always issued directly before the jal, the
0x1CAC0 store before it (target: store in the jal delay, so issued after the spill). 2E354 var_v0 (v0 vs a2):
the six switch-1 calls through void / (int, s8) / (u32, s8) / (int, int) prototypes, var_v0 typed s32 / u32 / s8
/ u8 / s16 with and without the (s8) argument cast (72 + 15): flat at 99.83, so the v0 ban is not the call

## kit CCCXXXVIII (agent-c 2026-11-04, run 282): uopt colours CONSTRAINED live ranges (>= 22 interfering LRs) first, by priority, and every UNCONSTRAINED LR afterwards in LR-ID order (the bit number = first appearance in the ucode); a hoisted loop constant that the target keeps in a low register (v1 / a0) is a constrained LR -- give it one more interfering LR with a code-free test inside the loop; a variable's LR id follows its FIRST appearance, so a declaration initialiser moves it ahead of everything (kernel func_800018F0 EXACT, 94.76 -> 100) <a name="kit-cccxxxviii-agent-c-run282"></a>

_Commit eefd4565b (kernel func_800018F0 NM 94.76 -> EXACT, 492 bytes, promoted out of NON_MATCHING; ROM byte-identical).
report.json reads 99.96 for it until expected/ is refreshed: see "Branch to a fake function label" below._

**Reading the colouring order.** `-Wo,-zdbug:6` (the dump compiler `tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/out/cc`
or `.../NCC`) prints, just BEFORE the `global coloring of FN` timing line, one line per LR in colouring order:
`N: N assigned (constrained) C` then `N: N assigned (unconstrained) C` (C = colour: 1 v0, 2 v1, 3-6 a0-a3, 7.. t0..,
14.. s0..; FP 24 f0, 25 f2, 26 f12, 27 f14, 28 f16, 29 f18). `-Wo,-zdbug:5` gives each LR's `adjsave` (priority),
`forbidden` and `:::interfere with:::` list, and the `index bit kind` table (after copy propagation) names every bit:
`isvar M 4 -16` = the local homed at -16, `isvar P 4 8` = the parameter at 8, `isop uixa` = an address expression,
`const------> 12` = a constant LR. Tools: `/tmp/claude-1000/c282/tools/dump5.sh SRC.c OUT FN` (cfe, prints the active
records), `dump6.sh` (same, level 6), `dumpN.sh SRC.cpp OUT FN LEVEL` (NCC).

**The rule (measured on 18F0).** In the run-281 body every LR had <= 21 neighbours except syms / arg1 / arg3 (23 each):
those three were `assigned (constrained)` in priority order, every other LR `assigned (unconstrained)` in ascending bit
number, each taking the lowest colour not used by an already-coloured neighbour. The three hoisted constants (12 / 1 /
-9, bits 137-139, created by code motion after every variable) were therefore coloured LAST: t3 / t4 / t5, while the
target has 12 / 1 in v1 / a0. Any change that gave the constants 22 neighbours made them constrained (the run-281 lead
`if (found == 12) {}` did, but it also made `found` loop-carried and constrained, so found took v0 and pushed syms to t0).
22 neighbours = constrained, 21 = not (18F0: 12 and 1 at 21 / 22, -9 at 18 / 19 stays unconstrained = t5 as in the target).

**What 18F0 needed, derived from the target colours.** With 12 / 1 constrained (priority below syms, so syms v0, 12 v1,
1 a0), the unconstrained LRs in bit order must give i t0, record pointer t1, slot pointer s t2, found t3, end t4 --
which requires found's bit to come AFTER s. The run-281 declaration initialiser `s32 found = 0;` gave found bit 6
(before arg1!); without it found first appears at `found = 0;` after `s = ...` (bit 35 > s at 28). So: drop the
declaration init (found is still written before every read), then add ONE loop LR that interferes with both constants
without being coloured below them: the store address held in a named pointer with a code-free test
`{ s32 *p = (s32 *)(off + (t = arg1)); if (p) {} *p = val; }` (the address becomes an LR -> 22 neighbours -> 12 / 1
constrained; in the loop copies the address shares t0 with the dead slot pointer like the target). The test must sit
BEFORE the store (after it: nothing). Last diff: an LR'd `addu` puts the variable operand second (`addu t0,t6,a1`);
the dead assignment `(t = arg1)` (kit at line ~3784, `x op (t = wanted_rs)`) makes a1 the first operand. Alternatives
measured on the way: `if (rel[i].off == 1) {}` before the store (98.32: 1 gets the extra use, priority 4.33 > syms,
so 1 takes v0), `if (rel[i].val) {}` (99.47: val becomes the LR in t0 instead of the address), `if (arg1 + off) {}`
(99.55: address LR but a2 in the loop copies and operand order) -- an unnamed address expression never reaches t0.

## kit CCCXL (agent-c 2026-11-04, run 283): the kit CCCXXXVIII creation-order rule in practice -- uopt colours UNCONSTRAINED LRs in LR-id (first-appearance) order, so a code-free test that makes an expression appear earlier in the ucode moves its LR ahead of a variable it should beat (gui 4568: `if ((s16)((x + w) << 2) > 0) {}` and a first-arm `if (y << 2) {}` give the Scis arm's xh t0 / y << 2 a3 / packet t1 like the target, 96.63 -> 96.93); most list functions have NO unconstrained LRs at all, and there equal-priority constrained LRs are also taken in LR-id order <a name="kit-cccxl-agent-c-run283"></a>

_Commits 9056cfd28 (gui_func_00004568 NM 96.63 -> 96.93, length 796 unchanged) and 4fbb06dc4 (post0b
game_libs_func_0005A2C4 NM 99.257 -> 99.290, length 1804 unchanged: `scripts/zero-use-sweep.py` re-run on the in-tree
cfe body found `if (base + 0 * (int)(rgba)) {}` on the F7 block's code-free base test -- re-run the zero-use sweep
after every structural change; a second round in `--lines` chunks, and rounds on E68 / E2D0 / 0F04 / 3714 / 329C /
3AE58 / 54E78 / 46790 / 4568, were flat)._

**Check first whether the rule can apply.** `-Wo,-zdbug:6` prints `assigned (constrained)` / `assigned (unconstrained)`
per LR. Counted over the run-283 list (NCC donors): post0b 4FD00 19 unconstrained, 46790 12, gui 4568 22 (+5
constrained); every other donor is 100 % constrained (36694 20, 42938 47, 48AEC 52, 4F2DC 30, 4B620 25, 3AE58 10,
34890 6, 4BAF4 43, 3B9C0 50, gui 0F04 46, 3714 37, game_uso 3558 21), and so are the cfe bodies bootup E68 (91),
E2D0 and post0b 5A2C4. In a constrained-only function the order is adjsave (priority) first; LRs with EQUAL adjsave
(common in loops: 0F04 has seven at 15.0 and five at 30.0) are taken in LR-id order, which is the only place the
creation-order lever still acts there.

**4568 (how the targets' colours were read).** Unconstrained order (bit numbers from `-zdbug:5`'s index table): the
Scis arm's packet pointer (`isvar M -44`) came before the `ucvtl` of `(x + w) << 2` and the `ushl` of `y << 2`, so it
took the lowest free colour first (a3 / t0) and they got the next ones. A code-free test of the SAME expression
(the bit is keyed by the expression) placed before the packet's creation moves its id ahead: the xh test sits in the
else arm right after `int xl`, the y << 2 test in the FIRST arm (the else arm would evaluate it early: code motion
hoists the shift to the test, -9 %); `y * 4`, `(y << 2) > 0` and `if (y << 2) {}` after the first-arm macro are
byte-identical / worse. Left: edg's first pool temp (M-16: the post-increment old value of the first next() AND every
MAX ternary result of the Scis arm -- one uopt variable, priority 6.75, constrained, v1) where the target has the
ternaries in t0, which then pushes y << 2's cvtl to t0 (target t3) and shifts the first arm's ugen ring by one.
Flat: unreferenced / code-free dummy locals in either arm, `DL::n` as unsigned / long, per-site next() / nB()
(`n = dl->n; dl->n = n + 1`) / nJ() / nJB() grid (81 cells), swapped arms (41.7), the 54-cell first-arm shift grid,
any LR-extending test after the macro (+32..52 bytes).

**Edg pool-temp slot merging is behind several list residuals.** A ternary result, a post-increment old value and an
inline parameter that edg puts on the SAME stack slot are one uopt variable; the target's colours show it merged them
differently: 4568 (above), post0b 34890 (the loop test's two ternary results sit on make()'s h / o parameter slots
M-12 / M-16 -> a1 / v0; target a2 / v1, i.e. presumably the slots of `a` (M-24, a2) and a ctor temp (v1); param-order / named-local / block /
while-loop variants of make() and the for test: flat), 4B620 (appends 1-2 count on the M-32 count var = s3, target s0).
post0b 3AE58: routing the first call argument through a zero-code accessor (`me(a0->x2C + off)`) does merge the
record-pointer ternary temp with a call-block temp (colour v1 -> a0, the target's is t0; below base); 13 other accessor
placements and dropping `if (a0->x2C) {}`: <= base.

## kit CCCXLI (agent-g 2026-11-04, run 281): agent-c's creation-order lever (kit CCCXL) works on in-tree cfe bodies too -- a code-free `if (<load expression>) {}` placed just BEFORE the statement whose web competes moves the load web ahead in LR-id order: post0b 469A8 96.02 -> 97.96 (field tests before the 12-argument call block, then arg0 / field tests found by re-sweeping), post 2E354 99.859 -> 99.891 (`if (D_raceD_E354) {}` before its load); and a value-preserving narrowing cast `(u8)(x & 0xFF)` costs one ugen temp without code, so it can move a run-209 folded use's ring offset to where the target spends it <a name="kit-cccxli-agent-g-run281"></a>

_Commits (agent-g branch): 0a4e4b316 (post 2E354 NM 99.84799 -> 99.85885), faa23372e (99.85885 -> 99.89143), f69ae70ac
(post0b 469A8 NM 96.01942 -> 97.52427), 46e8203fc (469A8 97.52427 -> 97.57282: `if (FW(arg0, 0x240)) {}` right after
the second `gl_func_00034458(temp_s1)` call, ahead of run 278's `if (temp_s1) {}`), 6be9fdaeb (97.57282 -> 97.86408: an arg0
load test -- 0x240 / 0x218 / 0x290 score the same -- between the a6..a10 argument locals and the 12-argument call), e08714cb2 (97.86408 -> 97.96117: a temp_v1 field
test -- 0xC0 / 0xC4 / 0xB8 / 0xBC equal -- ahead of that arg0 test); all at the target length (3684 / 412). Each
accepted test changes which later placement wins, so re-run the sweep on the new base after every step (rounds 2-5
on 469A8; round 5, 310 placements of 10 tests: every extra test is worse, <= 92.93)._

**Expression tests before the competing statement (469A8).** The 469A8 target holds `temp_v1->0x148` in t6 and the
held `+0x100` / `+0x78` bases in a2 / t1 (the 12-argument call's a1 copy of the vcall result is scheduled right after
the vcall). Variable tests (`if (temp_s0) {}` etc., 136 placements) and first-assignment orders (36) were flat;
the expression-test sweep (`if (FW(temp_v1, 0x148)) {}`, `if (temp_v1 + 0x100) {}`, ... after each statement) found
one placement: right after `temp_v1 = FW(arg0, 0x240);`, before the block. A second test of the SAME kind on another
block load (`if (FW(temp_v1, 0xC0)) {}`, or the 0x148 test written twice) adds another 0.58: 96.02 -> 96.94 -> 97.52.
A test of the inner load (`FW(FW(temp_v1, 0x148), 0xF0)`) is worse (95.15), and the test inside the block's braces
does not compile (declarations follow). Left: the a1 copy (`or a1,s0`) still issues after the block's loads, so
0x148 takes a1 instead of t6.

**Same lever on a global (2E354).** `if (D_raceD_E354) {}` immediately before `var_v0_3 = D_raceD_E354;` makes the
raceD load colour v1 like the target (`lui v1; lw v1; beqzl v1`, was v0 / v0 swapped with the o->0x48 temp). The same
test before every other global read in the function (13 placements) and before every o->field read (72): flat or
worse; the raceB load (v0 / constant 4 in v1 swapped) is not fixed by any test before it (a1..a4, <= 99.34).

**Ugen-ring alignment by a narrowing cast (2E354).** The run-209 folded use `(u8)(temp_v1_32 - 1) + 0 * (int)(arg0)`
cost one ugen temp in the o->0x32 decrement (ours t5, target t4) while aligning the ring for the rest of the
function; without it the decrement is right but the `sll / andi` of the 0x1C290 product (target t6 / t7) are one
behind. The temp the target spends lives between the two: `temp_v1 = (u8)((call(...) * 4) & 0xFF);` -- a cast that
changes no value and emits no code -- costs it there, and the fold-free decrement now matches. Folded uses placed in
the call arguments / product (`0x20 + 0 * x`, `* 4 + 0 * x`, `& (0xFF + 0 * x)`) are constant-folded before ugen

**1. raceB / constant 4 swap (2E354).** Target `lui v0; lw v0 (raceB); addiu v1,zero,4; beq v1,v0`; ours had the

constant went to a0; moving the selector into `var_v0` (its 8 / 0x40 web is dead in that block) gives the target's
selector t0 and constant v1. The last words there were the operand order (`beq v1,v0` target = constant first,

dropping the variable and reading the global in place at each compare (`((u32)D_raceB_E354 == 4) || ((u32)D_raceB_E354
== 0xA)) && (((u32)D_raceB_E354 != 4) || ...`, one CSE'd load, no store in between) makes raceB a load expression,

  off is spilled) that it also uses for `tris[i].d`, not `tris + off`; the donor read them through `off`, which gave

## kit CCCXLIV (agent-c 2026-11-04, run 285): an 8-byte frame excess with locals at the right TOP-relative offsets is a declared-word count BELOW the last fixed home -- re-seat a register-only local into a dead-stored pad's word (and pack an s16 into another s16's alignment hole) instead of deleting code; a BB-split code-free test can be swapped for a folded use on the next call's argument when the target needs the merge web in the SAME block as the argument setup; `if (0) { f = 0; }` dead multi-defs reorder a constrained LR without code <a name="kit-cccxliv-agent-c-run285"></a>

_Commits 4dbe4f58e (post0b 3B9C0 NM 96.52 -> 96.65), b5f885798 (3B9C0 96.65 -> 96.77), 4452a3a93 (3B9C0 96.77 ->
96.83), b49ba0b71 (post0b 3AE58 NM 99.63 -> 99.79). report.json before / after: 3B9C0 96.519714 -> 96.82796 (1116
bytes), 3AE58 99.63158 -> 99.789474 (380 bytes); NM lengths unchanged (no clip change)._

**Float identifiers in the zero-use sweep.** zero-use-sweep.py skips float variables by default; `--keep-float --vars
<the float locals>` found `ok = 0 + 0 * (int)(i) + 0 * (int)(nz);` in 3B9C0 (nz is set before the inner loop on every
path; the (int) conversion folds away, size unchanged): 96.77 -> 96.83. Run it with an explicit float `--vars` list (an
unrestricted sweep hits the 200 cap on the int identifiers first). Flat with float vars on 54E78, 36694, 4FD00, 0F04,
3714, 329C, 3558, E2D0, 5A2C4.

**3B9C0 frame 240 -> 232 (target).** The kit CCCXXXV counter (`NCC -Wo,-zdbug:1`, lowest `isvar M` offset; a script
is just the dump NCC plus `grep -o 'isvar *M *[0-9]* *-[0-9]*'`) read -124; d (M-72), p (M-48) and off (M-104) were
already at the target's top-relative homes, so the excess was the six words below off (v0 / v1 / ey / dx / dy and the
loop-block `self_al`). Block-scoped locals are homed AFTER all function-scope ones, so self_al cannot move up (making
it function scope changes code, 1132 bytes). What works: `s16 *v0` declared in the dead-stored `opad`'s place (opad and
its `opad = 0;` deleted: v0 is register-only, the word still keeps d / p on their homes) and `s16 ey` declared next to
`s16 ex` (shares ex's alignment hole above vt): lowest M -116, frame 232, code unchanged. Frame size is 8-rounded:
-118 still gave 240. Rule: list the M offsets, mark the words that are real homes (stored / reloaded), and move only
register-only locals into dead words above the last real home.

**3B9C0 dead multi-def.** An insertion sweep of `if (0) { X = 0; }` over the body found ONE position (after the ib
line) for X = f that re-colours the i * 12 tris base a1 like the target (96.65 -> 96.77). The same sweep with col / vt /
ok / nx / fv / v0 / v1 / ib / pp (320 variants), cnt / i / n / dn / t / off / nz / self_al, and `while (0)` forms:
flat. The remaining residual: f in s1 (target t4) -- zdbug:5 shows f adjsave 32.5 below vt 73.3 / ia*2 70 / ib*2 70
(the target order f, vt, ia*2, ib*2, ok explains every remaining int colour: f must land between 73.3 and the 100.0
dx / dy group); folded uses of f in the inner loop and `if (f) {}` tests: flat.

**3B9C0 inner loop as an index loop (decode note, not committed: same score).** `k = 0; do { v0 = vt[f->vi[k]];
v1 = vt[f->vi[D_3B9C0_t[k]]]; ... } while (ok && ++k < 3);` with an `extern s16 D_3B9C0_t[3]` gives byte-identical
code to the donor's hand-strength-reduced `fv` / `nx` pointers (uopt's strength reduction + linear-function test
replacement make the target's `fv++` delay slot and `nx != table + 6` compare). Likely the original source; `for`
forms (test at the top) are 8-16 bytes off. Keep in mind when a loop's cursor pair looks hand-written.

**3AE58 merge colour (v1 -> t0).** The run-272 `if (a0->x2C) {}` after the fv stores was a BB split: the entry merge's
block no longer contained the call's argument setup, so only v0 / s0 were forbidden and it took v1. Replacing it with
`gl_func_00000000(a0->x2C + off + 0 * (int)(a0->x2C), fv, ...)` keeps the extra x2C use (its LR still exists) in one
block with the merge: a0-a3 plus the x2C LR's v1 are forbidden and the merge takes t0 (99.63 -> 99.79). LEFT: the x2C

variable altogether (`if (var_v0_2 == 0)` directly) gave identical bytes. The zdbug:5 dump shows why: the `or` is
the LR `isop ucvt{<ichain of var_v0_2>|1}` -- the int conversion of the u8 source, which uopt keeps live from the
copy point to the propagated zero test -- not a variable at all.

**Fixing it.** The target's copy register (t0) is the colour of the switch-6 selector, whose 0x23-block web is
forbidden v0..a3 by the argument registers of the calls there. So (1) the selector role moves out of the pick
variable (var_v0) into a variable whose earlier web is dead there (temp_v0_2), plus one code-free read
`if (temp_v0_2) {}` in the D_E354_1C73C arm so its LR keeps the target's priority; (2) the copy goes into that same
variable at the head (`temp_v0_2 = var_v0_2;`); (3) the else arm re-reads the source before the test
(`var_v0_2 = o->0x14; if (temp_v0_2 == 0)` -- no store in between, so the value is unchanged and the load is
CSE'd: no code) -- with the source redefined on the use path uopt can no longer propagate the copy, so the copy is
a real `or t0,v0`. Alone that hands v0 to the copy's cvt LR (adjsave 3.0) and var_v0_2 drops to v1 (99.88);
(4) a BB split right after the copy (`temp_v0_2 = var_v0_2; if (1) {}`; also `if (var_v0_2) {}` or a code-free
`var_v0_2 != o->0x2C` test there) restores var_v0_2 = v0: 99.9294 -> 99.9403.

## kit CCCLII (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 289): edg frame-home ORDER rules measured on NCC micro-tests -- a class temporary that is a whole expression statement (`V3();`) or that is BOUND TO A CONST-REFERENCE PARAMETER is homed at the BLOCK TOP, ahead of every named local of that block; named locals follow in declaration order, then nested-block locals, then the inline parameter / return pool temps (by-value class parameters are POOLED: one home shared by every expansion); post0b 4F2DC's frame-top block is operator+'s const-reference operand temporary (95.7218 -> 95.733086 -> 95.770676 with an operand-order re-grid) <a name="kit-ccclii-agent-c-run289"></a>

_Commits (agent-c): e9b89715d (post0b 4F2DC NM donor, 95.7218 -> 95.733086, length 1064 unchanged, frame 424 = target),
39cce1b3a (operator+ operand order, 95.733086 -> 95.770676)._

**Home-order rules (NCC 7.1 -O2, measured with address-taken probes `sink(&v)` in /tmp micro files):**
- `int a; a = q; V3(); int b;` -> the `V3()` temporary takes M-4..M-12, a M-16, b M-20: an expression-statement class
  temporary is homed BEFORE the named locals even when it comes textually after one.
- `int a; a = q; *o = *u + *u; int b;` (operator+ by value) -> a M-4, b M-8, the operator's parameter / return temps
  below them: inline-expansion temps come AFTER all named locals of the block, whatever their statement position.
- `int a; { int c; } int b;` -> a M-4, b M-8, c M-12: nested-block locals after the outer block's named locals, before
  the pool temps. Sibling blocks do NOT share homes (two `{ SV s; ... }` blocks: two homes).
- A by-value class parameter of an inline function is a pool temp REUSED by every expansion (4FD00 probe: an
  `add3(V3 &o, SV s, int f)` helper gives both sums ONE SV home, where `SV s;` locals in the two inline expansions get
  two). A by-value copy is a struct copy (lwl/lwr/swl/swr for a 6-byte SV), not member loads.
- `const V3 &end = expr;` homes the bound temporary at the block top as well (4F2DC: end moved to M-24, 95.63).
- "Block top" is the top of the block the full expression sits in (-g3 probe: `*o = *u + twice(*u);` with
  `operator+(const V3 &, const V3 &)` -> the bound `twice()` result at M-12 above `int q` at function scope; the same
  statement inside `{ int b; ... }` -> the bound temp right after the outer named locals and before b); the inline
  functions' own return objects (`__V`) come after everything named (twice -52, operator+ -104).
- Below the outer named locals, nested-block locals and pool temps are homed in CREATION order: `int q; *o = *u + *u;
  { int b; } int r;` -> q M-4, r M-8, the operator temps, then b BELOW them (M-84); with the block before the
  expression, b is M-12 above the temps. So a target variable homed under the pool temps (4F2DC's end at M-340) is a
  nested-block local opened after those temps were first created (or a pool temp itself).
- Operand-order grids are worth re-running after any structural change: on the const-reference operator+ the 8-way
  per-component grid gave `V3(o.x + x, o.y + y, z + o.z)` (95.733 -> 95.771, 39cce1b3a).
- The DECLARATION POSITION of a class local with a user-declared (empty) default ctor is not free: 4F2DC's `V3 start;`
  moved from its use to before `Cam *cam` / `d = dir;` / the dir stores changes the code (95.11 at 1064, or 1044-1060
  bytes: `d * k` then reads the copy's registers instead of reloading d), although the home order only needs the
  declaration earlier. Treat "declare earlier to move a home up" as a code change, not a layout-only lever.
- **Naming the homes (diagnosis tool).** `NCC -O2 -g3` writes an ECOFF `.mdebug` whose local symbols carry every edg
  NAMED variable -- including the named locals of each inline expansion (`g`, `n`, `t`, the iterator `it`, the
  `__V<n>` return-value object) -- with its frame offset (M-relative), in block order; unnamed pool temps are the gaps.
  `/tmp/claude-1000/c289/t1/mdl.py OBJ` dumps them (HDRR at the section start, 12-byte SYMRs, st 4 = Local), and
  `g3l.sh SRC FUNC` compiles + prints `frame` and `off name` pairs. -g3 CHANGES the schedule (4F2DC / 36694 .text
  differ), so use it only for the home ORDER; on 48AEC the -g3 homes of the spilled g / g2 / cmd matched the -O2
  spill slots (244 / 232 / 256 on frame 352).
- **48AEC with the names.** Base (frame 352: `Ctx *gctx;` first, function-scope `Mtx *c2;` before cmd, unnamed mtx()):
  gctx -4, A -8, B -12, mtx -76, i / j / k -80..-88, c2 -92, cmd -96 (= the target's c at 256), then-arm load() `g`
  -124 (target -108), else-arm `g` -132 (target -124), first loop `it` -144 (target -144). The then-arm written
  `func_00000000(mt, cmd = gctx->mtx()); gctx->load(cmd);` (no push) puts g at -108 = target (only load's this / m
  pool words above it), else-arm g at -120 and it at -136; no else-arm spelling tried (push / push2 / push5 / me()
  depth / me(c2) / void* cast, 10 + 12) gives -124 with it at -144, and these then-arm shapes score 95.4 (registers).
- **4FD00 with the names.** Ours: a -12 ... d2 -60, the two inline sum() `SV s` at -88 / -108 (target ONE SV at -68).
  Two explicit `{ SV s; ... }` blocks with the named `p1` / `p2` floats folded into the test put the first s at -68 =
  target (the second at -88; frame 120, 71.5) -- p1 / p2 do reserve homes ahead of the nested locals; one
  function-scope `SV s;` after d2 shared by both sums (4 shapes): frame 112-136, <= 83.3. ONE nested block
  `{ SV s; <sum a>; <sum b>; }` (s reused) with p1 / p2 moved into a later nested block gives exactly the target's
  single s at -68, but frame 120 / length 988 (target 136 / 1004), 74.1 -- a layout lead for the next run (the
  missing 16 frame bytes / 4 insns are the inline sum() parameter traffic). Keeping the inline sum as
  `sum2(V3 &o, int f, SV &s)` on that one nested s: frame 136 = target and s -68, but 980 bytes (83.3): the target's
  length (1004) needs the per-expansion local-s code shape on a shared home -- not reached.
- The same dump works for cfe (in-tree C through asm-processor + `cc -g3`, multi-FDR string bases handled): bootup E68
  homes are timg -4 ... ult -40, arr -168, ..., padq -216, vs / ve, then 30 gbi-macro `_g` block locals -228..-344.
  E68's three spill slots are 8 LOW in the target (76 / 80 / 84, ours 84 / 88 / 92, frame 472 both; the spill area

  slot is tied to code changes, not a free lever (zero-use variant files re-scored with `spl.py`, which prints frame +
  spill offsets per variant).

**post0b 4F2DC (95.7218 -> 95.733086).** The target's 12 bytes at the frame top (sp+412, M-12) are the operand of
`start + d * -100000.0f` (copy chain 160 -> 180 -> 412, then the add reads 412). With `V3 operator+(const V3 &o)` the

`v` temp M-244, the product M-264, ..., the add result M-312, end M-340 = BELOW the pool temps): start / e declared

local. `V3 end(...)` / `= V3(...)` / assign-after-declare (3), `(start + d * k).kmul()` member on the result (4),

## kit CCCLIV (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 290): fix edg home ORDER by declaring a class local EARLY and leaving a code-free statement at its old declaration point -- an empty-ctor class declaration in the middle of a block is a code BARRIER (it changes what the following expression reads from registers), so moving the declaration alone costs bytes; keep a pad object / `if (1) {}` where it stood (post0b 4F2DC 95.770676 -> 95.8421, frame / length unchanged) <a name="kit-cccliv-agent-c-run290"></a>

_Commit (agent-c): d8c2d3294 (post0b 4F2DC NM donor, 95.770676 -> 95.8421, length 1064 = target, frame 424 = target)._

**The lever.** kit CCCLII's -g3 names put the target's homes in the order hits, start (M-188), e (M-200), d (M-212),
dir (M-224); ours had d / dir first and start / e far below. Declaring `V3 start; V3 e;` right after `hits` gives the
target's four homes, but on its own it changes the code (1040 bytes: `d * k` then reads d's copied registers instead of
reloading d -- the run-289 note "declaration position of a class local is not free"). The cause is the DECLARATION
STATEMENT, not the home: an empty-ctor class declaration between `d = dir;` and the product is a code-free statement
that still separates them. Putting ANY code-free statement back at start's old position restores the target's code:
the existing pad object (`PadK<4> pz;`, moved there), `if (1) {}`, `V3 q;`, `V3();`, `PadK<1>` -- all 1064 bytes,
95.7932 with start alone. The early `e` then needs its ctor body as a member call (`e.set(a, b, c)` with
`void set(f32 a, f32 b, f32 c) { x = a; y = b; z = c; }`, 95.8421); `e = V3(...)` (by-value operator=) is 1104-1116
bytes and member stores `e.x = ...` are 1052. Recipe: for a home that sits too low, declare the variable earlier and
leave a code-free statement (pad object or `if (1) {}`) where the declaration was; re-check length first.

**Frame accounting (NCC -O2), measured:** a named local or pool temp that ugen never references does not take frame
space unless something referenced is homed below it (a mini body with only `mid.set(a)` drops the unused named V3s
entirely); named scalars that are only ever in registers (4FD00's `p1` / `p2`) DO reserve their homes (block-nested
`p1` / `p2` land below the pool and grow the frame by 8). Homes keep creation order, so moving one referenced object
shifts every later one -- compare M-relative offsets (`/tmp/claude-1000/c290/t1/hmm.sh DONOR.o TARGET.o FUNC`
prints offset - frame sets, T-only / O-only), not raw sp offsets.

**4F2DC, what is left (95.8421).** M-relative pool: target `d = dir` by-value operator= parameter / return-copy temp
-244, product -264, add return copy -292, add result -312, end -340 (below the pool), outgoing args -408..-388.
Ours: v-temp -284, product -296, add -344, end -256 (named). end inside a nested block with the pad object moved to a
late nested block gives the target's v-temp -244 (frame 424) but the add operand temp then binds at the nested block
top instead of the frame top (95.68); end as a by-value parameter (`e.mulk(start + d * k, start)` member or free,
`s *= KV; if (1) {} set(...)` inside): v-temp -268, frame 464-480 (95.46); `const V3 &end`, nested-only-end, cam
expression (1072 bytes) / cam block scope, p / besti / cam declared early (no homes: flat), V3() stand-in + nested end,
operand / member-order grids on the new base (32), zero-use sweeps (--lines 49-62, plain and --exprs): flat.

**4FD00 (base 95.505974, unchanged).** `void sum3(V3 &o, int f, SV &s) { s.set(v0); o.set((s += v1) += v2); }` on ONE
block-scoped `SV s` gives the target's single s home and 1004 bytes (95.45, frame 144) -- the chained += inside
o.set() is what produces the target's double `move` pairs (`s += v1; s += v2; o.set(s);` is 980 bytes;
`s += v1; o.set(s += v2);` 1004 but deeper pool). Folding p1 / p2 into the test (frame 136, s at the target's sp+68,
every home but the set() parameter equal) costs 12 bytes (1016): the target evaluates both dots before the branch,
i.e. p1 / p2 are named -- and the target's 20 unreferenced bytes BELOW the set(V3) parameter (sp+0..20) fit block-
nested p1 / p2 plus a named `f32 r` in each dot expansion (both measured: they land below the parameter). What does
not fit: each chained `+=` adds 4 bytes of pool ahead of the parameter (target parameter M-116, ours M-132; zero +=
gives M-116); return-void / by-value / pointer-return / member `add()` / direct member arithmetic / loop forms all
change the length (952-1276). const-ness grid of every SV / V3 member (63): invariant.

**36694 (base 95.89888, unchanged).** A named `f32 k = s` in operator* moves the product __V to the target's M-68,
and operator/ WITHOUT k then gives frame 240 / 712 (95.64): homes closer, registers worse. The target's sub chain
120 -> 140 -> 92 (fresh return copy, final copy below the sub temps) is consistent with the subtraction sharing a full
expression with the product (`p - n * dot` without `a`) but every such shape is 704 bytes; operator= by value into r,
an inline `split(V3 t, ...)` by-value parameter (px / py / pz then address-taken: 720-736): lower.

**Other negatives.** 34890 loop-condition spellings (20): flat (a2 / v1 vs our v0 / a1 is the loop test temp).
gui 0F04 next() / nextp() / nextc() / nexti / nextq per-packet grid (100) and zero-use sweeps (plain 107, --exprs
lines 66-85): flat -- the target hoists only the xh MAX zero (a3) because its yh MAX temp is a0, ours v1 (free at the
hoist point). Home maps equal to the target (colour-only residuals): 4B620, 34890, 3B9C0, 54E78, 46790, 42938,
4BAF4, gui 4568 / 329C / 3714, game_uso 3558.
Later in the run, all flat: 200 random single / paired `if (1) {}` insertions each on 4F2DC (new base), 36694 (base
and the named-k / no-k operator/ shape), 4FD00, gui 3714 / 329C / 4568, post0b 54E78; 48AEC `register` / `const`

game_uso 3558 x / y matrix-row term orders x the stage / vb store interleave (108, spelling-grid).
gbi MAX / MIN spellings (`MAX(E,0)` / `E <= 0 ? 0 : E` / `0 < E ? E : 0`, MIN mirrored) on 4BAF4 (3 + 4 sites,
64 + 256), gui 3714 / 329C / 0F04 texrect xh / yh / xl / yl (81 each), 0F04 coordinate spellings (36): all flat.

## kit CCCLV (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 288): three no-code ring / colour levers close post 30AF4 (99.555 -> 100, EXACT 2112 bytes) -- a store-then-read-back of the same word through a DIFFERENT-SIGNEDNESS type keeps the stored value a ugen ring temp and spends one extra ring slot; a K&R parameter's signedness decides whether the jump-table index reuses the switch temp; a constant written plain (not `K + 0 * x`) joins the function's coloured constant LR; and a literal between two jump tables in RoData is a source literal, not an extern <a name="kit-ccclv-agent-g-run288"></a>

_Commits (agent-g branch): c19e69b82 (99.555 -> 99.905), acd4c8390 (NM 99.905 -> 100.0), 8f536a771 (EXACT on the ROM path via
the kit CCCXLVII match_imports natural-pin recipe: `src/match_imports/gl_func_00030AF4.c`,
`scripts/match-origins-gl_func_00030AF4{,-nm}.ld`, `scripts/match-bindings-gl_func_00030AF4{,-nm}.json`, 37
`snw_port_gl_func_00030AF4_*` carriers; the linked body equals all 528 target words on the first link)._

**Reading the residual first.** The run-287 hand-off said "two register colours left"; a straight objdump diff showed
four separate families: (a) the pre-switch hoist in v1 (target v0) with case 5 / 6 one colour up (D_m a0, 13 a1); (b)
the switch-1 index `sll t9,t9,2` (target `sll t0,t9,2`) and every t-ring temp of cases 0-2 one slot early; (c) case
2's `16` in a ring temp (target v1); (d) case 9 `sub` coloured v1 (target ring t9) with cases 9-11 + the tail two ring
slots LATE. Treat a "t-ring offset" as a COUNT: walk the paste of target | ours and note where the offset changes (+1
at the switch index, -1 at case 2's 16, +2 in case 9) -- each change point is one lever site.

**Levers (each emits no code):**
1. *Read-back through a different-signedness type* (case 9, family d). `*(s32 *)sv = sub; if (*(u32 *)sv == 1)`:
   uopt forwards the store, but the u32 read of the s32 word is a no-code `cvt` of the forwarded value, so `sub` is no
   longer one coloured web with two uses -- it stays a ugen ring temp (target `lw t9,60(sp); sw t9,0(v0); bne t9,at`)
   and the cvt takes the next ring slot (t0), which is exactly the +2 the tail needed. `*(s32 *)sv == 1` (same type)
   colours sub v1; a volatile read-back gives t9 but an extra `lw` (2116 bytes). Same word, well-defined value.
2. *Parameter signedness and the jump-table index* (family b). With `u32 mode` ugen computes the index in place
   (`sll t9,t9,2`); with `s32 mode` (the value is stored to an s32 field and only compared / switched on) the index
   takes a fresh ring temp (`sll t0,t9,2`), `sltiu` range check unchanged. `switch ((s32)mode)`, `mode + 0`,
   `mode + 0 * x` and other expression spellings of the SWITCH OPERAND do not move it -- only the declared type does.
3. *Plain constant joins the coloured constant LR* (family c). The constant {16} was coloured v1 for cases 5 / 8
   (zdbug:5 `>>>active<<<{16|1}`, `const 16`, live bbs of both cases); case 2's `gl_cmd = 16 + 0 * prev` kept its 16 as
   an operand of the folded uadd ({16|0}, no LR), so it was a ring temp. Written plain, case 2's 16 is one more
   use of the {16|1} LR and lands in v1 like the target. Check the constant's `>>>active<<<` record before adding
   a fold on a constant store: a fold there REMOVES the constant from its LR.
4. *Undo compensating folds after a real fix* (family a). The run-287 second `0 * (int)(sv)` on the case-6 D_n line
   only offset the case-9 ring; with lever 1 in place one fold gives the hoist v0, D_m v1, 13 a0 (the second fold's
   ucvt LR `{844|5}` took v0 ahead of the hoist: ord 2 vs 13, a shared neighbour).

**Literal vs extern between jump tables (decode fix, needed for the port).** The f14 store read `lwc1 $f4,0x18AC(at)`
between the switch-1 table at 0x1874 and the switch-2 table at 0x18B0 (switch-3 at 0x18E0). With `extern f32
D_30AF4_flt` IDO packs the TU's tables contiguously (0x00 / 0x38 / 0x68 from the .rodata base), so no single .rodata
placement reproduces 0x1874 / 0x18B0 / 0x18E0. A float LITERAL that needs the pool (0.3f, not 0.5f which is a `lui`)
is emitted in code order between the tables (0x00 / 0x38 literal / 0x3C / 0x6C). The value: bootup.uso RoData word
0x18AC = ROM 0xD9FE44 + 0x18AC = 0x3DCCCCCD = 0.1f (the jtbl entries around it read as game_libs text + 0x1466C). So
any extern float pinned INSIDE a run of jump tables is a literal: read its value from the RoData and spell it.

**Port checklist that held:** callees and the void aliases at their callee's address (baked jal words), the two
arena addresses at the values in their names, `.rodata 0x1874`, everything else 0; `nm -u` of the stripped object
lists exactly the symbols to pin; md5 of the linked 528 words = expected; `sha.py`-style `text_bytes_for` gives the
`raw_sha256`; ROM path logs `replace-body-skip: ... already matches donor`, NM path `replace-body ... 0x840->0x840 +
imported 186 donor reloc(s)`.

**Negatives (same run).** post0b 59E80: dead stores `r1 = 0` / `r2 = r1` / `r1 = r1` and `if (1)` / `if (c->dl)` /
`if (o)` after every packet (67 + 67): flat 98.553. The zdbug:5 dump explains the 0x402 pointer: uopt cuts the

## kit CCCLVII (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 289): post 33094 EXACT through a NAMED float constant (`f32 ten = 10.0f;`) plus a V3 member re-grid; a spill lands in the home of the variable that owns the live range (37540); the literal-vs-extern audit as a target-side scan -- every `lui at,0x0` + `lwc1/ldc1 $f,0x1xxx(at)` in a non-exact game_libs function is a bootup.uso RoData literal; post0b 37540's three pool aliases were 0.06f / 0.65f / 0.9f (96.518 -> 97.565, same length); gui 2DE0's "missing 4 words" are &D rematerialisations, not a decode gap <a name="kit-ccclvii-agent-g-run289"></a>

**post 33094 EXACT (404 bytes, NCC donor, 94.31 -> 100): a constant's colour follows whether it is NAMED.** The
two residuals were the else arm's a.x and the 10.0f scale. In the target, 10.0f is materialised into f12 (`lui at,
0x4120; mtc1 at,$f12`) and a.x is reloaded from its home (`lwc1 $f16,120(sp)`). Ours put the constant in f14 and kept
a.x in f12. Written as a named local, `f32 ten = 10.0f; b *= ten;` (instead of `b *= 10.0f` into operator*=(f32)),
the constant's LR outranks a.x for f12, so a.x is spilled and reloaded exactly like the target. Alone that is +4
bytes (92.49). Re-gridding the V3 member orders on that body (72: `*=` x y z with `+=` x y z) gave 100. Same family as
kit CCCLV's "a constant written plain joins the coloured constant LR". When the target loads a constant into a LOW
FP register and evicts a value that ours keeps there, try naming the constant, then re-grid the inline member
orders. Port: `src/game_libs/game_libs_ncc_33094.cpp` spliced over an empty `int` placeholder on both paths, the NM
donor block deleted, `gl_33094_emit = 0` pinned (baked `jal 0`), `D_33094_k = 0x128` already pinned.

**Scan (target side, cheap).** For each function under 100 in report.json, disassemble the expected object and list
every `lwc1` / `ldc1 $fN,OFF(at)` whose `at` comes from `lui at,0x0` with OFF in 0x1000..0x2400: that is a word of the
bootup.uso RoData (ROM 0xD9FE44 + OFF) read without a relocation, i.e. an IDO float LITERAL pool entry (kit CCCLV).
Read the word, spell it in the source. A second, source-side scan (`*(f32 *)((char *)&D_00000000 + 0x1xxx)` and
`D_xxxxx_YYYY[0xYYYY / 4]` aliases) finds the same set. In this tree the hits are: post 31A74 (0x1968 / 0x196C / 0x1970
/ 0x1974 = 0.1f / 0.98f / 0.1f / 0.8f), post0b 37540 (0x19F8 / 0x19FC / 0x1A00 = 0.06f / 0.65f / 0.9f), 396FC (0x1A10 =
0.01f; proven cap), 3B9C0 / 4F2DC (agent-c), 76F0 (cap); every other alias of this kind belongs to an exact function.
Note the literal pools come in CODE ORDER and are NOT deduplicated per function: 31A74 has two separate 0.1f words, and
37348 / 37540 each have their own 0.06f / 0.65f pair.

**37540 (NCC donor): 96.518 -> 97.565 report, same length (764).** The three `D_37540_19F8[0x19F8 / 4]`-style aliases
replaced by `0.06f`, `0.65f`, `0.9f`. The 0.9f one does all the work (the 0.06f / 0.65f pair alone is byte-identical):
`f32 L3 = 0.9f;` lets uopt treat the damping factor as a constant instead of a memory load that the preceding
`call()` could clobber, which moves the v90 / v6C copy colours toward the target. In the NM build the donor's `.rodata`
reloc imports as `gl_func_00037540_rodata` (replace-function-body.py renames donor-local section symbols); nothing to pin
for an NM-only donor.

**37540 second step: 97.565 -> 97.634 -- a spill goes to the home of the variable that OWNS the live range.** -g3
names (`mdl.py`) showed the target's `swc1 $f18,168(sp)` (the saved v60.x kept across the push call) is hx's own home,
while ours spilled to sp+72, the home of the inline `gr()`'s local `x` (`f32 x = n->v60.x; ...; return x;`): with
`hx = gr(...)` the register LR is x's, so uopt spills it into x's home. Reading v60 in a block straight into hx moves
the spill to 168 and shifts the block-scoped push vector to the target's 68..76: `{ Node *n = id(s); hx = n->v60.x;
hy = n->v60.y; hz = n->v60.z; n->v60.x = 0.0f; }` with `inline Node *id(Node *n) { if (0) { n = 0; } return n; }`.
A plain `Node *n = s;` gives the same homes but uopt hoists the s home load into the first compare block (94.20). The
id() parameter keeps the load in place (97.267 alone). Then the V3 member orders were re-gridded (72: ctor x y z,
operator= y x z, += z x y): 97.634. General rule: when a spill lands in a fresh or wrong slot while the target uses a
named local's home, check with -g3 which variable owns the LR in each build. Assign the value straight to the variable
that should own it; an inline's return local takes the LR otherwise.

Follow-ups on the literal body, all flat or worse: V3 operator= / += / ctor member-order grid (72,
base best), block-scoped pads / volatile pads around the `V3 v1(0, -b, 0)` push vector (the temp moves 60 -> 68 only
with a +8 frame), zero-use sweep over the body (53 sites, flat).

**31A74 (in-tree C): literals are byte-neutral (97.7305 either way)**, so not committed: on the build path they would
add words to game_libs_post.c's own .rodata and shift its jump tables. The tail residual is one adjacent pair: the
target's join block is `mfc1 a1; sb a2,35(sp); jal; swc1 (delay)`, ours always emits the sel home store `sb` last
(right before the jal), so the delay-slot filler takes `sb` instead of the 0x1CAC0 store. With the store written after
the `sel < 0` clamp (instead of before it) the rest of the tail lines up word-for-word and only the sb / swc1 pair
differs. objdiff scores that variant LOWER, though (97.16: it counts the swap as two inserts plus two deletes). Flat
for the swap: store as a call argument (`f(K, ACC = r)`, `(ACC = r, r)`, `((ACC = r), K)`), comma / split calls, the
kit CCXXXIV goto store block (with or without `if (1) {}`, wrapped, split call block: same, or +16 bytes with
jumps), sel clamp spellings (ternary, else-if, `else sel = sel`, int / s8 temp, `(s8)0`, `(int)sel < 0`), `&sel`
escapes (548 bytes).

**gui 2DE0's 4-word gap is not a decode gap.** Ours is 299 words, target 303. Aligning the two shows every block equal
up to registers except the &D_00000000 (CTX) web. The target keeps &D in t3 from the second rect append to the
third, and materialises it again inside the yl < 0 subtree of the RDPHALF_1 t-term: `lui t3 / addiu t3` at the arm
entry, then a split `lui t3 ... addiu t3` pair on each exit of the inner MAX/MIN. That is 6 words; ours re-forms the
address once at the third append (`lui s0; lw s0,0(s0)`) and has a nop where the target's arm-entry pair sits. So it is
a live-range split of a constant (uopt rematerialisation), the run-220 / 256 diagnosis. Flat: `(s16)` cast on the yl
test (and dropping the xl one), third-append spellings nD / next / nC / nextp / me(CTX) / me(me(me(CTX))) (12).

**35B1C as real C++ (decode, ties the C at 97.40).** `struct Ent { void *operator new(unsigned); Ent *next; Key key;
int a8; Ent(List *, Key, int); virtual void f(); }` (edg puts the vptr after the data members, at 0xC), with `struct
Key { int v; Key() { v = 0; } int operator==(Key o) { Key *self = this; return self->v == o.v; } }` and the duplicate
test written `k == n->key` (the BY-VALUE operator== parameter is the target's sp+60 copy of the node key). The
`this + 4 != 0` test (`bne s4,-4`) is the inlined Key() ctor's own null check, and the class operator new is the
`o ? o : alloc(0x10)` head. The `self` copy in operator== supplies the two missing home words (frame 72 -> 80 = target).
Residual, same as the C: the vptr store `sw t6,12(s4)` is scheduled before `addiu v1,s4,4; addiu at,-4` (target:
after). Flat: Key as a second base / Node base (vptr and key order wrong, 82-85), member-init a8, Key copy ctor,
`List::add` / `List::tail` inlines (+4 bytes).

**Negatives (same run).** 493AC: both loop tests over 14 x 14 spellings (`!= 0`, `!!`, casts, `+ 0` / `0 +` / `- 0`,
`?:`), and first-loop next() variants returning void * / int / unsigned / char * / const pointers: flat at 99.4318.
3BE1C off spill (ours sp+80, target 84; -g3 names show off has no home): an extra function-scope int, s16 / char
locals at every declaration position, `off` at every declaration position, block-scoping each local, de-naming a / b
/ hi / lo, hoisting r / d / n_al: never 84 (76 or 80). 59E80: one more `if (1) {}` or `if (c->dl) {}` after each
packet (40): flat; `+ 0 * r1 / r2` on the 3 / 0xFFFD ClipRatio words: +4..8 bytes. 3B6A0: the table pointer's
`+ 0 * x` counted use on other locals, statement placement (13): flat. 415A4: plain `a28 = 1030; a28 = a28 | 6 | 0x400`
families on tA / t / *t (15): 92.6..95.2 (base 97.30). 469A8 as C++ (`Self::run(int)`, vcall entries {s16 d, fptr}
at 0x60 / 0x18, a Glob inline setter): 69 -> 71, far below the 98.20 C; the target keeps more values in s-registers
and homes the 0xF0 word at sp+72. The named-constant lever elsewhere: flat on 37540 (0 / 2 / +-10 / 0.06 / 0.65, also
with a member re-grid), 3BE1C (10.0f at each declaration position), 3B6A0 (-50 / 0), 2DE0 (1024 / 2) and 415A4

## kit CCCLVIII (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 292): the kit CCCXXX "coloured split piece" lever on an NCC body -- when the target computes a pointer into a UGEN temp at one use and only a LATER assignment of the same C variable lives in a coloured register, read that first use through the plain expression (not the variable) and drop the earlier assignment; then re-test the folds fitted on the old body (kit CCCXXIX): post0b 3BE1C 99.166 -> 99.268; plus the zdbug colour-number map and LR-priority diagnoses for 3BE1C / 3B6A0, and a field-order false optimum in 37540 <a name="kit-ccclviii-agent-c-run292"></a>

_Commit 214197f1a (agent-c run 292). No exacts; no clip change (3BE1C length 1568 unchanged)._

**3BE1C (NCC donor): 99.166 -> 99.268, same length.** Target, per triangle: `lw t9,44(s5); addu t7,t9,a2; ...
lwc1 $f6,8(t7)` (t->d through a ugen temp t7) and later `lw t6,44(s5); addu v1,t6,a2; lb a1,0(v1)` (t for a / b in
the coloured v1). Ours had `t = tris + off;` before n and read `t->d`: the first piece of t's web was coloured (v1)
too. Writing the plane distance as `... - ((Tri *)((char *)tris + off))->d;` and deleting that first assignment
(t is assigned again before a / b) gives the ugen temp, but with the ring one slot off (97.98). The agent-g run-266
fold on the 0x100 test (`if ((r & 0x100) + 0 * (int)(cc))`) was fitted to the old ring phase; removing it puts the
whole triangle block back in phase: 99.268 (a 74-variant remove-one / remove-two grid over every fold in the body
picked it). Rule: a ugen-vs-coloured mismatch on ONE use of a variable means that use is a separate expression in
the source; split it off, then prune the ring-compensating folds.

**zdbug:5 colour numbers (uopt, -O2 -mips2, from the `>>>active<<<{id} lr colour` records matched against the
emitted registers):** 1 v0, 2 v1, 3 a0, 4 a1, 5 a2, 6 a3, 7 t0, 8 t1, 9 t2, 10 t3, 11 t4, 16 s2, 17 s3, 22 s8 (so
14..22 = s0..s8). Map a C local to its LR by its home: `-g3` gives the frame offset of each name, the ucode
`isvar M 4 -NNvreg` line gives the `{id|n}` with that offset, and the `>>>active<<<{id|n}` record gives adjsave,
forbidden colours and the colour. Tools: /tmp/claude-1000/c292/t1/dump.sh + g3l.sh.

**3BE1C residual (open): va / vb colours.** Target: va a0, vb a1 (both dead right after their element loads), hi
a1. Ours: va t3 (colour 10, adjsave 4.29, forbidden 1..9) and vb a3 because both LRs span the whole MAX / MIN block
range (blocks 28..47): agent-g's run-210 `ok = 0 + 0 * (int)(va);` and the `+ 0 * (int)(vb)` on hi are counted
uses there. They are structural, though: without a va / vb / vc use in the `ok = 0` arm the first inner MAX loses
its pre-assigned `(s16)ib` (two arms instead, 1564 bytes). Flat: the va fold replaced by ia / ib / ic / hi / lo /
k / r / t / f / a / b / off (1564 or lower), by `&va[k]` / `va + k` / `va[0]` / `&vb[k]` / `vc + k` (= base: still a va
use), explicit inner-MAX spellings (5 x 5 compare forms, with / without the va / vb folds: 75), and a second
remove-one / remove-two fold grid on the new base (129). Off spill (ours 80, target 84): 42 `+ 0 * (int)(X)` CSE
folds around the material call never give 84.
Partial lead: a block-scoped PHANTOM pointer `s16 *ph = col->verts[f->vi[2]];` (CSE'd with vc, no code) placed
before the va assignment, with the ok fold on ph instead of va (`ok = 0 + 0 * (int)(ph);`), KEEPS the pre-assign at
1568 bytes and makes va short-lived (kit CCCXLVI phantom) -- but the colours land elsewhere (va a1, vb t1, ib t0,
off spill 76): 99.026. Phantom defs vi[0] / vi[1] / nrm / tris / col / verts / face() at 2 positions (32), 36
position x hi-fold variants and a 74-variant fold re-test on that base: best 99.166, under the 99.268 base. A plain
`0 * (int)(n)` ok fold also gives va a0 at 1568 but demotes n (adjsave 60 -> 10, v0 -> t0): 98.69. A 200-variant
seeded random search over phantom index / position x ok / hi / lo / k fold targets: best 98.91. Extra va counted
uses (hi / lo / k folds, 41 combinations, to raise its adjsave): best 99.11.

**3B6A0 (NCC) LR priorities, read from zdbug:5.** Ours: inside (adjsave 80) -> t4, c (48.8) -> s2, f (43.3) -> s3, pt
(10) -> s8. Target: f t4, inside s2, pt s3, c s8, i.e. c LAST and f FIRST. The target also has `or v0,s8,zero`: a
