**1. Instrumented uopt (diagnosis only).** The dump compiler's recompiled `uopt.c`
(`tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/build/7.1/uopt.c`) rebuilds in about a minute with fprintf probes:
`gcc -std=c11 -O1 -fno-strict-aliasing -I<dump dir> -o uopt uopt.c <dump>/build/7.1/version_info.o <dump>/build/7.1/libc_impl_71.o -lm`.
The `cc` driver maps `/usr/lib/uopt` to the directory of its OWN executable after resolving symlinks, so put a COPY
of `out/cc` in a scratch dir next to symlinks to the other `out/*` tools and to the probed `uopt`. Probes used:
(a) every `f_gettemp` call site prints the temp count `MEM_U32(0x1001c3e8)` before / after; (b) in `f_globalcolor`
at the cost-split test (label `L469cc8`: `priority (lr+48) x (float)lr+28 <= f20`) print the LR record, `lr+4`
(= the LR number of the zdbug dumps), lr+28, the priority and the best cost `f20` with its colour `sp+220`.

in every BB holding GBI packet stores; per BB it takes the first temp not busy with that BB's region items. The

158, line 187, 192, 211, the three spilled, `vidx*2+2` 260, `+4` 264, plus the TRI1-shared 259 / 265), so the

## kit CCCLXVII (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 296): NCC inline temporaries are POOLED slots shared by every expansion (and across inline functions by role), so two values the target keeps in the SAME register inside ONE block can be one pool slot -- post0b 59E80 EXACT (99.835 -> 99.890 -> 99.945 -> 100, 1092 B) via `at(DLHead *d)` putting a packet's old count in the next() base-temp slot; the folded counted use's OPERAND is its own lever (`+ 0 * o->f104` beat `+ 0 * (int)(c)`) <a name="kit-ccclxvii-agent-c-run296"></a>

_agent-c run 296, base f50eebc34. Gains (report.json regenerated to scratch; gate each time: ROM byte-identical,
verify-blocks 6/6, non_matching_objects 0 errors, no exacts lost, 3248 -> 3249 exact, 94.224 -> 94.367% code):
post0b 59E80 NM 99.83517 -> 99.89011 (5d1f06512) -> 99.94505 (d91c02d04) -> EXACT 100 (822b3467d)._

**1. Slot map (zdbug:5 `isvar M 4 -NNvreg` + bbmap of the `>>>active<<<` blocks, /tmp/claude-1000/c296/t1/bbmap.py).**
Every expansion of `next() { int n = dl->count++; return &dl->buf[n]; }` uses the SAME two edg pool slots: M-40 =
the post-increment's base temp (`dl`, one LR coloured v1 for the whole body) and M-36 = the old value (`n`, a2). Named
locals of an inline function get one fixed slot per FUNCTION (nextB's d / n = M-120 / M-124 in every nextB
expansion; a different inline gets fresh slots). Which pool slot a temp lands in depends on the construct: a
post-increment through a NAMED or PARAMETER base pointer has no base temp, and its old value goes into the base-temp
slot (M-40) when the head arrives as an inline PARAMETER (`at(DLHead *d) { int n = d->count++; ... }`), into M-36 when
`d` is a local of the inline; `++d->count` puts the new value in M-40; `return &dl->buf[dl->count++]` uses M-36 / M-28.

**2. Why it matters (block-granular colouring, kit CCCLXV).** Two LRs in one block never share a colour, so a target
that puts the 0x1402 packet's n AND the next 0xB9 packet's dl in v1 inside one block needs them to be ONE LR. Every
separate-variable spelling had either 1402's n in a0 (no split) or the 0xB9 pointer in v0 (split after 0x1402);
`{ DLHead *d = c->dl; gs = c->at(d); ... }` makes n the pool base temp -- the 0xB9 next()'s dl -- with d its own v0 LR.
Then the four `if (1) {}` BB splits of runs 202-296 are all dropped (exhaustive 16-way removal): one block from the
0xC02 packet to the ClipRatio words, d / gu / gs live there, the 0xB9 pointer takes a3: **100**. Every remaining
lever is load-bearing (removing the in-if `if (1) {}`: 99.40; dlist's code-free `d` read: 97.50; the 1C04 fold: 99.84).
Rule: when two values share a register inside one block in the target, look for the construct that puts both in
one pool slot (parameter-passed head, post-increment) before trying BB splits.

**3. The folded counted use's operand is a lever.** On the 0x1C04 packet `gs = c->nextC() + 0 * (int)(c)` left a
phantom v0 LR (the uixa result) in the o-test block, pushing the o reload into v1; a fold-spelling grid (20 operand
forms x 2 vars x 3 statement orders, 119) found `+ 0 * o->f104` (and `+ 0 * (int)(gs)` with an `if (1) {}`): the o
reload back in v0, 99.890 -> 99.945. Swapping fold operands on 3BE1C (132: cc / cnt / list / i / max / out / col /
`cc->grid` / `*list` ...) and 3B6A0 (90) is flat.

**4. Earlier steps.** With the split after 0x1402 (its nextB n leaves the next() temps' block: v1) the fold moved from
the 0xC04 packet (back on next()) to the 0x1C04 packet on nextC(): its return temp lives into the o-test block and
takes a3 (99.835 -> 99.890, 128-variant C04 x 1C04 accessor x var grid).

**Negatives (59E80, ~1500 variants):** accessor-depth `me()` x method joint grid on the late packets (200), random 1-3
op mutation searches (method / var / split / fold, 4 x 200 from three bases), 20 nextB body spellings with folded n

M-40 slot but costs an instruction, 1096 B), a function-scope `int k` shared by 1402's n and 0xB9's dl (right sharing,
d / k colours swapped), a long-lived 0xB9 pointer (gw read by a later fold: t1, 98.2).

**Other negatives this run.** gui 2DE0: per-append `at(dl)` / `at2(dl)` head-passed spellings (texture + three rect

rematerialised with lui / addiu like the target's t3) and can never be the CTX web. Making every CTX use that same
expression (`(*(Ctx **)((int)&D_00000000 | 0))`, `+ 0`, `^ 0`, `- 0`, `* 1`) spills it across the loader calls (frame
184, 87.4): only the plain lda is rematerialised across calls. `Ctx **pc = (Ctx **)&D_00000000` IS the lda, but then

**0. The gain: a reference view for the re-read.** `d = dir;` through the by-value `V3::operator=(V3 v)` copies dir
into the parameter temp (sp+180 in the target) and member-stores d (212..220); the target then reads d's home for
the `d * k` products. Ours read the parameter temp (uopt equates `d.x` with the just-stored `v.x` and loads v's
words). `const V3 &dr = d;` right after the assignment and the product spelled `dr * k` breaks that equivalence
(the reads go through the reference's inline-propagated address) and the three loads become `lwc1 f,212/216/220(sp)`
exactly; it is zero code, frame unchanged (424). Other spellings: `V3 &operator=` / `const V3 &operator=` returning
`*this` (inert alone), `const V3 &dr = (d = dir)` (= the reference), `V3 *dp = &d; ... *dp * k` (= the reference),
`*me(&d) * k` (frame +8, 95.70), `*me(&d) = dir` (inert), declaration of dr at 13 other anchors (all = the gain,
compile errors before d's declaration). Kit CCCLXX's union view is the alternative when the target ALSO schedules
the re-read stores freely; this reference view is the cheaper first probe when only the read side differs.
Same lever, inert: references on `start` / `end` / `sw *= KV` (each unused reference home costs +8 frame; with the
PadK pad shrunk to compensate the code is byte-identical to the base), and on 3558's vb / va (reads through
`const Vec3 &vr = vb` at 4 anchors x the += / `e = vb - va` / va sites, 31: <= base).

**1. The as1 tie rule (31A74, measured).** `cc -S` prints ugen's output BEFORE as1's reorganiser, with the
`.loc` of every statement (the line where the statement ENDS: a call split over two lines carries the second
line). Inside one block as1 issues independent instructions by source line, lowest first; equal lines keep
ugen order. 31A74's mode-1 join: store (line 15443) above the call (15440) gives the target's `mfc1 a1; lui at;
jal; swc1`; store at the goto's line 15438 gives `lui at; mfc1`. The tail: ugen always emits `s.s G` (source
order), then the argument `mfc1 a1`, then uopt's caller-save spill `sb a2,35(sp)` immediately before the jal
(spills sit after the argument setup for every clamp / temp / ternary spelling tried, 24); the jal delay filler
then takes the instruction nearest the jal that is not an `mfc1` (an mfc1 never goes into a jal delay slot), so
`[s.s, mfc1, sb]` = ours (`mfc1; swc1; jal; sb`) and the target's `mfc1; sb; jal; swc1` needs the store on a
HIGHER line than the call. Line joins cannot do it (ties keep the store first; 192-variant join grid flat).

**2. ugen goto straightening.** `goto z; c: CALL; return; z: STORE; goto c;` is rebuilt by ugen (also at -O1;
not at -O0, so not cfe and not uopt) as `[STORE CALL]` at the goto site: one block, no jumps. The moved block
LOSES its own `.loc` lines (the store takes the goto's line) unless it starts with a code-free BB split
(`if (1) {}`, `if (m) {}`, `if (1) {} else {}`, `do {} while (0);`, `for (;;) break;` ...): then the statements
after the split keep their own (higher) lines -- that is how agent-g's run-228 mode-1 block works. **Only ONE
such line-keeping block merges per function: the one whose c / z blocks come first in the text.** Every later
one is not moved at all (+16 B: `b z` / `b c` stay). Standalone bisection (/tmp/claude-1000/c300/m/m10.c,
m11.c): the earlier block blocks the later one only when its c has code AND ends in `return` (or `goto` an exit
label) AND its z has the split AND code; a bare-`return` c, a z without the store, or an earlier plain
(line-dropping) merge do not block; an unrelated `if (1) {}` elsewhere does not block. Splitters that drop the
line (`while (0) {}`, `if (0) {}`, `switch (0) { default: ; }`, `goto y; y:`) never block and never keep the
line. Moving the call block before the computation, chains `goto j; ... j: goto z;`, arm gotos, blocks at the
function top / end, wrapping in `if (1)` / `do while (0)` / `{}`: no merge (580 B) or line lost.
31A74 now uses its one line-keeping merge on the TAIL (`goto z31t; c31t: f(..), c(..); return; z31t: if (1)
{} ACCS2_31A74 = r; goto c31t;`): `mfc1; sb; jal; swc1` = target, 98.12. Mode 1 lost its split (plain merge:
`lui at; mfc1; jal; swc1` + the b-delay mfc1 copy missing) -- that pair is the whole residual. Not found: any
second line-keeping construct (60 splitter pairs, 12 inline / loop / switch wrappers, the store inside a third
call argument -- ugen evaluates side-effect arguments first -- named promotable global, same-statement
forms).

**3. Line-join / line-split sweeps (cheap, worth running on every near-miss).** /tmp/claude-1000/c300/t/lj.py
(all single joins of adjacent code lines + random pairs), lj3.py (windows of 3-5 lines, pairs of windows),
ls.py (split a multi-statement line at each top-level `;` / brace), scored by vrf.py. Hits: 3BE1C's edge-loop
head `nx = D_3BE1C_c; fv = (u16 *)f; do {` on one line puts the `q[b]` lwc1 before nx's `addiu %lo` (99.27 ->
99.78; every mask containing both joins); the same loop head in its sibling 3B6A0 (`u16 *fp = (u16 *)f; do {`,
96.375 -> 96.65); 415A4's mode-word line split after the first `D_415A4_tA.a28 = (int)v;` (97.30 -> 97.35).
Flat (joins 100-200 each, windows 120-150, splits): 469A8, 35B1C, gui 2DE0, 493AC, 31A74.

**4. 3BE1C residual = off's spill slot only (sp+80 vs sp+84; 296 is reloc-only).** Layout facts: the spill
sits BELOW the whole named-home block (off's declaration position among the int locals does not move it; after
an odd number of s16 decls it drops to 76 = alignment); any volatile pad, at any scope, pushes it down; removing
the n_al home gives the target's top-relative offset (frame 232, spill 76, cx 120 = 240 - 112) but colours lose
(99.64) and the target has 4 more bytes BELOW the spill (24 vs 28 bytes of untouched slots between the saved
registers and the spill); merging dead-disjoint locals (v0 = va, nx = vc, dy = lo ..., 52) shrinks the frame to
232 without restoring the top-relative cx. Open lead: an extra uopt temp slot below off's (a phantom spill
candidate) with n_al removed.

**Negatives.** 493AC: a named-count `noop2()` at either / both noop sites x one pad removed (42): <= 99.52. 3B6A0:
3BE1C's loop-pointer spellings (body `tp++`, `<`, `&tbl[3]`, fold dropped; 11): best 96.75 at 796 B (away from
800, rejected).

**3BE1C spill-slot probe, late in the run.** n_al removed + one folded use of `n` or `t` in the hit block
(`out[cnt] = &tris[i] + 0 * (int)(n);`, `cnt += 1 + 0 * (int)(t);`) puts off's spill at the target's sp+84 with

question is which allocation sits between the saved registers (ending at 56) and the spill (24 bytes ours,

**1. The lever.** In an NCC body the `sw aN,home(sp)` stores of spilled parameters are issued in the entry block with
the line of the function HEADER, the first statement's instructions with their own (higher) line. Where as1 has a
free choice between them (an independent `sw aN` and the second half of an address pair) the lower line wins, so the
parameter store goes first. gui 3714: target `lui t4; addiu t4,%lo(CTX); sw a1,100(sp)`, ours `lui t4; sw a1,100(sp);
addiu t4` (kit CCCLXXV: 30 body-only joins flat -- the header line was never joined). Header + the five
declaration lines + the `if (arg4) {}` first statement on ONE line: the three tie and keep ugen's order -> the
target's (99.141 -> 99.922; every join depth from the declarations through the first statement gives it, joining
only the declarations does not). Remaining 3714 diff = spr in v0 (target t1), 4 words. vsig.py over the other 17
bodies: no change anywhere (their entry blocks already issue in the target order) -- check nd2.py for an
entry-block region first; if there is none, the header join is inert.

**2. Order scan (nd2.py on the committed bodies).** Order regions exist only in 3714 (above), 4BAF4, 4FD00, 42938,
48AEC, 36694, 4F2DC and 3558; 329C, 4B620, 34890, 54E78, 46790, 3B9C0, 4568, bootup E2D0 / E68, post0b 5A2C4 have
register colours only (no as1 lever applies). (a) 4BAF4's 0xEE add (`addu t1; andi t6,t5,0x7fff; sll t9,t6,16; sw
w0; sw w1`, ours andi first and w1 first): register-forced -- the target's andi reuses t6, which the addu frees, so
it cannot issue earlier; the inline add() body on 1-5 lines (15 masks), splits inside the call (4), open-coded
packet (4): <= base. An edg inline expansion carries the CALL line: re-laying the inline's own body never moves
anything. (b) 4FD00's `or v0,zero,zero` (return 0) is issued at word 145 in the target, 230 in ours, in one straight
block. Every way to give it an earlier line costs more: `int r = 0;` / `r = 0;` at any of 12 statement ends before
the dots (p1 / p2 declared up front or not, 60: 74-75, the variable homes and the face sums re-pool), an early
goto-placed `return 0` block (40: the block is materialised, 31-94), 37 return shapes (`return p1 >= 0.0f && p2 >=

**1. 35B1C (C, list-append constructor).** Target `lui t6; addiu t6,%lo(vtbl); addiu v1,s4,4; li at,-4; sw t6,12(s4);
bne s4,at; sw v1,52(sp)`, every straight spelling `... sw t6,12(s4); addiu v1 ...` (the store's line is below the
test's). The store has to be issued after the `li at` of the `bne s4,-4` (`(o + 4) != 0`) test, i.e. on a HIGHER line
than the test while ugen still emits it first: the kit-CCCLXXIV line-keeping goto block, in front of the test:

## kit CCCLXXVIII (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 300): a value the target holds in a LATER register than every free one (gui 3714 spr: t1 with v0 / v1 / t0 free) = the variable is REUSED for a later value -- one variable, one uopt live range over both values, so its priority drops and it colours after the short ranges it now interferes with (gui 3714 99.922 -> 100 EXACT); the header-line lever has no other candidate in the 18-body list; same-type local-merge sweep flat <a name="kit-ccclxxviii-agent-g-run300"></a>

**1. Diagnosis (3714).** The last residual was 4 words: `lw t1,16(t8)` / three `lh|lw aN,..(t1)` -- spr in t1 in the
target, v0 in ours. The `-Wo,-zdbug:6` dump (coloring-solve.py) showed spr's live range coloured at ord 0-2 (top
priority: one def and three uses in one block) into v0 under EVERY variant: spr's def moved into the alloc block /
after the BB split / onto the header line (6), expression form with no named spr / accessors / single-statement call
forms (19 + 10), `if (X) {}` BB splits around spr (46), folded zero uses of the texture append's dl / n / _g extended
into spr's block (15 + 15; they moved to other registers, spr stayed v0). A range that colours FIRST takes the lowest
free register whatever it interferes with -- so t1 means spr is NOT a high-priority range in the target: v0, v1, t0
being "free" around its uses is the tell.

**2. The fix.** t1 is also the target's register for the RECTANGLE packet pointer after the loader call (spr is dead
there). Holding that pointer in spr itself:

    spr = (Spr *)me(me(CTX))->nD();
    gSPScisTextureRectangle((Gfx *)spr, me(me(CTX))->nD(), me(CTX)->nD(), ...);

makes spr's live range span both values (uopt's ranges are per VARIABLE here, not per web): priority falls below the
texture append's dl / n (v0 / v1) and _g (t0), and spr takes t1 in both places -- byte-identical, 1024 bytes. The
Gfx * round-trips through the cast (Spr's alignment is weaker), every read sees a value written: valid C++.

**Rule.** When one value sits in a register that is later than every register free over its range (and the dump shows
it colouring early into a low register in your build), look for a LATER value the target puts in the SAME register
whose range does not overlap it; write both through one variable (cast if the types differ). Try this before BB-split
or zero-use grids, which cannot lower a one-block range's priority enough.

**3. Header-line lever scan.** The run-299 nd2.py order-only listings of the 18 bodies: 3714 was the only one whose
parameter home stores sit in a different order (36694 / 46790 home stores order-equal; 48AEC / 4F2DC differ only by
frame offset / colour). No further candidate.

**4. Same-type local-merge sweep (reuse.py: merge B into A when A's last use precedes B's first assignment).** 46790
(3), 3B9C0 (5), game_uso 3558 (9), gui 329C (2): none above base. gui 329C: spr / gpa / gpb over the four packet slots
(66, cast macros) and 4 packet variables x declaration order (75 partitions x orders): flat at 99.633; the texture

## kit CCCLXXXI (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 303): post0b 415A4 EXACT -- uopt folds only the FIRST identity OR on a known constant (a leading value-preserving `| 2` keeps the target's `ori 6` / `ori 0x400`); an LR whose BB contains a call cannot take v0 (a code-free `if (1) {}` after the call frees it); a folded address use (`0 * (int)(t->v30)`) makes an address CSE that holds a second register; the a2C store on a later statement's line fixes the as1 tie <a name="kit-ccclxxxi-agent-c-run303"></a>

_post0b gl_func_000415A4 NM 97.70 -> 99.26 (4f330b065) -> 99.42 (9852e6c93) -> EXACT 452 B in-tree C (69cb0aa5a)._

**1. Identity ORs on a known constant: uopt folds the first, keeps the rest.** The target builds the mode word as
`li v0,1030 ... ori v0,v0,6 ... ori v0,v0,0x400` although 1030 = 0x406 already contains both bits. With
`v = (float *)1030; ... v = (float *)((int)v | 6); v = (float *)((int)v | 0x400);` uopt drops the `| 6` and keeps the
`| 0x400`; any extra identity OR written FIRST (`| 2`, `| 4`, `| 0x402` -- all already in 0x406) is the one that folds,
so `v |= 2; v |= 6; v |= 0x400` emits exactly the target's two oris (`| 0`, `+ 0`, `& -1`, `^ 0` are removed earlier and
do not absorb the fold). Use it wherever a target keeps arithmetic on a known constant that the first operation of a
chain loses. (Folded zero-code expression on a well-defined value.)

**2. A coloured LR whose live-unit BB contains a call cannot take v0.** In 415A4 the mode word v (uopt var M -20, the
`-Wo,-zdbug:6` bit index of its `isvar` line is its LR number) was `assigned (constrained) 3` (a0) with v0 unused in its
region: v's definition sat in the BB of the `D_415A4_g3 = f(0)` call (return value in v0). A code-free `if (1) {}` right
after that call statement moves v (and t) into a call-free BB: v0 becomes allowed, and the colour order then decides
which of t / v takes it -- a folded counted use of v (`+ 0 * (int)(v)` on its last store) ranked v above t (target v0 /
v1). uopt colour numbers here: 1 = v0, 2 = v1, 3 = a0, 4 = a1, 5 = a2.
Diagnosis recipe: extract the function plus its typedefs from the asm-processor pre-pass into a standalone .c, compile it
with tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/.../cc `-Wo,-zdbug:6` (writes ./uoptlist in the cwd), map LR numbers to variables
through the "index bit kind" table (bit = LR number, `isvar M 3 -20` = the local at frame offset -20), read the
"assigned (constrained) N" lines.

**3. A folded address use creates an address CSE with its own register.** agent-g run 210's `t->a4 = 2 + 0 * (int)(t->v30)`
(once a gain) made `&D_415A4_t + 0x30` a CSE that lived from the a4 store to the Vec4 stores and was coloured a2 / a1 /
a0 (never v0: it overlapped v); dropping it lets the Vec4 base take v0 like the target (kit CCCXXIX: re-test old folds
after each structural change).

**4. Source-line ties for the last two instructions.** With the registers right the target's `lui v0; li t2,1; addiu
v0,48; sw t2,44(v1)` needed the `D_415A4_t.a2C = 1;` store on the line AFTER `if (1) { v = t->v30; }` and on the same
line as the Vec4 stores (`D_415A4_t.a2C = 1; v[3] = v[2] = v[1] = v[0] = 0.0f;`); the a2C store through the plain
D_415A4_t name (not `t->a2C`) keeps the record base v1 (t->a2C after the splits went absolute). The 200-variant random
line-join / BB-split sweep (generator: statements list, a newline-or-space bit and an optional `if (1) {}` per gap)
found the intermediate layouts.

**1. 469A8: reuse the variable for the later a3 argument, written as an assignment expression in the argument list.**
The target holds `temp_a3 = FW(temp_s1, 0xC)` in a3 (v1 free) -- kit CCCLXXVIII's signature of a reused variable. The
last call's fourth argument `FW(temp_s1, 0x60)` is also loaded into a3, so `..., (temp_a3 = FW(temp_s1, 0x60)), ...`
in the call makes temp_a3 one variable over both values and its first web colours a3 like the target. As a separate
statement before the call (`temp_a3 = FW(temp_s1, 0x60); f(..., temp_a3, ...)`) the colour is fixed too but the load is
issued before the a0 load (`lw a3,96(s1)` / `lw a0,536(s2)` swapped, 98.573); inside the argument list it keeps its
argument-order slot (98.786). kit CCCLXXXI 6.'s automated web renames were byte-identical in cfe because they renamed
whole definitions; this is a value the target evidently passes in the same register (here: the next call's argument).
The first `temp_v1 = FW(arg0, 0x240)` web (target v1, ours a1) is fixed by dropping agent-g run 281's
`if (FW(arg0, 0x240)) {}` test (the test's load starts a CSE that colours first), but that swaps the `move a0,s1` /
`move a1,s0` argument moves (98.738, 20 diffs); 11 replacement tests, a test after the reload and 150 random line
joins between the vcall and the argument block do not restore them. Dropping the `if (FW(temp_v1, 0x148)) {}` test too
makes the 0x148 pointer a ugen temp like the target (t8 + `sw t8,72(sp)`) but swaps s0 / s1 (104 words).
Diagnosis (cfe dump compiler on the asm-processor pre-pass, `-Wo,-zdbug:6`): colour numbers 1..12 = v0, v1, a0..a3,
t0..t5, 13 = ra, 14.. = s0..; t6..t9 are never colours, so the target's pDC in t7 (`addiu t7,v1,220` above the `&&`
branch, stored to the stack argument after it) is NOT a coloured variable. Writing the whole argument block as one call
expression puts the `&&` argument first (ugen evaluates the branchy argument before the others): 70 (32 variants).
Negatives: temp_t6 / &D+0x254 chains and pointer locals (10 + 28), the 0x148 load held in a dead variable (37).

## kit CCCLXXXIV (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 302): edg (NCC) inline-temp POOL rules -- the low frame pool is sized by the largest number of inline temps simultaneously live in ONE full-expression; slots are reused across statements, and a reused slot is ONE ucode variable whose block-granular live range is a colouring lever; why post0b 54E78's last 5 offset diffs and its FP colours are coupled; negatives on 54E78 / 4FD00 / 36694 / 5A2C4 / E2D0 / 3B9C0 / 4B620 / 34890 <a name="kit-ccclxxxiv-agent-g-run302"></a>

**1. Which inline constructs take a pool slot (NCC 7.1, measured on 54E78 by the ret / copy V3 temporaries' sp offsets).**
- TAKE a slot: a by-value identity inline whose body is `return v;` (`idv()`), an int-returning constant inline
  (`i1()`, any return type: int / short / char / f32 / unsigned all the same), `idv(1.0f)`, `idv(i1())`, a by-value
  `ip(const T *)` deref, a class-object temporary (`V3();` -- those go to the UPPER named-local area instead and grow
  the frame by 8-24).
- Do NOT take a slot: a const-reference identity (`const f32 &cr(const f32 &v)`, fully transparent: byte-identical),

_agent-c run 306, base 692241c91. Gains: 2138b210b (post0b 42938 NM 98.118256 -> 98.58869, 1556 B), 0a5d4ad9e (42938
98.58869 -> 98.65038, same length). Tools: /tmp/claude-1000/c306/t/ (sc.py / rund.py = run-304 NCC scorer re-pointed,
rund.py also takes whole-file variants `('@FILE@', path)`; shgen.py = per-occurrence macro-token swap generator,
singles + pairs, e.g. `_SHIFTL(` -> a doubled-mask `_SHIFTL2(`), /tmp/claude-1000/c306/v/ (variant files)._

**1. The ring lever.** 42938's inline `setvp(Vp *, f32 x, f32 y, f32 w, f32 h)` stores eight halfwords; the run-157
body carried one folded `& 0xFFFF` on each vtrans[0] / vtrans[1] (one ugen ring slot each). The target's store block
is `sh t8,0; sh t6,2; mfc1 t8; mfc1 t6; ...` -- vtrans[0] / [1] REUSE t8 / t6, which forces the vscale[1] `sh t6,2`
ahead of the second mfc1 (a WAR dependence). Ours had them in t9 / t8, so the `sh 2` floated to the end of the block
(the visible "store order" residual is a ring-phase residual). A grid of 0 / 1 / 2 masks on the four computed stores
(81 + 150 with `(x | 0) & 0xFFFF` and a triple mask): `((s32)(...) & 0xFFFF) & 0xFFFF` on vtrans[0] and NO mask on
vtrans[1] is the only form above base (98.589; the reverse `2000` on vscale[0] gives 98.527). Then the eight stores
re-gridded on the new base (random orders 200, single moves 58, mask x order 162): plain field order
`vscale[0..3], vtrans[0..3]` is a 98.650 optimum (the run-157 `vtrans[3] = 0` hoist is no longer needed). Rule: when
a residual is "store A issued late", check whether the target REUSES a ugen register (t6..t9) between A's value and a
later value; if so the fix is a ring-phase shift, and an existing value-preserving mask / cast is the cheapest knob --
move it, double it, drop it, one site at a time. Line joins inside an inline are inert (every expanded statement
carries the call line).

**1b. Two more gains with the same lever (and the PERIOD-4 compensation).** post0b 4BAF4 98.021 -> 98.617 (6279ad2c8):
the 0xEE add's `andi t8,t5,0x7fff` issued before the packet `addu` (target: `addu t1; andi t6; sll t9; sw w0; sw w1`,
again a WAR order from t6 / t9 reuse). One extra iz mask alone (`((iz & 0x7FFF) & 0x7FFF) << 16`) fixes that block but
shifts the ring for everything after it (97.68); the next value-preserving mask site downstream then needs THREE extra
masks (`F4B(self, 0x30, int) & 8 & 8 & 8 & 8`) -- the ring has four slots (t6..t9), so +1 here and +3 there put the
rest of the body back in phase (grid of iz 0-3 x flags `& 2` 0-2 x `& 8` 0-7: periodic in the `& 8` count with
period 4; `& 0xFFFF & 8` counts as one slot like a second `& 8`). gui 4568 96.935 -> 97.010 (fd7b8e510): masks on the
first arm's RDPHALF_2 operands, `(dsdx) & 0xFFFF & 0xFFFF, (dtdy) & 0xFFFF` (the macro's _SHIFTL keeps 16 bits, so
value-preserving); a singles + pairs search over 11 call-argument sites (200), then a 4 x 4 local grid. Method: list
every place a value-preserving mask can go (halfword stores, operands a macro masks anyway, flag tests `x & C & C`),
run singles + random pairs with 1-3 extra masks, and when one site fixes a block but breaks later ones, look for the
compensating 4 - k at the next site.

bodies) / I() on the compare or arm (24): the target's arms are the `E > 0 ? E : 0` layout WITHOUT the pre-branch zero

masks on the three s16 count stores (27); `if (1) {}` after every statement of the second loop (61). 4FD00: 0-2 masks
in SV::operator+= / set() (34). 42938 itself after the gain: per-packet nC / next / nD x `+ 0` (200), code-free tests

## kit CCCLXXXIX (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 304): reading a uopt FP colouring residual off `-Wo,-zdbug:5` -- same-priority global LRs colour in index order, an "expression LR" exists only in blocks with two or more refs of one CSE'd load, and every code-free test is its own BB split; post0b 54E78 NM stays 99.891 (2 words), all nine list targets flat (~2000 variants) <a name="kit-ccclxxxix-agent-g-run304"></a>

**1. How to read the dump (diagnosis compiler only).** `tools/ido-static-recomp-dump/.../NCC -Wo,-zdbug:5` writes
`./uoptlist` with one `>>>active<<<{hash|k} LR reg` block per coloured live range: `adjsave` (priority), `forbidden`,
`interfere with`, `live bb - <bb> <nref> ...`. `-zdbug:6` instead prints the ASSIGNMENT ORDER. On 54E78 the order is
priority-sorted and, for equal priority, by LR index (= first appearance of the candidate in uopt's tree list). The FP
register numbers map 24 -> f0, 25 -> f2, 26 -> f12, 27 -> f14, 28 -> f16, 29 -> f18. The `{1546|k}` candidates are the
`uilod p+off` loads of the Plane fields (one hash bucket, k = field, NOT an instance); an LR exists only in BBs where the
load is referenced twice (the squares `n.x * n.x`, `idv(n.y) * n.y`; the products are CSE'd away and recomputed).

**2. 54E78 residual decoded.** Ours: n.x LR (m[0][0], BB3 + the m[3][x] tail) f12; n.z LR f12 and n.y LR f14 in BB6
(m[1][1]..m[2][3]); the idv pool variable (shared by every `idv()` expansion) f16, but it emits no instruction; d f18;
products x*d / y*d / z*d f0 / f12 / f14 in BB8. The run-303 code-free n.z test after m[0][0] is what makes n.z's LR
index (14) lower than n.y's (17); without it (f1) n.y is f12 and n.z f14 -- both ONE register below the target's
f14 / f16 (99.783, nd 4). So the target needs a third LR coloured f12 before them that is live in BB6 but NOT in BB8
(the products must still get f12 / f14). Not found: (a) code-free n.x / n.y / d tests anywhere in BB6 (each test splits
BB6, n.y / n.z stop interfering: both f12); (b) more `idv()` sites in BB6 to raise the pool variable's priority (no
variant of 132 gives an f16 square); (c) distinct identities (idw / idr / sq / non-template idf / struct wrapper / pointer
identity `*idv(&s)` / `idv<const f32>`): fold to the same pool slot or move the frame; (d) block-local `f32 zz = p.n.z`
or `const f32 &zz` (a frame word); (e) accessor reads (`me(&p)->n.z`, `cr(p.n.z)`) CSE into the same candidate;
(f) literal 1.0f on m[1][1] / m[2][2] makes 1.0f a coloured LR (556 bytes); (g) inline-operator-parameter idv on dot's o,
cp's p, set's p, the V3 ctor's a / b / c, idv(x * s): flat or worse.

**3. Other negatives (all flat).** 4B620: idv on every inline helper parameter (addE / addO / addOK / add / addG / IBase /
AIter / op[] / next / cur / ref / inc / g1 / new) and on every caller-side argument; count-increment spellings for
appends 1-2 (named `n` = +8 frame). 34890: idv / idp / accessor forms on the next() ternary, its result and make()'s
parameters (187). gui 329C: idv on load()'s nine arguments, the rect / texture macro arguments, the fw / fh / x / y
sources. bootup E2D0: `if (arg4) {}` position x form, `dot *= k` spelling, k / lim statement swap (181 + 199).
3B9C0: idv wrap of every rvalue local read (51) and every pointer base (42), zf's parameter (idv / const-ref).
46790: ring-slot burns before the `(c / 16) * 1024` shift (front-end-folded `& -1` / `| 0` / `+ 0` / `<< 0` /
`(s32)(u32)` on the quotient, `(u8)(u16)` / `(u16)` on the column: all identical code -- only a ugen-level narrowing of a
provably small value burns a slot, and the column's `(u8)` already does); folded `& 0xFFFF` on the put() store (+12

register high (f14 / f16): 99.855, nd 4 (`/tmp/claude-1000/g304/b54_v55_squares.cpp`). Every 4-byte temp in the
translation expression shares that slot (pointer `*idv(&s)`, int `+ 0 * idv(0)`: frame / offsets kept, the pool still in
the product block, x*d / y*d swapped); a discarded `idv(s);` is folded by the front end (no slot: frame 144); comma-joining
the BB6 statements makes the idv temps real stack temps (560 bytes). LEFT for the exact: the run-303 translation-temp
placement WITHOUT a 4-byte pool temp in the translation full-expression (or a second 4-byte slot for it).
A named-local blocker works too: `volatile int u;` -> `f32 u;` (same frame word, frame 152 and the 80 / 100 temps kept)
with `(p.n.y * (u = p.n.y))` in m[1][1] gives a real uopt variable LR in BB6 (u, LR index 7, f12) and the target's
n.y / n.z / d / x*d registers; what is left there is the pool variable (still created by `idv(p.n.x)` / operator*'s
idv(s)) at f12 in BB3 / BB8: n.x f14, y*d / z*d f14 / f16 (99.638). Probe these two bases first next run.
Closest form (99.855, nd 4, `/tmp/claude-1000/g304/b54_F8.cpp`): the squares base above with operator*'s float idv(s)
replaced by a folded int identity (`V3(x * s + 0 * idv(0), y * s, z * s)`): the 4-byte pool slot is still created in the
translation expression (frame 152, temps 80 / 100 = target), squares / constants / d all target -- only x*d / y*d are
f12 / f0 (target f0 / f12): with no float pool read in the product, x*d drops out of the global candidates (local f12)
and y*d takes f0. Without any translation temp and with the pool in BB6 only (`V3 a; volatile int u2, u3;` pads) the
squares and frame are right but the temps sit 8 low (72 / 92). Test / split placement around the translation on the
F8 base (96 variants): flat.
On the F8 base `V3(x * s + 0 * idv(0), idv(y * s), z * s)` (or `x * s, idv(y * s) + 0 * idv(0), z * s`) gives every
product its target register (x*d f0, y*d f12, z*d f14; frame / temps kept) but ugen now issues the y product first
(n.y loaded before n.x, nd 6, 99.826): the identity's temp evaluation is hoisted ahead of the x component. Next lever to
try there: source-line / evaluation-order spellings that keep x first (kit CCCLXXIV line layout, ctor argument order).

**6. EXACT (a072c0b4f).** Naming the x product first fixes the issue order: `inline V3 V3::operator*(const f32 &s) const
{ f32 a = x * s - 0 * idv(0); return V3(a, idv(y * s), z * s); }` on the squares base (`(p.n.x * idv(p.n.x))` in m[0][0],
no n.z test) -> 54E78 100.0 (552 bytes). `- 0` rather than `+ 0`: x - 0.0f is the identity for every float (including
-0.0), so the folded term is value-preserving. Landing: the donor's ident() jal must be renamed to gl_func_00000000
(the target's USO jal word is blank; renaming it to gl_func_00034458 links a real address and breaks the ROM compare).
Lesson: when one lever fixes one half of a colouring and costs the other, look for a second, independent slot-maker
(here an int pool temp) that keeps the frame side effect without the live-range side effect.

## kit CCCXCI (agent-g 2026-11-05, run 305): the ugen t-register "ring" is a FIFO FREE QUEUE -- read the ugen order off `NCC -S` / `cc -S` (pre-as1, registers as ugen chose them), replay it with a 20-line simulator, and SEARCH for the invisible op the target needs before writing C; as1 MERGES consecutive shifts, so `x << a << b` is a zero-code extra temporary; post0b 46790 99.254 -> EXACT, allring scan of every NM function <a name="kit-cccxci-agent-g-run305"></a>

_agent-g run 305, base 11164eb8d. Exact: 71a7f6ba1 (post0b gl_func_00046790, 536 B, NCC donor). Tools: /tmp/claude-1000/g305/ (lru.py / lru2-5.py FIFO simulator +
search, sfo.py = compile N one-line spellings with `NCC -S` and print the ugen sequence after an anchor, allring.py =
register-class-normalised diff of every 95-99.99 % NM function in build/non_matching vs expected/)._

**1. The model.** `NCC -S x.cpp` / `cc -S x.c` (run in the source's directory, no `-o`: NCC refuses `-o x.s` when
x.s already exists) writes ugen's assembly BEFORE as1: macros (`div $14,$2,16`, `mul $24,$14,1024`), every
`and` / `move` still present, registers as ugen allocated them. Replaying post0b 46790's .s shows ugen's integer
temporaries come from a FIFO free list over $14 $15 $24 $25 $9 $10 $11 $12 $13 (t6 t7 t8 t9 t1..t5; t0 and the
a / v registers belong to uopt): an allocation takes the HEAD, a register freed at its last use goes to the TAIL
(operands freed in operand order). It reproduces all 40 ugen temporaries of the function, including the "skip" of
$10 after `and $9,$25,255` (10 had been freed later than 11). So a folded mask (kit CCCLXXXVIII) is one
alloc-at-head + free-to-tail: it rotates the queue, and the "period" is the number of free registers at that point
(post0b 5A2C4's folded `& 0xFFF` / `& 0x3E` / u8 sites have period 3 or 4 depending on the site: adding 3 resp. 4
redundant masks at one site is byte-identical to the base). as1 then deletes the redundant op: `and $25,$2,15;
and $9,$25,255` becomes `andi t1,v0,15` (the merged op keeps the SECOND op's register), and a `move` is coalesced
into its source (`mul $24,..; move $13,$24; ...` keeps t8). The FP temporaries follow the same FIFO over
f4 / f6 / f8 / f10 / f16 / f18 (bootup E2D0's final scale block replays exactly).
Checker: `/tmp/claude-1000/g305/fifo.py FILE.s FUNC int|fp [POOL]` replays a function's ugen .s and flags every
allocation the FIFO does not predict. The pool is per function: in every function checked, registers uopt colours
anywhere in the function are out of it for the WHOLE function (bootup E68: t6 t7 t8 t9 only, t1..t5 are uopt variables -- 0 mispredictions
over ~600 allocations; post0b 3B9C0 and gui 329C: int t6..t9 only, 3B9C0 FP f4 / f6 / f8 / f10 only -- 0;
46790 (t6..t9 + t1..t5) and E2D0 int + FP -- 0 each). Wrong pool = a cascade of mispredictions from the first wrong head.
`/tmp/claude-1000/g305/fsearch.py FILE.s FUNC POOL A B [PMAX] [list]` searches 1-3 burns and short holds for a
residual of the form "every allocation from P on has A and B swapped" (P <= PMAX); 46790 with P = the shift: none
(as in section 2); 3B9C0's t8 / t9 tail swap: none either -- the target holds &p in a ugen t9 where ours colours it
v1 (uopt), and a simulated hold there does not give a clean swap (the uopt differences come first).

**2. Using it.** Write the target's visible registers as constraints, the source's ugen op sequence as
alloc / free events, and let the simulator search insertions (burns = alloc+free, holds = alloc at i / free at j,
operand free orders, evaluation orders) for the smallest change that yields the target. Post0b 46790 (residual:
the `(c / 16) * 1024` shift is t8, target t9, and t8 / t9 are swapped through the whole unrolled loop): with up to
three burns anywhere, either operand order of the first-block addu, the high / low half in either order and with or
without the `(u8)` burn, NO burn placement fits; the only fits are ONE extra temporary allocated right after the
div and freed by (or right after) the shift, with the `(u8)` burn removed -- i.e. ugen `div $14; X $24,$14;
mul $25,$24,1024` where as1 deletes X and renames the shift onto $14 (a `move`, or an `and` as1 can prove
redundant). Confirmation: `idx = ((c / 16) & 0xFF) * 1024 + (c & 15) * 8` (no `(u8)`) gives EVERY register of
the target -- the shift t9 and the whole loop -- and differs only by the surviving `andi t8,t6,0xff` (540 vs 536
bytes, 99.13). THE FIX: `idx = ((c / 16) << 5 << 5) + (c & 15) * 8` -- ugen emits `sll $24,$14,5; sll $25,$24,5`
and as1 merges the pair into `sll t9,t6,10` (also `* 32 << 5`, `<< 2 << 8`, `<< 9 << 1`, `<< 1 << 9`; NOT
`* 32 * 32`, which uopt folds): 100.0 (71a7f6ba1). Lever: a shift (or a power-of-two multiply that becomes one) split
in two = one extra ugen temporary held across the op with no code -- the HOLD that burns (folded masks) cannot
give. as1 does NOT merge every pair: gui 329C's four `<< 2` texrect operands split `<< 1 << 1` grow 4 bytes each
(the shifted value is used twice / feeds a MAX test); E68 `* 2` / `* 4` / `<< 2` and 5A2C4 `<< N` / `* 4` / `* 8`
splits: flat or lower -- check the length. What did NOT work first: `& 0xFF` / `& 0xF` / `& 7` / `(u8)` / `(s16)` on c / 16 (as1 knows no bits of a div
result, nor of `sra` of a known 8-bit value: `((c >> 4) & 0xFF)` also keeps its andi; it only merges and+and), `(int)(long long)` / `(unsigned long long)` round trips (two moves + a dead `sra` / `li`),
`(int)(float)`, named / const-reference / `if (0)`-kept identity inlines, comma / `?:` / `1 ?`, local `r = c / 16`
(uopt colours it), `(c / 16 * 128 + (c & 15)) * 8` (uopt does not distribute the * 8), c typed u8 / s16 / u16 /
unsigned, `ch` in place of c. Side notes: uopt does NOT fold `~~x` or `-(-x)` (two `not` / `negu` ops reach ugen;
output not checked), and does fold `x | 0`, `x ^ 0`, `x - 0`, `+ 0 * c`, `& 0xFFFFFFFF` before ugen.

**3. allring scan (every NM function at 95-99.99 %).** Only post0b 46790 is a pure t-register residual (20 words,
0 other). Bootup E2D0 is FP-register-only (10 words + the rodata addend): its arg4 is a uopt LR (`if (arg4) {}`)
coloured f14 (zdbug:5 LR 82, forbidden f0 / f2 / f12); the target's f16 needs one more interfering FP LR coloured f14
over bb 7..13 (code-free tests of arg4 / lim / dot / arg1 / v[0].x at every statement end of the tail: flat).
FIFO cross-check: with f12 / f14 in E2D0's FP pool the replay already mispredicts at the first dot product, and the
target's first 96 words are identical to ours, so the target too has uopt users of f12 AND f14 somewhere; and a
ugen-loaded arg4 (no `if (arg4) {}`: f18 here) can never reach f16 in the tail (f16 is freed by the 0x9F8 product
and goes to the tail of the queue) -- but a COLOURED f16 arg4 would take f16 out of the pool for the whole function,
and the target uses f16 as a ugen temporary from word 14 on. Neither reading fits the plain FIFO, so E2D0's target
has something else in the tail block (an invisible FP alloc / free, or an exclusion that is per region, not
per function -- not established here).
gui 329C (15 t-only + 6) and 3B9C0 (23 t-only + 20) are uopt colourings with ugen consequences.

**4. Flat this run.** Mask doubling (singles, x2..x4, and +1 / +(period-1) compensation pairs over the 14 folded
sites) on post0b 5A2C4; ctor `PadK<1..4>` inside every inline body (agent-c kit CCCXC) on 34890 / 4B620 / gui 329C;
drop-each-code-free-test on 3B9C0; s16 / u16 casts and masks on 3B9C0's inner loop (all folded before ugen,
byte-identical); FP identities (`* 1.0f`, `-(-x)`, `+ 0.0f`) and the `1.0f + arg4` hoist grid on E2D0; 3B9C0 `num` /
`t` spellings (num -= d, named difference in qa / qb / sg / t, `(d - num) / dn`: all 90-97.5, the target's f2 LR is
the difference but naming it breaks the f14 0.0f / f20 n->z pair); 34890 named ternary result (`void *r` /
reused `o`: frame +4 or byte-identical, the two results stay v0 / a1 -- zdbug:5 shows the first one has no
interference at all, so the target's a2 means it shares a variable with a longer LR); E68 separate phase-2 / phase-3
manager variables (88.4); code-free `if (X) {}` at every statement end on 46790 / 4B620 / gui 329C.

## kit CCCXCII (agent-c 2026-11-05, run 308): a whole-arm t-ring shift can be the UOPT colour count, not a missing burn -- gui 4568's first arm is the PLAIN gbi macro (no split shifts / tests / masks) once uopt colours ONE more t-register (t3) anywhere in the function; reading the target's pool off the FIFO replay; an UNUSED inline parameter (passed a variable) is an edg pool entry that un-merges a post-increment slot from ternary results: gui 4568 97.01 -> EXACT; 31A74 / 3BE1C probes (flat) <a name="kit-cccxcii-agent-c-run308"></a>

_agent-c run 308, base b90fc0ec4. Exact: 25bc5167f (gui_func_00004568, 796 B, NCC donor spliced on both trees; NM
steps 834d43474 98.141, e4b0fe208 99.196, babef4031 99.623, 8cadced0b 99.849). Items 1-2 are the diagnosis, item 6
the fix (item 3 lists what did not work before it). Tools: /tmp/claude-1000/c308/4/ (sim.py FIFO replay with burns / holds,
s25.py / s5.py / s6.py target-constraint searches, rr.py = rund.py plus a diff count restricted to an instruction
range), /tmp/claude-1000/c308/5/dump.sh (NCC `-zdbug` into a per-variant dir; lr.py from c283 reads it). Gotcha:
`NCC -S` ignores `-o` and writes `<basename>.s` into the CURRENT directory -- run it from a scratch dir, never from
the worktree._

1. **Method: constrain the replay with the target, then vary the POOL, not just burns / holds.** Write the target's
   visible register per ugen allocation (from the final object, using kit CCCXCI's merge rule: a merged shift / mask
   keeps the LAST op's register, the producer takes the removed op's register) as a dict `{.s line: reg}` and score
   simulator variants against it. On 4568's first arm (`NCC -S` of the donor with the run-185 split shifts removed,
   plain `x << 2` / `y << 2`) no single burn, burn pair or burn + hold reached the 26 constraints; a hold of exactly
   one register from the w1 `and` to the end of the arm scored 26/26, and so did simply REMOVING t3 ($11) from the
   pool for the whole function with the plain macro (`(x + w) << 2`, no split shifts anywhere): packet 1 then

intrinsically forbidden cannot be fixed by priority -- change which variable carries the value. (b) Block-local temps
in sibling blocks are separate homes in cfe; hoisting them in declaration order is byte-identical and turns "which
local does this statement use" into a free search dimension. (c) To raise one LR's priority with folded uses, make the
folds DIFFERENT expressions (an identical repeated fold becomes its own CSE LR), and fold through a cast that is not

## kit CCCXCVIII (agent-g 2026-11-06, run 309): reading edg POOL SLOTS off the zdbug:5 bit table -- a target register shared by a named local and a `?:` result means both live in ONE pool slot; NCC reuses freed statement / inline-parameter slots for later temporaries (block-scope locals always get a FRESH slot), so a user local can only share a ternary's slot if it is itself a pool entry; a removed `?:` temp can be replaced by a code-free `(I2(0), ...)` pool entry to restore the later temps' slots; a slot shared with an a0-preferred call `this` is freed by re-spelling THAT call's accessors; gui 329C 99.965 -> EXACT; post0b 34890 / bootup E2D0 negatives with the mechanisms <a name="kit-cccxcviii-agent-g-run309"></a>

All results from `/tmp/claude-1000/g306/replay.py` (dumps via `dump.sh` at zdbug:5 / 6, 0 mispredictions on every compile
below) plus the bit table at the top of the level-5 dump (`{id|k} bit isvar M 4 -NNvreg`: every edg pool temporary,
inline parameter, inline local and named local is one `isvar` with its home offset; the `isop ustr{home}{...}` lines
right after it say what is stored there first).

**1. Map pool slots before writing C.** In gui 329C (base 99.965, one register left: the RDPHALF_1 x-arm MIN copy is
a0, target t2) the slots read as: -48 = the pool variable (texture `this`, switch value, CTX reloads, xh / xl MAX,
outer x `?:` -- s0), -52 = the second pool entry (the I4 texture copy, then the yh MAX, the yl MAX and the x middle
`?:` result: with run 308's MAXSPR only the x middle copy is left in it), -72 = the TEXRECT `dl->n++` lvalue temp AND
the x MIN temp (v0). Dropping MAXSPR on yl alone (`MAX((s16)(yl),0)`) puts yl back into -52 and both become a0
(99.913): -52 is ONE uopt LR across three statements. Its replay wish for t2 needs earlier-coloured neighbours on
a0 / a1 / a2 / a3 / t0 / t1 (it has no a0 neighbour at all), so in the target that slot IS spr: the same LR, not a
colouring accident.

**2. What can and cannot share a slot.** (a) A block-scope local (`{ Spr *spr; ... }` round the switch, also as int /
s32 / u32 with casts) gets a FRESH slot after the statement temps that precede it (-60 here), never a freed one --
99.16 -> 99.12 / 98.99. (b) Inline parameters DO take freed slots (an `ld(int fmt, Spr *spr, w, h)` switch helper put
fmt into -48) but moving the switch into any inline loses the s0 pool variable and the arg0 register (arg0 becomes
memory-homed): 64-88 % over 74 signatures / orders / keeps / references. (c) Spelling the x middle `?:` into spr
(`((C ? (spr = MAX, (int)spr) : (spr = MIN, (int)spr)), (int)spr)`) removes the -52 temp, keeps spr's def and gives
the target's v0 -> t2 -> s0 copy chain, but the MIN temp then leaves -72 (it is coloured a0 at adjsave 2.0 instead
of v0 at 4.5) and the x-arm ushr / MIN / (s16)dsdx colours rotate v0 / a0 / v1. Re-gridding the four append
spellings on that worse base (kit CCCLXVI, 200 random + 117-neighbour local search, twice, plus I2 / I4 pre-temps in
the middle arm) climbs 96.31 -> 98.60 -> 99.56 -> 99.668. A code-free pool entry put back where the middle temp was,
`(s16)xl < 0 ? (I2(0), <merged middle>) : 0` (I2 = `if (0) { v = 0; } return v;`), returns the MIN temp to its -72
slot (target v0 -> t2 -> s0 exactly) and, re-gridded again, reaches 99.685; left: the x MAX arm's ushr / zero temp
(v1 / a0, target a0 / v1: the x MAX temp's pool slot -60 is ALSO the loader call's `this`, a split piece with an a0
call-argument preference that colours first). The cure is a slot move, not a priority change: the three
`CTX->load(spr->tex, w, h)` calls through zero-code accessors (200 random of 16^3 receiver x argument forms:
`me(CTX)->load(spr->tex..)`, `I4(CTX)->load(me(spr)->tex..)`, `me(CTX)->load(me(spr)->tex..)`) give the load `this`
another slot: 99.808 (left: v0 / v1 swapped between the MIN temp, the x MAX zero temp and the RDPHALF_2 dl / count),
and a one-site re-grid of the texture append (`me(me(CTX))->nD()`; nDQ / nR1 / I4 forms also exact) gives
**EXACT** (gui 329C 99.965 -> 100.0, 1144 bytes, 20a1dcf34). Lesson: when a replay wish blocks on "taken by an
earlier neighbour with a call-argument preference", read the bit table for what ELSE shares that neighbour's pool
slot and move the other user (accessor / pool-entry spelling at that statement) -- grids over the statement that
owns the slot, not over the blocked LR's own statement. (d) A plain `(spr = (Spr *)(int)MIN(..), (int)spr)` is copy-propagated
(byte-identical, as kit CCCXCVII says) -- the surviving intermediate is the -52 temp, not spr -- and neither a later

the RDPHALF_2 words (byte-identical) changes that. uopt does NOT split a variable's disjoint webs (the -52 slot is one
LR over yh, yl and the x middle), so "one variable" really is one register.

## kit CCCXCIX (agent-c 2026-11-06, run 311): NCC spill-slot ARITHMETIC (where uopt puts a spilled variable, and why 3BE1C's `off` sits 4 low), the one-variable merges that do and do not hold on 3BE1C / 4BAF4, and the 2DE0 RDPHALF_1 pool-slot map, and an EARLY-ZERO clamp spelling (`(P > 0 * (z = I(0))) ? P : z`) that gives the target's zero-before-test + copy: gui 2DE0 97.492 -> 97.772 <a name="kit-cccxcix-agent-c-run311"></a>

Tools: `/tmp/claude-1000/c311/t/` (sc.py / rund.py / df.sh / rp.sh = c310's set, replay.py = g306's), variant files under
`/tmp/claude-1000/c311/v*/V.py`. Every number is the standalone objdiff score (`-c functionRelocDiffs=none`).

**1. Where a spilled variable lands (NCC, 3 data points on post0b 3BE1C, 0 exceptions).** The level-5 bit table lists every
uopt variable as `{id|k} bit isvar M 4 -NNvreg` (memory-resident objects -- arrays, address-taken locals -- without the
`vreg` suffix). Memory objects live at `sp + frame + M` (3BE1C: q[3] at M-52 = sp+188, cx / cz at M-108 / -112 = sp+132 /
+128). The `vreg` offsets are NOT frame homes (off is M-24 but never touches sp+216); they only size the area. The FIRST uopt
spill slot is `sp + frame + minM - 4` where minM is the lowest M offset of the function (vreg or not), and the frame is
`round8(|minM| + 4 * nspill + 76)` for this function (76 = 16 outgoing + 4 + 36 s0..s7/ra save + 20). Base: minM -156,
frame 240, `off` spill at 80. Dropping the named `cell` (a 4-byte vreg, M -12): minM -152, frame 232, spill 76. Adding a
used `int` after cz: minM -160, frame 240, spill 76. The target has `off` at sp+84 with frame 240: minM -152 needs
`152 + 4n + 76 > 232`, i.e. TWO spill slots (or 4 bytes of frame outside this formula) -- one vreg word fewer than ours AND
a second slot; no single declaration change reaches it (24 s16 / u8 / int type-swaps of ok / k / a / b / cnt / i / cell
placed next to the lo pad, lo / cell / r de-naming, d / r hoisting, a pz pad at 3 positions: all give 80 @ 240 or 76 @ 232).
So the 3BE1C `sw / lw a2,84(sp)` pair is a frame-composition residual, not a priority one; do not grid it.

**2. 3BE1C one-variable merges (base 99.778, vb + hi merged = run 310's equal-score base).** Target roles: a1 = {t->a, vb, hi},
t0 = {t->b, vc}, a0 = {r, va, ic}, a2 = {off, ib}, a3 = {ia}, t1 = k. (a) a = vb: writing the int INTO the pointer
(`vb = (s16 *)(int)t->a`, `q[(int)vb]`) keeps the code (99.676, the a / b colours then swap); the reverse
(`a = (int)col->verts[..]`) loses the hoisted-6 multiply -- ugen expands `vi[1] * 6` as sll / subu / sll once the
address is int-cast (97.13). Each freed variable must keep a home (a dead `a = 0;` at the top) or the frame drops 8.
(b) b = vc the same way + dead `b = 0`: 99.702 (25 insn diffs). (c) r = va in either direction rewrites the k / ia / ib
order (94-96). Replay on (b): vb's LR (save 11.43) needs > 20 to beat the CSE'd `va[k]` load LR (ia, 20.0) for a1;
distinct folded `+ 0 * (int)(vb)` uses on pointer arithmetic change the code (98.4 and below), code-free tests of ia /
vb / off in the 0x200 arm are NOT code-free (re-loads, 1576-1580 B), `if (1) {}` BB splits at 7 sites are inert, and
naming ia (`hi = va[k]`) is copy-propagated. Flat.

**3. gui 2DE0 RDPHALF_1 t-term pool slots (97.492, length 1204 vs 1212).** From the bit table's `ustr` lines: -108 = the
dtdy<0 MAX temp, -112 = the dtdy>=0 MIN temp, -104 = the middle `?:`, -100 = the outer `?:` (`: 0` stored there too). The
two missing target instructions (`move a1,v1` in the MAX arm, `move a1,zero` instead of a folded zero) and the &D
re-materialisations in t3 (ours a1 = the `pc` int cvt LR) all follow from ONE colour: the outer slot -100 (LR213) is v1 in
ours and a1 in the target. Its replay wish needs earlier-coloured NEIGHBOURS on v1 and a0 (it has none; the MIN chain
v1 -> v0 -> result are copies, not interferences). Assigning the t-term into a named local in any arm / level (13 forms,
kit CCCXCVII style) either collapses the copy chain (1196 B) or is copy-propagated byte-identically (kit CCCXCVIII: a block
or function local never takes a freed pool slot). `char *` / `Ctx **` / no `pc` (96.9-97.3), 68 code-free tests in the
macro slots, zero-use sweep (57): flat.

**3b. The early-zero clamp spelling (gui 2DE0 97.492 -> 97.772, 1204 -> 1208 B toward 1212; commit c9bbcdf64).** The
target's dtdy<0 MAX arm is `move v1,zero; move a1,v1; ...; blez v0` -- the arm's zero is materialised BEFORE the test
and copied into the result, but the test is still against the literal 0 (blez). A 36-form grid of comparison spellings
found the shape: putting the zero into the comparison (`(P > I(0 + dtdy*0)) ? P : I(..)`) gives the zero-first + copy
and the target length (1212, 40 insn diffs) but compares two registers (`slt at,zero,v0`, 97.24); evaluating it into a
local INSIDE a folded comparand keeps the literal compare: `((P > 0 * (xq = I(0 + (dtdy) * 0))) ? P : xq)` (xq a
function-scope s32 in a dropped volatile pad's frame word; read only in the arm that assigned it) = blez + early zero +
copy, 97.772. Variants that are byte-identical or worse: `0 * I(..)` without the assignment (= the register compare),

reads xq on paths that never set it (not kept; every well-defined initialisation of xq loses it: 89-97.5). Residual:
xq is a0 / the result v1 (target v1 / a1) and the &D int cvt still holds a1 (target re-materialises &D in t3).

**4. Other probes (flat).** post0b 4BAF4 98.960: the target's a3 holds the four clip half-extents AND the spilled ctx (one

are uniformly ctx a2 / dl v0 / n v1 (ours rotate per append); shared function-scope c / d / n through a comma macro make
them v0 / a0 / a1 and break the following appends (74-76). post0b 4FD00 98.645: the target's early `move v0,zero` (return
0 hoisted) comes from the first normal pointer being v1 (ours v0); one named V3 *n for both normals drops 24 B, any
named result `int r` adds 16 B, `return p1 >= 0 && p2 >= 0` = 44 diffs but 1016 B. post0b 469A8 98.786: the
target's v1 = {arg0->0x240 both reads, &D}, t6 = temp_t6 (a ugen temp); 21 merges / folds / 190 random tests / 200
zero-use: flat or worse (folded `0 *` uses are inert in this cfe body). post 31A74 98.121: the residual is only the
join block's `mfc1 a1` vs `lui at` order (target duplicates the mfc1 into the then-arm's delay slot); 16 store / call /
arm spellings flat. post0b 493AC 99.680: the grid loop's grid / w / tbl18 / end LRs want end > w > grid priority (target

## kit CD (agent-g 2026-11-06, run 310): gui 2DE0's &D reloads read as a SPLIT of the CTX `lda` LR (not the `pc` ucvt web), and what the sibling ports do to 2DE0: each 329C lever ALONE (s-term spelling, packet pointers, loader / append accessors, I2(0) / I4(0) entries) is flat or worse on agent-c's 97.772 body, but a RANDOM MULTI-LEVER grid finds the 329C s-term + new append receivers together: 97.772 -> 97.805; the same joint draws give post0b 34890 99.643 -> 99.798 and 4B620 99.693 -> 99.725 (statement-level pool entries are inert) <a name="kit-cd-agent-g-run310"></a>

all (LR322 coloured whole, not split; 97.574 at 1196 B). uopt splits an LR only via `needsplit` / `split` (kit at the
"uopt internals" section: eager neighbour split when a higher-priority neighbour takes its last colour, or the cost
split, which does not grow pieces into call BBs) -- so the target's yl < 0 pieces need a colour conflict or a cost

## kit CDI (agent-c 2026-11-06, run 312): ugen's goto STRAIGHTENING has four line-inverting shapes, and only ONE non-trivial splice per function survives -- post 31A74's mode-1 and tail line inversions each work alone in three new forms but never together; the frame-slot readings of 36694 / 4FD00 / 48AEC (pool entries above vs below the by-value temp); statement-level `I2(0);` pool entries and line-join sweeps are inert on every post0b NCC body <a name="kit-cdi-agent-c-run312"></a>

_agent-c run 312, base 70c6507ef. No score change committed (every probe flat or worse); tools in
`/tmp/claude-1000/c312/t/` (rund.py / sc.py / df.sh / rp.sh as c311, `ins.py` = one `I2(0);` appended per body line,
`ljv.sh` = c300 lj.py wrapper -- lj.py loops forever when N exceeds the pairs of a short body: keep N <= 60 there,
`ss.sh` = ugen `cc -S` of a variant into scratch; NOTE `cc -S` ignores `-o` and writes `<base>.s` into the CWD)._

**1. ugen straightening, the shapes that put a store on a HIGHER as1 line than the call it precedes** (31A74; ugen
`-S` read, `.loc` per instruction). The store and the call must end up in ONE ugen block with the store's line above
the call's (kit CCCLXXIV tie rule).
- (A) `goto z; c: CALL; return; z: if (1) {} STORE; goto c;` (kit CCCLXXIV, z keeps its lines through the split).
- (B) `goto k; c: CALL; return; k: COMP; STORE; goto c;` with COMP containing a branch: k is spliced up to the goto
  site; k's FIRST block takes the goto's line, but the later join block holding STORE keeps its own line; c (call)
  keeps its low line and lands after k. Mode 1: `mfc1; lui at; jal; swc1` = target, but the hoisted call constant
  `ori a0,0xa00` then carries the low call line and issues one slot early (95.74 alone).
- (C) `if (0) { c: CALL; return; } COMP; STORE; goto c;` -- c is moved DOWN after the store (backward-target splice);
  same result as (B). The same wrapper placed AFTER COMP (`COMP; if (0) { c: ..} STORE; goto c;`) is not spliced.
- (D) tail: `goto k; c: CALLS; return; k: if (sel >= 127) ..; if (sel < 0) ..; STORE; goto c;` (call block inserted
  just before the sel clamps, or just before `if (sel < 0)`), and `if (0) { c: CALLS; return; }` at the same place:
  tail `mfc1; sb; jal; swc1` = target WITHOUT an `if (1) {}` split. Inserted earlier (before `v = v - ..`, before
  `lp = ..`, before `r *= ..`) the tail is right but the hoisted `lui/ori a0,0x1000A00` then issues before the sel
  `sll a2` (call line below the sel line): 95.18-95.24.
- Plain `goto z; c: CALL; return; z: STORE; goto c;` (single-block forward splice) and chains `goto g; ..; g: goto z;`
  give the store the FIRST goto's line (below the call): no inversion, but they never block another splice.
**Only one of A-D is applied per function**: every pairing (A+C, A+D, B+C, B+D, C(mode 1)+D, C+C-tail, B+B, mode-1
B / C with the tail as (A) / (D) / at the function top / inside `if (0)`, the c block ending in `goto exit` / `if (1)
return;` / falling to an exit label) leaves the SECOND region unspliced (580 B, `b z` / `b c` kept) or keeps it in
place behind a `b`. So 31A74 stays at 98.12 (one region inverted). Also not it: the store in the callee expression
`(ACCS1 = acc, f)(..)` (= `jalr t9`, 568 B). A real fix needs a construct that inverts lines WITHOUT a splice (not
found) or one splice covering both stores (the mode-1 call would have to be reached from the middle of the spliced
region, which ugen does not straighten).

**2. NCC frame slots read from the bit table.**
- post0b 36694 (95.899): the target's product `V3(..)` temp sits at M-68 (ours M-72): ONE word between the return-temp
  copy (M-52) and it; ours has two (operator*'s `const V3 &a` and `f32 s`, M-56 / M-60). Member operator*, `s * n`,
  `mul(&n, s)`, member `sc(s)`, `this->` forms: all byte-identical (edg canonicalises them). The sub copy reusing M-52
  (target fresh M-100) and the bound difference at M-104 (target M-148) are not moved by `I2(0)` / `F2(0.0f)` / `VR` /
  `VI` / `VZ` pool entries at 14 positions (F2 in the binding, `(F2(0.0f), p - a)`: 96.07 but offsets unchanged), by
  value / ctor / function-scope `t` (89), or by `t = p - n * dot` in one expression with by-value operator- parameters
  (87-90).
- post0b 4FD00 (98.645): the by-value `V3::set(V3)` temp is ALWAYS the lowest slot (sp + frame + M); the target has it
  at sp+20 (M-116) with frame 136, ours M-132 (sp+4). Putting p1 / p2 (and the test) in a nested block moves them below
  it (M-124, sp+12, byte-identical score); one or two block-scoped dummy ints reach sp+20 only by growing the frame to
  144. Two words must leave the sum() inline region (M-72..-112: this, o, f, s, me's p, SV::set this / o, += this / o,
  the verts pointer); `void operator+=`, struct assignment for the first set, a Face& sumf, macro sums, local SV: all
  rewrite the body (63-98).
- post0b 48AEC (97.726, frame 368 vs 352): the `sw / lw a1,352(sp)` pair is cmd's MEMORY home (M-16, `Mtx *&c`
  parameter of pushQ); the target's pair is at sp+256 = a caller-save SPILL below the M area -- the target's matrix

**3. Flat sweeps (counts).** Statement-level `I2(0);` appended to every body line (one per variant): 3BE1C 81,
493AC 100, 4BAF4 70, 42938 39, 4FD00 16, 36694 20, 48AEC 47 -- all identical or worse (pool-slot reuse only moves for

commits edc73caf7 + 2ad0e7d6f + 593837f67 + a24f2b8b4 + exact e2a5b62bd; 3c / 3d below). Tools in `/tmp/claude-1000/g312/` (t/df.sh side-by-side, t/sc2.py = g291 sc.py that

**1. The lever (measured on the replay, kit CCCXCIII tools).** 493AC's grid loop: target grid a0 / w and tbl18 v1 / end
v0, ours grid v1 / tbl18 v0 / end a0. The replay said "end must out-prioritise tbl18 by 6600" (save 733 vs 7333), which
no fold can buy. The cheaper reading is a FORBIDDEN colour: with `virtual void hit(int, Rec *, int, Elem *)` the
tbl18 LR (bb 74..80, the j loop that holds the `this->hit()` jalr) has forbidden {a3, s0..s2}; with `virtual int hit(..)`
(call statement unchanged, result discarded) its forbidden set gains v0 -> tbl18 v1, grid a0 (v0 / v1 taken), end v0
(not a neighbour of the v0-forbid block), w v1. Every colour in the loop is then the target's (19-line diff -> 7).
Same length, no code change outside colours; NCC only lowers the discarded result of a NON-void virtual call into
something uopt sees as a v0 def. So: when a target register pattern needs v0 to be unavailable inside a loop that
contains a virtual / indirect call, try a non-void return type on that virtual (allowed: the result is never read; say
so in a comment).

`/tmp/claude-1000/c315/c315h9_1201/h15.cpp` (98.799, frame 232, 1116 B: v1 carried in `b`, dx in `col`, dy in `pp`)._

**1. What the 8 frame bytes are.** zdbug:1 home lists of the base and of `num = S - tris[i].d; t = -num / dn;` are
identical (lowest home M-116), and nothing is ever stored between the saves (sp+88) and the homes in either object, yet
the frame grows 232 -> 240. Probing the base with code-free extra locals: +1 int or +1..+4 s16 homes -> 240, +3 ints ->
248; removing the block-local self_al (-4) then +1 int -> 232. So the base has ZERO slack, and the num form needs 5..8
more bytes. Across spellings the frame tracks uopt's `numrdstr` (redundant stores removed: 2 -> 232, 3 -> 240): an extra
store-removed assignment to a float variable (`num = S; num -= d`; `t = d; num = S - t` -> 248; an `f32 kk` block local
-> 248). Disjoint block scopes do NOT share homes (self_al in its own `{}` and dx / dy / v1 moved into the do body: no
change), and the `zf()` inline parameters own no home.

**2. Fix: drop homes BELOW the spilled off (M-104), never above it** (d M-72, p M-48, off M-104 are the only accessed
homes). Carry dx / dy in pointer locals that are dead in the inner loop and rewritten every outer iteration before any
read: `n = (V3B9 *)(s16)(s32)(qa - v0[ia]); pp = (f32 *)(s16)(s32)(qb - v0[ib]);` read back as `(f32)(int)n` (value
preserving: the s16 truncation is explicit, the int read sees a sign-extended value). Frame 240 -> 232 with all homes
at the target offsets. A PARAMETER as carrier (`unused`) becomes a callee-saved LR with a home load (+1 insn) when a read
still sees the original value; `v1` carried as `(V3B9 *)b` is fine once b is dead after `d = b - a`.

fold (t f22) and adding code-free `if (qa != 0.0f) {}` / `if (qb != 0.0f) {}` tests after the qa / qb loads and at the
inner-loop bottom (0.0f f14). Every FP register then matches.

byte-identical: uopt's colouring ties are not broken by declaration order), and climbs (~4500 draws). The carrier choice matters: dx in `col` beats `n` (98.83 vs 98.67 at frame 240).

and b, now a carrier LR, loads into a1 instead of v0 at the top). Also flat this run: 34890 h-type / loop-result

## kit CDVIII (agent-c 2026-11-06, run 317): uopt never colours t6-t9, so a target base that lives in t9 is a ugen-local value -- post0b 3B9C0's held `addiu t9,sp,184` &p comes from an int-add address over a folded-index pointer cvt whose uopt LR as1 copy-propagates away; plus the replay arithmetic that closes the bootup E68 split lever and a pointer-typed pc reading of gui 2DE0 <a name="kit-cdviii-agent-c-run317"></a>

_agent-c run 317, base c97b38836. No score change committed. Tools in `/tmp/claude-1000/c317/t/` (`grid.py` / `sc.py` /
`hc.py` = c315 / c314 with c317 paths; `dump.sh` / `rp.sh` = g306's with this worktree's include paths, `rp.sh SRC TAG
FUNC` dumps zdbug:5 + 6 and runs g306 `replay.py`)._

**1. bootup E68: the "spread m over more blocks" lever, measured.** m's LR (`{1491|0}` / LR109) has 18 live blocks and
adjsave 1603.667. Thirteen `if (m) {}` (one after each phase-3 `E68_W(E68_NEXT(m), ...)`) take it to 29 blocks and
1146.095, and m moves s0 -> t1 (forbidden grows from v0..a2 to v0..t0), 98.650 -> 96.933 at 3052 B. Each code-free test
adds a block AND one weighted use, so getting below the ~220 that the kit-CDV split needs would take about 130 blocks.
The lever is closed for E68.

**2. post0b 3B9C0: t9 for &p.** The target does `addiu t9,sp,184` once and `addu t6,t8,t9` / `addu t8,t7,t9` (index
FIRST) for the qa / qb loads. t6..t9 are never uopt colours (colour 13 is ra), so the target's &p is not a uopt LR, and
every form that holds &p in a coloured register is the wrong reading. These forms do not work:
- `pp[ia]` / `(&p.x)[ia]` / `f32 p[3]`: an uixa expression LR or a const LR (a0 / a2), base-first `addu`.
- `ia * 4 + (int)&p`: the cvt of a constant is loop-invariant, so PRE hoists it to the preheader (LR t1 / a2).
- `ia * 4 + (int)(&p.x + 0 * (int)(ia))` for qa and `... (ib)` for qb (distinct per load): ugen folds the lda into the
  load offset (`addu t6,sp,t9; lwc1 184(t6)`).

The form that works is `qa = *(f32 *)(ia * 4 + (int)((char *)&p + 0 * (int)(ib))); qb = *(f32 *)(ib * 4 + (int)((char
*)&p + 0 * (int)(ib)));`. uopt still CSEs `cvt(ixa(lda p, 0*ib))` into an LR: pre-as1 `-S` shows `move $5,$0; addu
$25,$sp,184; addu $3,$5,$25`. as1 then copy-propagates the zero away. The final code has the ugen temp t9 and the
target's index-first order, while the LR's colour (v0 / v1) stays as a PHANTOM that still blocks its neighbours. On the
committed body (99.122) this gives t9 plus the operand order, but scores 98.746. The phantom takes v1 ahead of ia, and
the ugen FIFO after the &p alloc is [t6 t7 t8] where the target's is [t8 t6 t7]. `fifoq.py` with pool t6..t9 predicts
ours with 0 mispredictions. Back-solving the target's allocs (lw 44 = t7, &p = t9, ia*4 = t8) means ib is loaded without
a ugen temp and the queue at the remap join is [t7 t9 t8 t6]; ours is [t7 t8 t9 t6]. The remap arms' final code is
identical in both, so the target must have a hidden, as1-removed temp in those arms. That is the next lead.
I brute-forced statement orders with the FIFO model, starting from ours' queue at the join ([t7 t8 t9 t6]). In phantom
mode (the t9 freed right at the phantom's def) no order reproduces the target's allocs. Two orders work only in hold
mode: &p held in t9 across both loads, ia and ib each through a ugen temp, and the sgn load BEFORE qa / qb (tris,
ia-temp, &p, sg, ib-temp, qa, qb, or ia / ib swapped). No source gives hold mode. The only form that puts the base in a
register at all is the uopt-CSE'd (phantom) one. Distinct per-load folds, even with an `if (1) {}` split between the
loads, fold the lda into the load offset (pre-as1 `l.s $f0, 184($14)`). Source reorders of the ib / pp / qa-qb / sg
statements (38 forms, def-before-use only, three pp folds x three qa / qb forms) do not hit either, and every
sg-before-qa order scores <= 95.9. So the divergence sits before the join. A wider search (`/tmp/claude-1000/c317/sim/
sim3.py`, ours' join queue fixed, up to two extra hidden alloc / free pairs anywhere) gives 16 solutions. Every one
has the same skeleton: tris, one ugen temp, &p, the sgn load, a second temp, then qa and qb, with &p still held at qa.
The second temp can be ia / ib through a temp or any as1-removed copy. So the target's pre-as1 order has the sgn load
ahead of both f32 loads, with &p held, not phantom-freed.

The replay also showed why the committed remap fold matters: `+ 0 * (int)(col->remap)` on the ib line makes remap live
in the join block, so it interferes with ib. Dropping it gives remap 15 and ib v1, 97.85. A climb on the t9 body (8
dims: remap fold, per-load fold variable, sg fold / tests, pp spelling, `if (ia) {}` sites; 3 x 190) peaked at 99.050,
with &p back in v0: no gain over 99.122. Rule used throughout: a const LR saves (uses - 1) x weight per block, so a
constant with one use per block is "not colored (-ve save)" and ugen CSEs it within the merged ugen block.

**3. gui 2DE0: the RDPHALF_2 `int pc` is a separate ucvt LR.** It is LR86 (a1, save 1.2). The target's t3 is the
`&D_00000000` const LR (LR324, t3 in ours as well), split with reloads at the MAX / MIN arm ends. The wish shows LR86
would inherit t3 only by MERGING into LR324. `char *pc` / `Ctx **pc` does merge (1200 B), but the end piece then has one
use, gets -ve save, and ugen emits `lui s0; lw s0,0(s0)`. Every code-free use of a pointer constant folds or brings back
a cvt LR (`0 * (int)pc`, `if (pc) {}`, `*(Ctx **)pc` loads). Moving the pc definition does nothing, because the LR starts
at its first use; early `if (pc) {}` tests give <= 87.9. All flat (95 variants). The pointer-pc climb (`hc.py`, 190)
does find 98.003, but only at 1196 B, which is further from the target's 1212 than the committed 1208. The dims were a
`pc == (char *)spr` fold in dtdy, `if (pc + 0 * w) {}` at the end, and the RDPHALF_2 receiver through
`(*(Ctx **)(pc + 0 * w))`. A length move away from the target does not count, so it was not kept. A size-filtered rerun
(1208 / 1212 only) has a single survivor, at the base 97.805. The 1200 B forms show why: the RDPHALF_2 load of a
pointer pc becomes a direct `lui / lw %lo` symbol load, which is no use of the const LR, so the LR's end piece is never
coloured. In the 98.003 body the receiver `(*(Ctx **)(pc + 0 * w))` is an uixa(lda, 0*w) phantom (LR a1, the 3B9C0
mechanism). After as1 the load reads the const LR's own register (`lw s0,0(t3)` like the target), and the const LR is
no longer split at all. What is still missing are the target's split-piece reloads at the RDPHALF_1 entry and the MAX /
MIN arm ends (16 B) plus the t-term v1 / a1 swap. A second climb from that body (132 draws) stays at 1196.

**4. Smaller, flat.**
- post0b 34890: dummy inline parameters before / after h (int / pointer / char, 20) are byte-identical. A nested
  `make2` wrapper (4 forms) is inert or <= 89.4. The bottom-copy result is LR0 = h's pool slot (M-12, pref a1).
  The target's bottom v1 fits a cascade slot instead (ours M-36 = LR27, already v1). These are inert or worse: the X *
  local unnamed / block-scoped / split decl, an `mk()` inline (10), and 12 loop-condition `?:` spellings (best = base).
- post0b 4B620: the replay maps the residual to an s-register rotation of edg pool variables (the count LR39 is s3 in
  ours, s0 in the target).
- bootup E2D0: arg4's LR82 (save 0.333) takes f14 because only dot / lim / -lim (f0 / f2 / f12) are coloured before it.
  The target's f16 needs a coloured f14 neighbour, and no FP LR in that block could hold it.
