## kit CDXI (agent-g 2026-11-06, run 319): post0b 34890's bottom-copy v1 IS reachable -- edg's pool is per SIZE (char / short entries never take an int / pointer slot) and a loop condition evaluated in the SAME expression as the body call has v0 forbidden, so `do {} while (postR(f(it.cur->data), C))` puts the bottom result in v1 with every home of the target; but every form that moves the bottom off h's slot (M-12) leaves h with one weighted use, and h then either goes plain (320 B) or is coloured after Mid (Mid / Base flip) -- the target's h must get its weight from a loop value that as1 later copy-propagates away <a name="kit-cdxi-agent-g-run319"></a>

_agent-g run 319, base c97b38836. No score change committed (34890 stays 99.821). Tools in `/tmp/claude-1000/g319/t/`
(`grid.py` / `sc.py` = c315 / c314 with g319 paths, cfg files in `g319/s2/`); dumps via g306 `dump.sh` / `lrinfo.py`;
about 5800 variants._

**1. The bottom copy's register comes with its pool slot.** lrinfo on the committed body: h = M-12 (LR0, a1), make's
`o` = M-16, the `X *a` local = M-20, X-this = M-24 (a2), Mid-this = M-28 (a3), the ctor temp M-32, Base-this = M-36
(v1). The for-loop's top copy reuses M-24 (a2, right) and the bottom copy reuses M-12 (a1, target v1). Writing the
loop by hand (`if (C) do {...} while (C2);`) lets each copy take its own slots. In-expression entries `(I2(0), ..., C2)`
take the free slots in order: one entry puts C2 on M-16 (v0), FIVE entries put it on Base's M-36 and it comes out v1
(the Base LR has v0 forbidden by the alloc call). Entries of a smaller type (`I2((char)0)`, `I2((short)0)`) take NO
int slot, and `Z(int v) { return 0; }` / `{ return v; }` / `void Z(int) {}` entries take none either -- only an
assigned (`if (0) { v = 0; }`) or tested (`if (v) {}`) parameter is pool-resident.

**2. v0 is forbidden for a condition evaluated in the call's expression.** `do {} while (postR(gl_func_00034458(
it.cur->data), C2))` with `postR(void *r, void *v) { if (r) {} return v; }` (or a plain comma) gives the bottom result
v1 with NO entries (LR on M-16, forbidden v0). With the make() form every home is the target's (h 44, X 32, Mid 28,
`it` 48 / 52; a named `void *r` local instead costs a home word above h and moves h to 40). Natural-call forms
(`gl_func(D, KH2(o), new X(o), ...)` / `I2(o->h)`) put h on M-16 (home 40) or drop the frame to 48.

**3. Why it still does not match.** Every body whose bottom copy leaves M-12 has h with ONE weighted use (the
register call's a1, bb 17), priority 0.57-0.83 against Mid's 1.5 (or 6.5 once a loop / init temp lands on M-28):
h is either split and spilled (320 B, `lw t7,12(a0); sw t7,44`) or Mid takes a1 / v1 before it. Code-free `if (h) {}`
tests (up to 12, before / after the new, inside a loop-in-make body) add a block per use and never lift it; with the
loop inside make() h's slot is busy (the bottom lands on M-32 = v1, the top on M-24 = a2, exactly the target) but h
has no LR at all. Assigning the condition into h (`(h = (int)(C2), h)`) is copy-propagated by uopt. The only copy
uopt keeps is an inline's return through an `if (0)` block split (`I2(C2)`: pre-as1 `move $3,$5; bne $3`), and there
the ternary keeps the FIRST slot (h's) and the parameter the later one -- the direction is reversed (the source survives
as1, so the branch stays a1). The target therefore needs a loop value in h's variable that ugen emits as a copy FROM a
v1 temp and as1 removes. Best bodies of sections 1-2: 99.750 (KH2 + postR + two top entries, h home 40, bottom a1),
98.798 (make + postR, bottom v1 and every home right, Mid / Base flipped and top a1).

**3b. The reversed copy exists: `I3(it.nxq())`.** With an iterator method whose ternary goes through a NAMED local
(`void *nxq() { void *res = (me(this)->cur = nxt) ? (...) : 0; return res; }`) and a BB-split identity
`I3(v) { if (1) {} return v; }`, the bottom is allocated `this` (M-32), ternary (M-24), and only THEN I3's parameter,
which lands on h's M-12: pre-as1 `move $5,$6; bne $5` with $5 = h's a1 -- exactly the phantom the target needs. h's
LR gains the loop use (prio 3.67, a1 with the three spill / reload pairs), and as1 removes the copy, leaving the branch
on the ternary's register. In the committed for-form this swaps the copies (top v1 / bottom a2, 99.643); written by hand
(`if ((I2(0), I2(0), C)) do { f(it.cur->data); } while (I3(it.nxq()));`) the top is a2 and the ONLY residual is the
bottom ternary in a2 (X's M-24) instead of v1: 99.821, the committed score with a different single residual. One kept
dummy parameter (`nxd(int d0)`) or one statement-level `(I2(0), 0);` before `res` moves the ternary to Mid's M-28 (v1,
but Mid / Base flip, 98.976; Base / Mid / X `if (this) {}` grid flat); two move it onto h's M-12 or X's and wreck the
cascade (85). The free list at the bottom reads M-32, M-24, M-28, M-12, ... so the target's ternary on Base's M-36
(v1) with I3's parameter still on M-12 needs a temp order no first-fit source gives yet; next lead: a statement-level
entry pattern that frees M-24 / M-28 into a different order before the res statement. Flat around it: top entry
counts 0-5 (the bottom stays M-24 whatever the top holds), for / goto / `for (;;) { ... if (!x) break; }` / `while (1)`
wrappers (60), receiver forms (`(&it)->`, `me(&it)->`, const / static / free `nxf(LIter *)` / `nxr(LIter &)`, 36: free
and static forms add the Mid / Base flip), `I4` / `I6` named-copy chains instead of the method (44), and a 190-draw
random mix of dummies, statement entries, body me() depth, receivers, wrappers, top entries and Base / Mid tests (best
99.821 / 98.976). A block-scope `{ void *res; ... while (I3((res = C, res))); }` is the same copy without the method
(99.821, no `this` slot; the ternary still takes M-24). Any held OUTER entry (`I3((I2(0), ..., it.nxz(...)))` or
`(I2(0), ..., I3(...))`, 56 with 0-3 kept dummies inside) moves I3's parameter off M-12 and h goes plain (320 B);
tested dummies (`if (d) {}`) land on Mid's M-28 WITH refs (flip), `void *` / `LIter *` `&it` dummies merge Mid into
an s-register LR (frame 72). Moving the assignment into the body (`do { f(...); res = (I2(0) x5, C); } while
(I3(res));`) puts the ternary on Base's M-36 (v1, LR prio 11.3) -- the target's bottom -- but the copy then lives in
`res`'s own M-40 home variable (v0) instead of h's M-12, so h has no LR (320 B); entries in the condition do not move
it (42 variants). Statement entries `(I2(0), ..., 0);` in the loop body are inert BEFORE the call and, after it,
move I3's parameter off M-12 even at one entry (h plain; five also put the ternary on v1). Reusing h itself as the copy (loop inside make(), `do { f(...); h = (int)(C); } while (I3((void *)h));`,
h is dead after the register call so every read sees a loop write) keeps h's LR with the a1 spills and the top a2:
99.655 with `it` declared in make (its homes drop to 36 / 40), 99.750 with `LIter it;` (default ctor) in the caller
passed as `LIter &it` and `new X(o)` written in the register call (h 44 and `it` 48 / 52 right, X / Mid homes 4 low
because the in-call `new X(o)` result is its own argument temp at M-24 and X-this drops to M-28; bottom still a2);
`X *a = new X(o)` / `X *a; a = ...` put the top in a3 (99.571 for top entry counts 0-5) unless the top is
`(I2((char)0), C)` (99.750, the same residual: the `LIter &it` parameter's own pool slot still pushes X / Mid 4 low);
make() parameter orders (`LIter &it` first / middle / last) are flat; 1-6 entries in the h assignment give bottom v1
only at 328 B; `LIter it;` declared inside make() (first or after the kept test) is 99.655 (homes 36 / 40 again).
Slot count: the target has exactly three pool words above X-this (M-12 h, M-16, M-20) and X-this IS the new
result (a2, spilled at 32), i.e. make()'s (h, o, a) -- any extra pool parameter (`LIter &it`) or a separate in-call
new-result temp costs the 4-byte X / Mid shift, so the h-reuse copy only fits if `it` is reached without a parameter.
Open: that, or the caller-scope `I3` copy (3b) with its ternary moved from M-24 to Base's M-36.

**3c. No ternary at all: the single residual becomes v0 vs v1.** Writing the iterator step as statements
(`void *nxi() { void *res; if (cur = nxt) { nxt = nxt->next; res = cur->data; } else res = 0; return res; }`, no
me()) with `while (I3(it.nxi()))` and the two-entry top: no pool temp for the bottom value, I3's copy still lands on
h's M-12, and the bottom value is `res`'s own variable -- coloured v0 because nothing forbids it (99.821, the ONLY
diff is `move v0,zero` / `lw v0,0(t0)` / `bnezl v0` vs v1). The `me(this)` and `res = 0;` init variants give the Mid /
Base flip (98.798). Forbidding v0 without moving I3's parameter is the open step: the call-in-expression forms
(`I3((f(...), it.nxi()))`, `((f(...)), I3(...))`, a named body `r = f(...); if (r) {}`) leave v0; `postR(f(...), ...)`
around or inside I3 gives v1 but moves I3's parameter off M-12 (320 B); assigning the body call into a caller-scope
`res` that the condition then reloads (`res = f(...); ... while (I3((res = it.nxi(), res)))`, 30) is 320 B.

**4. post0b 4B620 (99.725).** The appends 1-2 old count is pool variable 592 (LR39, s3, shared with every later
count); the target's s0 holder is variable 720 (LR32, the appends 3+ inc() `this` / head). Index-expression entries `&head->buf[(I2(0), ..., head->count++)]` with and
without kept hi / lo (81) move the count to s2 / a0 but never s0; the 3b `I3` copy on the index
(`&d->head->buf[I3(d->head->count++)]`, with I2 / I3 nesting, 25) keeps the count s3 and adds frame 184. bootup E2D0 and gui 2DE0 were only re-read.

## kit CDXII (agent-g 2026-11-06, run 321): a value that must NOT take v0 is pushed off it by keeping an earlier call result live -- post0b 34890 EXACT: the loop body's call result held in a block-scope `void *rv` with one code-free `if (rv) {}` after the do-while keeps v0 occupied across the bottom step, so the step result takes the target's v1 (99.821 -> 100); random code-free test / fold searches flat on 3BE1C / 4B620 / 42938 / 4BAF4 / 4FD00 <a name="kit-cdxii-agent-g-run321"></a>

_agent-g run 321, base 83e022a60. Commits 80e14f05d (34890 EXACT, NCC donor renamed without `_nm`, spliced over a
placeholder on both build paths, NM_DONOR block replaced) and c9dcfc390 (4BAF4 NM, section 3); no clip change. Scripts in `/tmp/claude-1000/g321/t/`:
`rt.py` (random 1-3 draws of `if (e) {}` inserted after unique anchors, or `('R', old, template)` fold replacements,
with a per-anchor list of expressions that are defined on every path there), `tog.py` (random toggles of
`+ 0 * (int)(e)` folds per site), `grid.py` / `hc.py` / `sc.py` copies._

**1. 34890: the v0-occupancy lever.** Kit CDXI left one residual: the bottom step's result (`res` of the if / else
`nxi()` step) in v0, target v1. Random code-free tests (17-19 anchors in the ctors, make(), nxi() and the loop, 1-3
per draw, three seeds, 570 compiles) and zero-code folds on the step / body / make arguments (190) were all flat
(<= 99.821): no extra USE of anything changes which register the step result takes. What the target has instead is
v0 BUSY there: the body call's own return value is live across the bottom block. Writing

    if (top) { void *rv; do { rv = gl_func_00034458(it.cur->data); } while (I3(it.nxi())); if (rv) {} }

(rv assigned in the body, tested once after the loop; the test reads a value written on every path into it) keeps
the call result in v0 from the jal through the step to the exit edge, so the step result is coloured v1: every
instruction matches. Scope matters: rv at function scope (or before the iterator) adds a 4-byte home and shifts
h / Mid / Base spill homes down by 4 (99.857 / 99.762); block scope inside the guard keeps the target's homes
(100). The type is irrelevant (void * / int / char * / O * / Link * all exact); re-using the dead parameter `o` for
the result is exact too; a test INSIDE the body (rv dead at the step) is 99.821 again.
**Rule:** when a residual is "value X in v0, target uses the next free register", look for a value the target keeps
in v0 across X (a call result, a return-value variable initialised early) -- a code-free test of that value after
X's range, in the narrowest scope that reaches it, reproduces the occupancy without adding a home.
4FD00 shows the same signature (the target's `or v0,zero,zero` scheduled mid-way through the second face sum, so the
later nrm addresses use v1 / t0): `int ret = 0;` at 12 statement positions x 2 tails x 4 types (96) is <= 96.77 (at
positions before p1 ret adds register pressure and a spill, frame 144; after p1 it is coloured a0 and copied);
nine `&&` / ternary / inverted return spellings (9): <= 97.75 (1000-1016 B).

none above 99.778 (dropping the `ok = 0 + 0 * (int)(va)` fold gives the target's ia a3 / lo a1 but va t2 / vb v0 /
the k index a1, 99.714). Seeded from g316/a39 (99.357 standalone): one code-free test of this / cx / cz / cnt after
the 0x200 test gives 99.599, nothing higher. Without any fold the body is 1564 B and va takes v0 (98.45): the

## kit CDXVI (agent-c 2026-11-06, run 324): as1 orders a block's instructions by SOURCE LINE -- post 31A74 EXACT: a statement that must EXECUTE first but SCHEDULE after a later one goes into the body of a one-pass `for` whose STEP holds the later statement (`for (mode = 1; mode; call(..., acc), mode = 0) { store; }`): the call then carries the header's lower line, so its `mfc1 a1` is scheduled ahead of the store's `lui at`, and as1 copies the join block's new first instruction into the preceding `b` delay slot; second if(1)-split goto block in the same function does not merge <a name="kit-cdxvi-agent-c-run324"></a>

_agent-c run 324, base ab99a141c, commit 11b424123 (31A74 NM 98.121 -> 100, promoted in place: `#ifdef NON_MATCHING` /
INCLUDE_ASM dropped, no new symbols, ROM byte-identical, verify-blocks 6/6, no length change). Scripts in
`/tmp/claude-1000/c324/t/`: `grid.py` (objdiff fuzzy + instruction line-match per variant), `dd.sh` (score + register-level
diff), `dump.sh` (zdbug:5 dump, agent-g's g306 script pointed at agent-c)._

**What the residual was.** Mode 1's join block (after the `acc *= k` / `acc = 0.0f` arms): target `mfc1 a1,f0` (call
argument), `lui at`, `jal`, `swc1 f0,-13632(at)` (store in the jal slot), and the taken arm's `b` jumps one word past the
join with `mfc1 a1` copied into its delay slot. Ours: `lui at`, `mfc1 a1`, `jal`, `swc1` with `b ...; nop`. The ugen output
(`cc -S`) is the SAME instruction list in both orders (`s.s acc, ACCS1; li a0; mfc1 a1, f0; jal`); only the `.loc` lines
differ. as1's list scheduler takes ready instructions in source-line order: with the store on the lower line its `lui at`
goes first (and an at-using macro is never copied into a branch delay slot), with the call on the lower line `mfc1` goes
first and becomes the copyable join head.

**How the line order was reversed without moving the store after the call.**
- agent-c run 300's form (the store in an `if (1) {}`-split goto block written after the call, merged back by uopt) already
  served the tail of 31A74; a SECOND such block in the same function never merges (the second goto block stays out of
  line: +16 B), whichever of the two it is and wherever the blocks are placed (16 placements, with / without `if (1) {}`).
- Store-in-argument / comma / one-line / multi-line call spellings (17) all keep the store's line first: flat.
- A one-pass `for` puts the step's code AFTER the body but on the header's (lower) line. `mode` is 1 on entry to that
  block, so `mode = 1` is value-preserving, `mode` as the condition folds, and `mode = 0` is a dead store before the
  `return`: uopt removes the loop entirely and leaves exactly the store-then-call block, with the call's line now one
  ABOVE the store's. A fresh `int k` gives the same code; `for (; mode == 1; ...)` / `for (;; call) { if (..) return; }`
  are worse (the compare survives / the loop stays).
Use it wherever a residual is a pure as1 ORDER difference inside one block (same instructions, same registers) and the
earlier-scheduled instruction belongs to the statement that executes LATER.

**Negatives (this run).** The same line lever does not reach the jump-table range-check delay slot of post0b 396FC /
51AD8 (as1 still steals the default block's first instruction: default call in a for step above the switch, cases as
returns, 7 forms; default block / label / line-layout spellings, 14). A scan of every `sltiu at / beqz at` in asm/ finds
the exact jump-table functions that keep `sll` in the slot all have the default reached from more than one place
(after-switch code or table holes); 396FC / 51AD8 / mgrproc 1824 / titproc 116C have distinct table entries.
A 180-switch random mini-corpus (`/tmp/claude-1000/c324/m0/gen2.py`, IDO 7.1 -O2, 3..7 distinct cases + one default)
keeps `sll` in the range-check slot ONLY when the default head is unstealable (a store, an `at` macro such as a global
store / `lui`, a load -- as1 never steals a `lw` -- or a `jal` with its arguments already in place; a second 190-switch
corpus with 396FC-style spilled-parameter arms, `gen3.py`, agrees; a third, `gen4.py`, with the 396FC arms and
default first / middle / last, do-while(0) / trailing `if (1) {}` / label wrappers, fn-pointer / void / cast-argument
default calls, steals the move in 190 / 190); every stealable register-move head
(`move a0,a3`, the 396FC shape) is stolen. `-g3` (diagnosis only) keeps `sll` but hoists the move into the head block
instead (not the target either), so the target's default block is not reachable from these switch shapes.
**ugen FP temp model (new tool `/tmp/claude-1000/c324/t/ringsim.py CC_S FUNC`).** IDO 7.1 ugen hands out FP temps
from a FIFO free queue initialised `f4 f6 f8 f10 f16 f18`: each temp def pops the head, a temp is pushed back at its
LAST use (before its next def), several frees at one instruction in operand order. On bootup E2D0's `cc -S` listing
this predicts all 65 temp defs. Applied to the target: its after-clamp temps (1.0 f8, sum f18, then f4 / f6, f10 / f8,
f16 / f18) fit the model only as `li.s f8; l.s f16 (arg4 as a TEMP); add.s f18` from the queue `f8 f16 f18 f4 f6 f10`,
i.e. the target's arg4 is NOT a coloured LR at all (which is why nothing holds f14), and its queue at that point
differs from ours (`f6 f18 f8 f4 f10 f16`, the same with or without the 0x9F8 load as a temp) although every earlier
instruction is register-identical -- so the divergence is in ugen ORDER upstream (hidden by as1's rescheduling) or in
which loads are temps. Without `if (arg4) {}` ours does make arg4 a temp (520 B: as1 then puts `mtc1` before the
`lwc1` and drops the nop); the open lead is a body whose queue reaches `f8 f16 f18 ...` at the sum.
bootup E2D0 (99.542): zdbug:5 shows arg4 = LR 82 (adjsave 0.333, live bb7..13, forbidden f0 / f2 / f12 from dot / lim /

## kit CDXVIII (agent-c 2026-11-06, run 326): `-Wab,-R` (as1 scheduler trace) read on the open as1-order residuals -- as1 runs a SECOND list-schedule pass per block that pulls the fall-through block's head into the block (mgrproc 1824's `li at,1` fills a load-latency idle cycle; 396FC's default head fills the empty bound-check slot); the root tie-break is ugen order (first-visited node wins), newly-ready nodes are visited first, which pins 65EE4's jal-slot choice to ugen ARGUMENT order; no gain, caps re-confirmed with mechanisms <a name="kit-cdxviii-agent-c-run326"></a>

_agent-c run 326, base c2dcd8285. No source change committed. Scratch in `/tmp/claude-1000/c326/` (1 = 396FC, 4 = mgrproc
1824, 5 / 6 = 65EE4, 8 = mgrproc micro-corpus, 9 = 2E354 trace); grid = `c326/t/grid.py` (c324 grid with c326 paths)._

**Tool.** `cc ... -Wab,-R x.c -o x.o > x.txt 2>&1` (IDO 7.1, any -O) prints, per scheduled block, every node
(`inst` = final encoding, `lineno`, `aftercycles`, `afternodes: N/latency`) and each `Picking node` step with the
ready list. A function's blocks appear TWICE: pass 1 (ugen's block alone) and pass 2 (the same block plus at most one
instruction pulled from a neighbouring block). Find a block by grepping an instruction word (`grep -n "inst 8e0207d4"`).
Load -> consumer latency is 3 in as1's model (two cycles between); lui -> use 1.

**1. mgrproc 1824 (98.52; residual = `li at,1` of the outer switch's `case 1` compare scheduled above the `beqz`, plus the
external jump-table displacement).** Pass 1 of the block `lw t6,0x7EC; lw v0,0x7D4; addiu t7; beqz v0; [sw t7]` leaves
time 2 idle (lw t6 at 0, addiu cannot issue before 3). Pass 2 re-schedules the block with the fall-through block's head
`li at,1` (`lineno` of the switch line, `before 0`) added, and it lands in the idle cycle. The target keeps the stall.
Micro-corpus (`c326/8/b1..b9.txt`, 30 shapes): the pull happens whenever the block before the compare chain has an idle
cycle -- selector loaded in the same block (lw / lbu / lh), reloaded after a call, joined block start, if-else chain,
goto chain, default / return / case-order variants, switch inside `if (1) {}`. It does NOT happen when the selector
is already in a register (47F68 shape: no idle cycle) or when the selector load sits in its OWN block (2E354: the
`lbu t0,20(s0)` is a join-block head copied into a `b` delay slot, the `beqz` is a separate one-node block, so pass 2
has nothing to fill). In 1824 the stall comes from the counter load `lw t6` (scheduled first: aftercycles 5 > 4), not
from the selector, and the target has no other instruction to fill it, so the target's block is not reachable while
the compare block is exclusive. Flat: 122 line layouts of the counter / switch lines (joins, splits, blank lines,
one-pass `for` step / init forms) and 48 increment (`+= 1`, `++`, pre-increment) x selector (`unsigned`, `default`
first, leading / in-case `if (1) {}`, selector read into a reused local before the increment) combinations -- all
98.5211, byte-identical.

**2. post0b 396FC (98.66) / 51AD8 (99.15) bound-check delay slot.** Pass 1 of 396FC's head block leaves the `beqz`
slot empty (no idle cycle, nothing schedules after the branch); pass 2 adds the default block's `or a0,a3`
(`lineno` = the `default:` call line) to the DAG, i.e. the steal is decided between the passes, before any line
or latency question. A source guard gives the default a second predecessor and as1 then keeps `sll` in the slot
(`if ((unsigned)(a1[0] - 109) < 6) switch ...` with the cases returning and the call after): but the switch keeps its
own bound check, +12 B (`addiu; sltiu; beqz` twice, 97.91 / 624 B) -- 28 guard forms (four guard spellings x
brace / default / goto-label tails, if-else) all +12 or worse. Confirms kit CCLIX's addendum: the target's default
behaves as shared, but no zero-code second reference exists in C.
**Later the same run: 51AD8 EXACT (68c18cdea).** `scripts/zero-use-sweep.py` (default vocab, first 190 variants)
found `out->w54 = src->w54 + 0 * (int)(pp);` in case 211 (pp set earlier in that case): one counted use of a
pointer web in an UNRELATED arm and as1 keeps the fall-through `sll` in the bound-check slot (240/240 words). So
the "steal" is not a fixed rule of exclusive defaults: it follows the same pass-2 worklist as section 6, which any
change to the function's webs can reorder. Landed with the 52CD4 donor recipe (game_libs_o2_51AD8.c,
gl_func_00051AD8_rodata = 0x1BB4). The same sweep on 396FC (vars a0 / a1 / q / s / m / p / s2, with and without
--exprs, 310 variants) is flat; NOTE the tool's float-typed filter wrongly skips 396FC's pointer locals (they are
declared next to f32 ones) -- pass `--vars` explicitly.

**3. post1b 65EE4 (89.73, -Olimit 1 donor): the jal delay slot of calls 2 / 3 follows ugen argument order.** Trace of
call 3 (`f(&G, G.base)`, ugen `la $4; lw $5`): roots lui a0 / lui a1 tie (aftercycles 2) and the first-visited (=
earlier ugen node) wins, then the newly ready `lw a1` is visited before the older `addiu a0`, jal goes next, and the
leftover `addiu a0` fills the slot. The target (`lui a1; lui a0; addiu a0; jal; lw a1`) is exactly that walk with the
a1 load FIRST in ugen order. Only a side-effect argument reorders ugen: `(0, G.base)` evaluates a1 first (the slot gets
`lw a1`) but through a callee-saved temp (`lui s0; lw a1,40(s0)`, +8 B, frame 40, 97.10 -- not kept). 9 a0 spellings
x 6 a1 spellings and 22 more a1 forms (volatile view, `- 0`, `^ 0`, unary plus, casts, index forms, `?:`) x {call 2,
call 3, both}: ugen order unchanged (or worse). Prototypes (none / typed / varargs / void * / int) do not reorder either.
Statement lines do not help: cfe gives the whole call one `lineno` (args split over lines keep the first line).

**4. bootup 6204 / E9FC (`lui a0` before `sw ra`).** The prologue's `lineno` is the line of the opening `{` (a
multi-line header gives the `{` line), so a call can at best TIE with `sw ra`; on a tie the earlier ugen node
(`sw ra`) wins. No C layout puts the call's tokens before the `{`; an inline C++ helper (NCC) carries the CALL SITE
line, not the helper's. Dead without a different ugen order.

is the `sltiu 5` immediate (table length, cfe/ugen, kit CCLIX); titproc 116C's other words are v0 / v1 colour swaps

block, the two divisions) flips it, 122 blank-line layouts and 106 `if (1) {}` splits do not. The flips came
from legal source shaping:

  argument (`f(&D, var_v0 + 0 * var_v0)`, not `vt = self->vt + 0 * temp` after the call): the value no longer lives
  across the call, the a1 spill and its slot go (frame 48 -> 40 = target, sp24 / sp20 land on 36 / 32) and it
  colours v0 with `move a1,v0` in the jal slot (95.02 -> 95.66);

Sweeps (`c326/13/cfg10..15.py`): dead stores of every s32 field read in a test into var_v0 / sp24 / temp / sp20,
into var_v0 at every other read, and pointer reads into `varg`: the three above are the only gains. Rule of thumb:
when a function's residual is a ring / delay-slot pattern shared by many blocks, try ONE dead store of a loaded field
into a local that already has a web elsewhere (a fresh local is deleted by uopt and changes nothing; the same sweep
with a new `int ds` was flat on 1ADC, 116C and mgrproc 1824). Then (3a1d2eacf, 97.85): the switch-2 case-0 FP stores back in field order (534 / 538 / 548 / 550 / 54C:
shares the 1.0 `lui at` like the target, -4 B alone) TOGETHER with `if ((var_v0 = self->unk4E0) == 7)` (+4 B: the

source-line order (kit CDXVI) puts the 0x4E4 store first, as in the target (41 join variants elsewhere flat; the

entries are distinct arms for 0, 3 and a shared 1 / 2 arm. A fifth label would need a fifth value inside 0..3, so no legal C
switch with the target's semantics has a different case range or an extra label; the residual is the front end (kits
LXXVI / CXL / CCLIX). Keep the phantom `case 4: break;`. Same reading for 1ADC (`addiu -1; sltiu 4`: labels exactly 1..4).

**2. GAIN 76F0 97.90 -> 99.00 (2308 B = target; 6978defe6).** Target switch 3 (`switch (self->unk4DC)`, compare chain on
1 / 2) is `lw v1; li at,1; beq v1,at; move v0,v1; li at,2; beql v0,at`, the case-1 tail test reloads 0x4DC into **v1**,
and its false exits branch straight to the post-switch `!= 2` compare (`beqzl v1,+700; li at,2`), only the store / call
paths go through the reload block. Ours compared on v1 without the copy, reloaded into t0 and sent every exit through the
reload. Micro corpus (`c328/21`, `switch (s->a) {case 1: fades; tail test; case 2: ...} if (s->a != 2 ...)`):
- the `move v0,v1` copy appears when the 0x4DC load web stays live through case 1: one fade block gives it, two or three
  do not; a code-free use of the field after the fades (`if (self->unk4DC) {}`, or `while (0) { if (self->unk4DC) {} }`)
  restores it with three fades (in 76F0 only the position after the LAST fade works; before / between the fades: no copy);
- the direct `beqzl v1,+X; li at,2` exits need the false exits written as `break`s (`if (self->unk4DC == 0) break; if
  (self->unk30 != 0) break; if (self->unk4F4 <= 0) break;` instead of the nested `if (a && b) { if (c > 0) {...} }`):
  a nested-if false exit joins the store / call paths at the inner join, where uopt's PRE puts the reload for all of
  them; a `break` edge reaches the switch's own join, where the value is still available. Case 2 the same
  (`if (!(self->unk4F0 & 0x10000)) break; if (self->unk500 == 0) break; { ... }`).
Then a dead store `if ((temp = self->unk4F4) == 0)` (greedy dead-store re-sweep) puts the e[23] call's `lw t9; lh tN` in
the target order (no `jalr` nop), and run 326's `(var_v0 = self->unk4E0) == 7` dead store goes. Left: the switch-1 bound
check is the `beqzl` + `lw t3,0x500` copy again and the case-1 counter copy `move t3,t2` is gone (they cancel in length);
every t-ring offset after switch 1 follows them. The 2312-B variant `((u32)(temp = self->unk4F0) << 11)` (99.28) has the
counter copy and the call order but still the `beqzl`; removing run 326's `(var_v0 = self->unk4E4)` store flips the

bound-check slots trade through pass 2's worklist (kit CDXVIII 6); dead-store sweeps on both sides found no 2308-B pair.

## kit CDXXI (agent-c 2026-11-11, run 330): the jump-table default "steal" is decided by ONE EMPTY as1 BLOCK in front of the default -- 51AD8's exact fold works only because it moves a `.alias $8,$sp` directive behind case 211's closing `b`; re-assembling `cc -S` output through as0 + as1 by hand (byte-identical to the C path) proves 396FC = our code + that one empty block; the empty block needs a register-held LDA address used as a memory base (or unreachable unlabelled code), neither of which 396FC's target has, so 396FC is a verified cap; E2D0's FP temp FIFO checked exhaustively (no upstream ugen order reaches the target queue) <a name="kit-cdxxi-agent-c-run330"></a>

**1. The `.s` oracle: hand-edit ugen output and assemble it exactly like the C path (diagnosis only).** `cc -S` output fed

by hand with the C path's flags instead and the object is byte-identical to the C build (checked on 51AD8 and 396FC):
```
B=tools/ido-static-recomp/build/7.1/out
$B/as0 -G 0 -r4300_mul -mips2 -EB -g0 -O2 x.s -o x.b -t x.st
$B/as1 -t5_ll_sc_bug -elf -G 0 -p0 -r4300_mul -mips2 -EB -g0 -O2 x.b -o x.o -t x.st
```
(`/tmp/claude-1000/c330/t/sor.sh x.s`). This answers "what does ugen have to emit for as1 to produce the target?" in
seconds; then search for C that makes ugen emit it. Never ship the edited .s.

**2. 51AD8 re-read: the zero-code fold works through an alias directive.** `cc -S` of the exact donor vs the donor without
`+ 0 * (int)(pp)` differs in ONE line: `.alias $8,$sp` (the end of pp's no-alias region: pp = `&gl_ref[v]`, an LDA plus a
variable index, used as a load base) moves from after `lw $3,0($8)` (end of the call block) to after case 211's closing
`b $49`, i.e. right in front of the `default:` label `$48`. In the `-Wab,-R` trace that is the extra empty
`Initial nodes:` block. Moving only that directive in the non-exact .s (oracle) flips the bound-check slot from
`lui a0,2` to `sll t6,t6,2`. Rule: as1 treats the empty block (it ends with nothing and falls into the default) as a
second predecessor of the default, so pass 2 no longer copies the default head into the `beqz` slot and pulls the
fall-through `sll` instead -- this is kit CXXXII's "the target's default behaves as shared", made concrete.

**3. 396FC: the target IS our code plus that empty block.** Oracle on 396FC's `cc -S`: inserting `.alias $9,$sp` (or a
`.noalias`) after the LAST `b $41` (end of case 114, just before the default label) gives 153 words identical to the
target apart from the two rodata reloc fields; the same directive after any of the other five arm-closing `b $41`
does nothing; `.livereg`, `.loc`, `.set reorder` or an unreferenced label there do nothing. An unreachable
INSTRUCTION after the `b` works too (as1 deletes it, 153 words, slot keeps `sll`).
What emits those in C:
- `.noalias rX,$sp` / `.alias rX,$sp`: a register holding a GLOBAL LDA (`la`) used as (or in) a memory base;
  `.noalias rX,$gp` / `rX,rY`: a register holding a STACK address (`addu rX,$sp,K`) used as a base. The `.alias`
  goes after the terminator of the block that holds the region's last use (a folded zero-code use extends it, the
  51AD8 move). Only real register-based accesses emit them: `Xform *xp = &xf` stores, a `f32 *k` pointer to the
  0.01 literal, `if (xp) {}` / `0 * (int)xp` uses (c330/4 v1..v4) are folded by uopt into `80(sp)` / `lui at`
  addressing and emit no directive; as1 does not fold `la r; lwc1 0(r)` or `addu r,sp,K; swc1 8(r)` back (oracle),
  so any such access costs 4+ bytes.
- unreachable unlabelled code after a `b`: in four whole-file surveys (post0b, post, game_uso, bootup, timproc b5,
  game_libs, tail, titproc, mgrproc) the only case is the EPILOGUE of a function whose body ends in an infinite
  `for (;;)` (34548 / 3485C / 61478). 396FC's epilogue follows the default, so this shape cannot sit before it;
  `break; stmt;`, `goto out; stmt;`, `return; break;`, a call after `break`, `while (1) {}` / `for (;;) {...}` after
  the arm, the switch inside `for (;;)` / `do {} while (1)` with every arm returning, and an empty `for (;;) {}`
  after an all-return switch (c330/7 u1..u7, w1..w4) are all removed by uopt: byte-identical 98.660.
Extra case labels in front of `default:` (c330/7 x0..x9): `case 115:` / `case 108:` (table entries shared with the
default -- the 52CD4 / 40304 shape) DO keep `sll` in the slot (99.993 / 99.987, 612 B) but grow the table to 7 entries
(`sltiu 7`; the decoded USO table at +0x1A64 has exactly 6 words before the 1/32767 literal at +0x1A7C), so they are
decode errors, not fixes; out-of-range labels (`case 0:` / 200 / 1000 / -1 / 0x7FFFFFFF, empty-statement arms, two
labels) add a compare chain (+20..+56 B).
Whole-file census of `.noalias` definitions (c330/8, 9 files, ~720 directives): the register is an `la` of a global
(279 vs `$sp`), an `addu rX,$sp,K` stack address (vs `$gp` / other registers), or pointer arithmetic on one of those
(index `mul` / `addu`, struct-copy cursors: ugen's struct copy between a global and a stack object brackets the
loop tail with `.noalias src,dst` / `.alias src,dst`); none comes from a parameter or a loaded pointer. The only
`.alias` runs after a closing `b` in exact code are region ends of such registers (e.g. post0b 4F2DC's
`sp+248+i*12` row pointer). A steal-residual scan over every NM function at 60-99.99 % (`c330/t/stealscan.py`:
our slot = an instruction the target keeps in the fall-through block) finds 396FC only.
Every memory access in 396FC's target goes through sp, at, a param copy or a loaded pointer, so no legal
zero-code source form can produce the directive: **396FC is a verified cap** (the remaining word is this as1 block,
not a register / order question). Do not re-run fold / test / split sweeps on it. 51AD8-like targets elsewhere: look
for an LDA-based pointer whose last use can be moved to the end of the arm that physically precedes the default.

**2. edg frame allocation order (mdl.py on -g3 builds).** Words are handed out top-down in SOURCE order:
function-scope named locals first (declaration order), then, statement by statement, the pool temps each
expression needs (reused by type once freed) and the named locals of each block AS THE BLOCK IS MET -- a
block-scoped `{ int z = 0; if (z) { z = 1; } }` placed before 4FD00's final test lands at vfp-136 / -140 / -144,
BELOW the 12-byte V3 by-value temp at vfp-132 (z emits no code; each one costs a word at the frame bottom).
So a temp's offset is set by how much pool was allocated BEFORE its first use, and the words "below" a temp are
whatever is first needed AFTER it.

`vs.py` = spec-driven variant scorer (BASE + VARS list of replacement sets, cap 200), `dump.sh X.cpp N` = `-Wo,-zdbug:N` dump

forbidden summary, `dd.sh X.o` = register-level diff vs the target)._

**1. Read the colour constraint off the dump before touching source.** uopt interference is pure basic-block
granularity (checked on the whole 2DE0 table: no two same-class LRs that share a block are ever non-interfering, even a
`deadout` copy source and a `firstisstr` copy destination), and colours go out in adjsave order (v0 = 1, v1 = 2, a0 = 3,
a1 = 4, a2 = 5, a3 = 6, t0 = 7, t1 = 8, t2 = 9, t3 = 10, s0 = 14). 2DE0's x LR (60, blocks 10..17) is a subset of the
(s16)xh LR's blocks (10..23), so ANY a0 holder that forbids a0 for x also forbids it for xh: the target's x = a2 /
xh = a0 is reachable only if xh is coloured before x. That turned "find a lever for xh" into "raise xh above 1.0 and
remove n (2.0, a0)": `nextp()` (n is the load LR itself, no separate phantom) + dropping the run-309 `if ((s16)(xh)) {}`
(which had stretched xh to block 23) = xh 1.5 -> a0. Either change alone is ~91 / ~96 (other colours cascade).

of the packet LR: ANY two of seven s-term / t-term slots (21 pairs, all 99.109) lift it over the lda; one fold is inert,
code-free `if (_g) {}` tests before / after the stores are inert.

whose yl < 0 piece is reloaded at the join -- i.e. a split lda, which needs t3 taken by an earlier LR in the yl < 0

## kit CDXXVIII (agent-c 2026-11-11, run 337): gui 2DE0 EXACT -- the &D lda's cost split is reached from the COMMITTED body by deleting the split-blockers one at a time (full factorial, constrained on `lui t3` x 7), and the last missing neighbour-budget unit came from an append SPELLING (TEXRECT `me(CTX)->nD()` instead of `nextp()`), read off the instrumented BFS trace <a name="kit-cdxxviii-agent-c-run337"></a>

_agent-c run 337, base 06fa16ab6, commit 1f88022b2 (99.109 -> 100, 1212 B). Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/c337/`;
tools `c337/t/cmb.py` (all subsets of a toggle list, prints the `lui reg,0x0` register string per variant),
`grid.py` (slot x alternatives product), `cc3.py` (random climb constrained to exactly 7 `lui t3,0x0`),
`rmap.py` (aligns target / ours by mnemonic and counts target-reg -> our-reg substitutions), `c337/11/j.py`
(joins two `-Wo,-zdbug:5` LR tables by uopt VAR id and prints the LRs whose colour differs), `c337/11/nbr.py`
(an LR's interference neighbours with colour / adjsave)._

**1. Score the SPLIT directly, not fuzzy.** The kit-CDXXVI target pattern is "&D lda materialised exactly seven
times, all in t3, no `lui s0` re-form". A one-line objective -- the concatenated `lui (\w+),0x0` registers of the
function (`t3t3t3t3t3t3t3` = split in t3; `t3t3t3t3a1a1a1` = committed pc LR in a1; `t3t3t3t3t8` = remainder in the
yl >= 0 arm) -- classifies every variant without reading the allocator. Fuzzy on the split bodies sits 6 points
below the committed body until the very last step, so a fuzzy climb never finds it.

**2. Full factorial from the committed body (1024 variants, 6 commands).** Ten toggles = the differences between
the committed 99.109 body and the run-334 split body (xh I4, s-term MAX carrier, s-term trailing `(int)spr` read,
t-term xq-zero + `_g` fold form, yl >= 0 `0 * pc + 0 * _g` fold, `if (spr) {}` before RDPHALF_2, MS form, the
RDPHALF_2 receiver through pc vs CTX, the dtdy `0 * &D` fold, pc decl). Exactly two subsets split: {s-term MAX
carrier off, t-term simplified, yl >= 0 folds off, spr test off, dtdy fold off} (+/- xh I4). The trailing s-term
read and the pc receiver do NOT block the split (kit CDXXVI's "trigger" was body-specific). Then a slot grid over
the two MAX spellings (10 x 10) kept the split for 64 of 100 and showed the t-term spellings are all CANONICALISED
to one code (any zero-first / copy form without a live-variable fold gives identical bytes).

**3. Fold survival rule.** In the t-term `xq = I(0 + dtdy * 0 + 0 * V)`, the fold changes code only when V is a
variable LIVE in that region (`_g` packet, pc, x, y); folds of w / h (memory homes), spr (dead there), x0, `v - v`,
`v ^ v`, `v & 0`, `(int)(_g - _g)`, `(char *)_g - (char *)_g` are all removed before LR construction (identical
bytes), and `(int)arg0` keeps arg0 alive (spill + reload, 1212 B but 92.0). `0 * (_g != 0)` / `0 * !_g` act like
`0 * (int)_g` (the `ucvtl` of the pointer is not what costs the split).

**4. Colour diffs by uopt VAR id.** zdbug:5 LR ids are renumbered between bodies, but the VAR ids (`{1491|0}` =
the M-76 frame var) are stable, so `j.py com_u.txt new_u.txt` lists exactly which source values changed colour.
On the split body: the M-76 var had adjsave 1.0 vs 0.8 (one block fewer: the climb had dropped the I2 `if (0)`
block on yh -- restore it), and the s-term `>> 7` value (var 937) had 1.5 vs 3.0: in 329C's spelling
`((spr = (Spr *)(int)MAX(V, 0)), (int)spr)` V is used twice in the compare block, which puts it in a0 before the
(s16)yl LR and cascades (a0 / a1 / a2 / a3 / t1 all as the target). That s-term form alone: 97.013 / 1200, but
the lda remainder re-forms in t6 in the yl >= 0 arm.

**5. The last unit of the split budget.** Instrumented (`c334/t/adj.sh`) on that body: lda save 6 = cost 6 -> split
piece BFS with colours-left 13 (limit 26) accepts 47 / 37 / 42 and REJECTS block 48 (the yl >= 0 arm, s6 1 at
lr36 26): ONE neighbour too many. The append-spelling grid (texture x TEXRECT x RDPHALF_1 x RDPHALF_2 receiver,
128) found it at once: TEXRECT `me(CTX)->nD()` (`int n = dl->n++`) instead of `nextp()` (`dl->n = n + 1`): every
instruction word identical to the target (run 333 had moved TEXRECT to nextp() to free a0 for (s16)xh; with the
329C s-term form that is no longer needed, and nextp()'s extra n LR is the neighbour). Landed as the 329C recipe:
donor `gui_uso_ncc_2DE0.cpp` over an empty placeholder in both trees, NM donor block deleted, no rodata, jal relocs
as 329C. Lesson: when the instrumented trace says "N neighbours short", grid the cheap structural spellings
(append forms, receivers) on the split body before looking for new phantoms -- each spelling owns 0-2 LRs.

## kit CDXXIX (agent-g 2026-11-11, run 336): an inline's LOCAL takes a fresh edg pool word per expansion site, its PARAMETERS reuse words -- trading addF()'s `Gfx4B *g` local for a `put4B(Gfx4B *g, hi, lo)` helper frees the words a named per-site count (`int n = gfx->n; gfx->n = n + 1;`) needs, so post0b 4BAF4's ctx packets get their own count LRs at the same 0xF0 frame (99.409 -> 99.444); then a random round (B3 receiver depth 5 -> 2 + the final packet's BB split dropped, 99.480) and a per-site append-form grid (first packet back on the pool-count addO, 99.515) <a name="kit-cdxxix-agent-g-run336"></a>

_agent-g run 336, base 06fa16ab6. Three NM gains on post0b 4BAF4 (2c143ee6d, 47e4187c7, 6a091a664; 1692 B
throughout). Scratch `/tmp/claude-1000/g336/` (1 = 4BAF4, 2 = 4B620, 3 = bootup E68, 5 / 6 = 48AEC / 42938); tools
in `g336/t/`: run-335 `vd.py` (plus `vd2.py`: `MANG` / `LFN` for mangled ctor / method names and `.c` bases through
the dump `cc`), `pool.py DUMPDIR FN [MAXOFF]` (each `isvar M` pool / home word of the `-Wo,-zdbug:5` listing with
its LR colour, priority and blocks -- reads the word partition directly), `part.py` (per variant: which pool LRs
the ctx-packet blocks share with expression-packet blocks)._

**1. Where edg puts a temp.** Over the 4BAF4 sweeps (`pool.py` on ~900 dumps): (a) parameter temps of an inline
(`this`, hi, lo, me() / idv() arguments) come from a pool that is reused statement by statement -- the same word
serves the same "slot" in every packet, which is what makes one uopt LR span unrelated packets (kit CDXXVII);
(b) an inline's named LOCAL (`Gfx4B *g` in add()) is a NEW word at every expansion site and is never shared;
(c) a count read through k nested me2() moves the gfx / count words only once k passes the deepest receiver
chain of any other statement, and then the frame grows by the new words (all "pure" ctx-word variants of a
153-variant hold grid were 248-288 B frames). So separating a word costs frame bytes unless another site gives
some back.

**2. The trade that keeps the frame.** `void addF(u32 hi, u32 lo) { put4B(me2(this)->nextF(), hi, lo); }` with
`inline void put4B(Gfx4B *g, u32 hi, u32 lo) { g->w0 = hi; g->w1 = lo; }` (g is now a parameter: pooled) and
`Gfx4B *nextF() { int n = gfx->n; gfx->n = n + 1; return &gfx->buf[n]; }` (n is a local: one private word per
site). Frame stays 0xF0, the instruction stream is unchanged, and the three ctx-packet counts leave the expression
packets' count word: 99.409 -> 99.444. Spellings of the same thing (`int n; gfx->n = (n = gfx->n) + 1`, u32 n,
`gfx->buf + n`) are byte-identical; `int n = gfx->n++` and a put4B() without the me2() receiver are worse
(98.3 / 97.5); put4B() on the expression add() too: <= 98.56.

**3. Then the old spellings came back per site.** On that base a random mutation round (`mut2.py`, 200) found
B3 receiver depth 5 -> 2 together with dropping the final packet's `if (1) {}` BB split (each alone is flat or
lower): 99.480; a per-site grid of four append forms over the three ctx packets (63) put the FIRST packet back on
the run-335 form (local g + count through four me2(), `addO`) with else / final on put4B + named n: 99.515.
Re-grids on that base (first-packet nextO depth 0-7 x buf-side 0-2 x three add forms, 7-site me() depth sampling,
200 else / final named-count x put-receiver pairs, a mutation round): flat.

**4. Still open.** Residual = ctx a2 (target a3: 16 clip / reload lines), the ctx counts (t0 / a1 / a1, target a2),
the B4 MAX merge / inner temps (a1 / v1, target t0 / a2) and the B3 packet pointer (t0, target a2). The target's
a2 users (C0 in the clip, the ctx counts, the B4 inner MAX temp, the B3 packet pointer) and its t0 users (C4, the
first packet pointer, the B4 merge) look like two shared LRs. Clip operands wrapped in idv() DO join pool words
(C0 through three idv(): its first test lands in the receiver word -136, its second in the B4 MAX word), so the
"one pool word per register family" reading is testable, but no grid of C0 / C4 / ext wraps (96, plus 108 on the
second basin) moved fuzzy up. Negative: the receiver-across-call second basin (`recv->add(0x06000000, call(...))`,
ctx dropped, `ctx = 0;` dead store keeps the home) 98.24; a function-level count variable (frame 232; with
dead-stored pads 240 but 98.05); expression packets through statement-level `ctx = ...; ctx->add()` <= 99.39; the
`if (h) {}` / else-arm `if (self) {}` ctx-priority levers, `if (n) {}` in nextF (adds BBs, 97.7), BB splits between
the first packet and 0xEE (96.9): all flat or worse.

**4b. The ctx a2 / a3 swap IS reachable (scratch `g336/1/c2.cpp`, 99.385, not kept).** The first packet through a
named count with a folded use in the store (`int n = gfx->n; gfx->n = n + 1 + 0 * n; return &gfx->buf[n];`, put4B
receiver me2(this)) plus `if (h) {}` before the `& 2` test: the count LR rises 3.0 -> 4.0, is coloured before ctx
(3.6) and takes a2 like the target; ctx falls to a3, and with the first clip test flipped (`x > C0 + ext`) the
whole clip block, the 0x158 reload from sp+140 and the first packet's count / packet pointer are byte-exact. What
breaks: the expression receivers' pool word (-136) interferes with ctx in blocks 17 / 18 / 66 (the me() temp of
the ctx loads, the 0xEE / B3 receivers), so it drops from a3 to t0 (23 + 14 lines). Since the target has BOTH in
a3, the receivers and ctx must not overlap there; ctx loads at me() depth 0 (27 x 4 grid), a mutation round and
the receiver-across-call forms (120, <= 97.87) did not separate them. Note why ctx took a2 with v0 / a0 free: it
is live across the dlist call (spilled to sp+140), so the call's v0 / a0 are excluded -- the colour order is not
"lowest free". Kit CDXXVIII's method applied (full factorial, 1023 subsets in six 200-variant commands, of ten
atomic edits between the committed body and the structural bodies: first-packet addG, `if (h) {}`, clip flip,
ctx-load depth 0 x 3, BB splits before the final load / 0xEE / the final call, B3 depth 5; scored by a structural
signature = matching target lines over the clip, ctx packets, 0xEE, B4 and B3 regions, 177 lines, `g336/t/sig.py`):
best signature 143 / 177 is the c2 subset itself (99.385; committed 137 / 177 at 99.515), best fuzzy the committed
body. No subset gives the receivers a3 while ctx has it. Also negative: the else / final ctx packets as
`F4B(GS4B, 0x158, Ctx4B *)->addD(d)` with the dlist call INSIDE the inline (so `this` is a pool word spilled
across the call, the shape the target's sp+140 reload would have if ctx were a pool temp): 99.279 at frame 248;
every frame-240 compensation (nextO / addF me2 depths, B3 depth, put / local forms, 60) <= 90.6; the else / final
loads through dead ints (iz, or w / h / x / y for the final one) 98.84.

**5. bootup E68 (98.650): the target's shape is load + copy in BOTH phases.** Target phase 2: `lw t0,24(t0)` ...
`or v0,t0,zero` (the m variable, v0); phase 3: `lw t0,24(t0)` ... `or s1,t0,zero` (m again, s1, it crosses the

`blezl` delay slot that skips phase 2). Ours has the same load + copy shape in both phases but ONE m LR (s0) across
them. Volatile views of the MGR word (`MgrE68 * volatile *`, a volatile s32 view, a volatile char base) in phase 2,
phase 3 or both kill the copy instead (the load goes straight into s0) and free an s-register for self: 3012 B /
89.9-91.9; a const view, `&E68_MGR[0]`, chained stores into head / vp, other folded operands (arg2 / arg4 / k / cfg /
self / tlut) and dead stores between the phases (`m = 0;`, `m = m;`, ...) are byte-identical; a block-scoped m for
either or both phases is 88.4 (frame +8, self in s1 -- the block variable still takes a home), and code-free

without the phase-2 LR joining it.

**6. Item-2 near-misses checked for the pool-word lever.** 4B620 (99.725): append 1-2 forms (addG / addGN / addGI x
addOK / addO / addIK / addE / add x me() depth 0-2, 134) flat; free-inline named-count / put4B forms for appends

t8 / t9 ring + FP register residual, 48AEC (97.726) is the matrix concat's ugen t-temps, 42938 (98.856) is the
&D lda colours (t2 / t0 vs t4 / t3): no edg pool word involved, so the lever does not apply.

**6. Negatives after the exact (item 2, same run).** game_uso 3558 (93.853): the target's early vb loads + per-row
